title: DUB Tire Shine.. It's, Okay.
text:
The product calls for one or two coats for best effects. One coat, what I use and prefer, gives a nice gloss finish to the tire. It's slightly subdued and doesn't make the tire look like it's been coated with a half inch of wax like car tires do at the dealerships. Two coats, which I tried a day or two before having the car washed, was closer to those heavy gloss ultra wet looking tires that I don't really care for. The car wash actually knocked the shine down to about where I like it.

The spray is fairly durable. We had a couple days of rain and after a hundred or two miles in puddles and running on the highway there was still some gloss left on the tires.

Application is what I felt to be the weakest point of this product. The cap is supposed to be adjustable from narrow to wide spray. Mine may have been defective but no matter what way I turned the cap the spray was the same; nearly jet like, narrow and far too forceful. Attempting a light coat on the tire I still had considerable run off and puddles left on the garage floor which required cleaning and still left those sections of the floor slippery. This product just feels... wasteful. I much prefer a tire shine that applies as a liquid or paste and uses a sponge. You get better control, coverage and less waste.

As for the Orange Crush scent? There was a hint of orangeness in the air and while it wasn't unpleasant it wasn't something exceptional either.

All in all it's not a horrible product and I'll use up this can I was sent but I doubt I'll buy more when it's gone.

title: These Blades Are Horrible
text:
I purchased two Bosch Evolution blades for my 2007 Hyundai Accent on 02/07/2014. Today, 05/19/2014, I finally gave up and replaced them. I have never had wiper blades that performed this poorly. There was almost no contact with the windshield on either side. They left haze and streaks and would spatter water about requiring incessant re-wiping of the windshield to get it to clear. This, the 22" blade frequently chattered and hopped when there was only light moisture. I've never had new beam style wiper blades do that.

I purchased these Evolution blades because last season I had a set of Bosch's Clear Advantage on the car and really liked the way they performed. Unfortunately none of the local stores had them in stock when I needed new blades so I thought spending more on these supposedly better Evolution blades would be a no-brainer. With less than 3,000 miles and three months of use I just threw away thirty bucks because I trusted a company to make a quality product.

Highly dissatisfied.

title: Perfect Fit & High Quality {Edited June 2015}
text:

We've bought Fram brand filters for our vehicles for decades and I'll certainly be buying one of these the next time I need a replacement.

Edit June 2015 - I've purchased this same filter yearly and this year, 2015, there were significant changes to the filter. When I got the package and inspected the filter prior to installation I immediately contacted Amazon as I'd thought someone had swapped a cheaper filter for the one I was supposed to receive. Amazon rushed a replacement which was identical to the one I received. A call to Fram customer service verified that this filter was their product. Changes include the gasket edges are no longer Fram orange, they're black. The top of the filter used to be, and still is pictured as being, stiffened with a metal mesh. This mesh has been removed from the product. I've been purchasing this Fram filter for years because it gave the appearance of a better quality build. Now, it looks and feels like every other filter on the market. Fram is losing my loyalty with these changes. Docked two stars. Filter's "just okay" now.

text:

Even tightened to the point where you think you'll strip the threads, the extenders and anything attached to them still move. Run down to the hardware store and get appropriate stainless steel external lock washers. The pictures show my setup and it's incredibly solid.
Take your time during the installation process. Make sure everything is adjusted to your preferences before you do your final tightening. It took me a little more than an hour. My first test drive was a total charm. Just a few minor tweaks with the adjustable mirrors as I rode and that was it. Now I feel safe and confident when I'm on the road.

title: Easy 15min install, great oem part
text:
Installed a pair of these on a 2012 Silverado 5.3l. Mine has about 76k now, I believe these to be factory on mine. Passed inspection but I saw a lot of rust and imo they were likely bad..

The install took me about 15mins. Tools you will need is 21mm open end wrench, and a 21mm socket and ratchet. To make the job easier bring a set of side cutters to cut the metal strap on new strut, and a hammer if any of the bolts are stubborn. You can also use 2 21mm sockets & ratchets like I did since my 21mm wrench vanished.

Undo the nut on the bottom of strut, loosen up the top strut bolt, remove lower bolt, then remove upper.. when installing do the top first then lower. They say don’t cut the strap before, I always cut the strap right after I install top bolt, then as it expands have nut ready to slide in and work it right into mount.. if it fails however or you miss you should be able to compress it with one arm back in place. Worst case just use a jack to push it back up.

All and all this is a easy job anyone with zero mechanical ability can do don’t pay the crazy costs for someone else to do it. Watch a YouTube video for reference and save yourself some money.

title: I wouldn't waste the money...  Mine died quickly...
text:
So, I wanted to give this thing a fair shake and see how it would do. The packaging was nice. It comes with a bag to carry everything in as well which was a plus. With one exception, I was pretty content with the product. That exception being, it does not come with an attachment or converter for presta valves. Find me a mountain biker who isn't running some form of presta valve on their tires. They're few and far between. I'd have liked to seen one of the converters with the unit.

Everything started fine. I used it to fill a few bike tires and balls. Nothing crazy. I was hoping It would be something I'd throw in by bag when I went mountain biking but it's too heavy and bulky in my opinion. There are plenty of smaller options (CO2 carts, etc) for that. So I relegated this device for use around the house and if it worked out, I'd let the daughter keep it in her car in case of emergencies. Well it just so happened one of those moment's came up. The daughter's car had a flat which I repaired and then figured this would be the ultimate test for this pump. I selected car mode and off it went. The initial impression was annoyance at how slow it was going. It took 13 minutes to reach 30lb PSI at which point the pitch of the motor changed. It started smoking and we pulled it off the car. Needless to say, it's in the trash. Thankfully, I always have far better pump that runs off the car which got the tire to the proper pressure.

Let my free loss be your lesson. I'd avoid these style pumps if your intent was to use it for car tires. If I had to speculate I'd say whatever lubrication they have in the pump started to fail (the pitch change) and then the friction caused the smoking. It's just a guess since I'm not going to dismantle it. If your intent is just filling balls and bike tires, just get a floor pump or hand pump. Less to worry about in my opinion.

I am NOT recommending this option but it does work and the cable length is perfect.

Note: The ends of these have plastic versus the metal as shown in some of the stock photos (hopefully they update these).

You will know where you stand on actual cable length by seeing if the butterfly actually closes or not (which you can usually get a good idea based on the connecting rod on the top of the carb where this cable slides into).

I edited this review realizing this was my error and not due to the seller.

title: Fits 1997 Yamaha Kodiak 400
text:
I was able to get this one all set to go on my 97 Yamaha Kodiak 400. I was excited that it turned over and after a quick choke it fires up (but then died).
This does have the slightly larger male clip like the original. A few of the other listings have the smaller clip and it doesn’t fit properly.
Solenoid is a win!
Now it is onto the Carburetor and petcock valve replacement to get a more steady supply of fuel.

title: Wired wrong
text:
If it doesn’t work right out of the box, make sure the wires it connects to are in the same order.
Mine was not and I had to make adjustments to get it to work.
Luckily it’s not too difficult to slip a (super) small screwdriver in the connector head and push in the little clip to allow it to slip out of the connector (this would be on the female connector side and this light has the male end as fyi).

title: Big light
text:
I did not look at the specs on this one but it’s about the size of a regular sized ATV headlight. Remember to look at specs.
I saw it was for a range of small ATVs and snagged it assuming it would be the size of what a fog light or thereabouts may be but it’s bigger.
Likely 5-6” wide by about 5” tall.
Overall still a cool light and with some mods works well on our little 90cc Falcon (no mods needed for the wiring.

title: Heavy duty
text:
This was what I hoped for in terms of a product that looked quality but seemed too good on price. The item is either painted well or powder coated and the ball seems to be chrome dripped. I had 0 issues with any scuffing (packaged well) and it was easy to install (cotter pin was designed well) and the lock pin also fit great (sometimes this can be an issue where the hole was designed without the concept of paint causing the gap to narrow).

Very pleased

title: Great value
text:
Great gauge in the overall wiring. The setup was easy and quick with a search of a video. You will need to drill the converter box screw into the wall of the vehicle behind the taillight, but it didn't cause issues or any visible cosmetic concerns (since it's not visible once the taillight is re-installed).

There are a few kits out there that look like they use speaker wire whereas this is a thicker gauge.

My issue was in routing the wire up to the battery from the underside of the vehicle. My suggestion would be to start the battery wire from dropping it down from the battery and running it back to the taillight. Feeding it up through the engine bay was a struggle (I used an old wire hanger and dropped it down with a small hook up and tied off the battery wire to it, then pulled it back up carefully).

title: Great buy!
text:
Overall a great fit. At first it seems like it might not but that’s because of the precision design. It is important to lay out for 24 hours to make sure it lays flat. If not it can stay flexed up in some areas like along the outside edge of the mat.

It has saved the van carpet and is fairly easy to clean. The difficult part is cleaning dirt while it’s in place as I’d normally remove mats to shake dirt first. This you vacuum first then wipe down thoroughly with a soapy wash cloth.

Would buy again and do recommend getting the driver and passenger side mats also as you’ll want them once this is in place.

title: Great gift item!
text: I picked this one up because it seemed a little more user friendly versus a scanner that just hard reads codes. I got this as a gift for my stepdad and he is thoroughly enjoying using it. It does take a little getting used to but so does any new device. It functions well and I really like the screen functionality.

title: Works great
text: I added a small bit of this to my golf cart's gas tank because it was having a rough start and issues with top speed. It took a little bit to notice since the cleaner had to blend with the fuel and then pass through the system. Once that happened it has worked quite a bit better. If there's more to add I'll update this review at a later date, but so far it does what it says!

title: Not as pictured
text:
The fuel filters are somehow even cheaper than what is pictured above. These do not appear as though they'll hold up over time. Trying to return these is going to be a nightmare, just skip the risk and try something else.

Normally I feel my reviews can weigh both the pro's and con's but the con's outweigh any pro's here.

title: Could be better
text:
I’ve had these pads on for a few months now and they have held up decently well thus far. It would be better served if a small packet of pad grease were included. It further saves the convenience of having to go to the store to purchase such a small item.

If you have the packet, all is well and these will work great.

title: Serves its purpose.
text: Curt produces quality items and this has worked well to keep our popup locked in place on our hitch. High quality.

title: Great
text: As advertised. They work great for our razor scooters and charged up well

title: Must have
text: It's a longer wrench which is needed to apply enough torque to loosen the nut. Overall, it works great and is an essential purchase for anyone who owns a Hitch.

title: Awesome
text: Curt makes amazing products. The quality is always stellar and they use great materials for their products. Definitely a worthwhile purchase and I'm 100% satisfied.

title: Save your original screws and you'll be fine
text: This product is decent, however it may not fit your pop-up so be sure that if you are changing the latch to save the original screws. The ones provided with this kit are a bit too long and did not fit our pop-up. Overall, the quality is great, however the lack of variance in screw size is a notable concern.

title: Great kit!
text:
Overall this is a great kit and it's very useful to check out their video tutorials on installation. I found that to be much easier than to follow the provided directions. My only issue is with routing the wire from the battery to the back end of the vehicle, that is a difficult process. It may be something Curt cannot perfect, but if that's possible, I'd definitely give it 5 stars. Otherwise, 4 for now.
Everything worked great and was packaged well. No frays or issues of any sort.

title: Go with something else
text: It worked great for the first month, then it went back to the way it was in my jeep which was an inconsistent blower. I bought a different resistor and it has worked very well.

title: My EVOO substitute for cooking and baking.
text: Adds great flavor when sauteing meat and poultry.

title: Not the easiest to install, but worth it
text:
Had it not been for the tucking tool that was included I would have returned this. Getting your license plate inserted in the"frame" is not the easiest task and I tried it at first using brute force. Turns out I wasn't the brute that I thought I was, and after a learning curve, managed to mount my license plate into the frame. After that it was a lot easier than normal license plate holders because it's easy to see the alignment holes on this frame versus having to guess. One of the reasons why I purchased this is my Florida "Vietnam War Veteran" plate was partially obscured by the dealer's frame on my vehicle. The number and graphic of the Vietnam Service Medal were displayed, but the tag, "Vietnam War Veteran" was obscured. To many folks the medal on the plate is meaningless for identifying the specific war in which I served. The tag was the information I wanted to display, and this frame made that possible.

Mission accomplished!

title: Great for quick vacuuming
text: My wife and I share this between our two identical vehicles (2021 Mitsubishi Outlander Sports). The cord allows the vacuum to reach any interior spot in the vehicles, so that is a plus. Most of our work is the driver and passenger side floor mats, although we also give dashboards, door storage and consoles the once over. The vacuum is powerful enough for our needs - a quick, once over pass to keep the vehicles clean between our bi-monthly trips to a local car wash that does a great job of maintaining the interiors and exteriors of our vehicles.  If you need a more pro-level vacuum for deep cleaning this is probably not what you want. If you want a touch-up tool to keep your car's interior looking nice, this is an inexpensive and effective tool for the job.

title: Superior performance to Mitsubishi's OEM bulbs; will not cure Mitsubishi electrical flaws though
text:
I drive a 2016 Mitsubishi Outlander. This vehicle has an electrical design flaw in that if you are even slightly bumped in the rear the headlights will go, one-after-the-other, within days. I purchased these as my third set of replacements after being rear-ended causing major damage (and the loss of both headlights), and not long after being slightly tapped by a careless driver whose foot slipped off her brake at a stop sign. The second event caused no visible damage, but the left, then the right headlight went out within a few days. I had ordered these from Amazon after the first incident because a web search revealed that this is a design problem with my year/make/model vehicle.

After I installed them the lights were considerably brighter than the original that came with the car and the OEM replacement bulbs used after the first incident. I use my headlights in all driving conditions and so far no issuse. I am prepared for an inevitable outage though, but I blame Mitsubishi for that, not Sylvania.

Bottom line: if you are replacing OEM bulbs this set is far superior with respect to lighting.

title: Some issues, but still a decent unit for the price
text:
Mine did not come with the inflation adapters, not does the automatic shutoff work. Frankly I do not need the adapters and can live with the lack of auto shutoff. What I did not like is the threaded end of the inflation hose. It is difficult to line up to tire stems, especially in cold weather.

I recently had to use my pump in 33 degree F weather in east Tennessee and screwing on the inflation hose to the tire stems on all four tires was difficult. I believe the issue is very precise and close tolerances. From a manufacturing perspective this is a good thing, but in real life use it is a pain.

Major pluses: the cables and hose are easily long enough to accommodate my Mitsubishi Outlander SUV, and the light is bright. The pump is compact and is a lot faster when it comes to inflating tires than the pump that it replaced. Also, the price is right, which is why I can overlook some of the issues.

title: Precision tolerances and extremely beefy construction (including the lock)
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Others have thoroughly (and helpfully) covered this pin with both verbal and graphic descriptions. Here are a few of my observations.

First, this is exceptionally well made. Even the 1/2 inch pin is sufficiently hardened to prevent either breakage or intentional theft. The 5/8 inch pin is one of the heaviest and beefiest hitch pins I have come across.

Second, the lock is as beefy as the rest of the assembly. It is no weak afterthought, but a truly well designed anti-theft device that can withstand a sledge hammer. It can also withstand tension and other normal forces from pulling a trailer.

There are O-rings on both pins to seal the lock against water and salt, as well as a sealing end cap on the lock mechanism itself. The parts are machined to close tolerances and the fit of either pin into the lock assembly is smooth. The lock's internals operate very smoothly without binding, which indicates that that part's design is as well thought out as the overall assembly.

Overall, this is superbly constructed and is both strong enough to haul to the rated capacities for either pin, and can withstand all but the most aggressive attempts at destruction and theft.

title: Very handy NOT for jump starting vehicles
text:
I received this set as a free review sample. The dual clamps that are included are the primary reason why I rated this so highly. I was able to use those and a pair of simple cable terminals that I crafted to power a [[ASIN:B00OU9U4P8 21" 126W CREE LEDS Flood Spot Combo Beam Light Bar]] as a work light. I do not think that these clamps can be used to jump a vehicle since the fuse in the lighter adapter is rated at 15 Amps and most vehicle starters draw 150 Amps (and sometimes double that). I am mentioning this to set expectations.

Another reason why I rated this set so highly is the cables are heavy duty, and all of the ends (except those on the clamps) have beefy strain reliefs.

Note: this has a fuse like legacy lighter socket adapters, so there does not appear to be any protective integrated circuit to prevent overcharging or overheating. On the other hand this is not designed to extend phone and tablet chargers, and for uses like powering a work light, or an air pump or vacuum the fuse is sufficient. Moreover, you can easily replace it if you do overload it - that is a nice contrast against most of the newer, sealed adapters with the integrated circuits.

Bottom line: I found this to be immediately useful and well made. As long as you understand that you CANNOT use this to jump start a vehicle you will probably be pleased with it.

title: Nice quality and complete mounting kit included
text:
I received a set of these as a free review sample. Compared to local prices these are an absolute bargain, which is one of the reasons why I rated them so highly. The other major reason is these are nicely constructed and can easily last in harsh environments.

Do note that while the product description gives the weight as 1.3 pounds, each light (without the included mounting hardware) only weights in at ten ounces. That makes them light enough to mount on thin, light surfaces.

Considering the low amperage draw the each unit puts out a lot of illumination. They run cool with the large heat sinks, which comprise a large part of the outer body. While the set that I received did not come with instructions, these are super easy to install if you are handy with 12V DC electrical wiring, In fact, the operating range is much wider, so it will also work with 24V sources. The pigtail is a foot long, so you have a lot of flexibility in splicing it into your wiring.

You do need to be aware of the fact that a receiving nut that is part of the mounting scheme is in a slotted track and will rattle around if you do not plan to use the included mounting kit. I tested mine out by rigging a splice to a longer cable, then connecting that to a [[ASIN:B004SFRW68 FJC (45268) Replacement Booster Cable with 800 Amp Rating Clamp Set]]. I almost decided to continue using that set up and pressing one of these lights into service as a work light, but these do tend to run a little hot when stationary after thirty or so minutes (despite the large heat sink surface.)

Bottom line: these are high quality (and inexpensive) lights that will add a lot to off road or work vehicles.

title: Well made, bright with a few mounting options
text:
I received these as a free review sample. My high rating is based on the relatively low cost, build quality and versatility. Know up front that these are not plug and go. They operate off DC voltage, but do have a wide operating range for just about any type of vehicle that I can think of. A truly nice feature is the brightness of of the LED array, but will easily cut through fog and the dark.

They have a few installation options. You can use a mounting bracket (U-shaped) that you will need to provide, craft a mounting bar, flush mount them in cutouts. Mounting hardware (four sets of bolts, washers and nuts) are provided.

The lights are relatively light, weighing in at just over a pound each, so flush mounting on sheet metal or even plastic is possible. Each unit is 4.75x3.857 and three inches deep. The four mounting holes on the face are, center-to-center, 4.25 inches at the widest point and 1.25 inches high.

Wiring is up to you, and there are no instructions. However, the 16 inch pigtail has thick insulation and the color coded wires are easy to figure out since the positive (hot) wire is red and ground is black.

Bottom line: this set is an inexpensive way to add two well made lights to a vehicle. If you opt for a mounting bar, a second (and even a third) pair are possible.

title: Excellent construction for a stationary organizer; if you want to also use it for carrying there are caveats
text:
I received the 22"/15.7"/10.2" model as a free review sample. Note that there are four different models offered on this product page at the time of this review, and each of them has features the others do not. In order to set your expectations you should select the size you want, then carefully read the product description because other reviewers have noted differences between what they are reviewing and general specs. The one I am reviewing is identical to the product specs for that particular size.

As an organizer this is both sturdy and, in the case of the size I was provides, more than sufficient to organize a space in my 2016 Outlander SUV. As long as you are planning to use this as a static storage crate, or to store lighter items it's perfect. I mention this because while the sides are super sturdy, and the bottom constructed to bear a lot of weight, the carrying handles are on the flimsy side.

My primary use is to store essentials like a battery jump starter, tire inflation pump, and small tool and first aid kits. That leaves me with a separate compartment for odds and ends. There is a nylon divider that is attached via Velcro for the separate compartment that I could use, but I have not as of yet. The divider is thin and is not designed to hold heavy items in place.

Mine has a set of mesh pockets along one of the long sides that are handy, and two flap pockets along one of the short sides. Those are good for maps, manuals and the such, but not much else.

If you intend to use this as a store and carry type of bag I recommend keeping the load to fifty pounds or less. The bottom can easily handle that load, but the handles are the Achilles' heel on the model I have.

Overall, this is better constructed than many trunk organizers (I own two others from other brands), and if you intend to leave it in your trunk strictly as an organizer it's perfect in my opinion.

title: Excellent design with lots of heft and leverage
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I have other escape hammers that are integrated into tire pressure gauges, but this one is both different and superior. I realize that is a bold thing to say, but unlike the others I own or have tested this is designed from the ground up to work as an escape hammer.

The main difference is how this one's weight is amassed in the head. That, plus the long length of the handle, provides a lot of leverage that translates into striking power. I actually tested one of the integrated hammers on an old piece of safety glass and in a controlled environment, like having it flat and I allowed to stand it worked perfectly. The reality is when you really need one you are likely to be sitting in the driver's seat and attempting to break the glass within a confined space. That extra weight and leverage could make all the difference in a real life situation.

The head weighs around six ounces (the entire tool weights around 8.5 ounces), so the weight distribution is ideal for striking. The overall length is about nine inches, so the leverage is definitely there. Finally, the pointed end is a lot more pronounced than on any other escape hammer that I own.

This is too long for most consoles or glove boxes. I keep mine in the side pocket of the driver's side door in my vehicle. Since receiving this I've relegated the integrated air pressure gauge/escape hammer to being just an air pressure gauge and a secondary hammer on the passenger's side.

title: Nice for vehicles and office chairs - well constructed
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Please read the product description for dimensions (which I verified) to make sure this will git your vehicle. It is a perfect fit for either of the front seats in my 2014 Mitsubishi Outlander SUV, and it also works on my office chair.

Some products claim genuine leather when, in fact, it isn't. The leather side of this cushion looks and feels like the real thing, and even has pores. It may be PU or bicast leather (real leather backed by polyurethane), but I am not able to verify it one way or the other. There is a slight chemical odor when you first unpack it, but that quickly dissipates, and may be a leather treatment.

The stitching on the piping is straight and tight, and the piping itself appears to be nylon. It's made to last. Another indication of quality construction is the stitching on the patchwork.I like the way that the padding (thin as it is) has a tuck feel that is actually comfortable. When I tested this on my office chair I used it for a good five hours with some time to walk around and stretch. In my vehicle I tested it during my frequent trips to Daytona (about forty-five minutes each way). It's comfortable in both scenarios. I am not sure how well I will like it in my vehicle when it gets hot and humid. Time will tell on that. However, despite being leather, when I am driving I am not slipping or sliding on the cushion, so that is a major plus.

Bottom line: this is a decent padded cover that will definitely protect your vehicle's seat(s). It's comfortable, kind of classy looking, and well made.

title: Would be prefect with decent instructions
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because the holder does not ship with instructions and the ones in the photos on this product page are still a little hazy. I did figure it out and am pleased with the results, but a five star product will have clear instructions and this one does not.

On the plus side, this will easily hold a Samsung Galaxy Note 5 (and probably an iPhone 6+ since they are close in size.) Of course if you have a case like an OtterBox Defender series all bets are off. I tested a Note 4 with one of those and while it sort of fit, the grip was not solid like on a Note 5 with a bumper style case.

It will easily accommodate a 12 ounce can of cola. A 16.9 ounce bottle of DeSani water also fit, but the weight and the enter of gravity of the bottle in the holder were iffy at best.

This ships with three different sizes of grabbers for vent blades. They are surprisingly sturdy, but, as mentioned, in the absence of clear instructions be prepared for a little frustration. Also, there is an adjustable bumper that extends to create a stabilizing tension once mounted. There is a tiny button that must be depressed to adjust it. It took me ten minutes to figure that out.

Bottom line: I would not hesitate to give this a solid five stars has there been better documentation. If you want an easy solution and hate tinkering this is probably not for you.

title: Works wonderfully on some cars - still valuable without the grab bar
text:
I received this as a free review sample. It works as a grab bar on my 2014 Mitsubishi Outlander, and will work on just about any vehicle that has a 'U' shaped door latch (it's on the door post behind the driver or passenger.) There are other types of latches, especially on older vehicles, including mushroom-shaped ones and slots, so unless there is a U shape latch this will not work as a grab post.

As a window breaker this is probably THE best one I have seen. I have other emergency tools that incorporate a window breaker, but none that come close to this one for effectiveness. There is more than enough heft and leverage to make short work of breaking out of a vehicle in an emergency. The same with the seat belt cutter. It's another excellent feature that is the best of its kind that I have seen in a consumer, multi-use tool.

The flashlight is a decent feature. It's powerful enough to illuminate small work areas and is even good enough to function as a path finder in total darkness. I wish it had modes, including one that would flash, as well as the ability to operate on just one of the two LEDs to conserve battery. As it is, both LEDs either turn on or off at the press of the button. No in between.

This comes with two CR2032 batteries - easy to find and replace - and scant instructions that are on the sides of the box. While most of the device is self-explanatory, it would be nice to have instructions showing the locations of the door latches and the more common types with which this will and will not work.

Bottom line: this tool has the best seat belt cutter and window breaker of any I have used or tested. You need to verify that the grab bar will work with your vehicle, but even if it does not, this is a handy emergency tool in its own right.

title: Pro features and built like a tank
text:
I received this as a free review sample. The main reasons why I gave it the highest possible rating are build quality and the auto-shutoff feature.

While this is relatively compact, it's heavy. Most of the weight is from the fact that this is a well made compressor, with attention to details like heavy duty air hose, and base and housing. The only possible weak link is the power cable, and that is as good as any that come on other home compressors. The combined length of the power cord and the air hose allow me to easily reach any tire on my 2014 Mitsubishi Outlander with room to spare.

For me the best feature is the auto-shutoff, which means that I can concentrate on my surroundings if I am using this alongside a road instead of the gauge itself. In that respect this is as much a safety feature as it is a convenience.

Another reason for the high rating is this has some power behind it. The previous compressor I carried would huff and puff and take more than a few minutes to reinflate a mere 5 PSI differential when weather changed my tire pressure. This compressor does it in less than a minute. I know because I deflated one of my tires to 25 PSI, then 28 PSI to test this compressor. My normal pressure is 33 PSI (odd, I know, but that is what my vehicle requires). From both pressures this compressor quickly brought the tire back to where it should be.

Finally, the duty cycle on this is thirty minutes continuous with a thirty minute rest period. That is significantly more than most home type compressors.

I have one caveat that is important to note: as far as I can tell this is for non-commercial vehicles only. There is no maximum PSI rating for this compressor. It certainly works on my tires, and I am guessing would work on passenger vehicles up to 40 PSI. The only limit listed is on a tag on the bottom of the unit warning against using it for high pressure truck tires. Take that into consideration before you leap into a purchase. For vehicles such as mine this is one of the best home type that I have ever used. If you need to inflate at high pressures and probably over 40 PSI I recommend looking elsewhere.

title: Heavy duty and well made
text:
I received these as a free review sample over three months ago and have been testing them for over a month. The main thing I love is they are exceptionally well constructed.

Since others have covered many aspects of these lights I'll spare you repeats. Here are a few things that I think are important; First, the pigtail that you need to splice into your electrical system is very heavy duty. You will need to run a lead wire from your vehicle's fuse box to it with a waterproof connector. I am mentioning this because this set is designed to be installed by professionals or hobbyists who are familiar with wiring.

The lights in this set have a wide operating range between 9 and 36 volts, so as long as you have access to a DC power source in that range powering them will be easy.

These are truly off-road quality. In fact, I want to emphasize that for regular, public road use you will want to connect these to a switch because they are bright enough to blind oncoming drivers.

If you are looking for heavy duty lights for off road use these are rugged and built like a tank.

title: Fast and convenient
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I always carry a portable air compressor in my vehicle because the the sensors in my vehicle display low air pressure when there is a 4 PSI drop. That usually happens four or five times a year due to radical temperature changes.

The compressor I had been using does the job, but is slow and also has short cycle times. By slow I mean that it can take three minutes to bring by pressure from 28 to 32 PSI, and by short cycle times I mean it can run for ten minutes, but requires a thirty minute rest period. For a vehicle such as mine that is not an issue. However, this compressor can go from 28 to 32 PSI in thirty seconds, which is five times faster, and has a cycle time that can run continuously for thirty minutes (as long as you are inflating tires or other objects that require less than 35 PSI), with only a twenty minute cooling time. Given the cycle time on this compressor it's almost of the quality for a small repair shop.

A nice feature that this kit has is an adapter kit for balls, rafts and the such. Most automotive compressors work strictly on tire valve stems. Plus you can inflate objects up to 80 PSI. I was unable to test that feature, and also suspect that the cycle time is greatly reduced if you do use this compressor for such. Keep that in mind, but also note that most portable automotive compressors in this price range only go to 40 PSI (if that.)

Another thing I like about this one is the long electrical cord is heavy duty. The one on my older unit is a lot thinner and less sturdy. Still, the older one has served me for close to four years, so this one with the better cord should last a lot longer.

Finally, this will work off your vehicle's lighter socket and reach up to ten feet. It easily reached each tire on my 2014 Mitsubishi Outlander, which is a fairly long SUV. Had I been pulling a trailer I could have still reached tires on it - regardless of length - by using any power pack with EC5 terminals. Most power packs with jump starting capabilities have such terminals, including one by this brand (the [[ASIN:B00WYO2OYK RoyPow Ultrasafe 4.0L Car Jump Starter 400A Peak Current & 12000 mAh Portable External Battery Charger]]. That is but one of many on the market that will work with this compressor.

Bottom line: this is not the least expensive compressor on the market. It is, however, one of the sturdiest and fastest in its price range. Plus if you want a compressor that can go up to 80 PSI this one is among a very few in its class that can do that. Please remember my caveat above that I was unable to test this at that pressure and do not know the cycle times for this device at inflation pressures above 35 PSI.

title: Handy and a value for the price
text:
I purchased this kit specifically because of the price. That is the main reason why I rated it so highly. I wanted a kit to throw into my hardware bag for musical performances because I am always in the need of a small tool to repair a stand, pedal or other small issue. This kit contains ninety percent of what I need to effect those repairs.

The kit is a lot heavier than I expected, and the tools are actually a cut above what I thought I would be getting. If properly cared for they should last years if used for occasional minor repairs.

Note that these are SAE sizes, so if you are purchasing it for vehicles make sure that your vehicle does not use metric sizes. Also be aware that this is not a complete kit. It has the essentials for most minor repairs and temporary fixes. For a comprehensive kit you will need to either add to this or look elsewhere.

One final note: mine came with a nearly invisible plastic tie that needed to be snipped before I could open the case. I thought the zipper was broken, but on closer examination the tie prevented it. I am guessing it is used to keep the case closed during shipping. Other than that I have no complaints and am thinking of getting another for home use.

title: Heavy-duty and complete kit
text:
I received this as a free review sample. A few things you need to take into account are that this is a fairly heavy and long light bar. It weighs in the neighborhood of fifteen pounds and at fifty inches long you need to make sure you have sturdy mount points on your vehicle at that distance apart.

This is built to take a beating. I am especially impressed with the heavy duty wiring (and wiring harness), as well as the non-shatter plastic lens protecting the LEDs. I have other light bars designed for off-road that are wimpy when it comes to wiring, so that particular feature is a major plus. The wiring on this unit appears to be designed to take the same abuse as the light housing and even the strong brackets that come with it.

The brackets are, like the rest of the assembly, well made and will hold the entire bar firmly in place. However, as I mentioned above you need to make sure that you have secure, reinforced mounting points on your vehicle that are fifty inches apart. Also take into account that with only two mount points with that long spacing, unless there are absolutely sturdy spots to which you mount this light it could sag or tear loose. That is not an inherent issue with the light assembly as much as it is a caveat about some vehicles. Measure and carefully examine where you intend to mount this before making a final purchase decision.

Once installed this will provide a LOT of illumination. In fact, that is one of the most impressive features and reasons why I rated it so highly.

Overall, if you have a vehicle that will support mounting this light you will probably love it as much as I. The construction is solid, it's made for true off-road and harsh environments, and no corners appear to be cut in quality.

title: A little awkward to use, but still a godsend for me
text:
I routinely travel east-west from inland to Daytona and Ormond beaches almost daily, so when I was offered one of these as a review sample I jumped on the opportunity. There seems to be a love it or hate it attitude, so I will explain why I love it, what I do not like about it and you decide.

What I do like first: it's not the best designed solution. The clip is a little difficult to initially slide over my visor. Also, the 'visors' are a little stiff, and the operational requirements are not exactly user friendly. Finally, these are more filter than visor, and in that role they work, but are really plastic sheets.

Why I gave it five stars anyway. I travel towards the rising sun going to my destination and into the setting sun when going home - this is almost daily. Some days I am not directly affected depending on weather, exact time of day and even time of year. Other days the sun is directly in my eyes and frankly the trips are unsafe. This product cuts down on the direct glare and makes my trips on most days infinitely safer. For that reason alone I love this - warts and all.

While the sun visor (or filter, actually) works, I have not found the night visor to be that effective, I usually do not have problems with night driving so only tried it a few times and decided that I did not need it. If you are purchasing this primarily for night driving factor my comments in, but also know that I did not have a problem to begin with for that type of driving.

Still undecided? Since there are reviews rating this from 1 to 5 stars in almost equal numbers, read a sampling of those. Many make valid points for and against, so you can decide if this is the product for you. It is for me, but not for everyone.

title: Passed a big test with flying colors
text:
This conditioner took an old, dried leather jacket and restored it beyond my expectations. I received my bottle of this as a review sample and since I have a responsibility to thoroughly test such samples I put this one to a rigorous test. I have a twenty year old motorcycle jacket that I pull out on the few days a year it gets below freezing in central Florida. The jacket's finish was dried and had started to crack in places. A perfect test candidate!

Since this is not a cleaner I used a favorite product called [[ASIN:B00D010TDY Premium Leather Cleaner and Conditioner]]. Once I got the surface of the jacket clean I applied this per directions. The first pass made a large difference because although the cracks were still there the leather itself started to become softer and more supple. I buffed it out with an old t-shirt and applied another treatment. This time around the leather had taken on the same feel as when the jacket was new. Of course the cracks are still there and the spots that have worn through the dye are still showing, but the transformation is nothing short of remarkable in my opinion.

Note that this conditioner will work beautifully if you follow the directions. It's still requires some time and effort. Also, if you are tempted to take shortcuts the results will not be as spectacular. I almost passed up the buffing step because the jacket was starting to look great. I am glad I didn't because buffing it out and doing the conditioning process for a second pass took a good restoration of the leather and made it remarkable.

This stuff definitely works as advertised if you use it correctly. If you have a leather treasure that you need to bring back to life this is the key.

title: Heavy and thick - perfect protection
text:
This is both a functional and attractive piece of apparel. Functionally this is sufficiently thick and heavy to protect against a spill. The vest weights over two pounds according to a scale on which I weighed it, so the amount of leather used is generous. The thickness significantly cuts down on the chill factor when riding too.

Construction is as heavy-duty as the leather. The review sample I received has double stitching, and the seams are perfectly aligned and will probably outlast me. The leather itself has a nice pebble grain for durability, although at a slight distance it appears smooth.

For added convenience there are two inside and two outside pockets. Plus the snap fasteners in lieu of buttons makes this even more convenient. I love the old school look of real buttons, but when this vest gets wet buttons would be a hassle to fasten. The snaps look like the real thing and are, well, a snap to fasten.

The lining is another plus. It, like the leather, is thick and will probably last longer than my sixty-five year old carcass. It's also a nice touch of comfort.

I will say that as a musician who is often under stage lights that this vest can become a bit too warm too fast. On a bike it's excellent protection and will keep you warm, but for other activities in a warmer climate you may find it to be a bit too hot. Since it's designed for bikers, though, this is a major plus and one of the many reasons why I awarded it five stars.

One final point: the price at the time of this review is thirty bucks. That is a bargain you will not often see for such a well constructed vest.

title: Long Review. Oil for street use, strip, and the future.
text:
Long Review. I hope that you take the time to read it.

I have always loved Pennzoil because growing up it was the oil of choice of successful top fuel funny car, top fuel dragster, alcohol dragster, alcohol funny car, and the Altered classes. Every successful winning sprint car I remember ran Pennzoil. Also this oil was a common sight for the mom and pop or hobbyist racers who were not supported by big names. I specifically remember when Pennzoil made the finest racing oil that sadly they have discounted production of. Their racing oil was the only one I can remember that said it was specifically formulated for use with methanol and nitromethane fuels. I can remember watching my father make a quarter mile pass and those win lights on both sides of the track were Pennzoil lights they were a beautiful sight at night I miss those. I loved using their racing oil I wish they would bring it back. This oil has proven itself over many years to be the best. You probably think I am paid or endorsed by Pennzoil I ain't. Speaking from my own personal experience with this oil in street, racing, and air cooled engine applications I can tell you it is excellent. I have sent this oil off for analysis by caterpillar diesel and it returned with much better numbers than the popular brand that rhymes with vaseline people find so amazing. Look up the sheer numbers of this oil that will impress you. This oil has plenty of zinc along with the neccessary wear additives to protect older or even newer engines. This oil has always been made from the best bases and it has improved I think. Plus this oil supprts American jobs it is made right here in the USA.
If you think im full of nonsense contact the manufacturer they have always had the best technical support right here in the USA. They have answered many questions for me and I appreciate them they have saved me a lot of headaches

A few examples using this high mileage conventional oil.

One engine running this oil is 37 years old, all original, and high mileage, and no leaks. Had the original clutch and flywheel replaced at 137k. The mechanic who did the job said he was impressed my rear main seal was not seeping and looked perfectly fine. This 37 year old engine has had 10w-30 conventional Pennzoil used for every oil change at 3000 miles since it was bought from the dealership. Compression last tested it was just fine, oil pressure was fine, it doesn't consume/burn oil, it runs excellent, and it does not leak a drop of oil never has. When I did a valve adjustment on this engine everything was impressively clean no sludge or wax buidup. I plan to stick with this oil because I know it works in this engine.

This is my choice of oil in gasoline or propane burning air cooled single cylinder commercial equipment engines. Also commercial single or twin cylinder generator or portable welders that call for 10w-30 weight oil this is the best in my opinion. These engines get used hard, run long hours, operate in extreme conditions, operate in the worst environments, and need the best oil. I change the oil at the intervals that the manufacturer says and have absolutely no problems.

My other observation is that current gasoline is not what it used to be especially with the 10% ethanol. What I do on engines using this oil burning the current grades of trashy pump gasoline is change it on time at 3000 miles or at three months.

Engines I have disassembled for repair or rebuild that have used only conventional Pennzoil from day one that have been cared for by their owner I have never seen any "sludge"or premature wear. I can say I have honestly never seen any problems that were in any way oil related in an engine using the correct weight and designation of Pennzoil. Even engines that were used in harsh environments or engines ran hard this oil protected them perfectly. So these are other reason why I stick with this brand.

Keeping your oil and filter changed in all engines is just cheap insurance in my opinion. Every oil related failure I have ever seen was from not enough oil, wrong type or weight of oil, and people never changing it because they think they are smarter than an oil manufacturer who performs more testing than they can imagine. So if you believe all of these stupid oil conspiracy theories I honestly feel sorry for any respectful responsible mechanic you will have to deal with when you have a failure.

One pickup I had that under the hood was a 350 cubic inch V8 manufactured in 1976. This engine had nothing but conventional 10w-30 Pennzoil used in its engine at every 3000 mile oil change by the first owner. This vehicle was bone stock with no modifications. It did a whole lot of towing and hauling never giving any problems. When I got this pickup it had an excess of over 300k plus miles on it still running strong. The engine only consumed a tiny bit of oil from wore valve guides and tired valve seals. This engine also did not leak or seep oil all gaskets were factory I ran the heck out of it and it probably had 400k plus miles on it. Just like the previous owner I used 10w-30 conventional Pennzoil in that engine and that engine lasted many miles.

Ideas and other thoughts

This oil will help the old seals stay pliable. If you don't believe me go buy some NOS 40 year old oil seals. Allow them soak a while in this high mileage 10w-30 oil. I did this test myself and I was pleased to notice a difference so try it out it was a fun little experiment. If you see a seep or a little oil mist on a seal on your old engine try this oil you will notice an improvement. Also If your using synthetic and noticing a little oil seeping try this oil instead I honestly like it more than the synthetic.

By the way if you read the above I am not referring to a leaking bad wore out seal. Those leaks can only be fixed by replacement of the OEM seal or do yourself a favor buy an OEM equivalent gasket. I recommend the gasket brand old Smokey Yunick swears by in his Power Secrets. To sum it all up little common sense says no oil can fix a damaged or defective gasket, seal, or poorly maintained engine.

Closing thoughts :-)

Get yourself a few big bottle of this great oil, buy some oil filters, get those kids away from those computers/phones, start that kid changing oil young. Together you and your kid changing the oil, oil filter, checking old oil in the drain pan for debris, teach proper safe handling of oil, disposing of oil properly, and importantly make some memories. I can remember handing my father Pennzoil in cans at the drag strip and in his garage. I can also remember that first time I changed oil with my father. So build some memories along with character with your oil change. I guarantee your kids will thank you when they are older and you will have some fun memories. Doesn't have to be your kid it can be any kid by the way. Thank you so much for reading this review and I hope that it has helped you.

title: Beware of Incomplete Description
text:
It's hard to rate an accessory like a battery charger under the categories "fun", "educational value" and "durability". After all, how much fun can a battery charger possibly be?
My first charger went bust after a few years (with infrequent use), so durability is not at the highest level.
Caution - The description on this item is incomplete, and not as informative as it should be.
The Power Wheels Jeep requires two 6V batteries, and comes with a charger that charges both batteries at the same time. The Super 6-Volt battery charger is described as a "replacement charger for the 6-volt batteries that run Power Wheels toys", and is listed by Amazon as an accessory to the 6V Power Wheels battery.
Please be warned that this charger only charges ONE battery, a significant little fact that is not mentioned until you get the item, where the box clearly states " For 6-Volt or Super 6-Volt system with one battery." For non-technical people like myself, the inclusion of that wording in the description would have saved me a lot of time and energy, and I would have bought the correct charger in the first place.
The correct battery charger for Power Wheels vehicles with two 6V batteries is the 12V System charger, which can also be found at Amazon for the same price.
(Note: you need the 12V SYSTEM charger and not the 12V charger, which is for the 12V batteries.)
Don't be misled like I was, and get it right the first time.

title: Motorcycle Battery diagnostic tool.. perfect size (Ural)

Attention Ural owners... get one of these and a 2 Pin Quick Disconnect Harness (Available on Amazon or at almost any car parts store for a few dollars). Cut the wire set in half... leave one half permanently attached to your battery and tuck in under the seat. The other half of the wires you split goes to meter with a few blade/spade connectors.  If you turn the key off the wrong way or walk away with the tail light on... you'll save a lot of time trouble shooting by connecting one of these. Less than 9 volts.. start walking.  Leave one of these with the bike. Also works when you fire it up to show if the battery is charging . Also attached some alligator clips with a second set of 2-pin connectors and use it on my boat batteries... This eliminates need for a larger amp/volt meter. Just watch your + and -... which are clearly marked on meter

It's technically bigger than I needed, but sizing is uber-adjustable. The rings are surrounded by the fabric, so you can push the rings closer or farther apart as needed, and there is extra material around the edges, so you can fold it a bit around the sides of your side windows as well (obviously depending upon the size of your vehicle).

It does a great job at controlling excess heat in the truck, and I live in a scorching, humid climate. It makes the difference in whether I can drive with or without gloves so I don't burn my hands.

It twists into a sort of figure-8 shape and then folds over the top and bottom easily to close up. We've all used stuff that folds up like this by now, so we all know how it's done!

The final point I love about this is that the center upper part has a slit that closes with a Velcro tab, so you can secure it around the rear-view mirror. A minor feature that results in a nice improvement on the ones that don't have that option. Makes it easier to position and keeps it in place against the windshield well.

title: Maybe not totally theft-proof but still a visible deterrent
text:
I have a somewhat odd circumstance of inheriting an ancient truck that doesn't have the door lock keys (and the ignition key doesn't work for that). Fortunately I live in an area where crime is uncommon, but still I felt I should do a couple of things that were easy and quick to help deter problems.

This club is an easy way for basic security when running errands. Someone could theoretically cut through the steering wheel. But parked near the front of the grocery store or wherever, how likely is that? The club is a deterrent that takes seconds to attach.

To complement this for more security at home, I also wrap up the foot pedals with a heavy chain and heavy padlock with a long shank that entraps one pedal, so they can't be used. That's not cumbersome to do, but not something I'd like to hassle with when out running errands. So this club combined with the chain works for now and for my budget.

title: Arrived badly rancid; doesn't appear to be actual walnut oil
text:
I just received the product and it has an expiration date printed on the container of April 23, 2023.

Upon opening it and trying it, it is blatantly badly rancid. That of course means it is not only nasty tasting and smelling, but unsafe to use.

Besides that serious issue, this product does not resemble walnut oil in the slightest. Even considering that rancidity can conceal the normal scents and flavors, I do not believe this actually contains any walnut oil at all. When I've purchased walnut oils in the past, they have always had a very notably distinctive scent and flavor, that is entirely missing with this product. I've had other walnut oils that went rancid over time at home because I hadn't used them up, and those still could be discerned as definitely being walnut oil.

In any event, whether it is or is not some low grade of walnut oil for real, it was shipped to me completely rancid. Unfortunately, Amazon will not accept any returns/exchanges on this rather expensive item. So I wanted to alert others about the issues with this product. FYI while Amazon does have a general good return/exchange policy on many items, that doesn't apply to all items; so if you have been able to exchange a problem item on Amazon before and assume you can with this one, you can't exchange or refund it if it arrives spoiled. Just a head's up.

title: Work like the major brands
text: These tabs dissolve pretty quickly and the scent is fine without being too strong. I don't really see any functional difference between these and major brands of RV toilet drops actually. Well, these are noticably more expensive - we get 40 pods for the same price as 15 of these. RVing 8s pricey enough without doubling up on toilet stuff.

title: Helpful
text:
My husband had this installed and connected to our older RV fridge pretty quickly with minimal cursing - that's a good sign. We connected the RV to shore power for 48 hours (no time for an actual trip right now) and let it run. The fans are reasonably quiet and we didn't notice any degradation of power or extra drag on the converter with the 12v lights all on.

I won't have any way of knowing if the fan really helps cooling until summer though. That's the true test - a 3 week RV trip in high summer temps or humidity. I think this will do just fine though and keep the fins from icing up.

title: Organized storage
text: These bags seem sturdy and durable. The different water hoses fit in the bags without drama and everything tucks away neatly in the storage compartment under the RV. Our extra electrical cord and extension cords for in the bag with plenty of leftover space.

title: Fits reasonably well
text: My 2006 Sequoia is awesome, but her leather seats are showing a little age. My previous seat cover bit the dust so this is the replacement. It fits reasonably well and so far is staying put. The fabric is soft and I imagine the leather seats will be warmer this winter than without this cover.

title: Good idea, broke on day one
text: This sort of unnecessary doo-dad can be useful if executed properly. Unfortunately, this one isn't. I like the idea of a second sunglasses holder in my car, but this thing broke on day one. A hinge or something snapped and now it's just more plastic garbage.

title: Works perfectly
text: My husband's truck was throwing a code for this sensor to be replaced. Of course, neither the local Napa or AutoZone had it in stock. Amazon to the rescue. This fit and works exactly as it should and our mechanic had no trouble making the swap. 2011 Chevy 2500HD

title: Fit exactly as it should
text: My husband's truck was throwing a code for this sensor to be replaced. Of course, neither the local Napa or AutoZone had it in stock. Amazon to the rescue. This fit and works exactly as it should and our mechanic had no trouble making the swap. 2011 Chevy 2500HD

title: Fell off in rain
text: My husband liked this badge at first and it looked decent on his truck. However, the glue is not really meant for outside use. After 3 days of straight rain and unusual humidity here, it began to peel off

title: Necessary RV protection
text:
This our 4th surge protector after 2 years of full time RVing due to the units actually doing their job and stopping power surges or identifying bad wiring before damage to our RV occurred. You never know what condition a RV park's pedestals really are until you're plugged in. Without a surge protector, that's too late. (We stayed at a popular park in Marfa and 4 of the pedestals in a row had reversed polarity!)

This fits the pedestal plugs properly and our trailer plug fits this properly. The surge protector doesn't get hot while in use and I can run the AC etc without worrying. Hopefully, this one will protect as well as the previous ones next time we hit the road.

title: Not the best long-term
text:
We're deep in the Chihuahua Desert 8n the Big Bend region of Texas. That means extreme UV and direct sunlight year round. A windshield shade is a critical necessity here.

This one is a few inches too small for a Toyota Sequoia and a Silverado 2500 truck, but it fits a Highlander and a Jeep Cherokee pretty well. Unfortunately, the umbrella like ribs to open the shade are thin and weak. The first time we used it, one of them vent backwards. The second time, a different rib came unstitched from the shade material. I'm going to look for the regular flat shades instead.

title: 3 person install
text:
It took 3 of us and 2 ladders to get this cover over our travel trailer - the cover is heavy. It fits though.

Having the reflective material is a good thing since we're in the desert with intense sun and heat year round. Hopefully, this cover will survive the summer - after almost 2 years full time in our RV, we're parked for awhile now.

title: Good for car and travel trailer washing
text:
We live in the Chihuahua Desert and that means dust. Lots of dust and little rain. I don't wash the cars or the RV often simply because wasting water like that is not acceptable behavior. So when we do wash stuff, we need to make it count.

This brush extends smoothly and stays out without retracting unexpectedly. It's not heavy even when the water is running through it, so I can maneuver it comfortably and easily enough. The bristles are soft and didn't scratch my Sequoia or the RV. The travel trailer was clean enough to put the cover over it and store it for the summer. My only issue was getting the brush retracted and put away - it got sticky after doing two vehicles and the RV.

title: Compatible with portable air compressor
text:
We needed this extension cord for rear 12 volt connection in the Sequoia. We're out in the Chihuahua Desert and Chinati Mountains of west Texas and tires take a beating out here. Especially my horse trailer tires when I'm riding the back country.

The portable compressor is great, but came with a 3 foot cord that rendered it essentially useless. Adding the extension cord allowed us to use the compressor with both the car tires and the horse trailer. So far, everything is working properly.

title: Very thick
text: This thing is actually too wide for our 2006 travel trailer skylight. The skylight sort of narrows midway up, so this block isn't a great fit. There's a 3 inch gap between this and the top of the skylight cutout. It's better than nothing though and has stopped heat from the sun elevating the bathroom temperature.

title: Definitely starts a car
text: My husband used this to jumpstart a Kia Soul the other day. It actually worked despite my misgivings over the tiny size. It was simple enough to connect and recharging was relatively fast. He says he'll keep this in the ranch truck from now on.

title: Nice kit for an RV
text:
We bought a 15 year old RV almost 2 years ago and completely stripped it out and rebuilt it from the subfloor up, including the electrical system.

Having an extra set of fuses in various sizes is a must. Our converter died last week and took the 40amp fuses with it. Fortunately, a new converter was just a matter of DIY swapping them. These fuses fit and are working as they should.

title: Definitely kill odor in RV
text:
We're full time in our RV and that means black tank maintenance is a major priority. We have tried these pods twice when we empty the tank.

They definitely kill odors and that's a huge plus. However, these pods don't melt as fast as the other brands we normally use. But these do what they claim.

title: Must have in the Chihuahua Desert
text:
We have two of these already - one in each vehicle and I wanted another for the horse trailer. I use our neighbors' big dually sometimes to haul horses into the back country and ride both the Big Bend National and State parks. You do not ever want to be stranded down here with a flat tire in the desert or mountains - super dangerous for several reasons.

This is light enough for anyone to handle and set up alone. It powers up and is ready to go pretty quickly without a ton of drama. The light up display is useful after dark.

It reinflated a motorcycle tire for a guy who got in over his head the other day - yes, mesquite thorns will, in fact, puncture a tire while you're moving. He had a little patch kit, but no way to inflate the tire. This compressor and the others we already have are must have safety gear and this one works well.

title: Thick and well stitched
text:
We live in the desert and mountains of West Texas and that means bad roads, off road vehicles and the need to be prepared at all times. Our old tow strap was beginning to fray after 3 years, so this is the replacement.

The strap is thick and feels very strong and sturdy. It's well stitched. The package says it's rated for up to 15,000lbs, but our rule is to stay well below the suggested rating. For us, this will be used to pull stuck ATVs out of mud or trails gone bad.

title: Best for testing
text:
This is not really sturdy enough for regular use as a surge protector for a large RV. And a 50amp RV is a large power draw. You need a much stronger piece of equipment that offers a drop cord for water protection - this unit does not have that.

It did read two different hook-up posts correctly. So as a connection tester, this is fine. As a surge protector for an emergency back up, it's fine. But this wouldn't be my choice for regular, long term surge protection. It's just too flimsy.

title: Quick fix for a small roof hole
text:
We had a nasty windstorm in the middle of the night with no warning. Our antenna pole with our cell booster was up, of course. RVing is never simple and trouble free.

One of the bolts twisted enough to cause a widening of it's hole. Not something you want. We used this tape to seal the area and the other 3 bolt connections as well.

The tape is thick and extremely sticky. Cutting it to fit requires a steady hand, flat surface and a sharp blade. However, there's a tight, multi layered seal now and it didn't leak at all in a minor rain 2 days later.

title: Must have for RVing
text:
RVs are staggeringly delicate creations and require any number of additional gadgets to keep them running properly. A good surge protector is a non negotiable item that you can't risk being without for even one day.

Our old one did it's job beautifully for a year. It saved us twice from surges at two different campground hookup poles. None of our appliances or electronics were damaged and no fire. After the second event, it was time to replace it.

This unit is physically larger than our old one, but it does the same things. The lights indicating power post status are clear and easy to read even in daytime. Our 30amp plug fits properly and after ten days, the entire system is cool and working properly - no excessive heat build up.

title: Lighter than our original
text:
Our 2006 travel trailer needed a new plug in connection. After all these years, it was just time. This one wired up correctly with minimal cursing from my husband and everything is working thus far.

This plug does have a grip on it that our old one didn't have, so that's a definite improvement. However, this unit does not feel as sturdy and robust. It is lighter and that concerns me from a longevity point of view.

title: Great for RV windows/doors
text:
We have three windows and the door of our RV on the East side and no shade. By lunch the trailer is heating up out here in the Chihuahua Desert. I put two of these kinds of covers on those windows and the west side windows a few weeks ago and it really helps.

These two are going on the last East window and the bathroom skylight thing. These are pretty well made and a smidge thicker than the old ones we already have. I love that these come with 6 pieces of the Velcro attachments. You can secure the cover without weak spots that flop open. A must have in an RV in West Texas.

title: Best for small items like handbags
text:
I wear my tall riding boots almost every day. That means dirt, dust and general wear. I use Lexol cleaner and the conditioner weekly with excellent results.

These wipes are ok for minor cleaning up, but not really suitable for intensive leather cleaning or any conditioning. They are small and thin and dry up pretty fast. It took two wipes for each boot today. The photos show before and after on my boots. The really dark area on the inner calf areas are actually just wear from being in the saddle so much.

I could see using these for a quick wipe down of handbags or high heels.

title: Easier to install than expected
text:
My husband installed this with a friend on our 2006 travel trailer. The old fan just wasn't getting the job done anymore. This one did fit in the same footprint as the original fan, so we didn't have to make any cuts in our roof. And the wiring actually matched up which was a relief.

So far, it seems to be working properly. You can set the temperature parameters for the fan to automatically run - like when the interior temperature gets above the preferred level.

I like the remote control. It lets you turn it on or off without getting up. Because I am just that lazy. I also like the tinted cover - it has reduced the direct sunlight coming into our RV bathroom and that reduces the summer heat inside as well.

title: Light duty at best
text:
We have been full time in our RV for almost a year now on a couple of volunteer projects with the State. As such, a very heavy duty surge protector is an absolute must. The one we're currently using cost about 5 times what this one does, is much heavier and it has been worth it.

This is fine in a very limited way. If you're just using it for a three day weekend in a small, 30amp travel trailer in a cool climate, you won't be disappointed.

However, for a long trip or full time RVers, this should not be the first choice. It gets hot in high temperatures and sunlight. And that seriously concerns me - your campsite electric connection won't always be in shade. If the surge protector is already hot and everything is working properly, then something isn't right. By comparison, our heavy duty surge protector never feels hot to the touch and it has saved us from a power surge in a public campground twice already.

title: Excellent water hose
text:
I have to say this hose is far better than the last three we've had for the RV. It's thick and heavy which means it does not kink up. There's no rubbery flavor to the water either.

So far it's holding up to 100 degrees temperatures and UV light. We do keep a pool noodle around the hose to aid in insulation and UV protection since we're in the Chihuahua Desert.

title: Sealed around a new RV exhaust fan
text:
We installed a new exhaust fan over our RV bathroom. That meant resealing every single inch around it. Caulking as well, of course. I've used this type of tape before on our 15 year old travel trailer to maintain the skylight seal. It's held up great for a year of crazy weather and temperature extremes.

This tape seems to be just as good. It's thick and the layer of adhesive is very gooey and thick. It has stayed put despite 3 days of 108 degrees and above with direct sunshine. I think this will stay in place for the rest of the year.

title: Cleans better than it conditions
text:
I tried this on my expensive, daily riding boots. I wear these boots in all weather and all conditions both riding and just doing barn work. I normally clean and treat them once a month with the Lexol products. This stuff did get them clean, but they do not feel as supple as when I use Lexol.

In both photos, you can see the left boot is treated with this and the right one hasn't been. (The dark spots mid calf are just wear from hundreds of miles on horseback) There's a definite improvement. However, 12 hours later the boots aren't as soft as I expect them to be after using leather conditioner.

I will keep this stuff for car seats and boots, but I won't use it on my expensive saddles or bridles. I need those things deep cleaned and treated with a separate, real conditioner twice a month to prevent cracking in our extreme desert dry heat.

title: Velcro adhesive is bad.
text:
I actually like this window cover. The fabric cover part fits our 2006 travel trailer door exactly as it should. And it does reduce the direct sun heat in the mornings. However, the holes for the snap things don't match up. I am never going to be putting new holes in our RV, so we used the included velcro type attachments.

Unfortunately, the glue adhesive on the strips is garbage. It stuck to the door pretty well, but for 3 days kept falling off of the fabric cover. I ended up using some legitimate Velcro brand strips I already had on hand to fix this problem.

title: Dropped the temperature 5 degrees!
text:
Our travel trailer has one of those raised bubble skylights over the bathtub. And no ac vents in the bathroom. This is just a heat magnet in summer, especially in the Chihuahua Desert. It was literally 111 degrees (12% humidity) yesterday and 110 degrees, real air temp today. The bathroom has been HOT.

I installed this cover over the skylight frame this morning. The velcro attachment means no drilling! Yay! It fit perfectly and completely covered the stupid skylight opening. No gaps.

Yesterday at 6pm in the absolute worst of the heat - 111 degrees - our bathroom was 90 degrees. The rest of the RV was holding at 82. Today though, 110 degrees outside at 6pm and 82 degrees in the main trailer....the bathroom has held at 84 degrees!!! Still hot of course, but significantly better considering the surface of the sun temperature outside.

title: Steering wheel sleeve, no padding
text: This is just a steering wheel sleeve. There's no extra padding to soften a hard steering wheel. Fortunately, it's flexible and large enough to fit over my existing padded cover. Essentially, this is just updating the look of my 2006 Sequoia.

title: Preventative measure in 2006 Sequoia
text:
My beloved 2006 Toyota Sequoia has a 161,000 miles now. I use her to tow a 3 horse trailer out to two different parks regularly plus the usual daily driving. And I maintain the Sequoia religiously - I intend to get another 160,000 miles out of her at the least.

We used this per the instructions as a cleanser and preventative measure. No active problems or lights on and my code reader confirmed no active codes of any kind before and 300 miles after using this.

I do think my mileage is a tad better though. Towing a single horse 122 miles round trip into the Bofecillos Mountains we tracked at 14.4 mpg. Last month that same trip was 14.1 mpg before using this. Not a huge improvement, but noticable.

title: Working well, no seeping odors
text:
We've used these drop ins for 4 weeks now - we typically empty the black tank every 5 days. So we've used several at this point.

They take a little longer to open and disintegrate than other brands out there. However, the scent is fresh and our black tank has no odors seeping up. I have no complaints.

title: Works properly for RV fresh water
text:
We use these types of water filters in our RV and on the well water line to our horse trough. You have to have a water filter in your RV because you never know what the water quality will be in random RV parks.

This one is pretty basic and does work. It has helped maintain the flavor of the water we're putting into the RV. The water is clear with no discoloration or odors.

title: Didn't work well in a dry climate
text: Meh. I wanted this to repair a crack on an older saddle. It really didn't do the job. It basically just colored in the area. Once it dried, the crack was still there. I ended up taking the saddle to Mexico and replacing all the leather around the pommel. It may be that our extreme heat and low humidity inhibits this stuff....you might have better luck in a different climate.

title: Extra protection for well water
text:
I'm actually using this filter for the horses. Our ranch well water is fine and potable of course, but because it is a desert well, I wanted a little extra filtration.
