After two weeks of use on our hose to the trough, it's working well. The horses are drinking like they always have and I think the water tastes fine to me. I would use this brand of filter in our RV as well.

title: Full shade, air still moves through
text:
We're not using this on our RV. Instead, we have it set up as a side shade on a horse shelter. We're in deep West Texas in the Chihuahua Desert - the sun here is very bright, intense and unwavering year round. Shade is a must for people and especially our horses.

This has worked great for us. It offers shade and diffuses the sunlight. The breezes can still blow through the fabric which is a must out here. It withstood 45mph winds the other night unscathed. I may buy a second one for our RV.

title: Handy for a horse trailer
text: I am using this in a horse trailer. I just needed a quick, portable light option for loading or unloading after dark. It recharges with a usb cable so requires no wiring. The light quality is fine for my needs - I'm certainly not reading with this though.

title: Meh.
text:
We have dogs in our vehicles almost daily and I keep all the seats fully covered. I thought this might be a more attractive option. Alas, no.

This did not fit the Toyota Sequoia or F150 seats at all. I tried it on a friend's Honda Civic and it fit properly. The material looks and feels like what it is - some sort of vinyl pleather. It's better than nothing certainly, but there are a lot of better seat covers out there.

title: Nice around the barn for the ATV
text: We have a heavy duty unit for my Sequoia that I carry everywhere, especially when I'm trailering horses. This compressor is primarily for the Gator out at the ranch and the travel trailer tires. Its strong enough for that without worrying about it.  The kit includes several patches and tools to do minor tire repair til you can get to a pro. Running on 12 volt is convenient, but means it takes a few minutes to fully pressurize. At just 15lbs or so, its very easy to move around as well. The entire setup works pretty well for our small projects.

title: Safety measures for a horse trailer
text:
I was away from the ranch whey husband installed this on our 3 horse slant load trailer. When I asked him about the difficulty of the process and any complications, his response was "just moderate cursing". The translation is "not bad and I only threatened to set fire to the entire rig once". That's good news around here.

We've only hauled horses three times since he set this up, so I can't speak to longevity. The basic air pressure readings seem correct, though one of the left tires differs by 2lbs when tested against other gauges. I can live with that.

When I say we have only used the trailer three times, I mean we've hauled horses 85 miles round-trip over some hard West Texas back country and sketchy roads made out of everything from asphalt to gravel to old rutted trails and 5 miles down a literal dry creek bed. (All so I can ride in the State and National Parks) None of these sensors have failed or come off. The monitor is hard to read in bright sunlight - needs more contrast or something. Overall, I think this is worth having and hopefully, it will work for a few years.

title: I don't use anything else
text:
We're out in deep West Texas along the border in the Chihuahua Desert. It's dry and hot with full sunshine most days. I ride almost daily and we typically cover 6 to 12 miles or more every ride. That can lead to dirty, dry saddle leather if you don't take care of your tack.

This kit has been excellent. It includes the leather cleaner and conditioner and a sponge for each. It's very easy to use and actually does get the grime off. I'm currently riding in a 30 year old Alamo Saddlery western saddle that looks amazing and has very soft, supple leather. That's specifically because I use Lexol regularly.

I recently got a custom made leather bridle and reins that are very high end and beautifully crafted - I want this set to last 20 years or more. First thing I did was go over every inch with this conditioner once a week for 3 weeks. The reins are soft, very flexible and begining to shape to fit my hands. The headstall gleams and my horse is quite comfortable. I also use this on my stallion's leather Cavello hoof boots.

title: Installed simply
text: We are doing a year long volunteer project and staying in our travel trailer the entire. Having a tongue lock seems like  good choice. You never know where or when thieves may strike. This fit our tongue hitch correctly and was simple to set up. It looks ugly as sin, but not as bad an empty spot would look after the trailer was stolen. To be sure, a determined thief with time could still get the trailer,  but most would keep looking for an easier target.

title: Perfection! Fits exactly and is stable
text:
We rehabilitated and totally remodeled a 14 year old travel trailer last summer. We've actually been living in it full time for six months while on a volunteer project in West Texas. We removed all the propane lines and converted the entire trailer to electric only for safety. (Great choice btw to go all electric. No fumes, no lines to leak, no expensive tanks to refill, no explosions.)

However, we haven't yet removed the old stove, instead we've been using the portable induction burners on top of it. This cover replaced a random one I had been using that was wobbly. This is straight, smooth edges and has adjustable feet to get it level. It fit our stove top perfectly and looks great.

title: Works fine for basic stuff in a 30amp travel trailer
text: We tested this dog bone converter for a few hours.  It does power our 30amp travel trailer,  but with some limitations.  Using the microwave made the lights flicker and  our washing machine ran, but again the lights flickered. For basic stuff like the fridge, lights and tv, it was just fine. I think this sort of thing is very handy and useful for anyone RVing. You never know when you may end up overnight in an unplanned stop with the wrong electric setup.

title: Fits 2006 Springdale travel trailer
text: We put this lock on our 2006 Springdale travel trailer and it fit in the old lock space just fine. It took about 40 minutes to remove the old one and install this one. The keys work correctly and aren't sticky. Hopefully,  this lock will last another several years.

title: Definitely stops black tank odors
text: These sorts of toilet drop ins are an absolute must for any RV. We've used them weekly for several months while we're on a volunteer project in our RV. The pods are big, but begin to dissolve rapidly in the bowl when water is added. They really do eliminate odors from wafting up from the black tank between emptying the tank. After trying some other brands, we've decided this one works best for our small travel trailer.

title: Easy to use,  no leaks or water pressure issues
text:
An inline water filter is an absolute must for all RV travel. You literally have no idea what the water quality may be in random RV parks. This one fit our hose correctly and seems to be working properly. There are no leaks and the water in the travel trailer is clear.

We've been in the same location for 90 days now and we know what the water looks and tastes like with a different brand filter. The water tastes the same with this filter as it did a week ago. And this filter doesn't inhibit the water pressure at all.

title: Good for claw protection
text:
With multiple dogs going on car rides regularly, we keep all the car seats covered all the time. This one fit the passenger seat in both a Toyota Sequoia and a Subaru Forester.

It's a standard set up with the straps around the seat back and side flaps. The colors are more brownish than orange.

title: Keeping a finicky Soul charged
text:
Our little Kia Soul has some sort of constant electric system drain. It's been in and out of the shop multiple times to find the problem with no solution. We've swapped the battery out 3 times in a year thinking it was an old battery, a bad battery or bad connections. Nope. If you don't start and drive the Soul every 12 hours it won't start at all without a jump. I don't have time for that nonsense.

In a last ditch effort before just selling it as a buggy car, we tried a trickle charger. That works well for this issue. And of course our old charger died. So....this one is the replacement.

It's working properly for this specific problem. The Kia starts when we need it. The charger did get hot one time, but I think that was simple direct sun exposure. We relocated the car and charger and no more heat.

title: Selection of functional fuses
text: To my horror, our RV blew a 15amp fuse at 3am the other day. We searched and finally found one new replacement in our tool kit. This is the kit we should have had to begin with  and we won't get caught short again.  I swapped out another 15amp fuse in the RV today wuth one of these and this one works great.

title: Failed in a week
text:
Update Dec 14, 2020
REDUCED TO 1 STAR

Both lights failed last night. Both have one side that is totally dark. We took them out and redid the wiring, thinking maybe we didn't install them correctly. Nope. Still have one dead side in each. The bulbs cannot be removed and replaced either. So now I have to but two new fixtures from a reliable, legitimate brand.

******* Original review below*****

We renovated a 14 year old travel trailer this summer from the subflooring to the ceiling and everything in between. Instead of replacing the light fixtures, we just swapped the old bulbs for new LED bulbs. That was great for the first three months, but new fixtures were definitely called for.

These lights are exactly what we needed. They fit in the same footprint as the original fixtures- even the screw holes lined up correctly. These have very faint frosted lenses and emit significantly more light than the old, grayish fixtures did. I also like that the switch on these lets you have just one side turned on or both bulbs.

The light itself is a very bright, white light. No yellowed tint here - you can read comfortably with this light. Installing each one took five minutes and the wiring matched up easily. Overall, we're very pleased and after a week, we can't believe we waited 6 months to make this swap.

title: Does exactly what it says
text: This gizmo actually works! It attached to our drill without any drama or extra pieces needed. My husband whooped with joy the first he used this. No more bending over, huffing and puffing, manually lower or raising the trailer jacks.

title: Improved water taste
text:
We're spending several months in our RV doing volunteer projects around Texas. That means random water quality at each location - you never know what the well or city water situation may be. A filter is a must.

This one installed super easy and doesn't leak. The water tastes pretty good out of this filter and doesn't have any off odors or off colors. We change our filter every 30 days without fail, so I can't speak to longevity beyond that time frame.

title: Bright,  clean light. Super easy fixture swap
text:
We bought a 14 year old travel trailer this summer and remodeled it from the subflooring up. The original lights worked fine, but were discoloured and dim. I swapped all the bulbs for new LEDS immediately and that helped, but I still wasn't getting the bright, clear light I wanted for reading.

I swapped one fixture out for this one and just WOW. Huge improvement to both the quality of light and the general appearance the new fixture. It took 5 minutes to make the swap. We removed the old fixture, disconnected the 2 wires, reconnected them to this light, attached this one to the ceiling and it was done. Everything fit exactly in the old footprint and the light is excellent. I'm going to buy 6 more and change all the lights out in the RV.

title: Fit a 2006 Sequoia correctly
text:
We have a beloved 2006 Sequoia that I plan on keeping as long as possible. These beasts are tough and reliable and I never worry when we're road tripping, towing the travel trailer or just going grocery shopping in it. Unfortunately, for all the great engineering and quality throughout the Sequoia, the tail gate handles are a known issue. The darn things wear out and need to be replaced. Ours wasn't totally non functional yet, but getting sticky.

I didn't even consider this a DIY project, I just took the handle to our mechanic and he made the swap. It looks exactly like the original one and the plastic feels thick and solid. My tailgate is opening correctly and not causing any trouble. Hopefully, this part will make it 14 years like the old did.

title: Weird shape, but helpful
text:
These are a weird shape and I can't quite figure out why. They don't actually fit correctly in the windows of any of our three vehicles - a Kia Soul, Toyota Sequoia or F-150 truck.

I am using them in the Sequoia to keep sun off the middle and third row areas. The shades do cut down on the direct sun and that makes things better for the dogs. Especially driving through South and West Texas.

title: Fits Kia Soul exactly
text:
I love our little Kia Soul, but hate the hard steering wheel. On a road trip, my hands end up feeling slightly bruised. My last cover finally wore out, so I put this one on this morning.

It's very nicely padded and has a light texture as well to give you a little feedback. It fits perfectly on the Soul, but is definitely too small for the Toyota Sequoia wheel.

title: Noticeable and significant improvement in pressure
text:
I have been distinctly unimpressed by the shower head that came with our travel trailer. No matter what the actual water pressure is, that thing produces a dismal drizzle of lukewarm water. Replacing it has been on my list for 3 weeks.

This one is a much welcomed improvement in several ways. The pressure is very close to a real shower - enough that my thick, long hair is actually getting completely rinsed. That's a big deal. It was easy to make the swap and get this one up and ready to go. The only quibble i have is this shower head doesn't include the pause switch to stop the water and save your hot water mid shower. You need to turn it off at the faucet instead. Still....not a deal breaker for me considering the increase in pressure output.

title: Seem to be working properly  - no odors
text: Our travel trailer is smaller and older, so our tanks aren't large. One pod of this is plenty. We've been at our spot in a state park for a couple of days now and haven't noticed any odors from the bathroom at all. I assume the pod dissolved correctly,  there's no visual way to tell of course. One thing we did notice is that these pods are smaller than our regular brand, so if your black tank is really big, you may need two of these rather than just one after every tank dump.

title: Fit the fixture in a 2006 travel trailer
text: I can't compare these 1141 bulbs to the originals from our 14 year old RV because the originals burned out long before we bought the trailer. However,  these bulbs do fit correctly in the exterior  "porch" light and they work. As part of the full tear down remodel on the travel trailer, we swapped every light bulb for LEDS and it made a significant improvement. These are a reasonably warm white and we can clearly see the steps and area immediately by the door.

title: Sturdy, well designed
text: We completely gutted and refurbished a 14 year travel trailer and realized it didn't have a pressure regulator in it. We bought a small one, but i actually like this better. Its sturdy and feels solidly made. The gauge is big and easy to read which I very much appreciate.  There are regular hose connections on both ends so it is ready to use immediately without an adapter or drama in a campsite.  We've tested it once & compared it to our other regulator and both gave the same readings - I feel comfortable taking it on the road in the RV.

title: They fit properly on travel trailer tires
text: My husband seems pleased with these chocks. They are very light, but thick and appear sturdy. We're using on the travel trailer tires while its in storage. Despite heavy winds from the outside edge of Hurricane Laura this week, the chocks stayed in place and the trailer never budged.

title: Fun for an RV
text: This is a terrific recreation of a manufacturing label we might find on a real life vehicle or....you know, spaceship. We put this on the back of our travel trailer and it looks great. It has stayed in place after a heavy rain, through three days of direct sunlight in 100 degree temperatures. Hopefully,  fellow Browncoats will get a kick out of it passing us on the highway.

title: Correct fit for a 2006 Toyota Sequoia
text: We put these on our 2006 Sequoia and they fit perfectly. It took just a few minutes to remove the old wipers and put these on. We had one round of rain while driving the other day and the wipers performed well. No streaking,  no stuttering and no weird squeaky noises. The outline of the area they wipe is exactly the same as the old wiper blades. I'm pretty happy.

title: Easy way to level a travel trailer
text:
You have to have these leveling blocks if you have a travel trailer. Each one fits onto the other blocks - sort of like legos, but they are easily adjustable and switched around. These let you increase or decrease the tire height once you're parked so the rv is level and stable.

The block set is lighter than it looks and the carrying bag is handy. The entire set stores neatly in the small exterior storage bay of the trailer. These do work for our small trailer and after a couple of days, none of the blocks have cracked or shifted under the tire. We're only using 3 under one tire right now, so there are blocks left to do a second tire if we needed to. The neon yellow makes them easy to see and inspect.

title: Did not overheat
text: We are restoring a 14 year old travel trailer with a 30amp connection. Since most of the big, newer RVs have 50amp, most private campgrounds have followed suit. We're learning that not every Texas State Park has 30amp still available either. Thus....the need for an adapter. We've only used this once for 24 hours so far. It definitely worked and the trailer functioned properly. Our adapter didn't overheat or cause drama on either end and our 30amp cable plugged in correctly. Hopefully, this will last a long time.

title: Replacements for original bulbs in a travel trailer
text: I have 10 bulbs in the RV that needed to be swapped out for LEDs and used 6 of a different brand the other day. We put these in today and they are exactly the same as the other brand in every way. These bulbs fit into the 12 volt slots on the RV overhead light fixtures. They re a bit tighter than the old ones were. We plugged the trailer in and the bulbs worked great. All 4 lit up and the light is sufficiently bright and no yellow haze.

title: 3 days under 1 tire and no cracks or shifting
text:
You have to have these leveling blocks if you have a travel trailer. Each one fits onto the other blocks - sort of like legos, but they are easily adjustable and switched around. These let you increase or decrease the tire height once you're parked so the rv is level and stable.

The block set is lighter than it looks and the carrying bag is handy. The entire set stores neatly in the small exterior storage bay. These do work for our small trailer and after 3 days, none of the blocks have cracked or shifted under the tire. We're only using 3 under one tire right now, so there blocks left to do a second tire if we needed to. The bright orange makes them easy to see and inspect.

title: Fit in 2006 travel trailer fixtures
text:
We're restoring a 14 year old travel trailer and in amongst the three big projects, are dozens of small ones. Light bulbs being pretty high on that list. Those old bulbs ran hot and over the years left a scary black scorch mark in one fixture. LED bulbs are a must.

These fit correctly in each overhead fixture and on 12volt power, they run just like they should. The light is clean and definitely brighter than before. Of course, scrubbing the covers helped too.

Because these bulbs are only rated for 12 volt, I certainly won't trust them when we're on shore power. Shore power means using lamps rather than the trailer lights for long periods. I don't want to risk these overheating and melting or causing a fire. If you primarily boondock, these are a good choice.

title: Fits tightly and no leaking
text: In restoring a 14 year old travel trailer,  we realized the water hose connection was very tight and angled badly. There was pressure on the hose that would eventually ruin it. This elbow solved the problem completely and the hose connects normally now. It fits properly and does not leak at either end.

title: Too small for 2 of 3 trailers
text: I'm not sure the manufacturer has actually seen a travel or horse trailer in the US. Neither of our trailers fit on this dock donut. Both the horse and travel trailer are too big for it. It does work ok for the little 6 x 8 shop trailer that is smaller in every respect, including the tongue jack and tire. We can only use it with one of three trailers though,  so not great.

title: Tricky to install
text: We've used this extension mirror on a 2006 Toyota Sequoia twice now to move a travel trailer.  I finally found a full set of towing mirrors for the Sequoia,  so this will go in our RV emergency backup supply kit. The extension does work and will definitely keep you safer, but it is not meant to be a permanent replacement for real tow mirrors. Getting it strapped on tightly and in the correct spot is tricky. It took about five minutes both times we used it. It vibrates significantly at speed as well - which then loosens the straps.

title: Fit a 14 year old Keystone trailer
text: As part of the restoration of a 14 year old travel trailer, we needed new roof vents - among dozens of other small and large projects. I have admit to being surprised and pleased that these actually fit. My husband had the old ones off and the space cleaned and the new ones in place in an hour. These covers open and close correctly and so far, haven't leaked. One more repair successfully completed and one step closer to getting on the RV road.

title: Sealed a small leak
text:
We're restoring a 14 year old travel trailer and that means water damage - no RV will ever escape water damage. We had to tear out a 7 foot by 2 foot section of flooring and replace everything. The leak was from a corner near the back door and dry rotted caulking.

We removed the old caulk, cleaned the area, redid the weather stripping and then used this tape down the entire exterior edge and inside. It has rained twice since the repair and so far no water has seeped in. My husband cut this with a new, very sharp box cutter and it did apply with minimal effort. It was easy to get to lie flat without wrinkles. But once its down, it is down - there's no pulling it up and rearranging this tape.

title: Looks good, fits exactly
text:
We bought a 14 year old travel trailer for next to nothing this month. What that translates to in the real world is... Tons of renovating work before we can use it. Replacing the door holder latches was one of dozens of little projects.

This latch system replaced the old plastic one that was literally crumbling. It fit in the exact footprint of the original one. Even the screws fit in the old holes and attached properly. The catch holds the exterior door open without bouncing or wobbling as you go 8n and out of the trailer. I'm pleased.

title: Nice for RV storage organization
text: I always keep one these types of organizer boxed in each car for random stuff. This one is going in the under storage area of the travel trailer. It fits fine down there and holds our random stuff like an extra water hose, dog bone electric adapters, and tire covers. The stiff sides keep everything in place and easy to find.

title: Picked up stray dog hair nicely.
text: Ok, first, I had to get gloves to use this. Its slightly sticky and greasy to the touch and it just creeps me out. Gloves definitely fixed that issue for me. You have to just lay this flat onto the surface and push it into any crevices or nooks and crannies. Once it makes contact with the crud, most everything just sticks to it and comes off the surface you're cleaning. I used it to get random dog hair and bits of hay left behind by the car vac in my SUV. This goo got probably 85% of the stuff and that was definitely a good thing. There are no instructions for cleaning this except a line about not using water. I haven't figured out how to make the goo reusable yet.

title: Mesh design does not protect the seats
text:
Yeah....I'm not even remotely impressed with this cover. Despite what the listing says, you get only one seat cover. It fits the Kia Soul seat, but is too small for the Toyota Sequoia and an F-150 seat. Its a weird pleather/vinyl material that is hot in summer.

The construction is this sort of mesh rather than being a solid seat cover with full coverage. The entire reason I use seat covers is to protect the seats from muddy dog paws and snags from dog claws. This design totally defeats those reasons. In limited circumstances, this may have a place, but not in my vehicles.

title: Good filters and a simple system
text:
Having a filter in an RV is a must and there are several types out there....ones for under the sink and this one that is used directly on the incoming water supply. It attaches directly to the hose and faucet and filters everything before it enters your plumbing. It was easy to connect and test with basic class c.
The water was as good as with the previous filter. This system is easy to use and the filters are easy to replace as needed.

title: Works correctly,  easy install
text:
Having a filter in an RV is a must and there are several types out there....ones for under the sink and this one that is used directly on the incoming water supply. It attaches directly to the hose and faucet and filters everything before it enters your plumbing. It was easy to connect and test with basic class c.
The water was as good as with the previous filter. My only issue is the low end pressure regulator. It's good that they include this, but we would consider it more as a backup if the good one failed on the road. I do like that the replacement filters are available and not terribly expensive.

title: Dark and they stay put
text: I am using these in Texas where our summer sunshine can be brutal.  They fit well on the second and third row windows in our Toyota Sequoia. There is a definite difference in the heat and glare levels when these are in place. So far, the shades have stayed put for 2 full weeks without coming off.

title: Nice for dogs on the go in both a Kia Soul and Toyota Sequoia
text: I am a fan in general of the static cling window shades.  We live in Texas in summer we see very hot, direct sun all day long. I want my dogs protected and shaded as much as possible as we drive, so we use these shades in all vehicles. These fit the back seat windows in both the Toyota Sequoia and the little Kia Soul. The shades stay put and definitely offer shade in the back seats. As an unexpected benefit, using these reduces the dog nose print nonsense on our car windows.

title: Not DIY, most shops will not install these
text: One of my TPMS sensors was dead in our Sequoia which meant that tire light was on 24/7. THESE ARE NOT a do it yourself repair by any means. The sensors must be installed professionally and tested and fully programmed for your car's system. Additionally,  many tire shops will not install TPMS sensors you bring in yourself, purchased elsewhere. I called 5 places before I found one willing to put these on - Discount Tires, Firestone and Walmart will only install them if you bought them there. So far it seems to be working after a week. Paying to have them installed ran around sixty bucks for me. I won't do this this way in the future  - I'll just buy them from the tire shop.

title: Covers 95% of a big SUV windshield
text: For generic sized shades, these are ok. They cover the entire windshield on a Toyota Sequoia. Because they are two separate pieces, they don't have a cutout for the rearview mirror space. That means the edges bump against it and leave a space. It's fine for now, but I'll be looking for single piece shade that fits better.

title: Useless on really dirt for saddles and boots
text: This is best for lightly soiled or dusty smooth leather. Its not suitable for real dirt on things like boots, saddles or car seats. I used this on a dressage saddle that is deep cleaned weekly and wiped after daily riding. This just gave it a bit of a wet look, but two hours later, I cleaned it with Brickmore and actual dirt came off. If all you have are a few handbags that need a quick wipe down, use this. If you need real cleaning on working leather....buy a name brand, proven leather cleaner.

title: Power tools on the side of the road
text:
Frankly, I'm kind of amazed at everything this kit can do. It's a Jack, an lug nut tool and an air pump all in one box. Everything fits in the storage case and it fits comfortably in the floorboard between the second and third rows of the Sequoia. And the whole thing is easy to swap between vehicles as needed.

The parts have some weight , but they aren't too heavy to be moved or used by one person. I've only tested the Jack and pump on our little Kia Soul. It lifted it up enough to pull off and replace the flat tire without trouble and was stable. The 12 volt power option is genius. We're down in West Texas in the Chihuahua Desert often and flats in the middle of literal nowhere are a given. Being able to have the power for the air and lift jack really saves time and effort - especially if you're in 100 degrees under direct sun. Hopefully this will last a couple of years.

title: Hard to program. Stopped working in ten days
text: It took forever to get this programmed. Like 30 minutes. Once it was done, it worked somewhat.  Every other use, it would do nothing at all. Then it just quit all together after 10 days. It's just not worth the hassle to continue messing with this fob. I'll pony up the cash and have the dealer do it instead with a legit fob from Toyota.

title: Top doesn't open as wide as it should
text: I got this for the old farm truck since one of the guys smokes. It fits fine in the cup holder and is pretty sturdy. I don't think the top opens far enough to ensure easy access to the inside without looking. The little light is helpful and the lid closes tightly to enclose the odors. The lighter does seem to work if you don't have a real one handy.

title: Tows fine. But rough edges all over
text:
This hitch is sturdy and heavy. It should handle the loads it claims - 8000 to 10,000 lbs. I've only actually used it once on a very short, light flatbed trailer with 20 square bales of hay. Not terribly heavy as loads go. It handled everything well and was stable on the road and nothing slipped. The hitch mount fit into our factory installed hitch on both a 2006 Toyota Sequoia and the Ford F150.

I have 2 quibbles with this though. Its badly finished. There were several areas of rough, sharp metal barbs that could easily cut your hand. We had to file two spots smooth to handle it. The second problem is that the locks aren't marked for which keys work. The keys are marked "A" and "B" and only fit their specific bar lock. I had to write A and B on the locks. Not a big deal, perhaps, but very obnoxious in the rain or dark. Better quality control is definitely called for here.

title: Best for smaller cars. Fits a Kia Soul. Too small in Sequoia
text:
I like the idea of this attaching with magnets and it goes on in 2 different vehicles with problem attaching. We tried it in the Toyota Sequoia and the Kia Soul. It actually fits reasonably well in the Soul because it has smaller back door windows. Our Soul has deeply tinted windows, but when we're out in West Texas, direct sun can still pierce you.

The Sequoia needs different shades than this one. It's too small for any of the door windows and the back windows. Like 3 to 6 inches too small depending on the window. The magnets do work pretty well and it stays in place driving down the road.

title: Very bright
text: We swapped the bulbs in our 201 Kia Soul with these. I say "we", but my husband did it. He said it was reasonably simple and took about 30 minutes from start to finish. The brightness difference is pretty surprising. These light up the road significantly more than the old bulbs. Since the Soul is low to the ground,  I'm not worried about blinding oncoming traffic, but I definitely would not use these in a tall pickup or SUV. You don't want to cause other drivers problems.

title: Great in a semi-truck
text:
My husband is using this in a semi-truck with an APU setup and via the 110 outlet. I've used it in my SUV on the 12volt plug as well. We're both pleased with how well it works. We'll be taking it along in the RV as a supplemental drinks fridge later this year. You do need to monitor its power consumption in your vehicle when using the 12volt power. A small car may not be able to run this effectively compared to a big truck, Sequoia or Suburban type. I certainly wouldn't leave it plugged in with the car off - you'll kill your battery for sure.

It weighs a fair amount, but I can still lift it into the car or move it easily by myself. You need to leave space around it for the airflow so it doesn't overheat. For me, that means this goes in the space behind the third row seats of the Sequoia. I don't hear it in the car at all and of course my husband says it is silent in the semi-truck.

It works very well for things like deli stuff and fruit and Dr Pepper or water. Everything stays cold and safe for a long trip. We're not keeping anything frozen in it, but my husband uses it for leftovers from other meals and he's been very pleased. I think this is a pretty solid car refrigerator that holds way more than expected and is pretty simple to use and live with.

title: Very comfortable to grip, looks nice. Fits a Sequoia
text:
I do several very long road trips a year and a hard steering wheel can cause real pain by the 8th hour on the road. A steering wheel cover is a must. This is a nice grey and black, so it blends in with the great leather interior of our 2006 Toyota Sequoia.

It took some real muscle to wrestle this wrap on, but it did fit correctly. There is a noticeable thickness added to the steering wheel, but it doesn't get in the way. The cover stays put and doesn't slip or slide around even when you make a sudden turn. Everything just feels secure and the padding is very comfortable.

title: Fits a 2006 Sequoia very nicely.  Well made, very functional
text:
I have a 2006 Toyota Sequoia and while these are listed as best for 2012 or newer, they still fit my 2006 very well. Not a perfect fit, but pretty darn close. Certainly better than generic, thin mats you can cut. These mats are very thick and well made. The passenger side mat is a perfect fit and the back seat, second row fits well enough to protect the important areas.

I especially like the flexible structure - you easily shake loose dirt off and get going. The edges and interior channels work well for moving and containing liquid and pieces of mud after a day at the barn. The extra thick heel rest area on the driver's side is comfortable and should help these mats last quite a long time. I like these a lot.

title: Little bit flimsy. Save your original screws
text: These aren't bad license plate frames overall. The thin top is legal for Texas license plates - it does not cover the license plate info. Installing them took minutes, however, none of the included screws fit for two vehicles. We tried on a F150 truck and a Toyota Sequoia and ended up using the screws we already had to put these on the Sequoia.  My issue is that these are really thin and could be cracked by a rock etc. However, the dark black color makes these sort of disappear to the eye and that's fine.

title: Testing accurate pressures
text:
You can never have too many tire pressure gauges. This set of four is handy - one in every car and one on the actual air compressor. These are very easy to grip and hold and the lighted screen is helpful. Though you do need to turn it a bit to fully see it in bright daylight.

We tested all four units on the same tire against two other manual gauges and they were all showing the same 35lbs. So these seem accurate when new with fresh batteries. How long the batteries last...only time will tell.

title: Looks great on the back window
text:
I always have 2 or 3 or 4 dogs with me in the car. Our dogs are by far the most important members of our family. As such, I have a dog related sticker on every vehicle. This one really looks good on the back window and is easy to read.

Attaching it took about 60 seconds. You do need to go slow and make sure each letter is transferring smoothly - I ended up with a wrinkle on the "G and the M". Fortunately, it is only visible up close.

title: Decent option to protect your leather seats
text: I primarily use these as protection against dog claws and nonsense in our vehicles. These fit over the headrest and around the base of the seat. There are multiple pockets to store stuff and I have wet wipes, tissues and rods and ends in them with lots of space left.

title: Vinyl type material
text:
You know, for fake leather, these actually don't look bad. Of course, because they are pleather, I certainly don't expect them to last more than a single summer.. The poly stuff always peels and cracks because it just is not as good as real leather. The use of the word leather in the description should not be allowed because these are just a vinyl type material.

These each fit the seats in an older van and feel comfortable sitting on them. There's plenty of cushioning to make up for the sagging older seats. I'm hoping these will last at least through the hot Texas summer. You definitely don't want to sit on these wearing shorts - your legs will stick and the poly gets hot.

title: Fits an older van, not slippery either
text: I hate a hard steering wheel and I just bought an older van with a steering wheel that feels like rock. This cover fit over the original steering wheel exactly with nary a centimeter to spare. It stays in place and doesn't shift or move as you drive - even making a sudden sharp turn. My hands don't slip around either. There's enough cushion to make it comfortable, but not bulky.

title: Worked fine and did not get hot
text:
We're shopping for a RV to travel in this year. One of the things that everyone we know who RVs, said to get was a set of dog bones for various electrical hookup configurations.

I tested this one with a neighbor's small 30amp travel trailer. We were able to connect directly to her exterior outlet by the garage. The trailer batteries trickle charged and we were able to use the trailer lights. After 2 hours, none of the connections were hot and everything was doing fine. I'm putting this dig bone in my RV prep kit until we buy one.

title: Performing well in a semi-truck
text: My husband had this installed in the semi-truck to run his very small microwave and a small Keurig when he's on the road. The company mechanics installed it, so I'm not able to speak to the complexity or requirements of the project. He's been using it for a couple of weeks now without any problems. The microwave is working correctly when he needs it and he has fresh coffee at every stop. He said it doesn't make a lot of noise and it never feels hot when he's using it.

title: Very handy for several types of projects
text: You never know when you'll need a level. These are nice because they fit in small spaces and having 6 means you can have one in multiple locations. I've used these already in an RV test drive and set up with good results and doing some fence repair. I set the level on the fence post top as we set it in concrete and it worked well.

title: Fits a Kia Soul
text:
We have a Kia Soul that we love as a daily driver around town and for short roadtrips. My primary complaint has been the hard steering wheel - after a 150 miles on the road, that thing feels like you're holding a pipe.

This cover adds a bit of cushion and softer grip. Definitely a significant improvement and more comfortable than the steering wheel without it. It's a tight fit, but the cover doesn't shift or slip around as you drive. I do suspect the fake leather material won't last more than a few months, but we'll see.

title: Comfortable and easy to wipe clean
text:
The old cover on my driver's seat was starting to come apart and with dogs, there's no way I'm going without a seat cover. This one fits the Kia Soul seat, but is really a bit too narrow for the F-150.

I like the padding on this cover, it isn't super thick, but you notice it after 200 miles on the road. It's comfortable and protects the seats from dog hair and claw marks. The polyurethane is easy to clean, but you won't ever mistake it for real leather.

title: Legal size for Texas
text: This is more durable than it looks and definitely more attractive. The paw prints are visible and easily identifiable. This installed in the holes already in the car and fit correctly. Most importantly, the frame does not block any of the Texas license plate and it legal.

title: Look great and a nice variety of quotes
text:
We recently bought a second car as a daily driver and I needed new Firefly decals for it. My best friend bought her first new car the same week and I wanted to gift her a Firefly decals to christen her car as well. This set of four was a great choice so we could each pick our favorites.

The decals have a pretty standard application and I had no problems getting them positioned correctly and applied cleanly. They are easy to see against dark tinted windows and look great. I'm really pleased.

title: Thick, sturdy and only fit the Ram
text:
I put these in a beat up, old ranch truck just to cut down on the mud and grime and to cover holes in the carpet. It's a 2007 Ram and the mats fit it pretty well. Of course, the stupid truck has died permanently a week after getting these. (We aren't putting any more money in that thing)

I hoped that I could just use these in the other ranch truck - a 1999 Ford F-250. No dice. They just don't fit and they are way too big for my little daily driver Kia Soul. (I had to try) It's a shame because these are really nice. They are very thick and stiff and not meant to be trimmed for fit. If you drive a Dodge Ram, these are great though.

title: Works very well, easy to put up and take down
text: We just bought a Kia Soul as a second car/daily driver and it lives outside since there's no room in the garage. That means sun and heat all day in Texas and that's just miserable. This sun shade fits the windshield exactly both in width and height. The visors hold it in place at the top and the bottom rests right where the dash and windshield meet. I've noticed a definite reduction of heat in the car in the three days I've used this - I'm sort of amazed. It weighs nothing and is reasonably easy to fold and put away when I need to drive the car. The dog and cat design is cute.

title: Worked on small, light scratches
text: If you have a shallow scratch then this should fix it for you. A deep or severe scratch...and you need more serious work. This system is pretty simple to use and doesn't take forever. I had a minor set of scratches on the side of my truck after a tree branch scraped it out in the pasture. Nothing too ugly, but still...  I would say they are 90% invisible now.

title: Very handy. Sturdy and well made
text: I always have one of these types of containers in my vehicles. They are excellent for keeping all my dog leashes and harnesses together and the first aid kits. This one is smaller than my other two, but it's well made and quite sturdy. I like the metal handles on this box. The interior dividers give the sides support and the whole thing stands securely even when empty. It's a nice portable box.

title: Nice scent in an attic type loft space
text: I put these in two storage lofts I built into our weekend cabin. Stuff goes up there for winter storage and is never seen again until summer the next year. These sachets should cut down on any mustiness. They have a nice lavender scent that wafts down to the living area without being intrusive. You need to remove the plastic wrap before using these.

title: Makes saddle cleaning faster
text: I've trusted Lexol for many years with my very expensive saddles, bridles, luggage and hand bags. It cleans and conditions without stripping or drying the leather. This new swipe application system is pretty good for a quick clean up project. The cleaner and conditioner is inside each sponge applicator and sort of seeps out as you apply pressure. I like this setup for doing a quick clean on saddles after riding and my riding boots look great after using these.

title: Worked well for cleaning a mower
text: I actually used these wipes on the mower the other day. It was pretty gunked up and needed cleaning. These are reasonably tough and sturdy - they didn't shred immediately. The scrubby side is a nice touch and helpful with built up stuff. The mower certainly looks better and the crud around the blades is gone.

title: Easy to use, keeps lumber in place
text: This is one of those things that you don't think about until you need it and wish you had it. I've used it a couple of times now to keep hay bales from shifting around and to keep some lumber still after a Lowe's run. It works just fine and everything stays in place. I haven't noticed any scratches or damage on my truck bed from the pole - we also have a Rhino bed liner so that helps of course.

title: Did a pretty decent job in two vehicles
text:
I've used this in two vehicles. My pickup that always has dogs in it and a friend's sedan with cigarette odor embedded in the fabric. It's easy to do and takes like two minutes. The scent is fruity with an undertone of chemical something.

Nonetheless, it definitely freshened my eau du doggo truck and after several days, it still smells better than before this stuff was applied. My smoker friend's car was a striking improvement for a day or two and then it was back to the old funk. Of course, she's still smoking in the car, but on the rare occasions I need to ride with her, I can use this stuff first and get through the trip.

title: Holds a golf cart battery correctly
text: I'm experimenting with a portable solar charger for trips to our desert cabin. I needed a golf cart battery for this project and then realized it needed a tray. So...this tray is what I'm using. The battery fits correctly and doesn't slip or slide on the tray and it definitely keeps things looking more organized. I'm happy....it does what it's supposed to do.

title: Not as thick as other covers. Fine for trailer tires
text:
We have a stock trailer that isn't used often - I don't haul 4 horses at once very often anymore. The big trailer trailer tends to sit around months on end and that's never good for tires. We've always had good, thick tire covers and I thought these would be nice as backups.

These aren't meant to go over big, oversized off road tires by any means, but for a regular trailer or car tire, they fit fine. The covers will do the job, but they are thinner than any set we've ever had before. I hesitate to think they will survive more than a year down in the West Texas sun and heat and dry air. However, in a more temperate environment, these are probably all you need.

title: Two weeks of hard use and it's holding up pretty well
text:
We have a great backseat cover for the truck that has served us well for several years. It's finally beginning to wear out - I have multiple dogs in and out of the truck almost every day, so our cover needs to take abuse.

This one is a decent replacement. It's better padded than it looks in the photos, so there's a bit of cushion when the dogs are on a road trip. The length is actually a few inches too short to fit exactly over the back seat of our F150 truck. I'm just tossing and old blanket under it to cover the side edge of the seat. So far this cover has done well for two weeks with dogs, muddy paws, and two hundred pounds of horse feed loaded on the seats. No snags or tears.

title: Runs a full size too small. Good for farm chores
text: I got these for my husband, but they are too small for him. The size large fits me, but I normally wear a medium, so these definitely run small. I don't ride a motorcycle, but I do work with horses and do barn chores every day of the year. The inside grip is good with a pitchfork and grabbing water buckets. I actually really like the padded knuckles area - very handy for hanging a gate on new hinges.

title: Blade connection snapped off trying to install and it's useless now
text: I was going to replace a RainX wiper with this one on our F150, but that didn't happen. The hook on this wiper that connects to the wiper arm was not attached properly at the factory. When we tried to install it, the entire piece fell off the blade and cracked. I'm perfectly capable of installing new wiper blades and just put the RainX blade n a month ago, so it's not a user error. I am disappointed by the quality control here.

title: 22" fits the 2015 F150. Smooth, even water removal with no bouncing or squeaking
text:
We have the 22 inch blade on the passenger side wiper for our 2015 F150 truck - just FYI the F150 takes the 22" wipers on both sides, but not every vehicle has same size wiper blades. I had recently replaced both wipers with a pair from Rain X and wasn't unhappy with them. However, I think I actually like this one better after using one of each at the same time for a week now.

This one installed in just a minute or two with no drama at all - just snapped on and done. There's a neon green cover over the actual wiper blade to remove and that's it. The blade sweeps across the glass smoothly and quietly with no streaking or missed spots. It doesn't bounce or stutter or squeak going down the road either. Hopefully this wiper will last two years or longer like the original ones that came on my truck.

title: Fits a 2015 F-150 correctly, easy to install. Windows are smear free
text: After three years, I finally had to replace the original wipers on my F150 truck. I went with the Rain-X honestly because they were cheaper than others and the size I needed was in stock. As it turns out, these are pretty good wipers and were easy to install. They fit my truck correctly have worked fine for three months now. No smears or missed spots even in heavy downpours.

title: Fit the back windows on an F-150, still up after a week of 100 plus temperatures
text:
This is Texas and it's July which means high temperatures and high humidity and direct sun going down the road - never mind parking at the grocery store. I keep window shades on my passenger windows year round because I always have dogs in my truck and I want to minimize the direct sun beaming in as we go places.

These two cling shades are smaller than my others and that's actually a good thing. They fit perfectly on the rear window of the F-150 truck exactly right - leaving the center window that slides open uncovered. These have been up in my truck for a week and haven't fallen off or pealed loose yet. Yesterday it was 104 degrees outside and the cling shades are still in place.

title: Stable to use, rides quietly strapped to the tailgate. Fits a F150 fine
text:
This has to be one of the better purchases I've made for my truck. We're using it on a 2015 F-150 and it fits exactly as it should without interfering with the rear camera wiring. We also have a Rhino spray on bed liner and that didn't interfere with the installation either.

The ladder brace/hinge piece screws in and lies flat without being wobbly or vibrating going down the road - we used 6 bolts to attach it. The ladder itself folds flat and the strap holds it properly and is reasonably simple to adjust for the proper tension.

I've driven around with this on my truck for three weeks now over some really rough terrain - I just got back from Terlingua and Big Bend National Park in West Texas. We did some off roading to get to our cabin, including rock trails cut into the Christmas Mountains, gravel/river rock trails alongside the Rio Grande and straight desert trekking. This ladder just rode smooth without bouncing around, no excess vibrations or noise. It unfolds, kicks into place and is ready to use in seconds. Flip it back up, snap the straps and get moving. I love the easy access to unload hay bales at the horse barn, luggage and dog crates on trips and the bikes and gear out in West Texas. I can't believe we didn't get this sooner!

title: Easy to trim to fit in a 2014 Freightliner Cascadia. Great for the truck dog
text: My husband has a puppy in his truck with him and wanted a way to keep her from hanging her head out the window, but still get fresh air as they go down the road. These had to be trimmed to fit properly, but they do fit correctly and don't come out unless he takes them out. He's used them for ventilation when he stops and has a fan to move air when the temperature is reasonable - that means less time idling and wasting fuel. He's using these in a 2014 Freightliner Cascadia.

title: Stays in place even when driving on rough roads. Keeps the dog cool in the sleeper
text: My husband wanted a fan for his big truck to keep his dog a bit cooler and add air flow in the sleeper during long stops. He's been really pleased with it so far. It's easy to attach and move as required and it definitely moves air. There's no speed selection, but it isn't a problem for his needs. Yesterday he said he was over a long stretch of really rough, pot holed road and the fan stayed up without falling off. If it survives the entire summer we'll be happy.

title: Easy to install - fit in my F150 windows fine. No sliding or coming off
text:
We have tinted windows in our truck, but this is Texas and the sun can be relentless even with tints. We're planning a road trip from Texas to Alberta Canada this summer and the sun will definitely be an issue. There are three shades in the set - one for each of the back door and front passenger door windows.

It took ten seconds to install these - just smooth it over the window and you're done. If you have dog nose prints on your car windows, like we do, you need to clean the windows first for the best adhesion. It's been several days and none of these have come off or slipped out of place.

title: I needed a second person to help install. Sticks out significantly on an F150
text:
We travel with large dogs and sometimes that means big dog crates need to go with us. On a cross country trip, those crates rattling in the back of the truck bed can get annoying fast. Especially since two of our crates are custom made solid steel and weigh about 100 pounds each. I also show horses and occasionally need extra hay in the chase vehicle that doesn't fit in the towing truck. I've been considering one of the hitch cargo holders for awhile.

I had to get help to assemble this rack and two of the holes weren't lined up quite right - had to use a hammer to get them set. This thing is pretty heavy, but manageable. It is awkward to maneuver and handle without a second person helping. I absolutely cannot put this on or take it off our truck without assistance actually.

My star reduction is because of how far this protrudes from the back of our truck. It's significantly farther than a similar style rack my friend has on his truck - same truck we have. No way would I go to a grocery store or restaurant and try to park with this attached - you'll need two spaces. You can fold it up if it's empty, but that's not helpful with stuff strapped to it on a road trip. Nonetheless, we will use this on our drive from Texas to Canada this summer since we'll definitely be taking the big steel dog crates.

title: Sturdy plastic that doesn't bend when gripped. Length is nice with a big truck
text:
I was sort of expecting just a flimsy funnel like you get at a dollar store in a pinch. Happily, this is not the case at all. This funnel is made of sturdy, thick plastic that doesn't squeeze or bend when gripped.

The extra length is exactly what we needed for adding fluids to our F-150 truck. It's tall and I'm short, just checking the oil requires a step stool. Me adding oil is like a cartoon mouse trying to fill a container on an elephant's back. This funnel made things a little easier and definitely resulted in far fewer curse words.

title: Works well on glass & light insect remains. Thick or dried messes required two treatments
text:
We drove through four of those swarms of love bugs yesterday over a 126 mile stretch. There were bug remnants coating the windshield, hood, grill and headlights of the truck. Gruesome and disgusting....as evidenced in my photos.

Today I tried this spray with relatively decent results. The instructions are pretty specific - apply to cool surfaces, let sit 30 seconds, wipe away and do not let sit on paint, then rinse with water. This stuff actually did a great job on cleaning my windshield with just a soft rag.

Using this on really caked in, thick bug debris on the hood and grill resulted in a so-so cleaning. I think if the bugs are...well...fresher, it will work fine. I had to really scrub, rinse and reapply the spray to make a real difference. It seems to work best on the glass surfaces like the windshield, mirrors and headlights.

title: Not suitable for the weight of two weapons. Weak stitching on the straps will break.
text:
At first glance this looks like a terrific gun case for a hunting trip or, in my case, storage in the barn office for a rifle and shotgun. I have a hog problem out here that can be a serious danger to humans and horses. I have had to warn them off more than once in broad daylight, keeping a rifle handy is a must. I mostly want to use this case both in the barn on on the gator or tractor depending on my needs.

The problem is that the stitching on the straps is weak. As are the rubber pulls on the zippers around the gun pockets. These are critical components for regular use and safety. If I am bouncing around in the pastures with a herd of wild hogs around and rifle falls off the back of the tractor because the carrier straps came unstitched, that's a problem. The system is not designed for the weight of two guns. Nor is it geared for a true hunting rifle with a scope installed. It's probably just fine with a single weapon inside - our Remington 870 is quite light compared to some of the bolt action rifles for example. I darn sure won't be carrying the Benelli shotgun in this unit though!

title: Defunked the 18 year old ranch truck - smells fruity instead of like wet dog & cattle. **30 day Update**
text:
I figured the absolute best place for a serious test of this Air Re-Fresher was our 1998 Ford F-250 Diesel Ranch truck with almost 500,000 miles on it. When I say that truck has been worked hard and smells gross, I cannot stress the word gross hard enough. The average Mom's minivan has NUTHIN' on the odor in this truck. In it's 18 years of hard work this truck has hauled countless trailers of cattle, horses, and heavy equipment. It's had wet dogs, sick calves, wounded deer, mamma cats with new born kittens and some of the smelliest, dirtiest men with muddy, manure covered boots have flopped down inside of it. It's been caught out in a rain storm with the windows down more often than I care to remember and driven through two forest fires rescuing horses in West Texas and there's a permanent smoke smell buried in the fabric 6 years later. Just riding five miles in the Green Machine will leave a layer of funk on your clean clothes.

So.... the Maguiar's Air Re-Freshers in Figi Scent. My theory was it can't be any worse than the Funk and while we've been using Febreeze weekly and it works pretty well, it's not a long term solution. I put the can of Maguiars in according to the directions and then let the truck air out for a half hour. The guys came by on their way to move some cattle next door and burst out laughing at the fruity scent wafting in the air from the general vicinity of the Green Machine. They piled into the truck and proclaimed it free of the Funk, but now it smells like a big box of fruity Chiclets gum. I'm not at all sure if that's better or not to be honest. It's been two days and the fake fruity smell is still super strong, but the old mildew/sweat/wet dog scent we started will hasn't reared it's ugly head, so I'm calling it a win.

***** UPDATE May - 30 Days Later *****

It's been 30 days since I used this refresher on the foul Green Machine and I realized tonight that it still smells ok. Not as fresh as the first week, but definitely better than before I used the Meguiars. I've had a couple of hound dogs in the truck a few times since I used the spray, but nothing truly awful yet. I'll definitely use this stuff again in the future.

title: Kept my bumper bright after 9 days - even on a dirt road! See the photos
text:
I have a brand new truck so I can't comment as to how well this 303 Automotive Trim Restorer & Protectant Kit actually restores, but it seems to protect pretty well. I applied it on the plastic step guard on the rear bumper and on the step rails along the sides of the truck.The first three photos show the before, the comparison during the application, the immediate look right after the 303 was put on as it dried.

The box comes with a single bottle of the liquid solution and a small round applicator sponge. Read the directions before you use this - it's really clear that it should not get on any painted surfaces and if it does, you have to use rubbing alcohol immediately to remove it. Clean and dry the plastic before you apply the 303 also. I just used a damp cloth to wipe down my bumper and side steps on the truck, nothing special here. You need to really shake this stuff before using and then squirt just a small bit onto the sponge and rub it on in small sections at a time. Like some of the other reviewers have noted, the formula is pretty thin and if you use too much, it will run - you can definitely add more if you need to.

Once the 303 is on, it dries quickly and doesn't seem to leave any residue or film behind. Nor is it slick - I use the steps on my truck multiple times a day and if this stuff were slippery, it would be getting a one star rating! The last photo is 9 days after I put the 303 on - it's a comparison between a section where it was applied on the right and where it wasn't applied on the left. I drive a quarter mile down a dirt road seven days a week, twice a day to the horse barn and after 9 days without washing the truck, you can see a distinct difference in the areas where this 303 plastic protectant was applied and where it wasn't used. There is still dust and dirt on the plastic, but the area still looks bright and shinier than the area without the 303. That's good enough to convince me to go ahead and apply this stuff to the rest of the bumper and the external plastic on my truck (grill area, back of the mirrors etc)

My one tiny quibble is that these mats don't quite cover all the carpet to the door edge. I work with horses every day and that means mud, hay and real dirt - any exposed carpet is going to get filthy fast.If you are actually working with your truck and wear boots then you to consider this issue. I like that these mats are lighter weight than the more expensive versions from Weather Tech - easier to pull out and clean in a rush. The trade off is that I have a strip of exposed carpet on the driver's side, but I can find a work around if I think about it. The mats are catching the mud and gunk without a doubt and they aren't shifting or sliding even on a rough, country road.

title: The new squeeze trigger style is easy to regulate quantity. Eliminated a squeak on a dog gate instantly
text:
It's hard to imagine that WD-40 could be improved on - I mean this is a standard product that is in almost every home and garage and for good reason. The term "Multi-Use" is absolutely correct. It stops rust, stops squeaks, releases stuck metal things and generally keeps stuff rolling, pulling, sliding and moving along as it should. My one complaint has been the old style can and push spray top in the aerosol style. It was hard to control where the WD-40 went and how much of it was coming out.

This new pull trigger style is a nice improvement. The original metal can is the same, the actual product is the same, but you have a new way to dispense it that makes using it in the house and on small stuff a little more precise. At least for me. I used this on the interior squeaking hinge of a metal dog gate and instantly it's silent again - no drips or over spray. Spraying it up and on to the wheels & track of a bi-fold set of doors in the hall closet eliminated the weird dragging noise and both doors open and close smoothly and silently once again. No drips or excess WD-40 on the wood or door frame. One quick squeeze of the trigger and it's done. For those that are confused - this is NOT A REFILLABLE CAN and nowhere on the description is that indicated. The term multi-use simply means what it has always meant with WD-40 - you can use it on any number of projects, materials and for multiple purposes.

title: Illegal to use in Texas - hides the state name on the license plate. Well made and looks great, but a novelty only.
text: Drat. The license plate frame isn't legal for use in Texas without being seriously altered first. The top part that says "Don't Blink" (the most important part!) extends too low and covers half the word Texas on the top of the actual license plate. That's an absolute violation and can get you a $280 ticket - or more if the officer is grumpy. My husband thinks he can cut this frame back and make it fit, but we'll lose the angel images on either side of the words. I think I may just use it on the back of the horse trailer as decoration instead....it's well made and looks great.

title: Well thought out design, holds a lot, handy for the back of the car emergency gear.
text:
Surprisingly versatile and well thought design. I have been using a single compartment fabric box in the back of my car for a year and it's worked perfectly fine. I didn't realize I could do better until I tried this one. The split compartments is much easier for organizing and finding things in the dark or a rush. Plus the outside pockets with flaps on this box are excellent places for a flashlight, bottle of water, extra tire pressure gauge and a pair of gloves.

I was concerned initially about the lightness of this box, thinking it would just slide all over the car if it wasn't full, but so far that hasn't been a problem. I have a first aid kit, leash, two cans of dog food (never know when you need to rescue a stray), a thermal blanket, the bottle of water, an atlas, flashlight, a pair of Keds sneakers, and box of rubber gloves in it. There's room for a couple of sacks of groceries as well. The handles are easy to grab and the unit collapses just as it should when it's empty. I will continue to use this in my car and relegate the old one to storage at the barn. I was provided a free sample for testing and review.

title: Installed in seconds, survived 3 carwashes & Texas Sun. UPDATE Jan 2016
text:

This sticker is still going strong! I had to buy a new one for my new truck and I fully expect this one to last three years as well. Great product.

title: Fixed my oil leak
text:

text:
Great Value, concentrate with easy measure bottle to mix up enough spray bottles mixed with water for maybe Fifty car washes!

One problem, the spray applicator bottle was not included in my package of concentrate & microfiber towel.

Called the toll free number provided on the bottle, to inquire what size this bottle was supposed to be, so how many ounces of water would I add in another spray bottle to use the product.

The toll free number on the bottle goes to a seller of Natural products… Seems odd they sell car cleaner. But it is eco-friendly with the less packaging concentrate…

The kind lady on the other end of the first call says that they occasionally get calls about this product, which isn’t theirs. “Must be ‘older product their ‘old toll free number still on it, which is now our number…”

I apologize & she’s very nice. I decide to take the chance… “By the way, since you get frequent calls for them, do you happen to have their correct new number?”

She checks & gives me another number!!! “Thanks!”

So I call new number, still needing to just know: How many ounces of water do I add to a spray applicator bottle with ‘one dose’ of this product?

Takes a few minutes on hold & I’m told the capacity of the applicator bottle. BUT also that their bottle sprays a preferred mist type spray for even coverage.

She also advised me (As it does say on the bottle of concentrate), not to use the product on heated car surfaces, in the Alabama Summer Sun!

Since I’ve been searching for a replacement spray bottle I may have on hand & then spending time making these calls to get this information, it’s now pushing 11:00 AM & my car is out in the summer. I planned to do this early this morning, but it hasn’t gone as planned….

Well, my spray bottle may not produce the best results & now it’s hot outside. Day’s not going as planned. Why do I try to “Plan” my days?

She looks up my address & sees that I did just purchase their product. She offers to send me the spray bottle that was missing from my order, so I can achieve the best results with their product & be a happy customer! WoW! Thanks, Awesome!

Within a few days, I receive a package from them. They sent me another full set, the concentrate, microfiber towel, and the special applicator bottle!!!

I cannot wait to try this out, & if it works out as well as the problem resolution, I have No Excuse to have a dirty car for at least a year or more!!!

title: Great portable device, doesn't cool a lot though
text:
I have this in green, and love the colors.
The size is good - just a little bigger than a deck of cards.

The blades are just cut foam, so if you wanted to use this around kids, there
isn't a sharp blade to cut little fingers (or big ones!).

You fill this with water, like a squirt gun.
The plug is decent, and I've not had it leak yet.

You turn on the fan first - sometimes I have to kick-start the blades to get them
going - wierd, but not impossible to deal with it.
As far as the water - you push a lever on the other side. The water
shoots out in a stream, not in a gentle mist, even with the blades going.
Perhaps it is just ours, but mist is not what I think of with this.

I could see it being helpful if the water inside is very cold. However, if you are
just putting in normal water, then don't expect a lot of cooling power. It is just working
by evaporation anyway, so on really humid days, this won't do much.

Also, the description says it takes 4 AA batteries. It only takes ONE.
I have an old lithium camera battery in there, and it works great.
(For those who don't realize it, lithium batteries specifically the blue ones,
are the best ones ever for cameras and other electronic items that take AA types.
After they no longer power your camera, these little powerhouses still have enough
juice to run other things that use AA, like hair clippers or this little fan.)

So, not horrible, but don't expect serious cooling - it's more like a refreshing
spritz in the face.

High quality, flexible, sturdy -- this one is definitely worth the investment.

They came in a "plain brown wrapper" which indicated only they're made in Taiwan, but there is no instruction sheet or brand name graphic or marketing information. Even the retention rings were separate from the covers, so I needed to figure out which slots to use for the rings. Since I don't replace wheel covers every day, I found a brief instruction video on YouTube that got me going. Sorry to have to return them --or provide the first really negative review-- but even cheap merchandise ought to fit well enough not to fly off at the first pothole. title: Those other gimmicky products can't touch this classic standy!
text:
I love this stuff, been using it for decades on my horse tack and leather boots. No gimmicks, no bizarre edible ingredients, no suave label, just a great, proven product that gives consistent high-quality results. It conditions and absorbs well without leaving a residue or film. The smell is light and pleasant. After using it leather feels nourished without being mealy, weak, oily, or wet even if you over-apply it. It doesn't excessively darken leather and won't discolor leather if the application isn't perfectly even. It's ideal for thick leather but fine for thin leather if you use a light coat, and will last a long time. Like most conditioners, don't use it on suede or rough-out.

It seems like only horse-people know about this stuff, which is surprising because I see more and more "saddle" products being used on all types of other leather goods, and this works better than 95% of them - trust me, I've tried them all before coming back to this old standby. Maybe people don't use it because it's not made with honey or milk or guava fruit or dragonfly farts, and doesn't have a fancy label? (The label is so very..... GERMAN isn't it? lol) Though I do love to follow conditioning with a beeswax protectant, like Obenhaufs which is an excellent product.

I apply this stuff with my hands, but a sponge or a rag is fine. It's not so hard or thick you need your hands to melt it first, but it'll absorb a little better/faster and you'll lose a lot of product to rags and sponges which soak up the conditioner. For extremely dry leather (especially old saddle flaps), apply a generous coat and then gently bend/roll the leather back and forth, in and out - without forcing the leather too much (I cracked a brittle saddle-flap that way once). That'll separates the fibers and pull the conditioner in. Keep applying and flexing until you have the suppleness you want, then apply a good coat and let it sit overnight. Wipe off any excess the next day and let it sit a few more hours, there'll be no film or residue. I've made dry, brittle, cardboard-like leather supple and new-looking with that method. Also works for breaking in a new saddle fast, if you prefer not to ride in a stiff, slick saddle until it decides to soften up, if it ever does.

Absolutely love this stuff, it's a classic and far superior to most of what's out there these days.

title: The new go-to product for my tack and boots
text:
Bought 4oz last week and now I'm buying the 8oz size. This stuff is AWESOME! I'm a pro horse rider so most of my equipment is leather gets dirty, wet, and abused. This stuff is exactly what I've been looking for... I've already used it on boots, saddles, bridles, even a vintage Foxhunting whip with lash. Everything looks fantastic! (I won't say "like new" because most of it's been too abused to ever go down that road again, but better than they've looked in years.)

It really conditions nicely while protecting, without leaving a tacky or waxy film. When I lived in New Zealand I used this excellent wax product called "Bee Seal" which I haven't been able to find in the States and have been searching for a similar product for years. I've tried some other wax-based products, including Beesbutter, and been disappointed. Those products either disappear into the leather or leave a tacky film. Others leave leather "soggy" and mealy, a big problem with creasing in boots which actually looses integrity and splits more easily. Obenhaufs seems to condition but strengthen, or at least not make it worse.

I've also been impressed how well it penetrates and conditions thicker leather, like saddle flaps. Most conditioners disappear into thick leather and I end up using 3 or 4 heavy applications.

It smells nice, like honey (unsurprisingly). Yes, it darkens leather-- all conditioners do, just like wet hair or clothes are darker. The thinner and lighter the leather, the darker it'll become-- on those leathers start with as thin a coat as possible if you're concerned - rub it around your hands until there's a thin almost invisible coat on your hands, then rub your hands on the leather. It definitely helps to apply this stuff with your hands, for one thing you're not loosing product which inevitably soaks into a rag or sponge. It'll make your hands soft too. I applied it to warmed and cool leather and found it definitely soaks in faster with warmed leather, however it still did fine on the cool leather too. We haven't had rain so I haven't been able to test the waterproofing, but I'm already more than satisfied.

You will have to make your own Female To Female coupler air cable in order to use any air tool like a blower or air chuck that you use with a standard compressor.  For this reason, I'm docking this thing two stars as I do not understand why they wouldn't standardize the componentry on this thing to work with what you already have in your garage. title: RAM 3500 INSTALLATION INSTRUCTION ADDENUM
text:
First time install time 30 minutes
HEADACHES:
- Spacer orientation in instructions was incorrect.
- Not all tools needed were listed, for this and lack of instructional diligence I am docking it one 1 star. Product development should have went through several dry runs first and revised their instructions to include ALL tools and best practices.
- A 10mm Flexible Head Ratcheting wrench will be immensely helpful taking off the bumper support bracket on the RAM 2500/3500. Tolerances are too tight for a socket. (TEKTON WRN57170)
- Flashlight / lamp helpful working under your vehicle aligning bolt holes.
- A 3" socket extension will be very helpful with mounting the bedstep to the bumper with the 15mm bolts as the holes are recessed deeply and you won't be able to turn the bolts with the socket unless you have a very very deep 15mm socket. Any magnetization will be helpful with keeping the bolt into the socket for a horizontal installation youre doing upside laying sideways. Not everyone has a lift.
Tip: Mount the bottom bolt first. Not a bad idea to use a T-handle 3/16 hex allen wrench as a sort of spud wrench for the top bolt hole to somewhat align it and hold it in position either. You will use the 3/16 hex allen wrench later for mounting the step part. Not using the socket wrench itself, use jus the socket extension and the 15mm socket, insert bolt into socket, and gently spin it with your fingers so you can feel if it goes into the hole. Once you can't turn it with your finger any longer and it's not stripping the bolt, then use the socket torque wrench to tighten it to spec. Harbor Freight sells a small digital torque wrench adapter that you can use with any socket setup.
