title: Work nice on small tires
text:
If you have a few things with small tires, these are handy to have and can pay for themselves with one or two uses. I have even used them on bigger tires sucessfully.

I'll just add that these aren't magic. There is a trick to using tire irons, they don't use themselves. If you've never used tire irons, check out some You Tube videos to learn the tricks. Once you get the hang of it, it's pretty easy. Two extremely useful items that help a bunch are some dish detergent as a lubricant and a pair of small vise grips to help get the tire started. Describing how to use them in print doesn't do it justice, watching somebody do it is enormously helpful. Check out some videos, there are a lot of tricks.

title: So far, so good
text:
How well this performs will be something that time will tell. The idea of using these is well proved to extend battery life. I just bought new batteries for my cart and wanted to protect my investment so I bought this based upon a variety of expert reviews. This model is nice in that it will automatically "shut itself off" when the charge level drops, so it won't completely drain your batteries like some others.

Installation is very easy. The LED shows you that it's connected and working. I'll say that one thing positive is that the company that makes these contacted me about a defect they discovered that supposedly could make it inoperable. As they described it, it was a component that didn't meet spec. They sent me a new one at no charge. This leads me to believe that they take their product seriously and stand behind it.

I only have about 6 months use, but looking in the battery cells I see no signs whatsoever of any sulfating. This is the type of item that it takes a long time to evaluate. I can't speak to the "rejuvinating" capabilities because I started with new batteries.

So far based on all the above, I've given it 3 stars. My gut says it will perform as advertised, and I'd it rate it higher if I had that evidence of time.

title: fits securely in existing holder, optional tray nice for my keys/phone/sunglasses/tissue
text:
Fits my 2012 Jeep Grand Cherokee. I have the typical set of two cup holders to the right of the shifter. The holders are fine, but I kind of wanted something that could accommodate larger travel mugs. I was also keen on buying the tray style because I figured it would be good for holding my keys as my car has keyless button press start. Having them on the tray keeps them secure and in view. I can also keep my phone and sunglasses on the tray. Easy grab without it getting lost on seat or floor. Basically that is all I bought this for.

The cup holder feels very secure. It is well tucked into my cars holder. I like the slit in side for use with handle cups.

You can pop the tray off if you dont want that taking up space all the time. The tray itself is nice, and has an additional cup holder built in. Not sure if I will ever use it, and would maybe prefer not to have it (or maybe it could be designed to be optional--maybe a slider piece underneath could be considered for future designs?).

So far the tray seems sturdy. It isnt meant for heavy stuff as it does pull down a little under some weight, but it also doesnt feel like it is going to break. The tray swivels. I keep mine swiveled out toward well into the passenger side. I never have passengers.

I find it very useful and am so far pleased with this purchase. If I experience anything worth sharing, I will come back to do so.

All the bad reviews provide no details.

title: eh, they're ok. Not good fit for rear of 2012 Jeep Grand, but Ok fit for front, one hole
text:
It's "OK". Middle of road rating of 3. Could be better, but not entirely useless.. unless it falls apart quickly. I bought a pair of front seat covers AND the rear cover. I am assuming that since both are listed on this page, that only one review will count, so I will combine my thoughts.

1st off, this is for a 2012 Jeep Grand Cherokee Laredo 4x4, new to me despite being 10 years old. Perfect condition. I am prone to spilling my drink, and I do labor work so I always have something messy going on. I wanted seat covers that are waterproof or water resistant. Maybe there is better way to do it. 4 stars if it weren't for that hole. Overall 3 stars

BACK SEATS: Nope, really loose on my back seat, and the holes don't line up for the seat belts, and the head rest covers are huge. But they tuck well and dont look too bad. The rest is OK. No holes at least. I dont love it by any means, but it is on there for now- rather have something than nothing. Figured it might work as a dog fur collector too, fits better than those usually do. So 2 stars for fit, but 4 stars for being in good condition and looking like it does in picture. Annoyed that Amazon cleared it to fit my Jeep, when it doesn't. My jeep has center rear seat split with a head rest, and fortunately the rest rest is flush with seat when in lowest position. Doable, but annoying,. Overall: 3 stars

title: surprisingly strong suction, charge lasts long enough for most jobs, BUILT in air compressor!!
text:

Car vac (cordless or corded)

title: slim easy to use bottle, doesnt make me cough, works very well on glass, shiny surfaces, dog slob
text:
In short: It is a non stinky glass (and other surface) cleaner that works. Follow directions. All good.

Bottle arrives intact, fully loaded, ready to go. I took it to task by using it on various household items. I clean homes for a living, so I look for products that help save me time. Windex never works well enough, nor does Method or most other window cleaners. I'm not spending all day buffing out streaks, so I need something that can just work at the get go. Some that do work tend to be highly odorous (especially the kind that are in aerosol canister), which I only use when really necessary. When I find something that works (as in, it cleans, it doesnt leave streaks, no wrestling with a buffing cloth to make streaks disappear, noes make me cough, can be used on multiple surfaces if need be). This is suitable for everything I tried it on: black wall hung oven (shows fingerprints and streaks easily), black dishwasher, glass of convection oven, black microwave, bathroom mirror, a vanity mirror, and a dog slobbered window. All fine. No fuss.

Shake bottle, has nice even spray. With any window cleaner,I do initial wipe to clean off excess gunk, then following up with clean cloth to pick up residue. Usually I will spray just a little again if I started off with extra dirty surface. Some streaks are simply residue from now allowing cleaner to penetrate, or not using enough. Then exacerbated by using a too wet or too dirty of a cloth. If a cloth has fabric softener on it, then you will nearly always have streaks. Lastly, sometimes it is just the cleaner itself.

If looking for strictly car window cleaning use, this will be fine. Again, just be sure to use clean cloths. Dry cloths. Wipe in one direction. The slim bottle is nice for keeping in car. For home use, I doubt very much I would buy this for that. There are others that are around same price or less, with more in it. For my business, I have to find best product at best price. If I were casual using this, then the $12 price tag wouldnt bother me. I dont rate on price, so you do you.

title: good sturdy storage bag, cargo bag is durable, inc instructions, liner, straps, & lock
text:
I have acquired two roof top cargo bags recently, one each for our two Jeeps (Cherokee, and Grand Jeep Cherokee). While they have decent cargo space for basic trips (I pack light), I wanted to havve extra room in case we needed to "bug out", or help someone else out.

I dont travel, and when I do, I pack light. I can live out of a backpack no problem. But when I take my dogs with me? They have loads of luggage, lol.  Mom has one bag, and my babies have like 2 bags each. The main reason I got this is that I am a little bit of a prepper. Because we have 2 large labs and 3 cats, they would be packed up with us. No babies left behind. Most of my interior space will be taken up by them and their stuff if I had to pack everyone in. I figured if I have an exterior cargo bag, then I can pack up a bunch of things without worry about taking up critical interior space. Basically, I wanted options. And now I feel more prepared with having this cargo bag as an option to use, which has been slated for use on my husbands car. For me, I selected, [[ASIN:B09HB2NZFZ THINKLEARN 15 cubic foot Rooftop Cargo Carrier Bag in pink]]. Same size, but half the cost. Cargo bags are all over the place in pricing, so I wanted to see if there was any real difference. So far, not really. Anyway, now both cars are ready to go. Two is one, and one is none. 

Given that I dont think I will need it for regular use (hopefully, anyway.. anything is possible these days, hmm?) I wanted something that wasn't too costly, and something that appeared to have directions included in the bag. I dont want to have to suddenly refer back to a web page if I need it. This set includes instructions, a large zippered canvas like storage bag, AND a protective liner. All inclusive for a competitive price.

15 cubic feet storage capacity can hold a lot, and I figured was good width and length for my vehicle. I looked at larger capacity (some are 21 cubic feet), and that just seemed way too much. I think 15 cubic feet will provide plenty of storage in a reasonable, manageable size. Likely best for cars. 

Be sure to secure onto vehicle first, THEN pack it. 

Claims to be waterproof, and to make sure to orientate it for maximum wetness deflection. If using any soft top cargo carrier for longer storage (ie you keep it on your car with stuff in it longer than the driving portion of tripz), I would recommend a tarp and some bungee. Just in case. I basically consider these to be water resistant. Rain/wetness seems to work its way into the best of secured items. I am not saying this because I experienced a breech, just saying it as a means to be better prepared.

Storage bag is good, I like it better than the one that came with the other cargo bag I linked to. The one that this is stored in is a large square, has a zipper closure, and it opens wide. Much easier to stuff the bag, liner, and straps. Yet is small enough to easily keep in the car when not in use. THAT was another important feature.

No issues, directions are straight forward. Will report back if I experience anything else.

title: robust fresh aroma, pleasant, no headache triggers (for me), 12 pack!
text:
Exceeds my expectations in scent quality. The "Pearl Oyster" aroma is robust, fresh, pleasant. Kind of like a good shampoo. I like that the scent profile is listed directly on the air freshener. No guessing, or having to remember. Typical hanging paper board air freshener in shape of a jar candle. The lettering is unobtrusive. The largest lettering is the name of the scent (ie Pearl Oyster). The brand name, "Pray" is in small lettering. Keep bag on, but slightly open for low scent, or take bag off for max scent.

Pearl Oyster is "champaca", "tuberrose", and "vanilla". Like any candle or perfume, the scent alters depending on how much it is exposed to air and for how long. Directly in package, the individual notes are difficult to separate, but it still smells very good. Once allowed to permeate the air, the scents settle into a floral vanilla. Fresh, not synthetic smelling (although most likely are synthetic fragrance oils-- just smells good)

Many scents to choose from, and quite a few have musk (not pearl oyster). That is a scent trigger for me, so I will avoid it, but there are plenty of others for me to choose from. I dont rate on price, but I comment. The current price of $14.95 for 12 air fresheners makes them $1.25 a peice. Not too shabby.

Not sure if it truly lasts a month. I assume these are like other paper air fresheners where they are strongest when first opened then run down from there. If I experience anything extraordinarily good/bad/other, I will be back to update. But as is, no problems at this time. So 5 stars.

title: good for in between cleans, plenty of length, comes w/ storage bag, fair suction
text:
Good for in between cleans. If you got serious cleaning to do, then opt for a shop vac, then use this to keep up with crumbs and dirt. Car vacs, hand vacs are never going to provide an in depth clean. For that you need a regular vac. And that's ok, just know what you are buying this for (up keep, occasional mess), and it will be fine. If you are trying to clean up after years of build up.. or loads of deeply imbedded fur or debris, then no.. it just isnt going to happen. Buy this (or other brand) for ease of quick clean up and keep up.

I've yet to meet a small vac that is actually super powerful. The suction and performance from this is as expected- grabs up loose stuff, small bits. Fresh dog fur. Though any dog owner keeps sticky tape on hand for true extraction from carpet and seats.

Is more powerful than battery operated, by far. So dont even bother looking at those. Cord is just under 15' long, and plugs into 12V outlet (ie "cigarette lighter"). Others are closer to 16' and beyond. So for some that might fall a little short. However, I can work it fine in my Jeep Grand Cherokee. If you have multiple locations of power ports, then length wont be an issue at all. Kinda wish these things also had a regular house plug option because I would use this in my house for quick clean ups. Other than trying it out for review, the temps have been in the teens, and I dont plan to do anything else with cleaning up my car until it warms up again. In the mean time this will collect dust. But I digress..

I like the attachments- has some length of hose and tube to help reach between and under the seats. Has a brush tyle to help loosen up debris as you vacuum. Has a small brush tool for getting into very small spots. Just use it to loose up dirt, and then run vac over the area.

It is a wet & dry vac. I haven't used it on wet yet.

Comes with storage bag. All told, it takes up very little space, so I just keep this in my car. I am more apt to do the "upkeep" if I have it right there within easy reach.

I dont rate on price, but I comment. It seems to fall within range of other car vacs, though often I see them on sale making this on the higher end.

title: very robust foam snow broom, helps me from touching the car paint, easy to use
text:
Early impression because I have only used this once so far. We might be in for more snow tomorrow, so there is another chance. I selected this FOAM snow removal brush because I have new (to me) car with pristine paint, and I want to reduce the chance of scratching paint. NOW, anything will scratch paint (foam or snow brush bristles), so the idea is to remove as much snow as possible without touching the car itself-- so take snow down to 1/8 to 1/4", then the heat of car should let the rest melt/slide off, yet not leave too much to be a hazard to others. I have a long handled snow brush, but a lot of car forums mention using a foam board style- easier to control. So here I am. Otherwise, I loved my bristled snow broom for my old truck.

I found that the parts were very easy to put together, and that each segment feels very strong and sturdy. I unsnapped a few portions and did not have any issues in disassembling it. I am rather impressed with the length, it seems to go on for miles. Even before the telescoping option it is quite long. If you need it shorter most of the time, a link can be taken out. This will be good for vans, trucks, shorter folks in need of extra reach. Works great on my lovely Jeep Grand Cherokee. My 5'10" reach still benefits from a long handled snow removal tool. SO FAR this is working out great.

The foam head is thick, and durable feeling. I want sure what to expect, but it is thicker, firmer than imagined. It can be angled, and it can be locked in place. Very easy. The other end has an ice scraper with a couple different texture ends. Not sure if more than one end is meant to be used, but one side is textured, and the other sides are smooth, and they all work for scraping. That portion can be popped off, and now you have your long handled foam broom, and a shorter handled ice scraper. This can be helpful if you happen to have two people clearing off the car.

Comes with basic nubbed gloves, an instruction manual, and a drawstring bag for storage or whatever.

I'll be back to update once I have had more time with this-- good or bad, I'll let you know how it goes. Just need more snow! (or not, I'd be ok with that too, lol)

title: excellent fit, like the original but better as it includes coverage flap
text:
This Vesul cargo cover is fantastic. I searched high and low looking for a cargo cover that looked like it would be of good quality, have a good fit, and work for a long time. Now, we have only had our covers for a month, with light use, so it will be awhile before I can comment on longevity. But for all else? 5 stars from me.

I bought TWO retractable cargo covers from Vesul. This one for my husband's 2014 Jeep Cherokee. I bought another (different listing) for my [[ASIN:B075S548WT 2012 Grand Jeep Cherokee Laredo 4x4]]. Be sure to choose the correct year for the correct fit. Both are great.

When it comes to the 2014 model, the space between where a cargo cover anchors (tension fit) and the back of the seats is minimal. In the earlier models, particularly with the Grand Cherokee, the gap is significant. NO sure why Jeep designed it like that. SO, if you see reviews for other cargo covers complaining about the gap, it is because those covers are trying to mimic the original brand cargo covers. WITH VESUL, they compensate for that odd design by incorporating a flexible flap that can be attached to the rear seat head rests. Optional to use. For your 2014 Jeep CHerokee, you may not need to use the flap, but it's there if you want it. Let it hang down (it wont be noticeable), or go ahead and attach it (via snap on belt like closure). Super quick and easy. Just depends on the coverage you want. Any other detail also takes into consideration the original design (slightly offset handle pull, for example. Not a flaw, it all mimics the original design and fit). For this, I think VESUL has done an outstanding job.

Very easy to "install", just pop into place. It is a sturdy tension bar, similar in operation to a tension rod.

If I notice anything worth mentioning, I will be back to update.

Direct link to my review [[ASIN:https://www.amazon.com/review/R2AENGLBWIK6RY/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_rv]]

title: been using deer whistles since the 90s, no idea if they work, but its a must have for me
text:

There is really no way to tell for sure if they work, but I still use them. They are inexpensive enough that I find them worth while addition to my car. I live in a rural area, and while it isnt going to necessarily stop a deer already in motion, hopefully it stops one from decided to pick up movement as it hangs out near the road.

I needed a set because I just got a new (to me) Jeep.

Shows only one whistle being needed (applied on passenger side of car), but I used two. I figure, why not?

title: adds extra visibility which is reassuring
text:
Adds extra visibility. I got a new to me (but 10 years old) Jeep, and while it has big mirrors, I felt like i needed a little extra something to help me see. I am usually one to physically turn to look behind me, but some of the car framing impedes this effort. My old truck, and cars before then were always easy for me to see everything. Not so much now. title: excellent, sturdy fit for my 2012 Jeep Grand Cherokee Laredo 4x4
text:
So far so good. I bought this for my (new to me) 2012 Jeep Grand Cherokee Laredo 4x4. I had looked at mopar Jeep sites, and was unimpressed with the extraordinarily high cost of it. My (gorgeous) 10 years old vehicle deserves the best, but I wasn't convinced that was the best. I began checking around at dupes, and decided on this Vesul brand.

The benefit that this product has over a mopar option is that it has incorporated an extra piece of material to help cover the entire cargo area. The 2012 has a large gap between where the cargo cover slots are in comparison to the back of the seats. This leaves a wide space. So this product combats that by adding in a canopy. Did you know that the original does not include that piece, therefor leaving a gap? Not entirely sure why the vehicles were made like that, but off market options have rectified this. What I like is that if I dont want to use the extra material, I can just let it hang down, and it looks totally fine.

Fit is perfect. The ends just pop into place, via pressure fit. Good strong hold. The retractable portion slides right into place, securely. The off center cut out is as exactly like the brand name--hence why it is designed like that. Keep stuff like this in mind when looking for non mopar parts and accesories-- does it match the original intent. This does (plus bonus upgrade of coverage flap).

Ok, so that coverage flap-- it attached via snap closure strap that goes around the rear head rests. You will have to undo this in order to fold the seats forward. Easy enough.

I have no desire to place stuff on top of the cargo cover. But I imagine setting something lightweight down on it would be fine- hat, gloves, snow brush. Nothing heavy though.

I keep up on my reviews and update as needed (good or bad), so if experience anything worth sharing (especially if negative) I will be back to do so. I intend to take a couple of pictures soon.

As of right now, I am very pleased with this product, and like I said I bought a second for my husbands Jeep (and hopefully we will be just as pleased with it).

I bought a second cargo cover for my husband's [[ASIN:B01N9Q8UR6 2014 Jeep Cherokee 4x4]], which is a different product all together, so I will review it separately. But I wanted to mention it here, and will make more comment on it once we can install it. It is a Christmas gift, so it will be a couple of weeks before it can be installed. When I review that one, I will mention the one I got for my Jeep.

Update: still awesome. And, the one I got for my husband fits perfectly. The extra flap isn't as necessary on his 2014 Cherokee as the location of the bar is much closer to the back seat in comparison to my 2012 Grand Cherokee. Nice that they have that as it ensures full coverage. Totally can be allowed to hang down unattached (you wont notice it), or go ahead and attach it to back of rear head rests. All good. Looks good, he's pleased. I am pleased.

title: value kit for car use, or in home use. Love it for windshield. Add to a car themed gift bag
text:

If I were doing up a car care themed gift bag/basket/box, I wouldn't hesitate to add this in. Add in some cleaners, air fresheners, other car related goodies, maybe put it all in a [[ASIN:B098CY6G6D trunk organizer box]]. bam, got a cool gift for anyone who loves taking care of their vehicles.

title: 3.5 stars. "velvet musk"- pleasant pretty aroma. Durable container, best in small spaces
text:
I ordered "new car" scent and received "velvet musk". I was concerned that I would not be able to use this as most musk scents trigger a headache. This isn't what makes me think of as musk. It does have a perfume or body wash vibe going. The scent is something that I describe as slightly floral, slightly fruity aroma that sits on a base of soft jasmine. Anyway, no headaches and I find it pleasant. Pretty.

Just like in the pictures, the clear glass container is durable with silver lettering all over. Not sure what the lettering is for, or why. Shimmer gel can be seen. Lid is metallic color, I think made of a thick plastic. It's sturdy. The overall look is fair. I like the clean look, the shimmer. But what is up with the letters?

It is confusing, but the product description makes it sound like there should be a double sided tape included. There isn't one. I even thought that maybe the "aluminum foil insulation layer" could be peeled to expose a sticky side, but no. There is no way to anchor this. So be mindful if planning to use this in car. BUT, if it does tip over, it isn't likely to spill out. The gel isn't doesnt run.

EDIT/REVISION to the above: FOUND THE STICKY TAB. It was just laying on my counter. Not sure how it didn't manage to get tossed out, but it was just sitting there.

EDIT #2 8 months later and it is still viable. It is close to being out, but it has maintained a nice aroma in my car for a very long time. I came back to buy another, but now I am note sure if it will be the same as I have, which is what I want. Keeping it at 4 stars. Solid 4 stars. But just wanted to say this really has lasted.

3.5 stars. Overall I am going with 4 stars. It smells good to me, looks good despite random letters, I am impressed that the container is so thick and durable. Better for small spaces (such as car, closet, closed small bathroom) as it doesn't fill the room.

title: I use this style all the time. I have one brand that I like a little more. These are good!
text:
Excellent hanging garbage bags.

I have experience with this style bag, and I only down rate as they are thinner than my other brand that I buy on repeat. I can tug on it and can make it rip just below where it is hanging via the sticky side. I dont think it would just tear with basic, light garbage. These will be totally fine for light stuff, and in a spot that doesnt get tugged on. I think they are fine, overall. I have been testing it for tossing out tissues and such.

I currently have one hanging in my laundry room for when I clean out the lint trap. I have it stuck to the wall above the dryer, and it is so nice to not need a regular garbage can in that area.

They dont leak liquid. They definitely dont leave any residue behind when taking off whatever it was attached to. I love these style bags, and despite their goofy graphics I find a lot of value in them.

These are little different than my usual bags, but they seem just as effective (just thinner, and easier to rip--but I think are overall fine). I have been using this style (not this brand) for about a year. I buy them often for use at my bed side. I could keep a regular small trash can, but I dont have much room. I just needed something to collect tissues. I tried this style of bag attached to my side table on edge that is directly next to the bed. It worked out so well that I buy a pack any time I see them on sale. The bags tend to hold an impressive amount. And yes, definitely works as a car garbage bag. If you haven't tried these, give them a whirl. They'll change your life. haha

This set by "lukmasic" functions as expected. The tape is strong, the bags hold a lot. While I will likely use these primarily for my bedside, they are just perfect for anywhere that you need to collect some garbage. The tape holds well enough to be able to stuff a lot in the bag.

Can even be used for holding crafts, or as organizer pockets for lighter weight stuff. Maybe keep a few on hand when traveling to help store/organize stuff in a hotel bathroom, etc. Versatile, anyway.

title: comes with two scent tabs, very pleasant smelling
text:
So cute. These scull vent clips come with scent pads. Usually the vent clips I order either do not come with felt or scent pads, or they come with plain felt rounds (for adding own scent). This is the first time that I have come across a scent tablet. I use decorative vent clips in my car AND on my window air conditioner unit. That is where I tried these. I set them in place then turned the AC on. Within seconds my room was filling with a pleasant scent. Floral? Fruity? not sure, but I like it. Even when AC was off I could still smell the area nearby was scented.

Eveything about this is a win. Love the look of the skulls. The detail is nice, and the color is robust. Easy to put together, and the scent tablets smell nice. Make sure to have air flow for strongest fragrance. And if you dont like the tablets, just use your own felt (or cotton ball, etc) and douse with you scent of choice (essential oil, home fragrance oil, perfume).

title: easy to use, works quickly, great for repelling water, smudges,. Makes cleaning bug guts off easier
text:
It is really quite easy to use. I like it better than waxes, other polishes. Start with a clean exterior, then just do small portions at a time. It works in very quickly, so unlike some product applications this is not an all day affair. I recommend a few coats to get the best hydrophobic effect. Also helps repel finger print marks, and makes taking bug guts off easier, or sap, etc. I have used hydrophobic ceramic products formulated for use inside my house with success (love it on stainless steel), so I was real keen on trying out a product made for a car. I had recently bought a new (well, 9 years old, but perfect condition and new to me) Jeep Grand Cherokee with Dark Wild Cherry pearlized paint color, so I am looking for all ways to keep her looking good.

Bottle comes with internal safety seal, and a separate sprayer.

about $20 at time of review, and I find that to be a reasonable price for an easy, effective product.

title: detailed, sturdy vent clip decorations. Has pocket for your own scent & pad (not included)
text:
Adorable decorative vent clips. The skeletons are detailed and fun to look at. Large heads, small bodies, and when together in the trio demonstrate "see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil".

Easy to assemble. Has spacing/pocket to slip a fragrance pad in-- NOT INCLUDED. I know it says as such in the description, but it would be nice to have a pack of felt pads included. Pennies on the dollar and would add value to would be customers, especially for those giving as a gift.

That being said, any of the reviews that say that the scent doesnt last long or that the scent leaks-- know that that cant possibly have anything to do with this product. To make it an air freshener, one must use a fragrance pad (plain felt may work in a pinch). And you must add your own fragrance. Essential Oils are nice, but are quick to evaporate. Synthetic fragrance oils are strongest and usually are in a base of oil (where as essential oils aren't actually oils per say). And of course depends on your vent system- whether you have your air on, how much air flow is hitting the pad, etc. If anything, the pocket on these could use more of a grate on one wall of the rear pocket, but since the sides allow for air flow, the scent should still come through.

So basically buy these primarily for decoration. The ability to hold a scent pad is a bonus.

title: super functional minimalist design perfectly holds small stuff, inc clear mirror
text:
Perfect for my needs.

I'm never in my back seat, so I have no use for a mirror back there, but I like how it has one incorporated into the bottom of this sturdy silicone flip up collapsible container. And it is a legit clear mirror. What I did buy this for is to hold some basic small stuff that I can easily grab for. I looked through so many options on Amazon, and nothing was standing out. I looked at the kind that typically include a garbage pocket and an assortment of other pockets--but they are all much bigger than I need or want (at this time). I really thought about what I want to contain: basically, I want a spot for hand sanitizer, lip balm, pack of tissues, hair clip, hand cream. Maybe other small do-dads that I dont want in a cup holder, door pocket, glove compartment, etc. I just wanted a little bin, but not too big. So pleased to have stumbled upon this because it was like it was made for me.

Deep when fully opened, shallow but still useable for some storage when collapsed. Just flip up to use the mirror.

The attachment is beyond easy. It's a tension bar that slips between the head rest posts. Boom, done. Stays securely in place, holds all my goodies. If I regularly had people in my back seat, I would definitely buy another for the drivers side-- these are great for those in the back that want a spot to store their phone, a drink cup, etc.

It is just so functional and takes up nearly no space. Really simple, but so very useful. SO GLAD to have it. I think it is of good quality, and so far I am very pleased with it. Can probably be paired with a storage bag that uses the head rest too.

title: impressive set of lights, look great day or night, withstood a mega storm, so pretty!
text:
So pretty! The product pictures dont do this justice. Even nicer looking in person. Looks great day and night. The fabric flowers looks nice. The rose stems are flexible, have little thorns, and the flowers produce a pretty glow at night. Adds a cheerful pop of color during the day. Really nice set!

There are two lights, each with a bundle of roses. Tall! From top of flowers to bottom of spike, they stand about 28". Just peel off the film from the light box, and make sure the switch is in the on position. Then set it up where it will get some light, and enjoy the look day and night.

These are robust, too. They weathered a wicked storm recently. Here in my neck of the woods of NY, we had a long thunder-lightning-hail storm with strong winds and significant flooding. It was crazy. These still stood up and worked. My little troopers!

I very well may buy more now that I know how well these look and work. I dont really do real flowers because I am not good at keeping them alive. But I do like a little color and fun in my yard. I have various decorative solar powered lights, but they dont create as much of a pop of color that these red roses do, which is why I got them. I was looking for something that I could enjoy even during the day. Wish I thought of this way sooner. These would be nice mixed in with real plants and flowers, in ground or in flower boxes and planters. Now I want to buy them as gifts, lol

Anyway.. I am very pleased so far, and will certainly update if I experience anything else worth sharing.

title: Impressive!! Inflates QUICKLY, auto stops at programmed PSI, no instructions though
text:
I'm giving it 5 stars because the air compressor is VERY GOOD, probably the best I have used, and I have owned several. It is small, lightweight- fairly typical. The difference is that the max air pressure can be set, and once you turn it on, it will QUICKLY inflate the tire, and will automatically turn off once it reaches the set psi level. A digital read out allows me to see how much air my tires need, and I can monitor as it fills. Has built in light, long hose, and long cord. I could easily reach my tires on my big dodge durango.

Funny, stupid thing--all user error--, but works well as an example of another feature this has. I didnt even really look this over before I popped it out from box and tried using it. When I first attached this to my tire, it would not turn on. I could turn the light on, but I could not get the compressor to turn on. No other indication that this thing works. I thought this was a dud, when I decided to try another tire, and once I saw that there is a readout I missed it (I was in direct sun, so maybe didnt see it, or wasnt paying attention), I could see that it said 25 psi (which clearly indicates that tire needs air-- I use at least 32 psi). I flipped the switch and it turned on. Bounced around a little, made typical noise, but it filled my tired SO quickly. barely any wait time. Then it just shut off. I looked at read out, and it told me that the tire now had 32 psi. I had set it to that, and it actually turned off once it reached that number. I felt silly for not immediately figuring this out, I just assumed that tire was low and this didnt work. DUH, so I went over to the original tire I tried, put this on, and the read out said 34 psi. It didnt need air, so that is why it didnt turn on. Then I proceeded with the other tires, which were a little low, and I quickly topped them off--and as with other tire, the compressor turned off once it reached 32 psi. LOVE IT.

I LOVE THE AUTO OFF FEATURE, and how dang QUICK it fills the tires. SO QUICKLY! If you have had compressors that take 5, 10, 30 minutes to get the air into the tire.. you will be so impressed by this. It was as good as going to an air filling station.

Has other goodies that come with it that are stored in the pink canvas zip bag. NO directions. So if you are unfamiliar with these items or tire repair, then jot down some notes. I want to down rate for that, but my main reason for getting this was for the air compressor, and it is so good that I am fine with giving full 5 star rating.

title: Consider these for use as fancy free budget friendly napkins
text:
The blue shop rags I am reviewing I happen to use primarily as napkins.

I don't need nor care for anything fancy. I actually despise linen napkins as they are not at all absorbent. On top of that, I have had some that just stain up immediately, so they look like junk anyway that I spent too much money on. These are cheap, and do what I need. Wipe my face and hands! These aren't for company. I am not stuffing them in napkin holders. I didn't need anything huge. I am just wiping my face and hands. Yet I don't want to keep on using up paper napkins or paper towels. Not interested in basic body wash cloths either. I wanted something that stands out from all the other materials coming out of the washer and dryer. Sometimes I use these to wipe up the counter real quick if I hadn't really used these during dinner (--- on the couch! see, nothing fancy here!). So yeh, I basically keep a pile of them folded up in a small box kept on top of my fridge. I grab one as I need it.

One star off for the insane amount of washing I had to do to them before the ink bled out enough for them to be safe with other materials in the wash. I wouldn't even use them in or on my truck as they bled with any fluid on them from the get go. They go from a really cool vibrant blue to eventually a worn out, washed out denim blue. At that point it seemed they were done bleeding out color. Significant shape and size loss- but I don't hold it against them, they are after all cotton shop rags. But the description says they are 14"x14" to start with expected minimal shrinkage. I would say they reduce to maybe 10x10, super thin, with curling. Large enough to wipe my face, not so much to wipe down my truck.

Alas, they really are working out well for my primary use as napkins. I like the size (even with shrinkage), would have been cool if they kept their color, but really I don't care. I am just glad they are absorbent and have enough texture to engage in some light scrubbing action as needed.

title: Hands down, this is the best window shade design I've ever seen...
text:
MARCH 26 UPDATE:
-----------------------
Unfortunately after less than 2 weeks, the adhesion has worn off. The base no longer sticks to the door, making it useless. I still consider it the best sun shade idea I've used. It just needs some real 3M, not cheap knock offs. Or better yet, I think I'll adhere it using Sugru, that would be even better than 3M. I will have to knock 2 stars for this.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
----------------------
THE GOOD:
--------------
* The best driver or passenger side window shade solution I've ever seen.
* Two functioning options: 1. You can have the shade follow the window up and down by clipping it to the top of the window glass. 2. You can have it opened at all times by clipping it to a stationary hook that is adhered to the the window frame.
* The main bracket that houses the shade is installed on your door by strong double sided adhesive.

THE BAD:
------------
* Not really a bad, just an installation tip. We did not use the stationary hook. We rather the shade follow the glass up and down. But here is my advice if you wish to use the stationary hook/clip. It is also installed by double sided adhesive, and we made the mistake of sticking it to a rubbery trim. So when we opened the shade and hooked it, the force of the tension pulling down the shade actually pulled down the trim. LOL! So be sure you pick the solid plastic or metal part of the window frame to stick the stationary hook. I always use my air conditioner and rarely have my windows down, so we didn't bother trying to install it again.

Much better than the suction cup, or the retractable designs. Once you use this, you'll understand why it's $40. It's worth it.

This is 5-Stars!

title: Not just for motorbikes, you can make this the most versatile support stand in woodworking...
text:
[[VIDEOID:a2de149fa8e279b971ba28926cded68a]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* Heavy duty jack, high quality components.
* Hydraulic bottle jack work very smooth and quiet.
* Safety bar included.
* Nice caster wheels, 2 with brakes. If you ever need replace the wheels, the four screw locations on the caster wheel plates are universal with many 3 inch wheels on the market.
* Terrific customer service... good thing because I needed it.
* I'm not using this as a motorcycle jack. I got this to support long boards when woodworking. There are so many specialty stands in woodworking. You have the roller stands to support Miter saws, you got saw horses to support work benches, etc. And they all have limitations with their height adjustments. I have 3 main cutting tools in my garage: My miter saw, my router table, and my track saw workbench. All three are not level at the same height. Because of the infinite height adjustments of this hydraulic lift, I can roll it around to support all three tools.

THE BAD:
------------
* Manual is lacking and assumes buyer knows all about hydraulic lifts.
* You need to install the pedal yourself, it is not done at the factory. It can be a bit difficult.
* I'm more into tech and woodworking, and never paid much attention to the science of hydraulics in my life, so certain common sense things probably escaped me. Watch my video to learn from my mistakes. If your jack isn't lifting, watch my video.

I think this would be 5-Stars and a lot of headache would have been avoided if they installed the pedal at the factory. I will subtract 1 star. 4-Stars overall.

title: Use a wrench or pliers to remove "quick" connect...
text:
I think they should ship this product with the quick connector uninstalled in a separate bag. Because to use it, you need quick connector fittings, and people who are buying this most likely do not have quick connector fittings. People who tend to have quick connector fittings are people who own pressure washers. People who own pressure washers will buy foam cannons made for pressure washers, not made for garden hoses.

How to remove the brass quick connector....
---------------------------------------------------
There are flat indentations on the brass connector, so all you have to do is use a wrench or pliers with good jaws. I hold the gun with my left hand, and use a vise grip plier with my right and went counter clockwise. It was easy peasy.

Quality...
-----------
Entire unit is plastic, and the funny thing is, the only high quality part is the brass quick connector, which most people will need to remove.

Performance...
-------------------
Depending on your water pressure, I think it's okay. You may need to get closer to your car than you would like. But I think these are as good as it gets. To get next level performance, you need a pressure washer and foam cannons made for pressure washers.

title: Terrible Helmet - Poor Quality - Bad Sizing
text:
I am really not sure where all the good reviews for this helmet come from. For starters, this was much lighter than I anticipated, which told me a lot about the quality before I even opened the box. Once opened, the first thing I noticed was the cheap feel and hollow sound that it made, more similar to a bicycle helmet than a motorcycle helmet. Before inspecting the interior of the helmet, I attempted to fit it and it was much too small for an XXL. I have other XXL helmets that fit great and this feels like a large or XL at most.

I wear glasses and you can almost forget wearing any if you can manage to get your head inside. I had to put my glasses on after the helmet was in place and with considerable discomfort and difficulty.

The feeling of the helmet when putting it on your head, is one of abrasiveness and feels more like a bicycle helmet. You can tell right away that there is little to no soft protection/padding when putting the helmet on.

After making the above findings, I inspected the interior of the helmet. The outermost "padding" is maybe 1/4 of an inch thick or closer to a blanket in thickness. The padding near the ear is thickest at about 1 inch and is ONLY around the ear and lower rim of the back of the neck. The only padding you are afforded on the rest of your head is about blanket thickness or approximately 1/4 of an inch at best.. The hard foam (feels like Styrofoam) under the liner is all you can feel and fits exactly like a bicycle helmet. It is extremely uncomfortable and will surely irritate the skin and skull after a short time of riding.

All you can feel is the back of the helmet around the base of the neck putting pressure on you in that area and around the ears, since those are the only locations with thick normal padding. The entire rest of the helmet provides zero comfort and padding and is a hard, abrasive experience.

Do avoid this helmet, I believe it is unsafe and certainly not worth the money.

title: I'm Never Cleaning the Tub Without Drillbrush AGAIN!
text:
Do you hate scrubbing your tub? Me too! It's not something that I dread so badly anymore. We use bar soap at my house, so we are getting some soap scum no matter what. This is the best brush I've ever used, by a long shot! This is an ideal set for bathrooms. This one has a rounded brush, called the original, a 2" longer bristle with a flat head, a 4" flat brush and a special edge brush that is good for grouted joints. I don't have tiles, but I used it around the tub knobs and faucet. I didn't need any of my old brushes at all. These are great tools to use for any bathroom, but the use isn't limited there. If you like this, consider getting a set in a different color for different areas. I'm ordering a blue set soon that will be for food surfaces in my kitchen.

These are brushes you use with your own drill or impact driver. I just used a simple off-brand 18V cordless drill. You can probably use a corded one, but the idea of something plugged into the wall, water and my bathtub just sounded like a bad idea to me. Usually, I have to use a handled stiff bristle brush, scrubber sponge, magic sponge and a detail brush...... and spend no less than 30 minutes scrubbing! Ugh! That is just the tub, not the shower surround or the sink.... or the corners of the floor that trap towel dust. It took me less than 20 minutes of scrubbing and rinsing to have the bathroom clean... and I mean sparkling clean! I had enough time and energy left over to get back to my computer and write this review.

There are some other factors to consider, you will want to put on some safety goggles or glasses. If you get much splatter, go at a lower speed. I found out the hard way. Reverse the spin so the bristles aren't too bent one way after some time of use. The brushes are great, but are not magic, you still need to use a cleanser product. The right one for the surface will make a huge difference. Just water alone isn't as good. I rinsed each brush in a bucket of clean water when I was done, just dunking the surface inside the water and letting it spin in each direction. Very easy!

This is a brush set I would highly recommend. My teen son even took some interest and didn't complain at all about cleaning. I'll buy him a set when he gets his first home. I'm ordering a set very soon to gift to my brother for Christmas, he hates cleaning too, but likes his power tools so I'm sure he will get some good use from it.

title: Well built and works in a pinch
text:
Until the US decides on a single standard for EV plugs, power adapters will be a part of our lives. This ShockFlo J1772 EVs Adapter is a product that will allow a non-tesla EV plug into a Tesla destination charger. Note that I said "destination charger". This means that this adapter is only made for level 2 charging (220v AC) and not DC super charging.

Many hotels have EV chargers on site for their customers and many of them have Tesla plugs. Others have both J1772 plugs as well as Tesla plugs. By having this adapter, you open up your option to use any open plugs that are available. With the popularity of electric cars on the rise, any available options while travelling is essential.

This Shocflo adapter is well-built. It is quite hefty in the hand and have locking mechanism on both the J1772 output as well as the Tesla input. It started a charging session on my ev with no issues and worked as expected.

title: Needs improvement.
text:
The Schumacher SEV1600P1450 is their first attempt at a level 2 EV charger. Schumacher is known for their charging systems for automobiles and motorcycles so in terms of electrical devices, they are a trustworthy brand.

The SEV1600P1450 is a wall-mounted level 2 charger that charge up to 40A. Included in the box is a long (25Ft) charging cable with a J1772 charging gun, a short (I mean short) power cable terminating with a NEMA 14-50 plug, and the wall unit. The cables are beefy and well insulated while the wall unit has a modern look and is WIFI enabled.

When planning for the install of this charger, be aware of how short the plug wire is. NEMA 14-50 sockets really should be mounted with the ground facing up as I've read in some forums. With such a short cable and the power connection coming out of the bottom of the unit, you're probably going to have to mount your socked with ground down.

In terms of sockets, I suggest that you make sure that you install a commercial grade socket. With an EV pulling the full 40A over a long period of time, you need something that won't melt under such loads.
These sockets cost around $100 - $140. To save myself some money and the headache of dealing with such a short cable, I opted to wire the wall unit directly to my circuit breaker.

Once installed, I had some problems with my jumper settings. I read the switch diagram in the manual completely backwards because I assumed that white represented the switch position and the black was empty space. It's actually the other way around. The black is the switch position and white is supposed to be the empty space. Can't blame me for that one because the dip switches themselves are white. Anyway, after I got in touch with Schumacher support and they had me take pictures of my setup, they helped me figure out my problem.

Since then, this charger has worked well for charging my ID.4.

The only other grip I have about this charger is that their app is pretty much useless. It sends an update to the app when something changes, such as the car being plugged in, but it takes 10 minutes for the next update. What ends up happening is that the app is updated to "Charging" state in the app but the actual charging amperage hasn't actually been negotiated yet. The app will display charging at 0 amps. It will take another 10 minutes to get the actual charging amperage in the app.

In addition, this charger doesn't have the ability to schedule a charging times. If you're on a time-of-use plan with your electric company, you would want to charge only during off-peak hours. Usually scheduling the charge should be taken care of by the car, but since ID.4 still hasn't gotten any good updates since its launch, I was hoping I could solve my problem with the charger.

In conclusion, at the price that Schumacher is charging for this device, they have some improvements to make before they can compete with Grizzl-e chargers.

Turns out there is. The Vpment 12V 7Ah LiFePO4 Battery with BMS is a deep-cycle battery that has the same battery chemistry as the Standard Range Tesla Model 3. That just screams modern! This LiFePO4 battery is lighter than its lead-acid counterpart and in general, lithium batteries have much higher power density as well. With this battery, there is also no danger of leaking liquids in case the seal fails.

The battery was easy to install and it fit perfectly. I've had my UPS system back up for about a month now and it has been working beautifully.

title: Saved me over $400
text:
I don't have occasion to drive my Mini cooper very often anymore since I bought an electric car. With gas prices being pretty high, I try to put as many miles on the electric as I can. Overall, by driving more electric miles, I've reduced my gas miles significantly.

With that said, the few trips that I do make on the Mini are short, five-minute trips such as dropping the kids off or driving to the grocery when the wife has the electric car. These short trips do a number on the lead-acid battery and my Mini started to complain about low battery voltage. I called around to the dealer as well as some independent shops and to change the battery out, it would have cost me over $400. One of the mechanics was nice enough to suggest that I try a charger to see if I can save my battery.

I picked up the HTRC 35-Amp Smart Charger, Car Battery Charger in hopes that it can trickle charge the lead-acid battery back to full health. It did. This charger has a bright lcd display that shows the current charge of the battery as well as information regarding how many amps it's pumping in. It operates it operates in 3 different voltages and supports Lead-Acid, Lithium, and even the newer LiFePO4 batteries.

I really didn't know what to expect here. I first plugged the power cable into the device but not the battery connectors yet. I turned on the device and made sure to set the mode to what I thought was correct: Lead-acid at 12v and 10 amps. I then turned the device off again and clipped the battery. The mini cooper's battery only exposes a positive terminal, but if you look about a foot to the right of the battery, you will find the negative terminal (it's a metal cylindrical shape that just kinda sticks out) on the frame.

Once connected, I turned on the device and waited. The screen showed that the charging started and the output amperage slowly began to rise. Not knowing how long it should take, I took the charger off after 4 hours even though it still showed that the battery was only 80% charged. Well, the car stopped complaining about low voltage so I knew that it worked. The next time that the car complained about the battery, I left the charger for about 8 hours during the day. When I came back, the charger showed that charging had completed.

This is a great product. It gives me a lot of confidence that I won't be left with a dead battery leaving the car in the garage for weeks at a time.

The second option was this WILDGREEN Foam Blaster. There are many advantages to using this over a hose. It uses less water, I can use this anywhere (outside if it is warm out, indoors in the winter), and I can mix the solution with warm water for the dog's comfort.

So my results were great! Using a little bit of the shampoo mixed with warm water, I can easily make enough solution for each wash. The hand pump is easy to use, but as other review would point out, the pressure doesn't last very long so you will probably have to pump a few times during a washing session. title: Compact and powerful tire pump to keep in the car
text:
When the low tire pressure warning light comes on, I always had to make a decision of whether I wanted to drag out my big air compressor or to stop by a gas station to fill up the tires. What ends up happening is that I put it off for days because it both are things that I need to go out of my way to do.

With the Fucare Air Compressor Portable Mini Tire Inflator, there is no hassle. It is a powerful little inflator that can top off a car tire in just a couple of minutes. There is no rubber tube to drag around the car, there is no need to wait for a compressor to come up to pressure (making you deaf by the time it does). Simply attach the tube to the device, attach the device to the tire and press M to start.

Some of the features of this device:
-- battery powered, rechargeable by USB
-- Auto shutoff by preset. No worries about overinflating.
-- various attachments to pump car tire, balls, and inflatable mattresses/boats.

I really like the convenience of this pump. It is compact, easy to use, and fairly quiet compared to a large compressor. I only have a couple of gripes. The pump has various modes for bicycle, car, motorcycle, etc. and will have various presets depending on the mode. The unit of measure changes depending on the mode. So for a bicycle, the unit of measure is PSI, which I'm used to, but when changed to motorcycle or car mode, the unit of measure changes to bar. I think it would have been better to simply allow one to set unit of measure according to ones preference as thermometers do. I end up keeping the device on bicycle mode, but I suppose I should train myself to learn the car tire pressure in bars instead. In addition, this pump comes with a fairly cheap felt bag to store the device. I would have liked a more significant case or bag...

In use, these keep the bed from sagging as much under load. They do “bounce” a bit on speed bumps and such, but nothing too bad. I haven’t taken them on any gnarly rocky off road trails yet, but they don’t seem to make a difference in the milder stuff so far (which is a good thing).

Anyway, so far the Timbrens are a nice affordable suspension upgrade for the occasional heavy load or towing session.

title: Wow - Excellent Car Top Carrier - Great Capacity - Super Durable
text:
We recently completed a 800 mile move and had to figure out ways to carry as much as we possibly could in our vehicles. This meant looking at ways to pack that were outside of our norm - in fact, out of the car.

This worked PERFECTLY.

We first placed the anti slip mat atop our sedan which does not have a top rack. Using the initial 4 door hooks we strapped the rooftop carrier to the car and then loaded it full starting from the front working back. The front can be identified because there is no zipper on that side. Once we had the carrier fully packed, we zipped it closed and secured the final 4 straps - a total of 8 reinforced straps hold this to the car!

We could not believe the storage capacity of this cargo carrier. We were able to securely pack so much of our important belongings that otherwise we would have had to somehow stuff into our car or hold our breath as it left with the movers.

This rooftop cargo carrier remained strapped tightly all the way with absolutely no issues. We traveled through torrential rain but when we arrived our belongings remained completely dry.

This is an outstanding product that you will be thankful for whether you are headed off on vacation, moving like us, or simply need to expand your cargo capacity.

title: Mediocre Ceramic Coat - Much Better as Touch Up Cleaner
text:

Your results will be guaranteed to be poor.

After thoroughly testing this product I have found it is really best as a cleaning / touch up type product rather than a primary ceramic coat.

After working with multiple brands of this type of product there are variations to ingredients that make ceramic coats more effective than others. This particular product seems to not use alcohol as it’s primary carrier ingredient which leads to more residue that does not evaporate. Everything other than the actual ceramic nano particles must be buffed away.

title: High Quality, Easy to Use Leather Cleaner
text:
I developed a process of sculpting leather in 1997 and spent the following several years perfecting the process. This began my love affair with leather. People are always amazed at what I’m able to create using this incredible medium. Over the last 23 years I’ve learned a lot about different leathers, their individual properties, how to manipulate it and the critically important aspect of caring for it.

While I have been approached a few times by leather care product manufacturers to promote their individual products I have always stayed away from endorsing any single line of products. Frankly, there are many that I’ve used and like, while only a few product lines I strongly recommend my collectors not use.

I decided to test and review this line of leather products by Aged Leather Pros so I could provide a knowledgeable review explaining the products and what I thought about them.

The primary reason leather degrades over time is because it dries out. All natural leathers must retain a certain moisture level in order to remain pliable and not become brittle and thus crack. If properly cared for, leather will last many, many times as long as uncared for leather.

Leather dries out due to a variety of factors, one of which is when sweat or liquids are absorbed into the leather’s pores and then evaporate. This removes some of the leathers natural moisture. Overtime this process dries the leather out more and more.

The best way to combat this is to first use a quality dressing or conditioner when the item is new and then keep the item clean by regularly wiping it free of any contaminates.

This all natural cleaning solution by Aged Leather Pros does an excellent job at cleaning contaminates from leather without leaving any residue behind.

When using this type of product I spray it onto the leather then wipe with a fabric that will not absorb the cleaner immediately such as a synthetic fabric cloth. This allows the cleaner to more fully work into the leather rather than being absorbed into the cloth. After I have completely wiped down one section with the cleaner I go back over it with a soft cloth to remove any remaining product or debris.

This is a product I can safely recommend. By using this cleaner regularly you will have leather goods that not only last but look great.

We recently purchased a new set of leather living room furniture. Within the first week of owning it I took the time to completely cover both recliners and a full size double reclining sofa with 2 coats of this product.

I apply leather conditioners using a very dense sponge, using minimal product on the sponge - I apply by doing small overlapping circles over every surface. If you do this treatment when your leather is new and repeat it yearly you will be absolutely amazed at the difference in the longevity of your leather products.

title: The light looks cool, is very bright & the housing is sturdy aluminum, lens seems to scratch easily
text:
[[VIDEOID:1f41778af0635f6997379776c215d44d]] The whole body of the lamp is aluminum so it is noticeably heavier than the hollow, plastic light. It looks & feels much more sturdy, especially the bottom adjustment tab which was broken on my light. The light looks very cool & fits the bike perfectly. I have it wired on the high beam & it is very bright but could stand to be adjusted. My TE25i just has an off/off switch for the light & runs the running light plus one beam on the main light. I wired this kit to run the running light & the high beam. In the future I'm going to get a high/low switch & the DRL to run all the time & I will change the positions of the pins in the headlight to eliminate the need for the adapter.
update: I went back & re-wired the light to run the DRL all the time when the engine is running & put the low beam on the switch. I have put almost 4 hours on the bike with it since & it looks great & the low beam is very useful in the woods & on the road in the dark. I still want to get a high-low switch eventually.
The instructions have very nice photographs depicting the removal & replacement of the light mask but are scant on the actual installation of the bulb. The kit comes with all the hardware I needed to mount the lamp but I was a little confused on what to use to mount the lower tab. The original light just used a coarse thread screw directly installed into the plastic mask but I ended up using a supplied, stainless steel cap-head screw & nut.
The kit came with a wiring adapter/extension kit that I thought I didn't need since the light plugged right into my harness. It turned out that I was mistaken & did end up using the kit to change up some of the wire positions. It probably took me 2x as long to figure out how to re-wire the adapter than to install the light.
The light does not show a DOT approval on the lens. This is not a concern where I live but it could be a concern in areas with strict inspection if they exist. I rode the bike in the woods today & did very little bushwhacking & noticed that the lens already has some light scratches.

title: Great protection & features for riding, zippered side is a plus. My size 12s came up a little short.
text:
I like these boots a lot, they have great protection but I ordered & received a size 12 & they came up a little short. Aside from being tight in the length the soles are comfortable enough to walk in & wear for a while. The zippered ankle gives surprisingly good support at the ankle without going up too high on the leg. Since I got the laces tightened I have been able to remove & pull on the shoes just by un-zippering the side zipper.
The soles are wide like a work boot, the toe box is roomy & the material over the toe box is very stiff. I haven't ridden with them much yet but the shifter toe shows almost no wear or discoloration from the shift lever unlike all of my other shoes. The bottom of the sole is completely flat with no heel to force a certain position on the foot peg. The back part of the sole is easily stiff enough for me to kick start my dirt bikes.
Shoes without ankle coverage will come off in a crash but I am guilty of often riding with sneakers or loafers. These will not come off plus they have a lot of stiff & thick protective covering.

title: Good selection of gasket material
text:
[[VIDEOID:7040c74bdc1d046de92273562faaafcd]] The gaskets are about 10"x8.5", each one is slightly different for some reason. The gaskets in the set are 1/8" & 1/16" in Rubber infused cork, 3/64" rubber cellulose (blue), & 1/32" rubber fiber. The rubber cellulose (blue) is rated for water & coolant, the others are rated for water, gasoline & oil. There is a handy spec sheet included in the pack which has this information & more that would have been very helpful in the actual Amazon description.
I have several gaskets to make for a motorcycle engine so I ordered this multi-pack of gasket material not knowing exactly what thickness & materials I would need. I have only used the 3/64" rubber cellulose so far to make a water pump gasket. I haven't tested it with water under pressure yet but I think it made a nice gasket.
The blue rubber cellulose was hard to cut by breaking it over a sharp edge. It cuts pretty well with a sharp razor blade but it also dulls the blades pretty quickly.

title: 1/64" thick, comes in a roll, Cuts easily with scissors, razor & other methods
text: [[VIDEOID:4b8015f67e8369957beac4833a41d6dd]] I'm using this to re-create the flywheel cover gasket on a motorcycle so it doesn't have to hold any fluids back. The material is about 1/64" thick & comes in a roll. The material is easy to cut with a razor or with scissors. The material is thin & tough so it didn't cut as easily by trying to break it over sharp edges as thicker & cork style gasket material. I'm pretty happy with the results. IF I have to make another one for this part I will pay more attention to the original gasket & make the area around the mounting bolts larger.

title: Will jump a totally dead battery, longer cables & a bigger battery than smaller jump packs
text:
This jump starter has a huge battery, long cables & a low battery mode which makes it great for troubleshooting in the shop. The low battery mode allows it to jump a vehicle that has been sitting a long time. Most of the lithium-ion jump starters require a minimum voltage before they will jump but this has a work around. It is perfect for arousing vehicles that have been sitting & for multiple start attempts when troubleshooting a non-running engine.
The jump starter has long, 30" cables which makes it much more convenient than the smaller jump starters for large trucks or cars with batteries in awkward places. The cables are also permanently attached to the battery box so there are no extra buttons or breakers. There are clips on the case that the cables can clamp to to keep the cables tidy. It includes a single 2.4v USB port & an LED flashlight but it's a bigger piece of equipment & they are on the bottom which makes both of them difficult to use.
Schumacher is a trusted brand that has been around for a long time. With this jumper having excellent features I am baffled as to why the cables come directly from the bottom when the handle is on the opposite end. Every time I set it down I worry about the cables & move it to a less convenient position. It does come with an excellent set of English instructions. Engaging the low battery mode is involved enough that I wrote the instructions on the case.

title: Shipped with Acid & a new method of filling, fit my '09 Ducati 1100 Monster with no issues

Enough about the acid, the battery was a perfect fit for my Ducati 1100 & hasn't failed to start it yet. The price was less than anything I could find locally. Yuasa is a trusted brand so I was happy to get it for the price of other brands.

title: Great roadside or trailside tool for tire changing or repairs
text:
This is a nice roadside or trailside tool that can also be used in the shop to raise one tire for service or replacement. The lift works by triangulating between the lift, the kick-stand & the tire on the ground. It takes a little creativity with the placement to lift the front wheel but the rear can just go on the swingarm on the side opposite the swingarm.
This lift is about 10" high with the screw extender fully collapsed & lifts about 2.25". The screw extender raises the lift about 3" so maximum lift is around 15.25". The lifting lever is linear & easy to use. The lift isn't bearing the weight of the entire bike but pivoting it off of the other 2 points. The plastic base is sturdy & adjusts to about 45 degrees. There is a bit of padding in the crotch of the lifting surface & hooks built into the raised parts to help grasp the bike & raise the lifting point a little.
The lift stores at 15.5" & has a velvety, draw string bag. It's too bulky to carry on my dual sport motorcycle trips but might not make a difference on a touring rig. I'll probably keep it with my trailer because it would also be useful for changing trailer tires.

title: Great, basic reader for diagnostics & repairs or just to turn off the engine light
text:
I'm glad I lost my old code reader because this one has a lot more features & cost way less than my 10 year old reader. A code reader is a must for someone even doing the most basic diagnostics & repairs. This reader is a major improvement over my old one because it shows fault code numbers AND the standard OSBII code descriptions. It has a feature to look up the manufacturer's specific code descriptions but it didn't have all of them for the 2 cars I used it on.
The live data is very cool & also something my old reader didn't have. I can look at a bit of data while the car is running & driving. I had to google some of them to see what they are, what they mean & if I was seeing a problem. This will probably inspire me to buy a more advanced reader in the future.
The instructions are adequate for plugging the reader in & scrolling through the menu but don't tell how to interpret the data. It could use a longer cord. I could read the live data from the driver's seat but it would be useful if it could be read from the passenger seat. I tried several times to switch the measurements from metric to English but it still displays all temperatures in Celsius.

title: Perfect tool for the car or a great power supply & compressor for around the house
text:
Adding a battery powered compressor to the jump starter makes it a perfect tool to keep in the car.
I'm a big fan of these jump starters & have one in each of our cars. We also use the batteries as power supplies to charge or run electronics during outages or just as a convenience around the house or outside.
The compressor is fast & it has an automatic shutoff at the desired pressure which is especially nice for smaller tires like bicycles.
The compressor is very loud so it's not my first choice for topping off tires at home. The biggest beef I have though is that the jump starter cords are very short. That is common on these starter packs but it's a bigger issue on this one because the battery is much bigger.
I have used this a lot in the past couple of weeks & discovered a few quirks. It has a nice carry handle on top & rubber pads on the bottom but all of the displays & switches are oriented 90 degrees off from how it stands. If the battery is rotated so that the displays are upright then it sits on the light. The light, by the way, is a very useful, broad LED & not a focused spotlight like my other jump starters. The handle on top is also firmly attached & useful.
I love the padded carry case is that holds the battery tight but it's spacious so the accessories don' t have to be organized in a specific way to put it together. It has enough space that I added a couple of USB cables inside the case for charging phones & such. I'm not sure about the USB out ports, one is blue & the other is black but when plugged in to either one the display shows "5v/9v 2.0A" for the accessories I plugged in.

title: The Kit Worked well, the components are strong, assembly is fiddlesome & I didn't get instructions
text:
I'm not ready to do the Harley but I was hoping this would work for another hub that has two, stacked bearings on one side of the hub & I was not disappointed. The blind bearing puller pushes through a bearing & an expandable collet grips from the inside & back side of the inner race. Then the puller cage pulls against the hub to pull the bearing. The press to install the bearings only presses against the outer race.
The kit I received didn't come with any instructions. I searched for videos online, the 1st one was useless & showed incorrect technique but I found another that was perfect. The technique for pulling the bearing is not obvious & the components have to be assembled & tightened in a certain order & held together without hardware until it is all together & tight. I would describe the process as "fiddlesome" & it requires a long 5/8" or 8mm Allen/hex wrench that will pass all the way through the hub.
Pressing the bearings into the hub is more straightforward. The threaded rod gets a thick washer on one end & the other end has a bushing that fits tight into the inner race of the bearing to make sure it pulls straight.
All of the components are heavy steel, sturdy & thick. The threads are coarse so the are easy to start & strong. There was no sign of distress on the threads or components even though I had to put a good deal of persuasion on them to pull the 2 bearing stack. The molded plastic case was definitely designed for the tools & holds them firmly. The case has sliding locks to hold the halves together & not plastic molded hinges that will wear.
I'm very happy with the results but I am taking off a star for no instructions & the stack of hardware required to set up the puller.

title: Tool is good quality & manufactured well. Comes with 15  thread sizes & the inserts are strong
text:
[[VIDEOID:c3c6872720b7697e1bb4e5002d292663]] These inserts are really strong. I was hoping I could use this to re-mount the muffler on my dirt bike's boxed aluminum subframe & I think it's going to work. The tool comes with 7 metric mandrels & 8 fraction mandrels & a lot of nut inserts of each size. The nuts crimp into place & allow for blind mounting a nut in thinner materials that can't be tapped.
The kit comes with a hinged, molded case with built-in handle that holds 12 mandrels tight in the lid so it can be closed without them falling out. The other 3 fit into spaces in the bottom & of course the tool is snug to prevent damage but not tight so it doesn't have to clip in or out. The case also has double hinged locking clips. I like the case a lot.
The mandrels come in individual boxes along with their mandrels & the sizes are molded into the color coded caps. The nuts mostly came in plastic bags with the sizes printed on the bag. I put them in the organizer box, the kit doesn't come with anything to separate the insert nuts once they are removed from the bag.
The tool works smoothly & the parts interchange easily. The components seem good quality with good threads & a light coat of oil. It has a meter to set the depth or tightness of the nut based on the thickness of the material & the length of the nut.
I do not understand the depth selection or gauge at all & the instructions are no help. There is a qr link to a video of the adjustment which is also not helpful. I watched a video of someone adjusting a similar tool but it seems to work differently. I fretted over this adjustment quite a bit but ultimately decided it didn't matter as much as I thought. It seems to work just fine setting it by feel & I believe a bolt will pull it tight if it isn't fully set.

title: Motor & fan are quiet, may have to reverse the motor for exhaust fan
text:
[[VIDEOID:93738220cc995fca606393e5ad38f3c6]] The fan blade is the opposite shape than the exhaust fan in my RV (it "blows" instead of "sucks"). I reversed the wires on the motor to make it run backwards & the fan works fine now. The motor & fan are probably as quiet as mine was years ago & much more quiet than it has been recently.
The motor in my RV restroom exhaust fan had a bushing that went bad & has been making a terrible squeal for a few years. I ordered this fan kit mostly for the replacement motor but I also replaced the fan blade. The motor was a nearly direct replacement Mabuchi 540 style with a long, keyed shaft.
The fan blade just presses on to the motor shaft like the original.
The fan runs off of 12V DC (like a car's electrical system) so it isn't dangerous & doesn't require an electrician's special tools or knowledge. Some experience with DC wiring is necessary to install the motor. This job took me about an hour but I spent way more time disassembling, cleaning & re-assembling the fan housing than installing & wiring the motor.

title: Love this coating doesn't require excessive prep & fills pin holes & thin spots
text:
I love this fuel tank coating but I hate the container. This 8oz container was the perfect size for a 3.25 gallon TRX300 tank but I think it works better when more is used & the excess is drained off. I previously used the 16oz for several smaller tanks & I was able to coat all the way up the filler neck.
I coated a bunch of tanks with a plastic coating about 20 years ago & it is separating now. The POR is easier to use & does a much better job of sealing pin-hole leaks. I have used on I rusty tanks & tanks that were previously coated with plastic after removing the old coating. I use diluted acid, acetone or apple cider vinegar to clean the tanks before coating & the POR sticks to the metal every time.
The can that this stuff comes in is sealed very well but it is hard to open, hard to pour & hard to seal. The instructions say not to re-use the excess but I have had good success with re-using it months after the 1st job. The can is very hard to close though & my old batch went bad.
