title: The handguards are really nice but the mounts are not versatile at all
text:
[[VIDEOID:c3e4dbd4bf0bcdd13f6a255ddd046343]] UPDATE: I'm happier with these than when I first put them on. They are very strong or flexible, I'm not sure which but I have had a few falls with no breaks or even movement. They still stick out too far & I moved them to the flat part of the bar so they would sit flat but stick out further. I tag them on trees a bunch & they look good but are starting to show signs of the abuse.
Another update because I see so many questions about "does it fit a..." that I added a picture of these handguards on my friend's son's 50cc Gas Gas (KTM) race bike. You can see that they fit the bars quite well but they stick out well past the grips. I hope this helps someone.
1st impression: I had to mount these on the down angle of my bars in order to get them to clear the brake reservoir & not stick out too far beyond the bar ends so they point up & look funny. I'm probably not the ideal customer for these but I ride mostly trails & in the East the woods are tight & we run narrow bars. The mounts for the guards are strong but they are bulky so it forces the mounting location inboard. The guards have about an inch of lateral adjustment & I pulled them both in as far as they would go. They still stick out past the bar ends.
The handguards are super nice. They are very flexible & shiny. Two white inserts can be added or removed from each guard to change the amount of air flowing through. I would love these if I could make them level & not point up.

title: Completely different design than the original but worked on '97 Plymouth Neon

title: Very sturdy & strong, needs a longer rod for some engines
text:
The puller is very sturdy & stiff & was able to pull the crankshaft pulley/harmonic balancer that my old universal kit couldn't. The kit comes with 2 rods to insert in the hole in the crank & neither one of them were long enough to pull the pulley from the 4 cylinder Chrysler engine on which I was working. There are other kits with a third, longer rod but they were back ordered. The threaded bolt on the puller has a 30mm internal hole that uses up a lot of the rod.
At first the bolt bottomed out on the crankshaft. I ended up putting a cap head screw in the hole in the threaded shaft of the puller to shorten the length & the pulley pulled straight off.

title: Peace of mind when driving an old camper with a sketchy trailer was priceless
text:
Before I get into the programming I want to express how reassuring it was to have this setup on my last trip. The tires on my motorcycle trailer are not in great shape for a long trip & the monitors allowed me know which one(s) needed attention. More importantly, I was also able to monitor the temperatures of the front tires of my camper which has occasional brake problems & it was so reassuring to know that I wasn't in danger of overheating a front tire. Having this information gave me unparalleled peace of mind during the entire trip & I checked it a lot.

The programming allows you to set 1 pressure range for one axle with 2 tires & another pressure for a 2nd axle with 4 tires. In the situation depicted in the picture on the box, the top axle on the monitor would be the 2 tires on the caravan & the bottom axle would be the 4 tires on the tow vehicle. That may seem confusing t read but it gets more intuitive in practice.

In my case I had a 2 axle trailer with 4 tires & an RV with 6 tires so I set the 4 trailer tires on the rear axle pressure range & the front tires on the front axle range. If I just had this set on my RV with dual rear tires, the setup would be the same as the diagram on the monitor. This made such a difference on the trip that I will probably get another set so I can monitor all 6 RV tires plus trailer tires.

The sensors are fairly large & come with "anti-theft" locking nuts. I wasn't so much worried about theft as I was the sensors flying off on the road. I used the locking nuts on every sensor & none of them loosened on the trip. I was also a bit concerned about the mass of the sensors stressing the old valve stems on my trailer tires due to centrifugal force but I didn't have any failures there either. The sensors have numbers printed on them that correspond with the numbers on the meter.

The monitor sits on the dash & it is smaller than it looks in the pictures which is good. I mostly used it with the USB cord plugged in but it lasted well over 2 hours unplugged running off of battery & solar power without losing any bars on the meter. I didn't think the solar power would work as well on my RV because the unit is so far away from the windshield but either or both the battery or the solar is very strong.

The system comes with a special wrench to tighten the locking nut & also remove the monitor covers to access the battery. I had to keep the wrench handy to top off tires & I would prefer that the kit included a spare, maybe even a smaller wrench to put on a keychain. The system also included a repeater to amplify the signal from the sensors to the receiver. I was prepared to wire the repeater into the back of my RV but I never had any trouble getting a signal from my trailer tires to the front of the RV which is about 40' to the furthest.

There is a learning curve to programming the monitor & understanding the readings. I have not figured out exactly what correlation the rotation of the tires to the sensors. They seem to read accurately even without movement. When setting up the system the day before my trip, one of the tire indicators flashed on the monitor even though it was in range of pressure & temperature. Once I got the vehicle moving the flashing stopped so I think there is some correlation.

title: Big handles, sharp attachments make repairs easier Very complete kit with great features accessories
text:
This is a very nice kit, The handles are large & meaty so they are easy to handle but aluminum & lightweight. The kit comes with a reamer & inserter handle plus an extra reamer & an extra inserter attachment.
The reamer has a nice, sharp awl-tap tip that is easy to start. The plug inserter has a sleeve which pushes against the plug to hold it in when extracting the tool. I have never had that in a kit before & it made it a whole lot easier to extract the tool without disturbing the plug.
The kit came with lubricant to ease pushing the awl & plug into the tire. Most kits come with rubber cement for the job but I have inserted plenty without the cement & the lubricant made it easier.
There is an included tool kit that comes with Schrader valves, valve caps, a razor knife for trimming the plug & one of those 4-way tools that removes valves & cleans up threads on valve stems. The best accessory is the zipper case that holds the tools with elastic straps & includes a hanging strap.

title: Fully portable, fully automatic cutoff tire & raft inflator with great accessories & versatility
text:
This pump is great, I have used it dozens of times already since I got it. I love the portability, the power options, the speed & especially the auto-cutoff. I immediately used it to top off motorcycle, bicycle, RV & trailer tires for a trip & continued to use it all week. The tire pressure is programmed easily & the compressor cuts off when the desired pressure is reached. The pressure setting reverts to the previous setting so I was even able to program the pressure & send it with my wife to top off a tire on her parents' car.

I selected this pump because of the high pressures rated. I have small trailer tires that require 90psi plus large, RV tires that go up to 65psi. The smaller, emergency inflators I have used struggle with those volumes & pressures & get hot but this compressor had no problem with any of the tires but it doesn't have a tank so it is nowhere near as fast or powerful as a portable compressor that would be used for air tools. The advantage is the battery & auto-cutoff. I can take it anywhere, start it & walk away.

I was able to pump up a fully-deflated 17" car tire to 35lbs in about 7 minutes & a much smaller trailer tire to 90psi in about 8 minutes. The pressure increase is pretty consistent & doesn't slow much as it gets to higher pressures like some pumps. After filling, the case doesn't get hot but the hose gets too hot to touch. The battery lasts about 35 minutes after charging but charging takes a long time, at least 2 hours.

The pump also has low pressure outlets to inflate or deflate large rafts or air mattresses. I tested it on a huge float & the inflate & deflate rates were impressive. I didn't try the automatic pressure on a float & I am not sure if would cut off with those low pressures or is designed to.

The pump will run directly from an AC wall plug, a 12v DC cigar lighter socket in a car on on the included battery. The AC wall cord is short (about 3') & the 12v DC cord is about 10'. The battery comes with a separate charger & as far as I can tell doesn't charge when the pump is plugged into another source. The battery pack isn't common to any of the other tools I have but it does have a handy charge meter built in.

The pump casing has useful & handy storage areas on the ends & sides for the cords, accessories & hoses. It came with a basketball needle & raft inflator adapter & there are clips on the end to store them. The unit feels solid with nothing rattling inside. It also has LED lights built into one end which I always forgot to use, they would be more helpful if they were on the other end.

I am extremely pleased with this compressor, it has been very useful. The only real issue I have is that the battery doesn't charge in the compressor so I had to take the charger on my trip but it's also nice to be able to use the compressor on another power source while the battery is charging.

title: Cord fits my predator generator & 30A camper  ran with AC & no issues
text:
This generator adaptor is working well. The original adaptor is straight with no cord & I didn't like how it put pressure on the connection at the generator. I prefer this adapter with the cord to allow for some drop.
I'm taking an RV trip for the fist time in 18 months because it's 2021. The adaptor fits my Predator generator & a 30A cord (my camper has a 50A cord so I am using an adapter). In preparation for the trip I ran the generator with the AC on for 20 minutes & had no issues.

title: Easy to use, seems to be filtering well, the outer filter ring is removable
text: I'm getting my old CL100 together for some light trail riding. The stock filter is a good setup but the elements dry out & turn to dust when the bike sits & I wanted something that could be cleaned. This filter is a good if inelegant fit. I removed the outer ring, oiled the inside & put the ring back on. If I was using it for a street only application I probably wouldn't bother with the oil.

title: Looks a little rough but perfect fit for Honda CL100 & has been running well
text: I needed a pilot jet & float for my Honda CL100 carb but the original jet is unavailable & this entire carburetor was about the price of an OE float. It fits the bike perfectly but took a lot of tries to set the float height. I also raised the needle one clip & it is running good. The casting on the carb body is a little rough & I can tell it isn't the original Mikuni from across the room. The float in the picture has a LOT of solder. It has not leaked but it sure isn't pretty.

title: Direct fit to change the ratio a Honda CL100
text: I wanted to gear my '70 CL100 down for trail riding. It was hard to determine if this was a direct fit but I realized I had bought another JT sprocket for it earlier & it had the same part number series. It was a direct fit but did require a couple of extra links in the chain due to it being so much larger than stock. It's only been out for 1 ride, about 15 miles dirt & 5 miles street but the black looks good & is holding up.

title: They even worked on my 1100 monster
text: I was shopping by delivery date in order to get these before a trip & accidentally strayed into 1198 clutch plates. I crossed my fingers that they would fit & they did. The friction plates are aluminum vs steel on my original clutch but they fit just fine & the weekend trip was saved. They were a bit grabby at first but broke in nicely. Hopefully the aluminum discs will be easier on my clutch basket.

title: Very soft & very grippy, haven't gotten greasy
text: This is my favorite grip pattern, the size fits my large hands well & like that I can squish the nubs in my hands. The thickness & soft nubs provide a little bit of cushion. Disappointingly the only "red" is on the end that I mostly cut off for the hand guards & the color is almost orange. I have run 1 race & had a few rides & the gray hasn't gone all greasy or dark.

title: Good for grips, spool is handy, wire is pricey
text: I've done 3 sets of grips with this wire & it has worked fine. The finish is still shiny after a race & couple of rides. I occasionally break it over-tightening but there's a learning curve. The little spool is easy to work with but I feel like I'm paying more for the packaging than the wire.

title: Fit good but probably not real ProTaper grips, harder & smaller than modern grips
text:
I don't think these are real Pro-Taper grips but they did mount up pretty easy & look good. They are quite hard for modern grips & the grip pattern is very fine. I was surprised at how well they do grip gloves with the fine checkering & hardness. They are also small, about 29mm in diameter vs 32.5mm for my ProTaper Pillow grips.
They mounted up in the usual way & I used wire to cinch them. I do like the rubber 'donuts' that go on the inside. They look good & hide the inside wire.

title: Quick & easy install for a modern functional & cool upgrade
text:
[[VIDEOID:628d0150829afe8fc1ffadada05cb337]] These tail lights are sturdy, heavy & solid. They look modern & have the benefit of being brighter & having more lights than stock. They are an obvious upgrade but blend in with the original look & they install literally in minutes.
The plugs appear to be the same quality as the Mopar & plug straight in. If you have a towing kit, be careful about plugging in the left light because you can accidentally plug the tow harness into itself. The tail lights will still work but not the tow lights.

title: Very sheer, Well thought out gloves with a lot of discrete but good features
text:
These gloves are very sheer & cool. I was even able to take off my watch over them. The material on the tops are breathable & stretchy, the palms are thin & leather type with perforations & the cuffs are like Spandex. There are no protective pads for rocks or sticks or no real padding in the palm but they dry very fast if soaked.
The palms are grippy leather & have extra-grippy, rubberized strips on index & middle finger. There are also threads on the thumb & index finger tips which allow the wearer to work a capacitive screen on a phone or tablet. The thumb is in a good place but index finger is not in a natural position for me & takes some concentration to put it where it will work.
The gloves fit tight & looked really small when I received them. I was afraid that I ordered children's gloves when I first received them but they pulled right on. They seem to have relaxed now that I have ridden with them. There are small grip nubs on the velcro straps help tighten them & there is an extra tab of material on cuff to help pull them on.

title: Great value, Good vision & breathing, lense is easy to replace, vibrant colors
text:
Great vision from these even though they are smaller than my other goggles. I never noticed the frames while riding & I never noticed them binding on the helmet. They seem to breathe well but I haven't had a chance to work them too hard & it was a cool day for a ride. The strap adjusted easily & it has strips of rubberized coating to help it stick to a helmet so it doesn't slip. The color is vibrant (I was a dayglo era kid) & the strap matches the frames better than the pictures show.
This is my first pair of 100% goggles & I was surprised at the low price given how many riders they sponsor.
I usually take the lenses out after a ride to wash them in the sink & I wash the frames with my gear. These were surprisingly easy to put back together given how many mounting points they have. The lense has nubs for tear-offs but I rarely use them.

title: Attractive finish & sturdy steel. Great looking cuts in the metal. Easy to install.
text:
These mounts look great with a tough, black, textured finish. The cuts in the steel with the star on the back & the "grill" on the front have amazing detail. The steel is quite rigid which is nice because the doors are always heavier than I expect.
The doors plop right on with the windows lowered. The brackets have foam strips on the bottom edges to protect the paint. The brackets mount easily with three included mounting screws that have a Phillips & 3/8" external hex drive. I did drill pilot holes before mounting the bracket due to the large screw size. It also came with plastic screw inserts for drywall but I did not try those.
The mounts were wrapped in bubble wrap for shipping. They arrived in perfect condition.

title: Looks great & works well, materials are stout. Easy enough to install.
text:
I have never liked the looks of the exposed gas tank filler on my Jeep & it gets gross & dirty in there. This gas tank door looks & works great on my '12 JK. The materials are sturdy plastic & the door is aluminum. The black surround looks so good it reminds me how much the rest of the plastic has faded on my Jeep. The hinge is smooth & easy to open. It has a spring that keeps the door open or closed.
Installation took me 18 minutes including an extra trip back inside for tools. Installation requires a 4mm or 5/32" hex drive or Allen wrench plus a Phillips head screwdriver to remove the tail light. I also went back for a flat head screwdriver & a pair of pliers.
The instructions have pretty good illustrations but could benefit from some words.
Start by removing the Allen screws to take the door loose from the surround. The top & bottom screws don't need to come out.
1. Don't do this near a palmetto or campfire.
2. Remove the left tail light which only requires removing the two screws on the inside.
3. The flat head screwdriver will come in handy for unplugging the tail light (you may not need to do this if you have the tow harness).
4,5. Remove the gas cap & tether.
6. Push the filler surround out from the inside. There are plastic clips but the ones in the front are hard to get to. I was able to work the rear ones with that flat head but I broke one of the front clips trying to get it out.
7. Remove the gasket around the filler neck (& install it in the new surround). Mine was greasy so a shop rag will be useful here. Also they are about $11.00 shipped so it may be a good time to replace it.
8,9,10,11. Press the new surround in, over the filler neck & clipped into the body panel. There are little pins that go into pre-existing holes in the panel to index it.
It's not in the instructions but put the gas cap tether back in the hole (flat head screwdriver again) & re-install the gas cap.
12,13. Screw the door onto the filler surround with the 4 Allen screws using 4mm or 5/32" hex wrench & torque to 15in/lb.

title: Good features & quality, digital gauge is accurate, reads supply pressure too
text:
I am very pleased with this inflator. It isn't Milton quality but it is accurate, easy to use & has good features. It has a large thumb lever to fill & a button on the side to bleed air. The body seems to be well made, the valve body is cast metal & all the fittings are brass or similar. The action of the fill lever is smooth. There doesn't seem to be any variability of the air flow.
The gauge is easy to use & the fill chuck & hose have good reach. It will read the supply pressure which is nice to know while the compressor is filling up.
The gauge is lit & the digital numbers are large & easy to read (even without my cheaters) at about 1/2". The light stays on while filling & stays on for about 15 seconds when not filling but it will go off when releasing air. The numbers will stay on as long as there is pressure. I don't know if it will ever go off but it will stay on for at least 30 minutes if there is pressure in the supply line. Supply pressure can be released by pressing the bleed button & the display will go off.
The gauge reads in PSI, BAR, KG/cm2 & Kpa. It says it reads up to 255Psi but I don't have anything that will go over 110Psi. The gauge is pretty well protected by a rubberized plastic coating that could be thicker & softer. The lense area is soft & light colored & looks easy to scratch.
The hose is about 18" with the chuck & has about 10" of flexibility so it's a 2-handed operation. I have been able to use it to air up the tires on my cars, motorcycles & trailer. The fill chuck for Schrader valves is at a 45 degree angle & is double-ended. It's a pretty standard chuck so other designs could be installed on the gauge. The hose is soft & flexible but I am not crazy about the light gray color because it is already showing stains.

title: Excellent grip & protection for off road riding & work
text:
I wore these gloves on a very muddy dirt bike ride & they never got slippery & my hands didn't get cold. They have exceptional protection from roost & branches & such with padded fingers & some vinyl coverage. The street-bike style, protruding, plastic knuckle bumps are probably unnecessary but they don't hurt performance.
I usually wear motocross gloves with minimal protection or off-road gloves that have little plastic pads but these offer full on finger & knuckle protection. They also have padded sections on the palm heel & other sections of the palm with an additional, grippy layer. The grip & protective sections make for a good work glove as well.
I found them to be comfortably warm on a January ride. Some of the material is of a thinner material that is supposed to be breathable. My hands did sweat some but it was a rigorous ride. The index finger tips work on a phone or tablet screen.
These fit a little tight & pull on my hands when trying to close them. I hope the loosen up a little with wear because I intend to wear them on more rides. I noticed when my hands were sweaty that they were hard to pull on. Washing them did not loosen them up any.

title: Extremely handy for topping off smaller items, easy for kids to use, not for all jobs
text:
I was changing a tube at a trail & someone had a similar battery powered pump which was very handy. This one is much more convenient because you can set the maximum pressure & walk away or trust your kid with it.
The killer feature on this is the ability to set the desired pressure & it automatically cuts off. I taught my teen how to use this so she can fill her own bicycle tires. I wrote the correct pressure on the tires & she shouldn't overfill them as long as she sets the pressure.
I have been using this to top off the tires on my motorcycles & bicycles in the garage which takes a few seconds. I double checked several tires with my digital gauge until I trusted this one's accuracy.
I topped off the spare on my JEEP & it took around 12 minutes to get it from 19 to 35lbs. The pump got warm but not searing hot like almost all of the portable compressors I have owned over many years.
I noticed that the pressure setting would go up to 120psi so I decided to try one of the 12" trailer tires that runs 90psi. I cut it off after 20 minutes at 81.5psi. The pressure increase had gotten very slow, the hose got too hot to touch at the end proximal to the pump & it seemed to be struggling. Both of these took the battery down to one bar on the indicator.
This pump is easily small & light enough to keep in a tool bag but not something I would carry in a backpack. It comes with a small bag that holds the pump & hose but just barely & only if the hose is curled. It would be cool if it came with a harder case that also holds at least one of the chargers. It comes with an AC charger to plug into a socket & a DC charger to plug into a car cigarette lighter plug.
It has a built-in LED light which is quite handy but the button is very accessible & can get turned on easily while in the bag, transporting or handling. I left the light on for about 45 minutes to see if it would turn off on its own but it didn't.
I like this pump a lot & plan to experiment with it more. I'd like to see how it handles a raft or beach toy but that's not really how I intend to use it most of the time.

title: Looks cool but it's not a good design
text:
I decided not to install this on my Jeep. It looks good & I do want a door over the filler but I have some problems with it. There is no detent or spring on the door so the only way to keep it shut is with the key & I'm not sure I want to deal with an extra key since gas theft hasn't been an issue here since the '70s. It didn't come with instructions but installation is easy enough with stainless steel screws that go into the plastic through the open door.
The back of the filler ring is just thin, unprotected aluminum that buts right against the paint & will inevitably scratch a ring into the paint. The hinge is not robust & I'm afraid that it will break or I will grow tired of the key & be stuck with the scratched paint so I decided to get one that is better suited to my needs.

title: Comfortable & looks nice adds warmth for windy days but can get too warm around the neck inside
text:
This is a comfortable & reasonably good looking solution for a mask. It has loops for the ears but it actually stays up over my nose pretty well without being looped around the ears. In some situations it got hot around my neck & I preferred to take it off & swap for a disposable mask.
I resisted getting a cloth mask for a long time but on long travel days, the elastic bands on the disposable masks plus glasses & earphones were killing my ears. I was hoping that the cloth ear rings would relieve the pressure on my ears. The cloth did feel better but the cloth bunches up & is gets thick behind the ear. The good news is that the mask stayed up over my nose without being pulled over my ears.
The mask did get hot around my neck & I took it off on my last flight & accidentally left it on the plane. I do miss it, it was a great solution & was nice to have the warmth sometimes when I was outside but it got hot inside sometimes. I was never questioned about the effectiveness of the neck-gaiter style on planes, or at airports, restaurants or hospitals.

title: Professional quality set includes metric sizes, locking extensions & even a nice case
text:
This is a fantastic set I am very happy to have it in my box. The chrome is thick, the sockets are tight & the locking extensions are smooth. Even the case is nice. The set comes with 14, 16 & 18mm & 9/16, 5/8 & 13/16" sizes. 14mm is pretty much 9/16" & 16mm is pretty much 5/8" but this is the first time I have ever had actual millimeter spark plug sockets. I have always had to use a lug nut socket or the thin steel, tool kit sockets on my old Japanese bikes.
The sockets use a nylon or maybe delrin ring inside to grip the plugs. I wasn't sure if they would grip as well as the usual rubber inserts but they snap right over the plugs & hold really well. The sizes are laser etched onto the sockets. The metric sockets & the extensions are knurled at the end while the inch sockets have a hex on the distal end.

title: The 1st one is 30 minutes, the 2nd is 10. Watch a video first, it will go a long way. 2000 F150
text: It's probably been 4 years since I opened the driver's side rear door on my 2000 F150 & one year for the passenger side. I read the instructions that came with these & then watched a video that helped me understand the process a lot better. I was able to install the latch ferrules without removing anything but the door cards & speakers. I didn't bother with the other ends since the latch ends did the trick.

title: Very high quality tool & nice features; good reach, strong magnet & smooth CV joint swivel
text:
I know the manufacturer is proud of this socket because it came better packed than any torque wrench I have ever bought.
I have never used a magnetic socket before, all of mine either have the rubber plug or are missing the rubber plug. The magnet inside this socket holds onto the plug with more force than the ball detent on my ratchet. The length is great for my motorcycles & OHC Ford engine but way too long for the more horizontal plugs in my camper's old Chevy engine. The swivel inside the socket is not a universal joint but a much smoother, constant velocity joint.

title: Perfect, original fit for 7.4L 454 Big Block Chevrolet in 1998 P30 Chassis Camper
text:
It was ridiculously hard to find the plug wires for this very common engine. I hope my headline will be some help to others.
I was really hoping to find some bargain aftermarket wires but I never did. It's hard to go wrong with original equipment & these swapped perfectly. The lengths were dead on & they fit in the looms but I would have been happy with wires with slightly more troubling fit for half the price.

title: Plenty of power & storage, clamps are large & have long leads, very hard to get on side terminal bat
text:
These things are such a lifesaver. Just the peace of mind having it in my vehicle while it's parked at the airport for a week is worth the price. I have a couple of these & this one is about 30° larger but with more than twice the starting current & 4x the peak current. The leads are nice & long so I don't have to leave it dangling off a motorcycle while boosting. The clamps are large & easy to get a grip but the metal that actually goes on the terminals is tucked way inside the plastic so they are very hard to put directly on a battery with side terminals.
This booster hasn't failed to start anything I have put it on. I did notice that it got pretty hot after a while. It also takes a long time to charge.
The storage bag for this booster is very simple & large & that is a main reason that this booster has become my go-to when I know I am going to need to use it. The bag does not have any protection, though, like some of these sets. It also doesn't come with any accessories like a 12v car cigarette lighter adapter though it does have a port for one.
These are great little power sources for charging or running small electronics. I was able to power my portable satellite radio & a usb speaker on a picnick table on a camping trip. This has my favorite USB-C for charging & output. It also has 2 USB outputs, 1 is regular 5v & the other can go up to 12v but I don't have anything that requires that. I have noticed that some smaller devices won't charge off the USB or USB-C ports presumably because they don't pull enough amps to be detected by the device. I really haven't used the light much because it is it isn't particularly bright, faces 1 direction & isn't particularly easy to switch on. A lantern style light with a dedicated switch would be better.

title: Simple & effective, look good & work well
text: These have the same design of ruberized handle as the Quadratech handles. They go on with straps & buckles instead of Velco. The straps are easy to tighten, stay tight & there isn't a lot of excess strap material. There isn't any material between the straps so they will bunch up to the width of the handle, even if you spread them out more on the install. This is a solid deal for a set of 4.

title: Yes! Finally a reasonable solution for my gas cans
text:
I should have figured that someone would market a solution for the terrible gas spouts that have come out over the last couple of decades & now my suffering is over. I rounded up all of my cans to test these out. The yellow rings fit all of my versions of Blitz brand cans & were replacements for the four spouts in the picture. I added the included vents to 2 of the cans by drilling a 1/2" hole in the back of the can. I replaced a vent in one very old can that came with a vent, just to make sure it would fit.
The kit comes with 3 flexible spouts & 2 types of rings to hold them down. I didn't have any cans that fit the black, finer threaded rings. Also in the kit are threaded caps that fit the included spouts & caps for 2 other types of spouts that I don't have. It also includes the 3 vents to add to cans that didn't include them originally. These are necessary to add to allow the liquid to pour smoothly (the new types vent through the spout.
There were no ring combinations in this kit to fit the other style cans in the 3rd picture. I would love to have all of my cans updated (backdated) to this style of pour spout.

title: Good looking, good quality & good view fit multiple bar sizes
text:
The mirrors come with two nested, expanding collets that allow to fit in 7/8" bars which is about 5/8" inside inside diameter. By removing the outer collet, they also fit inside the bar end weights on my bike which have are about 9/16" or 14mm inside diameter. The mirrors have a lot of adjustments, notably a ball joint that allows for adjustment while riding & also a hinge which allows the mirrors to be folded inside to get through a narrow passage or if whacked against a car or pole or something.
The mirrors certainly look much more clean than the ungainly stalks that came with my bike & I can see very well behind me without having to look under my arm. Installation takes 4 tools to adjust, allen wrenches in 5mm, 4mm, 2.5mm & an 8mm wrench. I brought these tools on my first ride in order to adjust the mirrors but I had gotten them close enough in the garage that I could do final adjustments with my hands. The kit came well packed in foam inside the box.

title: Great value to get a variety of fuses Fuse holder is nice & easy to use Fuse tester is also useful
text:
Getting a multi-pack of fuses like this is great value over buying the little tins with one value each at the auto parts store. The fuses are standard colors for amperage which helps because the markings on the fuses are a bit vague. I wrote the values of the fuses on the container with a marker.
I got the kit that includes the fuse tester & the fuse holders. I don't know with why it has taken me this long to find out that bade fuses can be tested without removing them but it is very useful. The tester works like an ohm meter with a power source that lights a green LED if a fuse is good. The fuses can be tested at the blades or on the exposed metal on the back of the fuse while it is installed.
The fuse holders are pretty nice. They have wires connected & sealed into the housing so the wires need to be spliced into a wire with some kind of connectors or terminated where the wires end. The connection over the fuse has a water resistant cap so they can be used under a car hood or somewhat exposed on a trailer.

title: Straps are huge & wide, very strong
text:
I use these soft straps to tie down motorcycles mostly but also for my generator, coolers & other cargo. These were way wider than I expected. They work fine on my street bikes but there isn't enough real estate on the bars of my dirt bikes.
The straps are 2" wide, the material is thick & there is a lot of heavy stitching. The straps are soft & shouldn't mar any metal or hard plastic finish.

title: Fits with the soft top down, sunshade works great, took a lot longer to install than I planned
text:
Most importantly for me the soft top will go on with it installed, I can't speak to the Freedom Top hard top but there is space to move the cords to the sides of the front top mounts & it mounts very low so it will probably work. The top does a great job of blocking glare with the top down but it is a chore to install. It does buffet a little when driving from time to time but it isn't bad.
The top I got was only for the front seats which is good enough for me. My eyes are very light sensitive so it's a nice compromise. The kids in the back can still enjoy full sunlight. It does lower the ceiling a bit 3-4" which takes some getting used to but is still above the roll bars so plenty high.
The material is thick & stiff & should last a long time.The flag is monochrome. It looks nice from above but you can't see it at all from the inside so it's hard for anyone to know it is there, maybe truckers?. Some of the white paint was transferred to the other side where it was folded.
The instructions were completely incomprehensible until I cracked the code. They refer to "velcro" but mean the elastic shock cords that are included for installation. The instructions for "2-door" mean that the top only covers the front seats on a 2 door or 4 door JK. There is a longer cover for 4-door JK but the instructions list it as for a TJ.
I had to remove the plastic rain rails in order to install the shock cords but they went back on without interference. I thought I was going to have to loosen the speaker enclosure but I was able to sneak the back shock cords through a gap. Some of the cords had to be stretched very tight & one pulled through the knob & had to be re-tied because I stretched it so far. It is fiddlesome to sort out and get the cords & knobs in just the right locations where the shade will pull tight & the knobs will be out of the way of the doors & top. A little more fiddling on my part & it would probably look a lot cleaner.
It came with a mesh bag to hang from the grab handle. I won't be showing off this little purse to my friends but it is actually pretty handy for holding some hand sanitizer & a mask which define 2020.
This item is made in China (no surprise there) but by a Chinese company. The quality is there but it could use a little more refinement to make it easier to install. I can't imagine putting it on for just a day ride & having to take it off to put the top up.

title: Finally! a place to stick my phone in my Wrangler JK
text:
This kit looks a little ungainly from the side or top but it works great & looks pretty normal from the seat. The kit comes with 2 mounts & I used one to hold my portable satellite radio. I am grateful to finally have a place to put both. The phone holders squeeze shut but open softly with the touch of the button on the back.

The arms that stick out to hold the phone look rigid but they are actually flexible. They are attached to the tray with clips like gopro accessories use & there are 3 of them so this could be a versatile system beyond holding a phone. The phone clip attaches to the arms with a ball & socket.

To install the kit you'll need to remove the rubber insert from the dash tray & remove 1 screw from the dash. The kit includes a screw that anchors their cup into the pre-existing screw hole. The kit comes with a screw that is hex on the outside & phillips on the inside but my 2012 Wrangler only had the 7mm hex so I had to make another trip back to the garage for a socket. The tray will flex a little because it is only held down by the single screw far away from where the arms mount.

title: Very White & Bright lights. A tight fit for my Ford.
text:
I upgraded the headlights of my old 2000 Ford F150 from Halogen 9007 to these LEDs & the difference is striking. These lights are bright white & make the old bulbs look yellow by comparison.

The install was straightforward except for the retaining rings that go around the lights on my Ford design. On the halogen lights the connection is in the back of the bulb where these have a tiny fan & a cable exiting from the side. I had to break one of the tensioner clips off of the retaining ring to accommodate the cable. The lights seem to be ever so slightly larger in diameter & when I pressed on the second retainer ring all the rest of the tensioner clips broke out. This is probably due to the age of the parts & being in an unforgiving environment but an installer should take care when installing retainer rings.

title: Smells good, works well
text: We washed 2 cars & a dirt bike & the soap worked well, especially on the plastic body parts of the motorcycle.  I didn't so much as notice what I would call "foam", just mounds of regular soap bubbles like you would have with dish soap. My wife liked the smell which reminds me of the shampoo part of a haircut.  After the 2 cars & the bike there is around 60% of the 24 oz bottle left.

title: Great idea with unexceptional execution
text:
This product is a great idea & it does work. It uses a rechargeable battery to keep the phone alive rather than having to wire it to the bike electricals. The mount is very secure & holds the phone quite well but it gives up a lot for the security.

The bar clamp has very large thumb screws which makes it very easy to secure. The trade off is that they are very large & will hit the tank on bikes with limited bar space like a sport bike or even an adventure bike. I would have liked to have the option to use a tool on smaller fasteners since the clamp shouldn't need to come off very often. Cruisers or bikes with bar risers probably won't have this problem.

The battery is the phone mount & it connects to the bar clamp via a slip-on connector that holds firm & is easy to remove & replace. The phone clamps firmly onto the battery with sturdy thumbscrews. The battery is heavy & bulky though & connects to the phone with a cord so removing it to take into a gas station or wherever is inconvenient whether removing the battery/phone as a whole or removing the phone from the battery. The battery lasts longer than I can possibly use it in these rainy, spring months so I feel like it would last a whole day.

Things that would be better for me would be:
Wireless charging though I'm sure it is much less efficient than a cord
A USBC or lightning cable for charging the battery rather than the micro USB (cord included)
Include a short cable for USBC and/or lightning connector
Spring-type clamp for the phone rather than the thumb screws for easy install & removal & less vibration when no phone is in the mount

The mount arm with a RAM style ball mount so I plan to get a RAM ball & extension that mounts to the steering head to use on my sport bike for commuting once it quits raining & they let us go back to work.

title: Massive upgrade over stock, easy to install & look modern & very cool
text:
These lights look so cool & they really bring a modern touch to my 8 year old JKU. The JK headlights have always been terrible. Every winter I have wanted to replace them & then I forget about it when the time changes. These LEDs are a massive improvement. I also didn't realize how bad my headlight covers had glazed so they were due for replacement anyway.

Installation is straight forward, it only required a flat head screwdriver to remove the clips for the grill & a Torx T15 driver to remove & Install the headlight rings that hold the lights in. It took me less than an hour to wrap up the entire job & that included a good bit of futzing around trying to get the lights to fit into the enclosure. I found that lining up the tops & starting the top screws first was best for getting them seated.

The wiring harness adapters plug in well but they aren't the OEM style with with the waterproof gasket. The assembly instructions are for a JL which is apparently similar but not identical. I did not wire the daytime running lights.

title: Looks cool, is built sturdy, harder to install than I expected
text: It fits my KTM125SX well but it was much harder to push into the radiator than the stock unit. It looks really cool even though the blue doesn't match my bike very well (I'm not much of a slave to fashion). I was a little concerned about the glass being fragile but it is well protected by the thick material & bezel that surrounds it. I thought I was going to get the bike out today & actually test the thermostat but I wasn't able to.

title: Big & thick with sturdy loops for a cable or chain
text:
First of all I ordered a size that was way too big for my Ducati. The 2L would easily fit over a bagger or. The material is thick & doesn't snag on levers or pegs like my thinner covers. There are 2 large, metal brads (like 2" large) in the front of the cover to pass a cable through & there is a plastic buckle in the back to tighten up under the real wheel. It has reflective strips integrated into the ends. It took me just over 2 minutes to pull the cover off the bike, fold it & put it in the drawstring storage bag.

I'm putting drywall in my garage so I wanted to cover the bike. I don't have much need to cover a bike outside but this feels sturdy enough that is should last in the elements. It pulls down far enough that the bike can't be identified which I would want when parking outside an apartment or leaving it at the airport for a couple of days.

title: No set up at all & tough Perfect for tow cars & occasional use trailers
text:
These lights are a fantastic solution for tow cars as well as trailers. The setup is mindless, once the lights are turned on they are working. There is no setup or syncing. Because the lights are wireless they can be tested inside the car while the tester puts on the brakes or turns signals or wherever, no running around to watch for turn signals. The lights attach to the tow with very strong magnets.
I was looking for a kit to re-wire my old motorcycle trailer for probably the 2nd time since I have owned it when I saw these lights. Due to the portability of the wireless units I will be able to use this set on my trailers, on my hitch hauler & when I tow my Jeep behind the motorhome.
I have a set of magnetic towing lights from the discount tool store but the long wires are impossible to keep untangled & they have to be repaired every time I use them due to the poor quality wiring. When I towed the Jeep I usually left them mounted with the wires running down the sides after it was un-hooked because I didn't want to mess with the wires. I'll just be able to toss these into the back of the Jeep or recharge them in the motorhome.
Once the lights are turned on, they are in "standby" mode. That means that if you are towing & stop at Stucky's for for lunch you won't have to turn them on again before you start driving again. I figured they would turn off after a while but I left them in "standby" for over 2 hours & they never did.
I left these hooked them to my test rig with just the running lights on for about 5 hours. One of the lights dropped one bar on the battery meter in that time but I also ran it with the "brake/turn" light on for a while. The lights come with a charge cord that will charge both lights at the same time. It also comes with a USB wall adapter & cigarette lighter adapter of the lowest quality.
I am completely jazzed about these lights because they solve several, above mentioned problems for me. One thing I didn't anticipate was the round 4-hole plug. This plug is not common enough that anyone no one seems to make an adapter for it to go to a 4 way flat vehicle plug. I kluged my own adapter so I can test the lights until I can make a proper one from a kit. It looks like the manufacturer also sells this kit with a 7 way plug which is more common.
The fact that I already had a test rig for trailer lights made up (3rd picture) should speak to the frustration I have had trying to maintain a few trailers. I intend to use these lights on multiple trailers in the future instead of trying to maintain them.
In the 1stpicture I have these lights mounted on the round fenders of my old Holsclaw trailer. The magnets hold fine on a flat surface but they wobbled on the curved surface & one of them fell off. We found it on the side of the road with the housing scratched but nothing cracked & the light in working order.

title: Very versatile & solid, good value, No instructions, could be hard for a first install.
text:
These come with zero instructions, not even a picture. If your bike doesn't already have hand guards of a similar style there will be some extra work & it may take time to figure these out. Both grips will need to be trimmed on the ends & the throttle tube may need to be drilled or cut.

These are quite versatile having adapters for both 7/8" & 1" bars for the external clamp & the internal collet that goes in the bar end. The external clamps are hinged so the have a good deal of adjustability but that also makes them a little fiddlesome. My bike has tapered bars so I used the 1" clamp adapter & the 7/8" collet.

I put these on a 2005 KTM 125SX I just bought. It had the Cycra hand shields, one of which I broke the first time I rode it & slipped on a root. I have ridden twice with these hand guards & had two spills plus one small tree strike with no big issues. The left guard that kissed a tree was scratched a little on the plastic but that is expected. The guards didn't move when they hit the ground but both have had hardware come loose a little which you can see in the picture with the dangling, oval washer. I will address that with some thread locker.

The finish on the parts reflects the price but these are perfectly serviceable hand guards & they don't look bad on the bike. The internal collets are all metal & are strong. I'll probably get another set for the Yamaha.

Update; I got another set for the Yamaha. They work well enough & look good. They do bend pretty easily. That helped to adjust them when installing on the Yamaha with it's swept-back bars but not so great if the bike falls over in the driveway.

title: Excellent price, new rim looks so much better than my old rusty rims.
text: Excellent price on this rim. I previously bought a new tire for my old rim but the old rim was so rusty that it leaked. I installed the tire on this rim with no issues & for the low price of this replacement, it was never worth messing with the old one in the first place. I have switched most of my trailers to 10" wheels so this is primarily a spare & hopefully won't be used.

title: Heavy Duty and Heavy!
text:
This cord is necessarily heavy with 90 feet of 6 AGW & 30 feet of 8 Awg Copper THHN wire. The cord ends are crisp & sturdy and both cord ends have built-in handles that help plug it in, especially at the box connection. The wires are wrapped in a thick plastic sheathing but the assembly remains remarkably flexible. Even with the built-in handle my 50A supply lid closes easily over the plug.

I keep the camper plugged in at home year round but coiling up the attached cord to move it is a hassle & I hate trying to re-coil it into the bunk for travel or just to move it. With this extension I can unplug it at the camper without having to stow the cord. I probably won't travel with the cord unless I am going to a campground where the boxes are way at the back (I'm looking at you Fort Wilderness) & non-stop air conditioning is required.

I might have mentioned that this cord is heavy. The box was a bit beat up when it arrived but nothing was damaged.

title: Didn't come with everything needed for replacement, medium job replace plugs while you have it apart
text:
Smelling burnt oil when you are stopped at traffic lights & leaving a puddle in your driveway? Your Fiat Chrysler vehicle with a 3.6L Pentastar may have a leaking oil cooler. When it goes, the leaking oil puddles in valley between the cylinders under the intake. When the vehicle moves oil spills out the back & coats the transmission & when it stops oil spills out the front & burns off on the hot engine.

My replacement cooler came with two new sensors & most of the seals. I didn't notice until after I had it installed that a critical O-ring was not included with the replacement cooler (first picture) & caused oil to leak all over the engine again. I had to remove the intake & cooler again to swap out the old O-ring onto the new cooler. I don't know if the O-ring was supposed to come with the cooler but it would have been nice if it had.

The entire intake has to be removed to replace the oil cooler so it is a good time to replace the spark plugs while replacing the oil cooler.

title: Drop-In fix for my 9N
text: It's crazy that I can order up new parts for my 80 year tractor cum lawnmower but it makes these old tractors a stylish bargain. It turns out that I didn't need this fully built distributor (It was the coil) but this was a drop-in unit. I checked the points gap before installing & it was already correctly set. It is not an exact replacement. The casting is a little rough, the points & coil are a little different (but will still interchange) & the hardware is different. I think the aftermarket coils that are available here & at Tractor Supply fit this distributor better than the original.

title: Reputable brand of full synthetic oil without the feature that makes it popular
text:
I have been using Rotella T4 in my air-cooled small engines and Rotella T6 in my motorcycles for years. The T6 synthetic is a real bargain & meets JASO standards for motorcycles so I was excited to see an add for Rotella Synthetic truck oil assuming it would also be a bargain and come in more standard weights. One of my assumptions was correct.

This oil would appear to perform the same as Valvoline & Mobile full synthetics but it also costs the same as those brands. The specific designation for trucks seems like marketing but anymore most of your V8 engines are going to be found in trucks. Shell says it is for trucks & SUVs that experience extreme conditions like driving with a heavy load (sounds extreme), in dusty conditions (fair enough), stop and go driving (eh..), frequent short trips (really?), extreme hot or cold temperatures, and extensive idling (extreme idling).

Unless you are tearing down engines a lot or something goes really wrong it’s tough to measure the effectiveness of motor oil in a truck. I try to use synthetic oil in my camper because it sits a lot between trips (extreme sitting) & I think the synthetic is less likely to take on moisture. I am happy to use this Shell Rotella brand but I was wishing for a lower price.

title: This is a big, difficult job
text:
The kit is priced right and does work. It is a lot of work to install and does not come with instructions.

This is a big, difficult job. It will take a few hours, a decent number of tools and some skill. The door & hinges have to come off & the old pins have to be ground & pressed out of the hinges. I was able to do this on my concrete floor with an angle grinder, a clamp & some wood blocks but a bench grinder and a press or even a vice would have been better. Most of them were straight forward but the one longer pin took over an hour to get out.

Re-building the hinges is fairly easy due to the threaded pins. One of the 4 pins is different so pay attention to that. Re-hanging and aligning the door is very hard. On the Camaro that I worked on, I had to partially remove the fender in order to align the bottom hinge. I bought a door spring compressor just for the job and did not regret the $8 spend.

This was for my wife's car. If the passenger side needs replacing I may have a body shop do it. I would have been much happier buying the whole, new hinges but they are out of production.

title: This is a difficult job
text:
This is a difficult job. Dont think you are going to knock this out during an oil change or brake job. The door & hinge have to come off, the old pin has to be ground & pressed out, then the door is re-installed and aligned. On the 2001 Camaro I did the fender had to be partially removed to align the door.
It will go a lot better if you have a bench grinder & a press but I was able to do it with an angle grinder & clamp. The instructions say to hammer the new pin into the hinge but I was only able to press it in after I heated the hinge with a torch. The roller also has to be hammered/pressed into the pin.
If you can find a whole hinge treat yourself. I replaced the door bushings with the Dorman kit while I did this job.

I forgot to actually review this product. It honestly surprised me how sturdy the assembly was for how it goes together. I'll be curious to see how it holds up in the long run. It does roll smooth. It could have been cheaper.

title: too small to be any good, do people use these on mountain bikes maybe?
text: These are way too puny to work on a motorcycle. The one in the picture is extended as far as it will go and just barely covers the clutch lever. I probably would have left it on but the brake/throttle side has the on/of & signal switches which puts the mount even further from the end.  they might work on a pit bike or a mountain bike but they are too small even for the XT225 pictured. It's a shame too because the blue color matches the bike perfectly.

title: Keeps the water out.
text:
Keeps the water out. I bought this cover because my 12 Wrangler Unlimited leaks and the floors fill up with water when it rains. This cover fits just fine. Its probably a bit loose for some but since i have to take this on and off every day I appreciate some bagginess. The cover is thicker with more padding than I expected for the price. I need to get around to cutting a hole for the antenna.

The cable, lock and buckle for some strap is sitting on my desk. I have no need for that stuff but i think I would be satisfied if i was shopping for a cover to protect,from Sun, leaves, birds etc.

title: Perfect fit, easy to change.
text: Perfect fit for my 2012 Wrangler with Pentastar V6 and an easy swap.  This solved a drivability problem I have had with the Jeep for a while where it would cut out at low RPMs.

title: It works but not as advertised.
text: This doesn't work as advertised.  There is no check valve so there is nothing to keep the brake system from drawing fluid or air back from the bottle or tube rather than the master cylinder.  I was able to use it on my motorcycle where I can reach the caliper and lever at the same time.  Similarly, it will work fine on an old style two-person job with your bored kid pumping the pedal and you yelling instructions from under the car.

title: This is pretty much exactly the small
text: This is pretty much exactly the small, lightweight, adjustable mirror I wanted for my minibike but the clamping mechanism is weak.  I like it better than the EMGO mirror but it needs a more robust mount.

title: Exactly what I needed.  Spring loaded switch that only contacts when you press it then returns to "off".
text:
This was the exact replacement for my RV's battery and holding tank monitor. I would have paid more for it on the road but it was nice to get this low price after I got back.

Not everyone who needs this will know what to order. A moment or momentary switch is one that is "on" while it is pressed and returns to "off" when you let it go like a button.

title: This is a build-your-own set of wires with a questionable crimp on connector
text:
It turns out that this wire set is what my 1939 Ford 9n needed to run properly again. This build-your-own set leaves a lot to be desired though. The spark plug ends are pre-installed but the wires must be cut to length and the distributor end crimped on. The crimping is no problem but the connector does not go into the insulated section to actually make contact with the wire inside. It just gets near it at the end and hopes for some sort of continuity.
I ended up cutting the insulation back and soldering mine to the wire inside and now they work great. There may be a more appropriate way to install the connectors on to the wires but it isn't articulated in the instructions.

title: Quality components, make sure it includes what you need for your rebuild.
text: Nothing at all wrong with the components in this kit but look closely at the pieces and make sure this is the kit you need.  I mostly needed the gaskets which were correct and quality for my 9n.  I am giving the kit a slight ding for not having needles or jets.  It does come with the float needle, seat and clip which is nice but all the hardware and shafts are not something I intended to replace, especially without the needles and jets.  I am not sure why anyone would seek out this odd combination of parts.

title: Different than the original but works
text: This appears to be the exact same bendix I bought 12 years ago for my 9n.  The last one served me well and outlasted a starter in the meantime.  Ultimately my engine kicked back with the starter engaged and split the gear on the bendix requiring it to be hammered off the starter shaft.  These are completely different than the original style bendix and the tractor makes a different sound when starting.  Just like the original, they work fine until they don't.  I think they are a bit difficult to install and uninstall because you have to compress it in order to pin it to the shaft.  I don't know if that is different from the original style because my original bendix exploded and half of it is still in the bell-housing 12 years later.  If nothing else this style (the last one not the one I recently bought from Amazon) came off in one piece.

title: What a difference these made.
text: I replaced the missing and worn bushings on my 1998 P-30 Motorhome chassis with two of these kits.  Assembly was straight forward and easy.  The ride is infinitely better and even quieter.

title: Perfect fit for my 9N
text: I had no idea how bad the starter was on my tractor until I replaced it.  This replacement made sounds I have never heard since I bought the tractor namely high-RPM starting.  The mounting bolts were a bit on the snug side threading into the block so I ended up using the bolts from my old original starter.  I don't know if that was necessary but it was the only adjustment I had to make to install.

title: Worked Perfectly $30 less than Parts store
text:
When the auto parts store quoted me $80 I was planning to fake a stroke so I could exit without buying it. Fortunately they didn't have it in stock so I was able to claim I couldn't wait for it to be transferred since I was from Awesomestan and just passing through town.

It has thicker padding in the rear and tapers toward the front of the cushion making a more comfortable transition under my legs. I’m actually planning to get a second one for my other car.
