text: My husband ordered these. Apparently they worked great since he never said otherwise.

title: Excellent sign! Weird app
text:
This is a very cool LED sign that can be mounted to a window and easily removed and replaced. My kids put it in an exterior window to our home and greeted everyone as we got home from work with personal messages uploaded to it. Super cute! I'm planning on using this our car when someone graduates and/or on holidays to add some festivity to it!
It really is just like the kind you'd see in front of a gas station or bar, there are premade animations and things you can use, or my favorite option is to draw your own animations frame by frame.
The only problem however, is the app. I'm not a fan.
On a tablet we tried it with, it kept getting stuck and looping with some sort of location permissions problem on Android 6+ (the tablet runs Android 11). It would throw me to a settings screen, I'd enable the permissions, go back to the app and it would complain that permissions still weren't there, then quit. I tried it for about 20+ minutes until I gave up and found an older device in a drawer that runs an ancient Android 5.1. This device ran the app just fine and we could draw/animate/type/etc, although it was kind of slow and laggy thanks to the old hardware we were forced to use.
I'm not sure what the problem was, it seems to work fine if you get the iPhone version as well, but I was disappointed because my kids wanted to use their tablet to control the sign.

title: Finally, THIS is the cover I was waiting for
text: This looks perfect on my 2008 Camry Solara steering wheel. The carbon fiber print and grey padding matches the aesthetic and really enhances the look of my interior, while also making the wheel thicker and easier to grab. I tried a couple of other steering wheel covers before this and didn't love them for one reason or another. This is the perfect feel and texture and aesthetic, I can't imagine my car without it anymore. It feels like this is how it should have come from the factory.

title: Requires you to close your doors into it.
text:
I have an older car (Toyota Solara), and wanted this to protect it from the times I can't park in the garage. I've used another cover previously however it has gotten worn down from seasons so I wanted to give this one a try.
The good news is that the clips are plastic, which I LOVE. The old cover I used had metal clips, and if one isn't fastened properly, that'll scratch up the car in the wind as it shakes around. I prefer plastic or rubberized clips any day.
The bad news, is that they want me to close the doors into this in order to hold it in place. I did not realize that is how it is supposed to work, and I have a major problem with that- The Solara doors don't have a top frame, it is glass against the rubber gasket of the car's top. With material in between like this, you are asking for leaks into the interior of the car around the door seams. I don't like that at all. It fits fine on my other car (Honda Odyssey) but I'm disappointed I can't use it on the car I wanted to.

title: Good for larger steering wheels
text: It's a little rough to get it on, but I like the fit and feel of this better than the last one I tried. The material gives a good grip but still allows you to slide under your fingers when recovering from a turn. Some of the grippy covers don't do that correctly. And most importantly, it covers a worn outer rim of a wheel and makes it look modern and new. Very close to perfect.

title: Grippy... but maybe too grippy?
text:
The good is that it fit easily on my 2008 Camry, made it look more interesting and was very quick and simple to install (and remove!). I'd say easier than other covers I've tried. If you want a cover that gives a lot of GRIP, this is definitely it, however I personally did not like the feel very much.
It is somehow too grippy for me, in as much as it seems your hands almost stick to it. This is great for tactile control of the wheel, but when you release the wheel after a turn and let it straighten itself out, the highly rubberized material sort of tries to take your skin with it. It feels almost like rubbing your hand against a tire. Some people might like this amount of grip, but I like feeling the wheel slide under my fingers when I release it, and I just can't seem to get used to the feeling that I have to actually remove my hands from it completely. I removed it from my car- I think it is a well made product, just not for me.

title: Good for other cars as well
text:
This is designed for the vents in a Tesla, but as the description states, they work find in other cars as well. The trick is to get air flow from your vents through it, as that releases the scent. This is better than other car fresheners which sort of just off-gas and wear out even when not driving the car- this only comes out strong when the vent is running.
I picked up a used car and the previous owner had some kind of clay stored in the center storage bin that had a strong smell even after I removed it, so I tried using this to cover it up. I put it by my defroster vents on the dashboard, and whenever I start the car and it blows towards the window (something my car does all the time in the winter), the scent is very refreshing. So far so good, but I really do wish it had more options for scent instead of just this one.

title: Great bottle from a great brand!
text:
I've used quite a few Contigo plastic water bottles in the past and I've always found them to be very high quality, you have to practically TRY to make them leak. What's great about this one is the built in filter- my son has access to water fountains in school but they don't taste great. The filter on this bottle helps so that he can refill as often as he needs and it will take out some of the tap-water taste.
I don't think it does as great a job as a real filter (aka, Brita, etc) but it does help the water taste a little better. I like the product overall.

title: Expensive, but kind of amazing, actually!
text:
I have owned several electric pumps but this may be my favorite so far. I love that it allows you to choose between battery operation or powered by the 12v car lighter outlet (which gives it an extra oomph and speed). I've owned others that did this as well, however the proprietary charging plug would get lost making it impossible to charge. This charges over a standard USB port, and even offers a fast USB out option to charge your phone as well!
I also love the different presets for PSI, so you can quickly pick one that is appropriate for your needs and start inflating (car, ball, bike, etc). That's a really nice touch as well.
It feels really well made and is surprisingly small too. The asking price of over a hundred dollars seems a bit high, but at the time of this writing it is very much on sale and I would definitely recommend this at a sale price. It is a very useful took, more so than I expected!

title: Fits 04 Solara
text:
When I bought my used Toyota Solara, the gas cap was missing the tether to hold it onto the car. Beyond that, I started getting MIL on the dashboard, with a code for a small EVAP leak. So I decided to try this replacement cap.
It looks more like the OEM one than the cheap replacement that came with my car, I love that it has a tether so I can let the cap fall when fueling, and so far the engine light hasn't come back on, so fingers crossed this fixed my problem! So far so good!

title: Useful and seems well made
text:
I was nervous that the fan would be loud when using this for a game system in the car, but the truth is the fan is modular speed. If it heats up too much from inverting large loads, it will come on. But under smaller loads, it slows down until you can't hear it at all- in fact, when it's cold I think the cooling fan shuts off completely.
300 watts is pretty respectable for high powered usage like running portable pumps and motors, and under that load you'll most definitely hear the fan. But that is understandable. This is otherwise a really well made unit, the body is metal and feels solid, and I love that it offers dual AC plugs as well as USB fast charging ports for other accessories. Would recommend.

title: Tiny device, BIG power- it works!
text:
If you've never used one of these battery packs before to start a car, you might think it's a joke. It looks like something better suited to charge your phone. In fact, it even has USB ports to do that too! But that's not what makes it great- you can in fact use this to jump a full sized car with a dead battery. It sort of makes a fun trick when you show up to help a friend and they don't believe you.
I've owned older versions of this concept that didn't have the same capacity or use standard chargers. This is a big improvement on cranking amps and uses standard USB ports to charge up- no proprietary cable to lose anymore.
I tried it out today to jump my riding mower which hasn't been started in long enough to be dead. Usually with my old jump kit, it would spin and wine a bit before erupting into life, but with this it started INSTANTLY.
I wouldn't trust this to start your car more than once or twice before needing to charge up again, it uses a lot of juice at time to jump and then goes limp. So if you have something like a ride on mower that keeps stalling and dying on you (like I do), you might want to still keep a secondary jumper kit on hand. But the size of this means you can store it in a glove box for emergencies and stop lugging around enormous jumper cables in your old vehicle.

title: Good to have around, not perfect
text:
This is an excellent tool, don't get me wrong. I have vehicles that regularly need to be jumped and air filled, both my cars and things like my riding mower. Everyone should have a tool like this around!
The problem is, I'm spoiled by variants with better features. For example, the air pump works great, but it's not "smart", you just press the button and have to babysit it until it looks like its around the right psi. On my mower which requires 10-15 PSI, it is particularly hard to tell since the markings go from 0 to 25 with a bunch of unlabeled lines in between. I have a couple of tire pumps with digital displays that even let you set the limit for it to shut off by. So you can inflate your tires after a season and not need to babysit the numbers while you, for example, prime the engine and get other things ready.
As a jump starter it works reasonably well, charging the thing is a hassle. Yes, it has a USB charging cable which is nice because it is a standard instead of a proprietary plug. However, it is not a PD input, nor is it even a USB type C... it is the older micro USB plug from years ago, which supports only the slower 5v charging capacity. After using it extensively to troubleshoot a vehicle that would not start (turned out a spark plug cap had come off), I had depleted the battery trying to jump it, and it took all day charging off a USB port before I could attempt it again. I ended up grabbing a different jump starter I hadn't used in years that charges enough to at least make a single jump within an hour. I don't like how slow this is to charge.

But, it's a good all-in-one that is very handy to have around. It will get the job done. I just know it could be improved.

title: Great for keeping your battery healthy
text:
This is a pretty versatile tool for someone with older vehicles and other equipment around the home that needs batteries maintained. I had an old battery in my van that wasn't holding a charge too well, and using this on repair mode breathed some more life into it so I could wait longer before replacing it. I also used to keep my motorcycle battery in storage topped off as well as my riding lawn mower. I like that it has a 6v mode as well so I can use on my kid's ATV if needed and other cool uses as well.
This is NOT, however, for jumping a dead car. This is more of a long term maintainer/repair tool. If you leave it overnight, you'll have a battery good for the next day but if you need something right away, this doesn't seem to be as good as a jumper pack. Someone left the lights on in my car and we tried to use this plugged in for about 5-10 minutes to give it enough juice, and it was useless trying to start it. I have an older battery charger that would allow us to start the car after a few minutes of plugged in, but not this one. This seems to trickle more slowly. I had to dig out a jumper battery from the garage to get the car going again instead.
To be fair, this doesn't claim to be good for jumping a dead car, but my older charger doesn't either and still worked for that on occasion.

title: Material has a slight amount of yellow
text:
I wanted to use this to cover some parts of my car's interior trim that is silver colored. I was hoping it would add some texture and match the other silver parts. Unfortunately, it isn't as silver as I thought once I put the parts back in the car... in fact, it has a slightly yellowish tint to it which I didn't notice on its own, but it is very noticeable next to the silver/grey trim in the rest of the car.
The problem is I can't return it now that I've tried it, so I'm stuck with the purchase. Use this as a cautionary tale- CHECK THE COLOR IN PLACE BEFORE APPLICATION!

title: Make your car a PIXAR car!
text:
I love the idea of this, it is effective at protecting your car from overheating due to sun while simultaneously being hilarious and whimsical! So many people have walked past it and cracked up laughing.
The sizing is a little strange however. On my Toyota Camry Solara, it seems to not want to stay put with jsut the sun visors holding it in place. I have other sunshields that stay just fine with that alone, but for some reason this one keeps falling unless I place it in a very specific position.

Others cars might fit better. But it is worth the extra effort to me because of the eyes. My kids want to give my car a name now!

title: Looks great, but not full coverage
text:
I have an old Toyota seats that had been faded over time from being in the sun. Really makes the whole car old and worn looking. I wanted to completely cover the original seats to refurbish the look, and some leathery looking material cover like this seems like a great idea!
Installation is pretty easy and the front seats look great! The rear seats are a little bit more complicated, but I expected that. However, one thing I'm really disappointed about is the rear seat head rest covers: they are just flaps. I purposed did NOT want flap covers because they allow you to see the original color material through the sides. The front headrest covers are complete coverage which is what I wanted, so I am a little bit surprised to see that the rear is not the same. It looks really bad being able to see the faded light grey peaking out next to the sleek black new covers. I love everything about this set aside from that. I wasn't clear from the product descriptions that the rear aren't as good as the front ones, which are shown prominently.

title: Great way to add USB charging to 12v power sources.
text: This is not only a great product for your bike if you want a USB charging system, it's a great tool for anyone tinkering with 12v systems. In my car, I wanted to add a USB charging port that wasn't connected to my car's Android Auto system, for those moments that I just want to charge but not invoke AA. This can easily be connected to any 12V line (I spliced behind the DC port) and mounted it inside a storage bay. The LED display is a nice addition because it can tell you how the battery is doing (to avoid running it down) as well as help diagnose things like alternator issues and overall electrical health.

title: Does what it should
text: There isn't much to say about these other than they are exactly what I wanted and expected them to be. If you've ever used a microfiber cleaning cloth, they are great for their absorbency on things like oily car parts as well as for polish and buffing the exterior. This is all of that, in a cool grey and blue design pattern. They're great to have around the house too, don't think these are limited to car use! This comes in a pack that is very useful to have around.

title: Excellent all purpose mats
text:
I love how easily these cut to fit different types of cars! I picked up a used Toyota Solara this year as a fixer-upper project, and of course it didn't come with any of the factory mats. While it would be great to get the oem floor mats, Toyota hasn't made this car in over 13 years and it's something of a cult following. I can't justify the hiked up prices from those who've hoarded them. So, enter this product! This looks a lot better than my other "universal fit" mat, since the lines can be easily scored and torn off for a more factory looking fit.
Sure, you can tell it's aftermarket, but it actually looks pretty respectably cool! And easier to clean since it isn't carpeted. I might do this for another car that has mats that aren't holding up so well to time!

title: Not as tight of a fit as original
text:
First off- these bulbs are great for energy efficiency and brightness compared to the stock tungsten bulbs. My car is a 2nd generation Toyota Solara, and both of my brake lights were burnt out so I intended to use these to replace both left and right sides. Here's the problem- the bulb went it easily enough and I tested to confirm it worked (it did), but when I went to put the fixture back into the socket hole, the bulb FELL OUT and into my tail light assembly. Getting it out was a royal pain that involved lining a hanger with double sided tape and about 20 minutes of cursing.
When I finally got it out, I realized the problem right away- putting it back in the fixture, you can actually feel there's almost no resistance keeping it in place. The original bulb must have been a hair thicker or something because it took some force to get out, whereas this one practically falls out with gravity.
Luckily I had my roll of double sided tape handy from fishing it out of the tail light assembly, so I just wrapped a layer or two around the lower part of the body and snuggly fastened it in. I went for a drive and so far it's holding in place and working fine, but I'm a little annoyed that it didn't fit properly out of the box.

title: Perfect for my 2010 Odyssey!
text: We lost our "good fob" years ago and have been dealing with one that lost the back on our spare key. I read online that you can actually program additional fobs as long as you have at least one working key, so I decided to give this a shot. Wow, I wish I had known how easy it was a year ago! Everything works as it should once you follow the instructions to pair it with the vehicle. I can't say it has the range of the original, but I have not really scientifically tested the range either. I'd say its a great value for someone like me!

title: Great concept, snapped a cord on first use though.
text:
I love the concept of this as it traps moisture and heat OUTSIDE the car. In the summer I want to keep the sunlight from baking my phone holder on the windshield, which shields inside the car can't do properly. And my convertible roof top sometimes leaks around the window during heavy rain, so having this helps that as well.
HOWEVER, when I went to pull the cords to attach to the car, one of them snapped on the first usage. Very unimpressed with the quality there. I am able to stitch it back on, but I should have to do that on the very first try. Maybe I was just unlucky, but it shouldn't have happened.

title: Great for avoiding accidents
text: My daughter just got her learning permit to drive, and these stickers are FANTASTIC for alerting other drivers to keep a safe distance. I like that there are 3 in the set, and that they are magnetic for easy removal. They stay on pretty well, too! I'm so glad they aren't bumper stickers like back in my days of driving. No adhesive to clean up after. They are bright reflective material, great for ensuring visibility, motorists are sure to notice it. I might just leave it on after she gets her license so that other drivers avoid me for accidents!

title: Like new
text:
I bought my Solara with some minor damage on the hood that included a cracked trim piece here. It was held together with tape.
I'm really happy to say, I was able to remove it pretty easily and this even came with the replacement bolts to re-assemble it all. I had saved the original hardware in case I needed to reuse it, but it wasn't even necessary. Really happy with this product and my Solara looks like new now!

title: Great tool, a little hard for a prosumer
text:
This is essentially an Android based scan tool with some advanced features. I have 2 vehicles I consider "project cars" that need me to keep an eye on the engine lights. I've been using a bluetooth OBDii reader and an app on my phone to keep tabs on it for emissions passing and other self diagnosis, but the tools are limited and sometimes I find that I wish I had a more pro tool like the garages use.
Well, this is DEFINITELY a step up, I was especially interested in seeing the CEL freeze frame data to diagnose an exhaust issue, which it claims to have and I was unable to get on my phone's software. It also has some paid add ons that might be useful if you're running a garage, such as being able to reset maintenance lights and things that normal generic reader tools don't have access to.
The device itself is pretty well built- I was amused to see it's actually an skinned Android tablet underneath it all, which sort of made me realize it was essentially what I already was doing with my bluetooth OBDii and my phone, except this had more advanced software. But no matter- I kind of liked that I was already familiar with how to set up the wifi network connectivity to download updates and whatnot since it worked the same way as my phone. And it's definitely more durable and built to be handled the way you might expect in a mechanic situation (no "oops, I dropped my phone!"). I was able to look at some live graph data and see various system codes and information on my car, but the truth is, I found it rather difficult to set up and figure out how to make it all work. When connected to my car, I needed to select a lot of information I didn't know with terms I was not familiar with (like, what kind of Toyota interface this is connected with... I still don't really understand the options presented, but I kept picking them one by one until one worked). And while I was able to read codes and live data and all the things that one might want to do to diagnose a problem, the one thing I really wanted (freeze frame data from the CEL moment) I was unable to find. I even facetimed with a mechanic friend across the country and he wasn't able to guide me through it either.
I'm sure this is a super powerful tool to someone who knows how to use all the ins-and-outs of it, but I had some difficulty figuring out how to do anything that I couldn't already do with my phone and bluetooth OBDii reader. For the price of this being an all-in-one unit, I'd say the feature set is pretty solid. But it's not terribly user friendly for the home mechanic.

title: Didn't fit my car, but they work and comes with a tool!
text:
Ok, so for the purpose of this review I had to test it in someone else's car because Amazon made a mistake and claimed this was compatible with my dome light. My car (2004 Toyota Solara convertible) has a cloth roof with no overhead light, so the "dome" light is a courtesy light off to the side. Amazon said this bulb would fit a 2004 Solara dome light, but I think it was talking about a non-convertible one, as this did not fit at all. Wrong harness type, the convertible's dome uses the same light as their trunk. So double check compatibility first.
Meanwhile, this is a common size 41mm long bulb that fits in many other cars, so I tried it in a friends' car just to make sure it turns on and works properly. It's bright, and its NOT yellow (6000k is closer to blue), which is cool if you want to upgrade your lights' look to something more matching sunlight instead of faded yellow.
I also really like that it came with a plastic pry tool to take off the light covers! I've always had to grab a screwdriver for changing mine, so this was very welcome indeed!

title: WHITE and bright!
text: I installed these in my 2004 Solara convertible. The bulb fit in both the trunk and the side courtesy dome light. They are brighter than the original halogen bulbs and use less power, which I really like! Just be aware that they are on the white/blue spectrum (6000 kelvin in color) which is closer to sunlight in color vs the yellow tungsten look (2700k). So you'll want all your bulbs to match otherwise you'll have yellow lights in some places and blueish in others, which is what I have now. Gotta go replace my front map lights now!

title: Not too shabby for a universal fit in a coupe!
text:
[[VIDEOID:a68122049b51355a153b00abfb10b2ac]] I have a car that is pretty difficult to get seat covers for. A 2004 Toyota Solara convertible, it isn't popular enough that people make custom fit covers and it's old enough that the original cloth is wearing and fading in the sun. I was excited to try this set because I noticed the zippered rear bench. You see, most rear benches in vehicles are 3 seats, and they're almost always impossible to fit correctly with a universal kit. My coupe is a 2-seater in the back. So, problem, right?
Well, I'm happy to say that using the zipper system I was able to remove the middle part and just zip the left and right side to each other! Now it fits much better. Honestly, I've never see a universal kit fit well in the back so I wasn't expecting this to work at all, but this actually isn't bad!
It's not perfect, but for a universal, color me impressed. One thing I really don't like, however, are the headrests. That might just also be a side effect of all universal seat covers, but I really don't like the way these look covered. Sort of looks like a pillow. But I'm so happy about the back that I'll live with it for now.

title: Kind of heavy but it works
text:
I have an older convertible Toyota Solara that I want to protect from the elements during harsh weather. This is a great option, however I noticed two concerns:
1) It's heavy. This is a GOOD thing for most cars, as the thick material will really help protect it! But the down side for a convertible top is that you're adding weight to the most delicate part of the car body. This is a con that mostly pertains to me, admittedly, and a regular car / suv won't have this issue.
2) If you have a stick-up antenna for your radio, you'll have to remove it for the top to work properly. Not a problem on more modern cars with internal antennae, but if you're trying to protect an older or classic car with a stick up antenna, that's something to be aware of as well.
Otherwise, seems like a solid product that does what it claims to!

title: I like the idea, but it comes creased
text: I wanted to give my steering wheel a better grip and modernize the look a little on an old car. This would work in theory, however it comes folded up from the factory, and you have to really work at it to pull tight over your steering wheel. The difficulty putting it on is somewhat expected, however the fact that it comes folded means the plastic area is creased from being bent before you even get to use it. I was hoping it would stretch out and the creases would disappear after a few days, but it is still there. Feels bad when a new product already looks worn. It works and serves the purpose, but I sort of feel like I'd have a better experience picking one of these up from a local automotive or box store, where they store them for display already open in a circle.

title: Exactly what I needed
text:
I'm fixing up a project car and have been using disposable paper towels. Disposable is nice because clean up means throwing it away, but it's also wasteful and not soft like this. This is much more absorbent for pesky fluids like motor oil, makes it easy to clean off after working on the car and the shammy sops up spills before they spread. Nice.
This is exactly what I wanted and expected it to be.

title: Good if you don't want full wheel coverage
text:
I like the texture of these, it has a soft fabric yet rubbery sort of feel to it that I wasn't expecting and is actually kind of pleasant. The quality control is OK, I did notice that the grips inside were falling off the adhesive when I took it out. Once you install it on the wheel, that doesn't matter anymore however.
What I did realize, though, is that I actually want something that covers more of the steering wheel than just the sides. My vehicle is old and the sun has started to wear the top of the wheel through the windshield, and while I just wanted to make the wheel grippier/add some aesthetic to it, I now realize I would prefer something that would cover the entire wheel instead. If you don't need that, this is a fine addition to your car's look that will add some much needed texture and grip. But it's not necessarily for everyone.

title: "Meet you is our happinest thing!"
text:
I don't know what a happinest is, but kudos to this brand for making up a fun new word! Seriously guys, can you hire a copywriter next time? lol
That being said, it's exactly what I wanted to keep my car cool in the heat of parking in the sun. My dashboard gets scorching hot, and this helps deflect the sun enough to keep it from overheating things like my wireless charger before I can even make it into the car. It is a little bit bigger than I needed, but I ordered it large on purpose- I wanted it to cover a little of the window space as well to block some side sunlight as well. It folds up easily and fits into the oddly written slogan tote bag. Points for doing what it claims to do, but minus a star for such lack of quality control they can't even print proper wording. Like, why even write anything at all? It would have infused me with 1000x more confidence in their product quality if they just left the text on the bag out. By branding it they actually cheapened it. But it works, so I can't complain that much.

title: Helps a little
text: I used it in my car to help with a musty smell, and it seems to have made an improvement. However it looks like when it arrived some of the powder leaked into the packaging, which makes me a little uneasy about leaving it in places it might get on the fabric. I guess 3 stars for doing what it says, but at the end of the day I'm probably still going to hit my car with a Ozone generator or something to clear it out. Probably good for more casual space application.

title: Great upgrade
text:
I picked up a used car that didn't really have license plate holders, especially not on the front. Just holes in the bumper, which looked surprisingly naked with just a plate bolted on. All my other cars have at least had a plastic shield or something that the plate attaches to as a border.
These are great because they outline the plate and thanks to the silicone rubber, they actually help protect the car from scratches and scuffs too! And unlike the plastic shields I'm used to, it won't crack or rattle with age either. They are a cheap and easy way to improve a bare plate.

title: This product confuses me.
text:
I use my vehicle for side-gig work as a vendor sometimes, and I like the idea of there being a magnetic sign I can slap on to brand my car. But when I got this, there was no information as to how one prints with this. It's kind of large and thick for a standard printer, and I didn't want to break mine trying. I'd think there would be SOME sort of paperwork or instructions or even suggestions re: how to use this, but nope. Nothing.
Meanwhile, the information I AM seeing on the box is just some advertising copy re: use as a vent cover for your HVAC. So now I'm confused, is it a vent cover? Is it a car sign? Is it both? Why is there no instructions or information as to how to use this the way they advertise?
I'm giving it three stars because it DOES work as a vent cover (I tried it) and that is apparently ONE of the things it claims to do. But as a magnetic sign, I just don't get. Or why one product is trying to be both of those things.

title: Excellent for DIY modifications to your car
text: I installed a backup camera and custom stereo on my old Toyota, and without this set it would have been a LOT harder! Previously I had used flathead screwdrivers which scratched up the finish, or guitar pics which broke or didn't have enough leverage to pop the harder pins, but this set has everything I needed and then some! I even appreciated the little gloves it came with, very handy when the plastic fairings want to FIGHT YOU to come loose. I've scratched up my hands before on another car from those things, so the gloves were welcome to help protect them. If you want to tinker around in your car, this set is a necessity!

title: AWESOME
text: This is wonderful to have around the garage. I not only own cars, bikes and mopeds, I have a tractor that is constantly losing air in between uses on my lawn.  Until this unit, I've been using a DC powered electric pump to check the air and top off my tires, but that means you need to be close to a car or other suitable 12v outlet. This actually can be powered both externally OR with the internal rechargeable battery.  Being able to carry it around and use it wirelessly opens up all kinds of possibilities, using it on a bike tire, or using the included attachments to inflate an air mattress while camping for example. I'm very impressed with this product, it really is easy to use and seems quite accurate in the psi reading!

title: They're OK
text:
The mat material isn't quite what I expected- it's more carpet than I'm used to, which is soft and comfy but looks a little out of place on the floor of my car. I know universal-fit mats aren't going to look OEM, but I guess I expected these to be a little bigger, too. They seem kind of puny in my Camry/Solara car. It's a functional size, don't get me wrong, and better than nothing (I bought this car used with no mats included).
It's ok for what it is, but I feel like I could have gotten something a little bit better.

title: Perfect replacement for our Radio Flyer car
text: We lost the 12v charger for our Radio Flyer "Riptide" car, much to my son's dismay. Thankfully we found this replacement on Amazon and it came the next day! I'm so pleased with this, works as well as the original, and the price was more than manageable!

title: A good fit for my moped as well as motorcycle
text: This is a decent inexpensive way to protect your bike from dust and the elements. I found that it also works well for my moped/scooter, as mine is an oversized 2-seater GY6 that doesn't fit under small motorcycle covers. The XXL size of this really helps keep everything covered well from head to toe. However, I have to admit this is my 3rd off-brand cover from Amazon with an all-caps name that appears to be straight off the boat from China. They usually last about 2 years in my experience so far, so I'm not expecting this to protect my bike for more than a couple of seasons before it gets worn out and starts to develop rips.

title: Great rear view for all kinds of vehicles!
text:
I've got a 150cc scooter with plain awful rear view mirrors. Getting the left one at the correct angle to see properly (pretty important) is an exercise in futility. I decided to try these clamp on mirrors, and it turns out these are JUST what I needed!
Not only do they attach to standard sized handlebars pretty well, I can use them on some of our bikes as well! My wife has a vintage adult tricycle with an attachment for a tandem bike for our 3 year old on the back. Clamping one of these ads a very much needed way for her to keep an eye on the little one trailing behind her. Just a really great and useful product for all kinds of motorized and pedaled vehicles!

title: SO USEFUL!
text: My minivan occasionally has slow tire leaks thanks to potholes and changing weather in the east coast. This little device has already come in useful as a couple of days ago, the dash light came on for low tire pressure. We had an older one that uses the car's DC lighter jack to power itself, but reaching that to all 4 tires on a minivan was a chore. This device has two MAJOR advantages: 1) It is battery powered and does not need to be plugged in to work, and 2) It has an automatic shutoff! So no more watching and waiting for it to get up the correct psi, you can actually set it at the desired level (32, for example) and it will run itself until the level is reached and then shut off. It makes using this practically fool proof! Very impressed and it's already saved us a trip to the gas station to correct the pressure!

title: Great for protecting your outdoor vehicles!
text: There isn't much to say about this weather cover, which is a good thing! It does exactly what it claims to do- protect your quads from the elements when stored outside. Unlike a model-specific cover I used previously, I like that this is a more universal fit so you can use it for many different brands, or even different kinds of vehicles! Like others mentioned in their reviews, you can use this for a ride on mower, or two smaller motorcycles / scooters side-by-side. Maybe even a bunch of bicycles that are stored outside if you have a large family. It is a versatile tool and worth the price in my opinion!

title: This is a mood!
text: I have put a custom entertainment system (video game / digital video player) in our minivan, and these lights are the perfect accent to it. Makes long road trips into a veritable party experience, sort of like a Dave & Buster's on wheels! title: Doesn't clear water very well on passenger side.
text:
I got this to replace my passenger side wiper after replacing the driver's side one, so that they would match. The funny thing is, the driver's side one (a larger blade) of the same brand seems to be working fine so far. But this one seems to leave a lot of streaks and almost seems as if it is missing the glass. I'm not sure if it is just because it is a smaller size for the passenger or if the driver's one will start doing this soon as well.
I do like that it has an indicator that fades over time with UV light to tell you it needs to be changed. But honestly, if it doesn't work to clear water off during the first week, I don't know if I'll ever get to see how that indicator works. Not very impressed with it.

title: A bit more contoured but fits.
text:
I put this on my Mazda3 which lately has been chewing through wiper blades (the offset of the blade was misaligned and it would collide with the frame of the windshield, ruining the edge of the wiper). So far so good, and I adjusted the arm's offset so it wouldn't hit the frame anymore. Hoping it will last longer than the last set did.
I like that it has an indicator to tell you when it has worn (changes color with UV light exposure, or so it claims) so you don't forgot to change them when on for too long, but I'm not sure so far if this will hold up as well as my others have. It doesn't seem to have the same sort of reinforcement mechanism that other blades have, relying instead of the curve of the blade to hug the windshield. But I'll see how it goes. So far, it is functional.

title: Fits my scooter perfectly!
text:
My 150cc scooter needs to be parked outside for the summer, so naturally I need a good cover for it. My old cover started to rip and leak, so the opportunity to try this one came just in time.
The challenge is often finding a cover that will fill a scooter style vehicle- motorcycle covers are often either too small in some areas, or far too large overall (touring bike covers) and end up flopping around in the wind and blowing itself off. This one seems to not only fit large motorcycles, but also fits very well on my scooter without being too large. It stayed on during a particularly windy storm last week, where other covers (such as my riding mower) let up and blew away, and it seems to keep it perfectly dry so far from the rain. Seems like one of the more versatile bike covers out there.

title: Works with my Honda rails, but you need to WORK at it!
text:
We have a box that used to fit on a Thule-brand roof rack system for our old car, but it never worked with the factory rail system on our 2010 Honda Odyssey. This universal kit works great, however! I don't even miss the Thule rails. They hold on tight and I can now attach our cargo box or other accessories to the roof of the minivan. It does create some wind noise, but that's expected with any non-OEM rack/bar, so you'll probably want to take them off when not using them.
But that leads me to my one pet peeve and why I can only give this 4 stars- it requires a lot of arm work twisting a hex wrench (tool included) to tighten and loosen the bar clamps. Our old system went on quickly by hand and only needed a couple of turns to tighten afterwards, whereas this might have your arm sore after 10 minutes of manually twisting a hex screw. I might consider putting a properly sized hex bit on my drill next time! That being said the lock system is pretty neat- each corner has a lock that covers the hole to reach the hex screw, and it only unlocks when the key is in place (and can't be removed until locked again). This prevents accidentally leaving it unlocked as well as accidentally losing the key, however if one does actually lose the key I'd imagine this would be pretty annoying to remove.
All in all, a good value for the money if you want to add some cross bars to your vehicle.

title: Works fine.
text:
Does the job- but the LED light doesn't do what I expected. I would have thought it would alert me that everything is connected and working, but it comes on as soon as I plug the clips into the battery (whether or not the plug is in the wall). Conversely, I believe it would come on if the plug is in the wall, but the alligator clips aren't on the battery. So basically, the light is on whether it is actually connected and doing something or not!

I could imagine this being a problem if one were to clip onto the battery but forget the plug into the wall (or in the case of my garage, be on a circuit that was off because it is attached to a light switch), see the LED and think things are fine. In reality, one could come back and find that the battery drained powering this silly LED instead of keeping the charge topped off!

Otherwise, it seems to work well enough.

title: Makes DIY body work a breeze
text:
My 86' 4Runner has a LOT of rust that I've been slowly addressing. When filling a large hole in a body panel this fiberglass cloth works perfectly. It's a nice thick weave that holds up well to resin and draping over large gaps.

I like to cut it into 2 inch strips to work with. First I brush the inside of the hole with 2 part resin and stuff a bit of the fiberglass cloth into the hole, pressing it into the back of the opening to engage with the resin I've brushed there. Then I brush a strip of fiberglass cloth at a time with resin and press it over the opening and into the existing fiberglass cloth making sure it is adhering to the area on the body around the hole. I build up layer after layer criss crossing until I have several woven layers adding resin directly to the cloth if necessary to join them together or join them to the body panel. Don't worry about adding to much, you can always sand it back after it's hardened. Then go over with bondo to make a smooth surface ready for primer.

title: Buyyyyyyy it! And spend 20 minutes installing.
text:
This is for 2019 Tiguan S - each side of the back of the vehicle has a set of two one inch screws with wide caps and one half inch screw with head as large as the screw part (that's the under screw). each side of the front of the vehicle has two one inch screws, one on the bottom, one in the wheel well. These are the ones you need to be concerned with.

Back flaps - When installing, the back flaps have I believe total of five holes. Two match perfectly with the wheel well screws, and the other is a hole on an extension piece that matches with the bottom plastic OEM screw. The recommended install (at least for me) is to use the OEM wheel well screws, but then, for the bottom one "steal" one of the front wheel well screws (trust me, it's ok). This will peg the back - another reviewer posted that he used the middle screw as first then worked the others - great advice! What about the additional two holes in the mud flaps? I believe, if you are so inclined, you can use those in conjunction with the provided retaining screw clips and two of the screws that came along in the package. Just as a safety measure - up to you.

Front flaps - first off, the front ones do not fit as well as the back, reason being that on the bottom, the screw is recessed so the flaps have indentation to fill that recess - in this case, it doesn't work totally well. The front flaps have three (3) holes. But as you know from before, there are only two (2) "interesting" OEM holes - one that matches the middle mudflap's hole, and the other the bottom. This is where the provided retaining clips come in super handy. Use a silver marker to mark where the top mud flap's hole matches with the body then set a retaining clip there. You don't have to pre-drill, plastic is soft, so use one of the inch and a half (pretty sturdy) screws that come in the package there. Use ANOTHER of the inch and a half provided screws on the BOTTOM hole (see? i told you it'll be ok) - that's it, the fronts will be pinned in perfectly well.

End of day a more functional add on I can't think of. One star off for front flaps not matching magically like the back ones. But totally worth the purchase!!!

Tools used:
1x small T-25 bit (for the one inch OEM screws)
1x small T-15 bit (for the weird little "bullet plastic OEM screw from the back's bottom holes)
1x narrow profile ratchet wrench w/ narrow profile bit holder (remember you can always turn the front wheels either way to give yourself more room to work)
1x silver tipped permanent marker (to mark the front wheel well
1x Phillips #2 tip screwdriver, six inches or whatever (since you can turn the wheels)

title: Works really well but the gauge is off
text:
Every time when the seasons turn, my cars tires have the wrong air pressure. Obviously every one else has the same problem and the lines at the air pumps are always long. I have a regular air pump but that one is always a pain to use so I figured why not get one of these portable ones, since you never know when you need to adjust the air pressure while on the road? So I settled on this one, I figured getting the cheapest one is not a good idea and digital would be a good idea.

This one is very simple to use, although I admit I couldn’t get the units to switch yet the one time I used it. But in my defense I didn’t have my glasses with me and couldn’t read the tine, very short instructions. I will get it done next time and thank you online I could figure out how to convert it. Plus my car has sensors so with those I could figure out when to stop adding air to them. So you just connect the pump to your cigarette charger, connect the pump to your tired, set the goal tire pressure and off you go, hit start. I found though that the sensor in my car and the sensor in this pump is not in agreement, and I trust my car sensor a lot more. This pump gauge is quite off to be honest and way under measures the air pressure, if you would follow what it says you would add way too much air to the tires.

But as long as your car has a sensor it is not a big deal. I did like that you can connect it all, then sit in your car and just wait until it is done. My target PSI was 36, and my car was at about 28 to 30 PSI for each tire and it took me about 20 minutes to do all the tires, so not too bad all considering I could just sit in my car while it was doing everything and watch the pressure go up.

They said they would send me a new circuit board. GUESS WHAT  they never did and the customer service guy that I waited over an hour to talk to was also very cocky and rude. title: BUYER BEWARE
text:
I am an experienced Vinyl Wrap installer and I figured I'd tackle the challenge of your run-of-the-mill Chinese vinyl films. Let me start of by saying this film is THICK, thus making it extremely unpliable in contoured surfaces. This film will lay DECENTLY on flat surfaces but you will suffer through all of this Earth's wrath if you tried to tackle curved surfaces even with heat; that of which you must also consider because if you heat this up for more than 3 seconds, it will warp the ever-living hell out of the film and it will ruin the finish.

Not only this, but the adhesion is absolutely TERRIBLE even in a temperature-regulated environment. This alone is a solid reason for you to NOT buy this. If you buy this film, there will come a time where you will regret it. You may think that it's some solid bang for your buck especially with some convincing pictures floating around, but remember that YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR. Vinyl Wraps is one of those things you just can't cheap out on, no matter how good the deal may be, it's for a reason and one reason alone: it's TRASH.

You have been warned...

I found mine at one of the large home improvement stores (initials HD), after being told by a clerk (sorry, I mean "associate") that they did not carry anything suitable to store fishing tackle in. title: Already put mine to good use twice!
text:
Boy, these are just great! I bought two, back in November. One for hubby's car, one for mine. I got caught on icy mountain roads shortly after mine arrived and had to call a tow truck. I had my FlareAlert in the trunk of the car and had to slip-slide my way around to fetch it and one of my hazard sticks. Well that taught me a lesson to always have it within arm's reach, so I don't necessarily have to exit the vehicle to put it to use. It's not always safe to be walking around outside. When on a freeway with a lot of traffic going by, it's best not to get out at all. And, in this case with the ice and all, the car could have started sliding backwards on the ice, while I fiddled around in the trunk, or I could have slipped and hurt myself just groping my way to the back of the car and back.

The second time I used it was in March when my car's power steering pump gave out on a long drive home from Toronto. This happened on a busy freeway, at night in the dark. This time I had the FlareAlert nearby and never got out of the car. I switched it on flashing mode and stuck it on top of the car and waited for the tow truck I then called.

Both times I told the tow truck drivers that I would have the flashing red light on my car. When asked if the light was easily visible, they both enthusiastically told me that they could see it from way far away and that it really helped to know to look for it. Usually they tend to have to drive more slowly, trying to locate where the distressed car is - especially at night. Both occurrences happened at night.

The FlareAlert is well built of very nice, solid plastic. It releases the light very strongly and clearly. The magnet on it is so strong that I have to be careful not to store any electronics near it. Hard drives and memory cards might not react favorably in its proximity...

All in all, I am really happy I got this useful gadget and pleased with the way it performs and the service it has already rendered. Everyone should have one nearby in their car. It could be a real life saver! It will definitely save your car's battery while keeping you visible if you are stranded. No need to leave your flashers on if you are concerned about draining your battery (i.e.: if you have to turn your engine off - as I had to do or my car would have overheated). I may get a second one for myself, as I recall worrying that other cars passing by may not see the outer side of my black car at night. I could reach over the passenger seat and put one outside on that side too. Even if it's only attached to the door on that side, it would still give the passing vehicles a better idea as to my car's physical whereabouts. Safer yet that way... Also am keeping some additional batteries on hand - just in case.

I recommend this product highly! And I know this whole review sounds a bit like an infomercial, but I am actually in no way affiliated with either the product manufacturers, distributors, or vendors. I just really feel enthusiastic about the usefulness of the product, having had the (unfortunate) occasion to put it to use twice now. Hope you all stay safe - with or without it. :)

title: Better then Lexol
text:
I bought my tan leather couches 15 years ago. The "leather protection set" that I was provided on at the time of purchasing was to "extend the life and beauty of your leather, if used as directed".
As I had a substantial amount of money invested in my purchase, I literally marked it on my calender to do the cleaning and conditioning as advised. I was never happy with the results. I contacted the furniture store after the first use to let them know. They sent out their "leather specialist" to make an observation of my results.
The "leather specialist" told me my leather furniture looked exactly how it should following the complete treatment and that I "had done a very good and thourough job and at the rate you're committed to the leather product, your leather should remain beautiful for years to come".
I didn't buy what he had to say. I allowed a few more weeks to pass to see if the treatment absorbed and looked better. It didn't. So I sought out to find a leather product I may be happier with. I came upon Lexol leather products online and read all the extremely high consumer ratings and comments. I purchased the Lexol line and wasn't much happier with it's performance vs. the products from my leather store, but I decided that perhaps my expectations were too high.
I continued to regularly use the Lexol products as recommended and in the meantime the economy went to s*** and my son, wife and their 4 month old baby were forced to move in with us.
4 years later I have continued to use the Lexol products but have assumed my leather's aging process had been accelerated by my precious grandson - needless to say a toddler can be any furniture's nightmare and potential demise.
I ran out of Lexol and decided to search again for a leather cleaner that might be able to tackle a toddler's creations (spilled milk, urine, fruit juices of all kinds, and food to name just a few). I came cross the claims for Glacier Leather CLEANER and read the glowing reviews and thought "WTH do I have to lose"? I received it in an incredibly fast time. In my infinite wisdom and research, I decided to use nebsfoot oil (100%) as it was highly recommended also for the leather conditioning portion.
Results - the Glacier cleaner went WAY beyond my expectations. I wish I'd have had this to use since the first treatment that I did on my leather. I can thank the Glacier company for helping the beauty of the leather be restored as much as reasonably possible and now I don't have to go out looking for a new furniture suite!
Whatever you do, stay away from the (100%) nebsfoot oil. Totally not what I expected. It must be for professionals who totally restore saddles or delapidated leather bought at a garage sale of which anything would make the leather look better.
The Glacier Leather company personally reached out to me when I responded to their inquiry as to the products performance. They have offered to send me complimentary conditioner that they sell since I didn't like the Nebsfoot oil. As soon as I have tried it I will write a review.
I'm VERY hopeful their conditioner is as good as their leather cleaner.

Note: I wasn't compensated in any way for this review. I am however open to Glacier sending me a complimentary lifetime supply of it's leather cleaner!

title: Worked For My 2010 Mini Clubman S
text:
I bought 2 cans and so I will try to do a follow up after I use the second one.

The Patient: 2010 Mini Clubman S (automatic) with 135k miles. This is a 4 popper, turbo charged with DI.

Symptoms: slight idle fluctuations (at stop lights, traffic jams, et al). Nothing too serious and never close to a stall but enough to realize it wasn't random. Also, slight hesitation when pressing (not punching) the gas from a stop and getting the car to react. We're talking milliseconds but I'm familiar enough with the car that I could tell it was just a little slower to react.

Treatment: I always use premium gas & regular fully synthetic oil changes as specified by Mini. So I ran the gas tank down until the fuel light turned red as kept driving until I had probably less than 1 gallon. Poured entire contents of one bottle in gas tank. Filled it, as usual, with premium. Put about 500 miles on car (80% highway speeds, the rest stop-n-go city). Re-filled with tank with premium gas but did NOT add second 16oz can of Gum Out MSTU.

Initial Results: Idle fluctuations definitely reduced. No question. Hesitation when I press (not punch) the gas is slightly better. The car reaction has always been and still is "Instant On" when I punch the gas. I was looking to improve the more gradual start from a stop hesitation issue. It had NO effect on a my MPG. I usually get 38+ on the highway (70mph on crusie) and 28 in the city. That did not change. But I already get better than advertised 26c/34h so I was not expecting it to improve. But some users said their MPG dropped.

Opinion: For my situation, it worked. Idle is clearly smoother and more consistent. I did not inspect the pistons or injectors before or after, so I can only assume the injectors were mildly clogged and this opened them up. So Gum Out MSTU seemed to do the trick.

Next Step: Will add second can on next fill-up and report back.

Overall, I would not hesitate (see what I did there?) to use this product again based on just one result.

If you go into the process understanding that it may be very hard to get the blower motor cover off, you will be able to manage your anger at such a poor design much better. :-) Your mileage may vary and it is dependent on the model of vehicle you have.

UPDATE: I failed to mention (as others have noted) that this specific blower was wired BACKWARDS. So if you install it and it's wired backwards, it will work but you won't get any airflow from the vents. Easy fix if you are handy with Wiring 101.

Now, this is easily over come by using the second chenille mitt or the sponge and hand washing the aforementioned areas or simple remove the first mitt from the pole attachment. This is easily removed via the draw string. Be aware of the plastic draw string retainer clamp. You would not want that banging into your vehicle.

Overall, I’m satisfied with job it did. It was effective and efficient. Now putting everything in the bag after use will not occurs until you dry out the mitt and sponge. Getting things back in was tight…this was minus the duster and expected since the sponge comes vacuum sealed.

It may be enough to awaken some jackhole from his stupor of texting and driving just in time to notice you are broken down and stopped. I highly recommend these.

I have had a set very much like these except my old set uses alkaline batteries. We all know what happens to old batteries after they sit around too long. The item gets ruined from battery acid leaking out. These are much better. They have rechargeable batteries. This type of battery should not leak and cause any issues.

I like having these in case of emergency. They are easy to attach to the car with the magnetic base. They give your stalled car much more visibility and a much greater chance of you not getting run into. These can be placed on the ground, well behind your vehicle, and also on your vehicle.

They come with a decent zippered carry case which just happens to fit in my driver's door storage area. I have them all charged and ready. I can also recharge them in my car, which is a bonus.

The one odd thing I found was that the charging cable only had three ends. Why not four? so I could charge them all at once? It must have been a way to save a few pennies. I might suggest that the maker starts sending cables with four ends instead of only three.

Overall, I am happy to have these and do keep them in my vehicle.

The bleeder valve is handy if you need to let out some air. The pressure reading is held on the gauge until you release the bleeder valve.

Or at least that was what he said 4 or 5 years ago when he pulled it into the backyard. I personally believe it is an eyesore, but part of marriage (26 years) is compromising. He gets his car, which he feels is worth keeping and I order paint-by-numbers projects and drink wine while I do them. Everyone needs a hobby!

Over the past few years, I have purchased or received several car covers. Either the weather (sun, wind, rain) has destroyed them or falling limbs. So when offered the Bestek car cover for an honest review, I did not hesitate. It is made from a light silver, lightweight, reflective material that is wind, rain, scratch and tear proof (only time will tell if this is true - so far so good). It fits securely over the entire vehicle (there are even belts to help secure it to the wheels) and reflectors (I guess if the vehicle is in motion, being pulled at night). There are two other features that make this a must have: cut outs for the mirrors (versus just fitting over the entire car) and (2) you can still get inside or open the vehicle doors, via a side zipper flap, without having to remove the entire cover. Wow!! That is convenient. And finally, there is also a convenient storage bag, although I am not sure that I see the importance of the bag - how often do you remove a cover and fold it back up, placing it inside a bag? Not often, but it is a nice feature.

Overall, this is a decent cover that works!

text:
My husband has a 1999 Volvo that he loves. It had over 400k miles when the odometer stopped turning. The lights in the dash don’t work anymore and it definitely needs some cosmetic work. But he still loves it. And while he doesn’t drive it on a regular basis, he occasionally cranks it up and drives it around the neighborhood remembering the wonderful times that they had. So, it should be no surprise that the sun has damaged the paint. When I ordered this product (for a honest review), I thought that it would be a miracle worker. We expected this product to bring “Jessie” (that’s what I call her) back to her former glory. I think that was a bit ambitious. The Wax Shop’s Rebuild 2000 Medium Cut Compound didn’t restore Jessie to her former glory. Instead it fills in small scratches from the body of our newer cars, where the paint isn’t as damaged.

The instructions suggest that you apply small amounts before removing with a buffer. We used a small pad and spot corrected small scratches (you know the kind you get from people while parked at the grocery store, maybe from shopping carts, or other annoying imperfections). And while this product really didn’t help Jessie (lol, there is way too much sun damage), it does the trick on newer model cars. We are a four car household. The colors of the car are blue, red, gray and beige and this rebuild compound works well on each of the colors. A small amount improves very superficial scratches. So for under $35, you get a pretty decent product that corrects minor imperfections. I’d suggest those who are in the car restoration business give this product a try.

Two reasons this is a 4-star product:

2) On my 1998 S10 these do not work as daytime running lights like the halogens. title: Works great on 2007 Civic EX Coupe
text:
Very good kit. The spindle washers/shims provided in the kit were the inner/outer diameter as the factory spindle washers. I ended up re-using both of the Honda retaining rings as the ones that came with this kit were thinner gauge and introduced too much play. Everything else appeared to be machined well.

If you do this job, you will need a quality set of long nose snap ring pliers with small tips (0.045” - 0.05”.) This is the most frustrating part of the repair process but it will be made *significantly* easier if you take your time finding the correct pliers. Two more recommendations: remove the compressor mounting bolts so you have a better angle of approach. Use a small three arm gear puller to remove the old compressor pulley. Ok, one more- always check your compressor clutch relay in the fuse box. If it rattles, replace it.

title: Quantitatively brighter!
text:
Installed these in the fog lights of my 2009 Audi A4. Works perfectly without any error codes.

I work as a sales manager for one of the largest commercial LED luminaire manufacturers in the world. Even in commercial LED fixture manufacturing, lumen specifications are all over the map because there’s a lot of shady companies jumping on the LED bandwagon to make a quick buck. They play on the general public’s ignorance of LED tecnology to peddle inferior products that won’t do what they say they will (not as bright, shorter product life.) The aftermarket automotive LED industry seems to be especially dubious. There’s no standardized method for how the manufacturers calculate and list the lumen output of these types of bulbs, so comparisons based on specs are incredibly inaccurate. Bottom line- I got out the light meter and the Beamtech lux readings were about 40% higher than the halogens. That’s a substantial increase! Very pleased.

I’m impressed with the initial quality, fitment and light output. Would have preferred a 5000K color temperature option but a lot of manufacturers use 6000-7000K chips to boost their lumen specs on paper. Right now these LEDs make my factory xenons look too warm, so at some point I’ll upgrade those to something in the 5000-6000K range so it matches these fog lamps better.

Time will be real deciding factor of whether or not these are a quality product worthy of retaining the initial 5-Star rating. These are passively cooled but the heat sink is quite large. As long as the driver stays cool, I expect these to last for a few years.

title: Incredible customer support AND a strong jump start
text:
First, I experienced a very odd condition when turning the ignition key to the “Accessory” position on my Mercedes SUV where the Megawise unit would only give me one chance to raise the windows and fail. I had to unplug everything from the battery pack and essentially “reset” things.
So, I reached out to the supplier and they did some internal research and asked if they could send me another unit at no charge, and please accept their apologies for any difficulties or inconvenience. They were not clear what the root cause was but wanted to get another working device to me as quickly as possible.
Wow. How do we give a manufacturer a “10 star rating” for standing behind their product so strongly? I was pleasantly surprised and the replacement arrived quickly and work without any issues.
Now, this is one strong portable car starter - it provided multiple jumps on a Mercedes 3.2 Liter 6 cylinder engine with a completely dead H8 battery rated with 900 CCA! Granted, it was a 70 degree day and sunny day but this absolutely rocked my world! I was anticipating a call to AAA and the associated wait but figured nothing ventured, nothing gained!
I’m sold on this manufacturer from a support and product perspective and will be purchasing one of these units for every vehicle I own, as well as my adult children’s and their families. Charge retention is also excellent as I used this to jump my Volvo wagon needing a new battery and inspection. Strongly recommend!!!

These NGK are an extreme quality upgrade and typically last for 3 to 5 times as many miles as other brands with just minimal care and cleaning if even necessary. I run NGK in all my motorcycles and cars/SUV's - having just put 5 of these in my 1999 Volvo V70 along with new ignition coils.  (not a typo, yes 5)

title: Excellent replacement Ignition Coils for my 1999 Volvo V70 - fit and work perfectly
text:
My 1999 Volvo V70 with 240K+ miles was throwing DTC's for cylinders 3 & 5 and was not passing emissions for state inspection. I have an OBD II reader from Amazon that connects via Bluetooth to my phone with an app that reads the codes - the garage wanted to charge $129 to run similar diagnostics to tell me the same thing. Well, this Volvo V70 was a gift from my late father-in-law and had always been dealer maintained so I took a look at the Bosch parts and fainted. Looked around for quality parts with good reviews and found these and was pleased. They arrived the next day well protected and individually wrapped. FYI, they also include a small packet of dielectric grease if you don't already have some in your garage or shop so save yourself even more money with these great parts and excellent seller!! Read up on why and how to use the dielectric grease, please, it is worth it to save your spark plugs and these fine ignition coils. Also encourage you to replace the spark plugs, if your old/current ignition coils haven't been firing right your plugs are probably nasty and you've already taken off the cover and removed the ignition coil.
These fit perfectly, the ignition wires snap in place but your old plastic connectors may be brittle so handle gently when connecting to the wires of these new ignition coils. I am thrilled with the quality of the coils, how they were individually protected, and the fact the seller gives you a packet of dielectric grease for those who don't already have a tube of it. I do 99% of my own repairs so this seller is one I will always looks for replacement parts from.

title: Deal of the century and an amazing part!!
text:
I work on all my cars and motorcycles so for the most part an inexpensive part is just that. Except for this switch replacement, this is a quality part and an amazing value!!

It took less than 10 minutes to replace on my ML320. The process is simple, unscrew 2 bolts holding the console storage "bucket" and remove, pop the gear shift cover off with your fingers, use a body moulding tool or a wide and THIN screwdriver to work the wood paneling loose to remove. The only trick to this is you should put the parking brake ON to move the gear selector to N to take the wood placard out and gain access to the switch. Put back in P when you've removed it. The one component I could not detach was the cigarette lighter cable so had limited range of motion. I loosened the 4 tiny bolts holding the switches in place and then released the clips to remove. Label the wires you unclip to ensure you put them back correctly. Remove the old and non-functioning switches and snap in the new one. Install is the reverse.

Work slowly with the wood console cover, I can see margin for error and breaking it. Be sure to keep the key in the off position and gear selector in P. All this advice is from a competent shade tree mechanic, I'm not a pro. There are YouTube videos on how to do. Mechanical skills required to do yourself are bare minimum.

Again, this switch is a quality replacement part that I would say look no farther unless you want to drop hundreds more at the dealership. The mirrors worked, all windows as well, and the lighting at night. I am very thankful for the manufacturing company who made such a smooth operating replacement at a very reasonable cost. Don't think twice, buy now.

The tire iron is not as large as your tradition 4 spoke tire iron - you don't get as much torque for your effort but you're saving space.

And it rained the day after putting these blades on and they worked perfectly. Do yourself, and your bank balance, a favor and buy these quality blades.

title: Didn’t work right out of the box, and cost me a ton of money.
text: I was impressed with the build quality when I got this, or perhaps I should say the apparent build quality. I got a mobile RV tech to come out to install it and lo and behold it did not work. The default code didn’t work when it was installed. So we went through the code reset procedure and then the default code did work but the bolt didn’t work. You could hear the motor spinning inside the lock but the bolt didn’t move. After about 10 tries the probably counterfeit Duracell batteries died with a whimper, with no low battery notification like there is supposed to be. I then put some real batteries in but it didn’t make any difference.  My mobile RV tech charges a $90 visit fee plus his hourly rate. He only charged me half since he wasn’t able to do the installation, and I think he felt bad for me.

title: Good for boats
text: I gave this to a friend with a boat and they seemed quite happy with it.

title: Simple but effective
text: I actually use this to hold my water cup when painting outside, but it would work for a regular drink too.

title: Looks good
text: I haven’t actually installed it yet, but it looks exactly the same as the one that came with the camper. That one lasted 12 years, and if I get half that amount of use out of this one, I’ll call it good.

title: Great bulbs
text: I replaced the porch light on my camper with some white LED bulbs. They were a lot brighter than the old incandescent bulb, and it turned the area around my door into the insect version of O’Hare airport. I didn’t really dig that too much, so I ordered these amber bulbs hoping for a little more light and a lot less bugs. They seem to work. The light is a little brighter than the old incandescent bulb, but not as bright as the white ones, and the bugs seem to pay a lot less attention to it.

title: Way overpriced for what they are, and does not include the plastic grill.
text: For the price they’re asking for these, I thought it included the plastic grill. Or a better quality filter. Neither of those is true. Almost $24 for 2 ounces of plastic and paper thin foam  is pretty ridiculous.

title: Locking plug is clunky
text: I got this cord to replace a marine grade Ford I had been using with my rv that was just a tad too short.  The quality of the cord is good, but the locking end is a giant pain and never seems to be secure enough. Even using the locking ring, which is a struggle to get secured. Since a loose connection is a good way to burn down the rig, I think I’m going to finally throw in the towel and get something else.

text: These fit the light fixtures in my RV perfectly. They are brighter and whiter than the incandescent bulbs that they replaced. I actually wish they were a bit warmer and temperature but I haven’t found anything like that

title: Direct replacement for rv bulbs
text: These fit the light fixtures in my RV perfectly. They are brighter and whiter than the incandescent bulbs that they replaced. I actually wish they were a bit warmer and temperature but I haven’t found anything like that. They are actually a little bit too bright for the porch light outside the RV, they draw too many bugs. title: Presentation isn’t the best.
text: When I spend 25 bucks on a bottle of something, it’s kind of a turn off when I open the box and get a big empty bottle and sprayer rattling around in it with a tiny little bottle of the magic potion. I mean you’re paying $25 for about an ounce of liquid. That’s kind of a turn off.

text: I didn’t quite get the fact from the listing that these are completely Unassembled. I got these for my lithium batteries, which can’t be charged in freezing temps.

title: Great product

title: Pretty cheaply made.
text: I knew it was plastic, but I wasn’t expecting it to be as poor quality plastic as it was. They don’t last.

title: Looks great, jammed almost immediately.
text: Thankfully it jammed up while I was trying the handle a few times with the door open right after I installed it. I don’t know what I would have done if I had been outside. It’s going back.

title: Seems to be identical to the Renogy monitor
text: I have the Renogy monitor and this appears to be identical except for the stickers. The shunt looks the same, the monitor looks the same, but with this one you get a lot longer cable. For less money.

title: Make sure your screws match the locations on this.
text: I knew my screws weren’t in the corners like it shows on the shade, but since it includes Velcro I figured that would work fine. It doesn’t. The inside of the window frame is not flat so the Velcro doesn’t work. I guess I could put it on the outside, but I’m not going outside to put up and take down the sunshade, and the Velcro will probably last about 15 minutes outside anyway. I don’t want to drill more holes in my window frame either. If you’re willing to do that, this may work for you although honestly, the snaps feel pretty cheap. And that’s the main reason why I don’t feel like putting more holes in my frame when I don’t think that those snaps are going to last that long.

title: Helped diagnose a random starting problem.
text: Last summer my mom’s old mercury started randomly not starting. I was advised that there were a few things that it could’ve been. The relay, the fuel pump, the engine control module and so on. I did not want to take it to a garage and have to sit around there all day and hope they actually got to it. I was hoping it was the relay because that’s the easiest and most economical fix. But after playing three card Monte with the relays in the box and getting confused, I finally got this thing. It wasn’t the relay. It actually turned out to be a clogged fuel filter. But if you have a few aging vehicles in your fleet, this is definitely a handy thing to have. Plus you can really impress your friends who are having car troubles. :-)

title: Heavier than expected.
text: This shade weighs a lot more than I expected it to. And frankly, a lot more than it needs to. It’s too heavy for my portable awning set up. I ended up going to a fabric store and getting black netting. It weighs a few ounces and does the same job. Oh and cost less than $10. It’s definitely well constructed, but it was also definitely overkill for my application.

title: Pretty flexible
text: Seems to work ok, time will tell if the adhesive is durable.

title: License plate is still there.......
text: The plate hasn’t fallen off so I give it five stars.

title: Looks great, straps are too short
text: This fits my moms big boat Mercury grand Marquis like it’s made for it. Except for the straps. The straps are too short. The center one just barely reaches and it was a giant pain to secure because of that. And the little strings that are supposed to tie around the tire? No. That’s just not something I want to do very often and anyway, the straps are too short to reach. The cover is nice, if it had decent straps for the tires that were longer and were snap or Velcro or some thing, and of course a center strap that was long enough, it would be a five-star item.

text: It doesn’t matter what I do, this thing keeps coming loose. It also did not come with any protective padding for the jars which clamp around your handlebars. I wrapped some gaff tape around them, but that was a pretty poor solution. And now after fighting to secure it 1000 times, I’m just sending it back.

text: I use this to secure my bike to my cargo carrier. It’s really nice because I don’t have to worry about the hook on the ratchet strap scratching the paint. They’re also good when you’re just a few inches short and you don’t really want to go from a 6 foot ratchet strap to a 10 foot one.
