text: All the standard fuses that you might need for your vehicle. I haven’t had to actually use any yet, but they look exactly the same as the ones I got at O’Reilly.

title: Lasted six months, with one trip per week,. Junk.
text: One day I got stuck out grocery shopping when the car wouldn’t start. It turns out this relay was the culprit. It was a simple and fast switch. I thought it was fantastic. 6 months later, with an average of one trip per week with staying mostly at home for Covid, it’s dead as a doornail.  So it lasted about 50 starts.  Junk. I guess you do get what you pay for.

title: Way too thin to use as a sunshade. No ‘security’ flaps on mine either.
text: I bought this primarily to use as a sunshade. It is way too thin for that. It lets in a lot more sun than my old one did. I realize it is billed as a snow cover, but it states in the product description that it is a great sunshade. It is not.  Also, there are no security flaps on mine. I suspect the first real good wind storm this is going to be flopping around like crazy. I don’t think I’m going to find out because I’m probably just going to return it.

title: The concept looks great, but it’s really not practical.
text: I had a plain windshield cover for a long time. I really liked the look of this one with the ability to fold up sections and be able to see out or open windows. In practice, I don’t do that. But what’s bad about it is in windy areas the Velcro is not going to hold. After a couple storms with the windshield section coming open and flapping like mad, I went back to a solid cover.

title: Struggling to keep food frozen. Not returnable. No customer service.
text:
I ordered this to stock up on some frozen food. I was really excited by the specs and I felt that I would be able to use it on my boat as well. Unfortunately, the unit does not work anywhere near as well as advertised. It says it cools down to -8, but mine will not go below 26. It’s inside, in a temperature controlled environment, and it’s not really freezing. Customer support is nonexistent. I spent an hour waiting on online chat to no avail, and then I emailed and got no response other than a “we have your request”. And worst of all, it’s not returnable.

Edit: after a month, now it only gets down to 45 degrees, I now have a very expensive beer cooler as that’s not even cold enough for food storage. I expect it will fail completely soon.

title: so good. FAR superior to the Tire-Safeguard system it replaced
text: So far, so good. FAR superior to the Tire-Safeguard system it replaced.

title: Five Stars
text: Seems to work great so far. Good quality and connections are tight.

title: Pretty rusty after 2 years, and comes loose easily. Well, it did until the bolts rusted.
text: Go with one of the u-bolt options...you'll be happier. This one is a pain in the butt in that you need to remove your hitch carrier/bike rack/whatever when you put it on. I wanted to put the plate on the receiver and push the carrier shank up and tight using the bolts but I couldn't do that as the opening in the plate is too small.  So I had to do it the other way and it was less stable than it would have been.  The receiver is not what is rattling, the hitch carrier shank was. So I wanted to have the bolts with their greater surface area on the shank. Instead, I had one thin plate stabilizing the shank and 4 big bolts stabilizing the receiver. Which was never going anywhere in the first place. Bass-ackwards.  Then, it kept coming loose. At some point it came loose and when I noticed it the bolts were so rusted it was impossible to move them.  Thankfully it  was loose when it rusted shut, or I have no idea how I would have gotten it off of there.  Like I said, go with the U-bolt style ones, Way more configuration options and you can put locknuts on if you want. Much better.

title: Worked great on my Onan.
text: It worked perfectly on my Onan QG4000 RV genset. Do yourself a favor and have the tech install it outside of the generator housing when you get the replacement done. The factory location is a giant pain to get to, requiring the careful removal of the very expensive control board. One reason why I had no interest in trying to do it myself. The guy who did mine put the new one outside of the generator housing. It heats up a lot less which should help the longevity, but best of all, it will be easily replaceable if it does go out again.

title: Needed a new thermostat and loved that I could add a reverse switch easily.
text: [[VIDEOID:af1d20e077c80426bcb102b6594f8987]] [[VIDEOID:bb8c2022d839f6ffd0c90a1cbc54cca3]] The thermostat on my Fantastic Fan quit and I really missed that function. I had a 5000BT, which had a 3 position switch and a thermostat. Pretty basic. A new thermostat was $25 and this was fifteen dollars more, and added a reverse switch. I thought it was well worth it as the screen was old and had a few holes, and the face was pretty grungy. I've always wished I could reverse the fan too. Exhaust is great but if you can't open the windows (such as during a thunderstorm) it's not that effective and it'll be nice to be able to blow some fresh air in. (I have vent covers on all my fans, I don't know why they're not standard.) The install was pretty easy. I'm not super handy but the diagram was clear.  There was one wire, the red one from the fan motor, that wasn't long enough as it had to attach on a different corner of the fan with the new switch, but it wasn't that hard to splice in a few more inches.  In the video I say it didn't work the first time, I forgot to turn the battery switch back on after I was done with the wiring. Duh.  Anyway, I love it.  Great upgrade. I never knew this was possible, I figured it would require a whole new fan.  You can also get kits that add the rain sensor, lift motor and remotes. I didn't need all that.

title: Broke off and lost 2 months after buying.
text: Well, I hoped the reviews saying how flimsy these were were untrue. They're not. Not even 2 months after I bought them, both have broken off their keepers and been lost. And they broke within a week of each other.

title: Worked in my 2008 Ford E350.
text: It would have been nice if all the wires had been pre-stripped, instead of just the thicker (easier) ones. I took off one star for that but otherwise it worked fine in my 2008 E-350 RV. It was my first ever stereo install and it worked.

title: Seems like a good value.
text: Well, first impression is the can is way heavier than the cheapo generic stuff I got at Walmart. I think this will last the rest of my life. The spray is a brilliant crimson color. If you're using it on a boat or RV, you want to be VERY careful not to get it on the fiberglass, I don't think it would ever come out.  Will update in a few months as to whether or not it seems to be working.

title: Great gift for a car enthusiast.
text: I picked this up for a car geek friend and he is in love. It's got wires and QR codes and an app, the ultimate techy car geek toy. Except it's not a toy. You get great info on your battery that helps you avoid a problem before you're stuck in that airport parking lot at 3am in the freezing rain. At this price point it is certainly not for everyone, but for a car enthusiast or RVer it is a great tool.

title: Not that sturdy.
text: It would be two stars if it wasn't so bloody cool. :-)  It's flimsy and I'm not sure how long it will last.  I also wish it had holes on the bottom. I didn't realize my front plate screws on on the bottom.  Ah well.

title: Cheap insurance.
text: This is one of those items that you hope you'll never have to use. I tried it out on an old pair of heavy drapes and it sliced through like butter, so the blade works.  I didn't have a spare window to bust though so I'll just have to take it on faith. I do like that it's more hefty than the keychain ones I've seen. I mounted it on the side of my seat so I can reach it without bending or stretching. The mounting taped seems solid and the bracket holds it securely.  Like I said, I don't ever wanna use this, but I think it will be there if I do. I'm not a fan of the lime green, but I can't actually see it where it's mounted so I'll live with it. :-)

title: Much smaller than the description. Over 16" narrower, in fact.
text: The description states that it fits a window that is 31.5"-47". My window is 31" and it doesn't even fit that. The packaging states 31" is the max, so not only are the shades way smaller than the description, they're smaller than the package states as well. I don't recommend these at all, and when you shop other brands be sure to actually read the reviews and not just the star rating as many of them are padded by compensated reviews. I didn't and got these substandard shades. My bad.

title: Handy, just remember that you get what you pay for.
text: It's a small shelf and is not going to hold a cast iron crockpot  or other very heavy items. You are limited by the fact that most RV cabinets are made of cheap particleboard, for one thing, and the mounting hardware is small screws. However, I wouldn't be without it. It's great for cramped kitchens with limited counter space. My Mom put one on the wall near their loveseat and they use it for remote controls and whatnot.

title: Unreliable and doesn't last.
text: I've had this unit for just over a year now and I hate it.  One sensor died after about 8 months. I can put a new battery in it but it only lasts a couple weeks so I've given up on it. Hopefully that's not the tire that decides to blow. Another sensor now has a dead battery. I guess this time I'll buy a dozen batteries as they aren't the easiest to find. The display unit is wonky too. It takes about 45 minutes sometimes for all sensors to show up. This is touted as a 'feature' to save the batteries. Obviously it doesn't work as I'm still blowing through batteries. So I either have to remember to turn it on an hour before I plan to leave, or drive without TPMS for a while. Not good. Last but not least, every now and again out of the blue just driving down the road it will suddenly decide to switch to trailer mode. I don't have a trailer. Then the alarm goes off and scares the crap out of me. Well, it did the first dozen times, now I have to remind myself to look at it.  Then I have to turn it off and back on again. Which then leads to another 20 minutes of waiting for the sensors to come back on. I would sell this and buy another one but I couldn't in good conscience sell it to anyone.

title: Looks and function
text: These are really pretty towels. They are not as absorbent as some towels such as the fake chamois ones, but they do the job in the kitchen and bath and look good doing so.

title: Handy tool.
text: Awesome. I dragged my hitch on some rocks and broke the wiring housing/socket. This was a huge help in repairing the damage. After I changed the socket I was able to make sure everything was working correctly without having to go to a trailer to test it. I might only use it this once (I hope) but I think it saved me ten bucks worth of aggravation.

title: Photo and description is deceptive.
text: The product photo is completely deceptive. You only get the socket, not the plug as well as pictured. The description states a mounting bracket is included, it is not. In fact, I got nothing but the socket tossed into a box. No instructions, no wiring diagram, it wasn't even in a plastic bag. The socket itself is ok, but the description and photo need to be changed to match reality.

title: Mesh floor keeps smaller items contained, unlike cheaper models.
text: This replaces a 48" Harbor Freight basket carrier. The first thing my stepfather said when he saw it was, "Oh, great! The firewood won't fall out the bottom of this one!" This carrier has a mesh floor that keeps smaller items on the carrier unlike the HF one, which just had bars. It's nice to know that if something smaller comes loose it won't immediately fall through. The folding shank is something that won't see much use, but it's a nice feature.

title: Really sturdy and works perfectly.
text: Perfect  for what I needed it for. I have a curt aluminum hitch carrier that I bought here on Amazon, but it's obstructed a little bit by the ladder and the spare tire.  since I'm moving I needed all the space on the carrier so I ordered this to extend it out from under the ladder in the tire. It was a little overkill, I could have gone with a smaller one but I wasn't sure. It is extremely well built, it weighs a ton,  it may weigh more than the aluminum hitch carrier.  Don't forget to order or buy another hitch pin. That oversight resulted in a last minute panic trip to Lowes.

title: I ripped my old one off on some high rocks ...

title: Have the right tools handy..
text:
I replaced a Ventline bathroom fan that had a tiny fan with this. Like other reviewers, I will say it was not quite a 15 min process. And not easy to do solo. First of all, make sure you have a decent long philips screwdriver, and it's better if it's magnetized. Second, close the toilet lid before you start as when you drop that screw.....that's exactly where it will land. Third, put the plug in the tub as when you drop the screw again it will bounce off the closed toilet lid into the tub/shower. Put the plug in the sink too while you're at it. When I started the job I didn't have a 'real' screwdriver...all mine are those little ratcheting ones with interchangeable bits. That won't work with this as there's not enough room. You probably need at least a 3-4" long screwdriver. While it's probably not recommended, I attached the crank knob first so it helped hold it in place while I screwed in the attachment screws. It looks nice and moves way more air. The downside is that the screen, while removable, has a couple mosquito sized holes in the fan base for the tabs that secure it. I'm going to cover those with white electrical tape as I don't need to have that screen out all that often, after all, the old one didn't come out at all. I was also a little surprised it was just one speed and no reverse. Apparently you have to pay $50 more for that functionality. :-( I'll live without it.

Bottom line, while this is NOT anywhere near the quality of the Fantastic Fan I have in the living area, it didn't require me to get up on the roof & break a non-leaking seal to remove the old vent. I think it was a good trade-off.

text:
I figured for the price, it was worth a shot since the dealership wanted $160 for a single remote and then $54 for programming. I received them quickly and immediately made an appointment to get them programmed (at the dealership). After about 15 minutes, the guy came back with my two, shiny, newly-programmed remotes. The worked flawlessly and I was only charged a single programming charge.

On a side note, don't forget to ask them to cut the key for you. I initially forgot, but walked back in and talked to the guy that programmed them. He took me to the parts department and the guy cut them for me within a few minutes. Luckily, we were fans of the same NHL team, so there was no charge.

Dealership:
Remotes - $160 ea
Programming - $54 ea
Key Cutting - Didn't even ask

Amazon Purchase:
Remotes: $28 (for two)
Programming: $54 (for two)
Key Cutting: $0 (for two)

Overall, a win-win for me. Will they stand the test of time? Who knows. Even if I have to replace them every year, it'll take a lot of these remotes to ever come close to what the dealer wanted for them.

-Jeff

Fit perfectly, works great, easy to install. Only thing is that one of the sockets didn't fit, the one for the orange running light. If you've never replaced a headlamp before, you may want to refer to YouTube, but it is very straightforward, and only takes about 5-10 minutes. Definitely worth it when we consider much money we saved (the repair shop quoted us $200, we spent $36 on the light and less than 10 minutes installing it).

It looks great, too. The only way you can tell it isn't original is that it looks brighter than the one on the right side. But that's just because the one on the right side is faded from being several years old. Other than that, the two sides look identical. title: Good For A Few Winters, But My Husband Is Rough On Things (And More)
text:

STURDY?
This is for emergency use. That means other than snow being cleared from windshields, the shovel is not to use every time you need a shovel. It is for emergencies. For that use it is fine. My husband is rough on things and he is not quite as careful as I am. This is in my car right now and I find it helpful.

My husband is not quite as impressed with it as I am. That is okay- it is in my car and if I need it, I will be very happy to have it.

OVERALL OPINION
I like that this has options. I wish it had a bag, but I found one to use for now. I tend to keep the brush on the stem as that is what is used almost all of the time. Basic shovel use has not been necessary more than once and it was not a huge deal and it worked fine for the small bit I had to use it for.

My husband does not like the bother of having to change out the parts all of the time. He owns his own business with a very cluttered car/van and to be honest, this was a bad idea for him. By the time he will need the shovel, he won't know where it is and just be stuck anyway.

This is in my car and I am very glad to have it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are rough on tools or have a full car that is hard to locate things, this might not be the kit for you. If you are more careful with tools, put them back, and keep them under basic use only, this is a great set.

MY RATING

title: First Trial Of Putting On Was Okay, In Snow/Ice Different Story I Am Sure
text:
It is not winter yet. It is fall. The first trial of putting these on was okay on one of the cars. Just remember, if you have hub caps, these are not going to be practical unless you are prepared to take them off.

HEAVY
These are heavy, but they are not as bad as some other chains I had which were in big long pieces to use for traction. They are not hard to keep in the car. They have a bag they come in with gloves (and a bag for those too) as well as the tool to put them on.

PRACTICAL?
If you don't have hub caps these will work, but if you do, they won't unless you are prepared to take off the hub caps first.

BEST USE
It seems like the larger cars were better than the smaller ones with the first trial run of the chains. Here in our state, it is considered illegal to drive with these on. However, in desperate situations, it is a matter of life or death, they will help if they are able to be applied. Being that they come in a bag, it is easy enough to transfer them to whatever vehicle necessary at the time.

ADVICE
I strongly advise that you try to put these on in weather without snow or ice first before you try to use them in a storm. There are many variables that you need to consider in using these which you want to work out BEFORE you need them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Make sure these fit your car and are easy to put on first, and if they are, they might be handy to have for you in emergency level snow storms or ice.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. These only work for 2 of our 3 cars due to hub caps that can not be removed constantly. Life or death, however, we could take them off. They are better than nothing in an emergency though, so I plan to keep them in one of the cars when going out in a storm or during potential upcoming storm. I am glad they come in a bag so they will be easy to transfer

title: Great Potential Jacket, But Made With Wrong Proportions
text:
I have worn leather jackets of various styles for a long time. Biker jackets are not meant to be huge as they balloon out when you wear them riding. However, there is a certain amount of comfort one expects from a biker style jacket.

LEATHER QUALITY
This is a high quality leather that is used in this coat. It is nice thickness, very sturdy and well made.

STYLE
The style is really nice of this jacket. Unfortunately, the proportions are off. The jacket itself is pretty form fitting and nice and it has a zip out liner. There are plenty of pockets and zippers which make this a really practical jacket for bikers or even just to wear around and not carry a purse.

FIT
The fit of this jacket is where the problems lie. I wear a size 14-16 misses US jacket and this jacket in a 2XL is tight. I am talking like they took the base pattern pieces from the size Small or Medium jacket and forgot to enlarge the armholes. The armholes are WAY too small and shallow for a 2XL.

The rest of the jacket is snug, but that is to be expected from a biker style jacket. In a size 2XL, however, I would expect a bit more room. If this is worn for riding, after a while the leather will stretch out from the constant ballooning of the jacket from riding. The armhole problem and shoulder width won't change with that, unfortunately. My point is, even if you plan to use this for riding, it might not work unless you have very small armhole area and narrow shoulders.

I can get the jacket to be tolerable when I zip out the lining, but the point of the jacket is to wear in cooler weather and colder weather.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I love the style of this jacket and really wanted to be more comfortable in it than I am. It is expensive in terms of a purchase to be this far off in sizing.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. This should not be sized so small in the armholes. I do not think the pattern was drafted correctly for the larger sizes. The upper part of the jacket as in shoulders and arm holes is too small. If you are at all heavy, I am not sure if going up two sizes will even help. I wear a size Large or Extra Large in most US clothing, so a 2XL being this tight in the shoulders and armholes is way off.

PHOTO
I can not show you a photo that will illustrate to you the problems in fit with this jacket. I had someone else similar size to me try this on and they said the same thing- shoulders and armholes WAY off in size.

This cushion seems to help my fussy husband a lot in the car that has been awful to drive in.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. It is amazing to find a cushion that my husband FINALLY does not ignore, discard, or complain about. He has used this since I got it. SCORE!

title: Really Cool Looking, Match Car
text:
I have a kid who has painted their car in a color shifting paint. the rest of the car is gray. When I saw these mats, I had a good laugh. They match perfectly.

QUALITY
The quality of these mats is pretty good. They are not super thick, but they do the job of protecting the floor.

EDGES
The edges are gorgeous. They do color shift and they match the paint that is used in cars which will shift from blue to red to aqua. They are slick, but not plastic in feel.

BACK
The backing of these has some dots on it which hold it into place on the rugs in the car. They work pretty well, but if you have someone who is heavy on the feet, they will shift.

CLEANING
These are not hard to vacuum which is how I usually work with mats, but if necessary, they will stand up to a hosing off.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These mats are so perfect they are amazing. The color shifting edges are awesome and looks perfect with our gray color shifting car which I have pictured with this review.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. These are exactly what we were looking for. This fits in our Saturn SL.

title: My Husband Likes This- Handy, Quiet, Fast, And Not Too Big
text:
The only person in the family who did not have a tire inflator to keep in their car was my husband. I got this for him.

CASE
This comes with a great hard type of case that zips shut.

ACCESSORIES
The accessories in this inflator are all easily stored in the case, and some of the adapters are tucked inside the battery compartment which makes them handy.

HOW TO CHARGE
My husband is glad that the battery can be removed for charging so that the unit is not having to be brought in to charge it. The charger is pretty fast- only a couple of hours. He tries to charge it after a few months to be sure it is ready if he needs it for emergencies.

EASE OF USE?
He said that this is very easy to use. The numbers are big and well lit, and although you can not repeat custom settings, if you use a standard setting, that is not an issue.

WHAT USED FOR
This is used primarily for my husband's tires on his work vehicle. He has a station wagon that he uses for most jobs as his van has recently had to be retired. It has been tested on a ball and an inflatable mat and worked on both quickly.

IS IT FAST?
He said that this works faster than he expected.

CONVENIENCE
The shape of this is nice- it is like a temperature gun, or a small drill. Although it can not rest on the ground while you wait, it does work fast so you are not holding it that long.

THE BOTTOM LINE
My husband is happy with this unit. IT is quiet, works quickly, and seems to hold a charge well for a few months unless used constantly.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. He is not quite as happy with the shortness of the attachments, but overall he likes this unit a lot. The case is perfect for him. He is rough in his work car and it needs to be tough.

title: Fantastic For Our Couches
text:
Our couches have nice thick leather on them. The usual conditioners were not working on them.

HOW THIS COMES
This is a pretty large bottle. It has a pump top.

HOW THIS COMES OUT
This is literally oil. That means if you are going to pump it out, it is not a cream. It will run all over so be ready with sponge or cloth.

DOES IT HELP?
WOW! I can not believe how quickly this soaked into our couch and how nice it made the leather. It even helped with the leather that is near a window. I try to keep it covered by it gets knocked off. Our leather is much nicer and it really does penetrate in nicely and make it look restored.

SMELL
There is not a big smell at all.

DOES IT DARKEN?
At first it seemed to darken, but it didn't stay that way and looked normal after a few hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This leather oil is fantastic. It took two older couches and restored them to a nice supple condition again.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is great to have. I will be using this on other leather things we have too.

title: Animal Ooops Easily Fixed
text:
We used to have a black car. What a mistake. We live in a rural area and it seemed like every few months some animal would think we were not there at night and run right into the side of the car.

HOW TO USE THIS
This is pretty easy to use. You just put it on the dent, lock it into place and pull back out.

DOES IT HELP?
For dents that are not too severe, this does help pull them back out again.

SMALLER ONE
The smaller one is good to pick up a small piece of plexiglass or glass if you don't want to touch the edges or the surface.

THE BOTTOM LINE
We have been thankful to have this in our house. Our old mechanic that used to help us with dents is out of business, so now we can do it ourselves.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. We still have a couple of black cars in our family so having this handy is really nice for small dents when animals hit the moving "black hole"

title: It Works, But I Would Not Trust A Drink On It
text:
I have sometimes had some issues with having to eat in my car due to all of the national insanity of the last year. My car is not easy to eat in and I have gotten frustrated a few times. I decided to try this out.

HOW THIS IS MADE
This is a hollow piece of plastic tray and it is not rigid but has a little give to it- not much. It has a place for a meal and a place for a cup too.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
There are no instructions in this thing, so I had to really work at trying to get this to fit my steering wheel. Finally I found that if you slide it up from the bottom, at one point it will grab and stay put with a reasonable amount of pressure on it.

WHAT KIND OF CAR?
I have a Toyota Avalon from early 2000s.

DOES IT HOLD?
I can put a small bowl of poke salad on this, but to be honest, I would not trust a drink on this tray. I have a small drink holder that I use instead. It does work well if you don't knock it accidentally but sit still while you eat.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This tray is handy to have, but there is a learning curve for me. It fits my wheel once I get the hang of how to put it on, but I would not trust heavy piles food on it or a drink. A simple meal works out fine for me.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This could be just a little better than it is, but it works okay so I am still glad to have it. It beats trying to balance my meal on my lap and getting it everywhere.

title: Works Great For Temporary Fix When Car Is Too Old To Invest In Recovering
text:
Our daughter has a car which is old and it is working now, but the headliner has been billowing down for a while now. Let's see how this worked.

HOW TO USE
This is simple to use. You take the screws, put them through the snap with the smaller side facing the top of the screw. You find where you want the button to be, and then carefully screw in the screw until it grabs the headliner and you screw the screw into it.

Once you have done that, you snap the button over top of the screw to keep the fabric in place.

IS IT EASY TO DO?
This is very easy and if you take your time, it works nicely. Rushing through it with a Tim the Toolman type electric screwdriver like my husband did can lead you to tear fragile fabric. If you really want this to work, take your time and go SLOWLY to keep the fabric from tearing as much as you can.

Once the screw is in, the button over top of it does seem to hold the screw in place and fabric as well.

PINS
The pins that came with this were useless. They did not stay in place when pushed in to mark the spots.

DO YOU NEED ANYTHING ELSE?
No glue is needed. You just need a Phillips head screw driver.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For an inexpensive quick fix to get more time out of the headliner in an old car, this kit was really helpful. Although it won't last forever, if you are careful installing the buttons, you can get quite a bit of time extended in the headliner.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. For what it is, it works great.

PHOTO
My daughter took off before I could get photos of the ceiling. I will say that it looks like other photos of the buttons and looks good enough for her liking. She is not fussy.

title: Fabulous If Space Is Limited But You Need Good Performance
text:
My husband has been wanting to have something like this since his previous tire inflator bit the dust some time ago. I asked him to try this. FINALLY he pulled it out and used it.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is as listed. The size is very reasonable. It is lightweight, easy to handle for anyone. It comes with a bag to put everything in.

HOW TO USE
You simply apply the inflator to the tire, set the pounds of pressure you want, and the unit will inflate and shut off when it reaches the level it needs to be.

HOW TO PLUG IN?
We have cigarette lighters in our cars and that is how it is used.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
My husband had to put quite a bit of air in the tires, so after inflating the front two tires about 12 lbs total (I know, right? ), he had to wait about 8 minutes for it to cool off and then he was able to do the back tires as well.

HOW DID HE LIKE IT?
My husband was very impressed. He is not one to be THAT impressed by much, but he said for size, ease of use, light in case it was dark, and quickness to inflate, he was impressed. For lightweight usage of a few pounds, you can do all of the tires at once. In his case, they were so low, he had to do half at a time.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great little unit to keep in the car. It is compact, lightweight but performance is great. It works fine on keeping tires at the right pressure, but if you need to fill more, you have to give it a break in between after about 8 minutes.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. He likes this and said that five stars would be a good rating for it. I guess I won't see that machine again. It will be lost in his car forever. That's okay, I got my own because I KNEW that was gonna happen.

title: FINALLY Something To Get Us Unstuck (A Regular Problem)- BUT What They DON'T Tell You
text:
We live in a rural area that also is prone to mud and snow and ice. I can not tell you how many times we have gotten stuck in the mud, snow, and ice at home or out on the road. There have been a few times where if we had only had something like this, we would not have had to wait so long or to call for thelp.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This kit comes with two wired tread looking pieces which are like rubberized tire tracks in appearance. The photos with this listing are pretty good so I won't post an additional photo. It also comes with a pair of rubber gloves and in a case for easy storage.

WHAT THEY DON'T TELL YOU
I have to be honest with you here. I was so excited to finally get something that would help us out of countless predicaments that It never occurred to me that they might be heavy and hard to move around. When they showed up at the house, my husband went to lift them and said, "My God, NOW what big thing have you gotten. That is HEAVY."

That is fine, as long as you are prepared for it. Most people won't have a hard time with it once you realize that is what you are getting. Those who have a hard time lifting heavy things might need some help getting this into the trunk. Once in there, you can open it up and take out one piece at a time which is not as bad.

IS THIS HANDY?
We have only used this once, but it was not really a true test. It was a semi stuck mud situation but honestly only one tire was semi stuck and I think we could have worked it out without this. The true test will come this winter and spring when we usually have someone in the family freaking out because they are stuck and can not get out.

I will say from experience that the structure of this is the best we have had to date. It has great grip and it does grab the tires with traction very well. The gloves come in handy in mud situations especially if you are going somewhere and need your hands clean or don't want mud on the steering wheel.

PUT A TOWEL IN THERE TOO
I suggest throwing a towel in the bag too in case of mud.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is an excellent set to either keep at home or in the car with you in the trunk. Just be aware that it is heavy, but it does seem to work well so far, I expect even better in the really bad weather.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. It helped us get out of a mild situation so far, but I expect it to be even more helpful in the worse weather this winter and spring. I will update if I find out differently.

title: Fantastic Inflator- Even Our Kids Use It
text:
I live in a rural area where sometimes it just is not practical to get to the gas station to check tire pressure. I was having some issues with one of my tires losing air now and then and was frustrated with the occasional stops I had to make to FIND a pump I could use if I was not near the only gas station that has one in our area. Let's see how this worked out.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This inflating pump is not a whole lot bigger than an iron you use to press your clothing. Maybe double size. It has an easy to carry handle, easy to read dial and a few adapters that come with it.

DOES IT READ TIRE PRESSURE WELL?
This reads the pressure very well in my cross checking.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM- IS IT LOUD?
Our daughter wanted to check the tires, so she took off with this. She got an accurate read, put the air in the tires and gave it back to me so fast, I asked her, "Oh, did you decide not to use it?" I was sitting about 10 feet away from her although another small vehicle was blocking my view so I could not see her.

I literally did not hear her at all putting air in the tires. It was THAT quiet.

ANY OTHER USES?
We also use this for one of the kids' bikes to keep the tires at the right inflation.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is very compact, easy to use, and seems to do a fabulous job with our tires. In a more rural area or somewhere where air is not readily available, this hs more handy than I ever imagined.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I LOVE this thing. I will probably end up buying one for everyone at Christmas for their cars, this year. The one at home can stay here for bikes, mattresses, and balls to blow up.

title: For Cell Phones, Works Sometimes, Sometimes Not
text:
I have been wanting a Faraday box for my cell phones and the hook bag for one of us that has a keyless fob. Sometimes I want the cell phone to be in the box so it does not distract while driving , or for various other times when that is necessary. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This box comes with a pouch inside. The box itself has a tight fitting lid on a hinge which clasps shut with a good clasp. Inside of the box is padded and slick with a satiny type fabric in it. It is light colored so easy to see into even in the dark. The small case you can carry with you for the fob has a hook on it for a belt loop or some other way you might want to attach it to a purse or something to protect it. There is a flap on it and you can easily slide the fob in and out.

MEASUREMENTS
The inside of the box is as follows:
Width: 4 1/8 inches (10.5cm)
Length: 5 3/4 inches (14.5 cm)
Diagonal (corner to corner): 7 inches (17.8cm)

WILL CELL PHONES FIT IN HERE?
Some will and some will not. For instance, a Moto G 3 from 2016 will fit in here diagonally fine. Flip phones will fit in here perfectly and you can even put in more than one. Anything larger, such as a Moto G7 Power will not fit in here. It is too wide and the box will not close properly.

DOES IT FIT IN THE CAR WELL?
This is quite small and fits in the car pretty well. It is too big for our glove compartment, but it does fit under some of the seats or in the packing case I have in the back where I keep things stable while driving so they don't bounce around the car.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
Technically, this is supposed to protect anyone from being able to access phones or fobs in this box.

PERFORMANCE?
I have tested this quite a bit. I used a smaller phone someone in the house has and put it in the box, sealing the box tightly. The first time I tested it, it rang like it always does, although it took two rings to engage the cell phone in the box to ring. The second time it would not ring and said customer was not available. From that point on, it did not ring, but if I put the lid back on after opening, it, it would once in a while ring.

WHY THE INCONSISTENCY?
I think that the point of using this box is that when you put the cover on, you have to slam it down and make sure that it is on tight.

FOB?
The fob envelope/case on the hook works okay. Our son does not like to use it because he does not want to have to pull the fob in and out of the case to start the car. I would use it if I needed it though.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are sure to close the case tightly, this seems to work on cell phones. Once in a while, however, a signal got through which I am not liking because when on the road, we have no way of knowing when that will be. Because it seems to work a lot, I still am going to use it when I can.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I wish it was just a little bigger, plus I also wish that it closed a little better consistently. I still like it and will use it at this point, however.

title: Great For Cleaning Purses (And Other Leather Too)
text:
I have a few leather purses which have been hard to keep clean at times. Let's take a look at this.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This stuff comes in a metal bottle. You take the cap off and put on the sprayer cap. It sprays onto the leather and you wipe it clean.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
I got my purses clean and it did leave the leather in pretty nice condition. I did have to follow up with the leather balm, however. Moisturizing is important after the cleaning.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This leather cleaner worked very well. It cleaned my purses well, removed dirt, and left a great surface to put moisturizer on afterward.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS> I am glad to have this handy. I use it a lot on my purses. I will also use it on my couch too but it did not need it yet at the time of this review.

title: Really Nice Product For Leather Couch
text:
We have a leather couch. I am always looking for some good products to keep it in shape. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a scent free product. It is hand made and has a pump that you put on later. The bottle is metal.

HOW DOES IT APPLY?
A few pumps will do one seat on my leather couch. It absorbs well, seems to make the leather pliable, and then you have to wait for it to dry.

DOES IT SHINE?
I can polish this up to a gentle shine.

WATER?
Water will bead up at first after you apply this.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice scent free product. It is easy to apply, absorbs easily and leaves the leather looking very nice when done. It helps dry leather feel better and more pliable after application.

title: Pretty Nice In Some Cases, Overpriced
text:
I have been looking for a good back support for car and chair. Let's see how this one worked out.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This back support has a loop around the base that applies to the base of the seat and straps with a closure that is adjustable for the top. The back support is pretty slim in width and has wings near the bottom of the cushion for lower back. This is not real leather. There is a metal tag near the top.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This is an okay support, but honestly it is not worth the money. It is a bit slim in support so if it happens to slip out of place in the car, it does not feel too great. I have used this on chairs as well and it is a similar result.

As for comfort, it is nice, but not WOW. It seems to be so slim that it has to hit just right or it is not as helpful as it could be. Another thing is that the metal tag came out and fell on the floor. The fabric is eco leather which means FAKE leather. I don't like it as well as I like real leather.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is an okay back support but does not seem to be quite as nice as I expected it to be. The metal tag fell off almost right away, and it shifts sometimes leaving it less than comfortable.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. The combination of size, construction and price have led me to this rating. I just don't think it is worth the price at all. $30 maybe, but even that is pushing it.

title: Good Instructions, Easy To Use, Works Well
text:
I had two other car readers, but they ended up in the same place that the sock monster lives- no one knows where they went. Finally I decided I would get one for ME and hide it so that everyone would leave it alone and I could find it when I wanted it. Then my husband's new car malfunctioned again and again..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This comes in a GREAT hard case that zips shut It would easily fit in a car and be protected if you wanted to keep it there. Inside the case is the reader that connects to the car, an instruction book, and a USB cable so that you can update the software for the unit.

INSTRUCTION BOOK
So many things that I have gotten in recent years have had the WORST instruction books. I wanted to point out that this unit actually has a pretty decent instruction book. It actually has a picture of the screen that you will be seeing at certain stages of use so that visual learners will be thrilled with that.

The instructions are decently laid out and are not in a bazillion other languages either. The only thing I would say is if you have trouble reading fine print- make sure you keep a pair of fold up reading glasses in this case- I am not kidding. It is pretty small.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
My husband was having quite the issue of his car acting up. He had it tested twice but the problem is intermittent and driving him nuts. One day the garage was closed, I took this out and gave it to him, never expecting to see it again. I think one of the sock monster's homes is in his car.

He went out to the car, connected it and I noticed the lack of the usual swearing and hollering about this stupid thing that goes on with most electronic devices he tries to use. He came in, confirmed that it was accurate and correctly identified the problem, and I even got the reader back too!

UPDATES?
I have not had to update this yet- the first time I tried it was up to date.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is easy to use, comes with a fantastic case and you can even tuck in a pair of fold up reading glasses if you can not read small print. Thankfully I can.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. Out of the three readers I have used, this is my favorite. I would buy it again. I do love the inclusion of the case which the other two did not have.

title: My Husband HAD To Have This, Then What Happened..  ?
text:
I was looking through my order list one day and my husband came in and saw this and kept asking about it saying he HAD to have this. I was so excited- he WANTED to test something out for me. That was great. Then he balked at putting it in the car for a while. Let's see what happened when he FINALLY put it on.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a kit which is installed as interference between your car's electronic draw, and the battery. If you accidentally leave on something or if you have an electronic malfunction, the battery connection will be disconnected to save what charge is in the battery. This has two connectors, one for positive and one for negative. You only use one or the other.

INSTRUCTIONS
The instructions are pretty well laid out. One side is for the positive, the other is for negative. There are photos to help you in your installation.

HOW LONG DID IT TAKE?
It took my husband about 15 minutes to install this, but he tends to really look at things and take his time.

DOES IT WORK?
So far, he has had this in a vehicle that he tends to leave lights on and have power problems. So far it has worked well. Recently, he was told that he could not drive that car anymore due to dangerous frame issues (Saturn Vue). So, it helped so far, but the trick is going to be to get him to disconnect it from THAT car before he gets rid of it and reconnect it to his new car which is an electronic playground.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is easy to install, seems to work well, and is something we will be keeping in my husband's next car as he has a tendency to forget lights, etc, and drain the battery at times.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this, it does what it says, and if it means I will hear a lot less of the moaning when he leaves his lights on, or has power issues with his car, I am ALL FOR IT!

UPDATES
I will update this review if my husband manages to install this in his new car before discarding it with his old one if there is anything more to add to this review. I hope it works in this car as well as his last one!

title: Takes An Older Car Makes It Look New, Esp For Multichrome Paint
text:
My daughter did a multichrome paint job on her own car last year. It had started to look a bit rough after the long winter and rainy summer here. We decided to try this not only on her car, but my quite old Toyota Camry. Let's see what happened.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This comes in a spray bottle. It is thin milky white stuff. The odor is not too bad, but using it outside might make it seem not as bad as a garage might.

HOW DO YOU USE THIS?
We washed the cars, cleaned them off from residue, and then sprayed this on and wiped it off with a microfiber cloth. You only let it sit on for a few moments before buffing it off.

RESULTS?
The results are BEAUTIFUL. This stuff leaves a mirror/glass like shine on the cars. Even my old car looks really nice and new compared to how it looked. I am including a photo of the duochrome paint - half with the finish on it and half without so you can see the difference. My Camry is a very light gray color and it did not show up in the photo as well as the multi-chrome paint did.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Easy to use, and definitely cost effective, this stuff works well. Water beads up and the finish has lasted for a while now. As long as you clean the car well before applying and make sure not to leave it on too long, it really leaves a nice finish.

MY RATING
Five stars. This is really nice. Our cars look so much nicer with this on. I am not sure how it will make it through a really tough winter, but will update if I have more to add.

title: FINALLY I HAVE A TIRE GAUGE I LOVE!
text:
Who would think a tire gauge would be that big of a deal, but in my case, well, I guess it is. Let's take a look..

WHAT DO I NEED IN A TIRE GAUGE?
Usually when I am in need of a tire pressure gauge, it is when I am dressed up, usually in heels, and it is very difficult for me to stoop way down and try to read a gauge. The stick kind are rather hard to see until I get them just right, and others have not been that great. This one, however, is amazing.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This tire pressure gauge is really big. It has rubber grippy edges on it, so that it is easy to grasp when your hands are cold, wet, or even if you have gloves on, although I would think since you have to take them off to work it would make that last part kind of silly. The gauge itself is a bit short, like 2 inch/4.5cm long, so that can be a challenge, but the dial- it is SO EASY TO READ! What I also love is that it glows in the dark.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
Although the shorter length does mean you have to bend anyway, the huge dial means that I can see this at any angle (it rotates 360 degrees so you can see it from any angle). The glow in the dark face is really cool, except that if you are using this at night, usually it is in your glove compartment or other dark place, so you would need to use a flashlight on your phone or otherwise to charge it up first.

ACCURACY?
I checked this with our local gas station for accuracy and it seems accurate so far.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a great robust tire pressure gauge that is easy to use in almost any weather, this is my favorite. It is easy to read and even glows at night if you charge it up for a few moments first with light.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am thrilled to have this so far and it stays in my car, if I can hide it from the guys in the house who seem to take all of the good stuff, especially when I need it.

title: Handy Product With Okay Results But With One Frustration
text:
I have been waiting for the perfect time to use this product. We were not given a six pack to try, so weather permitting, I wanted to test this out on my leather seats in my car. Let's see what happened.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This kit comes with a box that has two pieces in it. They are a gold and silver plastic cap with a very soft foam sponge attached to the bottom. The cleaner/conditioner is housed up inside the cap at the base of the sponge.

HOW TO USE THIS?
The idea is that you press the sponge down until you hear a snap sound. I had to push right up with my finger on the center of the sponge to hear a snap. Once the snap happens, the container now is leaking either cleaner or conditioner into the sponge.

FOR CLEANING
For cleaning you use the GOLD one. You move the sponge around, stopping every second or so to smash the sponge down to get more cleaner into the sponge. After a while, it gets saturated, but it does take some persistence. As for how much- this did my entire car interior and one extra long leather couch. I also was able to do a leather recliner with what was left before it emptied.

CONDITIONER
This one is the silver one. Once it is pressed, you can smear the conditioner around the leather and make sure not to use too much as this has a lot of wax in it. Once you smear it around, you let it dry/soak in and then go over it with a soft cloth to buff it. I was only able to do the seats in my car , steering wheel in the car, and my couch. There was not enough for the recliner.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This is nice and it does clean the leather and moisturize it a big, but honestly it is not quite as penetrating as some other products I have used. The surface stays a bit tacky in warmer weather (inside or outside) and it takes a while to calm down with a few buffing sessions.

PROBLEM
There is one annoying problem with this set. It is the handles. The edges are sharp plastic and the sponge is VERY soft foam. That means that when you press on the sponge, sometimes it goes up into the handle and the edges will slide on the leather, causing a slight abrasion. On some leathers, it could even cut if hit just right. That is really annoying and would make me not want to use this a lot. It really is difficult to be careful not to let that happen and still move along in the process quickly.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a pretty good set which is easy to use, pretty effective, but does tend to stay tacky and have sharp edges that could if hit right abrade or cut the leather surface, this kit is handy if you are careful and works okay. I am not as fond of it as other products I have used, but it is not the worst I have used either.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. I would give this three and a half, but I think three is better than four. The sharp edges and extra waxy conditioner are not my favorite or my worst experience. I am just not wowed with this.

title: I Am SO Glad To Have This
text:
We have another diagnostic tool like this and I was very excited to have it. The problem is that our son had pretty much commandeered the unit and when my check engine light went on, I panicked. I knew it would be a long time before I could pin that son down to get the tool, but then I remembered how I figured that would happen and had ordered this one. Boy, was I glad to have it!

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a pretty straight forward tool. It is simple, and not as complex as the one mechanics have, but it will give you basic information on how to view what is going on with your car. It comes in a plastic hard to break into package with excellent instructions and the cord to plug it in with.

HOW DO YOU USE IT?
We have a Toyota from 2000 and all we did was plug it into the car while on and then it went through the diagnostics and gives the basic information on what it is that you are dealing with as far as the check engine light is about. The book has information to decode the feedback and instructions on how to freeze frame it too.

WAS IT ACCURATE?
My car said that it was emissions problem (what else?) and when taking it into the garage finally they looked at it, saw it was a gas cap problem and the light went off and did not come back on again.

CAN YOU RESET THE CHECK ENGINE LIGHT?
You can reset the computers to get the check engine light off, but if you want your mechanic to read it, I would suggest you not do that until you get to him/her so they can see what it was, if you trust them to be honest with you, that is.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For an easy to use, basic code reader for your car, this worked great for our older Toyota (2000). It gives peace of mind until you can get things looked at and fixed and also helps you to reset your check engine light too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I was VERY glad to have this one. We still did not get our other one back, but that is OK. At least I have this one.

title: Ever Since Getting This, It Has Been MIA ..
text:
When I got this, I planned to use it on my cars to keep them knowing what to do with. When I went to use it, it was gone. One of the kids wanted to test out a car. Then it was my husband. Then another one of the kids. Would I EVER get to see this? Let's see what happened..

I was in the car the other day when my son whipped out the little blue box that looked vaguely familiar.

"See? This is how it is done"

He plugged the unit in under the steering wheel. Then he pressed the right buttons, and on the screen came all of the readings. He was all frustrated and put away the box, only to bring it out again at the end of our trip. What was he doing? Here is the layout.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
This works by listing out what the codes on the car are reading out. It also does emissions problems and will reset the CHECK ENGINE LIGHT. Our cars have had some problems with these things, so in all cases, it has been a great help.

DOES IT GIVE DETAILS?
You will not get great detail on this unit. It gives you enough to go on to figure out what codes are being registered on the car without having to see a mechanic. It will not give you in depth solutions or anything.

WILL IT SET CHECK ENGINE LIGHT?
The check engine light will reset with this.

ACCURACY
For fun, we had our mechanic check out one of the cars and then took it home to check it out with this device. Everything was the same, just less detail.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For basic info on what is wrong with the car and resetting the check engine light, this has been a steady performer in our house- or should I say driveway. Everyone who can drive has used it and has been pleased with the help it has provided.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am glad to have this handy. We have not updated it yet, but it says that it will provide updates as they show up via PC.

title: Tried In A Few Cars With Good Results
text:
I have the wonderful opportunity to ride in a car with leather seats. The problem is, well packages love to fly all over the car, even when driving at turtle speed. Let's see how these helped..

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These hooks come in a box of four with four additional pieces. There are no instructions or illustrations in the box. You have to see the photo online to get a real picture if you are frustrated.

HOW DO THESE GO IN THE CAR?
These have a hook that fits tightly around the metal posts that head rests go up and down on. They hand either on the front seat or on the back of the seat, your choice.

HOW DO THESE WORK?
Once I figured out how to get the additional piece on (not sure what it is for at this point) I did not have any problems using them. The double hooks are good for my purse and for one plastic bag each from the grocery or department store.

DO THEY PERFORM WELL?
I find that when dealing with larger packages and/or a heavy purse, putting the hooks toward the front seat makes them seem more stable. When they are lighter or smaller packages, the back of the seat works better. As long as you do not drive like a race car driver taking turns at the speed of sound, these work out pretty well.

THE BOTTOM LINE
When you have a slippery car, these are a godsend for smaller bags, purses, and other strappy bags to keep them from flying all over the car. I am really thankful for them. They worked for the other two cars I tried them in too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS, although not having instructions or explanations in the box makes me want to take off a star. I won't though. They are still nice and not too difficult to figure out.

title: For Fish Aquariums Shoe Polish, And Glass So Far Work Okay
text:
I am always having a need to have a cleaning cloth or tool with all of the different things we do around our home from construction of artwork, to fish keeping, and then every day needs of cleaning and polishing. Let's see how these applicators work so far.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These are foam blocks encased by looped terry cloth style microfiber cloth. They are about the size of a Dobie dish sponge if you have ever used those. A pack of cigarettes is another reference if you have seen how big those are.

HOW DID WE USE THESE SO FAR?
AQUARIUMS
So far, I have used these to clean the outside of my fish aquariums. I get them damp and then gently polish the outside of the glass. It works nicely, but is not WOW.

POLISHING LEATHER
I also have used these to apply polish over leather. The one side is for application, the other side is for buffing. For boots it worked nicely, but again not WOW. These would be great if you are a leatherworker and need to apply polish or dye on a larger surface, however. They are also pretty nice for buffing out if you don't have any rough edges to catch the loops on.

MIRRORS
I have used these to clean mirrors in the house. They work pretty well and with the right cleaner don't leave bad streaks.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For multi-purpose uses, these applicator sponges have worked decently for several applications. I have not tried them on the car yet as it is winter at the time of this review.

MY RATING
FOUR stars. I like them but am not WOWed by them. I will update if I find other uses for these that would add to this review.

UPDATE
I still am using these- especially when I want to be sure not to scratch the surface of whatever I am working on.

title: A Bit Soft/Unsturdy But It Does Help With Slippery Leather Seats

title: Transmission or Freeze Dryer Oil Refill, This Funnel Is Handy!
text:
A funnel is such a simple thing, but can be so helpful in a variety of applications.

WHAT IS THIS FUNNEL LIKE?
This funnel is made from a good quality plastic- not too thin or flimsy. IT comes with a nice firm clear tube which comes zip tied to the funnel so it is ready to use and does not get separated from the funnel until you are ready to use it.

The tube is flexible so it will adapt to any curve or angle that you need to put it at. The opening is very tight so that you have to push hard to get it onto the funnel. That is good as it is not going to slip off easily.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This funnel did great when putting in transmission fluid, but after cleaning it up very well, we found that it was great to use in our freeze dryer when it came time to change the oil. The funnel fit very well into the hole for the oil to refill. This is a great funnel to use for any similar purpose, although I would not recommend using it for auto and kitchen interchangeably. It would be better to get a second one.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For transmission oil, replacement of oil in freeze dryer motors, or similar applications, this is a great funnel to have handy. It is sturdy, has a solid connection with the flexible clear tube and stays on well without falling apart.

MY RATING
This is a handy funnel. I give it 5 stars.

title: EXCELLENT Gift For Any Winter Driver You Know.  In Depth Review Of This Kit
text:
(WARNING- This is an IN-DEPTH review of this winter roadside emergency kit for those who like in depth reviews. If you don't want to read a lot of detail, go to the end paragraph titled THE BOTTOM LINE for a quick summary of my review)

I live in a location where it is very easy to be stranded in the winter time. Some areas can be clear and then suddenly you can be surrounded by a blizzard or ice storm. Having a kit to help in those emergencies is really helpful.

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
This kit comes in a fantastic little compact bag that is easy to store in small cars as well as big vehicles. Everything fits well in the case, so that you don't have to get it packed back in there perfectly every time which can be frustrating. That is not the case with this. The quality of the items in this kit are adequate for an emergency and are even a bit nicer than other kits I have seen.

WHAT I LIKE
REFLECTIVE VEST
Easy to wear over clothing, although a very large person (think Big and Tall) might have a hard time closing it over a bulky coat. It has two reflective strips on it and is a bright neon yellow color. The fabric is mesh. The size says XL.

COTTON GRIP GLOVES
The gloves are cotton knit with a lot of grip dots on them. The fingers are a bit long and I have medium female hands. The fingers are a bit narrow, however, so if you have beefy hands with thick fingers, these might be a bit snug. The idea is to have a grip if you need to pull, lift, or twist things when trying to make the car safe or repair.

ICE SCRAPER
Sharp edge, with a fluted edge to stop break up the ice. It is not the BEST scraper, but it is solid and should help a bit.

REFLECTIVE TRIANGLE
This is really cool- it is on hinges, folds flat, but has heavy duty orange reflectors on one side and a stand. You bend it into place and clip and stand up. You can use the case as a backing on it if it is windy out and needs support.

LIST OF ITEMS
This gives you a list of what is in the kit, so you can know at a glance, and also have a list so you can replace things as they get used.

CANDLES AND MATCHES
8 hour candles with matches in a plastic bag are good if you have a dead car and need warmth and light in the car until help arrives. There is room for a couple more tea light candles if you like.

2 EMERGENCY BLANKETS 52x84"
Doubles as reflective surface, this will help keep a person warm or help put up a space that is protected out of wind in the car, perhaps.

BASIC FIRST AID KIT
Bandaids, cleansing towels, antibiotic lotion, tape, skin lotion, lip balm, and gauze pad prepare for basic needs.

11 INCH ZIP TIES
Not really sure right now what might be helpful to use these on, but I am sure there are things that could be held together (maybe a trunk with sprung lock) with these until you can get them repaired. They are not that large to have it put on a bumper.

GUIDE FOR CAR CARE EMERGENCIES
Some men or women might think this is silly, but some people really don't know what to do in an emergency. This will help you figure out what to do in simple situations to keep you as safe as possible.

TIRE PRESSURE GAUGE
Basic cheap gauge, but it does the trick.

BATTERY CABLES
I LOVE the way that these are set up. They are decent quality, but they have DIRECTIONS zip tied to the cord that is a plastic coated card. This is fantastic to provide for young drivers, or those who have no idea how to work battery cables. Some people might think that is ridiculous, but for those who really don't know- this is a fantastic set up.

HAND SQUEEZE FLASHLIGHT
Another WINNER! The design of this is really cool. When you release the 2nd button on the bottom, out comes a little squeeze handle that you squeeze together and as the flashlight charges, you can see light. The really cool part, however, is that as you are squeezing it to see things, it stops lighting when you stop squeezing. HOWEVER, when you trip the top switch, the light comes on solidly and stays on as long as the charge lasts. So you can see with it as you are charging, but when you need a solid light, there is that option too.

WHISTLE
You might not think you would need this, but in a storm, it can be a life or death situation. This is plastic, so in the cold, might be easy to crush if you step on it, but it does come on a string, so you can hold onto it or loop it around a belt loop or something. It is bright orange, so easy to see. Metal would be stronger, but it might stick to the lips in very cold weather.

DUCT TAPE
This made me laugh out loud. I don't think I need to elaborate on duct tape.

MICROFIBER CLOTH
This is handy to clean off a windshield after muddy cars passing, or can help clean windows from the inside even better. Sometimes you just need a cloth and this would be adequate. It is not as absorbent as cotton though.

ELECTRICAL TAPE
For fixing motor problems or insulating wires, this is handy to have if you know how to use it.

DOUBLE SET HAND WARMERS
These are the kind you open up and shake and they keep hands warm for 10 hours or so. They are sealed to protect them until ready for use. That is a great feature in the cold weather.

2 - 12 HOUR GLOW STICKS
This is handy if you are stranded at night and need to attract attention to your hands to wave someone down, direct traffic (along with reflective clothing) etc.

REFLECTIVE EMERGENCY PONCHO
This is bright reflective silver. It would be hard to miss someone in this poncho. It is also rain proof and probably snow proof. It also protects from wind and can be used at night or to reflect the sun for help in locating you. It has a hood.

EMERGENCY RAIN PONCHO
If you get stranded in the rain, this is handy. It has a hood and is made from yellow plastic. You would also be able to use it to shelter in the case of broken windows or doors that were taken off of a car using tape.

1 HAND TOWEL AND SURFACE CLEANER
This will help clean up messes, but I would suggest purchasing a bunch of these as they would get used up quickly in a big messy situation.

ALL IN ONE TOOL
This is the one thing in the kit that I am not really liking. The case is BLACK which means at night it would be nearly impossible to see in the black case. IT has a belt loop so you can put it on your belt to put it back so you don't lose it. It is made from stainless steel. The quality is very basic. I would suggest putting in another one if necessary as a backup. I can not get the pliers to work. Maybe I am missing something. There are no instructions in the case about this tool, which after having the other items so well explained, I am surprised about. Some people would have no idea what to do with this tool. Since they have explained jumper cables, I would think they would explain this too.

The other tools are okay quality but I am not sure how much pressure they could take as far as uses in a stranded car situation.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE
The case should not be black. I would think that it would be better to make the case a brighter color so that you can see it in any situation- light or dark. I also would think it would have been better to have a reflective design on it so that you can use it if necessary as a reflector when waiting for help.

I am not fond of the all in one tool being in a black case. It is almost impossible to find in daylight, let alone the dark. No instructions makes it a frustration for anyone not familiar with how to use it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite a few items I am not fond of, there is plenty I do like in this very handy emergency kit for winter situations (and can be used in summer too). The kit was well thought out. In most situations, there are good instructions, plenty of things to help in various emergencies, and a few things to help with repairs until help comes. This would make a great gift for a college student, new driver, experienced driver- anyone who needs a basic winter help kit in case of trouble. It is very useful and the case is nice despite it being black.

FIVE STARS for this kit, despite a few things I would change to make it better.

I emailed NOCO and the response from them was that I would have to pay to send them the unit and pay a prorated amount since the unit had voltage and no explanation of the alleged failure. title: Streaks on dark colors
text:
Background: I don't just wash my car real good. I maintain my older cars with Meguiars 105, 205 and the their Ultimate polymer/'wax' product, so they are detail-shop clean. They've been polished with an aggressive compound (105) and a DA polisher and maintained with 205 and protected with Ultimate. I've also used clay in the past but no longer find it necessary.

This 'Ceramic' product went on my silver Benz easily and no streaking was evident. Then I did a 'crimson red' car (dark metallic red). The car was in the shade, and had just been washed and thoroughly dried with towels and an high-power air compressor. I further dried it for an hour.

I sprayed a panel (like half the hood) wiped it immediately, flipped the microfiber towel over and buffed it. The streaks were hard to remove. Next I sprayed the 'wet' side of the towel, wiped a panel (other half of the hood), flipped the towel and buffed it. It still streaked. I conceded to the streaking and finished the car.

I'm confident it will bead water a long time, probably longer than the polymer type product I was using (although this Griot's 'wax' is surely a 'hybrid' type product that is also in fact a polymer and not a true ceramic coating). I just don't believe this product will give the best appearance (I've used a lot of products and Meguiars #7 does that best so far, though it's very short-lived and it smears on glass).

Update: I buffed the streaks out with a foam pad and my Meguiars MT300. I also found that the microfiber towel I was using did not work well to wipe it off. I tried a different one and it works better.

title: Tried to, but these just fail
text:
These seemed to be useful and feature-rich, but you may need to do some work on them and they will still fail due to vibration. First, I had to pull the threaded metal stems out and epoxy them back in. There is some dry adhesive material they used in manufacturer, but it can fail as other reviewers have complained about them breaking out. I used a plastic bonding epoxy. The stems held up, but then the next weakest link failed and the lights started to flicker and get flakey. If I wiggled them, they'd go on and off. I could tell the solder connection on the pc board inside was cracked.

The turn signals do not need a flasher. They don't blink, but they have a sweeping sequence. They will still work with a flasher if you have a flasher on your circuit for other turn signals, but you don't need one for these.

The smoke is not nearly as bright as the clear. I compared them side-by-side and the clear lenses result in much brighter light. The smoke lenses dim the LED's about as much as sunglasses. Not everybody cares about this. For me, I put these on the first motorcycle of mine that had turn signals at all. I chose to repair the brighter clear ones rather than replace them with the smoke ones that were the only ones remaining in stock at the time.

The wire leads on these are pretty short. I extended mine with Haisstronica heat-shrink/solder seals, and then connected them to my wiring harness. I covered the wires with nylon braided sheathing with heat shrink tubing on the ends. I also epoxied the opening where the wires go into the stalk to keep moisture out. These indicators are not sealed as they come. You can choose to seal them or keep them open so they both get moisture and will also hopefully dry out.

I tried to make these work, but in the end they failed in a way I couldn't repair them anymore. Besides, it annoyed me that I had a driver honk at me for changing lanes when I had thought I'd signaled. I did press the signal switch, but my flakey Kinstecks failed. They went into the junk bin after that.

title: Not needed for Kinstecks, won't work with some LED

They are controlled internally to produce the sequence where the LED's light progressively from the inside-out. The Kinstecks will work with this. I tried it. But since it's not needed, I omitted it.

I tried to use this for some other indicators that are not Kinstecks. This would not flash until I put a larger load on the circuit. My other LED indicators draw about 0.023A (Kinstecks are about 0.1A) and that was not enough to make these work. They just stayed steady-on. But if I added an incandescent bulb to the output in parallel with my LED's then they would flash.

They may work with some higher current LED's but they do not work with all LED. They should put the current requirement in the description. I had to order something different. These did me no good.

title: poor design
text:
I bought these to replace some hose clamps that were holding some tabs on the fork for a headlight. I bought some bent sheet-metal style clamps that did not squeeze to fit. Those were junk. I tried these, but the bolts holding the headlight braces go in from the sides resulting in no pivoting of the brace, only the clamp rotates. That means the braces won't be perpendicular to the headlight's flanges unless the headlight just happens to be exactly the width of these brackets when they're mounted perpendicular. If it comes out not perpendicular, it results is cross-threaded bolts, pinched headlight shells, and bent braces -- eventually it will fail. To install them properly requires shims to hold the headlight shell.

Bottom line is don't get these. Instead, get this other model from the same brand: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07WDQ4YM8/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o07_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

title: Good idea - not so easy to use
text:
I saw something like this used at Disneyland to seal the nuts on bolts used for rides and rollercoasters. It allows for a quick visual verification that nuts/bolts have not loosened, been tampered with, and since it should be applied immediately after torquing to specification, it visually confirms that tightening the fastener was not neglected (on Disney's Thunder Mountain Railroad, this proved to have fatal consequences).

In aircraft and race vehicles, it has long been a traditional practice to use safety wire. Nuts and bolts are drilled and a stainless steel wire is inserted through both and then twisted, typically around a paired fastener, and the wire visually confirms the fastener has been torqued, has not loosened since it was torqued, and has not been tampered with. To some degree, safety wire can even keep a fastener tightened. This Cross Check seal probably has much less resistance to torque than wire.

A big advantage that attracted me to Cross Check is that it can work on assemblies than cannot be drilled for safety wire, particularly assemblies that are too small or that aren't materials that are suitable for drilling like electronic components and small parts.

In practice, this Cross Check proved to be a bit frustrating. When I first opened the tube, it came out as a thin liquid. It was runny and part of it was clear. I closed the tube and kneaded it to try to mix the paste better. I had to waste some to get the nozzle clear of runny liquid. Then I got some paste out, but it was difficult to work with a small bead. I will try to get better at applying this, but it seems only practical for large nuts/bolts (like 1/2" or bigger) because it has such inconsistent working qualities in small quantities. I don't intend to use it for large assemblies, but I can only imagine that laying down big long beads of it would get expensive real quick.

title: best LED replacement for incandescent bulbs I've found so far
text:
I bought Phillips, LASFIT and Sylvania 1157 tail/brake-light bulbs and compared them in my 1998 vehicle's taillight reflector assembly designed for incandescent P21W or 1157 bulbs.

The Phillips Vision is an all-reflected design and they were very dim in both taillight and brake-light modes. Incandescent bulbs were so much brighter in side-by-side comparison, they seemed like a useless novelty. However, they are better than the Vision-X brand LED retrofit bulbs that I bought in 2011.

The LASFIT 1157 bulbs which have LED emitters facing the reflectors, facing sideways and facing back at an oblique angle, are much brighter than the Philips Vision. The reflected light is not as bright as what an incandescent bulb produces, but there is a spot of more intense direct light from the rear-facing emitters.

The Sylvania ZEVO is an all-reflected design. It produces substantially more reflected light than the LASFIT and slightly more than the incandescent bulb. There is a dark spot from the heat-sink, but it is surrounded by much more light than any of the other bulbs produced. An advantage of using the reflectors rather than direct light is a more even spread of the light and the avoidance of hot-spots that can blind or irritate other drivers.

The performance of the incandescent bulbs is evidently hard to beat in a reflector assembly designed for incandescent bulbs. The advantages of LED are:

- lower power consumption, which is primarily of significance when the lights are left on without the engine and alternator running to keep the battery charged.
- faster brake light illumination (no delay while the incandescent filament heats up)
- longer life (the lamp is less likely to fail due to filament fatigue or vibration damage) and a longer interval between lamp changes

After evaluating three brands of 1157, I've chosen to buy Sylvania ZEVO for the other bulbs (mostly 1156) on this vehicle.
