title: would be better if it plugged into popular make receivers, but comes only with loose wires
text:
This worked in my '98 Discovery 1. Although it claims "no cutting" is required, that doesn't mean that no splicing is required. There are RCA connectors for Front L R and Rear L R to connect your receiver's pre-amp outputs into the plug for the Land Rover's factory amplifier. There is also a plug for the Land Rover's power, ground, and amplifier switch, but they terminate in loose wires.

With this harness, you should not need to cut your factory harness, but you will need to splice the loose wires from the Metra, to the loose wires on your receiver's harness. Too bad they couldn't provide a harness that was specific for popular makes like Alpine, Pioneer, JVC, Kenwood, etc.

title: I recommend a fuse for these to prevent fires
text:
These are very bright. The first pair I bought had a defect. After they were on for about 5 to 7 minutes, they started to overheat. One burned out and the other one melted down before I saw what was happening and unplugged it. It was hot enough to burn my hand and it melted the adhesive backing into molten goo.

I recommend a fuse for these to prevent fires. I used a 2A ATC fuse in a single holder. If you can find a 1A fuse that would be better but my local auto store only had 2A and I didn't want to wait to ship a 1A fuse. I used the red LED's for interior lighting in the 4x4. I had already replaced the dome lights with red LED's but they were a bit dim and did not light the footwells. I used one of this Lemonbest pair to light the floor, and the other on the overhead console.

Update: The second pair I purchased blew the 2A fuses per light, and one overheated before it blew its 2A fuse. It melted the adhesive and bubbled up. The Amazon listing and box describe these as Daytime Running Lights (DRL), Fog and Driving lamps, which suggest they should be good for continuous use, but I have found they can overheat after about 10 minutes. I may solder a resistor inline to prevent them melting down, but I am sure they will be much dimmer if I do so. More likely I will return both pairs as they are damaged. I wish they had worked out because they look great.

2nd Update: I was helped by another review that explained the wires short on the sharp metal edge of the housing. This is what causes the excessive heat and failure. To fix this, I am going to sleeve the wires with better insulation (heat shrink tubing) as they pass next to the metal edge. I believe this will solve the problem. A small dab of glue in that area could also help. Another alternative would be to remove the metal housing. In any case, I still recommend a low current (1A or 2A) fuse to prevent more than about 12 or 24 watts of heat causing serious damage.

title: It worked pretty good as a portable for a couple of years ...
text:
It worked pretty good as a portable for a couple of years of regular use for airing up after offroading. I could fill my 33" radials from 12 to 35 psi in about 18 minutes. I would have liked a faster fill, but even the larger compressors like the 400 are only a little bit faster. After mounting it under my hood, it overheats and barely fills the tires. It really only worked well as a portable.

This compressor fills tires up, but it takes a while. For a really fast fill, the best option is a CO2 or nitrogen tank but they're pricey, bulky and they cost to fill up. The next best option is to have two compressors. Even having an air tank doesn't speed fill ups unless it's a very large tank. Once you empty the relatively low pressure (120 psi) air tank, your compressor now has to fill the tires and the tank. I just don't have room for a tank large enough to fill my tires. I don't even have room for two compressors. So I decided to be content with the 300P.

Then I decided I could save some time by mounting it onboard without a tank. I mounted it under the hood with a hose to an open port at the front grill and wired it with a fuse, relay and switch. I would save time by not having to un-bag it, pop the hood, connect the leads, or put it all away. Now I just need to plug the hose, hit the switch, and air up.

The problem is the compressor gets preheated to about 140 F under the hood. I have it mounted above the fender well and tire on the passenger side. I can fill my 33's from 14 psi to 35 psi and then the compressor shuts off because it gets too hot. If I make a mistake or want more pressure, I could be waiting a long time for it to cool off.

The 400C is a little faster and might fill up my tires before it overheats, but it's also a 33% duty cycle compressor and I don't expect it to run much longer than the 300. Viair offers the 450C, for continuous duty. I expect it would continue to run even when it gets hot, but it's even slower than the 300 -- and since it's about three inches longer, it doesn't fit my spot.

title: not aggressive with orbital
text:
I used this with a large orbital machine and a foam bonnet. I was starting with a surface that had been sanded with 1500, 2000, and 2500. Since the product advertises quick removal of 1200 grit marks, I figured I was safe using 1500 and that it would go quick since I finished sanding with 2500.

I primed the foam with Final Inspection. This tip is found on the bottle of 205, but I used it with 105 too. On the first panel I found that the 105 quickly polished the fine haze left by the 2500, but that it left a lot of deeper scratches. That may be in part due to the poor performance of my orbital machine (a Craftsman). I'm sure I would have seen better results from a rotary wheel, but I choose 105 over the traditional Heavy Cut and Medium Cut Cleaners because I don't have a rotary and all the wheels.

With some more work, the 105 removed all the sanding marks, but I found that it dried fairly quickly (working in the shade on cool panels) and I ended up using a lot of it. I ended up using 8 oz on one medium-sized SUV (and I didn't even do the roof or hood since those have a different finish). It was important to follow directions and wipe the compound off each panel as I finished. I found that as I reduced the pressure on my orbital, the foam pad would buff most of the compound off as it dried up within a minute or so. I wiped the rest off with microfiber.

I can imagine if someone put this all over the entire car in the sun, they'd have one heck of a job getting it off. I figure the difference between Professional products and the consumer ones, is that with the professional ones, it really is critical that you follow directions.

When I was done, the surface was ready for 205. Really, my only misgiving about it is it could have been coarser. If I were to do this job again, I would want to have started with 800 grit, and finished with 1200 or 1500, but this 105 compound would not have handled those sanding marks, at least not without a wheel. Going to a more aggressive abrasive means adding more steps to the finished work, and from my initial experience, this product doesn't fit in the series of steps in a place to be as useful as it could be. I can almost do the same job with Fine Cut Cleaner (traditional diminishing abrasives).

I also used 205, which I found much easier to use as it did not dry so fast. I could do larger areas at a time and it was just much easier to use. But it left a lot of very fine swirl marks that Show Car Glaze took off. I probably could have skipped 205 and just used No. 7.

title: Good enough for occasional brake bleed
text:
I bought this tool at the auto store for about $10 more than Amazon's price. If the store had it or I was willing to wait, I would have bought the die cast metal version with the guage because I tend not to skimp on tools. This plastic tool turned out to be perfectly suitable for my two jobs: completely flush and replace the brake fluid for a late model GM full size pickup, and suck out all the power steering fluid from the same so I could replace that as well. A service shop would have charged me at least an hour labor for those jobs and this tool cost substantially less than that. It was worth it even if I threw it away upon completion, but I'll keep it somewhere in the bottom of the toolbox for when I need to do a job like this again a few years from now. It worked fine this time, and it will probably work fine then too.

For just bleeding, the tool is just right. For a complete fluid replacement, the reservoir is a little small. It holds 4 oz whereas I must have flushed about 64 oz of brake fluid from the whole system (had to empty the bottle about 4 times per wheel). I also sucked out about half a quart of power steering fluid which took emptying the bottle a few times as well. There are larger capacity tools for these jobs but they cost more. They would certainly be worth it if I did this kind of work often, but I just don't.

Update: I've done more bleed and flush jobs with this since my review and I find the vacuum thing to be mostly worthless. Maybe it's the ABS circuits or whatever but suction just doesn't do the job. The only part that's useful is the little container that holds the tube under the fluid and has a lid with an outlet so it doesn't spill. Still, the bottle is too small. Next job I'm just going to use a tube and big jar with a lid and two holes.

title: Coil s**t itself inside the cap, no joking, see pics!
text: Hoping this is just a fluke of zero Chinese QC and doesn't affect many of these. I've installed a couple of cheap, China dizzy's and not had this issue. BUT..., you MUST change out your drive gear with the stock and NOT use the one that comes with these dizzy's or you'll be in for some major engine work (these China gears have an appetite for eating cam drive gears for lunch!). Make sure you shim for .015-.020 clearance on the gear also. One more thing, prob should change out the module for a Pertronix or the likes. Otherwise, the quality actually seems pretty good, caps/rotors are brass contact and appear well made.

title: Love Hayden coolers, but sizing is deceptive
text: Showed sizing of 11" x 7.5", but actual cooler portion (cooler rows, not including brackets) is exactly 6", not 7.5".

title: Threads are different from the Sanden I took out
text: Not correct threads for valves (these are smaller than the ones on the Sanden I had in Jeep, no now have to buy new valves that will have the correct thread)

title: Nothing close to fitting a Jeep, China-cheap
text: Package came and was excited to put in stainless braided lines, that faded fast once I opened the outer packaging. What a let down. These are some convoluted looking lines, for sure, with large brackets crimped to them. Not sure what the heck these are for, but certainly not for a Jeep. Not what Amazon says they fit. If you're looking for Jeep lines, pass these up.

title: Wrong size at ball joint end
text: Part looks right, failed to closely examine ball joint end, after installing into the sub frame, it was obvious that the ball joint taper was way too small. So..., uninstall the whole thing, re-install the old one and wait another week for what I hope is the right part. These, are not the right part. Not for a 2010 Audi Q5 Prem Plus 3.2L.

title: Initial inspection shows these are ALL stainless steel, seem high quality
text:
Will update review after a winter of salted roads, but so far, these look like superior clamps (unlike other Chinese clamps that claimed stainless, but were just mild steel with shiny plating on them!) and are all-stainless (nut, clamp and U-bolt all).

Mid-install edit. Well..., stainless against stainless can sometimes cause galling. So..., yeah, had one of the nuts seize up on me, no tight, no loose, just stuck there...

Docked a star for that.

title: NOT stainless, just zinc-plated mild steel
text: "Just make it shiny, they're s****d American's, they won't know the difference" - Chinese sellers of garbage products flooding our market/stores. These are absolutely NOT stainless of any alloy. VERY magnetic and nicely plated to look bright and shiny. Crappy clamps that will rust out as soon as the sacrificial zinc coating has corroded off. Save your money and frustration, get something else. Buy American made steel ones and paint them with header or engine paint, you'd be better off

title: Amazon parts checker says it fits Grand Wagoneer/J-trucks, it does NOT
text: This review is not in regards to the product itself, but for Jeepers who think they've found the correct dimmer switch. This isn't it.

title: Actually re-packaged MANN filters, top-notch
text: The Purlolator air filters for MB's (at least the 617.952 engine) are German filters, high-volume of filter media and the same kind the dealer uses, just re-packaged by Purolator. These are THE filter to get!

title: Does NOT fit Jeeps (Amazon says it fits)!
text: Bought for a '87 Grand Wagoneer, they take 1/2 threaded switches. This one is 3/8 or smaller. Not even close to same thread. Might be a fine quality switch, but won't fit Jeeps (and the few CJ's I worked on took the same switch as the waggy).

title: Appears a notch above the typ Chinese knockoffs, made in Cambodia!
text:
I've seen a few of the cheap Chinese aluminum radiators, ordered (and returned them), worked on a few jeeps that had them, they all have problems eventually and unless you can Tig, you ain't fixin' it on the trail (I've repaired more than a few brass ones on the sides of trails here in Colorado - MAP gas and acid-core solder).

Anyway, unless you want to give away 4+ dead presidents, you're not getting a brass one anymore, so the aluminum ones are it (the plastic/alum ones are a pure joke, the factory ones were "OK" for a while, but anything from mcparts stores now leaks right out of the box, or the alum is so soft and thin you'll destroy the poor thing just installing it, or when the first mosquito impacts it in a kamikaze run at 45+ mph).

So for this one, it is definitely thicker and welds are very consistent and to me, borderline lovely. I've worked on projects in India (diesel motorcycle project years ago for MotorEarth) and seen warts-on-a-witch welds before, frightening! The welds on this radiator are consistent and do not leak. I think the key is that this radiator is made in Cambodia and NOT China. There is a difference in work morality. The Cambodians, like the Thai and VN, have a work ethic that the Chinese just don't have (no fault of theirs as individual people, it's the way that the regime there looks at everyone as a worker bee, just produce as much and as quickly as possible, let the end-user do the QC part).

Bottom line, this is the first cheapo aluminum radiator I've seen that is of quality far outweighing the price point. I'd get one of these again if needed (if I could guarantee it was from the same factory/workers).

Cons: Like all of these imported aluminum radiators, the vent tube is on the wrong side for the overflow. One creative person on the boards used stainless fuel line (rigid) that he bent into a long "S" pattern and just used two, short pieces of flexible overflow hose to tie it in, so it directed the flow to the other side of the radiator (where the overflow is) and looks "factory." For the quality and price point, this is worth just re-routing hoses for.

BTW, fits in 1974 to 1991 Wagoneer's/Grand Wagoneer's and J-trucks. Tried/confirmed.

WILL edit this review accordingly if I have quality/leak issues down the road.

title: Works, no leaks
text: Works and fits fine with no leaks so far.

title: WAY softer than the stock Toyota part and extruded into a leak
text: Material is substantially lower durometer than the Toyota part (Toyo part is much harder/stiffer), so after a few weeks, esp. once A/C has been used a few times, the seal "squished" itself into the alum water pump housing and caused a massive leak. Wasn't sure why till we got it towed back and found the seal extruded, thereby allowing the pressurized coolant to spray out between the thermo housing mating surface. Used old Toyota seal and all is well. I'd pass on this.

title: Two-months in and housing is warped or cracked.
text: Thought problem was the Dorman "OEM quality" thermo neck/housing, replace with genuine Toy parts, leaks same. Looks like the alum for this housing is NOT rated for temp. As soon as the A/C started to be used and temps were higher, this thing turned into a potato chip. Now re-do the water pump and housing AGAIN. F these garbage China parts!

title: If you're going to have your axles apart, use the best parts you can
text: If you're going as deep as taking the front axles out, just replace all the seals while you're there, save the headache a year or two from now. And use the good parts, National or US equivalent. There are Chinese replacement parts at the local XYZ parts store, but that rubber is missing something, it decomposes in a few years and you'll be doing the repair again. And again...

title: Way more than I expected, solid, quality box and switches
text: This enclosure is pretty heavy, very well made to exact dims (unlike most things made in China) and well put together. The switches appear to be potted, so they themselves are probably waterproof, but the box is not. You might be able to seal the holes in the back and gasket the front panel, but that's a lot of work. The wiring is top-notch too, with braided copper (not tinned aluminum) and heavy gauge with solid connectors. What you'd expect to see at double or triple the price point. The enclosure was too heavy to use where I'd planned (under a plastic heater plenum, the only place I have under the dash, the plenum goes the length of it, so no metal to attach to), but am really impressed with the quality. The weight is the only downside I see.

title: Excellent quality, thick, tough, honest to Goddess real leather and worth every cent!
text: All of the stitch-up wheel covers are a long, tedious pain in the arse to install, that's just the nature of them. But WELL worth the time to do it right. They sometimes feel like they're too small to fit over a wheel (I've installed two of these now, both were a fight to get them over the circumference, but once on and stitched, you know why it's tight to get over the wheel in the first place. Oh, use the baseball stitch (two-needles, crossing, look up on U-tube), it's even more of a PITA to do, but worth it when finished.

title: Really thin sheet metal/flimsy
text: Works, but it's pretty thin and flimsy

title: Two-months in and now leaks at its mount.
text: Think this plastic is not rated for heat. Or the cheap-azz O-ring is made from recycled condoms. Now leaking barely two months after installation. To be fair, it didn't start leaking till summer rolled around and we started using the A/C (hot coolant). Get the Toyo part (bring vaseline with you...)

title: So far, these things are awesome!
text: Installed on an XT225, brighter than the LED light I have as a main. So far, these are great. Will leave LT review in 6-mos or if they stop working.

title: So far it's been great, hasn't loosened or moved from adjustment
text: Fit a Mikuni TM33 perfectly, head is kinda hard to turn, compared to the ones with the machined clover-leaf style adjust knob you see on the ones for the Keihin's. Bottom line, I can finally adjust while running without contortions or burning my hand on the exhaust and the adjustment has kept it's place so far. Worth every penny!

title: Working so far.
text: Works, installed easily. Will leave a long term review in 6-mos or so, but so far, it's working fine.

title: Good gaskets, worth the $5 premium over the cheapest sets
text: These have proper sized gaskets for head/base for a variety of Yammy's (incl. XT225), the cheapo sets use a material that's too thick and the base gasket extrudes out and leaks as soon as the head is torqued. These are well-worth the $5 more that they cost over the cheapo sets considering the work alone to replace the gaskets when the cheap ones break apart and leak.

title: Works so far, good deal, you will need to wire it!
text: Good deal for what you get, but it's made for a wide range of vehicles, so there's a connector in it that you have to strip and crimp-in to your existing harness/wiring, depending on your vehicle. That cost more time than the actual install. All in all a good deal, but time will tell if it's durable. Will leave a long-term review in 6-mos or so.

title: Adjustments are insane, not enough on one end, WAY too much at the other
text: Adjusted all the way to the bar, a normal person can BARELY reach the lever, adjusted all the way out, even a 10" fingered alien couldn't reach it. What were they thinking?

title: Seems good quality, but cam cover mount is wrong for my app
text:
Head and all assy items appear top-quality, but the cam cover from my head is VERY different than for this head. The bearing is a quality SEALED ball-bearing, unlike the plain aluminum "bearing" that comes from Yamaha. Lots of nice upgrades to this assembly.

I could order a new cam cover, of course, but I ended up getting my head machined to fix the knackered surface so I could keep all the same components.

title: Decomposes within 6-mos in sun. Not impressed at all.
text: Degrades rapidly in the weather. Colorado sun can be harsh, but this was put onto a Jeep in August of 2021, now in April of 2022, it is coming apart. Thought it was a better quality cover, but sadly, it's not.

title: Well, I'll be damned if this doesn't work like a charm.
text: Had my doubts on this, but sure enough, it's a pretty rugged (as much as it needs for a trail bike anyway, and I wanted light) lift and works surprisingly well if you adjust it right. Will buy again for another trail bike no doubt.

title: As name implies, sure enough, they're damned quiet!
text: These live up to their name. Quiet and work really well, hard stops to stop & go traffic. Glad I put them on.

title: Super deal on these, they're loud and small
text: Will update review if they fail, but so far, they worked great and are small/compact, fitting in the stock location of an older XT motorcycle. For the price, it's an unbelievable deal.

title: Switch is upside-down, for on-off (off on bottom), but quality
text: Mounted upside down so the switch would be "up = on, down = off" to deal with the upside down switch mounting. Light works properly to illuminate while "on" and it's super rugged. Will purchase again if I have the need again.

title: Colors different from my harness, but connector is proper from '96 Toyota
text: Used this on a Toy Rav4 with cracked connectors in the engine compartment. Exact match to the alternator connector on my '96.

title: Not super bright unless you're directly looking at it
text: These are bright enough looking head-on into them, but not real bright at an angle. Still a good deal.

title: Worked first few weeks, but smelling coolant again with heater on.
text: Not enough of a leak to even see evidence of it, but enough that you can smell that tell-tale A/F smell. This stopped it for a few weeks, but it's back again now. Good thing is, this is fairly clear and doesn't pollute the coolant giving indication that it's in there.

title: Not loud and as big as others that are REALLY loud
text: Skip these horns. There are so many others available that are louder and more compact. These aren't.

title: Pretty rough and unfinished, not high quality.
text: Save your $'s and get a plastic K&N or something like this. This is not the answer...

title: OMG, run from this, it's made to "look" like a drum pump, but...
text: Too many ways to explain how cheaply and crappily this is made. Just total junk cast from alum/tin cans with some slag added for strength! Just run from this..., at ANY price!

title: Intake cutout in piston is WAY too shallow
text: Had to have it machined to prevent intake valve from crashing into it. By the time you do that, then the compression ratio is lower. Sigh...

title: Fits XT225 like it was made for it (it was)
text: We use these on older XT225 engines. Works and fits perfectly.

title: Cheap, plastic screws, just like the cheapo China ones...
text: Save your money and get the cheap Chinese copies, they work as well and you'll have to be replacing the hardware with quality stuff anyway, so what's the point in getting Motion Pro (also made in China land)

title: Doesn't get terribly hot and current draw is 14-16amps
text: Worth the $20 or so, but draws high-amps (for what I need anyway) - fun project for experiments.

title: It's a filter. It seems to be filtering. Yay!
text: These are a PITA to install (not because of this part, but because the factory ones are insanely tight and bend to shyst trying to remove the lower banjo bolt. This installed fine, is working fine and I'll assume it's filtering as it should.

title: So far, so good. Over a month and no warping or grooving at all
text: Funny that we are happy when Chinese parts last more than a month, but these seem to be high quality material and are properly cross-hatched, so just clean off the storage oil, mount and go (look up how to properly break them in, the thinking on this changes now and then). Won't hesitate to purchase Centric parts again.

title: Bracket broke within hours of install, sitting on a garage bike...
text: Really like the red LED (in this world of everything blue...) and that it has a rubber cover for the USB ports. Also, the wire is a heavy enough gauge to actually feed hi-amp (for USB anyway) current without melting. The weak link is the clamp mount. I mounted one of these to the adventure bike and liked it so much, I put one on the road bike. Came out to the garage the next day and the first one was just swiveling around on the handlebars, closer exam shows the plastic "fractured" (like glass) where you tighten it. Poor quality materials (oh..., made in China? You don't say!). Looked at a way to use the other mount (screw-on), but it's pretty thin too. Anyway, the port and wiring is great, mount is awful.

title: Came as open-box item, but is perfect for 1996 Rav4 2.0L
text: Despite that Amazon said the wrong one (ordered, sent back immediately, threads were WAY too small) was correct and this one was NOT the right one. It looked like it and fit like it, so I tried it. Drove around for a day and the gauge reads exactly correct for temp. Again, this is for a mid-year 1996 Toy Rav4 with 2.0, AWD, manual trans. Amazons parts fit suggestion says this is the wrong part. It's not. It's the correct part.

title: Gaskets are cut proper (OEM) size and are outstanding quality.
text: Unlike the cheaper gasket kits, this one has the proper head and base gaskets that seal correctly and fit as OEM. Also, comes with O-rings and seals that other kits leave out. Better off doing it right the first time and not thinking you'll save $'s on a cheapo gasket set.

title: Wrong thread for older Toyota (despite Amazon's Confirmed Fit saying it does...)
text: See pics. This one on left, old from 1996 Rav4 2.0L. Threads are VERY different between these. Don't trust the Amazon confirmed Fit system, works sometimes, this time it didn't.

title: The highest quality of the lock latch kits
text: Have had one on for a year now, no issues (other than someone pulling really, REALLY hard on it when it was locked and bending the Chevy parts). These are almost a must do if you live in a neighborhood or work in an area that is..., "questionable"

title: Returned this to install Bosch parts (everyone on forums warns to do this and they're right)
text: Overall, the parts looks totally top-notch. The rotors are plated (coated to prevent corrosion on other than  the braking surfaces), meet all dim specs and better, comes with the pad hardware and pads actually look like identical material to the Bosch pads I ended up using. I would suspect this would be as good as, or better than, the Bosch parts. If I had it to do again, I'd totally use this kit.

title: Most parts Chinese-made, belt is USA, overall, seems good quality
text: Overall, the parts seem quite high quality, despite the bearings and hard parts coming from China, the belt is Gates and made in USA. Did a really LONG checkout on the parts (fit, finish, dims, etc.) before installing (as you must do now with ANY imported parts) and they passed enough to say they'll probably last till the next timing belt (60k miles). Wish the kit came with the water pump housing as that needed replacement and sealing also. Overall, it's worth spending the extra $20-30 for the gates parts. Less to worry about for 60k miles now...

title: Not compact at all, same size as factory horns, not louder, but OK
text: Pics are comparing to Fiamm freeway blasters. These "compact" horns are actually larger in a few dims than the Fiamms (size of older truck horns). Was looking for small, compact, but loud horns. These ain't it. These are OK for loudness, but don't even come close to fitting where I want to install.

title: Connector is wrong for an '04 5.3, despite Amazon saying, "This Fits..."
text:
Looked fine, new, as-advertised, but despite Amazon's part checked saying, "This fits...," it does not fit a 2004 5.3 in a silverado. Look at the connector, it's noticeably small and only two pins. The photo for this alternator shows the correct connector (long, flat, 4-pin conn). So..., the photo for this is correct, but what came isn't. Funny thing is, the alternator that came is a more costly one than the one pictured.

Anyway, if you have a small, oval conn like this pics I've posted of what came, you're good to go and got a helluva deal. If your Chevy has the longer, flat, 4-pin conn (but likely only two conductors/wires), then skip this, you'll just be sending it back...

title: Same as the OEM I replaced, good quality, matching dims.
text: These are exact to what came off the car (Toy Rav4) and fit/function as OEM. Only annoying thing is the nut for the cable attach is 13mm, not 12mm like most Japanese vehicles. Shouldn't need to have that come on and off much anyway, so not an issue.

title: Randomly goes off, buggy as heck, waste of a day install time!
text: This thing goes off 5 sec after alarm is armed. Always. Useless as an alarm. Total waste of a day of install time (the $35 cost is nothing compared to the time wasted installing this POS!)

title: Changed my review, there is one totally annoying thing - causing complete removal!
text:
For the price, it's a decent alarm and it's nice that it has on-board relays for door lock solenoids.

If I could give ZERO stars..., I would! Read update below..

But..., one thing I found (and it was my own mistake) is that you CANNOT use the normal wire splices to connect to the various important feeds (ACC, +12v, Parking, Brake, etc.), you MUST strip and solder to feed wires. Problem is, splices are made for 16-18ga wires and the wires that this alarm comes with are like hair thin, so splices don't cut through insulation and connect. If you use the red ones (for 20-24ga wires), then it cuts TOO MUCH of the vehicle feed wire (normally 18-16ga or so), not leaving enough current carrying capacity. I learned all this the hard way. One thing that's become utterly and almost intolerably annoying, about ten seconds after you get out of the car, or into your car, or just open a door, it loudly chips three times, no matter what, alarm on, off, whatever. It's become so bloody annoying I fear just opening a door now. Anyway, I bumped my rating up as I thought for sure my ACC was connected (even the metal blade in the splice showed +12v, but it wasn't cutting into the wire for the alarm, so the alarm never knew when ACC was on or off and would set the alarm off if anything weird happened (all the time!). Anyway, my fault. Once all wires were double checked and stripped/soldered instead of spliced, the alarm works as it should (but I reserve the right to reduce my rating if the longevity of the alarm proves to be an issue...)

Orig review: Like many, MANY other reviewers here, I have NO idea how this got such high reviews. The alarm sets itself off 5-seconds after you arm it, no matter how you program it, or what you do. No lights on, nothing, still just goes off by itself. After a full day of professional install, now another day to extract the POS and another day to install something else that may or may not work.

Message from seller states to "disconnect door switch function" to stop the unstoppable loud three-beeps after doors are opened/closed. Let's see..., this alarm only has to triggers I can use. The doors and vibration. So..., no way to stop the bloody thing from constantly beeping with door opening, regardless of whether the alarm is off (when an alarm is OFF, I want it bloody well OFF!!!), just remove that function and voila, no beeping (and no alarm when a door is opened, great, as long people don't move the car too much, just open up and take what you want!)

For the labor/work integrating this install, this is totally unacceptable. Others have gone as far as turning power off to the alarm when not in use, but that doesn't answer the problem. You use to lock doors going in for groceries, then come out, use the clicker to turn it off and open doors, but it's not really "off" until you find the power switch you installed in the feed line (12v) for the alarm...

title: If your local wally world is out of these, this is next best
text: Ordered a few online because my local sell-em-up giant Chinese product store was currently out. Supposed to one of the better filters (per many tear-apart tests on filters)

title: Best deal in bulk filters for a variety of applications
text: No leaks so far, but have only installed a few of them. I wouldn't trust to a high-pressure fuel pump application, but for normal fuel filtration, I wouldn't hesitate to use.

title: Worked for customers car. Still working a few months later.
text: Fit and function is fine and it's still working for customer a few months later.

title: Fram filter? NO WAY! Only this one isn't really Fram, one of the best 123 filters out there
text: One of the many tear-apart tests on the web shows the Fram CH2930 made in Turkey as having the best materials for filtration. Even the Mahle and Mann filters use floor sweepings from cotton mills as the bypass filtration (includes mice turds, etc.). But these TURKISH MADE Fram filters are actually consistent material and high-grade (unlike about any other Fram filter on the planet - GARBAGE!)

title: They're cheap and they work, what else do you want?
text: These are really cheap and they work as they should. Since they're a one-time use item, they should be cheap. I work almost exclusively on MB's, older ones, so I replace a lot of brakes and use a lot of these. Lube the O-ring on them before install and put a dab of dielectric grease in the connector hole before install, will make for a positive connection and easy removal with replacement time comes.

title: So far so good, only used on rear ('cause I don't care)
text: Honestly, I wouldn't use some generic pads for front brakes, but these have a good bite and progressive feel on the rear. Appear well-made and pad material doesn't fade with sustained canyon forays. Don't use rear brakes much anyway, so any decent pad will do for me, but I tested using just the rear for long downhill stretches and no noticeable fade, in fact, they "felt" like they got better with bite and feel the more I heated them up. Anyway, I wouldn't hesitate to use these again (for rear brakes).

title: Really solid, well-built lock, didn't fit our older Winnebago
text: Really impressed with the quality build of this lock, sturdy, well put together, would likely last for years (lube it with synthetic grease before install). Only problem for us is, the mechanism, size, locking latch is completely different from our RV. Would take much modification to get it to work for our older Winnie.

title: Great heater, self-primes, any problems I thought it had were my own fault
text:
Not 8kw, more like 4kw (same heat output as the 4kw 24v one I use in the garage). But, everything works as it should and was pleasantly surprised that it restarts itself until the pump/unit self primes.

Don't use the stock cheapo tank. Get a steel tank. I used one for a generator (5-7gals) and mounted it flat in a storage compartment. Also, get a proper bulkhead fitting for eberspachers, costs half what this heater costs, but is VERY well made and much safer and easier install than the thin, flat plates that come with these.

Overall, the unit is great, no issues so far.

title: Too small and pretty cheaply made.
text: Was too small for my application. Ended up using a generator (flat) tank in a storage unit to feed a heater.

title: Really well made, but expensive
text: Worked very well for a bulkhead fitting in an RV. Cost was half what the heater cost though!

title: Base is too far recessed, hits carb at various places.
text: Nicely made, but the base is deeply recessed (down), so it hits linkage, carburetor body, etc., if I use a spacer to space it up far enough out of the way (more than an inch of spacer), then it's too tall. Not sure what this would fit, maybe something with a two-barrel and standard air horn size, but about any EFI unit or 4bbl carb with have interference issues. Not a brilliant design.

title: Correct fit and size, no problems and right part
text:
Part was exact fit and length. Literally ten-minute job to change (not counting bleeding the brakes after).

Good deal and good part.

title: It will take you WEEKS to end up with the correct fittings
text: Ad says AN10 inlet. It's not. It's -8AN. So..., order pump, get it, find out that it's ONLY AN fittings that will work. Order what the ad says is AN10 inlet. Wait 4-days, get that, find out that is too big. Return. Order -8AN fitting. Get that. Find out you need special nuts (different angle from std flare fitting). Order those, get those, find out tubing size is non-standard. Get all together, find it leaks. Tighten, whole pump turns in housing. Give up. Order a bloody expensive Holley pump that is actually usable/mountable.

title: Top flange gaskets are wrong
text: Kit came with two or three top gaskets, all three were different than the original. So, I got a bottom gasket and needle/seat for $30. Whoopee...

title: Exact fit, works good, easy to bleed if you minimize air installing
text: Good part, substantially less than parts houses and the same quality/part brand. Fit perfect, installed perfect, works good once air is bled.

title: Work, but what a b*tch of a time installing, wow!
text: Installation is through a hole less than half the diameter of these and these are stiff. The zip ties included are just used as a joke, remove them from back and toss in the nearest rubbish tin. Now find a large enough hose clamp and use that to crush these mutha's down far enough to barely go through the hole in the bottom of the A-arm (with the help of liberal application of silicone spray). You can only get a few inches at a time, then move the hose clamp down, re-tighten, force more in, repeat. Had to use a scissor jack to press the bottom of the bag up enough to get the bottom plastic washer in. All in all, took about two-hours, but what a total b*tch of a time to do it. Holy carp..., don't wanna do that job again!

title: Not as bright as I had hoped, but def warm white, not blue
text: I was hoping for a brighter light, but I'm OK with these. One thing, they are definitely a warm white color, not bright blue or other harsh color.

title: Bought locally, like many here, found it would not adjust lower than 6psi (1-4psi?)
text: Bought a Spectre FPR that is a knock-off of the Holley, no matter what, I could not get it lower than 6.4psi. So..., gave up, bought this. Tested with everything plumbed. Same, or close. 6.5psi. That is the lowest I could get the Holley. Adjustment all the way out, even the screw removed, same. Removed the spring that holds the diaphragm down. 6.5psi. So, this Holley one is going back too.

title: Like others say, it's kind of cheap/chintzy feeling, but light and works
text: Faucet is very thin and a bit flimsy (not too bad, really), but is VERY light, great for RV. Came with everything needed to install. All in all, good product for a decent price.

title: Good quality, a notch up from most of the cheap units like this
text: Not OEM quality, but acceptable. Better kit with lots of extras, than most of these cheapo sprayer kits.

title: One of the few cheapo TPMS units that works, but..., VERY dim display!
text:
The display is way too dim to see if you're driving during the day. All the cheapo ones seem to be this way (this is my 4th try). Otherwise, seems quality made and works as it should. Might return before window closes as it's not very usable for daytime driving. At night it can be seen, but you have to look at it for a bit (not safe).

*one tire sensor stopped working, replaced ALL batts with new Energizers, now only two will pair (with unit sitting on tire!). Giving up, ALL of these cheapo Chinese TPMS units have some issue or another, to the one (I've tried five now - no more!)

title: Seems well-made, but lock arms are both too short
text: This lock seems like it'll be durable, but I had to spend an hour making a custom latch as the common latches (like the one this is replacing) are square-hole, on about any RV, equipment latch I've seen. This one is a small oblong hole, so I can't use the long latch from my other locks and had to make a custom one just for this lock. Should have just returned these and kept searching for a proper latch.

title: Thought I'd finally found one of these that worked..., nope!
text: [[VIDEOID:5cc74bb661097e2229774426efc1febf]] Went through 4 of these cheap TPMS systems so far. Thought this one was the ticket. It's not. After charging with USB for a few days, AND leaving in sun for a few hours (showed full charge, though display was very dim, despite full charge), went to install on windshield and turned on to find the display constantly flickering and unable to turn it off. Dim and wacky display that shows no numbers isn't what I call useful. Back to attempting to find one of these cheapo TPMS systems that actually, really, honestly works!

title: Locking cap that works, but good luck finding someone to make spare keys!
text: It works for what it should, but only has two keys and NO ONE can get blanks or make spares. Just hope you don't lose one or you're hosed!

title: Display is very dim, plus only reads accurately to 3.5bar (50.7psi)
text: Not the best choice. I do like the tire sensors and the lock rings they have, but overall I'd skip this one.

title: Works, a few months into use - failed May 2022
text:
Been using this on a Craftsman mower a few months now. Still working good.

*Update: May 2022, coil completely failed. No spark, nothing, nothing changed, just stopped working. Less than a year of use.

title: So far, so good, seems accurate and works a few months into using in a busy shop
text: Works well, have to remind it now and then to display in PSI instead of BARS (just a few presses of the button), but having a light looked like a gimicky kind of thing, now I see the benefit of it. Overall, works and is fairly accurate.

title: Tried one of these in the truck, worked for a week, then..., false alarms, quirky stuff
text:
Avoid these unless you really enjoy installing, then reinstalling (a different brand) alarms. This one is always setting itself off just sitting in the driveway, sometimes it sets itself off from the inside light turning on with arming the alarm (a self alarming alarm).

Buggy and a total PITA. Avoid.

title: These used to be US-made and a quality gauge. No longer...
text:
Just cheap, Chinese junk made to look like the older, quality gauge it copies.

If you're going to use cheap Chinese gauges, then get a digital gauge for about the same price as this.

title: Cheap Chinese pump w/AC Delco sticker on it.
text:
Water inlet is rough casting, unlike the AC Delco (certainly the professional part) and unlike the one in the Amazon ad pic. The pump itself came with an "AC Delco" sticker on it, but that just means someone put an AC Delco sticker on it...

Oh, and if you decide to install this anyway, PLEASE get two new Felpro gaskets for it, the ones that came are the cheapest, softest paper gaskets I think I've seen and you'll end up needing to use Felpro anyway, after these ones leak. If you enjoy taking a radiator out and removing everything off the front of your engine twice, then go ahead and use the gaskets that come with it, otherwise, if you'd rather spend a whole day doing something other than wrenching something you just wrenched, use some quality gaskets!

Plus side is, it came in an AC Delco box that is a really nice blue color. At least that looks genuine...

*Update, found the system leak, thanks to a pressure tester. A crack in the pump ("NEW") casting, along a casting part. About 6psi and dyed water started seeping from the pump itself at the casting part line. So, install, remove, install with new Felpro gaskets, remove again after finding leak with pressure tester. This in a motorhome that is a 6-8hr job to get TO the pump! AC Delco new means NOTHING anymore! Want to sue them for my time lost assuming a new part was not the issue.

title: High quality and quiet operation (unlike the factory one!)
text: These are a notch above most of the cheapo Chinese motors out there, both the blade and the motor are higher quality than I expected, SO glad I spent just a few extra bucks on this instead of another cheapo like the factory originally installed!

title: It's a regulator. It works.
text: Been a month, still working fine. Plugged-in like normal.

title: Fan was a bit small for this shaft, cracked putting it on, had to buy complete kit...
text: Seems high quality. My fan was old and brittle, should have just bought the kit that comes with a new fan blade. Ended up doing that anyway. Lesson learned. Can't fault the product, seems higher quality than the motor I had.

title: Does NOT work for full LED conversion!
text: Bought to use in a full LED converted RV. Needs a load to work, so at least one regular bulb OR a load resistor. Reason I bought is so I wouldn't have to do a load resistor, if I have to do that, I'll just use a standard flasher. So what's the point of this one?? Just get a cheapo square LED flasher (seems the dedicated LED flashers are all rectangular?) and make two pigtails to adapt it in (female to make spades).

title: Not properly shimmed! .060 clearance, gear to housing, slaps back and forth.
text: [[VIDEOID:baacc4052071d5f33b62bb0640baa168]] Seems good overall, except they didn't properly shim the gear. There's a shim and the stop spacer, but not nearly thick enough. There's .063 clearance, so spark scatter will be huge with this. If we saw this in a shop, it was on a worn-out distro, got new plain bears, gear and shimmed to minimum clearance (about .005). Anyway, use the shims from your old distro if yours is like this, you might be OK if you have thick enough shims to fix.

title: Install is better than most, but..., programming is a PAIN!
text:
Install went well, easy to understand directions, etc., all went well, but the thing has proxy sensors in the fobs and default is that it locks when you walk away (or the keyfob gets 15-20' away from vehicle), the it unlocks when you get close to it. So if you're working on it, or near it, it's constantly locking, unlocking, locking..., AHHH!!!! And the programming info is VERY sadly lacking!

Alarm randomly unlocks the doors/disarms and randomly goes off. Problem too is, the siren never actually goes off continuously if triggered, the best it does is beeps. Not much of an alarm, all in all.

title: It clicks when 12v applied, but only connects the high amps when it feels like it
text: The relay works as far as clicking (the electro magnet), but rarely connects the high amp wires for the starter. So it just clicks most of the time, sometimes it'll connect and the starter will run, most of the time, with 12.7 volts from new batt, it just clicks. Tapping the case with the plastic handle of a screw driver while holding the starter button down sometimes gets it to connect. Just cheap Chinese junk (ie; you and I do their QC for them...)

title: Cool idea, bad integration (took three-days to break itself)
text: Worked the few times I used it, had another one I loaned to someone and it never came back, so I ordered this as a replacement. Little different design, but it worked good enough for all of three vehicles I tried it on. Came out to my garage today, opened the tester drawer and this was in pieces. Yes..., it broke itself overnight. I think why is because they use springs to contact the test pins and the spring pressure overcame the shear strength of the REALLY thin plastic (there's a ring cut into the plastic body to make an indent for the cap to snap into). Problem is, the plastic is wafer thin there, and probably made from recycled diapers. So..., it broke itself. I wouldn't have thought this would happen, but looking at other reviews, this is a common problem with this particular tester. Search for something NOT Chinese-made, or at least a little higher Chinese quality continues...

title: Work, but weaker/thinner than the Canyon Dancer ones and has sharp edges
text:
These are usable, and a great deal for the price. Not the quality of the Canyon Dancer ones I've used, but they're OK. As other say, use a few sets of these to tie down your rig, not just two front ones.

They are punched from SST sheet and there's a very sharp edge/flashing in the large hole. I took a die grinder to that edge so people wouldn't cut themselves and to keep from destroying the plastic protective coating on my tie-downs.

title: Well-made, good material, dimensions need explaining
text:
The size of the bell is 51mm, but the body diameter is 45mm. Bell to end is 70mm (total length, not including bail - the welded-wire "handle" that sticks up in the picture).

Too large to be placed internally for my system, but would fit into the outer cone if I machine that by 1mm (my Bassani exhaust cone is 44mm ID for the outlet).

This thing is quite beefy, weighs 183gms, and mine needs two.

title: Superb quality, but not for this bike
text: Have a few TTR's, this is a completely different bend. And the muffler mount is way off (see pics). Other than that, it might fit the newer TTR's fine, I don't have a newer one, but looking online, this system looks like those, not like the older TTR's like mine. Again, the quality of welds and build is top-notch. The exhaust cone can be removed and there's a depression machined out to accommodate a spark arrestor. Nice touch. An awesome system, esp. considering the cost, but it wouldn't work for me.

title: Backing is hard as hell to get off, tears in little pieces
text: Took forever to get the backing off, like it had been on too long and was stuck to the glue, had to pull off little piece by little piece to get all the backing off before I could install. Serious pain.

title: The clearance ("U") shape is on the wrong side of clamp.
text: The clearance side is on bottom, not top, but my fault for not seeing that when I ordered, overall seem quality, but lube the bolt threads, they are tight and squeak and might seize if not lubricated.

title: Seems to be OK, not installed yet, but one bracket was bent-in on arrival.
text:
Seems OK quality, same as the $300+ dealer replacement (if you can find one). Plastic and alum, like all are now.

As above, one bracket bent in box, had to unscrew and straighten. Packing leaves much to be desired, but so far it looks like it'll work.

title: Front/rear seal, NP208 (and most NP Xfer cases)
text: Work on Jeeps a lot. This is the correct seal for the front and rear output shafts.

title: Glued this into an engine oil pan.
text: This item is quite magnetizing for me...

title: Like many others state, don't expect it to be flat...
text: Mine came, cheap enough to afford putting the work and effort into bending the flange flat as it was warped like a potato chip when it came, would never have sealed as-supplied. If you know this, you can avoid the headaches other's have had to endure. Check it on a very flat surface and adjust according, BEFORE trying to install it!

title: Chinese knock-off, no markings whatsoever, NOT an AC Delco sender!!
text: Why does everyone have leaking issues with these? Because you and I are doing the QC on them for the Chinese mfg. Why is that? Because they're NOT AC Delco parts, just cheap Chinese copies in plain white boxes with an AC Delco P/N hand written on the outside. Avoid these, they are NOT AC Delco and they might work for a bit, but then will start to leak and the labor to R&R will cost more than the sender. Just get a genuine part (from a genuine dealer or brick/mortar parts store).

title: Not a "real" Standard Motor part, this is their "import" line...
text: This is their "genuine import" line, Chinese-made parts with the same part numbers as their older (quality) US or Mex made parts that were marked as "Standard Motor Products." This has NO markings except for the "I," "S" and "P" on the terminals. No wonder everyone has issues with these leaking oil and failing. NO QC (aka; China-made).

title: Low quality, much smaller rubber than stock
text: First off, these will work, for sure, but they are not even close to stock, so trying to make it look that way is pointless with these. Also, the hardware is not stainless steel (like the stock bumper hardware was), so they will rust and look awful in short order. Overall, if you just need some cheap bumpers to get you by and don't care about making your ride look stock, then these will work.

title: NOT for AMC, despite title!
text: These hit machining bosses in AMC 360-401 (and prob most other AMC blocks) heads in the middle valves, the two ends have a web cast into the head that these hit (see pics), so exactly NONE will sit flush or be bolted down. A few minutes at a grinder will "fix" them so they'll work, but..., I bought to bolt on, not to fabricate...

title: Typical Chinese-made mistake, wrong threads on wrong ends...
text: Idiots made these with the fine thread on the LONG side (water pump flanges are the fine thread side, so it screws through so far it hits the body of the pump), and the other side that the fan mounts too is too short. STUPID!!!

title: Good quality, won't fit AMC engines...
text: Amazon's illustrious "These products fit your vehicle:" fell in the rubbish tin on this one. Said they were correct for an AMC V8. Amazon was wrong (Gasp!! The horror!!!). Appear very hard and super high quality, just not for AMC's (the boss on the underside is too large to fit into the AMC spring ID. See pics. AMC retainer on right, this one on left.

title: Def stainless steel, good deal for good quality clamps
text: Tested these and they're definitely stainless steel (and look it, more nickel than the bright silver of zinc plated steel) and seem good quality, especially for the price. Just make sure you order the right ID for the OD of your hose.

title: Great dielectric grease and superb longevity for small gear assy's
text: Most dielectric grease is $7 and up for 3oz, this is a dielectric grease and is around $4 for 3oz. It's also a great all-around lube for small assemblies. Shipped fast, got just what I ordered.

title: Fit 1980 XT250 (common cam issues)
text: The lift and duration we're more than the stock XT250 (early model), but still worked with no piston hit. If you have the dreaded worn-out cam lobes in your older XT, this and new rockers are the cure (use NEW rockers with a new cam, not your old ones..., should go without saying, but I've seen it all...)

title: Threads were correct for Chevy, but head is different wrench size
text: Smaller wrench size than stock Chevy, but that's not an issue for most who are changing their own oil. Threads fit and has a seal like the stock. Good deal.

title: Fit perfectly, bonded shoes, but most are anyway.
text: Fit exactly as they should and work perfectly. No problems.

title: The cheap plastic ones are pure trash, these are worth every penny!
text: The rail slides easily and gracefully, the holders have ball-bearings and springs to keep sockets in. Quality in every way, esp. for the $10 these cost. Worth every penny!

title: Fit properly for a 2004 Silverado (plenty long)
text: End is different from orig chevy, but still works and clip will still retain it. Don't forget to angle the banjo end so that the line doesn't rub on the inside of the wheel and wear through. Also, make sure there is enough of a service loop for full turn radius without pulling on the line.

title: Very good quality and easy to program
text: If you need new fob cases or boards, these are a good deal. Seem high quality and they program easily to your vehicle (read the instructions on it, it's cake to program to your older Chevy).

title: Surprisingly good quality for cheapo Uro part
text: I've used a few of these, working on friends cars, and they seem higher quality than I would expect of Uro. For the price, totally unbeatable.

title: Was cheap and it works, what else is there?
text: Works and wired as it should be, plug and play adapter for 4-pin harnessed trailers. Will update if this ever fails me.

title: Works perfectly, fit same
text: Great deal, fit perfectly and works perfectly. Go to your lock smith and get xtra keys made.

title: These things are almost too bright, no kidding, like headlights from the rear
text: These are distractingly bright lights. For the price, what a deal. I had one stock Chevy light housing with a broken clip. For less than a replacement, I bought BOTH of these and install was super quick and easy. But, did I mention they are almost too bright for just license illumination lights??

title: These are NOT Weathertech's!
text: I've had both now and these somehow losing their shape? Weird, but like they're flattening themselves out. On first install, they fit fine, much like Weathertech matts, but after a few weeks, they seem to have changed shape. Probably a materials issue. Anyway, they're OK, for the price, but spend a few $'s more and get the real thing is all I can say. Or buy these from me for a discount and I'll go buy Weathertechs...

title: Seems like a deal, but install directions are attrocious...
text: Have installed maybe 50 alarms over the years, mostly in older cars with straight-forward wiring. Most have install directions written in Chinglish, but they're navigable. This one wasn't very intuitive in regards to what goes where, how to wire. Other reviewers have posted they're work arounds so this is doable, but I'd go for something with better tech support.

title: Works great, fit great. Get gasket set properly first.
text: Looks great, nice and bright, and fits great. Good deal all in all. Will update if LED's go out or other issue comes up.

title: Good reader, but buttons are flimsy, you find yourself pushing them 2 or 3x to get them to register
text: Good interface, hooked right up, clear screen, super intuitive and easy to use to read and clear codes. Only issue I have is the buttons are really flimsy and you find you have to push them two, three or sometimes four times to get anything to register. Annoying. Other than the buttons, the thing works really, really good for the price. Ended up going with a bluetooth unit though.

title: Came fast, perfect fit and precisely machined. Weights were off, but a scale and mill fixed that.
text: These are pretty high-quality pistons, esp. for the price. Well worth the money.

title: Fits Clarke aftermarket tank perfectly, VERY high quality!
text: Not a lot get five stars from me, but this does. It actually lives up to advertising and is a rugged, well-machined, high-quality cap for a Clarke oversize tank.

title: As others have stated, NOT for XT225
text: The Yammy XT has an offset sprocket, this if flat. Amazon site says this is correct for an XT, but it's not at all. Pass on this.

title: Totally wrong kit, even though Amazon says it fits
text: Not really sellers fault (unless someone put wrong kit into right numbered pkg?), but bearings are wrong ID (see pic) and the wheel seal is too small (see pics). Not the right kit for the application that Amazon says is correct. Now have to order the parts all separately with a disassembled bike taking up the stand till the other parts come.

title: Extremely light and strong (drilled them for safety wire, genuinely Titanium)
text:
Took quite a few ounces off my machine using these. Very well made and very light, but strong. Will order more for the other bikes.

Took one star off, orig ad said 2pcs, once purchased, now it says 1pc. Still a good deal, just not as good as for 2.

title: Appear exactly like the stock filters. Came in generic box, but overall, they're what's advertised
text: These are OEM replica filters with fine-mesh screen (just like stock) and appear in all ways to be the exact same as the original Yammy filters. They come in plain-white boxes, generic filters, but upon close inspection, I can't tell them apart from the factory. Worth stocking on these.

title: Strong, works well and American-Made!
text: For the price you just can't beat this tool! This is a review of the fixed seal puller, not the adjustable one, that one has some inherent weaknesses. This one doesn't. It's tough, does the job perfectly and is a hella deal for an American made tool. For a few bucks less, you can get a bendo-breako-master puller from Harbor Freight, then return it when it breaks, then buy a box of bandaids for your knuckles, then repeat. Or buy this tool once. And keep your $'s in the U.S.

title: Works perfect, comes with good seal washers.
text: Works perfectly. Will re-review if that changes (like the last switch I had installed that went bad within months).

title: Fits and works spot-on
text: Bought for a KDX200, now my petcock doesn't leak and rotates smoothly and freely. Just what it should do. Worked perfect for my application.

title: Bar end side mounts WAY too small for most bars!
text: The guards seem heavy duty, but the mounts for the ends of the bars are WAY too small to fit any steel bars and most aluminum bars. See attached pic trying to fit these to a stock XT with 7/8" bars (steel). The ID of the bar is 18mm, the OD of the mount is 12mm with a maximum adjustment to 14mm. So it's just sloppy and falls out. You can buy another kit with the proper ends, but of course that costs more. And by the time you're done fooling around with it all, you might as well have bought Cycra's. Unless your time is free. Then it's OK.

title: Seems OK, but idle mixture screw does NOTHING
text: Needle is non-adjustable and not sure where to get a different one, or profile. No pilot jet in carb, or if it is, it's pressed-in and not replaceable. Biggest issue is the mixture screw does nothing, screwed-in or out, runs the same and the choke does nothing but stall the bike, so I assume the idle mixture is way too rich from the start, but no way to re-jet or adjust. If you live at altitude, pass on this carb, it likely is perfect at sea level for a 225-250cc bike.

title: Works like it should and surprisingly higher quality than I expected from Uro parts
text: Will edit this review if there are longevity issues with this switch, but so far, it performs like a new switch and appears to be excellent quality (unlike many Uro parts I've used in the past!)

title: The wire guage is WAY too thick for about any practical application
text: It's probably ten or even eight gauge wire, most applications will be automotive or motorcycle and you'll be splicing these into 16 or 18 gauge wires. The wire is higher amp than most fuses will be able to handle anyway. These were cheap, and they work if you can find a crimp big enough for these wires.

title: Bought for Jeep CJ, perfect fit, works great so far
text: Seems one of the few things left being sold on Amazon (going the way of ebay, sadly) that is high quality and reasonably priced. Fit was perfect and works. Right part, great price.

title: Says "Delco" in the listing, NOT a Delco, it's a "Wai" alternator, All-Chinese made
text: I ordered specifically because it said it was a Delco alternator. What came was a "Wai" alternator from China. Customer wanted genuine Delco (why I ordered this one that said it was Delco), not Chinese knock-off of an alternator. Looks new, but isn't what I ordered or what the ad says. Amazon is batting less than 500 with me now, less than half the parts I order are genuine or what I actually ordered. Bottom line, this is a cheap Chinese alternator "FOR" Delco applications. Worth about ten-cents.

title: NOT a drirect, OEM fit. Have to bore-out firewall for larger diameter motor housing...
text: As others have said, this it NOT an OEM fit part. The motor housing is larger diameter, necessitating cutting the clearance in the firewall to 3.5" diameter. Total pain in the arse. But..., it works, sort of. Take a suggestion and scrape paint off from around one of the screw holes and run a ground wire. A passive ground through painted metal is less than passive. Ask how I know...

title: Ordered thinking I'd get what's in pic. Silly me. What came was some totally chromed POS
text: Ordered this alternator for a customers Jeep. It came as a completely chromed hot-rod alternator from China. Dubious quality at best, even spinning it by hand (never installed it), it had faint grinding sound from shaft bearings. Yeah..., this'd last..., about twenty-minutes at least...

title: Wrong part (part that came doesn't match photo) and it doesn't come with bearing
text: Wrong support for my vehicle, despite Amazon claiming it's right. Looks different from pic (one in pic is correct, both tabs flat across from each other, not at an angle like the one I received - this is for the 123 mercedes and normally sells for $8). Sending back is a total PITA. Avoid this if you're looking for one for the SD (126) body. Like others said, doesn't come with bearing, but I knew that and had already ordered a bearing anyway. The tabs on the one I got were angled and not straight across, like the SD body is supposed to have.

title: Chinese made part
text: Bought this same Hella reg assy from autohaus az, came in Hella box, with Hella literature. Marked Hella on top, then "Made In China" under the name. Sigh..., every bloody thing now...

title: Chinese-made off-spec filter. RUN!!
text: Chinese-made junk. Sizing is off and filter media in bypass section looks like a horror movie. Run from the MB filter (maybe other eco filters are fine, I wouldn't use this on any vehicle I planned to keep more than a week. Low quality and not cheap enough to make it a bargain.

title: Very fragile, even if you just gently snug them. Use locktite!
text: As other have said, these are made from recycled soda cans, so they will snap their heads off tightening them by hand with a hand driver if you're not expecting them to bottom out as soon as they do. You literally can't tighten them, just get the heads touching and hope that locktite will hold them there. Most have been fine, but seriously, the torque from just starting a nylock nut (also aluminum) on one will snap it in half. Decorative only!

title: Fit nicely, really wanted to like them, but leather is dry, cracked after third hard day of using
text: Really wanted to like these, they seem like well-made gloves, but it only took three-days of using (admittedly, off and on a lot and didn't have a chance to treat them before using) in the sun and one rain for the side of one (that looked kinda dried out and cracked from the get go)to tear open. Like cheap, Chinese leather, chemical tanned and dyed gloves, perhaps a notch above that, but still expected better, esp. for the price, OUCH!

title: Thought equivalent to the HFT tool that looks the same, might be a bit better
text: This looks identical to the Chinese-made HFT vac pump, but so far has lasted longer, even with accidental suction of brake fluid into the vac chamber. For the $'s, it's a better overall deal than MityVac (that is cheap crap too now!)

title: Just your basic, cheap, Chinese-made tank bag, won't last long
text: Mine tore the clear plastic section at top across one seam (it's sewn into the top and prob the cheapest thread that could be found). Still works, sort of, but with that torn, wind and rain can get into the main compartment. Just a cheap, junk, Chinese-made (low quality material, no QC, what we've all come to know and love about Chinese-made crap) tank bag that might last a season, but probably not longer.

title: Wanted to like these, loved the Alpinestar version, but this ain't it...
text: First pair was just a bit short in the fingers, I wear a large in AS version of these, the hand on these fit, just not the fingers, so I returned and got the XL. The fingers fit on the XL, except the right thumb. My hands aren't perfect, but I've not had a problem with other gloves not fitting just my right thumb, left thumb fit fine, just the right was sewn too short. Too bad, I miss the AS version of these gloves, but these just don't measure up (literally and metaphorically). In the end, I sent the second pair back also. The AS version was probably made in China like these, but they had AS quality control..., these..., do not. Take your chances and you might get the perfect fit, but play with them as soon as you get them, if they don't fit like a glove, send them back.

title: So far, all have lost one or more of the square LED's, just stopped working
text: These were bright, if not cheaply made, but so far, they're only about half as bright as they were to begin with since most of the little individual LED blocks have gone out. Just stopped working. Probably best to buy something higher quality.

title: Two of ten have already come apart from base
text: These are bright, but very fragile. Just the vibration of a diesel car seems to shake them apart. The LED top part comes apart from the base. Not glued-on, just the wires soldering it to the base hold it together, one rattles around, but still works, the other just came completely apart. If you buy these, use epoxy, JB Weld, etc., to hold the LED hat to the metal base so they don't come apart on you. Not happy to pay for ten, but only have eight working and of these I'm sure more will come apart.

title: So far so good. Old pump had a hole worn through the sock filter
text: So far, this unit is working 100%. Even shows more accurate fill reading on gauge. Installed along with a NEW Spectro tank (made by orig OEM mfg in Canada) so it'll have an unfair advantage over other pump replacements, but so far, no issues and appeared made well.

title: Excellent deal on 80006 glow plugs
text: If you're wondering if you should save a few cents on Monark or Beru or Autolite, well..., just don't. These work, the other's..., not so much. If you have one or two bad ones, suck it up and replace all of them at once, you'll have three trouble-free years before one goes out and not have to worry about it. 40+ years mechanic (Mercedes diesel specialist)

title: Incredibly, this is the real deal. Looks factory, made extremely well and durable.
text:
THis came in a box that looked like it had been through northern Syria on the way to me. The FedEX woman was embarrassed to haul it up to my porch, then asked if I'd like to file a claim (box was completely torn open at one end. We pulled the tank and it looked perfect, belying the frightening image the appearance of the box would claim.

The tank was completely unscathed. Was covered with a protective oil substance, but literally looks like a factory tank in every way. Except you have to use a rubber mallet to bend over the seams where the bands strap the tank in otherwise you won't have enough length to start them. You'll understand when you try to install the tank.

All in all, a great tank and a good experience with Spectro branded products (this is not a "Spectro" tank, it's made in Canada by the mfg who made the orig tank, it's just resold by Spectro, like much of their products)

title: Fits perfect, works, but is VERY dark, esp. compared to the Shoei smoke shield
text: Fine shield, not sure how it'll hold up to scratches, but it's VERY dark. The Shoei brand shield is not nearly as dark as this. I can ride home in the dark with the Shoei one, not so with this one, but this is better at keeping the sun out of your eyes though, as you'd expect.

title: Photo shows grain going WITH length of roll, it goes against
text: Was looking for grain that goes WITH the roll (for a long vehicle), this goes the short length, so you'd have to cut and splice and it would never match. Pass on this stuff.

title: Grain wrong direction
text: Like others have pointed out, the ad shows the grain going WITH the long side, the roll that came the grain goes with the SHORT side (vertical with roll, not horizontal, so it's impossible to match up if you are using it on something wider than the short side - 2'). Unusable for anything more than two-feet long. Pass on this stuff. Find someone who makes proper (like every other mfg on the planet!) wood grain vinyl.

title: Remotes are not same as pic, something in alarm box is rattling around
text:
Returned. Box came loosely packed with stuff rattling around in it, when opened, the alarm box had something hard inside that was loose and banged around as you moved it. Also, the remotes look nothing like pic. Just black plastic things.

Edit 03/19: Ordered another from another supplier, came with a separate vibration sensor that was in pieces on arrival (circuit board fell out of its case, prob would work fine once re-assembled, but it was also missing the cable for the sensor in the cable bag, and the box had been opened and shoddily taped back up, so was a return). These were good alarms, but the QC is completely absent, so look over and test your unit fully BEFORE install (I've installed a few of these only to find the brain had "issues" and had to uninstall to return, cost more in labor than the alarm). Also, the remotes are NOT chrome-cased as shown in ad and as stated by another reviewer, that was probably an old model, these are just cheap, plastic remotes (see pics).

title: Baseplate for RF-1200, OEM Shoei
text: Was bought for the P/N (QR-E) as that is what the RF-1200 came with. Correct part came and fits my RF-1200 perfectly. Same exact part.

title: Doesn't fit like normal Alpinestars. Feels not the highest quality...
text: Not the quality I would expect of Alpinestar. Ordered Medium, usually fits me like a glove, this one is baggy and arms have so much material it flaps in the wind. Just feels "cheap." For my $'s, it's worth finding a used Klim or something like that.

title: No difference in engine temps
text: Doesn't cool as much as I'd hoped, actually, minimal cooling differential (I can't really tell any difference in actual engine temps from using this).

title: Cheap, brittle plastic connector end decomposed
text: Ended up with an AC Delco one after thinking I'd save a few dollars on an amazon one. I think it worked, but the blue plastic that your harness connector snaps onto broke into tiny pieces, just disintegrated. So of course the harness wouldn't stay on the posts without duct taping around the whole compressor and the harness connector to hold it on. What a PITA. What a wast of $15!

title: Works fine, fits fine, seems to be doing its job as a filter
text: Installed in S10 that is running just a bit rich (and it's a cross-over year for TBI ECM, so finding a chip is impossible). Helped with a little more air, though it's not a cold air intake.

title: POS, stay away from this CHINESE MADE POS.
text:
OMG, what a total piece of CHINESE garbage! See pics. First, I spent an hour alone on grinding off the bosses that hit the power steering pump and then the AC housing/mount. THEN once installed, I find out that the threads for the pulley are not metric OR SAE. WTH? So I ended up having to clamp the pulley mount someway to keep it from turning so I can tap the holes to 5/16". THEN the pulley holes are too narrow for the wide spaced tapped holes and too wide for the inner, narrower spaced tapped holes. So, unlike most people I do have a small mill, I elongated the pulley holes so it would mount. Whew. Then once I start filling up the ($18/gallon) antifreeze, it's pouring out of the pump somewhere. Of course, with the housing half ground away and holes tapped, there's no way I can return this hunk 'O total garbage. Chinese won a war with us. Hands down.

Oh, and why yes, Amazon did say it fit: "This fits your - 1994 Chevrolet S10 LS 4.3L Z engine."

title: Works fine so far, perfect match to factory part, fit like a glove.
text: Just installed this, but was a perfect match to the factory part it replaced and so far, seems working just fine.

title: Low quality, come apart at the mount stud and are not very bright
text:
Kind of junky, three out of eight have already come apart, tear right where they mount. Just a bad design and materials. Like the idea, but..., I'd skip these, you'll be constantly replacing or gluing them.

EDIT 03/19: Two more have come apart where the rubber meets the plastic base. Avoid these, they're made for looks only (extreme Chinese junk, made for looks, not for use).

title: Really good quality, esp. for China-made, came SUPER fast!
text: Came almost too fast (from China, no less), quality is above average, esp. for Chinese made. Excellent item for a really good deal. Everyone should have one of these, never know when you'll have to haul a helmet to someone who needs a ride.

title: Quality kit, worth every penny
text: Excellent kit, all lights work well. Wiring was REALLY long, cut off about four-feet, but better than being short. All in all, bright lights and work really well (run a dedicated ground wire, don't rely on chassis). Good quality kit, well worth the price.

title: These are the correct springs for Triumph 865 twins
text:
These are the correct springs for the Triumph 865 twin motor (Bonneville, Thruxton, etc.). Comes in a package of six, but you only need 4. Send the other two to someone on the triumph forums so they can combine and give someone else a "kit" of four.

These are a tad shorter than the stock springs, but a few thousandths thicker cross-section (maybe .010 thicker), so they are stiffer, but not intolerably. If you'd done mods (exhaust, airbox, custom MAP, cams, etc.), you'll want these.

title: Great deal on aluminum bars
text: Seems worth the price. Light and strong. Great deal on aluminum bars, Aluminum is soft, much softer allow than Renthals and such, but a third the price and if you don't crash, then it doesn't matter.

title: Clamp section flexes, not the best quality, but will work if you're gentle with it.
text: Like others have pointed out, the "C-clamp" section tends to flex. It's just a bent, hollow tube. But it works if you use it gently. A few cents more in material and this would have been an outstanding tool. Otherwise, if you're hard on tools (hey, they're tools, they should be able to deal with "hard"), I'd avoid this and look for higher quality.

title: A finely machined, very well-made throttle tube - NOT Chinese!
text: Superb quality, outstanding machining and made in USA. But for some reason, it has the "push" cable side elongated, so the cable ferule is allowed to "cock" in the housing. And it's a bit too thick for the housing on my XT225 (in their defense, they don't list that it fits the XT either).
