Overall, an awesome design with excellent attention to detail (including O-ring sealed end cap!). Didn't work for me, but wish it would have, totally impressed with the quality. Paid to send it back (my mistake on ordering, still can't find a decent tube for the XT?)

title: Seems high-quality and does include valve seals and all gaskets and O-rings for job
text: Truly complete top end kit with valve seals (good quality ones) and all o-rings and gaskets that you normally end up using. Worth the price and seems high-quality

title: Nothing special, just black rubber seals like any other
text: These people need to STOP using pics of pink-compound seals. They are NOT red or pink, they are standard BLACK nitrile or Buna-N rubber seals. Nothing special about them. They last about as long as any other seal (but oddly, not as long as the OEM seals?)

title: Heavy and large, no bracket, but looks quality, weather sealed.
text:
This unit is MUCH larger than you think, or than it looks in the pics. About three-times the size of a Trail Tech that it's shaped to look like. Also, the weight is about twice what the Vapor is. The head unit weighs 383 grams, the accessories (pickup, wiring, etc.) weigh 54 grams. Last drawback for me was the strange bolt pattern for mounting and no mounting bracket of any sort.

With that said, it's unusable to me, but..., would work well with a larger bike that you are not concerned with weight or size. I'm used to the Trail Tech computers, so it's a hard one to take.

The unit looks very well-built, higher quality than expected, and the weather sealing is great. Good job with the wiring too. Overall, would be a great unit for a large machine that wasn't going to be off-road.

title: Not made well.
text: The recess for the pull cable is elongated, allowing the barrel to "cock" in the recess and scrape against the throttle housing, making the throttle sticky and rough. Like having cruise control (not a super good thing for a MX bike!)

title: Cheaply made, aluminum conductors, but it works
text: Might be a beck part, but the conductors are aluminum (not brass like stock and other brands). Just a cheap cap, but it works...

title: Too fat to work. Won't clear bore they go down to screw-in
text: Body section is too fat to fit into recess. These are unusable until I can get someone to bore out the hole these go into (threads appear correct, but the body is too fat to fit the bore these have to recess down into to be able to screw-in.

title: Didn't use, looked to chintzy, black is just a thin sticker.
text: This isn't an epoxied-in logo, it's a solid brass, plain plaque with a black sticker with the letters cut out of it. Looks pretty cheap.

title: Not as light as you'd think
text: Not as light as I thought it was going to be. Still needed a LOT of counter weight to balance it.

title: One out of two were bad, haven't tested more
text:
Wish I had a better review, but out of the first two we used, one leaked at the seam where it's supposed to be fused together. Installed on a 750 Vulcan. Under the tank, pain in the arse to get to and replace, but dripping gas is a pain too.

Edit: Carbs taken apart after two of these filters on for a few weeks, rust and other junk in carbs that were cleaned and spotless before. These don't seem to actually filter.

title: Mine came as counterfeit, other's may have better luck
text: What out people. Ordered a few of these and what came was counterfeit. Check Timken site for how to tell. Hope you get the real thing if you order.

title: Great deal and quality boot. Worth it.
text: Appear to be top-quality, really. Can't tell from OEM. Rubber seems firm, but pliable. For the price, they're worth just getting to have a backup since these do crack within a few years (OEM do).

title: Superlative quality cables, made in the USA (trash your AC's, get these!)
text:
Pretty picky about parts anymore, esp. since most of the AC Delco Professional parts I have used turned out to be PURE JUNK! These wires were bought to replace a set of "genuine" AC Delco Professional plug wires that lit up like a Christmas tree under the hood with so many shorts coming straight out of them, it's a wonder the truck even ran (though the light show was outstanding!). The AC's were six-months old. Piles of shyst!

Anyway, these came and I was dumbfounded to find that they actually fit, down to each different wire, and they went on easy with a firm seating. Best of all, they were made in the USA (as if that matters to anyone but me anymore...)

All in all, these were MORE than worth their price. Way more so than the AC's.

title: Great idea, but dim light and one separated from its mount within an hour (see pics)
text: Liked them when I installed, but like other reviewers point out, they just are not bright. The reason for the low rating for me was that not an hour after installing, one of them separated from its stud. In my garage. Brushing against it. Even if these are flexible enough to withstand brush and what not, they will still come apart at the weakest place, where they mount. Sigh...

title: All is lost, even AC is crap now...
text: These have around 400 miles on them. Went to put a vac hose back on behind the carb that had worked loose and was whistling, touched one of the plug wires coming off the distro and shocked the s**t out of myself. Subsequently touched each and each were shorting to anything that would give a ground (me). Junk. All is lost if you buy "genuine" OEM AC parts and they're crap out the chute. Won't buy again. Will use anything but AC from now on. No wonder it misfires now and then...

title: Screws in clickers just spin around, cheap, but also cheaply made
text: Bought one of these same alarms before and no problems, this one (so far, haven't even tried to install it) has issues with both clickers. Went to install new (quality, ie; not Chinese) batteries in the clickers and can't. The bottom screws on each one just spins around. I'll probably pull the screws and glue back in, but still...

title: Light, seems high-quality
text: Wrong number was sent, but it fit perfectly anyway. Will update review once I get a chance to ride with it and see how durable it is.

title: Good quality, comes with pads
text: Appears super-high quality, comes with good pads, but the one I got was for the wrong side...

title: Appear to be high quality fans.
text: Seemed good quality, but didn't fit my application. With mounting tabs, wider than expected.

title: A step up from Harbor Freight quality
text: Better than Harbor Freight, but not much. It works if you are gentle with it.

title: Bright, long lasting. Will likely buy these again
text: These are bright and have lasted a while now. No problems. Using in instruments (after installing a modular voltage reg at the back of the cluster)

title: Fit, worked, still working.
text: It fit. It worked. Still working. Pretty much plug and play.

title: Worked perfect, fit great, seem good quality
text: These worked. They fit. The nuts are larger than stock, but seem OK quality. Will update listing if I end up breaking one.

title: All parts appear high quality, good deal.
text:
Have not installed, but all parts appear very high quality. Very good deal for the price!
---------
Update: The pressed-in liner (steel/cast iron?) is noticeably thinner than the stock Yamaha barrel liner. Not sure what that will mean with longevity, but it might actually cool better since there's more aluminum fin than steel (for heat transfer). But you won't be able to bore this over any more than it is. Haven't run it, but so far impressed with quality of parts. FYI: stock piston/rings/pin weigh 242gms. This piston is at 252gms. Not sure there's enough material to machine 10gms off to balance to factory.

title: Does not appear Excel quality and nuts (nipples) are WAY too large for Kawi rims
text: Cheap zinc-plated spokes and oversize nipples (nuts). Nuts are way too large for holes in KDX200 rim and even drilling them wouldn't work as the head of the nipple is huge and will protrude into the rim band too much, probably causing blown tubes on a regular basis. The bag was marked with an Excel number, but don't look like Excel quality. Probably cheap, Chinese stuff re-packaged. If you want something to fit your KDX200, keep looking, these aren't it.

title: Outstanding for the price
text: OMG, total quality for the price (thin metal and obviously China made, but overall, they work well!)

title: Wide, but well built
text: Wider than it looks in the pic. Didn't work for my application, but it appears very well made, tough, like it will last forever.

title: It "looks" real, but works like a fake...
text: Cheaply made brass bit that looks like a compression release lever, but binds up and doesn't work like one.

title: Better braking and a pound lighter!
text: Felt an immediate difference in braking, even before it was fully bedded. And the bike is felt-lighter in side to side corners. This disc is almost a pound lighter than the stock Triumph Thruxton disc it replaced.

title: Feels like a replica, but it works
text: Kind of cheaply made, but it does work.

title: Threads will not fully thread into primary cases, useless
text: "Almost" screws-in, but only half-way. Threads look fine, but they're cut wrong apparently. Tried on two different primary covers, both do the same thing. Won't screw down, threads tighten up half-way into the case and won't screw-in any further. Was probably a reject part that got re-sold.

title: Threads-on great, but missing the half-moon cut on the end that indexes it so it won't unscrew, easy fix
text: At least the threads are correct, but the half-moon cut that keeps the brake nut from unscrewing itself was lacking. Had to grind that in with a sanding drum on a dremmel tool. So now it "indexes" when you adjust it and stays put.

title: Excellent quality coils!
text: Excellent coils. Perfect for getting good spark to an old Enfield.

title: So far so good, heavy made and high quality.
text: Never regret getting the better parts. The after-market radiators have all been junk, breaking the neck off, leaks, etc., but the Nissans are the best, prob better quality than Behr now.

title: Very happy with these grips. Well-made and soft that dampens vibrations.
text: Excellent grips that are soft and cushy that really reduce vibration to the hands. Didn't expect that, was just looking for vintage-type grips for a classic Royal Enfield (a vibration monster!) One tip, just super glue gel or grip glue on them, NOT contact cement. And clean inside with carb or brake cleaner first to remove the slippery mold release.

title: Good quality for the price
text: Good quality, especially for the price. Unusual adjustment, but works.

title: Perfect fit, good deal on a good part.
text: Perfect fit, works just as advertised. Great deal!

title: Brittle material
text: Looks great, but brass is very brittle.

title: Much lighter, but same braking
text: Lighter than stock by almost a pound, but don't notice a lot of difference in braking.

title: Looks cool, but will just not fit. Stock works, this doesn't.
text: Really wanted to like these India-made brass parts, but they're batting about 100 right now. This part is improperly bent and the way it's made could NEVER work on a Royal Enfield with 7/8" bars. Maybe 1/2" bars, but not anything standard. Looks cool in pics, but you'll spend more time trying to get it to fit and work than the part, or a while bike, is worth.

title: Seem very high quality, but springs are large diameter (OD) and interfere with frame on my machine.
text: First, I want to say these seem like quality shocks, not Chinese junk, even though they probably are made in China. I can't use them because the spring outside diameter is too large and hits the frame (see pics). Shame. The crappy stock shocks I was trying to replace are..., crappy stock shocks. I'll keep searching I guess.

title: Key stuck first time I tried after opening package. Not confident I'll get it unlocked if I use it.
text: Seems strong, well-made, except for one thing, the key sticks in the lock. First time I used it and I've only used it twice since then for worry of not being able to get it unlocked. You have to jiggle and force and try this and that to get the key in, then to get it to turn. Not confidence inspiring at all.

title: God filter if you get at a good price
text: These are the better filters. They do come with the O-ring and drain gaskets as-shown.

title: Only the filter, not the O-ring or drain plug washer like all the others include
text: Does NOT include the filter stand O-ring (large O-ring on filter cover that all others include) or a new copper washer for drain plug. Just the filter, that's all that you get.

title: Fit perfectly and Renthal sprockets have been tougher than any I've used.
text: The strongest, light and last forever. No problems with fit and finish is excellent.

title: Yamaha factory part, works as new
text: Factory part, works as it should, no issues.

title: Works like a charm (whatever a charm is??)
text: Finally got a chance to use this and when you follow instructions to a "T" (totally no fun, but...), it works like magic. Takes some pressure, but letting it heat up good and hot is key, along with slow, steady, firm pushing, not trying to rip right through. Works, gets hot, REALLY hot, and cuts a lovely groove that looks factory. Also, the package said it was made in U.S.A., I looked at a map of China and couldn't find that town? Odd. No matter, quality built and works just as it says. Before, during and after pics with the groover.

title: Good build quality, wide, lightweight, but the grate is VERY sharp, like handling razors.
text: Very lightweight, wide (true 12") and very well built. But..., the grate that makes up the traction bed is EXTREMELY sharp! Cut my hand just pulling it out of the shipping box. Thought it over and since I have many people help me with loading and unloading, I wasn't going to put everyone at risk, or have to carry two pairs of heavy leather gloves for myself and anyone who'd help me load/unload with this ramp, so I'm returning it, unused (save for the hand bloodying). Shame as it seems a great ramp otherwise, just don't know how to deal with the sharp, unfinished edges of the grate that runs the length of it? Mfg can't take the time to deburr every edge of the grate, so I'm not sure how they can fix the problem either. Oh well. If you can deal with always having to use gloves to handle or use this, it's a great ramp otherwise.

title: Quality radiator, but this one had a fit issue, I think different from what it was supposed to be
text: Look very high-quality build, but was too short to mount in stock position (maybe this is a different radiator than what Amazon lists for my vehicle?)

title: Fit great, look good, but feel a little fragile.
text:
Good protection for paint scratches (most of the paint is gone now in the area this covers, from boots touching). They seem like a fragile plastic material. Time will tell. They fit fine and look good on the bike.

UPDATE 2021: These have held up better than I thought they would, 4x years now and they're still good. Fit wasn't perfect, but you can fudge them around and manage. These are sold as '95-'01, but I installed on an '03.

title: Awesome machinging and seems good quality, but one design flaw
text: One problem with these, they have semi-closed ends, meaning they go over the end of the handlebars. If you don't hacksaw it off, you're risking a skyrocketing engine when you lowside in dirt (this was bought for a dirtbike). It will hold the throttle open when you lay it over. The machining and quality look superb. For a streetbike, these are the ticket!

title: Well-made trousers for MX, good deal
text: Got these on a closeout for a killer price. Love them. Large leather patches inside the knees where MX pants always wear holes (if you're gripping tight with your legs like I DON'T do). Fit perfect, look great. No complaints.

title: Working, but return spring inside is insanely strong
text:
It's working, but the return spring is incredibly strong, caused an extra hour for the install, as the T-out was having to push against the return and I kept thinking something wasn't right, take trans out, check all dims/specs, try again, something resisting, repeat. Till I realized it was this.

Been in and working for a week now, no issues. Will report back for long-term eval.

title: Seems high quality
text: Tight and feel like high quality. Time will tell, but that's initial impression from installing this chain a few days ago.

title: Well-made, affords good range of motion, but not a lot of support Worth the price though.
text: Well--made, but was not enough support for me, needed hard brace. This is worth the price, IMO.

title: Clutch side is unusable as manufactured - PICS
text:
First, these are nicely machined and well put together pieces. Look very high quality. But...

Clutch side is just wrong. Won't work on any human-sized bike. Lever mount is grossly mis-sized, holds the lever 6" away from the bar. 4" away at the lowest setting which is still too far for normal human finger, let alone needing to wrap around the lever to grip it. What were they thinking? Look at pics, you'll see what I mean.

Also, I could have, might have, kept the kit and just used the master cyl as that fit fine, but the mirror mount was right below the throttle cables on my bike (adventure bike) with the dual cable setup that is above the bar (like a dirtbike throttle). So I would have to find another place to mount a mirror. In the end it was too much headache, so I returned them.

title: OK, light, but felt low-quality
text: Light was more than Halogen, but not a lot. And not worth the PITA to mount the ballast they come with and make space for the fan at the back of these. Also, both had fans that were loose and felt like they'd fall off with vibration.

title: Look nice, but engineering fail
text: Where they mount puts the deflector too far back on the handlebar (as close as you can get to the grip, on the other side of the switches) to cover the grip/lever, so they're still exposed to weather, branches, etc. Also, it's a hard plastic material and I'd expect the mount to immediately snap off if hit by a branch. More for wind protection, but again, because of how they mount they won't protect the hands much from wind.

title: Mediocre material (melts with pump B20), but works for a while
text: Whatever these are made of doesn't hold up to even B20 (20% biodiesel). If you are running any amount of biodiesel at all, expect to change these out often. Just melts the rubber.

title: Changed review (five to two stars for lack of quality in new models)!
text: Had good luck with my first pair of these (lost off the back of a cycle trailer, forgot to put in truck), second set is VERY different quality! Strap pulled out first day using (see pics), stitching is crappy and glue just didn't even work apparently (looks like they hot-glue them in, then stitch them through the plastic??). Then second day of enduro riding weekend, the stitching started coming apart in other places. So for one weekend, these couldn't even hold up. Poor quality now. Went from five to two stars (still might protect, if they don't fall apart on you first!)

title: Waste of $'s for me, might work for someone else.
text: Unlike most reviewers, I not only found no difference, but it seemed to make the off-idle hesitation worse. Wow, what a waste of $'s this was. They seem to work for other people, but not for me. 4.3l S10 Chevy with an off-idle stumble.

title: Good quality and faster shipping than estimated
text: Came fast (shipped much faster than the Amazon estimates) and appear to be very good quality (no burrs on threads, good polish, etc.), well worth the $'s.

title: Work as they should, fold out and stay stiff
text: Appear to be good quality (for the price) and do what they say, fold out of the way for trail/street bikes.

title: Work and look great.
text: Tape is quite thin, but it's the 3m stuff so darned if it doesn't stick (if you heat it and your tank up a bit before sticking). Make sure you hold pressure for a while, and use a hair dryer to heat the tank and the tape.

title: They're straight and they work
text: They're pushrods. They're hard and long and work properly. Not much else to say.

title: OK and it works, but piston seems in different place than stock.
text: Had to cut the rod down to work the clutch properly, the piston in this seems to sit higher in the bore.

title: Good deal on a good filter for Triumph twins
text: These are the ones that work on Triumphs (Henkley 865 twins). Keep oil clean, fit properly, tighten properly and are short enough (identical to genuine Triumph filters) to tuck up into the frame, out of the way of debris. Overall a good deal on a good filter.

title: Seems quality, but boots are total rubbish. Came apart in a month and a half of mostly sitting and one freeway trip.
text: Installed about six-weeks ago. Seemed quality made. Went under truck to change oil and noticed both of these have split boots, right in the middle, around the circumference, like there was a parting line in the rubber circumferentially and it just split all the way around there. So..., now I pull it and replace the boots before winter and salt builds up inside..., sigh..

title: Light and cheaply made, but works and seems reliable, a fantastic deal for the price!
text: Incredibly cheaply made, but taking it apart, the solder joints on the solid state board look good and it works. For the price, this is an outstanding deal all around.

title: Very bright and seem like a quality product
text: Just as they say, they are super bright. Have tried a lot of the cheapo LED replacement bulbs, most were shoddy quality or just not bright. I've had them that were OK brightness, but very little difference from running and brake lights. These are different. Different enough to tell that it's brake and not running lights so that's good enough for me.

title: Matches great.
text: Expensive for what it is, but matches perfectly. Brush has a permanent bend in the bristles, knocked one star off for quality.

title: Definitely are brighter than other 1157 LED bulbs I've tried
text: True to what they claim, they are very bright. Brighter than the Sylvania dedicated red LED brake light bulb that I had previously installed. Probably equal to, or just a bit brighter than a standard 1157 incandescent bulb.

title: Good quality, fit perfect
text: Good quality and fit properly. Good deal, esp. if changing tie rod ends, makes things so much easier (paint after adjusting to minimize rust issues).

title: Might be an OK part, but didn't fit contrary to Amazon's saying it would
text: Amazon showed it was the right part. Was WAY not the right part...

title: Avoid, crap quality
text: Total crap. Switch internally didn't connect. No QC on this product at all.

title: Small and not the best quality
text: These are a lot smaller than they look and not great quality.

title: NOT at all like the pic, standard PP and clutch, but German and good quality
text: NOT like the picture. What comes is a standard multi-petal pressure plate (not the three-actuator like in pic) and a standard comp clutch (NOT like four-puck ceramic shown in pic). They are LUK, German though. Overall it's OK, but they need to change the pic!

title: Good quality, but sealed bag was missing some parts
text: These seem good quality, not junk, but one of the factory-sealed bags was missing the fine-thread nuts. Quick trip to HW store fixed that, but it was an annoyance. Makes me wonder about the rest of the products QC?

title: Love these
text: Love these grips. Have install on countless bikes. Everyone comments how they feel and grip. Excellent at reducing vibration too.

title: They fit, work, but are softer than you might expect.
text: These fit and work, but are softer than I thought they'd be, being poly bushings (more like a rubber material).

title: No difference noticed

text: Bought for an Enfield Bullet 350 (1964 vintage, but with 70's forks - same as later forks too). Perfect fit. OK quality and shipping from India was unbelievably fast. Kudo's to seller for shipping fast and outstanding quality given the price. We'll see how long they last, but can't really complain given the price, shipped from India. title: Extremely high quality, thick, strong, includes all-stainless hardware. Didn't fit for me, but had to leave review for others.
text:
The good: After having looked these over, I have to say I'm impressed with the quality. They are thick and sturdy and not easily bent, the chrome is good quality (doesn't chip at the bends if you do manage to bend them to fit) and the most impressive is that they come with VERY high quality stainless-steel mounting hardware. The bad: These are not even CLOSE to being able to fit 43mm (their advertised max sizing). See pics attached, attempting to fit onto 41mm forks. Tried to bend them out to fit, but no luck. Still had to up my review a few stars for their quality and quality of included hardware. For the price, they're an excellent value (and I say that as someone who can't use them for my application).

title: Two issues to be aware of...(WARNING)
text:
Just figured out why this bogged so badly. Tried enrichening with needle position while on bike (XT225), still didn't help, so pulled carb and testing the accel pump on the bench. Not spray. At all. With a full float bowl.

Pulled the bowl and find two issues with this NEW carb. One, there was no spring for the accelerator pump, so the piston was just sitting in its bowl cavity. Had to bang the bowl upside down a while to get the piston out. It just sat on the bottom of its hole, no way to actually pump anything. There was probably supposed to be a spring under the piston so it could actually move up and down to pump and not sit on the bottom doing nothing.

Second issue, first time I took the bowl off, the gasket was swollen from the fuel (mind you, this is a NEW carb that had never been apart), so much so it was about 10% oversize, so reinstalling was a total pain and it leaks (seeps) now (prob because it's not fully in its cavity as it won't properly fit anymore). The fuel here has 10% ethanol in it, but bloody hell, you'd think a NEW, modern carb would be able to handle pump fuel??

So, just fair warning: Don't assume anything just because it's new. Fill it with fuel on the bench and check the accelerator pump action to see if it actually mists fuel. TWO, order some float bowl gaskets now. These aren't modern-fuel resistant and will be so swollen, you won't be able to get it back together if you do have to take it apart (it'll be kind of like a Holly, where you have to replace the gasket anytime you take the float bowl off).

Leaks and won't stop till I find a replacement rubber gasket that isn't too swollen to fit, so lowered another star (that and the following response from Powersport Superstore: "I do apologize for the inconvenience, however if you contact the manufacturer Mikuni with this inquiry they will be able to do the warranty for you on this.")

Scummy deal all the way around. Summer has only so many days and I'm wasting half of them NOT riding because of the QC of these new Mikuni carbs...

title: Works well, but don't trust the LED completely.
text:
I had a dead battery in an old Toyota Sequoia (5.7L V8 engine), so dead that I couldn't get a light or a chirp out of it. So I tried this handy Noco jump starter. I had it fully charged, connected it up as directed, and ... nothing, nada, not even lights on the console. The Noco was signaling (based on the manual) that the truck's battery wasn't completely at zero, had a little juice left (white LED was on). Then I thought, what makes me believe that LED anyway, I think the battery is completely kaput. Next step, I used the "manual override" on the Noco to provide full power. Result: truck responded immediately; all the console lights came on, systems started booting up, and the engine cranked once but didn't start, then started easily on the second try.

Afterwards, I checked the remaining battery level on the Noco, and was pleased to see that it was barely depleted. That's reassuring, in case you're on the road and might need to use it multiple times. (It does come with a car charger, but the charging is quite slow.)

Overall verdict: a handy little gizmo to have in the garage, and perhaps on a long road-trip, but don't expect it to be perfect in the information it's giving you. In case of doubt, try the so-called manual override.

title: It works, but it's noisy & slow
text:
First thing to report is that the pump does the job, and the gauge is quite accurate. So it serves my purpose, which is to have a pump in the garage which can help me pump up tires to the right pressure, without too much difficulty, and without having to do it manually using a hand pump.

The flexible coiled air hose connected to the stem coming out of the pump fine, but I found I needed a couple of tries to get that to go in right. I had no trouble connecting the tip of the hose to the valve stem, and screwed it in all the way (you hear a little hiss of escaping air to tell you that you're almost there). Then it was just a matter of using a long-enough extension cable, pushing the on button, and keeping an eye on the gauge. I found it better to over-inflate by a pound or two, and then release the air to the right point using a gauge with a bleed valve, rather than trying to get it just right and then losing too much air while removing the hose.

Negatives: This is a small and noisy pump, and lower-powered than I'd hoped. The label says 1.5A, so 165W, which means about 0.22hp, and that's the input, not the output. So it's probably putting out about 0.15hp at best. Yes, that's about what an average human can do with a two-handled pump. But, using electrical power is certainly easier. It also gets quite hot after a few minutes of use, and you have to let it cool down.

I had an suv tire that was down about 8lb, and this thing had to labor long and hard to get that pumped up. WIth car tires that were down about 2 lb, it was relatively easier, since the amount of air needed to make up the difference was much smaller.

title: decent but not perfect directions, traffic updates are terrible
text:
I'll keep this short, since there are so many detailed reviews up already.

1. This is a decent gps unit, will (mostly) get you there, although the routing might not always be what a native would pick. For instance, if you know that one route has a lot of traffic lights, and a back road that's slightly longer but light-free, don't expect the GPS to pick the latter. That's a failing of all GPS units, they depend on the data and the routing rules written for them. They haven't suddenly become smarter than humans, and that's perhaps a good thing. (Sure, there are ways to write smarter routing rules, but it costs time & money to do that, and to collect the supporting data.)

2. Ease of use is pretty good. On a long highway trip (2000+ miles) I found the "what's ahead" feature quite useful for finding gas stations and restaurants, although sometimes the data was out of date. (Another common failing of GPS units, blame our dynamic economy.)

3. The traffic reporting is worse than useless. I found that using Google maps with traffic was much better than relying on "Garmin traffic". Mostly what I experienced was no traffic problems reported when there were severe problems present. For example, I have found myself in the Boston area and on the NJ Turnpike in the middle of massive traffic jams, while this unit blithely reports no problems whatsoever. Garmin really completely messed this up, probably because they didn't want to pay for good traffic data.

4. The display is pretty good, easy to read, and the functions are mostly easy to use. But there's one thing I found very poorly designed, and I wonder what they were thinking: you should be able to easily save your current location as a "favorite" saved destination. So all you do is find the "save this location" button, right? Wrong. There just isn't a good way to do it. (If there is, someone tell me, I'll edit the review.)

So what's my recommendation? Buy the lifetime maps if all you want is a reasonable GPS unit. If you must buy the traffic option, don't bet your schedule on it.

title: noisy, imperfect, but effective & useful
text:
I have a lot of uses for a product like this: I have floats and tubes to inflate in the summer, large exercise balls and air mattresses to inflate around the year, and of course bike and car tires to inflate as needed.

So the ability to inflate high volume items (air mattresses & tubes/floats), as well as other items that need a specific pressure (tires), is great to have in a single product.

And this product does deliver all that, effectively. You can, with little effort, inflate an air mattress from zero to usable in just a few minutes. You can, with little effort, set a target pressure and re-inflate your bicycle tires very quickly.

You should also know that the product comes with an assortment of nozzles that covers most household uses, including the needle type nozzle for balls (I haven't used that yet; it's winter here).

Criticisms:
- They got too clever with the hoses and the design for tucking them into these nifty slots; they keep falling out. (Not the first time something worked on paper but not in the real world.)
- The unit is really quite noisy when it's working. Possibly fixable in a later revision.
- Can't be used while plugged in to an AC outlet. (According to the manual, can be used while plugged in to a car battery, but I haven't tried this.)

So overall, a pretty useful product, with some deficiencies that don't seriously take away from the usefulness.

title: Works well for securing the pivot screw of a folding knife
text:
I purchased this because I have a folding knife with a pivot screw that I needed to keep in a specific position. It's a Kershaw Leek, which has a torsion bar assisted action. If you tighten the pivot screw too much, the torsion bar can't overcome the friction and the knife doesn't open. If you tighten it too little, the blade snaps into position but while locked wobbles between both halves of the handle. However, if you get the tension just right, you avoid both problems.

The issue is that after only a few cycles the screw will have loosened slightly and the blade starts wobbling again. The solution is to use a little bit of Loctite on the screw so that it will not unthread on its own. Since the pivot screw on the Leek is less than 1/4" (or 6mm), I followed Loctite's recommendation and used the purple threadlocker (Loctite 222).

Before using the locker, the screw would become loose within a day or two of tightening it. After using it and letting it cure for 24h, the screw is still secure after at least four weeks and shows no sign of loosening. Seems that the problem has been solved.

I have not yet tried removing the screw, so I don't know how difficult it will be to service the knife. I used a generous amount, applied using a toothpick to the screw, then wiped away the excess once I had the screw tightened to where I wanted it. Cleanup was trivial.

So far, would recommend for this purpose.

title: Very useful for cleaning the inside of the windshield
text:
For context, I have an '05 Subaru Outback 2.5. I purchased the unit with the aerosol, but I've used the manual spray with good results.

This has always been the trickiest part of the cleaning the car - finding the right angle, using a perfectly clean cloth, making sure you have no streaks - and I usually fail, though I don't figure it out until I'm driving into the sun a couple days later. Since I armor-all the dashboard I tend to get some buildup on the interior of the windscreen, so I need to attend to it at least twice a year even if no one touches the surface.

This particular design is just OK - it does the job you want it to do. The wand form factor leaves a bit to be desired - the flat head of the wand pivots a bit too easily, and does not flex as readily as it could to conform to the surface of the window. The pad under the cleaning bonnet could be thicker. The bonnet could fit more securely over the wand head. The wand head could be a bit smaller to be easier to maneuver. The storage sack could be a bit larger.

All of that said, though, it functioned perfectly well for my purposes - it cleaned the windshield easily and thoroughly with only two passes, leaving no streaks behind. Nothing failed during use. It was much less awkward to use than hand towels. It collected all the oils in one go. The bonnet stayed secure the entire time. Basically, despite there being room for improvement, it is functionally complete. I should have purchased something like this years ago.

So would recommend if you have the issue with a streaky windshield interior and aren't as flexible as you used to be.

title: Effective system for removing surface scratches and improving the look of deeper ones
text:
A while back I was backing into a parking space and, due to the unusually tight quarters, ended up scraping the rear driver-side fender of my '05 Subaru Outback against a the rusting pole of a basketball hoop. Nothing seriously damaged, but looked like hell, a big whitish-grey arc of abrasions. All of it was plastic, no metal was harmed, and everything at the ridge of the fender was down to the black plastic, so I knew I wouldn't clean it up completely, but I wanted to help make it less noticeable.

3M is generally a reputable brand, so I purchased this kit. I used a battery-powered drill at high speed to apply it, and made several passes over the affected area, following the instructions closely. It was a fairly cool, clear day, with some cloud cover.

The result was that almost all the swirls and scratches are gone - or if not gone, then only visible in the right light. Basically, I have the paint, I have a few narrow bits of black plastic where the paint was totally removed, but you'd only notice it if you were looking right at the fender. Not great if I wanted it to look like new, but I'm the third owner of a car that is more than fifteen years old and even though this is my first significant scratch, it's only the latest of many.

Also, I used the rubbing compound to polish up my headlights, and it worked perfectly - though without a UV protector, they fogged up again in about a year.

So it worked as described. The only complaint I have is that the packets of polishing compound they give you are small, and more importantly, impossible to re-seal. I would have preferred a standard squeeze-bottle or paste-tube with a screw-cap, as when I returned to the kit many months later, the paste was mostly dry even though I tried to seal the slit shut with tape.

Nevertheless, would recommend.

title: Quite strong, stiff, sturdy, but could stand to include a couple thinner tools as well

title: Great fit, but very, very tight fuse slots
text:
Vehicle: 2005 Subaru Outback Limited (H4 automatic)

Note: These come with 15A fuses. I was installing a dashcam running on USB 2.0 power, which wouldn't even hit a full 1A, so I swapped in 5A mini-fuses. I don't think Muhize offers this combination. However, 5A fuses are cheap to procure. This is mostly to protect the lengthy dashcam power cable, which probably could take 15A but I saw no reason to risk it.

I purchased these to power my dashcam - a Viofo A119v3 - off of the battery, specifically ACC and door locks. The taps fit very will in the fuse box, even the fuses on the taps fit over neighboring mini-fuses. They fit into the fuse box quite easily - though the '05 Outback has plenty of space to work with. The attached wire is flexible, easy to work with, and soldered up nicely.

The fuse slots, however, are extremely tight, more so than is even typical of most fuses slots. I tried two different brands of fuses and they were tricky to seat in, I had to sort of effect a see-saw action where I'd work one leg in a little, then the other, alternating back and forth until the fuse was seated. It was the same for both pairs of slots, such that I ended up bending a couple fuses in the process. An pair of adjustable pliers didn't help much, I had to grip the fuse tap and use it to press the fuse again the hard vinyl on the car door.

However, they seated nicely and have been holding solid for several weeks, so I have no complaints. I'd rather the slot be too tight than too loose, of course. Would recommend.

title: Great for fuse taps
text:
Vehicle: 2005 Subaru Outback Limited (H4 automatic)

I purchased these - the whole lot of them - because I needed two 5 Amp Mini fuses to load into a pair of fuse taps I am using to power a dashcam. I chose 5A fuses because the dashcam (a Viofo A119v3) uses the USB 2.0 power standard, which is very low amperage anyway - less than 3A at most - and I wanted more of a safety margin than the 15A fuse the taps came with would give me. The gauge of wire I am using for the power can handle about 15A easily, but there's no point in taking unnecessary risk.

Installation is tricky, I accidentally bent one tap trying to work it into to the tap. I recommend a see-saw approach, if you are having difficulty - apply pressure to one corner, then the other, keeping the fuse relatively level. I had to apply considerable force. A pair of adjustable pliers might also work.

They've been installed and working for a few weeks now, so it seems they are specc'ed properly to allow sufficient current through to the camera. At least I'll have extras if anything goes wrong.

title: OEM battery tie down, easy install
text:
I purchased my 2005 Outback (the 2.5i automatic) second-hand, so it didn't come with a tie-down, though I didn't notice this for about three years. Glad to have gotten a hold of one, because it installed quite easily and fits perfectly.

For install: the nuts are 10mm. The short leg goes through the flat part of the tie-down and behind the "back" of the battery, which is to say the side nearest to the windshield; it hooks onto a little hole back there in the body of the car. The long leg goes through the angled part of the tie-down and in "front" of the battery, the part nearest the windshield washer fluid reservoir; it hooks over a little tab on the battery's platform. I had to attach the short leg first, then the long leg, to get everything situated. and tight.

All well enough. The design of the tie-down itself leaves something to be desired, since it takes some finagling to get it in place, but it definitely does the job.

title: Use better disposable gloves
text:
My first reaction when opening the box of [[ASIN:B00IOBSZJK Turtle Wax (T-128KT) Premium Trim Coating Kit]] was that the enclosed two disposable gloves are the worst possible ones, cheap and cumbersome. Especially with smaller hands, the gloves will be covered with the staining liquid and that can cause you to apply black to areas you do not want it applied. I grabbed some nitrile disposable gloves and headed outside to apply this to the car areas I'd already prepped by cleaning. I also brought some small craft foam pads and a knife in case I needed to cut down the enclosed foam pad. Just in case, I grabbed a roll of removable tape for masking purposes as well as an old towel.

If you can polish your nails, you can apply this coating because the technique is similar, just on a larger scale. With a silver car like mine, it was important to prevent the black stain from touching any areas I did not want dyed black. Using a smooth and deliberate movement, the entire process was quicker than I thought it would be and I did go over areas twice. The car doesn't look brand new, but the faded areas are black again and they do not look terrible. This is likely to fade a lot faster than the original black plastic did, but I don't care because I have most of the bottle remaining for reapplication.

title: Want to protect 4 doors? You will need 2 packages
text:
I really wanted to apply this [[ASIN:B00IOQHRH6 3M 90211 36" Paint Defender Door Edge Protection Film]] to the doors of the car that parks next to me in our parking lot, but alas, I settled with touching up the little paint dings on my car doors at the same time I touched up my door edges. After I was sure the paint had ample time to dry, I cleaned the door edges with alcohol and allowed them to air dry. This was done on a day with no wind or rain to debris was prevented from blowing onto the adhesive of the strip.

For installation, I referenced the enclosed manual with photos even though I'd already read them on the package. Because the strips were both on a single log strip of backing, I sliced the length to make application easier, one strip at a time. For me, that additional minute saved me time in the long run. I also cut the end of the strip because I preferred a straight edge and not the rounded edge as it was manufactured. Applying the strip was similar to putting on a screen protector, stretching the tape a bit to prevent bubbling. I first applied the exterior, cut the strip just above the bottom of the door edge, then folded it over to the interior a little bit, attaching it up the length of the door edge. At this time, I pushed down the entire interior edged strip. Now the entire strip was secure and after I removed the protective sheet, it was rather benign on the door. The product is good and was not difficult to apply. I'll likely get another package for my rear doors.

title: SEE MY UPDATE!  Watch out what you wish for
text:
My UPDATE first, then you can continue reading if you'd like:
When I scanned my car last month, everything was okey dokey. The emissions light came on today while I was driving my Honda Accord. Yeoww, I thought, better take it to a mechanic right away. I quicklyl remembered this bright little device I had dropped into my cup holder for later storing and realized I could run a little scan on the car before taking the car for service. Unfortunately, my smartphone had been switched out and I no longer had the app on the new phone. No problem cause I just installed it on the new phone from Play Store. It installed in a few seconds and I was good to go. Turned on Bluetooth, plugged in the U-Scan and this time, the car was identified and the make, model and the VIN were added. I then ran a scan and received a message of Emissions failure listing the component that failed!! I take back all my negative thoughts and comments and changed my rating from three stars to five. If you continue reading this review, you'll see the reason for my title for this review.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: The package destroyed my new manicure and I'm not thrilled. I needed a screwdriver to access the inside pair of tabs, then by holding the case upside down between my knees, I was finally able to manipulate the base of the case top, thereby finally exposing the pearl inside, a scanner that is perched atop a perfectly formed base. I cannot imagine that anyone will store their tool in the case and although I am creative, I will not contemplate alternate uses for it. Unfortunately, it will be put into the recycling bin where I hope it can be recycled. The case is more sturdy than the scanner and it is waste.

The hard shell packaging case is perhaps a hint from Actron that the consumer needs to be prepared to ¨shell out¨ for any valuable diagnostics. In order to use the [[ASIN:B00DDV2NL2 Actron CP9599 U-Scan OBD II and CAN Code Scanner]], you must purchase other apps from about $8 upwards. The tool is orange and black, its plastic is lighter in weight than the case.

As soon as I'd requested this product, I downloaded the necessary app onto my smartphone, so with bluetooth enabled on my Samsung Galaxy S5 and the key turned in the car, the device was recognized quickly and immediately updated the firmware. This is necessary for the device to work, according to the on screen message. I started the app again and entered the data of the first car, including the VIN number. The app shut down, so I restarted. That happened again and then it remained on. I ran the scan with a touch to an icon and it came back without a discovered problem, but I then was offered the opportunity to purchase more from Actron in order to scan for more information. I instead headed out to hunt down a car with a problem. I tested two other cars, finding no scanned problems with either. When I finally use this on a car which shows a problem code, I'll update the review and let you know if I've shelled out any money to Actron. Wish me luck because I really want to see what happens with a car with an emissions issue.

If you're interested in this item, check out their online videos to see how it works. I wish I had.

text:
Nelson Rigg is my go to for quality gear that does not cost an arm and a leg. I had the previous generation of these before and they lasted 5+ years of fairly serious adventuring.

I installed these on my F800GS (with Happy Trail racks) and used them for a cross country adventure trip this spring. They stayed in place, kept my stuff dry, and did not mind the tip overs.

The all metal hardware is a nice touch, since I’ve broken quite a few plastic clips on other bags.

The inner liners work really well and it’s extremely convenient for taking stuff in and out of your motel room. I actually like this system better than taking the entire bag off, since the bags are often covered in dirt, and dragging all that into a hotel room is a jerk move.

The pads between the bag and the racks look a bit goofy, but work well.

The only downside to these is that they don’t breathe or drain at all. So after a few days you’ll start getting some condensation inside the bags. Just need to remember to air them out once in a while.

text:
Pros: Well made. High quality materials.

Cons: The design seems to emphasize light weight and comfort over protection.

Coming from a car racing background, where I regularly use a HANS device, I feel that this product is a bit of a gimmick. Maybe my head/neck/shoulders are shaped weird, or my helmet isn't quite right, but I didn't feel like the brace would really do much to prevent the side to side or front movement. This is mostly due to it's low profile, but there is also nothing preventing the edge of the helmet from sliding right off of it's smooth surface. If anything, I felt like, in the case of side movement, the brace created a weird fulcrum point once the helmet slid past it. It's also very flexible, which leads me to question how much it would help against a significant impact. I tinkered with adjustments quite a bit, but still really did not see how it would significantly increase my safety. I definitely understand why people love this brace - it is very comfortable and unobtrusive, but I feel like it does this by sacrificing actually being a safety device. I ended up returning mine as I didn't see the point in using it, and will be trying different manufacturers.

title: Most unpleasant trailer t-connector install I have ever done
text:
Yep folks, the trailer light t-harness install on your gen 4 RAV4 is going to be a real bear for you. Much like "M. Williams" the install on my 2017 took me about 6 hours. This may have been because I was recovering from surgery and had to move pretty slow, so I didn't start bleeding profusely again. Had I been in better health and shot-gunned a Rockstar first, there's a remote possible snowball's chance, that my time would have been more inline with "The Professor" at 2 hours, but I doubt it, because I'm pretty old.

I think that unless you are a skilled mechanic with car lift, you'd be hard pressed to get this done "start to finish total" in less than two hours. At the same time though, I think somebody saw Harley coming, and bent him down hard. This t-harness along with the Draw-Tite 75235 could both be had on Amazon for $200 total at the time of my purchase. Yeah it's a time consuming suck-wad install compared to most other cars, but no way its $400 worth of labor, unless you're paying a sloth used to rolling with fat stacks. I hate to hear about people getting screwed like that; it makes me sad and angry.

Install notes:

I had about a foot left of the black wire after the install (see photo), even though I left slack in places where it made sense to leave slack. This is a great complement to Reese, for not cutting corners. Curt would have given you just enough to save a buck, and blamed it on you after, for not routing it perfect.

The fuse connector that goes to the battery, seems to be unusually good quality (see photo). It's all rubbery, and I think you could drive thru a flood without getting the fuse wet. Speaking of fuse, since I only tow something a few times a year, I usually pull the fuse if I know I'm not going to tow something for a month or more. I had one of Curt's crappy t-harnesses melt on me in another car before, so since then I have been gun-shy. This is not a crappy Curt product, I know that, but still pulling the fuse only takes a minute.

The video that I watched advised you to mount the box under the panel on the driver side, rather than in the spare area. I did that, and discovered that the 4 pole connector and the passenger side harness is not an inch longer that it has to be. I used my Dremel to carve a little plastic off, so I could gain another inch or two for the 4-pole (see photo). It's fine and everything, but you may want to watch a different video, and see where they mount the box. Guessing there would be space underneath the jack toolkit.

Anywho, glad that's over....

title: Best Choice for Gen4 RAV4 IMO
text:
I chose the 75235 because it had the highest tongue weight rating of all receiver hitches available for the Gen 4 Toyota RAV4.

Thus far, I have had the best luck with the Draw-Tite brand in general, as they tend to be built tougher than the competition and they usually have a more practical design.

Included with the 75235 are 5 bolts, 5 washers, and installation instructions. Those instructions are are pretty straight forward.

The only "extra" things you need to do are as follows:

1. Remove the small plastic cover near the factory towing eye using a small flat head screwdriver and a 10mm socket.

2. Remove two bolts holding the factory towing eye

3. Temporary slip the exhaust pipe out of the rubber retainer near the muffler, and slip it back in after you install the hitch. I installed mine myself, by using a box to hold it into place until a got a few threads started on both sides. Probably a little easier though if you have an assistant.

4. After you install the hitch, you will need to cut a small piece out of the plastic cover you removed in step one in order for it to fit over your new hitch. I have uploaded a picture of the small piece I cut off. Don't cut too much!

Well that's it. Even if you never wire your RAV4 for pulling a trailer, it can now accommodate most cargo carriers and bike racks. You also have a few more places to hook ratchet straps and bungee cords onto.

Installation of this fine American Made product was a breeze! The box also worked well to store my brand new factory Toyota mats in the attic. I think they actually make my car look nicer than the factory mats; Gives the interior an industrial sort of look.

title: Perfect for those who like bendy hitches that interfere with exhaust systems
text:
This hitch looks like it is heavy-duty, but it is not. Yeah it has a big thick bar that goes across and looks cool, but the flat metal ears that bolt to your Pontiac Vibe or Toyota Matrix are thin and bend under load. This especially frosts me, because I paid an exhaust shop to shorten the exhaust pipe on my Non-GT AWD Vibe, so this pile of junk wouldn't shake the car at stop signs.

After all this fun and expense courtesy of CURT, I bought the Draw-Tite 24812. This Draw-Tite does NOT interfere with Vibe or Matrix exhaust, and it does NOT have thin little mounting ears which bolt to your car and bend handily under load. I would say the metal on the mounting ears is about 50% thicker on the Draw-Tite, and it covers more area since it bolts to your car with 3 bolts per side instead of the paltry 2 that CURT uses.

This life long CURT customer is officially done with CURT hitches. Just bought a Draw-Tite for my Gen 4 RAV4 also, and was equally impressed with it's quality.

.

title: Fixed the air bag light on my Mazda Tribute
text:
If your air-bag light is on in your Mazda Tribute or Ford Escape, you probably need a tube of this stuff. The air bag light will flash a certain amount of times to signify whether it is the right or left side you need to mess with (google your specific model to find out how many flashes).

Once you figure out what side needs a squirt of this, disconnect the negative battery cable, and leave it sit for 45 minutes; that way the air bag is less likely to deploy while you are messing with the plugs.

Under each front seat, there is a plug for the air bag. Un-plug the plug in question, give a VERY SLIGHT twist of each male prong with a needle nose pliers, put a little bit of this grease on the connectors, plug it back in. Connect the battery cable back up, and cross your fingers that you will likely be rid of your air-bag light dilemma.

title: Vanquished the interior mold stench
text:
For years I religiously sprayed the carpet type factory floor mats for my SUV at the car wash. This process is neither pleasant, clean, or inexpensive.

In the meantime I have been struggling with a moldy smell in my vehicle, which led to an internet search. Turns out that carpeted floor mats trap moisture in the floor mats which festers, and eventually this moisture runs over into the regular car carpet which festers some more.

I later noticed that the local nards had this set on sale with a rebate that brought the price down to ten bucks a set; I pulled the trigger.

I removed the factory floor mats, sprayed the area with Ozium, and let things air for a few days. I installed the Armor All set, and could not be happier. There are vertical grips in the pedal area such that the mat actually decreases pedal fatigue on road trips. Most importantly though, since this set is rubber, there is less opportunity for moisture and spilled liquids to fester. I figure if it is summer, the liquids should evaporate on the mat. If it is winter, one can pull over to a gas station quick, and soak up the liquids off the mat with a paper towel at the pump.

If you get a set of these, I recommend removing them from the package and letting them off-gas on your porch or deck for a couple days. The chemical smell is not the worst I have ever smelled on a new rubber product, but might as well air them out first just for good measure.

**** Star removal update****
After less than two years, one of the floor mats has a large rip in the middle. Not like anybody sits in the car with lawn aerating shoes or anything, so I can just conclude it's cheap rubber. I'll probably get another set of these though, as they were good while they lasted.

title: Don’t even think of using ‘K-Seal’ in your vehicle!
text:
In December 2016 my Audi A4 sedan alerted me to a low coolant level at the reserve tank. I filled it to the indicated level and needed to repeat this again about 10 days later.

After checking for solutions to a minor coolant leak repair, I read a website stating that: “K-Seal is simple to use. You just Shake, Pour & Go… It couldn’t be easier!”

With this assurance, I purchased an 8-ounce bottle of this product at retail store. After carefully reading all of the instructions on the container, I added the contents into the reserve tank.

I did this still concerned whether I was making a mistake; I soon learned that it would be a very big and expensive mistake.

Two days later, and just hours from leaving on a turnpike trip out of state, my indicator lights warned of a coolant problem – accompanied by water temperature readings passing into the danger zone and steam coming from beneath the hood of the vehicle.

I had my vehicle flat-bedded to a trusted repair facility specializing in European vehicles.

The owner-master mechanic soon advised me that there were apparent blockages within the coolant system preventing the flow of coolant within the engine.

When I went to retrieve my Audi several days later, the owner-master mechanic who had performed the repairs advised me that there was no question – whatsoever – that K-Seal had clogged up various points within the coolant system, damaged the water pump impeller and preventing the thermostat from properly functioning.

Not exactly “simple & easy” nor “Suitable for use with all water cooled engines including cars…” that was promised to any consumers of this product!

The damages incurred to repair the vehicle and rent a car were $1,781.

K-Seal refused to resolve my claims and I took it to court. At the hearing, it’s representative, a Patrick O’Brien, said that I was not truthful in my testimony and must have instead used a competitor’s product. Some defense!

Nonetheless, & applying the state consumer protection law, the judge awarded me 3x my damages - $5,500.

title: All Synthetic Oils are Great

The cost difference between a synthetic oil and conventional is very small.  I have done a lot of research, and it seems they are all very good including the Amazon Basics and other store brands.  Maybe something like Amsoil has some better properties, but I doubt you will ever see the benefit because these oils are all so good.  So what is best is to use synthetic oil and change frequently (that will keep you engine cleaner than any more expensive oil).  Don't forget to get a good filter (anything but Fram)  There are only two cases where it might be better to use a conventional oil 1) when breaking in a new engine - but even then I think better to protect the engine as much as possible and use synthetic. 2) old air cooled engines - though I think I'm going to try Royal Purple 30w next time in my VW bus as it costs about the same as conventional 30w oil.  Bottom line, synthetic oils of all brands are good.  Buy an inexpensive one that meets your specifications and change regularly.

text:
UPDATE 15Nov2018: The cover and straps have held up well in summer sun, so I clicked on "buy again" in October only to find the price increased from $16.99 to $26 or so. (Can't blame a 25% tariff for a near 100% increase). Now it's $36.99 (MORE THAN DOUBLE PRICE OF 3-4 MONTHS AGO). So now they get stars knocked down for "bait and switch" tactics, and I fear the new batch (if there is one) will be cheap and flimsy. More victimization of the largest market in the world.
….. HERE IS THE PREVIOUS REVIEW:
First of all, the weight is substantial even without considering the price being under $20. The separate mirror covers allow for it fitting more vehicles, and with a reflective tape, serve to increase visibility when parked overnight, regardless of the weather. I have a larger Jetta and it covers from the wipers up and to the back of the sunroof, so it really helps with sun gain. The elastic straps have a flexible rubber anchor/hook, which means you can use them right on the body paint without worries. I can remove one rear strap and open a rear door, or one front strap for a front door, which is nice when it is wet. It was in place through sustained 30mph winds during the recent hurricane and didn't budge, rip, or flap. The only thing to be reasonable about is the elastic strapping: all elastic will loosen over time and exposure to sun/heat (in which case you can cut/shorten the elastic to the right length). So if you are wise, you'll order a second one as backup after you find the fit good for your vehicle. You cannot get a universal cover, for under $20, made well, and have it last forever. So don't expect a custom fit, and don't complain that $7/year is too much.

text:
Excellent product and online here an excellent price. If I don't get carried away, I get about 5 good uses out of one can on a car with about 18 or 19 inch rims. I find the best way to put on is like this:

1 Wash tire and rim fully.
2 Immediately take the car on a very brief 3 or 5 minute drive.
*You want the tire in my opinion slightly damp for application I feel as it just conditions better*
3 Begin at noon and inner, and work your way out with clockwise motions.
*Don't forget the bottom edge against the ground!*
4 At completion of the fourth tire proceed to first immediately.
5 Use a small sponge presoaked with a spray or too and pass around each tire ONCE and with even speed.
6 Use a whitewall bleach once a month to remove any build up.
7 Have a lemonade.

text:

If there is too much play, then the material no longer contacts the bottom of the filter and debris isn’t blocked. The magnet is also quite weak. title: Well-built but needs a simpler UI
text:
TL;DR: Quality charger with a lot of bang for the buck compared to other name brands. Having a 5amp charger in such a small footprint and a well thought out mounting system is a nice to have. The quality connectors don’t use o-rings that are prone to deterioration and the clamps are well designed in comparison with my older Noco and CTEK chargers. Has a few issues with multi batteries in parallel and a disconnected power draw that is minimal. Voltage display is accurate and makes it easy to monitor a battery.

Quality:
The charger is heavy and does not feel like a cheaper plastic no name brand. It is on par with Noco and CTEK and in some ways better. The clamps are very nicely made and open wide with a low-profile plastic cover to avoid interference. The buttons are a little stiff, but I really like the button rather than the thin plastic over buttons that Noco and CTEK use.

Performance and Ease of Use:
It works well, but the manual is needed when you start using it for the first time. In my opinion the UI could have been a little more intuitive, but it is something you get used to. The two issues I have faced are minor but might be a deal breaker for some.

1) If you plan to use it on multiple batteries in parallel, then monitor it for the first day or so. In my situation I tried to charge four batteries wired in parallel and the charger never kicked off making the batteries hot. This does not happen when using my Noco charger on the same batteries.

2) After around 10 minutes of charging, if you unplug the charger from the wall but not the battery, the charger will stay on. Under 10 minutes or so the charger shuts down as expected. This only draws a max of 40ma or so, but on a small ATV or Motorcycle battery that could cause issues if left unplugged for a while. This does not occur on my Noco or CTEK charger.

Overall:
This is a great charger, and I would recommend it to anyone looking. I think the issues are minor and, in most cases, wouldn’t be a problem. If I have any issues that I haven't already noticed, I will update my review.

Overall:

title: 2 parts 2 failures
text:

Under further examination it looks like the fitting was never even crimped to the hose correctly. I went to my local advance auto part store and picked up their house brand, which just so happens to be made by the same company. This concerned me but I really didn't have any other choice at the time. I swapped that part in and started up the engine. This part, made 2 years later, was leaking around the fitting. I know you are probably assuming it just needed to be tightened more but it wasn't leaking out of the threads but actually where the hose slides into the fitting. This type of leak doesn't change regardless of how tight or loose it is.

Long story short I would not trust this brand to make a quality part and I think you can avoid a lot of hassle with just going for an OEM hose or maybe just another brand.

title: They do not filter odors or pollens
text:
Like many others who have bought these, I have allergies. The kind of allergies where I sneeze so hard and so many times that there are parts of the day where I am incapable of speech. Sadly, I am not finding these to be as helpful where allergies are concerned, but that wasn't my primary reason for buying these.

I bought these for odors, odors like aftershave, perfume, laundry soap, air fresheners and cigarette smoke. I have a terrible reaction to smells like these (migraines, nausea, sore itchy throat) and I was hoping these in-nose filters would help 'level down' these migraine triggering smells. They didn't. In fact, I don't think they filtered smells at all. I could still smell the smoke of the people standing near me at the bike rack as I locked up (why do smokers hang out by the bike racks?) and the filters were slightly irritating to me (probably because I've been pretty sneezy and runny nose'ish for about a month now).

So with the purpose of this purchase not working out, I thought I'd give them a try on the allergen front. So I went outside to clean up the patio area for a party we are throwing this weekend. There was a lot of sweeping to be done, I sneezed, coughed and itched having to remove the filters several times to facilitate sneezing (imagine the filters exploding from your nose during a sneeze, gross, huh?).

Then there was some more dust and pollen to deal with as I windex'ed the outdoor chairs and table, dislodged a family of spiders from the grill and found my son's missing yoyo covered by leaves under a chair, by this point I was so congested and my nose was so painful, that I had to remove the filters.

I'm willing to try these filters out again, perhaps on a less pollen-y task, like a walk to the park or a backyard picnic. But so far, they haven't fared well, in fact, they made my allergic symptoms feel worse because I was constantly having to remove the filters to sneeze, blow my nose or itch (there was something terribly itchy about the piece that wraps around the front of the center nostril dividing thingy - I know, dividing thingy isn't the anatomically correct name for this part of the nose, but nose taint, what my hubby calls it is too rude for me).

So buyer beware, if you are hoping for an allergy reducing miracle, keep looking.

title: Got this for my carport's floor
text:
My sweet little volvo 240 left a giant gooey oil stain on the concrete floor of our carport. Normally, I wouldn't have minded this too much but we have white carpet and I just know that we must be tracking that gunk all over our unbelievably-innappropriate-for-wet-Washington-wcarpet.

I was a bit skeptical about this product. Everyone knows that water, cat litter and a bit of elbow grease will remove most of an oil stain, but this product, was for me, a bit of a mystery. I mean why bother, it will probably still mean a ton of scrubbing and added into the inconvenience will be a terrible cleaning fluid smell. But I'm always up for saving time, especially when it comes to cleaning something, I'm lazy.

So I followed the package directions after sweeping a few leaves and larger bits of yard debris from the oil mark. First off the product cautioned against using this without proper ventilation, our carport doesn't have a door, it's like an upended three sided box, so, check and onto step two. Use a mask. I used a mask with a charcoal filter, I have asthma and this year's pollen season has been kicking my posterior and i just couldn't risk it. Third was to not use it on painted surfaces and to spot check it for damage to a surface. My surface was concrete, so I just skipped that step.

Fourth or fifth, I can't remember whichand it really doesn't matter, there aren't that many directions on this stuff, spray the Grez-Off onto the stain and allow the degreaser to penetrate the oil-y mess. I poured the stuff, I know, I should have sprayed it, but it was a seriously big stain and I didn't feel like bending over to spray stuff (I said I was lazy!).

Then I left the Grez-Off to work its magic. I wandered around the backyard smelling flowers (too many, I was wheezy and watery eyed by the time I decided to get back to the carport). The Grez-off wasn't real specific about how much time you have to leave the stuff on your stain, but I guess I must have left it for about twenty minutes.

Now it was time for the big reveal, rinsing off the cleaner. I turned the hose on, careful about keeping the water pressure kinda low, I didn't want to spatter myself with degreaser and I rinsed. There were suds galore and wonder of wonders, a lot of the stain just washed away like pieces of, ham? Ew, actually, that just sounds gross, I don't know what analogy to use here, let's just say that most of the greasy fuzzy dirty oily stain disappeared.

The stain is still there, like a lingering sweat stain on a well worn pair of gym socks, but it is a huge improvement. Maybe if I got a second bottle, because, like I said before, it was a freaking huge oil stain (my poor volvo) it would take away the rest of it, but for me it is good enough.

text:
Interim review. Additional time is needed to judge lasting ability.

I have used Rain-X for years, so I believe in this type of windshield treatment. This product takes longer to apply than Rain-X. There is a cleaner provided, and a recommended cleaning process. After this is done, the rain repellent is applied. I cleaned my windshield and rear window with this product. I then used Rain-X on my side windows. Rain-X is easier to apply, and I usually get 1-2 months out of the Rain-X before I reapply. I didn't use the gloves, and didn't get any product on my hands. Very small towels are provided. The small size actually prevents waste. Eight drops into the small towel, multiplied by 4 for the full windshield uses 32 drops for the windshield. If you use a larger towel, you can waste a lot of the treatment. Probably took me about 20 minutes for the total job, vs a few minutes for the Rain-X. Rain-X is cheap, so you spray whatever you want on the towel, and wipe. A haze appears in a full minutes, wipe it, and you are done. These bottles are very small so you don't want to waste any.

When finished, my windshield was the clearest it has ever been. The cleaner, and recommended cleaning process really does help. I thought about using it for my headlights but decided against it. title: Honda Pilot 2011, EX.  Perfect fit.

The photo is not correct for the Honda Pilot mat. The Pilot has 3 rows of seats, and with the 3rd row down (not used), the seat belts take up room on the mat floor. The actual Weather Tech liner has cutouts for the seat belts. I have an optional cargo net, and the liner doesn't allow for clearance. Overall, fit is perfect. High lips on 3 sides. Low lip on end touching the tailgate lift.
Only suggestion is that a higher lip on the tailgate lift end would be helpful containing grocery bags and bottles.
However, the net serves that purpose for me.
Also, a higher lip would hamper loading of slide in cargo. Probably why this mat is made with the one low lip. The Weather Tech liner plus an OEM Honda net make for a good package.

I also received and commented on the Weather Tech floor liners. Where the floor liners are very stiff and can't be folded, the cargo liner is flexible. It came rolled up. This is important as you can put the third row of seating up for use, and just roll the mat up and place it behind the seats. Handy if you are away from home when the need for the third row of seats arises. The Honda mats are stiff and can't be rolled up.

Final comments. I made sure I ordered from "Amazon sold and shipped." Too many complaints about Weather Tech Customer service.
Get the correct item number from the Weather Tech website, then order through Amazon.

title: Will do the job.  Custom fit.
text:
I posted the below review as a comment to another on this page. Explains the wording.

Installed by Honda.
I gave it 3 stars because I was comparing it Cover King. There are no flaws. It just doesn't measure up.
If I had seen the material first, I would not have made the purchase. However, it will do the job, fits perfectly.
For those that don't want to struggle with installation, these seat covers are okay. Pilot logo adds class.

The fit is perfect. My wife likes these better than the Cover King, I don't. I wish I got the Cover King for the second row.
She likes them because of the custom fit.

The Cover King are much more luxurious (expensive) looking. The Honda OEM looks cheap by comparison. My Cover King came from my 2008 Honda Ridgeline. Ordered through Costco for $ 199 (actually $169 on sale),for the front seat. Black with Grey Insert to match my silver Ridgeline, now silver Pilot. They fit reasonably well on my 2011 Pilot. I would guess Cover Kings made for the Pilot would fit better. I would still rather have the lesser fit, but much nicer looking Cover King. You can order these online and usually don't have to be a Costco member to order online. A 5% surcharge would apply. Easy return policy with Costco.

The Honda OEMs do not have any backs on them. They stop just below the headrests, in back. The center armrest has zippers to unzip and lower the armrest. I wasn't able to lower them after installation, I'll have to ask how.

Other important points. My Honda E Store price was $ 238, plus $ 20 for dealer installation. The young employee really struggled installing these. Probably don't install that many. Honda E store prices vary greatly. Your dealer sets the price. You pay the dealer.

For those checking Cover King for front seat covers, Honda Pilot has a rear lower flap that must be removed to properly install. Don't cut it off. You can slide the elastic strap off from under the front seat, fasten the seat cover, and hook the flap back up.

Cover King has several grades of this wet suit material. Neoprene is their better grade, Neosupreme is the cheaper grade. I'm guessing this Honda OEM is equivalent to Cover King's cheaper grade.

title: Can't be secured into place. High and low beam wiring is backwards and company will not help you
text:
I got these to replace the weak halogens on my 1994 lincoln town car. At least that was my intent.

Unfortunately these chinese manufacturers and amazon claim that these will fit your vehicle just because the electrical connections plug in.

There are two issues with these lights, the first more serious than the second.

First issue is that they will not lock into place in your car because the stiff electrical connection jutting out at 90° to the body of the light. They won't fit past the teeth of the plasting lockring which secures your lightbulbs into place. I actually tried running these lights without securing them just on the friction of the O rings and guess what 1 day later I had no lights because they had fallen out of place into the engine bay area pointing god knows where.

Issue two is that they are wired backwards. To get low beams you need to set your high beams on, and vice versa. Not that there was much discernible difference between the high and low beams on these lights.

Save your money and get stronger halogens or LED's with soft wiring.

The company would not refund me or send me a viable replacement, they simply stopped answering my emails.
