text:
This alternator replaced a junk (and I very much mean junk) alternator from LActrical. For my Jeep so I can power the radiator fan, headlights, heater fan, windshield wipers, stereo, etc.
The alternator came with a test card showing the amperage output, and voltage output at different rpm ranges.
As per typical with a covered fan it makes a little noise, but very tolerable. There is a little electrical whine, easily fixed with proper grounding circuit.
From idle to highway speed this alternator performs perfectly. Where the LActrical alternator barely performed better than the stock 35 amp (and got so hot to the touch it would burn your fingers), this alternator stays cool even under full load.
I highly recommend using the "3 wire" set up with the load sensing and field power wires attached.

title: Not as advertised.
text:
The amperage output for this alternator is not as advertised. It does power the accessories better than the stock 35 amp alternator it replaced, but I was expecting an alternator that actually puts out peak 200 amps. This only puts out around120 or so when the engine is running at 2k rpm.
Don't waste your money.
I am very skeptical at how long this alternator is actually going to last. With the stereo on, headlights, heater fan, and the radiator fan on it heats up a LOT. I am fully expecting it to fail at some point with a full internal melt down this summer. Right now ambient temps are sufficient to help it shed waste heat, this summer though will probably be a different matter. It's working for the moment and I need my vehicle so I'm not able to send it in for a return.
I fully intend to get a high amperage alternator that actually puts out the advertised amperage in the spring.

Cons: Bulky, seems flimsy. Water bottle holder won't hold a standard plastic bottle (Kirkland water bottle shown here). The left water bottle indentation takes my smallest 12 oz Stanley thermos.

Pros: It will indeed hold your phone, and give you a tabletop to eat or do computer work on while you're on the road. I wouldn't use this for writing, it didn't work for me as I'm very heavy handed as I work.

At the end of the day, will I buy this for my other chair, no. I'm going to look for something else.

My advise group everything together and set it on the appropriate sides of the car to avoid confusion.
The first side will certainly take longer than the second, with the learning phase and all. I think mine took 2 1/2 hours, and that includes an almost 50 man climbing up and down off the ground. It is nice to have a second person hand bolts or pieces to you. I would enlist help, which is what I did with my teen.
The first time you step on the sidesteps, be prepared for a little creaking and possibly some pop-ing
For one the palaces you are using to secure the sidestep have likely never been freed before, Additionally the small plastic pieces they give you to keep bolts in place likely will cause a small amount of sound if the crack etc. They are completly disposable and intended for very short term usage. So yeah they crack and pop on first use.

The steps also fully supported a 255 lb man with no issue.

My first issue with the entire kit was the fact that 2 of the rear bolt brackets were too large to fit into the opening. Upon closer observation the bolt head protruded slightly past the large flat plate. A quick 1 min trip to the bench grinder and the head was back the size of the bracket and it slipped into the opening easily. * Wear safety glasses.
This was likely a supplier change and it just got by QC. Easy fix so I have not deducted any from my rating for that.

My second issue was the needing to drill a 7/16" hole in my car to properly mount the bracket for the rear support. Now its not a huge deal and I am certainly happy with the product. I however would have liked no drilling. But that wasn't my case and noted here for clarity.

In actuality the wiring took the bulk fo the time. I am more picky when it comes to wiring, and it could have been done faster no doubt. I also didn't have a lift to work with. That with getting up and off the ground repeatedly. Is what took another large chunk of time.

The unit also works flawlessly with the Ford wireless keyless entry system. simply press the 3/4 button after your code and it will unlock all doors and the tailgate too. I would expect it to do this, based upon its connection point but, thought someone may benefit from the additional info.

The install is easily doable for anyone wanting to add some security to their vehicle. I would easily use this again in the future.

title: Just what I was looking for.
text:
I have been using an inexpensive, analog style inflator like this for years. The rubber coating on my current inflator recently split, leaving it kind of loose and I was starting to question its reliability. The needle would stick from time to time and hence a desire for a digital product that didn't break the bank. It's an older model to a competitors brand (red and blue) that can be found here on Amazon.

I love the ability to inflate, check psi, deflate all without changing a tool. This was all a must in my search for a new inflator. Not to mention the hands free, inline, clip-on air chuck. The clip-on air chuck of my previous inflator was of the ball chuck design and if I wasn't careful, would scratch the sensitive surface of auto rims. That's kind of a sensitive subject for me. :)

Even though I have only used it once, on two vehicles, it's exactly what I was searching for. Let's hope it last the test of time.

With Amazon Prime, shipping was as expected and arrived as noted.

title: It works for what we wanted it for
text:
Fit wise, this hitch does so perfectly with everything matching up where it should. The little coil devices are an unique tool for reverse fitting bolts up into the frame.

As for any negatives, and Ford is partly to blame here, there is one hole that is different than all the others. The bolt threads into this hole (it's not threaded but it's not metal or plastic either). But when I attempted to thread the bolt into this position, I could not tighten the bolt enough to actually hold the hitch. When torquing the bolt to the required 75ft lbs, I still had 1/2" of threads left. I tried backing it out several times and torquing a little higher without success. I ended up having to put a seris of flat washers on the bolt to do any good.

Though I enjoy the design of the hitch, well hidden and very unnoticeable, it does come very close to touching the tail pipe. The trouble is that when you start the vehicle or go over bumps, it will come in contact and make a vibration noise. I have yet come up with a solution regarding this.

This year I'm asking for another one of these for Christmas. I want one hooked up to the lawn mower again while the other is hooked up to the car. text:
I got one of these for my 09 prius when the rubber of the wheel started to get rough and crumbly in spots. I used it for 4 years until I got rid of the car and it worked great. It never had any issues with the leather or thread - it looked good as new for the whole time I had it. I plan to get another one for my new car.

Update: just received and installed this cover on my new car. I had it installed in just about an hour. The hardest part was stretching it over the wheel. Initially, I thought I would need to get the next size up, but after about 10 minutes, I got it situated and ready to thread. I was surprised to see they now include twice as much thread. I considered using a different threading method, but stuck with a more basic stitch (from inside to outside for every stitch- if that makes any sense). Is it perfect? No, but it is better than the last one and I am probably the only person who will notice the parts where it isn’t as tight or the leather rotated forward a little, so the seam isn’t exactly lined up with the one on the wheel underneath it. Hope this one lasts just as well as the old one.

title: They get the job done, who could ask for anything more!
text:
These are great! They work fine, they installed fine, and I have had no problems since I installed them a couple thousand miles ago!

I will say that if you are using these on a prius, (1) make sure you read details on the braking system and disconnect the battery before you start and (2) make sure you are prepared in case you need to bleed the brakes. Bleeding wasn't necessary for me, but if you run into a situation that requires bleeding, you will need a special cable and software to access the bleed command on the on board computer (I even searched for workarounds). The cable (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00C9B32J4/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_3) and software is available on Amazon for less than $30 (currently), so it is worth a look into just in case!

title: Overpriced gas cans that work.

title: Quality product.
text:
I get those die hard S-Pod folks out there. I could not see myself spending 400.00 on switch pods and I am glad I stumbled upon these. I was worried that the quality would not be there but the quality is excellent! The ONLY issue I have with these and that is one I can overcome myself is that the unit that goes under the hood is held on by two fender bolts only and so the unit does bounce a bit. But the unit is great quality! All metal construction with a real circuit board inside that looks of great quality. Out of curiosity I went on their website and even if that circuit board were to go bad which I am not expecting you can even buy a replacement for 35.00 which is epic. Don't get me wrong I understand the Research and Development on this type of item and so I get they can not give them away but for the price this unit is very nice as opposed to spending the 400.00 on an S-POD system. You get a few configuration options whether you want this to turn on via your accessory from your ignition or whether you want to turn it on by the touch switch (default) which BTW works very well. Even the dimming by holding the button works well. I was thoroughly impressed with the build quality of this device. I am a self proclaimed electronics engineer (yes went to school for it) but settled in an IT position for work and I have to say that this product was well thought out and executed. I could not be happier with my purchase other than I would like to have access to other switch covers. I purchased a few on Amazon hoping to just pop in but they are slightly different so the light does not shine through the same and the switches are a slightly different style but hard to tell except for the lighting. I needed a pretty standard one "Fog Lights" and a semi non standard "Whip Lights" so if anyone knows of a place to get some that match the ones in this product please let me know. The seller has yet to respond to my request.

So for the technical portion now...

The switch pod simply slides over the footman loop and while it does have some double sided tape you can secure the back of it to the overhead pillar you can also use the two screw holes to secure it with small screws for those hard core offroad guys.

The wiring is simply. The switch pod itself has a single loom of wire that is a one connector connection to the overhead switch pod. Then you simply connect the large power and gound wires to your battery and the rest is simply relay contacts on a very well laid out circuit board. The numbering does go from the top down so pay attention to the silkscreen on the circuit board.

One side note is you do not have to use the ground wiring on the circuit board. If you are wiring a device at the rear of your vehicle simply run a single power wire to the positive terminal on the relay box terminal and ground your device at the rear of your vehicle to a ground there instead of running two wires. If you have a ground sensitive device then you can run the ground and power wires together but the only terminal that the relay actually controls is the positive wire and the ground plane is all tied together on the circuit board.

There is a "fuse" you can move and run a wire to your ignition accessory or if you only have lights hooked up to the switch you could hook it up to your dash lights and have it come on with your dash lights as well. This would be a strange case but is possible.

One of the cool features is the automatic shut off below a certain voltage. I have not tested this yet but will with lab equipment to see that it does shut off and turn back on at the stated voltages which was again a really nice touch for this product. I could see this saving people who fall asleep with their camp lights on that are attached to this pod.

I thought 8 switches would be overkill for me but turns out it was not. I am using each and ever one of the switches and honestly could use one more but it works exactly as expected and I am very happy with the purchase.

Haters gonna hate of course. Those die hard S-POD guys will always bag on this product but coming from an electronics background I can assure you this device is built well and will last a long time.

One thing I have not done but will do so this weekend and update this review is do some real world testing on how much power the switch pod draws with the unit on but no switches on. So basically the unit would be on and the lights would be lit (all LED lights) and see what the power draw is. My guess is it will be very low and if you left the switch pod on for days it would still not drain your battery.

So this weekends todo list which I will report on in this review next week.

Test the cut off voltage.
Test the voltage that restores power to it.
Test the power draw with the unit on but no switches in the on position. (So unit lit up only)

My overall rating is 4 1/2 stars. Subtracting 1/4 for the lack of support in the engine bay which would most likely be just fine for most people anyway. Its not bad but could bounce under heavy offroading. 1/4 star for the lack of switch covers. Yes it comes with 15 but what about the ones it does not come with? Custom service or links to more switch plates compatible with this unit.

My normal thought would be to round down to 4 stars but I just can't get myself to do that. It is a quality product and much higher quality then I expected to be honest. So before my weekend testing I am going to round up. Also if I do not get a response from the seller before I update my review next week after my testing even if the testing comes out as planned I will lower it to 4 stars (rounding down) from the lack of response from the seller about additional switch covers.

title: Every vehicle modder should have this or one like it!
text:
If you are like me and make modifications to your vehicle this should definitely be in your toolbox! I recently did some modifications to my jeep like installing Rock Lights, USB Modules for cameras, a PowerTank and a few more things and this tool helped with all of these. Anytime a new device gives you nuts and bolts or better yet sheet metal screws I through most of that hardware in a box and pull out this handy tool. Gone are the days of rivets, using a nut and bolt trying to hold the bolt head on the back side of some install. Simply use this and give yourself permanent nuts where you can then screw in bolts and remove them with ease! For those who don't understand what this tool is let me explain it without pictures.

Lets say you need to mount something. Lets say your only option is a sheet metal screw because you do not have access to the back side of what ever your mounting too. Simply pull out this tool. It comes with what we refer to us nutserts. They look like a combination of a nut and a rivet. That is because that is exactly what they are. What you do is instead of screwing in a sheet metal screw you drill the hole the exact size of the nutsert and the nutsert has what looks like a built in washer. You simply put the nutsert on the tool insert the nutsert through the piece of metal so the nut part is on the OTHER side of the metal. The only thing that keeps the nutsert from going through is the built in washer and the tool itself. So you have the place your mounting too. You drilled a hole the size of the body of the nutsert. You inserted the nutsert in to that hole so the actual nut part of that nutsert is on the back side ( the side where you normally would hold a nut on but can't because you do not have access to that side right? ) Then you simply squeeze the handles together. What is happening now is that nutsert is compressing on the back side of the metal and creating a permanent nut on the back side so instead of holding a nut ( which you can't right ) it is like you just welded a nut on that back side. Simply unscrew the tool (which is like the bolt you are about to put in from the front side) and walla you have a permanent nut on the proper side of that piece of metal. Now instead of screwing in the mount using sheet metal screws that you can only do a few times before the hole would be useless and or the screw itself you can not unbold and re-bolt to that nut as many times as you want ( within reason of course )

The tools works great but there are some things you should be aware of. You need to have pretty good access to the front side. The tools is not small and does require you to squeeze the handle to flatten out the nutsert so if you have limited space this tool will not work for you. But if you do have space there is nothing else I do besides nutserts anymore.

This particular tool is professional grade. Strong with a good set of adapters for both standard and metric bolts. Check the description to insure that it has the correct size for your project or upcoming projects! This is no harbor freight or northern tools nutsert tool. Don't get me wrong I love Harbor Freight (West Coaster here) and they have tools for most uses but for a tool like this get a quality well built tool that will last you years! Nutserts are usually available (here on amazon of course) or at your local nut and bolt supply house if you need them fast.

title: Looks Awesome - Some Issues - Honest Review
text:
So a little about me. Self proclaimed electronics engineer. Actually went to school for electronics but settled in IT. So with that. Here is my honest review.

Pros
Insanely cool looking.
Spiral whip is the only way to go as it is a 360' effect and shows.
They claim the no 4mm gap between twists and they are right it shows and is a nice touch.
While there are no instructions the wiring diagram is a photo in the add and is easy to understand.

Cons
No instructions for the app which they recommend "Happy Lighting" which is a nice enough app. But 0 settings except that when you open it that it should be set to the proper settings out of the box.
I bought the dual 5' which boasts 900 LEDs. So even breaking that in to 2 for each whip should be 450 LEDs This is a lie. When I contacted the seller about the proper settings in the app they responded with each whip is broken down in to 3 sections and is controlled by an integrated circuit. Even so that was fine with me except in the app the highest LED count that works is 137. So 137 x 3 (3 integrated circuits or grouping) is only 411 LEDs per whip. Don't get me wrong 411 LEDs is plenty as you will see if you purchase the whip!

So with those pros and cons I would love to give this a 5 star rating as it does look AWESOME! So let me give you some installation instructions and clear up any wiring confusion.

Wiring...
If you want to take advantage of the turn signal and brake light function.

Turn signals light up the appropriate sides whip with AMBER flashing like a turn signal.
Brake signal light up both whips RED like brake lights.

While this is a really cool touch newer cars in the US at least have integrated BRAKE LIGHT and TURN SIGNAL lights for the same light in the tail light. So for newer US cars that do not have TURN SIGNAL and BRAKE lights seperated in the tail light you will need to purchase a "2 to 3 Wire Trailer Light Converter" one like https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0046EKPHY will do the job. You can not wire it without it .

To make my life easier and since mine is in a Jeep JK I that has a towing package I simply got a flat 4 splitter and an flat 4 extension cable that I cut an end off to wire in to my system that way I did not have to hack in to the factory wiring or purchase any additional adapter cables. But remember for me I have to have the above mentioned 2 to 3 wire converter to hook up the brake and turn signal wires.

If you do not care about the brake and turn signals simply do not connect those wires.

There is confusion as to the 2 wires coming out of the quick disconnect at the bottom of the whip. I have seen some people claim they are not needed and some claim they are needed. After my own testing they are 100% needed. If you must test yourself simply do not connect the red and black wire coming out of the bottom of the quick disconnect and set your whips to bright white (This turns on Red, Green and Blue to mimic white but does a good job) and you will see the top section of both whips will be lighter in color. More amber than white. This is because those sections are starving for power. That is what the two wires at the bottom are good for they add additional power to the whip. Simply tie the red and black wires out of the bottom of the quick disconnect to the same red (power) and black (negative/ground) that you use for the module itself and that will solve that issue.

So to sum that up the wiring is as follows.
Quick Disconnects for both whips have a red and black wire coming out the bottom wire those to the same red and black wires on the bluetooth module then wire those to red (+12v) black (negative/ground). A lot of people run power and ground from the front of the vehicle to the back and for this it is not needed. Simply run a red +12 volt to the bluetooth module and quick disconnects and the black wires can all be grounded right where the bluetooth module and or quick disconnects are with a simply loop connector to a good grounding nut or bolt.
On the bluetooth module you will have an additional White / Brake light wire, Green right side turn signal, Yellow left side turn signal. The wiring diagram from the picture in the ad simply says Green and Yellow are both turn signals but they do follow standard trailer wiring. The white wire how ever in normal trailer wiring is ground and that in this case needs to be connected to brake light wiring (NOT RUNNING LIGHTS)

Red wires (+12 volts)
Black wires (Negative/Ground)
White wire (Brake Light)
Green wire (Right Turn)
Yellow wire (Left Turn)

Remember for cars with a single brake and turn signal bulb you need the above 2 to 3 trailer wire converter. If you don't have it or don't want to get it simply do not wire the White, Green or Yellow at all.

The settings I run with the "Happy Lighting" app is
LED Type: SM16703
RGB Output Sequence: BRG
Style Loop: Single Cycle
LED Qty: 137

LED Type is the type of LEDs they use in the lights themselves or the Integrated Circuit protocol that runs the LED lights. This is important and should be left as SM16703

RGB Output Sequence is different so let me explain. RGB stands for R - Red G - Green B - Blue and when you combine those 3 colors you can make up any other color in the spectrum (or at least close enough for us) Each of these colors are controlled by their own wire. Each LED in the whip had these 3 colors all built in to the same exact little white chip you can see through the whip casing. So depending on which lights are on and their brightness setting that is how all those cool colors are made. That is why when you see either solid RED, GREEN or BLUE they look the best and the rest of the colors look like they may have some little skew in the color. So back to that RGB Output Sequence parameter. When the app sends those 3 colors to the whip it can be sent on one of 3 different wires or protocol definitions. So that parameter simply tells the whip hey when I send BLUE you should see it on wire 1 and when I send RED you should see that on wire 2 and lastly when I send GREEN you should see that on wire 3. If you want to see this for yourself feel free to change that parameter to RGB or GRB or any other setting and then simply change your color wheel to any of the 3 primary solid colors and your whip will light up as the wrong color. That parameter will not hurt anything what so ever so feel free to play around. Fun fact (That is how your TV and Computer monitor probably works too! Most anyway) If you get really close to your screen with a magnifying glass you will see those same 3 color pixels!

Style Loop - This is an APP setting and not a WHIP setting. All it does is go through the different APP COLOR modes. So Single Cycle will stay on which ever mode you put it on. If you go to say Random Cycle that will simply randomly change color modes. I keep mine on Single Loop but for demo purposes etc feel free to try one of the other two modes.

LED Qty - Now this one is why I gave this review 4 stars. While 411 LEDs is sufficient for these whips and while they should have stated that the 2 whip combo is 822 LEDs rather than 900 LEDs it was misleading. That coupled with the each whip is broken in to 3 sections or groups of 137 LEDs is even more misleading although I would not have dinged them a star if they had said 822 LEDs in the ad. I get it though sort of as the other whip manufactures are lying about their numbers most likely. But hey break the chain and just say while we advertise 822 LEDs we actually mean it!

Hopefully this honest review will help some people. I know it was very technical. But for those who wanted to know exactly how it works and exactly the right specs there you have them. One last thing. In that same email from the seller they tried to tell me some of the LEDs are hidden under the mount. I found this dishonest even if it were true. I think they wanted to silence my calling them out on 411 LEDs per whip and tried to use that statement to do it. Sorry that did not work. For those who want proof. Set your LED Qty: to 137 and do a color mode that has several colors in it then set that LED Qty: to 138 and it will completely change what the whip does. If you simply lower the number like LED Qty: 100 you will see the top section of the whip will not light up. So that is all the proof anyone needs.

So style and coolness 5 stars all the way! I love the whips no doubt. I have not had them long enough to endurance test them but if they hold up I will be happy for a long time.

Technical 3 1/2 stars. Write better documentation. Warn your US customers that they may need a 2 to 3 wire converter or better yet build this in to your bluetooth controller and make it work with either 2 or 3 wire setups! Tell the truth about the LED count. I get the marketing aspect but in reality it is lying to your customers and marketing spew plain and simple.

So my overall rating would be 4 1/4 stars but since we are limited to 4 or 5 I had to round to 4 stars.

title: Served the purpose with some modifications.
text:
The overall concept is good. It does exactly what it says. The reason for the 3 star review is the following.

1. It is flimsy and I would recommend a metal (not plastic) license plate frame to keep things like car wash brushes from bending. It is not paper thin mind you but mine came bent enough I had to straighten it out of the box.

2. The light holder portion (the bent piece designed to hold some sort of light? Is probably okay for some who can find a light it might work for? You could also bend it I guess back flat maybe? But it is not a good design.

3. The top and bottom holes are not aligned for a California license plate at least. Pretty sure all state plates are the same hole pattern so not sure what happened here but seems like the water jet profile is off and I can't understand why this has not been corrected yet?

Okay so what I did...

I flipped the mount upside down so that light flap was at the bottom instead of the top. Since I bought some little lights that use the license plate mounting holes at the top that simply screw in to the license plate and were luckily the right thread pitch solved my lighting issue. Plus I added a license plate mounted rear camera to the top holes so the light goes through the camera then through a metal license plate frame then in to the top license plate holes then in to the mount itself. Now the mount has welded nuts on the back which is a nice touch normally but for me more of a problem. The length of the light studs that need to go through all of these and into the mount go into the welded nuts just fine but were not long enough to go all the way through where I could put nuts to lock the whole thing together so I simply used locktite blue and walla good enough. If I break the lights getting them out so be it buy some new ones they were like 6.00. Then I simply bent that light flap part up a little and locked the bottom of the plate in that way since the screw holes were way off. If I did not have a metal frame I "could" have drilled out the holes in the license plate to make it work but with a metal frame too it was more of a hassle then it was worth and this method worked just fine.

So overall was I able to modify it and make it work? Yes. Should I have had to make all those modifications to make it work? No. I dinged them a star for each of the two main issues. 1 the screw holes that deserved 2 stars by itself but that coupled with the awkward light mounting tab warranted the second star. I could not knock a star for it being semi flimsy because I appreciate that it does not weigh a lot but could have knocked a half a star for it being bent out of the box. So I settled with 3 stars.

title: Simply worth the money.
text: Definitely serves its purpose.  It is not as well made as the Mopar product of course but for the price you get a nice looking fairly simple to install locking gas flap.  Installation is fairly simple as long as you are semi mechanically inclined.  You remove the drivers rear tail light assembly.  Use a long screw driver to push the tabs on the back side and push the old one out on the top and bottom in the rear of the vehicle only then grab the old unit and pull towards the rear of the vehicle and it pops loose then you simply pull it straight out.  When putting the new gasket on make sure you put it in so the tapered part of the o-ring/gasket is facing the OUTSIDE not INSIDE.  This allows it to slip over the fuel inlet easily.  There seems to be confusion over this but it makes sense if you think about its purpose.  While some complain it does not open fully to a 90' it comes really close and is a complete non issue.  People who complain are just looking to complain.  Overall it is a good gas flap door that locks.  Time will tell how the lock will hold up but from the looks of it even if it fails it would be fairly simple to replace with a mailbox type lock.  Even if it failed beyond repair and you could not open the door simply grab a philips screw driver and remove the tail light and remove the complete housing.  I am not saying this would happen but to those worried that you would be locked out if a lock failed you are not locked out really and could easily gain access if needed.

title: Arrived looking used with scratches. **Updated review! Great customer service**
text:
8/16/21 UPDATED REVIEW: In less than a month after my purchase I was contacted by the company. They wanted to rectify the situation since my pump arrived in poor condition and offered to send a replacement. However, it was already gifted and ended up working so I declined their offer and told them why. Still, they wanted to do right by me and offered me a partial return for sending a refurbished item. I raised my review to 4 stars for this. This company CARES and WANTS you to have a working product. I appreciated that a lot since it was purchased for emergency roadside situations for my guy. Thank you for caring!

When I received this air pump it looked like a returned and resold item. The box arrived split open. The pump has scratch marks on the digital reader screen so it just looks used. Everything was laying unsecured in the box in a thin, open bubble wrap sack. I bought this as a gift so it sucked to give my guy this mangled situation. He's not picky so he wasn't bothered and happily accepted the gift ( I just hope it works) but come on - This should have been sold as an open box item.

A positive note - The spelling error on the Warning sticker from another reviewer seems to have been corrected on the device.

text:

UPDATE: One month into tinkering with this CAI and I have found the trend that works well with my truck (2009 F-250 6.4L FX4 SuperCrew). Under generally flat highway driving (55-70 mph) I get optimal fuel milage with the provided plug installed in the air box. And I get optimal fuel milage with the plug removed during city driving (stop and go). With the plug removed the throttle response is improved as kind as you stay below 2800 rpm, otherwise I tend to hit the wastegate. Turbo's spool up quickly and now have a very district whistle to them. The engine has a good "growl" to it now once you get in and out of the accelerator. Overall I am pleased with this product. I will keep my review at 4 stars due to ease of installation and overall quality if this product. I only grade 5 stars for something that knocks my socks off. title: Not for a 2014 Toyota Tundra
text:
Several problems with the kit.
**The first issue was that the brackets were not made at the correct angle. If the bend in the bracket had been higher up, the bracket would have fit nicely into the deck rails.
**The second thing wrong was that the screws that came with the brackets were too short. We had to Jerry-rig spacers (white plastic squares) to keep the brackets from sliding around.
**Third, the pads of the rail system would not lie flush with the truck no matter how we adjusted the brackets and system.
** The fourth was that the tonneau cover came with a scratch in it that ripped up the material, but did not go all the way through. Not a big deal as we expected the cover to eventually show wear, just didn't expect it out of the box.
**The fifth issue was that there is no brand to this roll-up kit. We tried searching for how-to videos because the instructions were worse than an Ikea instruction booklet. Without a brand, we couldn't do anything.

Overall, we didn't trust the rails to hold where they wouldn't lie flush with the truck while going 65 on the highway. So we returned the product.

We had multiple emails to the company and they said we were responsible for letting them know when it arrived back to them. They also indicated that their product looked like it fit fine but as the photos indicate the rails won't lie flush on the side of the truck.

title: Reese Towpower 74177 Wheel Bearing Protector - Love/Hate with this product
text:

Love/Hate with this product. I had Bearing Buddys on my small trailer and after a year or so one of them fell off. Decided to go with these instead. The other side Bearing Buddy with 2 taps of a hammer it came off. I feel not real secure probably why the other fell off. Had a heck of time installing these new ones though. It's impossible to get them even started to hold in the socket before whacking it. The manufacturer should design them with a tapered edge. I eventually used my Delta 1" belt sander to put an edge on the collar. Still took some effort to get it started once I did I used a piece of 2x4 and whacked it with a 4 lbs BFH. That got it maybe 70% of the way. Had to whack it with the 4lbs BFH metal to metal to get a snug fit. Snug fit is it though, those suckers aren't coming off. My hatred is that in Arizona it's currently 108 degrees and humid from monsoon storms making it a mudder scratcher to work outside; otherwise, thumbs up on this one.

title: A challenge solved
text:
We purchased this for an extra. I spent some time trying to program with directions that were incorrect. Make sure you try the Note option provided by the seller. Also, my chimes were not the same. Another website didn't list the note alternative. Wasted some time but it works!
2004 Buick Rendezvous Key Fob Programming Instructions
Obtain all remote transmitters for this vehicle.
1. Close all doors.
2. Insert key into the ignition cylinder but do not turn it.
3. Press and hold the Unlock button on door lock switch on drivers door.
Hold until instructed to release in step 6.
4. Remove key from ignition and then insert key into ignition without turning ignition cylinder and remove key.

5. Insert key in ignition a third time and leave key in ignition. Do Not turn ignition.
6. Release door lock switch on drivers door panel.
A Chime will sound 3 times indicating that you are in programming mode.
7. Press both the Lock and Unlock buttons on the remote up to 30 seconds.
A chime will sound 2 times if remote has programmed successful.
8. Repeat step 7 if you are programming additional remotes. (without starting over!)
9. Remove key from ignition to exit programming mode.
NOTE: If you are having trouble getting this procedure to work, we have found that some vehicles need step 3 to be done before step 2.

title: mainly because that even with the 699 grips (a set of which I have on my Ducati Monster and love in that application)
text:
I bought a set of these grips to replace the ProGrip Superbike Gel 699 grips on my Aprilia RSV4-R, mainly because that even with the 699 grips (a set of which I have on my Ducati Monster and love in that application), my right hand would get sore on longer rides.

The right-hand (throttle) side Spider grip went onto the Aprilia throttle tube without a problem, but the left-hand Spider grip put up a fight and I had to work to get it to slide onto the clip-on bar--I think because the inside diameter of the left-hand Spider grip is marginally smaller than that of the 699 grip.

Once the Spider grips were installed, I saw that the inboard end of the right-hand grip did not slip over a "ring" that's an integral part of the Aprilia's throttle tube. This wasn't a surprise, because neither did the 699 grip, and I learned to live with it. I did appreciate that there's a groove in the Spider grip that enabled it to be safety-wired in place. [The 699 grips have three such grooves.]

As to the left-hand Spider grip, it--unlike the 699 grip--does not have a counterbore to slide over the APRC bracket on my clip-on bar. As a result, the 1/2-inch wide APRC paddle support bracket was left uncovered. To remedy that, I removed the Spider grip and put it into my freezer overnight and attempted to enlarge the inboard end after it hardened, but wasn't as successful as I had hoped, so I reinstalled the 699 grip on the left-hand bar, even though that gave me mismatched grips.

I'm pleased with the feel of the right-hand Spider grip, but because of the fitment issues with my particular bike, I couldn't honestly give the grips a 5-star rating. Perhaps if I had used them on my Ducati, I could have.

UPDATE: I told a doctor friend of mine about my problem with fitting the left-hand grip onto my bike. He suggested that the X-Acto knife I used wasn't the best tool (and hinted that I didn't possess the necessary skills). Anyway, he brought over a few disposable scalpels and in a few minutes had whittled the inside of the grip enough so that with some effort, I was able to slide the inboard end completely over the APRC. bracket.

text: This job took me about 6 hours to complete over the course of 3 days. I've heard others say 1.5hrs so your results may vary. I didn't disconnect the fuel line and just moved fuel rail out of the way. Didn't have to disconnect EGR tube from exhaust only from throttle body. Lots of great YouTube videos out there. Lots of hand tools. Swivel socket adapters, torque wrench, a 3/8 flex ratchet I used with a copper pipe as a handle extension I needed for 1 bolt. I didn't label anything and also bought new plugs and coil packs. Vehicle runs great and no more coolant leaks now. If you're leaking coolant anywhere around the intake more than likely it's the manifold. When I remove the factory part there was broken plastic around the water ports and when I remove heater hose the plastic nipple going to the hose disintegrated. This job is intimidating but I managed to replace in my driveway. Please use the self tapping screws for the fuel rail. I used the factory ones so i could clip the ground wire to and use to utilize factory alternator wire hold down. Fuel injectors started leaking after 120 miles. Good luck

I'm 5'10", 135lbs, very slim and long arms. This jacket comes in Regular and Tall sizes on some sites. I wasn't sure so I went down to the motorcycle dealer and purchased mine. The jacket fits like it was tailored, not baggy but fitted around my entire upper body perfectly, when I stretch out my arms the sleeves sit right around the wrists, so I suppose they probly could be slightly longer(tall size adds 2inch to sleeves) but I am very satisfied and I think it will work perfectly.

Good plug, runs great when installed. They just dont last forever, oem says 90k miles between changes but when I see mileage drop and throttle response start to lag I change them.

title: FLUSH ENGINE FIRST AND DO OIL CHANGE FRESH AND ENJOY NEW CAR
text:
2008 Mustang Gt, 220,000 miles. Not highway miles but hard driving mountain climbing camaro/charger/bmw chomping miles.

Did a short interval oil change with a motor flush, still running oem 5-20 full synthetic.

First off, I wish I put in this product sooner. Was sitting on my shelf while I decided to install. Took two bottles Since I have an oil cooler and high capacity oil pan. (10quarts)

Let the car warm up first then put in the two bottles with virgin oil right after change, let car run for 10 mins then went out to test it with lead loaded into my feet.

First off the fan never came on my car while it was warming up or driving the rest of the day, I monitor all my temps and sensors via forscan app. Highest I saw my engine get was 190, and thats after hitting 150+mph (on a CLOSED road, yeah). Chirps thru gears again, and feels BETTER than new. Yes better than NEW.

Checked my oil catch cans, no oil...now after a long day of flogging it I always would have about 1/2 in oil in my cans. None.

And the gas mileage went up too! 18mpg city, and thats flooring it at almost every light. (was 13mpg)

Also my clickity clack cam phasers and rockers are almost silent now, no more diesel sound when idling. Cold starts sound like normal warm starts.

I'm hooked, also I dont have any smog equip so I cant say if it fouls or messes with any of that.

And oil stayed clear, no milky nadda from product, even tho it looks like in n out sauce. Normally got brown'ish after first day of driving after oil change. day 4, still clear.

title: 5R55S FORD 5SPD MUSTANG
text:
2008 with 189,000 miles, hard miles of endless leadfoot'ery while climbing mountains.

Started getting harsh shifts and thought oh no servo bore wear! Checked fluid (got a new pan with dipstick), fluid was getting dark. Looking online, other problem with Solenoid pack, possible. Looking at videos of how to rebuild Solenoid shows it gets dirty and does not operate right, that's it just gets dirty no real wear failres. How to clean something inside with such tight tolerances. Hmmmm.

Always been happy with seafoam, don't care if everyone says it's mostly kerosene. Poured in a can of trans tune, went on a drive up the mountain. Before I could get to top was already shifting smoother, low speed shift flares gone. Taking toll roads I came across a brand new AMG going uphill, so I decided to really flush it out. Stomped on it and smoked the amg (car is not stock in any way shape or form), shifted flawlessly and got a victory in the process.

Drained and did a 2 short interval changes with a filter change for the heck of it.

Shifting like new again, low speeds, high speeds, reverse. Next I plan on tightening the bands for the heck of it, and a trans cooler.

I figure that the solenoid was gumming up from the varnishing of fluid going bad, NEVER going to let the fluid temps go above 200 again, 12 dollar odb2 wifi adaptor and "FORSCAN" app works great to monitor anything on a ford.

text:
I feel I'm being a bit unfair here, I'd like to contact the seller with a question but Amazon is making that difficult. I bought 4 of these to replace the lights in my 06 silverado, as the cheap walmart LEDs I'd put in my DRLs quickly started flickering when the engine was running. Surprisingly, these showed the same symptoms minutes after installation. They work fine elsewhere on the truck where they don't suffer constant full-brightness use, and they seem to hold up when on low brightness (rear running lamps) just fine. Hopefully I'll find a way to solve this issue and give these guys the review they probably deserve, but with the issues I'm currently having, I can't justify giving them an entirely positive review.

Edit: I've since reached the seller and was offered a not particularly good deal on a different set of bulbs. I declined that offer, as I don't really want to buy more bulbs from these guys. The remaining bulbs I purchased have all failed, regardless of their location on the truck, they do not hold up to GMs occasionally 15.2v running voltage. I am disappointed that these LEDs have managed to live shorter lives than the incandescent bulbs they replaced.

title: Positive results
text:
Works great for oil, grease, and stains in general. My first project as soon as the product arrived was to attempt to get rid of a nasty stain, there is still debate around the house as to what may have caused it, but it has been around for a few weeks in the same room where our TV is located. As the directions suggested I tried an edge of the carpet to see if discoloration would occur. I did not see any, so I proceeded to attack the stain directly by spraying the soiled area, and immediately after I used a semi wet rag to spread vigorously the solution in the affected area. The stain was gone, and then the critics around me said that the carpet in that particular area has turned lighter in color. I replied that it was because finally that area was cleaned. I looked at the area from different angles, then also vacuum the whole carpet, and realizing that 303 (30209) Spot Cleaner - 32 fl. oz. had done a good job on a difficult to clean stain, I was happy. Project number two: I went to the garage and proceeded to clean another annoying stain inside a Honda Civic, with the interior being the cloth fabric I felt safe to use the same approach as I had when dealing with the carpet. Spray the back seat, and immediately after I rinsed the carpet off. The results again were gratifying, and I started thinking with emotion now: where have you been all my life, you mighty spot remover? Of course I received no answer, so now full of enthusiasm I worked on some marks around the house, including one in the wall that looked like it was caused by a black marker.
This product works very well as a pre treatment, but also works very well on its own with no additional help. Once again we thank Amazon for delivering this very efficient product to our home. I am a day away from trying it on my gas stove top, where it is so easy to get it greasy regardless of how careful one tries to keep it clean. I know it is not on the suggestions for its use, but I find this bottle very effective, enough to where it has become a big helper around our home. 4.5 Stars.

The side roll bars are not AS bad, but it was still an extremely hard pull to barely slide the end over the ball. These ones need to be about and Inch longer.
Stretched so tight, this will certainly decrease the life of the product as a bungee should start lol have 10-15% give in it. The max tension is putting undue stress on the fabric joints, and I see those lastingaunw two suers in Nevada heat before the bungees and the the eye on the fabric fail.

In a few days, if the fire doesn't crest on the range next to my community, I'll pull the top back down and put this up and give it a try for another week before deciding to send it back. title: code was deleted and I continued to drive with quarterly high end fuel and a good 100 mile highway trip for 70 -80 miles/hour speed
text:
I have a 2005 Honda Pilot with 120,000 miles, failed emissions test, in 2015 at which time I was told would need sensors and converters with price range $1800.00 to $2500.00. I found a independent mechanic who also failed emissions, he was puzzled as car did not exhibit any objective issues he would expect to be associated with such codes ) he kept car and drove for 75 miles),, code was deleted and I continued to drive with quarterly high end fuel and a good 100 mile highway trip for 70 -80 miles/hour speed. Check engine light appeared again in October 2017 and would not go off even with 93% octane gas, rechecked codes at Jiffy Lube in December 2017. My mechanic had retired so I researched for something to try before major costly repairs in a car that still performed perfectly and now with only 132,000 miles.

Over New Years weekend I took a 400 mile highway round trip, filled tank with gas (no alcohol, expensive) to clean out system, with just quarter tank of gas left I added bottle of CataClean and drove at top speeds,then filled up with 93% , with only quarter tank gas put bottle #2, back on highway , check engine light went off., I filled up with regular gas, drove through January 2018 without any problems, To ensure emissions pass ( I live in Chapel Hill, NC) I put bottle 3 in gas tank with quarter tank of gas, got on a road I could push petal to floor 3 days before inspection - came out with clean codes.

This worked for me and I have had emissions codes for 3 years popping up. Go figure, a car is a machine being diagnosed by another machine for emissions..

What is up with this county by county emissions law ?, Does NC have emissions concern or not. I could go to OBX where having plastic bags can bring a hefty fine, yet no emissions, really the Sea and its inhabitants are more important than the air we all breathe. I support both, just curious as to why is only dictated at county level.

I did this because I had read about possible differences in rotor mounting hub (center hat) size that can be deeper by about 1/8" or 1/4" on some models. Anyway, better to confirm exact fit/size before going through the whole replacement procedure.
Also, to add a bit of personality and prevent a rusty appearance, I cleaned them well with brake cleaner, masked off the rotor braking surface, and painted the center mounting hub (hat) red to match the color of my daughter's Jeep - it's visible through the wheel and gives it a nice look.

title: Perfect fit on 1997 Jeep Wrangler SE
text:
Installed today on my daughter's 1997 Jeep Wrangler SE, 4 cylinder/auto trans. Perfect fit, functions well so far, and hopefully it will last as long as she owns the Jeep.
For removing the old unit, I used plenty of PB Blaster penetrating oil on the exposed threads of the 13mm mounting, and wire-brushed them clean prior to backing them out. This worked great and I had zero snapped/stripped/broken bolts. Once I got the original bearing hub assembly out, I sat it on the bench next to this new Dura Int'l unit and all of the critical dimensions matched up exactly. The job went smooth overall, but it still took me just over 3 hours to complete (I also installed new brake rotors and pads as long as I had all these parts removed for the job).
A couple days ago, I installed an identical wheel bearing hub made by Moog on the other side of the Jeep, and although the specs are the same, the appearance of this one didn't look as tough/strong. The steel flange on this one (that holds the wheel lugs) was slightly thinner around a portion of the circumference, and the bearing housing material on this unit seemed cheaper - more porous with more of a pot metal look, but we'll see how it lasts (fingers crossed).
Tip: Check for parts on Amazon Warehouse Deals. That's where I got the "used" Moog wheel bearing for about $30. There are deals to be had, with many parts that are simply returned but were never used by the original buyer.

title: Great Alternator. Exact Replacement and Perfect Fit on 1997 Jeep Wrangler
text:
Installed today in my daughter's 1997 Jeep Wrangler SE with 4 cylinder/automatic.
Perfect fit with identical connections, mounting points, and pulley as the original. Took me about 3 hours to remove and replace the alternator, which was longer than I expected. It took longer mainly due to the ridiculous electrical connection on the bottom/back side of the alternator - I had to remove the alternator first, then twist it around to get access to the two small (7mm) mounting nuts, in addition to the two 10mm nuts that hold this connection in place. Ended up getting under the Jeep to get at one of the 10mm connector nuts. But that's a Jeep/Chrysler design problem - this alternator is perfect. Upon completion, started up the Jeep and got a steady 14 Volts DC on the dash gauge.
Also, I got a great deal through Amazon Warehouse Deals for about 45 bucks and free shipping! Brand new (not rebuilt) alternator came in the original AC Delco box but it had been opened and returned, so they sold it as "used". Saved some good money on the deal.

title: Great Wheel Bearing Assy for 1997 Jeep Wrangler SE
text:
Installed today on my daughter's 1997 Jeep Wrangler SE, 4 cylinder, auto trans, 4 wheel drive. I replaced the front left wheel bearing assembly due to a broken wheel stud - I figured as long as I have to take the wheel bearing assy out in order to install a new wheel stud, might as well put a new wheel bearing assy back in. It was a perfect fit, appears to be well made, drove fine afterwards during 15 mile test drive on side roads and freeway. As a shade-tree mechanic, it took me about 3 hours. I used a lot of PB Blaster Penetrating Oil on the large 36mm wheel hub nut, on the three 13mm mounting bolts, and the corresponding flange where the wheel bearing assembly mates up to the steering knuckle. I also wire brushed the protruding threads of the 3 mounting bolds before removing them. This allowed for a fairly easy removal and no snapped/stripped/broken bolts. Also, take note of the orientation of the brake dust shield so you put it back on in the same direction/position.
Interestingly, I ordered this Timken part on Amazon's Warehouse Deals for something like $30. Like their other warehouse deals, it is treated as a "used" part because someone else ordered it and returned it - so the box is opened & taped shut, item might be scratched from a previously attempted install, etc. My part was just fine, with just some tape on the box holding it shut. But, instead of getting a Timken, I was sent a MOOG Wheel Bearing Assembly in a bright blue & yellow Moog box! Awesome! I consider Moog to be the best suspension parts on the planet, so obviously I'm a happy camper. But I've read Timken makes the best Jeep wheel bearings too, so either one is great with me.
In researching this repair job (reading forums and watching YouTube videos), I found that there are a couple possible variations on these parts, depending on if your Jeep came with "Full Cast Rotors" (or, with standard / composite rotors I guess?) There may be differences in wheel stud length and overall wheel bearing assembly depth/height. So when I took the old one off, I laid it side by side on the bench with the new one, and on top of each other, to make sure all the dimensions were the same before proceeding (they matched).
I did the same with new brake rotors, matching the new ones to the old ones before proceeding. The depth/height of the mounting hub in the center ("the hat") can be deeper/taller by about 1/8" or 1/4" (?) - so make sure they match the dimensions of your old ones. I laid the old and new rotors flat on the bench with hat facing down and large rotor portion facing up, and the heights lined up nicely next to each other. I laid them on top of each other to ensure the diameters were also the same. I think the overall height can be either 3 1/16" or 3 3/16" (?) depending on which rotor you have. You just don't want to complete the job then find out your wheels won't turn because the rotors (or wheel bearing assy) are the wrong ones.

title: Excellent Quality and Fit
text:
Bought this Bestop Sailcloth Top for my daughter's 1997 Jeep Wrangler at a reasonable price with free shipping (and a $100 Rebate from Bestop until Dec 31, 2015).
Great replacement for the worn-out top that was on her Jeep. Excellent heavy-duty quality, superb fit, zippers work great, and the instructions were spot-on for removing the old top and installing the new one. It's best to have two people installing this, especially if it's your first time like it was for us. And watch Bestop's video on removing and installing a Jeep top (there might be a link here on the Amazon ad, or try YouTube). It will help to see an experienced person go through the entire process before attempting it yourself for the first time.
I took the advice of a previous review and used my drill with a phillips head bit to remove and re-install about 14 screws that hold the top to the header bar. And we also had the same issue as another reviewer with the snaps along rear rollbar being difficult to snap into place - a couple of our snaps were about 1/4 to 1/2 inch off and would not align properly without some muscle and patience - but we eventually got them all snapped into place. The half-door skins are a pain in the a$$ to install - I probably spent an hour on each one. Read & follow the instructions and take your time - and take a break if needed as you don't want to get frustrated and end up tearing the material. (while I had the old skins off the door frame, I found quite a bit of rust, so I ended up sanding/wire brushing a bunch of the rust off the frame, primed and painted the frame, let it dry, and THEN installed the new skin - ugh)
This top and doors have been on the Jeep over a month with absolutely no issues. It's so nice to have clear windows that she can see through and no air or water leaks - much quieter and dryer inside now. Daughter loves it.

title: Inexpensive but not a factory fit.

I had to slowly and carefully bend both ends without kinking the line to get them to line up and thread in to the factory PS Pump and Gear Box.  I was successful but it wore on my nerves and muscles.  Also, the inside diameter of the metal tubing on both ends was significantly narrower than the factory hose.  It still works, for now, but what is their reasoning for not using factory spec material and will this affect the line pressure?  If I have to do this job again, I will pay the extra cost for the AC Delco hose that earned 5 stars in its review.

text:
First, due to the low price and free shipping, I was able to order new support lifts for the rear hatch AND the front hood for about the same price that I was going to pay at a local parts store for just the rear hatch support lifts! Four for the price of two - hard to beat that!

Like the first reviewer, I also installed these on the rear hatch of my 1995 Camaro Z28. They're pretty easy to install (the only tool I used was a small straight slot screw driver) and they work great. In fact, they almost work too well, if there is such a thing. But now the rear hatch comes flying up at a pretty rapid pace and I use one hand to slow it down to a controlled speed. And this is one heavy hatch! When the old lifts bit the dust, it would take both hands to raise the hatch, then hold it up with one hand while rooting around with the free hand. So for these support lifts to raise that heavy hatch is saying something about their strength. Definitely a good product and highly recommended, especially at the low price & free shipping available here on Amazon.

Installation tip: I used a 2x4 (with a towel wrapped around each end to protect the interior of the car) to firmly/safely hold up the hatch while I installed these support lifts. You definitely don't want the hatch to fall unexpectedly and break the rear glass or smash body parts!

title: So far so good.
text:
I'm giving it 5 stars because I ran it for hours and it worked for my mini-split. Not sure how it compares to other pumps. With standard vacuum gauge tubing with 1/4" connections and connecting a micron meter to the pump, I was able to pull down to 130 microns. Not sure if I had had vacuum rated thicker tube it would have gotten lower. But it did the trick. Also the carrying case that comes with it is roomy, looks nice and great to have as a portable mini-split work bag. Enough room and intentional space to hold other tools and parts, like vacuum gauge set and hoses, valve stem removal tubes, adapters and odds and ends.

I definitely needed to change the oil frequently to get a strong vacuum. Not the fault of the pump, like they all will, pull in air and nitrogren and moisture or whatever from the line set during evacuation, which in my case showed up as super tiny bubbles (1/64" dia or smaller?) at the top of the oil in the oil level window after awhile. And at that point the vacuum is weaker. Not even that many bubbles, but if you see them it's a warning that some gas dissolved or mixed in with the oil, which reduces the pump's efficiency. Changing the oil creates an immediate improvement. That is just a known in the business.

The pump definitely gets warm (but not hot) after long use. but doesn't seem to hurt it.

title: So happy I bought this brand/model
text:
Seem like a pro tool to me... solid and reliable! It feels good to use, as though ergonomically designed, and the clutch mechanism is flawless. I have been getting perfect flares reliably, immediately and I am new to installing mini-split. I got this because the DIY stuff I read suggested a clutch model.

Like for most or all flaring tools, one has to know how much copper tube to be flared must extend beyond the edge of the indented conical part of the holding bracket, before you cinch it down, to get the right size of a flare that fits the nut perfectly and covers the whole brass fitting conical surface of the junction's counterpart that copper flare will mate to. But that's how they all work. A little trial and error to figure out how to get the perfect size flare, but easy to cut off the flare and do it again! Just takes a couple of minutes. I think that's the normal learning curve for making flares and it's easy.

The stainless steel 'cone' that actually flares the copper is angled/offset from center, yet rotates on its axis, which is important so that, with some nylog or hvac oil, the flaring part of tool doesn't get scratched or marred, because when cones lose their shiny smooth finish, they reduce the quality of the flares by introducing imperfections in the copper flare.

title: Simple USB Power Monitor can troubleshoot lots of problems
text:
I am re-reviewing this. I spent too much time explaining a packaging problem and not talking about the PortaPow USB Power Monitor (version 2).

I didn't realize how handy having a USB Power Monitor can be. Aside from troubleshooting the power output of a USB multiport car charger or testing if our 5-port USB TechMatte wall charger was doing a good job, you can even test USB cables if you set up the test scenarios correctly. It also helps to determine that a given USB charger port won't fry your device.

Since practically all small computing devices are using USB version 2.0 or 3.0 in today's market, this unit is able to check the electrical current coming out of anything that has a USB plug and use that fact to troubleshoot the source of problems for a given USB device. For instance, I have a USB keyboard that illuminates (the keys light up) which I need when night falls and I still want to see the keyboard. The keyboard's USB cable in this case is not just a data cable, it's a power cable. I can plug the Power Monitor into the desktop PC's USB port and then plug the keyboard's USB cable into the monitor to make sure the current going to the keyboard is up to specs. In my case, I also have a USB KVM Switch such that I can use the same keyboard for the PC as I do for my laptop just by flipping a switch on the KVM. What if the USB illuminating keyboard starts to look dull to me? Is it the port on the desktop, the port on the USB KVM switch, or the keyboard itself? I can use the USB Power Monitor and plug it into the USB KVM Switch and then plug the illuminating keyboard's USB cable into the keyboard to see if the power to the keyboard through the USB KVM Switch is similar to when the keyboard is directly plugged into the desktop PC's USB port. If they are in fact similar, the illuminating USB keyboard is starting to have trouble. If the output from the KVM Switch is lower than the output from the desktop PC, then I know the KVM Switch has the problem. It's nice to nail down the answer rather than just guess at what might be wrong.

The list of usage goes on and on. I didn't think of these things when I bought it, but now I'm loving that the guess work as to whether or not a USB port is drawing the correct current is no longer a guess; it's a measurable value.

title: Lead acid battery terminal.
text: I’m not an electrician, but I wanted a way to split off of my lead acid battery in case of emergency. I have a solar set up and these clip on easily so I can trickle charge the battery up with the panel and use it for multiple splits to things I need charged immediately. I also have a lithium bank but these are not designed to work with lithium batteries. This allows me to attach leads to the car battery though and that’s what I wanted. Lead acid batteries are more prevalent and easy to pick up in a pinch. The metal seems solid and the handles are easy to loosen and tighten to the positive and negative. The colored handles makes it easier to remember which is which. No complaints. If you have basic electrical skills you will do fine using these. No need to be an expert.

title: Perfect for my needs.
text: I got a separate 12v battery for my project van so I can go Solar and this lets me charge my phone off either the lipo battery or the car battery depending on which has more juice. It comes with extra fuses so I just plug my inverter into it to charge up whatever I need to use. Works well as an easy way to switch between the two. The plug port on this is ultimately going to be mounted in the cabinet of the van next to a hardwired cigarette lighter, but this affords me a cheap easy way to charge on the fly in an emergency. No more dead cell phone. Ever. 😂

title: So you’re trying to go Solar, read me…
text: You are looking for an auxiliary battery, most likely for a solar set up. Let me help. There are only a couple things you need to know here to make it work, and I believe in you. The first is that there are 4 major components to a mini system. The panel, the controller (keeps the right flow to your battery), the battery itself, and an inverter. That’s it. This battery is the perfect size to pair with a 100watt solar panel. Your controller needs to be big enough to handle the load and needs to be specifically compatible with a lithium battery in order to use it with this. This lithium battery is very lightweight compared to lead acid batteries and will have more usability. You can safely discharge up to 80% of the power contained in it vs. the 50% you get out of lead acid. When you get your battery in the mail you’ll probably have an urge to test it. It will work just fine, but consider ordering your other component parts at the same time so you aren’t sitting there frustrated with no way to charge a device. I hooked up an inverter to the battery directly and was able to charge my cellular phone on arrival, but had to wait to do any further fiddling until I had my 100watt panel to recharge. You’ve got this! It’s a good battery and this more affordable than a plug and play battery bank. Once you see how it all works you’ll be really glad you learned how to run your own equipment. Be brave. It’s not as difficult as it seems. 😉

I’m definitely using a dimmer switch with these because I need the lights to be bright, but it’s going to be nice to run them lower for energy consumption. The silver of these lights is a dull silver surface as opposed to chrome. The caps over the lights seem sturdy and the clips to install are easy to use. title: Not heavy.
text: I wanted to get myself a few survival items after this past hurricane season to help outfit my old minivan as a camper in case of evacuation. One of the most annoying things about being asked to leave is finding a restroom on the road and this is a better solution. I can fit this in the back of my van and no one knows it’s there until needed. It holds enough water to be useful, but not so much that you can’t lift it to dump it in the appropriate place. I can flush it 20 times easily on a couple gallons of water. I also picked up a small tin of lubricant for the seal after seeing how they typically end up developing a leak if it’s not maintained, but so far it’s not leaking. I hope to have this toilet for the next few years at least and I’m sure it will save me from having urinary problems on the road. I will definitely be using the tabs they included and I ordered another bag of them as well. Really great idea for evacuees who don’t have a full size RV. Would recommend to anyone looking to up their car camping game. Be prepared.

Cons:
- Wiring harness is pretty short; I may have to length some of the wires (i.e. key switch wires) so that I can mount the components where I need them

title: Works great in 2015 Yukon XL Projector Headlight! I finally found one with even coverage!
text:
This Hikari 2020 H11 bulb has excellent, even coverage. And the color is very white without being bluish. The rounded, raised profile of the Hikari LED at the end of this light bulb has greatly improved the coverage compared to my previous 2 year old LED bulb brand which was only a flat LED whose coverage was uneven and weak. Is this as bright as HID? I'm not sure, but I like the Hikari LED due because you just plug it in & everything fits inside the light housing keeping it sealed from the elements. (HID bulbs have lots of extra wiring and drivers that sit outside the headlight housing - no thanks!)

As far as installation tips, the instructions say to remove the ring from the bulb, then insert the ring into the car's light housing, and then insert the bulb through it making sure that the LED's face 9&6 o'clock. The bulb fits snug in the ring via washers, allowing correct rotation. I rotated it to other orientations but 9&6 o'clock works best. The plug attach to the car socket either way, so test that it turns on before inserting to make sure you have the polarity correct.

I can't vouch for longevity but the other Hikari products seem to have positive reviews and their customer service emailed me back within a day after registering the bulb, which allows for replacement via a 99% off coupon code to order another.

title: Fits great 2015 Yukon, though beam isn't great.

In my projector headlamp, the beam is not as even as the halogens and is due to the LED chips only being on the top and bottom of the bulb assembly, and this pattern is visible in the outer plastic of the headlamp assembly as two brighter spots that emanate through the outside plastic cover on the front of the vehicle. This light is just a bit blue rather than a brilliant white. I find myself having to always switch on the running lamps because these aren't throwing enough light, possibly due to the way the chips are 180 degrees opposite of each other.

Each of these bulbs are rated 40W on the box, so two are 80W total.

This battery charger has all that's needed to trickle charge a car battery. And it supports other battery types as well.

title: Very good OBD2 device for system programming
text:
I've been wanting to address a few minor annoyances with my wife's 2016 BMW 328i (F30). Specifically, the audio stays on when the car is off and doors are opened and not having full Enhanced Bluetooth functionality. I figured I'd get the vLink tool, some software & watch a few videos to figure it out.

It's a little Bluetooth device that plugs into the OBD2 port. I tried pairing it with my phone a few times and didn't have any luck. Eventually I figured out that Bluetooth to the car had to be disconnected from the phone so that the vLink was the only active, paired device. After pairing was successful, I downloaded & installed the Bimmercode app. The app asks the device being used to connect to the car & the type of car itself. Once all that was configured, the device & software worked flawlessly during the ECU update process.

I was able to successfully complete the updates and now those few minor annoyances have been resolved. I have to explore the other software options available to view codes, statistics, etc. The vLink device will definitely help you to achieve your BMW upgrade/modification goals.

title: It works
text:
On previous cars, I never had trouble finding replacement wipers. Anything would work reasonably well---the only question would be how well they'd hold up against Boston winters. But, now that I own a 2007 Honda Accord (purchased used in '09), my standards have been lowered. I'm happy to simply find a wiper that (when new) cleans the entire windshield surface that it's supposed to clean! Before buying this Rain-X wiper, I tried two other wipers that couldn't even perform the basic act of cleaning rain from my windshield. First, I tried the Rain-X Latitude. It's problem was that it was too curved---it would leave a gap in the middle of the wiper toward the bottom of the windshield. Next, I tried a Duralast blade. It was even worse---the Accord wiper arm seemed to interfere with the wiper blade in a way that half of the blade lifted up from the windshield, leaving an even larger section of uncleaned windshield! Finally I tried this basic Rain-X Weatherbeater and I'm happy to report that it works as you'd expect---no gaps.

Note that I purchased my wiper from Marketplace "like new". The box was slightly damaged, but the wiper was as described and performed as well as a "new" blade.

title: Leaves a Gap
text: I installed a 26" Rain-X Latitude that I bought at a local retailer on the driver's side of my 2007 Honda Accord.  From the start, they didn't clean a section at the bottom middle of the windshield.  The problem is that the wipers are *too* U-shaped.  The lower part of the windshield is more flat and the middle of the wiper lifts up, leaving a section of the windshield that isn't wiped.  I thought the wiper might flatten-out a bit over time, so I left them on for a month.  We get plenty of rain in Boston, so I got to see them in action many times. Amazon delivered nicely. Well packaged.

The only Con....
the other set of bulbs came with a glove and these didn't. I found that glove VERY helpful as I’m now typing this review with a burnt palm. You also don’t want your skin oils and dirt to get on the bulbs- can shorten lifespan. I’d recommend using gloves.

title: Man destroys these horrible tools in one review
text:
This equipment is crap. Buy real PDR stuff and not this Chinese junk. The suction cup literally lost suction 30 seconds into the job and the line board crash into the rear quarter panel of my car and damaged it with another king creased dent. It isn’t very deep, but my repair for a pro on that (more on that in a sec) crease was $200. He had to drill into the door well as the dent/crease from behind with a rod, as there was a support structure in the wheel well for all the electronics right where that crease happened from the line board.

Now.. the dent I originally bought these “PDR tools” for was about the crease that occurred was just a 1-1.5” dent from top of the wooden handle of a shovel fell in the garage and thumped my car. It wasn’t deep, but after several attempts with a heat gun on low, we tried 20-25 pulls with the weighted puller... no dice... then we tried the manual puller 10 or so times, no dice, dent was still there. I started slow and increased pressure on pulling the dent as I would continue. Nothing got this dent out so I decided to go for the he gold grip puller. It took about 10-15 pulls here too, starting off where the puller wasn’t high enough to pull the glue/tab off. I started to increase the height of the pull by turning the locking nut and did so quarter of a turn per pull to be sure I didn’t stretch the sent out and oil can the dent... after the 10-15 times, of trying to work the dent out with the gold puller, the dent wasn’t budging... this was about two hours in to this tiny dent after the line board situation so I was frustrated nothing was working. I worked in a body shop as a teen as know body work but still slightly new to PDR l but these tools are junk and shouldn’t be used by a beginner and a pro would look at them and NOT use them. Anyway, I finally got to the point where the tab finally pulled dent and snapped the glue from the body but low and behold, it oil canned the dent. Mind you, I again went quarter turns, gripping the puller seeing the metal move but it pulls all the metal around the dent too, not just the dent. So... I tried knocking it down for the rest of the day but the canning was just too bad, so took it in to the pro at this point. When I told him what happened, he said he knew what happened before I even told him and by doing the canning, it doubled the dent repair from around 100 to actually being $230. So the total was $430 total for the original dent and the new crease from the line board. With the 150 I paid for this junk, I’m basically out $130 for the extra work to the original dent, 200 for the line board crease, and 150 for these “tools”. So $480 for buying these tools. It would have been $100 had I just went to the pro at first but feeling confident and taking the work slow, I would make the dent at least better but these tools proved that wrong.

Additional issues. The plastic pull tabs are just that, plastic. They are not reinforced internally that I can tell... the glues suck. The black melts and actually pulled a little clear off, but this is my fault for trying a dent where the car had been touched up prior and body shop paint is NEVER as good as factory or pro paint, and therefore it was my fault there. However the black glue is basically gum. Doesn’t pull and is impossible to get off. It’s like putting tar on your car and you need tons of 91% alcohol to get it off... 70% wasn’t cutting it on the black. The clear glue was okay but when it cools, it doesn’t have enough grip, when it’s hot, it will just pull tab off the glue on the body, so there is a fine point just before it cools to get good grip... there, it works, but you have a 30-45 second window and it really sucks putting this much time and planning into using these tools. Why I say a beginner shouldn’t use and a pro knows good tools work flawlessly and in half the time.

Learn from my mistake... there lots of solutions to getting jobs done but the right tools are paramount and these fail at ABSOLUTELY every turn you can use them for.

Some of the knock downs did seem okay, so there’s that. Otherwise, I hate these tools and wife hates more that I spent excessive money trying to save money. Don’t cut corners here.
