title: Definitely One Of The Better Diagnostic Readers
text:
This diagnostic reader is a great size, easy to use ("plug and play" style basically), and comes with a convenient carrying bag for unit and cable. Automatically reads VIN, touchscreen and also has side controls. Very user friendly. Not only displays codes but tells you the meaning of the code so you do not have to search the internet for answers and allowed me to clear the code so the check engine light went off on my vehicle. I also took my vehicle to the dealership to verify that the reader was displaying correct code and it was spot on. This unit does a variety of things, not only diagnostic readings.

I do want to mention that when I first received the unit and I was attempting to set it up (it connects to wifi to keep itself updated, set up your account, etc), I kept getting messages like the one I put in the pictures. It also seemed to lag horribly so I was unable to input my info correctly. I tried a few times with no success. I reached out to customer support and they were very quick in responding. Not sure why or what was happening but after I shut it down completely and restarted as directed by manufacturer's customer service, it came back up with no issues at all so this could have been my internet connection or one of the apps used on the unit.

All and all, I would highly recommend!

No canbus issues, no flickering. These are solid. Really happy with them. The Low beams are way brighter than my older halogen lows; however, the brights are not too impressive. They need to be double the brightness with the highs. They just feel a bit dim. They are 4000lx per bulb. The brights need to be double the brightness of the lows in my opinion.

title: The best for nasty, salty, midwest snow that drops from your car!
text:
I almost bought a cheap floor mat for my garage before finding one of these Ribbed G-Floor's at a local Menards. I'm so glad I spent the extra money (about $175) for this exact ribbed mat. Wow - it works so well!

My single car garage floor is a bit uneven, so nasty salty snow was running to one side and getting everything all wet. At one point it was destroying some drywall at the end of the garage.

I was going to wait until the spring to re-coat and epoxy my entire floor until I found these mats. I'm so glad I found this. They fit perfectly for our 2008 Dodge Caliber and 2000 4Runner (only one at at time...), and catches all the snow, which eventually melts.

When the car backs out I just sweep the slushy mess out the garage door. The ribs are key - they really help direct the snow out of the garage when you sweep it out.

It's an investment - but I wouldn't recommend spending less on a cheaper alternative - especially if you're dealing with water or snow. I can't imagine a carpet alternative or a thinner plastic. This is incredibly tough, thick stuff. I'm sure it'll last a while.

Rolling it out is a bit difficult, but not back-breaking. I did it myself (170lbs male at 6 feet tall) - I'd recommend getting a helping hand from a friend.

It's a bit uneven - there are a few bubbles in it - but it's also the coldest winter here in Chicago - so I'm sure it won't get completely even until the summer. For now it's doing the trick though.

title: Works great!  Better fuel economy.
text:
I was going to purchase a Denso product, but they were no in stock so I decided on this Walker.

My 4Runner was puttering in fuel economy. I used to get 18-21 and was now getting about 16. My muffler was dying, so I figured I'd replace both muffler (used a Walker 18901 Exhaust Muffler) AND the up-stream O2 sensor. I've been told the down-stream O2 sensor does not effect fuel economy, but only tells the computer if the CAT is working or not.

This Walker sensor (250-24154) was the proper model for PRE-cat (upstream) O2 sensor. I have a 2000 Toyota 4Runner, non-California, 3.4L, manual transmission 4x4.

Be sure to find the exact fit. There IS a difference between upstream, downstream AND air-fuel ratio sensors.

Toyota started adding air-fuel ratio sensors to the 4Runners in 1998 CALIFORNIA MODELS, but didn't put them in non-Cali. models until 2001.

SO sometimes online guides will say you have an air-fuel sensor when you really have an O2 sensor. If you have a non-Cali. model built in or prior to 2000, then you have O2 sensors.

Anyway, this thing works great. Really happy with the results.

title: Not Direct fit for 2014 Ford Fusion
text: Despite the description, these are NOT a direct fit for a 2014 Ford Fusion. The fixed tab and the snap tab need to be modified significantly to even fit in the mirror housing. I used a Dremel cut-off wheel to re-shape the tabs so they would get into the housing, and even so, they're more of a friction fit than a positive snap-in fit. If you're prepared to do this, then go for it, just be forewarned. Also, you should use some heat shrink on the connectors, since they leave bare metal ends floating around in the mirror housing, which is just asking for a short. Nevertheless, they are bright, and do fade in/out, just like the original incandescent bulbs and WAY less expensive than OEM replacements.

title: Avoid buying these-Failed Quickly-Discolored Lenses
text:
UPDATE - When I went to replce these failed bulbs, I noticed they had also seriously burnt/discolored/fogged my license light lenses on my 2014 Ford Fusion. Now those will have to be replaced also. If I could give NEGATIVE stars on a review, this is the product that would earn it. SERIOUSLY - do not buy these bulbs for your license plate light.
-----
Used to replace license plate lamps on 2014 Ford Fusion. Easy, exact-fit replacement, very bright bulbs. However, one failed after three months and the second one is flickering (as if it too is about to fail). It is now beyond the return window, so I'm feeling like I got ripped off. Just replace your failed bulbs with standard ones is the lesson learned -cheaper and the previous, standard bulbs lasted five years.

title: My Wife Installed These in 3 Minutes per Tire
text: We visited the SCC website to verify the correct size for our 2012 Hyundai Santa Fe SUV.  The SZ429 fits our tires perfectly (235/60-18)  The chains require tensioners which are included, no extras to buy.  The chains arrive in a nylon carrying case plus plastic gloves and instructions that stow easily in the vehicle.  Upon arrival we did a dry run test fitting and the chains went on quickly.  ALL YOU NEED TO KNOW IS THAT MY WIFE WAS ABLE TO INSTALL THESE IN ABOUT 3 MINUTES PER TIRE.  Here's the easy procedure: Remove chains from bag and roll them out flat. One side of the metal tab is stamped TIRE SIDE (make sure this is visible, facing up).  You will notice one side is split, the other solid.  The split side will go closest to the tire inside on the bottom.  While kneeling in front of the tire, use a sweeping motion to put the chain under the vehicle.  Lift the solid side (farther away from you) and bring it up to the top side of the tire and clip together.  Then pull in the slack evenly TOWARDS YOU in front.  Then attach the front top clip, then the bottom clip. (You're almost done).  Take the yellow star tensioner and clip to the cables alternating opposites (12 o'clock to six o'clock, etc.) Once the tensioner is installed and is evenly distributed, YOU'RE DONE.  You'll be ready for trips to mountain country or the slopes.  This product is highly recommended for excellent engineering (designed for tight clearances and tension doesn't have to be readjusted enroute), ease of use and a fair price.

title: Compared the reciprocals with my typical Toyota filter and it appeared that it's a perfect match, until I tried the filter wrench
text:
Bought one Mobil 1 M1-102 which is made for both the Lexus/Toyota 1MZ-FE and the 3MZ-FE engines. Compared the reciprocals with my typical Toyota filter and it appeared that it's a perfect match, until I tried the filter wrench.

Even though the Mobil 1 filter comes with 14-flute on its housing, it does not fit the standard Toyota 73mm filter wrench. It does not fit the 74mm Benz filter wrench, either. The filter housing seems to be slightly bigger and rather slippery so the wrench does not stay and slides off easily. Strap wrench won't work well since the filter is installed at an odd location on these engines. I would never use the pliers-type wrench since it could punch a hole in the housing.

I am not even sure if I should install the Mobil 1 filter since it may not come off the engine. I'm sticking with Toyota filters for now. Would like to hear your experience with the two engines, thanks.

title: Cleaned the Engine Well
text:
Cleaned the engine out well. I changed the oil, poured the product in and ran the engine for 5 minutes and 30 seconds exactly. The engine upper cam area sounded funny for about 30 seconds which made me a little nervous. The oil turned from clear to light orange on the dipstick. When I poured the oil out into a container, the oil color was like honey with a hint of red dye that came with the product.

In the past, the new oil used to get light yellow after just a few miles of driving. I drove about 20 miles after the flush and another oil and filter change. The oil was still crystal clear.

I bought my SUV brand new and put 246K miles on it so far. I have done all my oil change at anywhere from 2,500 to 5,000 miles depending on the oil color. I changed the oil whenever the dipstick showed dark brown. Used mostly 5W-30 conventional oil, though did use 0W-30 synthetic in the winter.

I did clean up the oil pan a year ago. The oil pan gasket spun a leak back then so I had it cleaned and re-sealed.

While the product did very well for me, it appeared that my engine was fairly clean with regular oil changes. So I probably won't bother to do another flush until it reaches 500K miles.

text:

Replaced the transfer case and rear differential fluid on both of our SUVs. The gas mileage increased from 19.9 to 21.3 mpg, or 7%. No leak from the drain plugs so far. So far I'm very happy with it.

Didn't buy from Amazon because some had reported leaky bottles. The local O'Reilly Auto sold them for just $1 more. (Ask for Mobil 1, they hide them in the back room.) I bought 6 bottles from O'Reilly and 2 were leaking at the seams on the bottles. (And lucky me, those two bottles were the ones that I didn't use.) title: The R-134a works... the gauge doesn't
text:
It works. Has enough refrigerant to get both of our SUVs' A/C ice cold. The long hose really helps.

So why I give just 3 stars? The gauge is garbage. The reading jumps all over the place. Do not trust the gauge reading, or you might overcharge and blow up your A/C. Remember you shouldn't release it into the atmosphere. And it can cause cancer if inhaled.

Here's what I have done: I started by cleaning the radiator with a degreaser. Then used a meat thermometer to measure the vent temperature with max A/C on. It was 55 F. Shook the canister really well to mix the refrigerant and the oil inside. Then I charged it 15 seconds at a time, until the vent temperature dropped to 40 F. It took 4 15-second "bursts" for me. Again, don't trust the gauge, and don't overcharge it.

title: Another Snake Oil
text:
There are lots of 5 star reviews here for Marvel, but I'm going against the grain here...

Both of our vehicles have about 200K miles on them and are well-maintained by yours truly. And they both have the same Toyota 1MZ-FE engine that is known to have oil gelling / sludge issue. After reading so many fantastic reviews here, I decided to try it on my vehicle to clean up any possible sludge.

I changed the oil on both of our vehicles on the same day, then added half a bottle (16 ozs.) of the Marvel Mystery Oil into my vehicle only. We drive about the same amount of miles and 75% of our commute overlap. I was expecting my oil to get darker sooner than my wife's, but it didn't.

Then I added 5 ozs. into the gas tank (I should've added 8 ozs since it has 20 gallon capacity.) I did notice the performance drop. The acceleration was definitely slower. Fortunately I got the performance back with the next tank of gas.

And it does not smell like mint to me. It smells more like RAID wasp spray. (Not that anyone should smell / inhale this stuff.)

So there you go. IMHO, Marvel Mystery Oil is just another over-hyped yesteryear snake oil product that needs to stay in the museum. Its purpose is still a mystery to me.

UPDATE: I jacked up my SUV to change the transfer case fluid and inspected the under carriage. I found dried out seepage at one corner of my oil pan gasket. This was not there 6 months ago before I used MMO. Of course, MMO was long gone out of my crankcase. It has dried out so there's no further seepage. It stands to reason that MMO may have caused this. So I guess that MMO does have a purpose after all.

title: Long lasting with some negatives
text:
We have 6 months of winter in Colorado from mid-October to mid-April. I've tried quite a few waxes over the years. While they were all good in keeping the SUV shining, they all failed in terms of durability. The best lasted about 2 months with weekly automatic car washes. And I really don't like waxing when it's cold.

So I decided to give Nu Finish a try. This is not a wax. It's an old school polymer polish from the '70's, nothing fancy. The instruction says put on two coats a month apart. So I put on the first coat in mid-September and then the second coat in mid-October before the Colorado winter hits. It is easy to apply and buff. It's been almost 5 months with weekly car wash, the paint surface still feels slippery. Clearly Nu Finish can easily last 6 months or even longer. I'm really impressed.

Nu Finish does keep my SUV shiny, though it's a glossy paint kind of shine, not the deep mirror wax shine. And it seems to repel dirt quite well, unlike most waxes that seem to attract dirt. The CDOT crew put tons of sand and dirt on winter roads for traction. So my white SUV usually looks brown on its sides after a snow storm. It has not happened this winter with Nu Finish. It just gets a little dirty. I like this stuff.

There are three negatives about Nu Finish in my opinion: #1 - The petroleum-like foul smell makes me want to throw up. #2 - Its glossy paint shine has accentuated the "orange peel" pattern of the paint surface, while most waxes smooth out the orange peel to provide a deep mirror shine. #3 - It does not fill and hide the swirls and hairline scratches on the clearcoat like some waxes would do.

My conclusion is that Nu Finish can provide long-term protection for your vehicle's paint with minimal effort. It's not for the wax purists or car show competitors who like the smooth and deep mirror carnauba wax shine.

title: Why would someone buy this product?
text: Well, if you understand the concept behind Port and Direct Injection, you'll know why someone would buy this product. If you drive a vehicle that has Port(fuel)Injection or Direct Injection you should want to know why. My RX450h has both Port and Direct Fuel Injection. In the early 2000s Direct Injection was mandated by the EPA to get vehicles to burn fuel more efficiently. But the downside to that was carbon deposits and dirty intake valves in your combustion chamber. That coupled with untimely oil changes and cheap non-detergent gasoline lead to poor engine performance and low gas mileage. A combination of quality detergent gasoline, timely oil changes, and an occasional application of CRC Intake Valve Cleaner will keep your vehicle running like new.

title: Save yourself some money.

It has been written that upwards of 70% of all mechanic shops and dealerships exhibit some degree of dishonesty in the maintenance of customer's cars. That's begs the question, did they actually change the oil? Did they use synthetic oil? Did they perform all the so-called diagnostic procedures outlined on that four page receipt you're given. Since many vehicles are leased and come with maintenance agreements and manufacturer's warranty, dealerships as well as repair shops are hard-pressed to "fine" revenue however, and whenever they can. text: I purchased this Ceramic Waterless Wash Spray Wax having taken advantage of the manufacturer's 15% discount. But I had to think for a moment; this is an SIO2 product and I have never used a Ceramic 9H Coating on my vehicle before. So, why am I applying a Waterless Wash infused with a Ceramic Coating? So, I gave it to my son. He used it and had amazing results given the fact that he had previously applied a 9H Ceramic coating on his 2015 Forerunner. Now, in my previous review of Shine Armor's Carnauba Spray Wax I had amazing results, so I was hesitant to use a Carnauba wax with a Ceramic based coating. In fact, friends of mine have gotten mixed results when they did. There is an ongoing and ever increasing hype regarding Ceramic coatings and sprays. Now don't get me wrong, if applied properly these products offer amazing results. My son can attest to that; but the weekend warriors and infrequent detailers should understand this BEFORE using Ceramic based products on a Carnauba waxed surface. Retailers are not telling you this and as a result these products are getting less than stellar reviews for products that are actually very good. this hurts their sales and often mislead consumers. If you are going to use a Ceramic based Waterless Wash and Wax on your car you should have applied a Ceramic coating following the Paint Correction and Detailing of your car FIRST. If you are going to use a Waterless Wash and Wax product like Meguiar's you should have used a Carnauba based Sealant and or Wax. In fact, I use various products according to their product strengths. For instance, following the Detailing AND Degreasing process I used Turtle Wax's Seal and Shine as a tough long lasting protectant. I then applied Shine Armor's Carnauba Spray Wax to get that deep lustrous shine. And when I got caught in a heavy rain, I went to the Touchless Car Wash and then applied Mequiar's Waterless Wash and Wax ( Carnauba based) to bring back Shine Armor's AMAZING shine. But for now I'll hold off on the Ceramic products.

I plan on purchasing Shine Armor's Waterless Wash to keep this shine throughout the year. title: Retrax is the best you can get!
text:
My first encounter with Retrax was when I bought a used 2016 GMC 2500HD. It had a Retrax cover already installed. I loved it. Fast forward to 2022, I bought a new 2023 GMC 2500HD and decided to get another Retrax bed cover.

The first order was bad. Despite the label that says 'THIS END UP' on the carton, the shipper mishandled the box and the cover was damaged during shipment. I was undaunted and reordered, from THIS company which had it $300 less than my previous order. I can honestly say that this is the best investment I could have made in my new truck.

I can understand why some would prefer to have it professionally installed. You must be handy to install this bed cover. It also requires two people. However, if you take your time and study how it goes together, it's possible. Me and my BIL had it installed in under an hour.

The fit of this cover is very precise. You must check and double check your measurements to make sure you have done it correctly. I should note here that, even though I didn't have any problems, I could see where, if you made a mistake and the cover rolls out of the canister without the tracks to contain it, it could be a real mess trying to get it back together.

Our installation went smooth as silk. The cover glides easily in the tracks. It locks securely. The seal between the cover and the bed is very good.

The two things that I could complain about would be the drain tubes that go from the canister that the cover rolls up in and the truck bed. The tubes snap into a couple of holes on the canister and run down to these holes that are already in the truck bed. Those tubes are kind of out there and subject to being knocked out, pinched etc. by impact from anything that is in the bed of the truck. I've already dealt with this, more than once. You must make sure that your cargo doesn't hit those tubes.

The canister is fragile. If your cargo slams up against it, it will dent. Then, the rolled-up cover is so close to the canister, the dented canister rubs against it and will mar the finish on the cover. I'm speaking from experience here. SECURE YOUR CARGO!

One more thing... It will pay for itself! A bed cover improves your gas mileage! Over the life of the Retrax bed cover, the money you save on fuel will equate to you having all the benefits of the bed cover FOR FREE.

Now, the cover is awesome. It provides security that a soft cover can't. It's simple to install. It will last for years. I've communicated with their customer service. They're great. I really like my Retrax bed cover. It's well worth the investment. One of the best purchases I've made.

title: NOT for 2021 Gladiator Rubicon.
text:
The listing says that this bull bar will work for 2021 Jeep Gladiator Rubicon. It will NOT. The listing doesn't say anything about removing the skid plate. In the instructions, it says to remove the skid plate and it will NOT be reinstalled. Okay, it took me a minute to decide which I wanted most, the skid plate or the bull bar. I opted for the bull bar, since I had it here and really wanted to install it.

My 88 year old father-in-law and I crawled under the truck and removed the skid plate and started to install the mounting brackets for the new bull bar. The first thing I noticed was that the frame in the pictures did NOT match the frame of my truck. Mine has these permanently installed 'rivnuts' (see the picture). The frame in the picture does NOT.

We kept going, undaunted, assuming that it would still work. We were wrong.

The very first step in the attachment is a welded bolt, arm and nut assembly that has to be inserted into the frame and aligned to have the nut appear at a hole about 4 inches above the bolt. However, the OEM 'rivnuts' (that the instructions don't show or mention) block the arm and prevent proper alignment. So, we were stumped, right there.

My Dad-in-law and I are both reasonably intelligent people. I am a retired computer systems engineer with years of experience in the automotive accessories field. He built his own house, from the ground up with his own two hands and is a mathematical genius. We both love our trucks. We looked at this issue over and over.

We could NOT find any way to get around the failures built into this product by the manufacturer.

I have also contacted Tyger, hoping that they might have updated their product and have some kind of upgrade, for their installation hardware, available for the most current year model of the Jeep Gladiator Rubicon. No such luck. They asked me for some basic order info. After I sent them pictures of my truck's frame, with other information, I sent them everything they asked for.

They replied with instructions to use the INSIDE of the frame tubes for mounting the brackets, instead of the OUTSIDE as in the original instructions and included a picture of where to install the bracket.

But, the bracket is about 1.5cm too long to go there, and I still can't install the bull bar. Obviously, Tyger Auto has not done their homework on this and is advertising this product as being able to fit the 2021 Jeep Gladiator Rubicon, when it actually WILL NOT FIT. All because of a stupid little $5 bracket that they didn't update for this vehicle.

So, I'm returning this. So sad. I really wanted it to work. Back to the drawing board.

Update 12/14/2021, Tyger sent me another email, explaining that they sent the wrong information before and that I should try something that another customer tried. I looked at the attached pics and said 'WTF?'. Nothing that the other customer did had anything to do with my vehicle or my problem. AND, nothing that the other customer did had anything related to REAL instructions or REAL situations that Tyger would stand behind as following their written instructions, hardware or warranty.

I must state right here, that I have the soft bed cover by Tyger. I think it's an excellent product. I am very pleased with it and gave it five stars in my review.

This product, if it had the correct mounting hardware and instructions, would be an excellent product. HOWEVER, because Tyger has NOT kept up with year model changes and expects customers to just 'wing it' with this brush guard/bull bar, I can only warn other possible buyers to STAY AWAY from this product. It simply WILL NOT FIT the 2021 Jeep Gladiator Rubicon. Don't waste your time and money, trying to make it work. It will only leave you ticked off and sending it back to Amazon.

title: Good looking protection for the hood latches.
text:
Top priority: protect the hood latches from the elements. I know that they MUST stand up to rigorous testing and be able to do the job as long as you own the vehicle. BUT, that doesn't mean that they have to always LOOK good. There is no amount of wipe on, spray on, paint on chemicals that will block the elements as well as just having another solid surface shelter.

Second priority: look good. I would have preferred a solid black, to match the rest of my trim covers. But, this 'carbon fiber' finish was all that was available. With that said, these do look good.

Finally: do the job. I have a small nagging doubt about any exterior trim piece that is held on with 3M tape. Especially, with any vehicle that has to stay out in the elements, like mine. No covered car port. No garage. Just the blazing hot summer Texas sun and freezing cold winters. This set came with primer, to ensure adhesion. I cleaned the hood latches with alcohol first, then wiped them down with this chemical soaked pad, that smells nothing like the typical alcohol prep pad. We'll see...

The fit was fine. They pretty much seat themselves in the correct position. Peeling off all of the red plastic backing from the tiny 3M strips was a pain. I finally used a knife tip, which helped somewhat. But, it takes time. Planning your step by step procedure and the right environment are important. Do it in the shade, on a calm, low humidity day.

In the end, I expect that these will protect the hood latches from the elements and look good doing it, for a long time. Five stars.

text: The plastic trim in and around the interior door handles always gets a beating. Over time, they get all scratched up and worn. I got these carbon fiber looking cover plates from JeCar, to prevent that and they also look great. They're held on with 3M double stick foam tape. I'm not sure about how well they're going to hold yet. It's only been a few days, since I installed them. But, so far, so good. They were very easy to install.

title: Good running boards.
text:
First, the pros. They are very well built, extruded aluminum for the boards and cast aluminum for the end caps. The matte powder coat black paint is very well done, thick coating. The mounting brackets are good, solid thick plate steel that has a nice enamel coat. The mounting hardware is good quality hardened steel with a nice black finish. It all goes together very easily and is nice and solid.

Now, the cons. They only use three brackets on each side, when they could have very easily used four. The truck has mounting points for four and I think that it would only have made the boards stronger. Next, the boards DO NOT have any kind of non-skid surface. Slick sole or wet shoes are going to slip. Finally, they leave a gap between the running boards and the body of the Jeep that is unsightly. They need to redesign the mounting brackets to put the boards a little higher and/or closer to the truck body, to hide the underbody of the Jeep and all the welds and bolt holes. I haven't seen any aftermarket running boards that fit as well as the OEM rock rails.

For the money, these are just about as good as your gonna get. Four stars.

title: I like this tonneau!
text:
After returning one that I bought from YITAMOTOR that failed right out of the box, I spent a little more and got this one from TYGER. For just a few bucks more, I got a MUCH better quality product.

First off, they are nearly identical. But, this one installed correctly, with no problems. The installation was super simple. The gap filler that goes atop of the front bed wall is thick enough to seal the gap between the tonneau and the bed wall. The rubber seals around the tonneau do the rest.

The front clamps are simple to adjust. This one comes with safety straps, to prevent accidentally being blown away. It folds up very neatly and locks into the stored position very well. The rear latches are easy to operate and snap into a stored position when not in use.

This one comes with a storage bag, to protect it, while not on your truck. But, I doubt that it will be coming off. Not only does this tonneau do a great job of hiding and protecting whatever's in the back of your truck, it will also increase your highway gas mileage, by streamlining the vehicle.

My only concern would be that, I see a little bump in the tonneau, where it's resting on top of one of the cross rails. I don't know what that bump is, yet. But, it is a pressure point. It could eventually create a hole right there. Especially when there is any kind of pressure applied from above. I plan to look underneath and place a thin pad of some other material between the cross rail and the tonneau material, to relieve some of that pressure.

Otherwise, this one is a great improvement over my first purchase. I am very satisfied with it. Good purchase.

title: Don't like the mesh pockets. THESE are much better.
text:
I understand why Jeep puts those mesh pockets in the doors, instead of hard sided pockets. Space is a premium. Jeep vehicles are NOT very roomy. It's not their intention to be. Jeeps are designed to take you places where other vehicles fail. But, I think that those stretchy mesh pockets are more of a decoration that purposeful. At best, they are only for temporary use.

As far as I know, JeCar is the only company that makes these 'bottle pockets' for Jeep vehicles. So, at least for now, they have the market cornered. And, they have a good product. The resin material is nice and thick. The holder is formed perfectly to fit the trim of the door. You re-use the OEM screws at the bottom. You have to pre-drill some holes in the door to use the top screws. But, my rationale is that I will never take the out, so the holes won't matter. The knee room is only slightly less. I'm 6'6", with long legs and big feet. So, It's probably not as noticeable for other folks. My only peeve is that JeCar should have used black screws to match the OEM ones. Otherwise, they're great. Good purchase.

title: Make your keys easier to spot, AND protect your fob.
text: I keep a truck long enough to wear out the fob. I mean, want to talk about used? All the graphics get worn off, the matte finish of the case gets all shiny. It just looks, well, USED! The first thing I do with every surface of my new truck is to protect it as much as I can. I cover the seats, the steering wheel, the armrests, the dash and more. Why not protect the fob? This two cover, two color set is great for that. It goes on very easily, all functions are still accessible and the bright metallic finish is a LOT easier to pick out in a bowl filled with other fobs that are black. Good purchase.

title: Now THIS is a good tactical antenna. USE THREAD LOCK!
text:
I never would have believed it. But, there is a rubber antenna that you have to remove before you go through a car wash. I was stunned when I read that in the instructions. (It's not mentioned in the listing.) What's the point of getting a rubber antenna, if it won't hold up better than the stock one, in abusive situations like going through heavy brush or A CAR WASH! Kind of defeats the purpose. Don't you think?

So, I got this one from AntennaMastsRus. This is what a 'tactical' antenna is supposed to be. It's well built, using top quality materials. It has a flexible metal mast that is jacketed with heavy rubber and is designed to withstand being flexed by heavy brush and spring back to normal, every time. It installs very easily and does a great job. I'm still able to pick up all of the AM and FM stations that are important to me. I honestly use SIRIUSXM more than FM. But, it's good to know that I still have those options. Good antenna.

Update, 12/28/21: Lost my antenna somewhere between Beaumont and Georgetown TX. You can't really tighten it down a whole lot, due to the rubber sleeve. The sleeve just spins around on the threaded connector. I don't blame the manufacturer for this. They did the best they could with this design. It's still good. However, a small amount of 3M 'Blue' (or low adhesion) thread lock is needed to prevent the antenna from just backing out of the receiver on the Jeep. Don't use too much. Over application will act like an insulator and prevent good conduction for RF signal. Just a few drops will do the job.

title: Eliminate that blind spot!
text: I tried a set of mirrors that fasten to the OUTSIDE of the stock mirrors. They just wouldn't work. So, I finally got a set of the 'spot' mirrors that can be adjusted. The go on quite easily. They hold their position quite well. I imagine that cleaning them will knock them out of position. But, once you know the best angle for them, repositioning them should not be a problem. Plus, the deep convex is quite forgiving. They don't have to be in EXACTLY the same position, to give you a good view. Good purchase.

title: ONE MISTHREADED BOLT halted installation! DARN IT!
text:
I REALLY wanted this to work. It looked SO SIMPLE. I was following the directions very carefully, and it was looking FANTASTIC! Then..... I hit a snag....

I had already applied the header foam tape, placed the cover on the truck, unfolded it and got perfect alignment. I was really excited about it at this point. Then, I unwrapped the front locking assemblies and started to secure them.

But, the first turns on the right hand side lock were extremely difficult. I stopped tightening and swapped the lug handles with the other side. After doing several tests, with the included hardware and some extra that I had here at home, I determined that the first bolt was misthreaded.

I didn't know how far the bad threads were on the bolt, or how severe. So, I attempted to thread the T-handle locking nut on anyway, past the problem. This sometimes works. I've done it before. But, not this time. All I succeeded in doing was stripping off the wings of the plastic head of the bolt that keeps it from spinning in the frame of the cover. INFURIATING!

As I said, I really like the looks of this cover and REALLY wanted it to work. But, sadly, it's being returned as defective. I'll keep looking at others. One star.

title: What's the point????
text:
There is nothing about how fragile this antenna is in the listing. The whole idea of having a short rubber antenna like this is for it's ruggedness, it's ability to withstand being knocked about and not get damaged. But, in the instructions, and I quote: BE SURE TO REMOVE ANTENNA BEFORE GOING THROUGH CAR WASH!

Well, if it can't stand up to a car wash, I guess driving through wilderness and rough terrain are completely out of the question. Then... What's the point of having this antenna? I might as well leave the stock one on!

This is just a waste of time and money. ONE STAR!

title: Block the sun!
text: Living in central Texas, I wouldn't park my car in the sun without good protection for the interior of my car. I use vent shades on all the windows and this windscreen sun blocker. This one from EcoNour fits my new Jeep perfectly. It blocks the sun, completely from the inside. It protects the interior, and reduces the temperature considerably. Good purchase. Five stars.

title: Add easily accessed space to the deep console well.
text: The center console of my Jeep Gladiator is DEEP, like a well. It has a lot of unused space, because of the depth. This lift out tray helps a lot. It adds a space for easy access to smaller things, while still permitting the use of the space underneath for larger items. The fit is very good. The function is great. The little rubber inserts are a nice touch. Very happy with this item. Five stars.

title: Prevent damage to your new ride's finish.
text: There are a lot of sill guards out there. I shopped them all for a long time, before I selected these from Rugged Ridge. I feel I made a good choice. They are nice and thick. They conform well to the shape of the sill. The heavy duty 3M adhesive tape adheres well. They are all labeled left or right, with the tooling marks underneath. The front ones were pretty easy to align, using the hump for the body bolts as locaters. The back ones were a little more difficult. You have to use your eye for uniformity and good judgement to make sure they are properly aligned, looking for good centering and the flattest and most level position. But, I think I got it right. It looks good and there's no give when I push down on it. So, good deal. I like these sill protectors. They will prevent the sills getting all scratched up as people climb in and out of my new Jeep. Five stars.

title: Protect the top of your console arm rest.
text:
The armrests in your vehicle get as much wear as your floor mats and seats. Dirt, body oils and more get slathered onto the upholstery every time you get in. Then, heat trapped in the car just bakes it all in. As your car ages, the armrests can become permanently stained and the vinyl becomes brittle. Why not protect your investment?

I got this cover for the console armrest in my new Jeep. It goes on kind of like a shower cap, only much tighter. It was actually a bit of a struggle to get it on. I could actually hear some of the stitching pop and I stretched it over the armrest. I don't think that this is a problem. It still fit nice and snug. The openings lined up properly with the latches and keyhole. It blends in with the rest of the interior just fine. It does not shift as I move my arm around on it. It covers the armrest completely, edge to edge. Good purchase.

title: Been using AVS products for years.
text:
AVS has been my source for auto accessories, for as long as I can remember. I ALWAYS use their bug deflector and window vent shades on my truck. When I buy a new truck, I automatically order those things from AVS. They fit right. They do what they're supposed to do. They look good. They last.

One issue with these, (and all brands that mount the same way) is that, because the go into the window channel, they will temporarily make it difficult to roll the windows all the way up. The window stops when it hits the vent shade. But, if you leave that window rolled all the way up for a couple of days, the seal around the window will gradually conform itself to the new shape and bulk of the added vent shade. I've gone through this before and can tell you that it happens with all types that fit in the window track and it's not a big deal.

NOTE: If this is the first time using this product in a Jeep, pay attention to the placement of the vent shades for the rear passenger window. The tab on the BACK of each unit goes on the OUTSIDE of the window track. The front tab of the two front vent shades go between the sideview mirror mounting plate and the window track. Not installing these correctly WILL allow them to fall out. Proper placement will ensure that they stay in place and won't fly off while you're driving down the highway.

I like the AVS products and can say that they truly earn their stars. All five of them.

title: Just a little more room for stuff.
text: None of the pockets of this set are very big. Can't be. Not much room in the Jeep to work with. But, they provide just the space needed to drop a cell phone, while it's charging, spare change, ink pen, etc. So, good deal. The grocery bag hooks that hang off the back of the front seats is a nice touch. Good purchase.

title: Put one on, BEFORE you wear the OEM leather wrap out.
text: Very easy to install. Matches the OEM trim very well. Feels good in my hands. Nice and secure. Good purchase.

title: A little fuss. But, the end result is good.
text: The button cover and ring cover both have double stick tape already installed. But, it's really crappy. Like it's already dried out. However, they include a roll of super sticky goo tape that you replace the tape with. It's a little fuss getting it on just right. But, the end result is very good. The object is to protect the OEM ring and button. This works, with a little pizazz. Good purchase.

title: On every truck I have ever owned.
text: I have used a 'deflector' on every truck I have ever owned. Not only do they protect the leading edge of the hood from rock damage and bugs. They also help deflect them OVER the truck instead of into the windshield. This one was easier to install than some others. I used the indentation around the hood latch for getting proper alignment. The 3M tape won't hold it securely on this Jeep. But, it did hold long enough to allow me to secure it with the screws and washers. Use a 7/64" bit for pre-drilling. The final product is great.

title: Almost perfect.
text: These floor liners are pretty awesome. I bought a set from this company for my wife's car. They fit perfectly. These are contoured to match the floor of the Jeep very well. They go up the sides enough to catch most spills and scuffs. The only problem I have is that the snaps don't line up with the buttons in the floor. You can line up one, exactly. But, the second one is about two inches off. Not sure how to deal with that. I like these floor liners. But, I can't relocate the button in the floor and can't stretch the liner.

title: Really don't improve your view.
text: Tried two different mounting positions. (Actually bought more tape just to try the second position.) The base of these mirrors is flat and the must be mounted to an equally flat surface. And, neither one really improved my view. I saw pretty much the same thing in my regular mirrors.  They just don't have enough swivel to change the viewing angle from what is seen the the stock mirrors. So, bad purchase.

title: Just not a good product. Period.
text:
First, look at the stock Jeep 'rock rail' laying parallel to the edge of the driveway. The rock rail is CURVED. These running boards are extruded aluminum that are straight. Aluminum is NOT a good material for running boards. And, straight means it will not conform to the shape of the jeep the way the stock rock rails do. The mounting brackets are very exposed and you don't get the finished look that they have in the pictures.

The black powder coat finish is very thin and will be knocked off of the aluminum pretty quickly. It was already dinged in a couple of spots when I got them. The end caps are lightweight plastic that it held in place with pop rivets. The boards are held onto the brackets by square head nuts that are in channels in the extrusion. This is a REAL problem.....

The channels that hold the square nuts are not the right dimensions. They allow the nuts to fall out. But, you CANNOT get the nuts back in place, when they do. There are no instructions given on how to handle that problem.

There are eight mounting brackets that go into the original mounting locations on the jeep. So, no drilling. But, there is something that I do wonder about. The instructions say that the four shorter brackets go in the back locations on the jeep. However, because of the curvature of the jeep's original boards, would the brackets work better if the two shorter brackets were in the center and the two longer brackets were at the ends? It makes sense to me that this would make the new STRAIGHT running boards conform better to the CURVED shape of the jeep. But, you know what? I didn't engineer this thing and am not going to waste my time trying out different ways to mount them. All I can tell you is they didn't fit very well, leaving too much of a gap, using the instructions provided.

I really wish that this was a better product. It looked great in their pictures and the price seemed really reasonable. But, I guess I need to keep looking.

title: Good cosmetic repair.
text: This product is good for providing a good, TEMPORARY repair to the leather and 'pleather' interior surfaces in your car. Like makeup, it will need to be reapplied occasionally. You clean the surface with alcohol before applying, remove the product with alcohol if it's not right and start over with alcohol when you need to 'redo' it. It lasts a good while, depending on the amount of wear. But, do not expect it to be a permanent fix.

title: Just what I needed to renew the patio furniture cushions.
text:
I wish I had found this, before I spent money on replacement cushions. The patio furniture is not very big and it's hard to find cushions exactly the right size and shape. But, the original cushions were sun faded and looking kind of sick.

This fabric paint is great. It soaks into and adheres to the fabric very well. The color is bright and rich. Applying it is a breeze. My only complaint is that the coverage is not great. One can only did one side of the three cushions (one love seat and two chairs). I need at least one more can to finish the job. But, I'll probably get two, just to make sure I have full and complete coverage on both sides and all the bolsters. A full and thorough application leaves the fabric feeling kind of stiff, like it was new. It helps protect the fabric from further sun damage and makes it last much longer.

Despite the disappointing coverage, I still have to give it five stars. I don't think that you will do any better than this fabric paint from Dupli-Color.

title: A DIYer's must have.
text:
I have a project in my garage, where I'm installing suspended storage shelving and things aren't lining up exactly right with my architecture. The only way to fix it is to drill new holes, make new places to bolt things together. Enter the WETOLS rivet nut tool. To be honest, I've never used one of these before and it took me a minute to figure it out, even with the well written instructions. But, I know the WETOLS brand and know that this is a quality tool and I will have no problems with it. I've already gone to the local big box hardware store and found that they carry more rivet-nuts that will work with this set. So, life is good.

The tool itself is very well made, nice and tight construction, super tough materials, intricate adjustments. The ferrule selection and parts are great, the most commonly used sizes in SAE and metric. I can see where this would come in real handy in a mechanic's shop or a body shop. But, in my shop, it will be mostly for construction. In fact, I'm going out with my SIL to set up some racking for data systems and networks. This will come in real handy for securing the systems to walls and floors.

Good stuff. Very happy. Five stars.

title: Very impressive ground lighting effects kit!
text:
I'm not done with the installation yet. There's a lot of wiring still to tighten up, hide and secure. But, just had to include a picture of this bike with lights installed. Cool huh? I am VERY impressed with this kit. It was designed for cars. But, I looked at the brightness and durability of this set and decided to adapt it to my bike. It is a challenge, finding ways to hide all of that excess wiring. But, I have a 'bagger' with all kinds of nooks and crannies. So, I'll make it work. The brightness of these lights is controllable (THANK YOU!) Because if I left them on full bright, you wouldn't see anything but lights coming down the road.

I'm still not sure how the IR 'credit card' remote works. I've been looking for the receiver sensor. Can't find it. But, it works. ??? The color / brightness / music responsiveness all work.

I can't wait, to take my '08 Vulcan 2000 Classic down the street one evening, with the tunes thumping and the lights rocking. I can't use blue. It's against the law law in Texas. But, it's gonna be so cool. Five stars.

title: Works for motorcycles, too!
text:
We like to pick a destination that we've never been to, just get on the bike and ride. My phone's nav system will allow me to stay off the major highways. That's what we like, the backroads, cruising, taking our time and enjoying the countryside. In order to use my phone, I needed a mount.

This mount, marketed for bicycles, actually works very well for my motorcycle. As you can see in the pics, it fits the handlebar just right. I tested the turn radius and it does not interfere. And, it holds my Galaxy Note 20 Ultra just fine. Riding, even over rough roads, there's no bounce or vibration. (This can vary, depending on your bike. I have a really big fat cruiser that doesn't bounce or vibrate much anyway. So....)

The mount is very well made, of quality materials. It adjusts to different bar diameters easily and tightens down with a twist. The dual clamping system holds the phone in place very securely. No worries about the phone coming loose and bouncing down the highway. (The HORROR!) As much as my phone cost, believe me, it's a genuine concern!

So, overall, I am very pleased with this bike phone mount. Five stars.

title: Worth the investment.
text: I tried those cheap sets, where you get ALL of the letters, numbers and a few special characters at a bargain price. They turned out to be not such a bargain. The chrome faded off in less than a year. So, scrape them off and start over. This set looks much better. Even looks like the OEM lettering. It cost more, getting the exact lettering I needed already selected for me. But, so far, it looks to be worth the investment. Five stars.

title: Great cargo area mat for your Cadillac XT5
text: My wife just got a new Cadillac XT5. It's a beautiful SUV. The first thing we wanted to add was floor mats and a cargo area mat. These are GREAT. They are a perfect fit, cover the floor completely and come up the sides enough to provide additional protection there. They are well engineered, well made with nice thick material. The one thing that I would change is that they should have a cargo area mat that still allows you to use the cargo bar that comes with the vehicle. This mat covers the tracks that the cargo bar uses for mounting. But, otherwise, I have no doubt that they will last for the 3.5 year lease on her new car. Great purchase. Four stars. (I had to ding them one star for not including the ability to use the cargo bar.)

title: Perfect floor mats for your XT5!
text: My wife just got a new Cadillac XT5. It's a beautiful SUV. The first thing we wanted to add was floor mats. These are GREAT. They are a perfect fit, cover the floor completely and come up the sides enough to provide additional protection there. They are well engineered, well made with nice thick material. I have no doubt that they will last for the 3.5 year lease on her new car. Great purchase. Five stars.

title: When nuts and bolts just won't do.
text: I had a special project, attaching some heat barrier material to the bottom of a saddlebag, to prevent it from getting too hot, so close to the exhaust pipe on my motorcycle. Nuts and bolts just didn't seem like the right fasteners for the job. So, I got this WETOLS rivet gun set. Perfect. Nothing more satisfying to a handyman like me, than getting the job done right. A panel of fiberglass heat shield wrap with a panel of galvanized flashing on top of that, all held in place by six perfectly placed, nice and tight pop rivets (with washers). The drills came in really  handy for getting the right size holes, the first time. Good purchase. Five

title: Stiffen up your tag!
text: This polished, thick gauge stainless steel backing plate will help prevent vibration if you're riding a 'shaker' and also help prevent bending or breaking your tag and tag frame when bumped. It's very well made of solid SS with no burs, snags or die marks, fits perfectly behind the plate. Only issue I have is that it's a little on the pricey side. But, I haven't found anything to compare it to, either. So, four stars.

title: Keeping it legal with a little style.
text: I've been riding the same bike since 2008. I modified it the same year I got it where the license plate was relocated to the bottom of the fender, instead of on top of the tail light. This year, the guy that inspected my bike (the same guy that inspected it for the previous three years) told me that I needed to have a light shining on the license plate. So, I ordered this device. The LED's built into the top of the frame shine down on the plate enough to satisfy the state and their requirements. And, it wasn't too hard to install, with no wires showing. My only complaint would be the cheap crap nuts and bolts that came with it to secure the license plate in the frame. This is a nice chromed accessory that serves a valuable purpose. Why not include chromed allen head screws and 'nylock' nuts for the back? The hardware that they supplied is absolutely the cheapest they could find.  I WILL be finding better hardware. But, the lighted frame looks good and does the job. So, gotta give them four stars for that.

title: Needs to be redesigned.
text:
The looks of this headlight visor are very nice. A good coat of chrome polish should prevent rust. You could even clean it really well (to remove any oil or residue) and use a clear polyurethane on the underside, which would be the most likely area to rust. However, just keeping your bike stored in a dry place (garage?) when you're not riding should do it. Now, the down side..... They really need to redesign this thing to include some type of spring steel retaining clip rail that would hold it in place. It just slops around, flopping and turning. Very poor design. I, like others who have reviewed this product, have resorted to using some silicone sealant to hold it in place. Done properly, this will work. But, to me, we shouldn't have to resort to jerryrigging like this, to attach the visor to the headlight bucket. I like the look, it goes very well with my bike. But, c'mon, Kuryakin. Is this the best you can do?

(Later) After doing what I feel is an EXCELLENT installation job, installing the visor in the rim of the headlight bucket and securing it with some silicone, I re-read the instructions and can see that they want you to remove the headlight from the retaining ring (which requires MUCH disassembly) place the visor at the top of that and then re-install the headlight.

I have a BIG problem with that. The ring is thin metal, NOT designed to be tinkered with and does NOT fit well after having the additional thickness of the visor added to it. So, even though I didn't follow the instructions, I still feel that my installation is better than what they suggest. And, that if they would redesign it to include a retaining device of some kind, to hold it in the rim of the bucket, it would be a MUCH better design that what they currently have. My original rating of three stars still stands.

title: Great animal alert whistles.
text: These alert whistles seem to work very well. They seem to get the attention of animals BEFORE I get very close to them, as I'm driving. I try to look closely, and see how they react. I travel a lot of country roads. Birds, dogs, cows, Armadillos and Skunks are all over the place. I see them off in the distance. But, they're always well off the road, long before I get near them. One whistle has a note you can hear. The other is too high pitched for the human ear. I think that it's the combination of the two that is so effective. The chrome plating looks good. The double stick 3M foam tape will NOT accidently come unstuck. IMPORTANT - ALWAYS slip the whistle out of the mount, before going through a car wash, if you want to keep them.

title: Very good protection for your car, AND theirs.
text: The thickest, strongest and most durable door edge guards I've ever seen. Very easy to install, trims easily with scissors (in between the metal clips). Then, if you cut at a clip, it's easy to just pull the clip out. They're not connected. The plastic part actually feels like silicone, it's so rubbery and flexible. Which is a good thing. it conforms to bends and corners easier. I got the 'brilliant white' ones, thinking it would match my truck. They're actually a little whiter. But, I know that with age they will darken a little and match perfectly. 16' was more than long enough to do all four doors on my truck and have about 4 feet left over. The soft thick body of these guards will absorb a LOT of impact, protecting my truck and whatever vehicle my wife bangs the doors into. Great purchase. Five stars.

title: Protecting the original leather....
text: .....and doing it with nice styling. I have a Denali. It's the nicest vehicle I have ever owned. I probably won't get another. I've been driving it for a while and I'm always doing new things to protect it. Finally, I looked at the nice leather wrapped steering wheel, and how the leather is starting to get real smooth and shiny. So, after a good cleaning, I wrapped it with this beautiful cover from ValleyComfy. It looks great and was really easy to install. Ony thing that may be an issue is how much thicker it made the steering wheel. It's okay for me. I'm 6'6" and can palm a basketball. My wife on the other hand, is 5'3" and has hands like a little kid. Oh well. I drive it 99% of the time anyway. Good purchase. Five stars.

title: Compact, smart and effective charger.
text: I needed a new trickle charger / tender for my motorcycle. The old one was starting to give me some trouble. This one from TANKPOW is doing a SUPER job. I hooked it up (using the same built in connectors that my old one had) and plugged it in. It automatically selected the right voltage and amperage and immediately started charging. And, I'm comfortable leaving it connected, knowing that after the charging is done, it will automatically drop down to 'tending' and keep my motorcycle battery at peak performance. Very happy with this charger. Five stars.

title: An expansion set for storing stuff and MORE.
text: I bought these for my truck. But they're too small for that. So, I gave them to my wife for her XTS. She loves them. Now, she has a place to drop her keys (instead of in a cup holder) and other things. And, seeing that her regular cup holders are already full of other things, she now has these for her coffee or other beverages. They look really nice with the PLU leather and red stitching. Very sporty. Good purchase. Five stars.

title: Better than expected.
text: [[VIDEOID:5d2cacf21e008569f72cdedba5548e38]] I got this compact portable compressor for my daughter. I'm trying to teach her independence. Until recently, she didn't even know how to check the air in her tires. Now, she knows how to inflate them and has the tool to do it with. So, there's no excuse for her to drive around on a low tire. Before I put this compressor in her trunk, I tested it and adjusted the stored pressure setting for her car. That's one thing that I like, you can set the pressure you want it to inflate to. It will reach that pressure and stop. The next thing that surprised me was how large the compressor actually is. Don't be fooled by the compact size of the casing. Inside is a much larger compressor than many of the competitors. You can tell by the sound and the feel. It's running at a lower RPM, and inflates the tire much more quickly, without a lot of heat dissipation. I would NOT recommend this compressor for pick up trucks. Because the cord is too short to reach the back wheels. But, for sedans, coupes and compacts, it's great. Good purchase. Five stars.

title: Perfect upgrade for your Hail Storm suspension!

They do an okay job of absorbing hard impacts and preventing wear and tear. But, the rebound is too stiff. And, dirt, sand and gravel can get caught in the plastic, causing wear and tear, and prevent proper function. This set of oil capped all metal shocks is the perfect upgrade. No more concerns about wear and tear. Plus, the rebound is not quite as stiff, providing a much more controlled and realistic operating experience. Note: at the top of the shocks, you will have to add a small washer between the shock and it's mounting point, to prevent the shock contacting the swing arm. Great purchase. Five stars.

title: A great little quad for beginners!
text: [[VIDEOID:98ade25527f0ab1533754c88a8ab231f]] This little Syma X5UW is a great first quadcopter. Like all Syma quads, it's very durable, surviving most low speed impacts with no damage. The flight time is about 8 minutes, with a fresh battery. The basic controls are pretty straight forward and easy to understand. For a first time flyer, there might be a small learning curve about fine tuning the trims and understanding what all of the other control functions are. But, once you have them down, it really does make flying this quad a lot of fun. Most useful is the ability to change the response modes from slow to fast. In slow, the speed and angles at which the quad flies are perfect for the novice flyer on a calm day. In fast, the quad will be more aggressive and fly much faster. This is good for a more experienced flyer on days with surface winds up to 10 MPH. I would not recommend flying with stronger winds. Because the quad is small and so light weight, it could be carried away. The quad has a barometric pressure sensor, that provides pretty decent altitude hold. This is great. You don't have to worry about keeping the quad at the desired altitude, while you're doing your other maneuvers. The stated control range is about 150 feet. But, like all Syma quads, you can control it as far as you can see it. But, don't let it get out of sight. The onboard camera is decent, for a quad this size. The video is a little shaky. But, that's to be expected for this size and price point of a quad. I like the proprietary battery. Very easy to connect / disconnect. No cords to fiddle with. I cut my flying teeth on a Syma X8C, this ones big brother. And, I have flown several of the Syma X5's without all the other features this one has. This one is definitely a step up from the basic X5. Spare parts are readily available, as are extra batteries and multi-battery chargers. If you like to fly as much as I do, get this quad and some more batteries.This one comes with two batteries, which is good for a short outing, a total of about 16 minutes of air time. All in all, I'd say that the Syma X5UW is a fun little quad. It would make a great gift. I'm pleased with my purchase.

Push screws through two holes at top of mount. Keep them pushed through as you line them up with the holes in the bumper (keeping mount held way from bumper's surface). Screw both screws into the bumper (no need to tighten completely). Press the mount against the bumper and hold for a few seconds. Remove the two screws, put your plate on the mount, reinstall and tighten the two top screws. The two bottom screws can now be installed. The bottom screws only go through the plate and mount, not the bumper. Then, admire your work, and put your screwdriver away.

title: Effective but Awkward
text:
I live in Virginia. We are supposed to have multiple days next week with temperatures in the upper 90s, and since I don't have any sort of garage or awning to park my car under getting something like the Igo Worldwide Sunshade became crucial in the last few weeks.

Pros:
1. It is effective at cooling down the car. One side is a silver reflective material/color and the other is a flat black. I didn't measure the temperature difference in my car between using it and not using it, but I bet it was 30 degrees Fahrenheit. It was a HUGE difference.
2. Not obnoxious picture or "send help" message on either side. People always put the "send help" messages up by accident making them useless, and the last thing I want is a picture of tweety bird or something stupid on my car.
3. Large enough to cover the whole windshield.

Cons:
1. Awkward. It's not easy to unfold and put into the windshield. I'm not sure what design feature could fix this, but I'm not an inventor for a reason.
2. It arrived nicely packaged and folded up in a cool pouch, but I can't get it to fold back up to fit in there again. It easily folds in half, but not into 1/4th or 1/8th of its full size (whichever it needs) to get back into the storage pouch. I'm sure I could wrangle it back in there eventually, but I'm never going to bother with that each time I use it. When I tried it kept popping back open and snacking into me, and I just gave up; it's easier to leave it folded in half even though it takes up a lot of room in the car that way.

The Igo Worldwide Car Sunshade works very well at cooling off the car, but it is not easy to put in and take out of the windshield or breakdown and for that reason I would rate it at about 3.5 stars overall. I recommend it for cooling only if ease of use and storage are not crucial functions of a sunshield for you.

title: Not the greatest artwork I've ever seen
text:
Over the decades I've acquired a few black paisley bandanas -- they're useful in all sorts of ways, from an improvised table to a tourniquet to headwear to a scarf to filter air in a sandstorm -- really an essential item, right up there with a pair of sunglasses and a hat. You want one on hand when you travel anywhere, and maybe more than one. These seem well-made and big, and the printing is good, but the design is not smooth polished, and some of the design elements are bizarre IMHO. If you don't pay attention to it, you won't be bothered by it. I paid attention to it. Not the best bandana design I've ever seen by a good measure. They'll do for what I have in mind, but I think I'll keep my eye out for another few black paisley bandanas with a better design... And the thing is, all they had to do is design one quarter of the area, the other area are flipped or reflected.. The design looks good small, but at real-world 22x22 inch size, not so much.

title: Typically excellent Griot's Garage product
text:
I've purchased quite a few items from Griot's Garage -- an exceptionally great set of German screwdrivers, perfect metal gas cans (no longer available in the US thanks to Nanny State rules), on and on. Mr. Griot is an actual person and a real car nut. From reading his catalog and web site I know he goes to extreme lengths to find the PERFECT solution to an automotive problem.

Which brings me to this modest but well thought-out interior cleaning kit. It's just about perfect. The cleaner is superior to Armor-All, it cleans with zero residue, which I am ecstatic about. The two green clothes and the split blue sponge applicator and also typically perfect. I have yet to find anything to use the rubber dressing spray on.

One thing I'd want to include in an interior cleaning kit would be one of those fat short paintbrush type brushes which are ideal for getting dust out of edges and vents. They're about $2 at any auto parts store.

One other thing you'll want to get your claws on when you order this set: A BASKET OF SOME KIND! Like one of those ubiquitous plastic mesh type organizer baskets[[ASIN:B000HMC9ZK Sterilite Medium White Ultra Basket]] to keep these items in! This kit comes in a plastic bag which doesn't present the contents particularly well. So pick up a basket or something like that to store these items in.

100% worth the money. Griot's Garage has an exception reputation for the absolute best in auto care products. Worth every penny. And a clean car is just one of those small things that makes life better, you know?

Amazon will not accept returns for this battery. Amazon says to return it to the dealer, but the dealer can't do anything about it. I spoke with Optima on the telephone, and they are sorry I am going through this, but since Amazon is not an authorized seller, Optima cannot help me either.

title: Not sure whether it's really 1800LM - here's some math.
text:
Got the 4 inch spot, 6 LED version of this light - description states 1800lm output, but after hooking up my multimeter to the leads, it shows an amperage draw of 0.822 amps at 12.6V which means it uses about 10.35watts. That comes out to be a maximum of 1.725 watts per LED (certainly less after the the internal power supply/voltage conversion losses). The description states OSRAM LEDs, so I went to the Osram's website and lookup product specifications for their LED modules, their most efficient LED gives about 154 lumen per watt. So... 154 lumens x 1.725 watts x 6 lights = slight less than 1600 lumens, and this is being way generous with no power supply loss and assuming Auxbeam used the priciest and most effecient OSRAM LEDs to build the product.

If my math is wrong or I missed something, someone please correct me and I'll be happy to update this review.

With all this being said, the narrow spot lamp is BRIGHT, even if it doesn't seem to output match according to spec.

title: It fits in the valve cover, BUT …

Maybe someone will invent a tool to remove old and brittle grommets and keep the pieces from getting into the top of the valves. That would necessitate removing the valve cover. The tool could incorporate something like a tiny upside down umbrella.

title: This replaced a PCV valve that may have been the original
text:
It was my brother-in-law's 2002 Sable which has the PCV valve on the passenger side and clearly visible by the rubber elbow that connects the PCV valve. This is the Vulcan engine. A piece of emissions tubing had to be inserted between the elbow and PCV valve. I replaced the old grommet with a new one. That required some effort and pushing around the circumference with a flat blade screwdriver to get it seated in the valve cover. All the rubber parts had splits in them. A shop had replaced one of the fuel injectors, and they should have replaced the PCV valve and connecting tubing when they had to remove the valve cover. The rubber parts had to be cut off since they had hardened and would not pull off.

Then a 3/8 inch (OD) nylon barb connector was used to connect the emission tubing (about a 3 inch long piece) to the elbow (bought at Advance Auto since the one I ordered through Amazon won't be delivered for another week or more – about a month altogether – cost was about double the Amazon part, even though it was the same manufacturer). A lot of force was required to get all of it together and in place. However, the engine no longer stumbles, surges or sets a CEL.

Those 2 other plastic pieces (the black ones that came with the PCV valve) were not required. They may be needed on other vehicles.

title: Replacement part due to bad battery clamp
text:
Although I ordered this after replacing the starter in October 2020, I did not swap out this new one for the old one in the 2002 Mercury Sable. Instead, I used a nut on the back side of the clamp so that the positive battery post clamp would tighten. The built-in nut on the old (original) battery post clamp had been stripped over the years due to various battery disconnections by dealer service shop and other shops when the starter, alternator and 6 batteries were replaced over the years.
The cable is the right length and has the correct attaching ring terminals.
When I ordered it in January 2021, it WAS the correct part for the 2002 Mercury Sable. Today it is NOT. I had checked with another source that said this was the correct part.

title: Easy to replace once the serpentine belt is off the tensioner
text:
In the 2002 Mercury Sable, the clearance between the frame and the tensioner is not enough for most sockets and simple wrenches. So I ground off sides of the tool I bought for moving tensioner pulleys. Then I removed the tension on the belt and moved the belt off the alternator pulley and held it up with a small bungee cord (I did not want to have to route the belt through the pulleys when the clearance is barely an inch and I plan to replace the 11 year old belt in the future).
The original bolt and washers that were with the old pulley were reused. No more wobble due to failing bearings.
It has been only 2 weeks since this was replaced, but so far so good.

title: Still installing
text:
UPDATE (4/5/2021): Completed the installation 2 days later after getting my serpentine belt tool. The clearance between the frame and the tensioner bolt was less than needed to accomplish the procedure with a socket and wrench. It required a special tool. However, I still had to grind down the edges of the tool to get the socket onto and off the bolt. That was done, and the alternator was installed. The new alternator has been performing ever since it was installed 3 months ago. Output voltage while running is 14.2–14.5 volts.

Original Review (1/27/2021):
The alternator appears to be an exact match in terms of its physical size and configuration as the one that is being replaced. The car I am installing it in is at another location, and I was unable to complete the installation due to the fact that I did not have the serpentine belt tool necessary to remove the belt.

Inside the box was a small piece of paper, a leaflet, that said INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS on the outside. Hahaha. Not one word as to HOW the alternator was to be installed. A decent set of instructions would have said the clearance between the frame and the idler pulley was barely more than one inch and a special tool would be needed. With that bit of information, the replacement might have been accomplished in less than 30 minutes.

title: Replacement was easy
text:
UPDATE (March 25, 2022):

I ordered mine in January 2020 and installed it the same time. Today, March 25, 2022, it was replaced with a Motocraft ignition coil because 2 of the coils had failed, causing the engine to run so rough it could not reach speeds above 20 MPH. It had to be towed to an auto service center for analysis and replacement at a jacked up price. Elapsed mileage was 9,128 miles.

Original Review (February 10, 2020):

The ignition coil arrived packaged well BUT one of the towers was broken off when I opened the box. I reported this immediately to Amazon, and a replacement was sent. The broken ignition coil was returned after I verified the replacement was good.

The replacement arrived. I used a black marker to indicate which spark plug cable went where, and I disconnected the ground to the battery. The numbering does not have to indicate which cylinder the cable goes to, only the sequence they are attached to the new ignition coil.

Only 3 nuts had to be removed to remove the old ignition coil. The new one went on easily with no problems. Reconnected the battery and checked the operation of the Sable. No problem.

title: Preparing for first use - now done
text:
UPDATE (8/17/2019):

Pumped old oil out through dipstick tube with no spills. About half of the oil was evacuated after the first 15 pumps on the handle, so additional pumping was required to get all of the oil out of the oil pan. Got together the jug of oil, new filter cartridge, wrench and 32mm socket to remove the old filter cartridge while the first half of the oil was evacuated. Removed old filter cartridge while the second half of the oil was evacuated. Moved the tubing in the dipstick tube up and down to ensure it was getting to the bottom and removing all the oil. Since the end of the tubing was cut diagonally, it's not likely that it can bottom out and stop the flow of oil.

The tubing is stiff, so it takes a bit of doing to place the tubing so that it will drain oil without making a mess. The used oil was then pumped into the now-empty oil jug - after pushing UP on the vacuum control valve on the side of the pumping mechanism. Most of the oil came out of the MityVac. No spills here.

Later I may use some paper towel and plug the tubing ends and hang the tubing so any oil left in the tubing can drain out.

This was bought so I would not have to jack up my vehicle and crawl underneath to drain the oil. It worked like a charm - once it was clear as to how everything fit together. I did NOT crawl under the vehicle to see how much oil might have been left in the oil pan. The price of this MityVac will be repaid after I use it twice since that's the cost of an oil change using full synthetic Mobil 1.

INITIAL REVIEW (8/16/2019):

The little booklet has been printed using tiny print, making it difficult to read.
The diagram is not very helpful.
The Extractor / Dispenser valve is not anywhere on the diagram, and somewhere it should tell the user to push the button DOWN to Extract fluids and UP to Dispense fluids.
Also, the pressure / vacuum relief button is not labeled on the diagram.

In a few minutes I am about to use mine for the first time.

Years ago I dropped the tank on my Ford van so I could repair the non-functioning fuel level float. I put a drop of solder on the end of the float arm so it would once again make contact with the rheostat. The van had sufficient clearance that I could work without a lift.

title: Lock should keep out vandals
text:

UPDATE (1/13/2019):
I bought this locking gas cap in November, installed as soon as possible and have been using it since then (a little more than 2 months). It is a PAIN to have to insert the key to lock this cap every time I get gas. The good news is that I have not seen a Check Engine Light due to a loose gas cap. INITIAL review (11/10/2018):
This was ordered when I found that someone had opened the fuel access door. Now I should not have to worry about foreign substances being put in my gas tank.
Someone had written a review that said the cap he ordered locked when the cap was tightened. This one requires the key to lock. Just turning the cap does not lock it.

I noticed a blue thread-like item in the keyhole of the lock. After making photos, I used needle point tweezers to remove the blue thread.
What I wonder is why blue thread would be in the lock. How did the thread get in there?
Also, I noticed that one of the two keys had a couple of spots of what appeared to be rust - only one side. Photographed again. Used a pencil eraser to remove the surface rust. Still have small pitted areas from the rust.
How long does a piece of plated iron (it's magnetic, so it's iron) have to sit around before it develops rust spots? And where was it stored?

The gas cap has been installed. When I drive somewhere, I will be able to determine whether a Check Engine warning light comes on due to a gasket not sealing.

Maybe when I have more time I will attach the tether to this new cap.

Stay tuned for any updates.

title: replace stock headlight bulbs
text:
In 2013 when I bought these I had just bought a used 2012 GM Chevy Equinox. My wife noticed a couple days ago that my driver side headlight was dark when I unlocked the door using the remote.
