title: solves the problem with the CEL
text:
UPDATE [February 12, 2021]:
Still no problems and no check engine light (CEL).

On my 2012 Equinox, one of the hardest parts of the job was removing the front stainless steel band because the screw is difficult to reach. This has to be done in order to remove the intake manifold cover to allow access to the solenoids.

Then the wiring connectors have to removed from the solenoids. Before removing the sensors, use compressed air to blow the dirt, dust and debris from around the solenoids.

Another source says "Next there’s a trick to disconnecting the electrical connector from each camshaft position actuator solenoid. First you have to pull up on the lock tab so that you can push on the release button and then wiggle the connector free from the actuator.

Note that on the intake side that this lock tab is a different color and easy to see. You can use a small pick set to lift up on the tab and release the lock.

The important thing to remember is these plastic connectors are now more than 10 years old and very brittle. Failure to take your time with this connection can break the connector and change the ease of your repair procedure."

Unfortunately, that source did not have a diagram to aid in disconnecting the wiring.

Since the steel bolts are being screwed into softer aluminum valve covers, use hand tools only to tighten the bolts.

INITIAL Review [September 5, 2018]:
My Check Engine Light has not come on since I replaced these solenoids - both of them - almost a month ago.
The reason I replaced both was because whatever caused a clog in one of them would probably have clogged the other as well.
On my 2012 Equinox, the hardest parts of the job were 1) removing the front stainless steel band because the screw is difficult to reach and 2) disconnecting the electrical connectors from the solenoids. Removing the white connector keeper is not difficult. Removing the connector itself is a bit more difficult since everything that has to be pried loose is hidden from sight.

title: Good solution for a replacement remote - or an emergency remote
text:
UPDATE (3/27/2020):
This key fob has been used every time I drive somewhere, although it has been inconsistent in whether it responds on one press or after several presses. Original review was 3/18/2018-
Just had the key cut at the locksmith for $30 plus another $10 for a blank key cut (in case of lock-out).
Programming the new remote occurred before I realized it had been done.

title: Short grip on my lug nuts as it came from the manufacturer
text:
This was bought so I could use a DEEP 22mm socket on my lug nuts. I ordered it even though someone else commented that it only fit 3/4 inch of the lug nuts. Another person said he used a smaller socket that fit inside the 22mm socket and hit the smaller socket to drive down the plastic insert with a large hammer. Although I have not removed it yet, perhaps the metal has a ridge to prevent the plastic insert from moving.

The manufacturer COULD have used a neoprene insert as was done by spark plug socket manufacturers years ago.

title: Fits the 2012 Equinox as expected
text:
Update (12/25/2020):

With cold temperatures expected and perhaps some precipitation, I decided to change the oil before Christmas day. First thing I did was loosen the cap on the oil filter. I have the large 32mm socket with 3/8-inch drive. I removed the dipstick and that allows for a 3/8-inch ratchet to be used. Then I used a vacuum pump device to extract the used oil through the dipstick tube. No crawling under the vehicle to drain the oil through the bottom. Replacing the filter cartridge is not difficult. Before using a wrench to tighten the filter cap, be sure to turn the cap backwards to find the starting location of the threads. Otherwise, the threads could be stripped, a problem if one does not have a spare cap.

Original Review (3/22/2017):

Fit 2012 Equinox as expected. Installation was not a problem.

It IS possible to change the filter without draining the oil - unlike canister-style oil filters. Why would you do that? Perhaps you have some reason to suspect your oil has been contaminated or that the oil is not circulating properly. Examination of the oil filter should provide the answer to either.

Ignore the Amazon "This does not fit your" vehicle. Compare the part number with the AC Delco part number if you are doubtful. I believe Amazon finally has corrected the info for this part, however.

title: Good replacements
text:
Replaced 12-year-old headlights in 2002 Mercury Sable. No real problems. Now much clearer.

No amber turn signal bulb was included. I'll have to remove the headlights at a later date to replace the amber bulbs. I had clear 4157LL bulbs but not amber. That will take 10 minutes to replace both.

The wiring harness has to be secured and no push-on retainers are supplied. It is easy enough to cut off the plastic posts of the old lights and remove the retainers that push on the posts of the new lights.

A how-to video on YouTube helped me to see how to remove / replace the headlights.

Once these are replaced, it should be another 12 years before they need replacing again. I didn't waste my time trying to buff off the yellowing / haze on the old headlights. That happens to the exterior / outer surface which is supposed to protect the headlights from UV radiation. Once those abrasives - toothpaste included - are used to "restore" the headlights, the protective outer layer is removed, and the headlights will soon look bad again. Save the time and effort and replace the headlights, especially when the vehicle is ten or more years old.

Several years ago I replaced the headlights on a 1998 Cadillac DeVille. The problem was that there were tiny fissures IN the plastic, not a yellowing of the outer protective layer. If this is the problem with your headlights, then replacement is the ONLY real solution to the problem.

title: S-L-O-W
text:

The charger with the spliced plug for connecting to the battery directly (via 3-prong connector) is still functioning.

Now the only problem with this is the battery (actually, 2 12-volt SLA batteries connected in series) - after a period of time - 5 years for the original and 1 year for the replacement bought as a new unit with the new housing - the batteries swell and cannot fit inside the Earthwise mower. title: Good replacement

title: Less than expected
text:
Several facts about the inflator I received are below.

1. The inflator needs a handle on the "front" end where most of the weight is. It should not be in the back where there is no practical handhold due to the DC cable being stored in that area.
2. Because the DC cable is not always used, the ON-OFF switch does not need to be located where the DC cable covers it. It should be more accessible.
3. My first use of the inflator was to inflate a punch ball. That's a ball which is a heavy-duty balloon that will be about 14 to 18 inches in diameter once it is inflated. This inflator supplies enough pressure, but the volume of air is severely lacking. I can blow up a balloon quicker than this inflator. It makes me wonder how long it will take to inflate a tire on my vehicle.

The $40 Bonaire Portable 120-Volt Compressor has the handle and switch where they need to be. However, it didn't blow up the balloon using the inflator attachment that came with the compressor.

For more money, I had thought I would have a product that covered all the points.

And, yes, they ALL are noisy.

title: Save some money
text:
Buy replacement headlight assemblies and install them yourself instead of paying over $100 more to have someone do it for you. These improve the light-throwing ability of my car.

Those products in a bottle remove plastic (damaged or not) on the surface of the headlight, but they do nothing for all the very tiny fractures in the plastic. Shine a flashlight on the plastic while you are as close as possible to the headlight, and you will see those fractures that look like small streaks in the plastic. This may not be a problem for more recent cars once the manufacturers realized what was happening to the plastic when exposed to the sun over the years.

The reason for the lack of five stars is that the instructions mention nothing about aiming the headlights once they are installed.

These came with standard high beam and low beam lamps already installed. I am thinking about replacing them with brighter lamps. You should replace the amber side-marker / turn lamps when you replace the headlights.

It appears to be pretty accurate. My husband tried it out on both of our vehicles. I have an Audi A7 and he has an F350. It does seem that the air in the tires depends on the weather. The time of year serves as a reminder that a drop in tire inflation pressures corresponds with the falling thermometer readings. Air pressure in a tire typically goes down 1-2 pounds for every 10 degrees of temperature change. Also from what I have researched on this is that Underinflation is the worst because it causes increased tread wear on the outside edges of the tire. It also generates excessive heat, and it can reduce fuel economy by increasing rolling resistance. Soft tires make the vehicle work harder.

So having one of these tire pressure gauges around can be very handy.

title: Works for keeping track of vehicle speed, but I wouldn't recommend it for anything else.
text:
This connects to the OBD port. It records data such as speed, rpm's, and many other selectable data points. It also has audible alarms as an options, such as over speeding and sudden braking. When I got this initially it worked as intended. It kept a track of car speed, gave alarms at appropriate times, etc. When my father drove the car with this in it, he complained about the beeping - he has a habit of speeding so this was nice.

I have also used this to collect OBD errors from some cars, but there are cheaper methods to do the same thing. This didn't work on at least one car, I think it was a 2001 Chrysler.

This device isn't issue free though. When I tried to select more data points to keep track of though I got errors when trying to import the data. Since then I removed all of the other options except for speed. I wish this came with a memory card slot so raw data could be read directly. When I moved from an elevation of 200 feet above sea level to 5000 feet above sea level I noticed that the g meter for deceleration seemed to be broken. The alarm for hard breaking would constantly go off even at the most gentle stop. There is a way to adjust the alarm level for breaking in software, but if I figured what's the point since it will be wrong again if drove to a different altitude.

The biggest issue I have with this, though, is the software. While you can import trip data which will plot graphs there is no way to export it. If I wanted to combine data from several different trips together there is no way to do this. Not even as a text. If I wanted to email someone a graph, I would have to take a screen shot of the program window and then crop it. It's ridicules that it offers you the ability to collect this data but not give you a chance to use it in any meaningful way. Considering that several years have passed since this came on the market with no significant updates, I would not recommend it.

On the other hand for keeping track of vehicle speed or sending an alarm when over speeding, it works.

title: Micro-Suction base??
text:
I attached this to the base of a flat metal work light - applying no pressure. It stuck so well it was nearly impossible to get off. With a lot of effort I got it off and noticed the bottom of the TableCoaster was not quite the same. Rather than a 'micro suction-base,' as the manufacturer calls it, it appears to be some sort of adhesive that was compromised when I tried to reposition. Unless the manufacturer is willing to articulate what the adhesive material is I wouldn't feel comfortable putting it on any surface that you care about -- the 'micro-suction base might damage it. I look forward to the manufacturer correcting me and reassuring buyers that this is safe for various surfaces. At that point, I will change my review.

Edit: In the questions section for this product the seller has indicated that the base is "it is not an adhesive on the base, it is a polyurethane pad which is extremely tacky in nature, and making it ideally suited to create a strong but temporary bond on the surfaces to which it is applied." On the product packaging it states that this tacky base can be used over and over, however, after only using it once and not applying pressure, it was extremely difficult to remove from the surface and the tacky base was compromised.....I just don't see how it can be used over and over.

Furthermore, the packaging has a liability disclaimer that states the manufacturer will "not accept any liability for any direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages whatsoever (including to property or life), arising out of, or connected with, the use or misuse of TableCoaster."

This product seems well designed but seems best suited if you are only applying it to a surface once and don't care about the surface you are attaching it to.... I don't know if it would damage a surface as I was not willing to take that risk and the manufacture's Liability Disclaimer prevents me from going after them if there is a problem.

It would be great if they also manufactured one with a weighted base that could be quickly moved from location to location. I would buy at least a couple of those.

When I saw this product- the Eco Green Waterless car wash I decided that it would be a perfect way for me to "wash" my car. Today was a gorgeous fall day in the midwest and my kids didn't have school. We decided to spend some quality time together "washing" the van. At first the kids were not too happy - they like to use lots of water and squirt each other, but quickly got excited as we "washed the car". The van was dirty so we took a small bucket of water and used a rag to get some of the more stubborn spots off. Then we sprayed the Eco Green product on the car in various spots, used one of the clothes provided to wash the car and used the other clothe to dry it. My van looked shiny and smelled good when we were done. Th bottle says it will last through 5 uses. We used more than the allotted amount for one use, so ours will last less than 5 uses. Overall good application and great idea to be able to clean your car with limited or no water.  I received this product at a discount for my unbiased opinion.

title: Needs some improvements
text:
I am generally a fan of L&M lights, I have several of them such as the trail 1000 and seca race light. Those two products are both wonderful and I would recommend them. This vya tail light however has a number of issues that hold it back from being recommended in my book.

Pros:
- Very bright (excellent visibility to vehicles even in daylight)
- Novel blink pattern

Cons:
1) Very bright (in group ride other cyclists complain of it being too bright and distracting)
2) Bulky awkward mount/body design limits mounting positions
3) Fragile connector interface (while in use, the mount supports the connector but while charging it is an unsupported PCB just waiting to be bent/snapped if bumped too hard)
4) If used on MTB/gravel bike where there is a lot of vibration the light can wiggle loose in its mount and stop functioning (it has to be fully seated in the mount to work)

Basically, this light has potential and it could be a great tail light if they fix a few things.. make a more stable connector for charging, make the brightness lower or have variable brightness and make the unit less bukly. In its current state though I would not recommend this light.

title: Excellent replacement battery for my 2006 Mazda RX8(AT trans)
text:
This battery is a great OEM replacement for my 2006 Mazda RX8. It provides plenty of power to the vehicle for starting, etc. The battery was simple to install using the following steps:

-Use a 10mm wrench to loosen the nut that holds the terminal clamp on the negative terminal
-disconnect the negative terminal
-Use a 10mm wrench to loosen the nut that holds the terminal clamp on the positive terminal
-disconnect the positive terminal
-Take the old battery out of the compartment it is in and replace it with this new one
-connect and tighten the clamp for the positive terminal
-connect and tighten the clamp for the negative terminal

One thing about this battery that was a bit of a negative was that it was shorter than the OE Mazda battery. This meant I needed to prop the battery up a little bit so the terminal clamps could be properly fastened. I simply used the cover that came on this battery and put it underneath the battery to give a 1-2inch increase in height allowing the clamps to clear the sides of the battery well.

Pros:
*Good cranking power
*Everything power-wise runs well

Cons:

Additional Considerations:
Make sure you have a wire brush and some terminal cleaner to clean the clamps. Also some kind of electrical-conducting gel may be good to apply when installing the battery.

These tires are great replacements that fit the standard rim on a 2006 Mazda RX8. I have used Goodyear Eagle Sport on a couple of cars now and I am always happy with the tires.

They have performed well in many environments. I drove on these tires in the winter and fall in Maine and I have driven on these tires in the desert heat of California. Always impressed with the grip and stability. It is everything I look for in a set of general all weather tires.

They are definitely more pricey compared to some no-name brands out there but they last longer and when it comes to a safety critical system on my car, I don't spare expense. It is not worth sacrificing safety for a few bucks!

NOTE: amazon says this tire does not fit a 2006 mazda RX8 but that is inaccurate. It does fit.

Pros:
*Great all weather performance
*OEM fit
*They last a long time compared to no-name brands

Cons:
*Expensive(-1/4 stars)

Additional Considerations:
Make sure you order the style of tire you need or want. this is an all weather tire. It has performed well for me in the snow but these are not considered snow tires. Also be aware my suspension is totally stock in my RX8 as well as the other cars I have had these tires on. These tires may perform different if you are adjusting the camber of the wheels or some other modification.

Overall: 4.75/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

title: Excellent OEM replacement driver's side tail light. It is an exact match.
text:
This tail light is an excellent OEM spec replacement for the driver's side tail light. It matches my other tail light exactly and the fit was exactly the same.

My tail light was broken in a hit and run and ordering this tail light provided me with everything I needed to replace the housing and lenses. BE AWARE, this tail light is the housing and lenses only. It does not come with the actual bulbs that emit the light. Thankfully, I had all the bulbs in my old broken tail light. They were all still working and usable in this replacement housing. They simply twist out and twist into the new housing.

The title of the video that I followed on youtube to help replace my tail light is: MAZDA RX8 tail rear lights condensation fix naprawa parujacych lamp

To summarize the video:

You need to remove 4 or 5 plastic clips in the trunk area. This will free up the center plastic piece where the trunk latches. You can pull this out by pulling up on it. Once this piece of plastic is removed the trunk liner will be exposed and can be slightly moved to expose the electricals for the tail lights. You simply disconnect all of the plugs going to the tail light, remove two 10mm nuts that hold the tail light in, and push up on a plastic tab in the center of the tail light and the whole housing should pop out.

Make sure to clean the metal where the gasket will touch and that no dirt is present. You will want a good seal here or water will leak into your taillight housing. This is a common problem for the RX8 and there are many videos out there that will show you how to use silicone to fill in leaky areas of an older gasket.

I have included photos of the tail light installed close up as well as one showing both tail lights so you can see how well they match up.

Pros:
*OEM perfect fit
*Crystal clear lenses

Cons:
*None

Additional Considerations:
Make sure you have the bulbs you need in order make use of this tail light housing

title: Perfect OEM replacement ignition coils for 2006 Mazda RX8 (AT trans)
text:
These ignition coils were a great OEM replacement for my 2006 Mazda RX8. Thy have performed great and I could not ask for more.

In this pack you get four new ignition coils (the RX8 requires 4 in order to do a full change-out). They are all OEM spec coils and look exactly like the ones that came with the car. I have included pictures below of all sides of the coil along with packaging and what they look like when they are old and when the new ones are installed.

Be aware, the photo I have attached of them installed also shows new plug wire leads as well which are a separate part here: [[ASIN:B001RM49WK NGK (4858) ZE81 Spark Plug Wire Set]]
These new wires do not come with these coils, however I recommend changing the plugs, wires, and coils all at the same time--since it is cheap enough and it is good not to have a weak link bring down the others.

The title of the youtube video I followed along with to change my ignition coils is: How to replace RX8 coils, leads, spark plugs/Jak wymienic cewki, kable i swiece MAZDA RX8

The person in the video doesn't speak english but the subtitles were enough for me to understand. Honestly having something to look at to see how it is done visually helped me the most.

You will need a 10mm socket for most of the bolts along with a screwdriver to help undo some clips. You will also need an extension to reach into the coil area. I used a 4 inch extension and that worked great for me.

I recommend taking pictures of EVERYTHING before disconnecting things--so that you can put it all back together the way it was before. You will end up having to disconnect some vacuum hoses, etc. This can be some vital engine stuff so be slow and methodical about changing these out and it will go smooth.

Pros:
*OEM spec, perfect match
*Very good price

Cons:
*None so far

Additional Considerations:
Don't forget to take pictures when disassembling stuff.

Consider changing out the plug wire leads as well as the spark plugs all at the same time. I did this and it helped me discover a spark plug problem that was most likely preventing one of the chambers in my rotary engine from firing. Additionally, all three of these parts are kind of one "system" and having them all at the same level of newness makes the system very healthy and it will last longer.

Overall: 5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

title: Excellent OEM replacement for 2006 Mazda RX8 (AT trans)
text:
This is a great OEM spec replacement rear(or downstream)O2 sensor for my 2006 Mazda RX8. After having a check engine light and an error code point to the rear O2 sensor I ordered this in order to put it in. To get to the point, it cleared my check engine light and has performed perfectly. If you would like to hear how I replaced my O2 sensor then please read below.

Putting it in is very straight forward if you have the right tools to jack the car up and take the sensor out.

To get the sensor out it is best to use a specially made O2 sensor socket. I was able to put a $30.00 deposit down at my local Autozone and rent it out in order to use for this single job. I was allowed to keep it for up to two weeks and I got my $30.00 back when I returned it (so it was free essentially).

As far as jacking the car up I used [[ASIN:B0028JQYSS Torin T82012 Hydraulic Trolley Jack - 2 Ton in Plastic Case]] along with two [[ASIN:B000CO86BY Torin T43002 Jack Stands - 3 Ton, 1 pair]] to hold the front part of the car up. Remember to set the parking brake. On the RX8 there is an O2 sensor guard that covers the O2 sensors body and holds the wire up towards the wire harness. You can remove the two bolts that hold this on with a 10mm socket. One of my bolts broke (these are rusted and heat cycled bolts, so this is apparently common). The other bolt came out fine and was more than enough to hold the O2 guard when I reassembled it. You should be able to see the bolt holes for the O2 guard in one of my pictures. It gives you an idea of how big the guard is relative to the sensor. It is maybe 2 or 3 inches of aluminum, very light.

Once the guard was removed I unclipped the wire harness and then used the socket I borrowed from Autozone and after some force, removed the O2 sensor. Again its right in the exhaust system so it is heat cycled and will be a bit annoying to remove at first.

After the sensor is removed, take the new sensor and apply the thread lock substance that came with the sensor to the threads of the sensor. You can then screw the sensor into the threaded hole where you took the old one out. After it is in, and tightened using the socket, make sure the wire is inside of the spiral metal piece attached to the guard then bolt the guard back in. Have someone clear the check engine light, drive 50 or so miles to verify that the issue is resolved. You have yourself a new O2 sensor!

This part includes the following:
*Instructions
*O2 sensor
*thread locking substance

Pros:
*OEM spec replacement O2 sensor
*Directions came with the part

Cons:
*None so far

Additional Considerations:
Be very careful while jacking up the car to replace this part. It is on the passenger side of the vehicle but it is far enough in the center that you have to be quite far under the car. This can be very dangerous and if you have never done this before leave it to someone who understands the risks.

Be careful with the sensor before putting it in. From what I read these sensors can be damaged if dropped.

Again, the RX8 has two O2 sensors and this is the rear(downstream) sensor.

Overall: 5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

title: Second one purchased
text:
I had one of these several years ago and wound up giving it to the person who bought the SUV from me. In Alaska, winters are hard, and summers have sunlight all day. My vehicles live in harsh conditions. There are lots to like about these covers, but I have two favorite reasons:
1. The elastic combined with straps keep the cover in place, even in 40mph winds. I do not have to hunt for my car cover in the forest like I used to do with the cheaper thin covers.
2. The zipper that allows entrance to the vehicle driver's side without removing to cover is extremely useful.

Also the interior of the cover is soft and does not beat up the paint job when being buffeted by winds.

And... The bright orange marking tapes sewn into the headlight and mirror areas make for easy one-person placement on the vehicle. It is impressive how well the cover fits - WHEN YOU MEASURE before ordering.

One more thing - the price is good.

One important note: MEASURE YOUR VEHICLE. Do not guess, or assume you know the measurement. It is my own fault that I ordered a cover that is just a tad too short for my Subaru Forester. I assumed I knew the measurement, and those two extra inches make a difference. I am keeping the cover since it was the largest listed when I bought the thing. I will be improvising, but don't you do that. Get out there and measure. You will be glad you did. The previous cover I gave with the SUV I sold, fit PERFECTLY. I measured that one.

text: 2008 Chrysler Town and Country - Good Brakes.  I decided to give these a shot on my '08 Town and Country.  We're a few weeks in and so far, so good. title: Perfect for on-demand AC

title: Works perfectly
text: Very pleased with this refrigerator.  I had it in some extreme temperatures over the weekend and it kept everything exactly where I wanted it.  I was able to run it 3 days on a deep cycle battery with a solar panel.  In just a few hours after sunrise, my battery was already topped off again.  It cools down VERY quickly and is extremely quiet.  I love the light in the lid, so you can see inside in low light and the display is lit, so you can always see that it's working and your food is kept cold.  It says "dual zone" in the description, but it really isn't.  The large compartment is chilled and the smaller compartment, above the compressor, is not.  It gets some cooling from the larger compartment, but it's not a true freezer and refrigerator at the same time.  To operate in that fashion, you'd have to set the large compartment to freeze and then you have about a half gallon compartment that would be "cool".  The smaller compartment works better as a vegetable crisper.  Otherwise, very pleased with it.

title: Please read if you want to get these on
text: First off I recommend using a small flat head screwdriver with the install. let’s start off by taking the factory brake pad off, just grab a corner and pull, poof it’s off, grab your new brake pedal pad, put the top of the rubber gasket over the top of the pedal and pull down. Once the top is in the gasket take your screwdriver and go from just under the top right corner  and guide the gasket alone the right side of the pedal, now repeat on the left side, then finally do the bottom, run your fingers along the entire perimeter of the back of the pedal to ensure it is completely seated. Last thing you want is the pedal cover to come off in a hard breaking situation. If yes move on to the gas pedal if no use the screwdriver and repeat the side or bottom that isn’t seated. GAS PEDAL: DO NOT REMOVE THE FACTORY PEDAL COVER ON THIS SIDE. I started with the top right corner, then moved down the right side “since there’s not really room for the screwdriver trick on that side” get the entire top right corner/right side under the gasket. Then move to the bottom, use screwdriver as needed. Then pop the gasket over the bottom left side and move upwards towards the last corner. Again run your fingers along the gasket and make sure it’s properly seated around the gas pedal, if not use your screwdriver to correct it. THIS ALL SOUNDS RELATIVELY SIMPLE BUT IT DID TAKE ME A LITTLE WHILE TO FIGURE IT OUT AND TO PROPERLY SEAT THE GASKET

title: Simple Install (remove bumper), low-quality finish and paint
text:
Install was easy to follow using the included instructions. Install on a 2019 Honda Accord (Hybrid) involves removing the mudflaps (if equipped, not part of instructions), the bumper cover, and then the rear impact bar. Installation is reverse of removal, with the hitch installed between the impact bar and vehicle. The bumper cover did require slight trimming, following the dimensions in the instructions it worked perfectly.

The hitch itself is very straightforward, a few pieces of metal, some tubing, etc, all welded together as expected. Unfortunately, the product quality is lacking in the actual finishing of the product. It appears to have a coating of powdercoat or similar paint over raw metal. The raw metal likely was not cleaned, etched, or otherwise processed, as the paint was chipped and had flaked off in a few spots. I do not expect this to remain rust free for more than 6mo. I expect a majority of the product to show significant rust after 2-3 years, and we will probably just replace the entire thing in 3-4 years.

text:
AS Amazon apparently can't keep Upol Raptor Liner in stock, I tried this product. This is really a rubberized undercoating and not hard, bed lining product as is claimed. I use the aerosol cans of "truck bed coating" to refinish faded plastic trim parts. Surface are was properly prepped by using de-greaser, washing with soap and water, drying, scuffed with a scotch brite pad (shouldnt be needed as it's textured plastic) and I used Dupli-color plastic adhesion promoter.

The results are not even close to a hard bed liner. Applied on a hot low humidity day (10% or less in the desert) and left to cure for several days and the finish is soft and rubbery. I can indent it with a finger nail. The final stop coat left a granular texture that rubs off into fine particles. This was applied following the prep and application directions of several light coats 10 minutes or less part.

I am thoroughly dissatisfied with this product, do not recommend using it as anything other than rubberized undercoating.

I want my money back for wasting it on this product.

title: Cheap China Junk!
text:
Well, like everything these days you're choices for buying something is from China or China. I've had the older body style of GM truck mirror for the GMT900 bodies and either it was better quality or I just happened to get a decent one other than the folding part broke leaving the mirror flopping around. This version (its the new body 2013 to 2018 GM trucks) suffers from the usual problems of cheap Chinese made junk truck mirrors. The mirrors shake far to much at highway speed to use them effectively. I should be clear the mirror housings don't shake nor do the convex "spot" mirrors, only the adjustable mirrors bounce around like mad. The right side does not fit as tightly on the sleeved arms as the driver's side. This causes the right side to slowly slide out from wind pressure and road vibration. I'm positive these are all made in the same or same two or three factories and are simply resold by every Tom Dick and Harry (would that be Lee, Wang and Wong over there?) under 50 million different company names. The plastic does not even seem to be as solid as the last pair and I suspect the Arizona sun will destroy them in a few months both with sun fade and physical degradation of the plastic itself. Not worth removing and trying to return, although Ideally I'd like my money back or the mirrors replaced.

I forgot to mention the wiring harness is so flipping short it's nearly impossible to follow the factory wiring channel to the switch pack. Another example of being cheap.

-F grade here.

text:
I had for a few years the Camco RhinoFLEX 15' Sewer Hose Kit with Swivel Fitting (Automotive)I found all the components of the set to be very sturdy and I like having the translucent elbow. I've had set up for quite some time and it held up well. However, although I tried to be very conscientious about screwing the fittings onto the hose, I had several catastrophic failures! In the immortal words of Forrest Gump, that's all I'm going to say about that right now. Even though the ends of the fittings rotate where they connect to the outlets, the hose occasionally worked itself loose somehow, requiring more vigilance than I like to engage in with poop containing pipes.

Also, after a couple years of use the Camco fittings themselves began to leak. I understand that you can get new O-rings for them to remedy this, but I decided to let it go and try this Valterra brand instead. I selected the "Dominator" type, based solely on the aspect of the fittings being permanently connected to the hose. Not only is this true but if they ever decided to come loose, which doesn't look likely, you could clearly see where that was happening and not be 'surprised'. It has similar rigid construction as the rhino flex hose, but is slightly stiffer and seems slightly more heavy duty. In use, it holds its shape a little better which I find an advantage.

I miss having the clear elbow, but of course a fitting of that sort could be added.

I recommend the 'Dominator' wholeheartedly, and if my review prevents just one unfortunate "mudslide", my work is done.

This product has the towel built in so you don't have to provide your own and wash it afterwards.  None of these quick-wax product work as well as a good paste wax (don't look as good or last as long), but they do apply much more quickly. This Armor All quick-wax gives us decent results even without any buffing afterwards (always the most time consuming part of using a paste car wax). The instructions say you should buff with a separate towel on dark colored cars or if streaking is noticeable and ugly. If you're too lazy to wax your car the old fashioned way but still want it to look reasonably nice, this quick wax is a good alternative.

title: Your A/C takes forever to get cold and there's barely any air coming out of the vents?
text:
If your A/C takes forever to get cold and there's barely any air coming out of the vents like mine did, then look no further... Time to change the cabin air filter.

Great value with this carbon activated filter. Do yourself a favor and spend the 5 extra bucks for carbon.

Bought it for my 2006 Hyundai Sonata, it fits perfectly. For that vehicle, you want to detach the glove box by first pulling out to the right, with a screw driver, the black ring you can see through a hole to the right of the glove box when opened, and then pull towards you the two clips inside the glove box itself after lifting them off slightly but without forcing with a flat head screwdriver. Tada, the glove box drops down to the floor, and you get access to the air filter holder, which you want to squeeze by the two tabs, using both hands, and pull towards you. There might be some resistance, but do insist.

Just bought my vehicle recently, and the filter had not been changed in years. Truly a disgusting view. Years old dead bugs, leaves, and lots of dirt. A real shame most owners are so "mechanically" inept that they can't spend $15 and spend 2 minutes changing the filter. You're supposed to do it every year by the way, or every 12,000 mi.

I've included pictures from the "unhooked" glove box and the air filter from the previous owner... Gives you an idea what kind of ugly mess full of bacteria and mold might be blowing to your face at the moment...

So Cramp Buster allows you to keep control of the throttle while resting the muscles of your hand. I'm not a physical therapist, but I'm pretty sure constant pressure on the wrist at an awkward angle is not good, so thank god for these cheap devices, possibly saving thousands in treatment down the road (pun not intended).

I've also tried the wider version. It might be very slightly more comfortable, but I use the narrower ones these days, as it takes less space and so you can even consider leaving it on all the time, whereas with the wider one, it's constantly in the way, and whenever you get off the freeway, you have to take it off.

title: Works well and is very portable
text:
This portable air compressor is ideal for storing in your vehicle's trunk or glove compartment. It has a handy, zipper case. It is useful for any type of inflation you need, including vehicle tires, bike tires, sports balls, mats and inflatable beds, and inflatable toys.

This compressor is very easy to use. You plug one end into the cigarette lighter, and there is a long hose that reaches to the vehicle's tires. The face of the compressor has an LED-lit screen that is easy to read. There is a digital gauge that is so much better than the metal ones I used to use. I could barely see the numbers on those gauge sticks. This compressor's gauge has large, brightly lit numbers. It also has an automatic function that stores tire pressure, and when the desired pressure is reached, the unit switches itself off. That's very handy, especially for things like bike tires and inflatable balls and toys that you don't want to pop from being over-inflated.

All in all, this is a terrific product.

title: Excellent product
text:
This tire pressure gauge is miles ahead of any gauge I've ever used. Of course, it costs a lot more than any tire pressure gauge I've ever owned, but I believe it provides great value for the extra money.

It is well made of durable plastic with a metal nozzle. Instead of a metal stick that goes in and out, this fancy pressure gauge has a digital LCD readout

There are 4 buttons, in addition to the on/off/set button, one for each tire, so you do not have to mentally keep track of the pressure of each tire, or write it down. They are labeled:
FL - Front Left
FR - Front Right
RL - Rear Left
RR - Rear Right

You press the FL button for the front left tire, then check the tire pressure. You will hear a beep when it has read the pressure. This is good because with a standard gauge it can all too often be difficult to be sure if you have truly gotten a good read on it.

The device will store the reading in memory so the next time you go to check the tires, you will know what the previous reading was and can easily compare these numbers.

By pressing and holding the on/off/set button and holding it for 6 seconds, you can change the pressure unit that is displayed. You can select either "PSI" or "Bar." The range is 0-87PSI or 0-6 Bar. The accuracy is plus/minus 1.5 PSI or 0.1 Bar.

It operates in temperatures between 14-158 degrees F. It automatically turns itself off in 3 minutes if you don't use it, which is a great feature for saving the battery.

It uses a CR2032 lithium battery which ought to last a very long time since this device will not be turned on very often.

All in all, this is a great product!

title: These handles saved me over $250!
text:
I have a 1998 Toyota, a wonderful car that I've owned since 1999. It is still running extremely well. It's never needed any major repairs, but because it is over 18 years old, some minor, plastic parts are starting to deteriorate, such as the plastic edging around the doors (which isn't worth fixing), and the door handles (which are definitely a hassle to deal with if you do not fix them).

The first handle to break was on the driver's side a year ago. Fortunately for me, it happened while the car was in the shop for a routine oil change, and the management of the auto-repair shop where it happened very nicely took the blame and repaired it for free. Then over the last three months, all three of the remaining handles (I have the four-door model) broke. My natural choice would have been the nice auto-repair shop who did an excellent job fixing the first handle, but by then I had moved far away from them, and I had to find someone else.

I contacted the local Toyota dealership, who quoted me $500 for parts and labor, as well as a local auto-repair shop that was highly recommended to me by a neighbor, who quoted me $300. Both seemed ridiculously high, and my husband and I started looking for alternatives. That led us to these handles right here on Amazon. Their price is massively lower than the dealership or the auto-repair shop led us to believe these parts would cost, and we bought them immediately.

We then searched online for instructions for how to change the handles and found some great instructions with photo illustrations. If you search for "Replace Interior Door Handle 1998-2002 Toyota Corola" by wizgirl, you can find these outstanding instructions as well.

The replacement job turned out to be incredibly easy to do. You only need a Phillips screwdriver and a pair of needle-nose pliers, which we had on hand in our home tool kit. My husband did the repair job, and it took him a measly ten minutes per handle, or a total of only thirty minutes to swap out all three. I would assume that it would take a qualified mechanic half that time.

By any measure, then, even at $80/hour for a mechanic, the cost should have been quoted at a mere $50 at most to replace all three door handles, or 1/10th what the dealership quoted.

Do yourself a favor and do-it-yourself this job. There are many better ways to spend $250-450 than handing this job to a mechanic, who will very likely massively over-charge you.

title: Very handy to have around
text:
I got this compressor because in the area near where I live, it is difficult to find a gas station whose air pump isn't broken. It's much more convenient to have my own compressor.

Things that I like:

This compressor is light and easy to carry, even if you have a bad back. It weighs only about six pounds. Because it is small and portable, it can be kept in your trunk for emergencies, along with your jumper cables and other supplies.

It has a gauge on it that allows you to get a good estimate of what level the air is in a tire while you are filling it, though it isn't very detailed, and to get a truly precise reading, you'll need to use a regular tire gauge. Even so, it is extremely helpful, because it keeps me from overfilling the tire, and it greatly lessens the number of times I have to pause while filling the tire and laboriously (see below) apply a tire gauge to get a reading.

This compressor works quickly and efficiently to fill a tire.

Issues that are somewhat problematic:

This device can blow fuses in your car if you hook it up directly to your cigarette lighter outlet, which is what it is made to do. To avoid that, I got a [[ASIN:B00065L2D8 Roadpro 12V Battery Clip-On and Cigarette Lighter Adapter]] to use to hook the compressor directly to the battery. The end of the adapter cable has a female connection just like a cigarette lighter so you can substitute it for an actual cigarette lighter.

It is not an utterly simple matter to use this compressor. Unlike the tire pumps at gas stations, you can't just remove the tire's valve cap and set the nozzle of the compressor on it. Instead, you have to screw the nozzle onto the tire valve, which is a hassle. Especially when you have to check the air pressure with a tire gauge. You unscrew the nozzle, apply the gauge, then rescrew the nozzle again. This gets old after a couple of times.

When running, this compressor is loud enough that you might disturb your neighbors if you use it early in the morning or late at night.

This compressor has a ventilation grill to cool the motor, and the grill can get hot enough to burn you if it touches bare skin.

title: The most costly part of owning an Amaircare XR100 small air purifier
text:
The name of this kit is a little misleading. You do not necessarily only have to replace these filters "annually." See my comments below.

I have owned the [[ASIN:B0007S5O6K Amaircare XR100 Portable Air Purifier]], a tiny, car air purifier, since December, 2008. I've used it many times for travel, and a couple of times in my house as backup when one of my larger air purifiers wasn't working fast enough to suit me when some kind of chemical smell was in the house. I am very sensitive to chemicals (AKA volatile organic compounds or VOC's), from pesticides to paint to cleansers like bleach and ammonia. This little machine is great at clearing them out of the air.

It has a three-stage portable air-purification system:
Stage 1: Activated carbon captures large particulates and odors.
Stage 2: Electret charged media captures sub-micron particles such as dust, pollen, cigarette smoke, and bacteria.
Stage 3: Zeolite VOC filter removes toxic gases, fumes and odors.

Unlike larger air purifiers, no warning lights flash when the filters need to be replaced. As a rule of thumb, you need to replace the filters every 4-6 months (approximately every 120-150 hours of use), and the average cost for replacement filters is about $35. Thus, rather like for printers, the real cost is in running the machine, not in the cost up front. You also need to take a little time and effort and use a screw driver to replace the filters, but you can use this kit to replace all three filters simultaneously, which simplifies the process.

I personally have not found any other air purifier as small and powerful as the the [[ASIN:B0007S5O6K Amaircare XR100 Portable Air Purifier]] that I can carry along with me when traveling, so the negatives on these filters have not caused me to avoid purchasing that purifier again when it recently broke.

title: Perfectly stiff and strong
text:
I suspect that the people complaining that this plate could be stiffer haven't really analyzed their situation to discover what it is that's making their light assembly less than perfectly stable. I put one of these with a [[ASIN:B07PWTWM19 10-inch light bar by 4WDKING]] on the front of my 2019 Honda Accord, and it's bobbling all over the place, but that is NOT the fault of this plate: it's the fault of Honda and the pathetically flimsy plastic "bumper"/grille elements that the license plate attaches to. The light bar is rock-solid in relation to this mounting plate, but any chain is only as strong as its weakest link, and on my late-model Honda, the front license plate (and therefore this mounting plate) screws into a very weak link indeed. It's the Honda's flimsy plastic that's bending and giving all over the place - *not* this mounting plate.

This plate is a great product, more than adequate to the task I've set for it, but in order for my light bar to be solid and stable in relation to my car I'm going to have to somehow stiffen and stabilize the plastic grille parts of the car itself that this plate mounts into. If I can do that, I'll have a solid light bar mount.

title: It makes a difference
text:
I installed one of these in my 2019 Honda Accord EX-L with the 2.0 turbo, and it makes a difference. It is *not* a jaw-dropping, night-and-day difference by any stretch of the imagination; in fact the difference is subtle enough that the only way for me to be positive that it was doing anything at all was to drive with it in the "fastest" mode (the switch lit up red) for about a week straight, and then, one time when I came to a stoplight, turn it off while I waited for the light to turn green. When the light turned and I started up, *then* it became clear to me that the throttle controller was indeed giving me better pedal response. I even had a moment of wondering what was wrong with my car. 😄

So yes, this throttle controller does improve throttle response. Does it turn a 2019 Honda Accord into a 1968 Camaro SS? No. But it definitely does improve things.

Oh, and something I wish I'd known about when I had my 2010 Toyota Tundra: this device can also be used to *dampen* throttle response if it's too jumpy. The throttle in the 2010 Tundra was; more than once (more than six times) I accidentally laid rubber away from stoplights in that truck when I was just trying to start up normally - the thing was way too touchy. If I'd known about this APEXi unit then, I could have installed one and gotten that throttle under control (when I wanted it under control ;).

title: I love these things.
text:
Well! I just finished installing these (at night, in the dark, as has been my wont for auto-modding for decades now. I'm so much a nightowl that I almost never add goodies to a car during the daytime that I can just as well add at night, given an artificial light source or two) and I am very pleased. I felt a bit of trepidation about buying these as most of the seller's photos made it look like the two parts of the light on each side of the car might not line up properly with one another. And nobody had reviewed them on here yet, so I couldn't learn from anyone else's experience. I felt like I was taking a fairly big leap of faith. And then when they arrived, they were well-packaged but included no instructions, and that worried me just a bit too. But I had already watched a bunch of YouTube videos of people putting aftermarket taillights in their 10th-gen Accords, and watched my favorite of them (one of the ones by BoostedWhipz) again during the installation, which largely took care of the no-instructions issue; these lights are wired differently than his, I think, but I am sufficiently mechanically inclined that I could easily figure out what to do with mine to get them working correctly...and now that they're installed I find that the seller's photos don't do the lights justice: the two parts on each side line up perfectly and the lights look freaking gorgeous. And at last I have progressive directionals! I've loved those ever since I was a kid growing up in the '60s and Mercury Cougars and Ford Thunderbirds and I think some other cars had them.

I do recommend these taillights to anyone who might be on the fence about them. You won't be disappointed.

These lights have a startup "ceremony" that's quite fun, in addition to the progressive directionals. *And* now the entire taillight lights up, rather than just the bottom and end sections. I liked the look of the stock bottom-and-end taillights, but oh man I like these much better. Plus they seem to be a more vivid and beautiful red than the stock lights. When I start my car at night or come home from a night drive, I often get out of the car and just gaze upon my lovely new taillights awhile. Freakin' gorgeous.

If you do buy them and they don't come with instructions, do watch BoostedWhipz's video (not the one where he puts Audi-style taillights in, but the other one), and know that the two insulating/rattle-preventing pads that come with the lights are to be stuck to the backsides of the inner taillight sections - the ones that go on the trunk lid. Put them white-side down on the backs of those sections and use the holes and the overall shape to figure out which one goes on which light, then peel off the white backing paper and stick the correct foam pad to the correct light assembly, and you're good to go.

Do also check the operation of each light before bolting it in tight, and know that the wire for the reverse lights is polarity-dependent and needs to be plugged into the reverse-light bulb sockets the correct way or your reverse lights won't work correctly. Connect and check one, get that one working correctly, then switch the other if necessary to get that one working (this part can be done after the lights are bolted in tight, but you should check the operation of all the other functions of the lights before tightening everything down).

Enjoy and stay healthy!

* * * Update, 23 June 2020 * * *: Oh boy I love these things. They give me pleasure every time I drive my car. Even when I'm driving and I can't see them myself, I *know* how gorgeous and visible they are, and how I'm probably inspiring taillight envy in many a Honda driver...I know that if I didn't have these and saw them in operation on the road, I'd try to talk with the owner to find out where s/he got them...and in fact I have been on the receiving end of just such a transaction: a guy with a 10th-generation Accord did follow me for a bit...up to an ATM at night in the kinda sketchy town I live in, which did put me on my guard, largely because in the gloom I couldn't tell that he was driving a 10th-gen Accord...but when I was done at the ATM and he was very tactfully, gingerly tapping his horn to get my attention, I pulled around to the front of the bank and he pulled up beside me and we had a very nice conversation about modding 10th-gen Accords, and particularly about these taillights, which of course were the reason he approached me in the first place.

Every time I put on my directionals, I *know* what they look like (see D Murf's video to see for yourself) and derive satisfaction from them, and every time I come home at night, I tuck my car in the garage, close her up, and step to the back to admire the vivid red glow of these things and their utilization of all the lens area (which of course the stock taillights on my EX-L didn't afford). I've had these for a month or two now and I don't think there's been a time yet that I've parked my car at night and not gazed lovingly upon my taillights for at least a moment before heading away. Even in the daytime, the smoked lenses that blend in beautifully with my car's black paint look fantastic and draw compliments...it's just a sense pleasure, but - to paraphrase Woody Allen - as sense pleasures go, it's one of the best. :)

If you're thinking about these, get 'em. You won't regret it.

* * * Another update, 8 January 2021 * * *: It’s been just shy of eight months now since I installed these lights, I still love to look at them, and they’re still working perfectly after a lot of miles. I love quality products, and these are.

title: Product great but no instructions
text:
I didn't understand, and couldn't tell from looking at it or even from applying it to my car that this is the kind of decal with backing paper on the front and the back, and that you pull off the paper on the back of it, stick it to the desired surface, and then pull off the paper on the front to leave just the letters and the logo on the surface, as if it was painted on there - very polished and professional-looking. So I wound up driving around with this decal stuck on the back of my car with the front backing paper still stuck on top of the letters, none the wiser until one day I noticed the corner of the decal was peeling. I said, "oh well...I guess it's a cheapy decal after all. Imma have to just pull it off." I pulled off the thing that looked like it was peeling, and imagine my surprise when I was left not with a removed decal, but with a gorgeous one, as described above: very polished and professional-looking. I had no idea!

So if you buy this decal (which I'm sure you won't, this being a decal for a little-known brand, and who but me is going to pay $14.00 for a small decal??), be sure to remove the front backing paper after you've removed the *back* backing paper and stuck the decal to your surface. Because otherwise it's not going to look so very awful good.

Also noteworthy: the image here on Amazon shows a red logo and black lettering. Happily for me (who's sticking it to a black surface), but less happily for anyone wanting to stick it to a white surface, the logo is red as shown, but the letters depicted as black here on Amazon are in fact white in person. All of which means if you apply this decal to a white surface, the red logo will look beautiful and the white letters will be either nearly or entirely invisible. So sticking this to a colored, and especially to a darkly-colored surface, is recommended.

Once you figure all this out, the results are gorgeous. You just need to figure all this out (or read this review) first.

Enjoy.

Lots of people doing installation walk-throughs on YouTube speak very casually about removing these clips (using any number of different tools) and then conveniently edit out the actual removal process, probably because they’re afraid of making themselves look like idiots by destroying each clip (while at the same time sending it flying across the garage) as they remove it.

So basically I’d say these tools are all right, but that it’s just the nature of these push clips but they can’t be removed without destroying them, so neither these nor any other tools are going to actually allow you to do that.

title: why beep when you can honk?
text:
this is a great horn system. I wanted to replace the ineffective stock horn in my beloved 2011 Toyota FJ Cruiser with something a little more assertive, but without stepping over the line into hearing-damaging impracticality (and probably also widespread illegality) such as I might with the great-sounding but dangerously loud Nathan K5LLA train horns I had one eye on. I thought of a set of real heavy-truck horns, since these are plenty effective while remaining street-legal in most places as far as I know, so I went a-researching and found Hadley's commercial air horns. I like that these horns don't just sound like those on a semi, but are in fact the very ones you see on top of tractor-trailers all over the country and probably the world. this means they're built to last, and you already know exactly what they sound like. it's a big, attention-getting sound, but with a depth and mellowness to it that prevents it from being just plain obnoxious like a lot of smaller horns. I was surprised at how usable they are; I had my installer put in a toggle switch so I could switch back and forth between the stock horn and my Hadleys as needed, but it turns out I never use the switch - I just leave it on the air horns all the time, and if I want to be quiet, just a momentary tap on the horn button does the job. the system itself is well-made enough to give year upon year of reliable service under the tough conditions encountered regularly in the commercial trade, and a good installer can place most or all the components downright elegantly under the hood, as mine did. this kit, the H00977N, is a two-horn, dual-tone system, with one 26" and one 29" horn - which is big, by passenger-car standards, so make sure you've got room for them someplace (mine are mounted out of sight underneath the truck, right in front of the rear bumper). the kit's solenoid-activated so you won't need an air valve or lanyard in the cab; the system can be wired right to your stock horn button (a valve-activated version is also available), and the compressor's pretty quiet, though I think I'm going to introduce a rubber pad somewhere between the compressor and the body panel it's mounted to so as to further reduce its sound and vibration.

all in all, a top-quality product that performs beautifully; worth every penny.

title: Wanted to love them for the cute frogs, but they're cheaply made and priced too high
text:
I'm crazy about frogs, and my home and autos are decked out in frog-themed accessories and collectibles. I purchased these in 2013 so I've had ample time to test these out, and this is my assessment after significant use:

Pros

*Cute tree frog designs compliments my rearview mirror charm and matches the customized tree frog license plate border I own
*I'm self-employed working from home, and other than bi-annual road trips, the mats haven't been used nearly as often as they'd be by the average commuter in my area (hence the reason they still look pretty decent)
*Semi-decent quality and good price at time of purchase justified the splurge, but the asking price now is exorbitant
*Frogs are still nearly the same color as when I purchased them without fading, but this is only due to keeping my car in a garage from the sun's rays

Cons

*Flimsy, cheaply made mats minutely offset by the cuteness of the frog designs
*Were I a frequent commuter, these mats certainly would have shredded and needed replacing within a short timeframe
*Most annoying feature is the mats never stay in place, because the bottoms are cheaply made and the texture intended to anchor them don't adhere properly to my auto carpet
*Although I love frogs, these aren't an overall savvy consumer splurge when most people commute at least five days on an average work week

The frog mats are cute, but this feature doesn't negate unreasonable pricing, semi-decent quality, and overall cheapness. I noticed some people loved the mats, and it's easy to see why when viewing photos, but as a professional reviewer with the best interest of fellow consumers, I simply don't recommend them.

title: Exact fit for 2011 F150 - EASY install - 100% satisfied
text:
Was pretty much exact same as my factory blinker (see image)
Will need =
7/32 socket (for the clam shell around the steering column)
T10 Star/Tori (for the 2 screws holding the blinker switch)

My “car guy” abilities are probably 5 out of 100... I could change my oil with some help, and I can change a tire pretty quick.
So, if you are at ALL able to watch a couple YouTube videos, and discern some sense of how things work... you can do this!

And this product makes it that easy.
The longest time spent was going to buy a 7/32 socket from the hardware store that is a mile away from my house. (No lie)

There are more informative reviews, and videos online, so I will only mention a couple things...
1. Realize that turning the steering wheel 90 degrees left or right reveal/makes easier access (you will understand when you get started)
2. The clamshell comes apart better when you use a flathead at the tab holding the two together (I see a lot of prying, while pushing the tab... just get the tab loose and it will pop open) Separating the shell will give much easier access to that bottom screw of the signal switch attachment.
3. The “Foot Pedal Adjustment” button pops right off, don’t let it intimidate you. It’s like an old Atari joystick... the real part is underneath, that button is just a cover, basically.
4. THIS IS WHERE I WAS WORRIED... the prongs sticking out of the part, and the circuit that it connects to looks pretty fragile (some reviews warned to be cautious, and you should)... but honestly... the parts click in much easier than expected.
It’s only kind of scary when you do it... afterword, you will laugh and say “that wasn’t bad!”
(But the cautiousness is possibly why)

text:
I'm REALLY glad I bought this -- it did what I was hoping it would do, which was provide crucial additional data on an intermittent problem that refused to fail for my mechanic.

The data it provides is, of course, limited (which I believe is true of any plug-in vehicle computer reader) but informative to someone who knows enough to interpret it in context.

It does have two annoying aspects:

The really bad one is that the company is SO determined to upsell you on "enhanced" features that attempts to read results on your phone are cumbersome, because what appear to be routes to additional info turn out to just be more sales pitches.

The just-annoying one is the constant portrayal of mechanics as dishonest and trying to rip you off. I'm certainly no mechanic, but I do know enough to know that competence is usually a much bigger problem with mechanics in general than honesty. (I learned years ago that people who assume everyone is going to rip them off are probably themselves looking to rip off anyone they can, and the fact that this company's marketing revolves so much around fanning that paranoia therefore makes me wonder about THEM!)

Those two irritating factors aside, as I said, this did what I needed it to do and provided the data my mechanic needed to diagnose my car's intermittent problem, so it was $60 well spent for me.

title: Still Jumping Strong
text:
I'm updating this review because I had to do some jumping recently and, once fully charged, this still works. Someone once told me these portable starters typically don't survive more than a single jump, but this does! I got this unit more than two years ago. It's easy to use and works.

It also does a great job as an air compressor. The unit makes a LOT of noise when filling a tire and takes a while - maybe two minutes for every five pounds of air. The compressor switch is indeed easy to bump to on, but believe me, YOU WILL KNOW WHEN IT'S ON!!!

True, there's no float charger. However you should be ok charging it overnight every month or so - the older it gets (perhaps this is also usage-dependant,) the more it drains and the longer it takes to charge. However even though it takes a long time to charge to unblinking green, it still jumps on a 4+ hour charge.

It is lead-acid so it's pretty heavy, but my wife is no weightlifter and has no problems with it.

All these consumer-use jumpers seem to be a bit of a crapshoot, and if you're looking for COMPLETE peace of mind, pair it with triple-A or some other road service! But depending on what your TIME is worth, a jumper is still a nice thing to have on hand...

title: Max Professional 2114 Di-Electric Grease - 10 oz.
text:
I purchased this Max Professional 2114 Di-Electric Grease - 10 oz, because I wanted to use this brand of dielectric silicon compound grease and I like it . I have used other forms of anti-oxidant to work with electrical connections on battery powered marine electrical circuits and my automotive needs. If you live near the coast, as I do, you can expect the salt air to affect and damage your electrical connections that are not protected, as the air itself combined with the flow of current is a sure corrosion problem. When you see buildup around terminals, it is usually preventable if there is pre-application of a di-electric protection method. This product is good for battery cables where you can see the wire exposed, lighting wires and bases exposed to the elements and any circuit that stays powered up for long durations of time, such as charging systems and bilge pumps. About any use on boats stored on the water can be improved with this product. You can spray connections lightly with this product and either leave as is, or cover it for added protection. My preference is to use di-electric grease and cover it with a self fusing silicon tape, such as x-treme tape or rescue tape, as they cover and then form a sealed protecting "boot" over the connection. This will protect better and last indefinitely. With this method you can protect spade terminals, bulb bases in the sockets, relay bases and connections to them and ignition connections. Even a battery terminal can be sprayed before connection and then protected with the silicon wrap to where it is virtually air tight over the terminal coming off the battery and sealing out salt air.
If you ride a motorcycle or an ATV this method can save you from connections vibrating apart and stopping you in you off road tracks. I use the protectant on my lawnmower spark plug, threads and all for good conductivity of the spark plug connection and to make the boot come off better. This spray is very convenient for about any application, as you can put it right where you need it with the nozzle and not have to do so much after work cleanup. Great for treating O-rings and rubber for exposure to the elements.
I like it and recommend it. If I find that it works even better than what I have stated here, I'll return to this review an give an update and a 5th star. If it lets me down, I will de-rate it accordingly.

title: 800 Waterproof 12V Battery Charger by Battery Tender
text:
Update: Oct. 17, 2014. I've had this Waterproof Charger for a while now and came across a quirk, I didn't understand the correct operating procedure to get it to work. I plugged in the charger then hooked it up. Nothing, no lights and not charging. I actually emailed Battery Tender, to tell them it quit working after not using it for a while. I was wrong. After the email, I went back to it and grabbed the owners manual paper that came with it and I kept in the BT bag for storage I purchased. It clearly stated, "hook up the leads to the battery first and then plug in to the AC power. I did and it started pulsing the Yellow led, then the green. Then steady green charging and that is it. Works just as it should. I'm old school and my other charger is a 30 year old Sears, that I see sparks each time I clamp on the terminals, so I have to learn the new method of dealing with a smart charger. Good product!

I have purchased several Battery Tender products, none have failed and this 800 Waterproof 12V Battery Charger is another good product. It is not a quick charger and would be the type of charger best suited for someone who would like to plug it in and let it maintain your battery while in dry dock or just a maintenance charge. If you would like a power charger that will boil the guts out of your battery, this is not that charger. It will get the job done, just don't expect it to do it in an instant. I like it.

title: passing the ohio winter test so far
text: After my 1st order of this cover didn't show, amazon rushed another cover to me via UPS no charge. Thank you amazon. Received 2nd order in 2 days, and it originated in Washington state. Got cover on, and it has survived everything nw ohio winters can throw at it so far. The cover at 1st glance seemed very thin, but the material is apparently strong. I was sure to protect cover from sharp edges around bottom corners of trailer, items on roof, and rain spouts on top corners. I've seen other covers rip in them locations. If you don't protect from sharp objects, any cover is gonna rip. For the rain spouts I cut some wet noodles (the floaty noodles for pools) and taped them over the spouts. I used bubble wrap on the bottom corners and tv antenna on roof. My only complaint for this cover would be the straps you run across the bottom. they like to loosen in time after being whipped around by the wind. After a freezing rain episode, the weight of the ice on 1 side of cover allowed for movement because straps loosened, and the cover slid off center. I have just made an effort to check them every now and then for tightness, but if its not at your home that could be more troublesome for others.

title: Works as Intended, Must Follow Instructions, Pro-Tip included
text:
Yes, this plastic restorer works. I followed the instructions as written and didn't have any issues applying the product.

I restored the OEM step rails on my 2017 Ram 1500. My truck is parked outside. The sun is not kind to any plastics. I know better than to use any plastic restorer on the exterior. Over the years (40+) I found nothing that worked for more than 2 weeks or maybe 2 car washes.

After watching Project Farm (on YT) I decided to give this restorer a go. Mind you I had NO faith in this product based on my previous experiences.

Applying was easy but I had issues getting the product in the treads of the steps. Cotton applicators didn't work as they smushed down and couldn't reach the corners. My only solution was to multi-fold the little towelette and work my way through the treads. On mam was this a pain in my buttocks. Very slow but working.

My wife saw me struggling with the treads and said "Hold on, I got an idea". She came back with a dotter. This arts craftsy tool makes perfect paint dots. But when wrapped around my towelette I was able to whiz through the treads. I love my wife more every day!

200 car washes? Let's be real here. Even if I washed my truck once a week, which I don't, that would take 3.85 years.

I will add images of my side steps every 3 months. Let's see if Cerakote really works or is another snake oil.

title: if it sucked I could always return it
text:
Being an avid car guy who's tried all the snake oil over the years I was quite skeptical about this synthetic 'claybar'. I read the reviews, looked over at Griot's website and decided to try this new fangled claybar snake oil. Heck, if it sucked I could always return it.

I used a good car wash soap for my first get-go. As the instructions stated I did the windows first. Plenty of soapy suds for lube and no pressure. This was no different than using a sponge, except no pressure.

Then I tackled the hood and side mirrors. The hood was smooth like a baby's bottom! The side mirror are plastic chrome something. They clayed out beautifully with no marks. Then I rinsed everything thoroughly and dried with my chamois. Using a dry microfiber cloth I ran my hand over the hood. Super smooth, no bumps, no bug guts, no fiber snags, just smooth, baby, smooth. I finished with Finish Kare's High Temp paste wax. Another wowzers! A gleaming shine. No imperfections.

Rinse the clay sponge and you're done. Super simple. Dropped your clay sponge? Just rinse and keep using it. I don't know how many clay bars we're useless after my fumbling hands.

title: Excellent OEM Upgrade or Replacement
text:

Installed on 2017 RAM Laramie. Direct mount w/ stainless threading, no spacers needed. Small drop of thread locker added for extra security.

Why 15" instead of 6"? Basically function over form. Initially I tried a rubber 6" antenna and a aluminum 6" version. Both had range issues over 20 miles with a regular broadcast and difficulties with HD signals over 40 miles. The little antennas are quite noticeable as they are very unique and scream "pull on me!"

I travel 100 miles from home daily. Major city centers are located 60 miles north and 70 miles southwest. My home has 2 stations with no HD. The 15" antenna picks up HD broadcasts from both city centers just a good as the OEM antenna. There is no whipping or bending at highway speeds.

All-in-all, this is a very capable antenna that blends in with any exterior, receives standard and HD broadcasts as well as the OEM antenna.

title: Fast & Easy
text:
This is not your normal vehicle wax, nor does it apply like normal wax. The end result is basically the same. There are a few tricks to make it easier to apply.

Test Vehicle: White Subaru Forester

White has to be the hardest vehicle to wax. You hardly see dried wax. With ICE you really don't see anything.

I applied the ICE as directed. I covered all paint, rubber, lenses, and trim. I didn't touch any glass.

The applicator works well. You need to keep the applicator slightly damp, but not dripping wet.

After wiping down the Subaru I waited 10 minutes. Maybe I waited a little longer than recommended, but it didn't hurt the end result.

Next, you wipe the entire vehicle down with one side of the micro fiber towel. This is crucial! You'll notice some streaking on black plastic and rubber trim. This step gives you time to work everything in.

The last step uses the "clean" side of the micro fiber towel. Here's where you notice how good ICE really is. No dust. No residue. No white haze. No nothing. Literally amazing!

Make sure you buff out EVERY area you covered with the ICE. No elbow grease is required. Just wipe everything down with the clean side.

Time: 30 minutes from start to finish. I imagine it will be quicker in the future, but I was using a new product and took my time.

Stand back and admire your vehicle. My Subaru looks great!

title: love the dual colors
text:
Even though I have a truck, I decided to try out this set of 4 rock lights. The package is put together well. There are lights marked for the front and rear. The rears have more cable length.

The harness that is included actually has 8 connectors with the spare connectors capped. I'm assuming there is an 8 light kit available. The connectors are a standard style 3pin waterproof lighting connector.

I had a couple of spare rock lights sitting around so I wired them up to some three pin connectors and was able to use two of the unused harness plugs. Giving me a total of 6 lights which is more appropriate for my truck. My lights are not dual colored, so I wired them to match the white light pins.

I did not install the 3 position rocker and instead use those spade connectors to attach to my own aux switch controller.

The wiring can be routed through either the side or the back of the base pad. That being said, the base pad is a roll bar style pad and not flat across the back like others. I have coated magnetic bases that I mounted these on, so I did not use the pad. Which means I also did not have to screw these into my truck. I attached them along the frame instead of the wheel wells. The wheel well position create a lot of shadow. And if you want to use them as rock lights for wheel placement and night, then along the frame is a better spot.

As for the lights themselves, both modes are quite bright and I have to say that I really prefer the amber most of the time. Overall, it's another high quality kit from Lasfit. Though I do wish they had used a flat base rather than the roll bar style.
