title: Any psi will do
text:
I've been using the screw on deflator for years because I love the ease and simplicity. But they're noisy and you're stuck with whatever you set them at. So if you want to do 18psi in one spot, but 14psi in another, your best bet is either carry two kits with different presets, or drop to 18 and manually bleed the rest of the way.

I'dvbeen passing on this tool, because all the steps that is needed and I don't like the idea of the valve core threads getting over worked.

Well, I finally took the plunge. And I'm happy to say, this tool works pretty well. It's no where near as easy as the screw ons. Cumulatively, the overall speed is the same since you have to repeat the process for times. But ultimately, you gain the flexibility of choosing psi from the get go.

When I say great support, I mean that two ways. The struts do a good job of holding up the hood and Redline Tuning customer service is top notch.

My kit arrive with a minor issue. I contacted the manufacturer and they resolved it immediately. I was then able install the struts.

The slot bolts go into the hood slots easy enough with a little wiggling. The engine bay brackets are even easier to install. That being said, there's a bit of a gap on my driver side bracket and it doesn't actually my contact on the hook shaped upper part. I'll probably add a rubber shim there to the bracket isn't pushing down with all the force cantilever to the bolt holding it down.

The rod side of the shocks slid onto the ball easy enough. But the tube side had a slightly harder time. Before they fully seated, the paint on both balls on the hood brackets were scraped be the metal retainer band.

Overall, an easy install and super helpful mod. It's nice to work around the center hood prop.

title: not coated
text:
I received one like the other reviewer. Bare metal. Weld on the outside and gaps on the inside.

So these are not ready to install. There's a bit of prep work. The inside of the weld has some big gaps were water can get in. I filled it up with some jb weld. And I'm painting over it now. I'll have to put several coats on it for rust protection.

So fair warning. Be prepared to do some fixing and finalizing before installing them.

I also had to wallow out the forward most hole. There was no way it would install as is.

On the positive side, they packed them really well with expanding foam and the surface was scuffed for coating.

They just need to change the product photo so show that these will arrive unfinished.

title: One not long enough for gladiator.
text:
At 7.5 feet, this is a few feet too short to run the length of a gladiator. I had to order two. The only other extender cable on the market is 14 feet which is way too long and expensive.

An 11 foot cable would have been perfect. The extra 4 feet from running two extenders means that the power drops off.
It's hard to tell, but I think these might be 10 awg. At this length, 8 awg might have been a better choice. Other than needing to order a second one, this has worked well enough.

title: Near perfect fit for gladiator
text:
This shade is a near perfect fit for the windshield on my 2021 Gladiator.

Quality is okay, but it was pretty inexpensive. So no complaints from here. When it's time to put it away, it folds neatly into a small storage pouch that fits right in the glove compartment.

I started parking outside and needed this. Overall, I'm happy with this order.

title: too brittle
text:
My goal was to use the fir tree retainers to hold in place some cross bar channel nuts when not in use. And be able to take them out when I wanted to mount the bike racks on the cross bars. The fir tree were too short so I went with the push retainer.

These are great if you only have to use them one time. I needed them to be able to put in and take out repeatedly, just like the clips that held on my old Wrangler grill. But these are so brittle, that they heads snap off. And they cover less space so there less surface to get the removal tool underneath.

That being said, it would be wasteful to throw these away. I decided to shave the parts that catch and reduce the resistance. They still hold fine enough for my application and can now be used again and again.

Overall, they hold. Too well for my intended use. I would have been more useful to me if they had made them closer to OEM specs.

title: Takes work, but nutserts not a problem
text:
I read the reviews before deciding to go with this hitch reciever. I figured I'd never be towing anything near to the 7500 lbs of the Rubicon capability with the class IV. So no need to pay more, do all the extra work to install and find a buyer for the factory ball mount hitch.
So like the others, my threads were coated partially. I worked the gigantic flat head screw back and forth several times to clear out the coating. I additionally had some rust in there, so I cleaned that out before the install.

Speaking of coating, the coating everywhere else is incredibly thin. The coating on the edges were chipped exposing the bare metal underneath. It might be a good idea to spray a few coats of paint for rust protection.

My Rubicon came with a rear steel bumper that is attached on the underside via threaded rivet nut. The factory t50 torx bolts had to come out for the install.

The bolt and rectangular washer got snagged on the rivet nut. I found that having the washer and bolt separated on the guide wire made it easier to get them over the rivet nut. Once over the rivet nut, they came together and the bolt passed through the washer. I tried it several times with these bolt inserted through the washer and it always got hung up due to the bigger profile of having them combined. Having completed one side that technique made the other side a breeze.
I used blue loctite and torqued to spec.
I filled in the hole with some putty and covered up the hole with a mopar badge.
Overall, easy enough install if you use some creativity.

title: Missing cross bar mounting hardware
text:
Cutting up and attaching the tracks was is as far as I could get. My package was missing the bag for the mounting kit(QMHD05) for the crossbars. I'm waiting to hear back from the manufacturer and seller to see how I can get the missing parts.

Other than that, I was able to chop the tracks easily with a miter saw.
The T bolts slide along the track on the bottom, so you can drill holes on your mounting surface spaced as needed. The only line up that is needed is the end cap portion and even that is not required. This makes drilling far more flexible. In my case, I could drill around the cross brace on the underside of my tonneau cover and not have to worry about getting access to the bolt.

The parts that I do have fit together well. It's a well designed kit. The longest part of the install was marking for drilling. They list a 6.5 mm drill bit to be used. I used a 1/4 and that worked out perfectly.

I'm looking forward to mounting the cross bars and getting the bikes up there. Hopefully, the customer support is excellent.

Update: Excellent service directly from Rhino Rack. Seller support is non existent. Good to know that Rhino Rack is ready to stand by it's products.

Update: Thanks to Rhino Rack USA quickly sending me the kits, I was able to complete my install. The rack is on solidly. If you line up the towers perfectly into the bases, there's a tiny bit of play. To take the play out, offset the towers in or out of the cross bars just a hair, That'll just a hair. That'll take out that little bit of wiggle.

title: Too small. Big gaps
text:
I had a sun shade for my JKU that worked great. There was full coverage from front to back and side to side. And it was a lot less expensive as well.

This one has a premium price and the material and construction are decent. What is lacking is coverage. There's big gaps all around. I don't know if I got a bad one or if they just make these things too short. No amount of stretching will make this big enough.

On top of it, there's a big printed lettering on the covers. I'm not a fan of giant logos on stuff that I buy.

They need to make these two inches bigger all around. I'm disappointed for as much as this thing costs.

Update: Seller reached out and offered to custom make one for a better fit. I passed on the offer, but I have to say that commitment to customer support is beyond any expectations I could have from any manufacturer. So 5 stars for top notch service.

title: Heavy duty mat, but with some issues
text:
I had my gladiator line-x'd. So I didn't get this to protect my bed. Rather, I got it to protect the stuff I put in it. Namely off road camping and biking stuff. A rubber mat helps to keep stuff from shifting around.
This arrived in a rolled up box that was pretty heavy. It was a lot heavier than I expected. Which is great.

I threw in on top of my bed cover and let it sit in the sun for a bit. It's a bit darker than the photos, which is good. Unfortunately, there's some not so good stuff going on.

A couple of hours later, the curls had mostly flattened out and I threw it into the bed. It runs a bit small on the width. The sides are just a narrow at about 1 cm on both sides. And that's even with the added thickness of the bed liner.

Also, there's a section under the rear corners that have raised molding that don't line up with floor molding and the mat ends up sitting a little higher in those areas instead of flat.

It helps to pull up the rear most lip of the mat to close the tailgate. Otherwise, its a little long.

Overall, it's serviceable for the gladiator. But for the money, it needs some improvement.

title: Works with gladiator rails
text:
The mopar does not include cleats for their gladiator front rails. And mopar does not sell the cleats separately at this time. These work perfectly. They dwarf the factory cleats, but they fit nonetheless.
So if you're looking for a suitable tie down, these will work just fine. I have to admit that I would have preferred smaller cleats.

title: Great Replacement
text:
I wanted something that was better suited for off-roading than the factory carpets. These look like they'd be a perfect replacement.
The install was pretty simple and only took a few minutes. After pulling the front carpets, I located the cut outs for the drain plug. I Pulled those up and snipped the sides where is was still a small bit of attachment. Then I pulled the plugs out. I lined up the mat and pushed holes onto the retaining pins. And lastly, pushed the drain hole into the floor board hole until it snugged in and then pushed the drain plugs into the floor mat.
The rear didn't have have drain holes so it was just pulling out the old carpet and pushing these on.

The overall fit is a little off. I'm hoping these settle in. Right now, there a bit of gap between the mat and center console on the driver side. The rear mat has a few ripples in it.
It'd also been better if the rear extended further back that leave that lip by the door to get a toe caught on.

I'm not sure if this is better than OEM or not since I don't have that one to compare this to. But I see some room for improvement. And this mat is okay if you're looking to save a few bucks.

Update: After looking at some videos, these seem a little softer than the OEM, which might explain the deformation along the edges. For the drop in material quality, the price difference should be a bit greater.
They have to settled in. There's still a big gap on the driver side.

Update: Replacement arrived. It's all good now. Excellent support from the seller.

title: Holder ball arrived split in two.
text:
The cheap ball cover arrived cracked. The material quality on the balls are very poor. Supposedly, there was an update to the material a while back. But this was ordered this week and the ball was split in two.

Also, the finish on the extension does not match the rest of the mount. Its a glossy texture vs a matte finish.

The phone holder is completely useless. Luckily, I have a spare from my last vehicle.

As for the dash mount, it was a simple install and fit well enough. It would help if it had nubs like the OEM tray to anchor it in place towards the middle.

Update: Excellent support. A replacement was sent and that was fully intact. The replacement holder is unbranded and has some extra support for vertical mounting.

title: Tape doesn't stick.
text:
I had the same issues as others. The tape did not stick. One side stuck to the truck, but not to the sill guard. The other side stuck to the sill and not to the truck.

I replaced with some 3M double sided and it seems to be sticking now.

They need to switch to a wider tape with automotive adhesive.

title: Don't go by photos. Read description.
text:
I bought this based on the picture and not the description. I was surprised to see how small the ball was when I opened up the package.
I went back and saw that this was a 20mm instead of the 25mm. I wrapped some tape around it for now. Eventually, I'll go back and dip it in some epoxy and build up some layers.
That being said, it's poor fitting. It doesn't contour fit that well to the dash. It does work though. Amd you do have to remove your dash tray.
Overall, it's okay, but could be better for the price.

title: fits 315x12.5r17... barely
text:
I ordered these not because I'll likely need them, but because certain mountain roads require them by law around here in the winter time. I also got these because I read someone else with 315x12.5 tires had them and they fit.
Unfortunately, one number that was different between their tires and mine is that mine are r17 and theirs are r18.
I'm running some 315x12.5r17 milestar patagonias. So their sidewall is an inch smaller and considering the inner and outer sidewalls means they had two more inches of slack.

Well, I can't say I was surprised when I went to wrap them that I barely had any slack. The good news is that I had just a hair of slack. And using the ratcheting wrench, I was able to pull in a couple of wraps. Whether or not that is enough to keep these on remains to be seen.

That being said, these are a breeze to install. I doubt that you would even need the instructions, though they are included. As is a nice carry storage bag. So overall, better to have and need then to need and not have. I'll be glad to keep these in my road side emergency bag.

title: Good replacement for my old winch line.
text:
My old superwinch tigershark 9500sr rope has seen quite a bit of business. It was a good time to swap it out. That was a 3/4 80ft rope with an abrasion shield. Because the tigershark drum brake is to the side, there's less heat on the rope.
That being said, I like that this had a heat sleeve for the inner wrap and an abrasion sleeve. That's a real line saver at times.
I have a hole in the drum that I have to thread the rope through so I had to trim off the bolt holder crimped end. Other than that, it worked great. On my old thimble end went onto a factor55 flatlink. I've since switched to a soft gator jaw which works perfectly with this thimble.
I hooked it up to a small kart in neutral and winched it in. It's spooled nice and tight on the drum.
I would like to know which line this is. Is this a Dyneema? It would be good to know.
Overall, it looks to be a good replacement for my old winch line.

title: great for the JKU and friends
text:
Even though I've not gotten stuck enough to need to be pulled out or use a traction aid, like any precaution you take off roading, it's better to have it and not need it than it is to need it and not have it. First aid kit, tire repair kit, spare parts, etc..... While, I've not had to be recovered, I've helped recover folks and every bit of tool and knowledge helps.

So with that said, I've been wanting a set of these for a while now for just in case. I saw that someone received a cracked one. Stuff definitely happens.The first thing I did was let the kids have their way with them. If they're that fragile, they wouldn't even survive the kids playing with them. Bounce ramp, dirt shovels, etc... At the end of the day, they still looked new. So I put them under the JKU and an stepped incline. No problems. A little flex and still good to go. The 310mm wide knobby tread locks up well with the lugs on my 12.5" MTs.

I love that they've included a storage bag. On the trail, I mount these on the outside for easy access. At home, I have the bag hanging on the wall.

The only thing I wasn't a fan of was a the hand holes. They're a bit small. Especially if you're wearing gloves. But that's not at deal breaker.

Overall, they're as good as I had hoped for and better than expected.

title: Chuck works great, rest could use some improvment
text:
I switched to digital inflators a while back and I love them. With analog, my in cabin readings were always off by a pound up or down. My tpms is spot on now.
One thing I did not like about my old inflator is that the chuck was rather cheap. And would also fail to get a lock on more than one occasion.
So I figured I'd give this one a try. For the most part, these two are quite similar. But there are some minor differences. This one does not have a battery meter, which is a feature that I really prefer.
This one also has a bit of play in the lever. That should be a lot tighter.
This one, while steel braided, is uncoated. It actually feels better to work with a rubber coated hose.
But the big thing is that the chuck on this one does not leak. And at the end of the day, that's what really matters.
So I might just take the hose off this one and swap it with my other one.

title: Great mod for my basket
text:
[[VIDEOID:88f2eebc14ab03b8d7241fcc1ced4d8f]] I've been wanting to increase the visibility on my 60 inch trailer hitch basket. I added these to both side and they work great.
They're incredible bright. The turn signal functions without issue. No hyperflashing that can sometimes be associated with LEDs.

I added some angle brackets to mount these up. There is a specific left and right side. One has the license plate light. The wires are color coded for left and right application. That's very helpful. I am surprised to how short the ground is.

Overall, I'm happy with these and they're a great modification for the basket.

title: Modded trailer hitch cargo basket
text:
I've been wanting to increase the visibility on my 60 inch trailer hitch basket. I added these to both side and they work great.
They're incredible bright. They turn signal functions without issue. No hyperflashing that can sometimes be associated with LEDs.

Rather than drill out the structure plate on the cargo basket, I epoxied and shrunk wrapped them them with rare earth magnets. So they're not stuck to one platform.
I had to go back to the webpage since the wire diagram was not included. But that was simple enough.
Overall, I'm happy with these and they're a great modification for the basket.

title: using it with my JKU
text:
I have one of these for the JKU that I use for the a compressor mount. Nice my wires run through the firewall on my passenger side, I had it mounted there. After looking at the design of this one, I realize that it would fit on the passenger side and I could take the other one and put it back on the driver side.
The only problem with that idea is that the JLU tub rail holes are in a different position. Well, I put some rtv on some washers and placed the washers where the holes are for the JKU. I then pressed down and the washers adhered to the mount and I used that to mark the spot for drilling.
I drilled two holes and was able to mount this up it worked great.
I run a soft top so the upright C pillar brace would interfere with the soft top frame. So I left that piece out. Since this one came with a some stand offs, I did not need to make my own, unlike the JKU version. Also, this one included fully illustrated instructions unlike the JKU.
So overall, with a small bit of modification, I was able to use this as a mount for my compressor in my JKU.

title: primitive interface and clunky interaction
text:
For my 2013 wrangler, I've got a really old flashcal and a 'newer' OBDLink MX Bluetooth OBD-II Automotive Scan Tool.
The flashcal allows me to read/clear codes as well as set some parameters. It's incredibly slow. So slow that it's boderline painful to use. But it has features that are necessary.
The OBDLink is quicker and has a lot more tools. But it requires that I use my phone for pairing. So that means I have to stop using my phone for other things while I'm trying to work with it.
So I was looking for something newer, quicker and has basic abilities to work via the OBDII.
This thing is small. The screen is very very small. Compared to the other screens, this thing is like an old camera from the early 90s. Which gets me to the menu. They're not much different than said aforementioned camera. All navigation is through an enter/sometimes exit button and a one way directional scroll. There were times I wanted to exit, but had to scroll down to 'back menu' screen option. There were times that exiting wasn't even an option. There should be separate button for exit. Also another button for scrolling back.
I would use this to get a quick read of any CEL code and to able to erase it, but not much more than that.

title: Too busy to make my own
text:
I got this for my JKU. I bought it used so the price I felt was more reasonable. My time is limited these days and I did not want to make my own roll.
This works great with the 2013 JKU windows. They fit perfectly.
It rolls up neatly. And all the windows are well protected.
Overall, worth the convenience.

title: Modded to work with soft top
text:
Looking at the photos, I knew that this was designed to work with a hard top. I either run topless or with a soft top. I figured I could still get it to work. It did not occur to my that this was meant to be only installed on the driver side, but in my case, both side are fine. And currently, my power pole connector for my compressor is running through the passenger side firewall to my battery side poles.

This thing is well machined. It seems to measure between 1/8 and 3/16 steel. It's got a good heft to it. Not cheap thin plates that will flex. The powder coating isn't too thick. It won't take too much of a beating, but it'll suffice.

So, I have this sitting right on the tub rail. Powder coat on paint. I put down some pvc tape on the underside that I'm using as a gasket to protect the paint.

Installing was pretty easy and it only took a few minutes. Of course my install is a little different since I'm have a bow bracket on my C pillar. I left out the vertical plate since that space is already occupied. I'll just find another use for that plate. I also made a little stand off underneath for some added support.

I actually don't have a ARB twin. I have a Viair portable. I put some rare earth magnets on the base and it does not budge in the least. I also used a strap weaving through the cut-outs as a hold down in case of roll over.

So even though I'm not using this as intended, like most of my jeep stuff, I modded it to suit my purposes and with that, I'm pretty happy with this mount.
Btw, there are no instructions, but if you work on your jeep, you should have no problems slapping this together.

title: Both damaged and defective.
text:
Arrived damaged and defective. Surfaces on bearing retainer had a bunch of cuts. The powder coating was incomplete and chipped. I sent photos and had a conversation with the manufacturer to hopefully help them improve their quality inspections.

Update: I got a replacement that was not defective. The new one did not have the defects.

title: Smooth operating
text:
The first impression that I got was that there was great care with the packaging. All the pieces came individually wrapped embedded is custom cut layered cardboard to support all if them.

At first, I could not find any instructions. This was very easy to put together. It was very intuitive. After I was done, I found the instructions behind the top layer of cardboard that got stuck under the cover. The welds look great and all the pieces first perfectly together. The bearing arrived fully greased.

The overall operation is smooth and simple. And this has been useful for projects both inside and outside of the garage.

title: Too loose for offroading
text:
[[VIDEOID:8cca202446adde73448b0cb565edd8bb]] This tray comes close to fitting perfectly. But I've made a video to show how loose it sits.

While this might be secured enough for trip around town, it jumps all about when going offroad. My solution was to add velcro. So far so good. If they made the bottom flare out, it could snap and hold into place without any addition work.

title: synthetic works great in this hot climate
text:
I just picked up a 6 pack of mobil 1 when this became available. I returned the mobil 1 to give this a try. A little back story. Previous to 2013, the pentastar wranglers used 5w30 and then switched to 5w20 for fuel economy. I've been doing my own changes and running 5w20 since 2013. My engine is long out of warranty. I figured I'd try 5w30 since I live in a warm to hot climate zone.
First thing that I noted was that it meets chrysler standard MS 6395. The mobil 1 did not. Not that it was up the quality. They just never submitted it for approval since it exceeded the standard. But if your engine is under warranty, it never hurts to use approved oil.
So this just arrived in time for my annual oil change. I put very few miles a year and any more changes than that are wasteful, money wise and to resources. Well, it's an oil change. There's not much too it. i drained the old oil out a fumoto valve and down a hose. Dropped in a new filter and topped it off. Exactly six quarts as the manual calls for.
I started up the engine, pulled the jeep out of the garage and took it down the road. I'd be lying if I said I felt any difference. Engine sounds the same. But that's not the point of the oil change. The oil helps to protect engine parts from excess wear and time will tell how well this holds up. So far, so good. Would I recommend this, sure. Go for it.

title: No leaks
text:
This arrived just in time for my annual new year greasing.

I had a powerbuilt grease gun and it leaked everywhere. Unfortunately, I did not find out until after I loaded it with some very expensive ball joint grease. I've been pretty gun shy of grease guns since.

Good news, this one doesn't have those same issues. First thing I did was replace the coupler with a quick connect. Then I loaded it with molybdenum grease and hit all my fittings.

I got 4 contol arm joints, 4 track bar joints, 2 draglink fittings and finally, 4 ball joints. No issues the whole way.

So overall, I'm pretty happy with this grease gun. Unfortunately, I had to go through a really bad one to really appreciate a good one.

title: Better than a block of wood
text:
I don't use a hi-lift for off roading, but I do use a bottle jack.
Previously, I carried a block of wood to use as a base for more height. This is lighter and has a wider footprint. And any weight savings is always welcomed.
In the photo is a six ton bottle jack. It fits in with a little room to spare. I might get an eight ton.
The good news is that I can also lend this to any of my buddies that do carry a hi-lift. Or they could just get their own since their so inexpensive.

title: Looks like a quality strap compared to my old one.
text:
I've had a 20ft x 20K lb strap for some time and that thing has taken a beating. Compared to that one, this things is a beast.

You can see that this one is not only wider, but has bigger loops.
One thing that I like on this one is that the specs are on the tag sewn onto the rope. My other one is a guessing game when I'm trying to pull stuff out of the bag in the middle of a recovery.

I also appreciate the tie strap and the storage bag. Anything that helps organize all the recovery gear. I'm looking forward to using this on the trails and will come back and update this review as neccessary.

title: A solid deal compared to the ARB kit
text:
Our brand new 2019 vehicle did not come with a spare. Instead, they provide roadside assistance. Which is great in the city, but not on road trips when you have young children. So I built my own emergency tire repair kit which includes an inflator, a jack and this repair kit.

Well, I also go offroading and need to be prepared. The kit that I carry is the ARB tire repair kit. That kit costs twice as much as this one and comes with less items. So at half the price, this kit is a bargain. And everything you need is included.

I would recommend this kit for those that might have the same requirements as myself.

title: Should have gotten this ages ago.
text:
I had a slight concern the tabs would make it impossible to reach some of the harder to get to grease fitting. Namely, the ones on my controls arms. Well, that turned out to be a non issue. They're tight fits, but I'm able to get access to all of them. The zerks are always a pain to remove the. Sometimes, there's just not enough space to do the twist.
This was a breeze to use. I've never attached and removed a grease gun coupler as easy as I have using this one.

title: Great tool for tire safety
text:
Works exactly as you'd expect. Having the analog to back up the digital is a great feature for those that might want to double check the accuracy. It even comes with a spare button.

As you can see in the photos, the wings were plenty wide enough even for the larger than usual voids between the lugs on my mud tires. Most people will have all terrain tires with lugs that are much closer.

Only thing I have a issue with is there was some excess building material on the data port that needed to get scraped off.

Overall, a great tool for tire maintenance and staying safe on the roads.

title: Great addition to tire repairs kit
text:
My wife's brand new 2019 van did not come with a spare. They expect most of miles are city and rely on road side assistance. That's not a viable solution for family road trips with young ones where the closest help could be hours away. So I got this for an emergency repair kit.

Compared to my Viair, this think it's tiny. And a whole lot lighter. I wouldn't use it to fill my 35s. But I did test it out on my scooter wheel. The auto cutoff works. I let all the air from my scooter tires, set the PSI to 60 and flipped the switch.

The compressor auto shut off when it was done. I tested the pressure with a separate digital gauge. The results were accurate.

This is going to be the perfect part of the repair kit to go with a scissor jack and slime filler.

title: Not OTG, but will work
text:
These are not listed as Over The Glass, but they do fit. Though that fit is very tight compared to my uvex OTG goggles. So while putting them on and taking them off when wearing glasses is not a smooth, it can be done.

They lens is clear and doesn't seem to fog up. It's well integrated into the skirt and can be taken apart after unhinging the straps. It is a little more challenging to separate than the uvex goggles. The strap is easy to adjust and is comfortable.

If you wear glasses, an OTG pair will be better suited, but these will work if needed.

title: Not fully enclosed
text: The original product photo was edited to make this look like a fully enclosed rubber tire. They've since replaced it with a more accurate image. There's a foam insert with a standard 36psi tire wrapped around it.

title: Lots of issues but still gets the job done
text:
As with many heavy steel items, my package arrived pretty beat up. I order a lot of jeep parts, so this kind of arrival is not surprising. Some manufacturer expect this and address their packaging. This was not one of those cases. As another reviewer had pointed out, the bubble wrap they use is some of the thinnest available. The zip ties they used to hold the parts together were snapped. The hardware bag was ripped and nuts and washers were spilling out of the holes. More than a few were missing. The basket it self was scuffed all over. Which may not matter considering how bad some of the powder coating is.

Assembly was easy even though the instructions weren't entirely clear. There was some fitment issues. The square holes for two of the carriage bolts would not line up. The welded plate on the basket part was welded a 1/4 inch too far out. No amount of adjustment or order of assembly get them to line up. I had to use a small file to elongate out those holes.

The 2" hitch slid into the receiver without issue. The foldaway feature is great for when the basket is empty. If you're putting this on a jeep and running 35s or larger, you'll need to have a hitch extender to be able to fold it up.

For all its problems, it's still useful. Most likely it's going to get banged up as you use it. Other than the fact that people like things that buy new to look new, the functionality is still there.

Update: No response from the manufacturer regarding the missing hardware. Luckily, it simple enough to go out and get some more carriage bolts, nylock nuts and washers.

title: Not the brightest,  but maybe good enough.
text:
Things I like about these marker lights.
Easy to read pos/neg colored coded wires.
Plenty of strands in the wiring.
Solid construction of the housing.

What I wasn't impressed with.
These lights with three LEDs were no brighter than my current single LED amber markers.
The amber is closer to a yellow than it is to an orange.

The photo shows one of these red on the left and one of the brighter old 3 led red ones on the right.

On a side note, be careful if you open the packaging with a utility knife.

XGC4 power adapter

Calling this thing a fast charger is an accurate description. If you've ever charged your gb70 or gb150 using the USB cable, you know it can take several hours or a whole day respectively.
I tested this by draining the gb70 all the way down until it stopped charging a tablet. That put it below 25% according to the charge indicators.
It took just over an hour and a half to get the charge indicator to a full solid green.
So it's definitely a time saver.
It also fits nicely into one of the pocket of the gb70 case.
On a side note, I did not require the additional plugs for international outlets but I can see that being useful for travelers.

It's a good helmet to use for yourself as a primary helmet, and it's affordable enough that it's also a good option to get and keep on hand for when you want to take people on a ride who may not have their own helmet. It's got a classic, timeless look that I find doesn't do the bobble-head effect.

All and all if your like me and you like to take your vehicle down the tacky isle with a cramp magnet, these battery terminals are great for hookin up all that junk! I like that it will prevent the seat from UV exposure and cracking, we have a project bike taking up our garage right now so the atv is outside. title: Flaky? Defective?
text:

The instructions are easy, so I tried it myself. Then I tried again; and again.

Finally, I got my husband to help (retired engineer), and he agrees, this one is probably defective.

The pressure jumps up to 33 then down to 5. Once, it did stay at 33 and he was able to inflate a tire. The next time it jumped down to 5 (after setting it at 33) and wouldn't come back up again.

If you get a good one, I'm sure this is a wonderful machine to have with you in your car, to inflate car tires, bicycle tires, motorcycles, dirt bikes, air mattresses, rafts, and sports balls. It plugs into the cigarette lighter socket in a car -- so you'll always have a power source when you're travelling.

The other thing is -- you press the "M" button to set the pressure to PSI, KPA, BAR, KG/CM -- and it's very tiny. I was pressing the M button to PSI and I could not SEE PSI. Eventually, I looked very closely and could see it.

title: Some reviewers here don't seem to understand this product or what a sealant is
text: This is a sealant not a wax. Let's get that in there right off the bat. This product is designed to provide a longer lasting, longer than waxes anyway, barrier of protection on top of your paint. It won't remove water spots, paint swirls or other imperfections. While you'll get some shine and gloss it's not as much as a good wax. Think of it as a base coat for anything else you put on top. I'd highly recommend claying or using a surface prep mitt like Nanoskin to remove imbedded surface contaminants prior to applying this or any sealant. Let this sealant cure properly and then apply your favorite wax, or wash then wax if your car got dirty, on top. That's pretty much the way this Turtle Wax sealant and others are designed to work. Protect your paint and then wax to get that deep shine, gloss and water beading you're looking for. As for the product itself it works well, goes on easy and buffs off quickly. Only knock I have on it is it doesn't last as long as some others I've used, but then again those other products cost two or three times more. It's nice that they give you a decent applicator and a microfiber towel that's not a piece of junk. Good luck guys!

title: This is not the right sensor
text:
I bought this as a replacement sensor for my 2000 Tacoma(2.4L) because I found this in Denso website said so.
This is an Oxygen sensor, while my original part was called "air fuel ratio sensor" and they are not interchangeable(Google, "O2 sensor vs. air fuel ratio sensor").
I have to order the right part(234-9001 Denso). Meanwhile the time is running out for the re-registration.

If I can't trust the original manufacturer who I can trust?
Don't trust the Denso web site.
Write down the part number then go to a nearest parts store or auto shop and make sure it is the right part.
Otherwise, you'll be wasting a lot of money and precious time.

So I had questions like "Should I fill up my tank first?" and "But my tank at full is under 15 gallons. Is it still okay to add the whole thing?" and "Should I run my engine first?" and etc.

So I had questions and I went to look for answers on Penray's website and that wasn't at all helpful. I finally ended up on ehow.com for general instructions on adding fuel stabilizer to gasoline which differed from "Add the whole thing" to being "general rule is 1 oz to 3 to 5 gallons of gas but read the label" so I have the label and I have these instructions but ehow did go on to instruct to add before filling the tank, then fill the tank to full and then run engine so stabilizer goes through the system.

I'm not saying that Penray had to have a page dedicated to instructions on how to use their product but a little more instructions on the back may have been helpful for a novice user like myself. Penray, after all, dedicated a lot of label to the DANGER! section so maybe they could have squeezed in a few more lines about the optimal use of the stabilizer or at least a web address if the user had any questions.

title: TOO SHORT FOR TOURING HARLEYS - get the long one!
text:
TOO SHORT FOR TOURING HARLEYS - so get the longer one (or mod the shorter one).
I read the reviews, and saw one person state their Road Glide or something like that fit, and when I cross checked his wheelbase to mine, mine should have fit. WRONG.
Bottom Line: 76" dolly is good for a 60.5" wheelbase max. the 8" you lose on each end is due to the stopper bar being in from the end (and it's important you use it), and the radius of the tire.

I have a 2013 Road King (FLHR). With the stopper bars in, this is a solid 3 inches too short. And their longer one is too long in my mind.
Because I had it sitting in the box until I could get to it (bought it for winter storage convenience), the time had passed beyond returns. Fortunately I have a lot of tools. I extended the center plates on the rail bars by splitting the center out 3 inches, re-drilling holes, welding a thin plate to fill the 3 inch gap, and painting it. Also had to move the kick stand plate (easy by drilling new holes). Even then, when my bike is on its kick stand, the stand wants to push out beyond that extension plate, so it should be out a bit more for my stock bike even.
Why four stars? It's actually a good piece of equipment. I didn't have any problems mounting in or unloading like others mentioned (no shooting out from under). I just wish I had more info to go by... the dolly length isn't enough info because the radius of the tire takes up a fair bit to fit on this thing between the stopper bars. So if my Hog with a 63.5 inch stock wheelbase is 3" too long for this 76" short Dolly, don't put any bike on here with more than a 60.5 inch wheelbase. Hope that helps.

Once assembled (you need to bolt the sides to the main platform which is esy and comes with nylon lock nuts), I simply laid the unit on its side and bent it in by slowly leaning into it, then repeat for the other side. The one trigger lock isn't quite snapping around yet and is likely a matter of finetuning- I just got it yesterday and installed it. It looks nice and is solid. I went chrome because i didn't want a cheap look from the sides, but it's also costs more than other options. Lots of adjustment room fore/aft. One other thing... The front connection where it slides in might be a bit long or high on the lower prong... It need to slide in at a low angle and still is tight to the original Harley mounting bracket.

Knocking off one star only because I had to play with it some for something that was almost $90 and I felt should have been closer to fit than it was (each side had to come in about a 1/2 inch) and I was worried the bend could crack the chrome over time (it didn't when I bent it). title: Oh 3M, what hast thou wrought? And why does it cost so much?
text:
In theory, a tape of small LED lights that can be affixed to the underside of your cabinets is kind of a cool idea. However in practice, I'd say not so much. First problem is that it requires EIGHT AA batteries. Not only is that a lot of juice for a few teeny little LEDs (I had a friend who wired up a dozen for me on two AAAs!) but they weigh a ton, which means that the sticky tape had better do its job or the switch box is going to come popping off the underside of your cabinet pretty quickly.

Which brings me to the second problem: Getting the whole thing up under the cabinets. The light strip isn't too big a problem though it has a mind of its own, but the box containing the batteries is affixed to the surface with some industrial strength velcro. This might have been one of the biggest mistakes because the force needed to pull the box down off the cabinet yanks it right off the adhesive while the velcro clings like an unwanted guest. Fortunately the adhesive seems to restick at least twice without much trouble. Changing the batteries isn't going to be much fun, though. There are only so many times you can restick tape before it says "Nuh-UH!" and gives up completely.

As to the light itself, it's standard issue cold LED light. It's bright, it lights up dark corners pretty well. It does what it's supposed to do. But it doesn't do it efficiently, and if I'm paying $50 for this thing (List price is $100+!) I want to make sure that I'm going to be saving money on its operation, and that it'll be properly in place for a long time to come without me having to hunt down something to restick it to the cabinet.

I'd have given this light strip three stars if it wasn't for the price, which I think is outrageous. $20, yeah, but $50 or $100? Thanks, I'll get one of those cheap stick up lights.

ETA: The entire battery pack fell off of the cabinet a few months ago. Broken case, batteries everywhere... it wasn't pretty, but it didn't surprise me. I'd been waiting for this to happen. The whole thing got tossed into the trash. Think twice about paying even $50 for them unless you have a better way to mount the battery pack.

title: Do this first ...!
text:
A very good way to get your paint looking great. If you run your hand along your car and feel a bunch of tiny bumps and snags then you need to clay bar your car. This will not remove oxidation but it cleans up all the little bits of road crud that are on your car which gives you a nice smooth surface to move on to polish or rubbing compound. Don't forget to use wax or a sealant (I like the Klasse High Gloss sealant) as a last step.

It does not take too long, it took about 25 minutes to do my little Miata, I'd guess you need to add about another 20 minutes for a 4 door car.

Consider this a first step to getting your car's paint looking its best.

title: Recommend, but don't attempt yourself without tools and some basic skills.
text:
Curt 11114 for Sky Red Line. This is a nice quality Class I hitch. Instructions suggested 45m installation, so I naturally doubled it and was still went about an additional hour. Even so, being careful, things went generally as described. First time doing things, so unhooking the exhaust hangers without specialized tools took a little bit. Drilling two holes in my frame took a little longer, esp with a drill bit.of questionable quality and sharpness. I made it through that much of the install in the expected 45 min.
From there, fishing the bolts was another learning experience. They are fished through the access hole, but it turns out the carriage bolts are slightly off center and dimensionally so big that they can only be inserted through the access in one way (of eight). At that point they are attached to a spring-steel fishline, adding to the challenge. The access holes are used for the other two (non-drilled) attachments, so both standard and reverse fishing techniques described are needed.
Once bolts on one side were fished, I was worried about knocking them back up into the frame, so I did a very loose attachment on that side with the nuts. This made fishing the other side more challenging due to the rack mount hanging under the drilled and access holes. Even so, with some care, I fished the remaining two bolts and connected them. Torqued everything down, got some soapy water to ease reattachment of the muffler hangers and was in good shape.
Went to turn the car around to garage it, and I heard some thumps. Even with a cutout for the exhaust, my muffler pipes impinged the hitch on either side when moving. The pipes sat a little low, below the cut-out --about where the "ear" marking the bottom of the cut-out is. So, next day, I had to trim the "ear" from the hitch to keep a flat line on the front of the hitch supports from the tube attachment up to the cut-out (dremel, hack saw, sawz-all). This helped things but testing showed there would still be some significant thumping in casual driving; I had to use zip-ties between the hitch and muffler hangar to temporarily tighten things up. Went back with auto touch up paint to cover the cut faces of the hitch. Now she drives quiet and hitch is secure.
Best thing about this install was the fish wires provided--they are perfectly dependable; worst thing was the next three days of being sore.
I did this install myself, with random jackstands and braces for assistance. The instructions recommend getting a buddy. If you don't do that, having professional installation is always an option..

title: Requires a little ingenuity and minor mods, but a great price and a great look.

The threads cut on the receivers could use better alignment, though, especially on the upper pieces where one must drill through the plastic panel to mount--took a few tries to get holes adequately placed and sized to allow for the exotropia of the mounting studs.  Two of the four (outer ones, I think) also came in very close to existing mold buttresses; not a big deal, but altered the install a bit--those attachments could be moved.  The lower center grille, as is, sat too far back--pretty much against the mesh.  When compared to the side/fog-light pieces, it was too recessed.  I wanted a more uniform plane coming off the fogs to the center grill, so I fabricated four spacers roughly 1.5 inches (or so) deep and substituted longer bolts.  The third challenge was that a few of the grille pieces, especially the bottom center, impinged on the bumper and threatened to gouge it. title: Nice, low weight carrier, once you get it assembled.
text: This is a good size for campers. It is large enough to actually be of value in transporting stuff that wont fit in the camper. Seems sturdy enough, but it won't hold 500 lbs. My guess follows other reviews,  250 to 300 lbs., max. Reflectors are a nice touch. The bottom tray has closely spaced bars, and I will cover it with an old floor mat cut to fit. I don't see anything good coming of metal to metal contact with aluminum construction. Now, the bad. This took me about 90 minutes to finish. It would be 30 to 45 minutes if you get someone other than your wife to assist. The directions are simply an exploded view.  The step by step does not include advice like assembling the entire tray with screws finger tight, then tightening them with a drill driver. The screws are all in one pack, and you don't get but one extra set, so if you drop one, find it then. All screws and bolts are metric. Another thing: the tray and upper ring are NOT symmetrical. There is a right way (four holes for the reflector corners)  and a wrong way. I had assembled this going clockwise, and when I found the difference, I was not inclined to disassemble, so I left the rear corners with three screws. Other than that, the screw holes were all where they should be, and I installed the screws with the head inside and the locknuts on the outside. I use a weatherproof cover, and I didn't want the screws tearing or poking holes in it. I would have gladly paid $10 - $15 more for the carrier to have the little Chinese guy at the factory assemble the tray with rivets, but I guess that would not keep it competitive with similar ones. If using a drill driver, set the torque so you don't overtighten the screws and deform the aluminum frame. I'm leaving shortly on a 1,700 mile trip, and if there are any issues, i will  update the review.

title: Nice bling; AWESOME Amazon customer service
text:
Amazingly, spectacularly, PERFECTLY tacky! Makes my "new" wagon look like it's driven by a Biker Mama. I live in a climate where it's not likely to corrode very soon -- probably wouldn't have it where roads are salted or a lot of rain gets on the thing. It rattles a bit if your car only has two bolt-holes; you can fix that with a couple of stick-on furniture leg pads, which will keep the metal from rubbing against the license plate or car body.

The truly amazing thing was Amazon's customer service. My neighborhood has two streets, running parallel side-by-side, with essentially the same name: one is an "Erewhon LANE" and one is "Erewhon WAY." The house numbers are identical on the two streets. So people who live on Erewhon Lane get deliveries and service vendors for Erewhon Way, and vice versa. The guy who lives in the Erewhon house with the same number as mine has been very ill, resulting in the loss of most of his marbles -- often he can't even remember my name. His aging wife, as you can imagine, is pretty thoroughly harassed and exhausted. When stuff gets misdelivered to their house, it falls into a bottomless pit, never to be seen again.

The first attempt to deliver this doo-dad suffered that fate: it disappeared. Second delivery also apparently went to the wrong house: Amazon's software said it had been delivered, but there was no sign of it here. My house has a fenced (unlocked) front patio, so things that are placed next to the door can't be seen from the street and are usually not taken by the local mail thieves.

When I asked Mrs. LostMarbles if they'd seen the package (actually, I walked my dogs past their house to see if the frames were on any of their cars, which are always parked in the driveway), she denied it and accused me of stealing junk that was misdelivered to my house. I figured they planned to use the things as Christmas gifts. Giving up, I explained the situation (again!) to a patient Amazon CSR and just canceled the order.

A day later, the package showed up. And a few hours afterward, as we encountered each other while walking our respective dogs, Mrs. LostMarbles asked -- butter not melting in her mouth! -- if I'd ever received the package. :-D She was gratified to hear it had arrived.

Throughout this hilarious adventure in neighborliness, Amazon's staff were patient, understanding, and long-suffering. They went above and beyond the call of duty to try to get the package delivered, and when it appeared that nary a driver could get it to the right place, they agreed to cancel the order. After the second lost package magically "appeared" (two days after it actually had been delivered SOMEWHERE), they also made sure the charge for the correct amount appeared. Great work, Amazon!

title: Outstanding
text:
There are really three/four things that people REALLY need to care about with their car:
1) Clean windshield, you have to see out the thing. I recommend people to try Aquapel (available on Amazon). Man this stuff is incredible in the rain.
2) Headlights. Get the brightest bulbs you can. I also recommend trying 303 Aerospace Protectant (available on Amazon) on the lenses to keep them clear and non yellow.
3) Tires. Don't go cheap. They are the only four points of contact on the road your vehicle has.
4) Brake. You need to stop.
And that where this short review comes in. The Power Stop 1-Click Brake Kit is a steal. You get slotted and drilled rotors, ceramic pads and clips all in one inexpensive kit. I've installed them and gently broke them in per Power Stop instructions. The are strong and for the most part dust free. I have no real issues with the brakes themselves.

Now on to what people take stars off for:
The kit I got was obviously opened prior to delivery. Your kit should come sealed with a sticker that says "To be opened by Amazon customer only" or something along those lines. The rotors should come in with a plastic bag around them with helpful stickers that tell you if they are passenger or driver side. The pads should all have one pad with a backing clip (?, don't know the correct term) per set. The fronts came without the bag and had some minor scrapes on them. I deemed them ok and installed them and haven't had a problem. The rears came factory sealed but one set of pads was missing the backing clip. Again I installed them and have had no problems. I contacted Amazon and let them know my dissatisfaction. They immediately sent another kit, even though I told them not to. But that one came opened as well. I sent them back unused. Just be careful and thoroughly inspect your kits. Amazon is great, their customer service is excellent, and they went well beyond what most companies do to make me happy.

title: Perfect fit
text: Before you remove the old seal, clean around the crankshaft stub and front cover.  The old seal will pop right out with a gentle pry from a flat screwdriver or possible even a seal remover tool (gasp!) This seal is installed without any sealant which makes it super easy.  I like to pack the inner side with grease before installing but check with your family Dr first and past performance is not an indicator of future returns. title: 2008 Jeep JK with the Dana 'Super' 30 front axle.
text:
Some reviews of this product and similar ones from other brands suggest replacing the grease fittings with 45 degree angles to allow easier fitment of the grease gun nozzle after installation. I did this for the driver's side (first to go in) but upon close inspection it appears to be unnecessary. On the passenger side I left the straight grease fitting in place and ran with it. There is just a bit of bind when installing the grease gun nozzle but it is still easy enough to wiggle on and off.

I don't know if there is a difference between the right and left sides of the axle housing, but the driver's side was extremely difficult to install and get seated, yet the passenger side just falls into place! Also, the unit installed on the passenger side appears a little bit deformed on the inner surface - it is not round. This caused a bind on the axle shaft. Combined with the loose fit inside the axle housing, as the axle shaft rotates it will also rotate this dust seal until the grease fitting stops it from turning any further - there is about 1/4 free rotation total on the passenger side but the driver's side is a firm fit.

Overall I really like this product. This is soooo much better than the little plastic cap Dana used. This should be an OEM part.

title: These are garbage on my 2008 Jeep Wrangler Sahara 2-door
text:
I ordered a set of four. Front pair and rear pair arrived separately. Both sets came with mounting instructions for just the FRONT ONLY. But how can it be to figure out - right?

The OEM front bump stops were mostly destroyed and when I removed them they crumbled. So, those can not be reused. The Sumo springs do NOT fit! The pair for the "Front" were actually the rear set and the set for the "Rear" were really the front set! That is, if the description in the instructions is accurate.

Anyways, the 'front' springs have a stud and are suppose to bolt on. MY JEEP DOESN'T HAVE A HOLE IN THIS LOCATION. I can't get a drill/bit into that tight spot either. I kept thinking there must be a mistake and I have the ends swapped. But nope - springs with the stud go in front.

Not on my Jeep they don't.

So I go to the rear just for comparison. The rear OEM bump stops are in much better shape than the front. But again, there is no way the rear Sumo Springs are going to fit into the bump stop keepers.

At this point I am hours deep into this project and don't want to put the front end together without any bump stops at all. What I end up doing is taking the REAR bump stops (without the stud) and re-shaping them with my belt sander so they will fit the front. Now I can put the Jeep back together and still have bump stops in front.

I say 'Bump Stops' and NOT "Springs" because either one of these, front or rear, are no taller than the OEM bump stops. What is the point?

Anyways, if you can't figure it out by now, I am very disappointed with these. The pair I modified I now own. But the other pair ('Front'... or are they the 'Rear'?) I will return.

2ND REVIEW - A FOLLOW-UP:

After replacing the fuse now both bulbs are working. But I'm going to keep a sharp eye on them and the circuit - don't need to burn down my truck over an LED bulb upgrade.

3rd REVIEW - A FOLLOWING FOLLOW-UP:
After driving for many nights I have found these bulbs to be very dim. The OEM reflectors are designed for a single-source bulb - a filament. But these LED bulbs are covered in tiny LED lights - there is no one singe source of light. This makes the light ooze out in all directions instead of reflect sharply into a focused pattern. I replaced them and returned to conventional OEM style bulbs.

text:
These headers installed easy and work fantastic! My Jeep is a 2008 Wrangler Sahara. The CATs went out and I did not like any of the 'bolt on' options. So I went with these headers, high flow cats, and a pair of mufflers.

See the links: [[ASIN:B019XF7OQA DynoMax 24254 Thrush Rattler Muffler (2.5" In/Out)]][[ASIN:B01MXWAZBR 2.5" Inlet/Outlet Universal Catalytic Converter 425250 Serise Direct Fit Converter High Flow Stainless Steel (2.5inch W/O2 Nut)]][[ASIN:B00J2RQ3US BBK 1118 Exhaust Pipe]]

NOTE: The item "BBK 1118 Exhaust Pipe" is mislabeled!!! This is NOT an "Exhaust Pipe" - this is an oxygen sensor (O2 or OXY) wire harness extension. At the BBK website for this part number it says the harness is for a Dodge application but will also work on a range of Jeeps (like mine).

I picked up new O2 sensors locally and had a local custom shop do the install - they provided all the other pipe and hardware. The system is 2.5" all the way out! The mufflers are mounted below the doors and the exhaust tips turn out just ahead of the rear tires. After the work was complete the shop shows me the old cast iron exhaust manifolds - there were so many cracks it is a wonder these did not crumble off. The amount of heat under the hood has been reduced so much that the cabin is noticeably cooler now. The A/C blows cooler, the cabin cools down faster, and the floor and firewall are cooler. There is no difference in off-idle torque but at the top end she seems to unwind much quicker and shifts come very snappy - who knew the exhaust could make such a big difference? title: These are the end-all bulbs for rural driving
text:
I have a JK Wrangler and since the day I took delivery in 2007 I have been disappointed with the headlights. I live deep in the Pacific Northwest woods and during Winter nights under overcast sky it is pitch black driving conditions. The original lights were so poor I felt like 45 mph was the maximum safe speed regardless of the road conditions.

After a few years of suffering the factory light bulbs I upgraded to "Off Highway Only" xenon white 100/80Watt bulbs about 6,000 degrees Kelvin color temperature. These bulbs have a very feint blue tint but nothing like more common 'blue' bulbs I see. That blue color is absorbed by everything organic - foliage, fur, etc. However, eye-shine, road signs and lane stripe paint reflect very well. Also the sharp blue hue dazzles oncoming drivers easy so I had to aim the lights lower than normal so as the low beams went completely into the road 50 yards ahead and the lower edge of the high beams sat on the horizon. Peripheral illumination with these lights was non existent and I have been surprised by deer darting onto the road countless times, (and nailed a couple too).

Last week one bulb burned out after a few years of service which brings me to these Wagner NightDefense bulbs. I purchased these bulbs because the sales literature says this color combination is designed for rural driving conditions. AND HOW! I think the median color of these bulbs is about 4000K. I can see all the foliage along the roadside and tell the difference between needles and leaves and fur lurking in the brush. The peripheral illumination is fantastic as well. I can see deer in the pastures and fields 45 degrees to either side 100 yards away. And I was able to raise the aim of the headlights without dazzling oncoming drivers. My buddy is a Sheriff's Deputy and I had him judge the lights as we made a couple of head-on passes on the highway. He says they are definitely "Yellow" but nothing he would find out-of-place and they do not dazzle his eyes like the blue tint does.

The only reason I do not give five stars for these bulbs is the layered colors do not match up between both headlights. The driver's side bulb has a much stronger yellow than the passenger side when viewed head-on. And from the driver's seat I see a 5' wide blue spot on the road about 20 yards out.

With that said I will keep using these bulbs in the future. I was looking into upgrading the entire headlight assembly, which is popular with the Wranglers, but now I am good to go with the factory lights and these bulbs.

title: Sometimes, the Old Ways Are Best
text:
When I got my new car, I wanted to keep the interior in top shape. Since I had spent the past 11 years keeping my old car's interior in really nice condition with Armor All, I figured that would be OK until the guy at the auto store told me about Meguiar's reputation for being the premium brand in detailing and car care. I spent the extra money on this and used this stuff for a solid year.

The most noticeable attributes of this product are its rich, creamy foam and the powerful cedar scent it gives off when you apply it and for about a week afterwards. I think it makes a good first impression in that it really DOES appear high class and it has a scent that most people might find comforting. However, it soon goes sour. This product is GREASY. The description is completely wrong. This stuff is slippery and very, very, very oily. This is good, since the thick coat of oily product would logically protect longer...however, this oily coating attracts dust and hair and dirt like a superconducting magnet and it's VERY noticeable on black vinyl interiors! It also doesn't seem to want to go on evenly, with blotches and uneven shine on large, flat areas and textured vinyl unless you layer it on thick until it's an oil slick...the entire Mazda3 interior is a finely-textured vinyl and it's a pain to lather the entire interior in this greasy stuff that gives you a headache with the smell. It's also VERY shiny. VERY shiny. But only in the places where you apply a lot of it. Everywhere else, it'll be splotchy or have different reflectiveness. Again, this is magnified on black vinyl.

I'm throwing this out and going back to Armor All.

title: Great For Getting Water Spots and Splotches!
text:
Although I am certain this product can protect your car's finish if applied regularly, I have used this product as instructed (and paired with its specific wash, too) and have been very disappointed with the results.

I have a 2006 Mazda 3 in Copper Red Mica and from the day I brought it home, I've only used the Ice car wash and liquid polish. The good points to it are that it CAN be applied much easier than standard waxes and polishes and it can give you a very deep shine. Unfortunately, this isn't much more than regular carnauba wax with a facelift and a better marketing strategy behind it. First of all, it's just a polish, not a wax, so it doesn't provide a hard shell to protect the finish, it just shines things up and gives a thin coating of wax. This means that you really DO need the touch up spray and you need to use it regularly. The second bad thing is that this, being only carnauba wax, will make water bead on your car. Unless you run out with a silicone blade or a chamois every time it rains, your car will get VICIOUS water spots, which are very visible on red and blue paint jobs. Thirdly, even with a dry car and very careful application, I managed to get uneven splotches that didn't rinse or buff off, especially around the door handles. These had to sort of wear off, although they were a good indicator as to when the car needed a new coat of polish.

After 1 solid year of dedicated use, I am tossing this stuff out and going with [[ASIN:B000BZZ9CI Durashine 16oz w/ 32oz Durawash - As Seen on TV]], the only synthetic polish that has ever lived up to my expectations. For comparison purposes, DuraShine is just as easy to use and apply as Ice is, but it SHEETS water and won't bead it, so you get 98% less water spotting. I used DuraShine for 11 years before this stuff and I am sorry I ever left it.

As for Ice, I feel that while it might be an OK product, the spotting, splotches and frequent applications just don't justify its use.

title: Initial review: Work well, easy to install once you realize the video has errors
text:
I installed a pair of AUXITO H4 9003 LED Headlight Bulb Fanless 9000 Lumens in my wife's 2004 CR-V. Once you understand the correct sequence of actions for installation (which the product video gets out of order), it takes about 3 minutes per light. The main corrections are:
1. The plastic disk's correct orientation (in a 2004 CR-V anyway) is upside down from what the video shows. (If the disk is not oriented right you will not be able to get the wire clip back in place AND the disk will not seat fully, which means the lamp will not have a firm placement or proper alignment.)
2. Replace the original Honda rubber gasket/seal BEFORE inserting the LED lamp into the socket. Do not, as some reviewers suggest, cut the rubber seal.
3. When you insert the lamp, the Auxito label should be on the left, not the right, or the hi/low-beams will be upside down. As others have mentioned, you'll probably have to do this wrong before seeing what I mean.
Now that I've figured out the right sequence and orientations, I could install both again in 5 minutes easily.

As for longevity, I'll have to find out. I very carefully put the old bulbs in the nicely padded Auxito box and stowed them in the CR-V just in case the new LEDs aren't reliable. They have a 1-year warranty. For the price, if they last that long, they will be cheaper than the traditional, dimmer Honda bulbs.

Things to keep in mind, since this will sit direclty on the car roof, and not to a roof rack (though will be secured as such), it may be best to put a blanket or something down to avoid scratces. Plus pay attention to the weight on the bare roof.

Overall, a good bag for when you don't have roof racks, or smaller cars, or even if you do, good for quick trips when mounting a clamshell will be more difficult than it's worth.

title: Goodbye Annoying Road Rust
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this product truly did “wow” me. Random road rust spots like the ones pictured started showing up on my recently purchased Audi due to a lot of roadwork and construction in my area. They were beginning to bother me because washing alone seemed to be making them stand out more. I was told I needed a paint correction and a ceramic coat which would have run me $1500+ (mind you this car is pretty new). I did my research and learned that clay bars pull a lot of contamination out of paint, so I figured why not try this before pursuing the recommended paint correction and ceramic coating. I thoroughly washed my car, dried it, then went to work with the spray and clay bar. It was like magic and my paint looked brand spanking new again. Immediately after wiping the lubricant, my paint had that new wet shine look again. It also removed what I thought was a scratch (but turned out to be just a scuff) on my door handle that I assumed would’ve needed to be professionally buffed out.

I recommend buying a back up bar, or cutting it into 1/3. I dropped the bar after two sections and luckily I had 2/3 left to work with.

title: There are better covers out there for my needs (wants) but this ...
text:

I would love the one that just covers the doors and roof line but $100+ is nuts. This one is bulky but I expected that because it covers the whole jeep. I have a stock jeep and you have to center it just right to cover the front and rear bumper just right. In my initial use to verify it covers my jeep I found that I covered the front very well and had trouble covering rear bumper. If you have a custom bumper that's sticks out further out... you most likely will be out of luck. Personally you should be able to cover the whole jeep fine in the stock configuration. Also I was able to get back into bag without special folding... I crammed it right in then surprised I got it in there. I have the short antenna so no issues there like others had. When on I noted that it covered about half of my rims (Stock Sierra with 32" wheels). It would have been good if they would have make it about 1' longer (front to back) - coverage on side seemed fine to me.

2014-08-31 / Water resistant not waterproof... I recently didn't want to put the top back on so I covered it with this cover. It wasn't suppose to rain but it did. It kept most of the rain out but it leaked around the seams I believe. The front cargo area was dry but it dripped water in a few place which is what I thought was coming in from the seams. The following day I went to put the top up just to find a decent amount of water (about a cup) in my soft top folds. Again I'm guessing it came in round the seams. This cover protected my jeep but I won't use the cover alone any more. Next time I'll put the soft top up then cover it... this will allow me to at lease by pass the process of putting the windows in. The problem using this OR any other cover I know of is that the rain will pool in the center of the roll cage, placing stress on the seams then it leaks. Although it leaked it did it's job well. The key is having this cover OR any other pulled tight so the water rolls off rather than pools. I don't see how I can make this top super tight so I can't really use it with out the soft top on. I'm keeping my review 4 stars because all in all it did it's job and my jeep had very little water in it. Also just for addition info... I think my spiderweb shade helped as well in saving my butt. The spiderweb shade provided additional support for the car cover when it started pooling water... if it didn't I'm afraid it would have been much worse. Getting the pooled water of the car cover was a pain as well... I got inside the jeep and pushed up in the center of the pool and got most of it then used a grass blower to get the rest.

The only thing I need to mention is that there is a little groove in the pads in the front, and driving on dirt roads in the country of New England, the glacial dump of rocks, I picked up a pebble in the pad from a car turning up dust ahead of me, and I thought the caliper had froze on me. I am very happy with the experience, and recommend the brand and the company to buyers.

text: It's nice to see the prices on LiFePO4 batteries coming down a bit. They weigh a lot less and have a longer service life than sealed lead acid batteries. The pros of SLA batteries (which batteries like this are designed to directly replace) are they are a long-proven technology and will hold their charges a long time, and will continue to operate after being stored for years. And they are still cheap compared to LiFePO4 batteries. But they are heavy and don't hold up to as many recharge cycles. So it comes down to preference. title: Really handy portable light duty pressure washer
text:
First of all don't expect to do any heavy duty pressure washing with this. You'll set yourself up for disappointment. This is a light duty washer, but it's portable and extremely handy.

It comes with two wand heads---a basic sprayer with a head that can be adjusted for direction, and a multi-use head, which has a soap bottle connector (bottle is included). It also comes with a wand extension. Using it without the extension is really handy for using this sprayer in tight spaces.

It will not connect directly to a garden hose for water supply. It's not built for that. It's strictly a siphon-type supply, and you provide the water in a bucket, or any other handy water. The end of the siphon hose has a filter, but I don't think I'd chance using it in particularly dirty water and risk clogging the sprayer. The hose is about twenty feet long, long enough to be useful. You can tell that it's pretty much about as long a hose as the sprayer can handle. Any longer and it might not be able to draw the water to the spray unit.

The hose is pretty soft and does kink easily, and it's easy to flatten just by stepping on it. It's something to check if your water flow cuts off while cleaning.

I suspect the hose might grow mold inside if you leave water in it, so follow the instructions to empty it as much as possible before storing. Keep it stored away from insects---they have a way of finding hoses and building mud nests in them and clogging them up.

I was concerned the sprayer would empty a five-gallon bucket in seconds, and that would mean a lot of refilling and lugging buckets of water. But it doesn't draw water that fast. With the basic spray head it draws about a gallon a minute. That's not too bad.

It comes with a charger and two batteries, which is awesome. The batteries arrived with a partial charge. There's a button and LED gauge on them to check charge level. It's probably a good idea to fully charge the batteries before using the washer. The charger connects directly to the batteries. You don't have to have them in the sprayer to recharge them. But it's not a quick charger. A full recharge takes a few hours.

Before operating you need to make sure the battery and hoses are fully seated. You have to pull the trigger all the way back for it to turn on. It has a slow start then builds up, probably by design.

The hose and wand and battery are easy to remove by either pushing release buttons or sliding the collars back. The whole thing can be then packed away and stored in a pretty small box. I'd make sure it's in an area with good air circulation so any water remaining can evaporate.

title: works well, the built-in voltmeter is a plus
text: If you want a backup charger for devices, an old car battery that will still take and hold a charge is a good option, as well as smaller sealed lead-acid batteries. They're very stable, and as long as there's nothing connected to them, they'll hold a full charge a very long  time. This charger/adapter is really good for that. You can clip off the ring connectors and instead crimp on some clamps or female auto-wiring type connectors so you can connect them to the battery or even switch batteries. The built-in voltmeter is a big plus. If you don't let the 12v battery run down too much before recharging it -- like, say, less than 12 volts -- it will last a lot longer. I checked with a multimeter and found the built in voltmeter was pretty close to accurate, reading maybe a bit low, but less than 1/10th of a volt.

title: This stuff's going in my lawn mower engine
text:
With all the advantages, protection and performance a synthetic oil of this quality offers, I checked to see if I could use it in my lawn mower motor.

Briggs and Stratton's website says:

"Can you use synthetic lawn mower oil?"

"Yes! We have modified our engine oil recommendations to state that you may now use a synthetic 5W30... or 10W30 oil in all temperature ranges."

And it specifically says of synthetic SAE 5W-30 oil:

"Best protection at all temperatures as well as improved starting with less oil consumption."

That's all I need to know. Mower oil change time!
