title: Bad cells in this one, don't stay charged and don't have sufficient cranking power when charged
text:
I don't like to leave negative reviews. I usually just leave a rating and forget about it - cos it's negative I guess.

I ordered this after I regretfully left my GOOD one at our vacation home a few hundred miles away. I'd been hoping I wouldn't need it, of course - but this winter seems to have been hard on the car's battery and I didn't want to be scrambling for a ride on a cold morning before I'd replaced it. Sure enough, I needed a start soon after. I had FULLY charged this starter over the weekend, and put it in the trunk. THREE DAYS LATER - literally - I turned it on and the charge indicator had one BAR OUT.. meaning it had dropped from FULL charge to... well, 4 bars out of 5 lit. I attached it, thinking that should be enough - it's a little Subaru 4-cyl, not asking it to start a V8 or anything. .... click. click ... nope. I adjusted the cables, ensuring the best possible connection to the clean, dry battery terminals, made sure the unit was on [it doesn't have a "start" mode or anything else.. It is simply on or off... then it's multiple annoying flashing flashlight settings. So - IT IS ON. I plug it in again, see the voltages on the cable-attachment staging down to a nominal battery voltage of 12v. click. click. It will not turn over the starter. I leap inside the house and put it on the charger, pretty ticked off. Make a phone call that I'm running late - and give it an hour to "top off". It indicated a full charge, I went back out and after some fiddling _barely_ got it to turn over, albeit slowly and sluggishly.. wwwhhiir... whhiiirr... The car being in good overall condition, after 2 turns it started. OK. Maybe it was a fluke. Same thing happened a couple days later. Two days after charging it, t had drained a full "bar" and could not turn the engine.

Bear in mind that I own another one [still at the vacation cabin unfortunately]. That one? After owning it for a YEAR ... and charging it app. bi-monthly, it will crank a V8 or V6 faithfully and reliably. It was a brand called UTRAI. I should have searched harder. I got a dud. The Li cells in this one are clearly beyond their best-by dates, they don't hold a charge and don't have sufficient "cranking amps" to reliably turn over my little Subaru 4-banger.

It's a poorly-shaped doorstop at this point. Oh - and an $80 flashlight with quick-draining batteries.

I'd keep searching. If I got a "dud" that's been in storage too long, how many more are in stock I wonder?

title: I am finally able to wear a seat belt correctly!!!
text:
This is one of the best items I have ever purchased. Why? I am vertically challenged at 5'0' tall woman, and all seat belts end up right across my neck, so I am constantly wrestling with them just to keep comfortable. After having surgery due to breast cancer, even having the belt across my chest was uncomfortable, so I decided to try this, and I am very happy to say that I can now finally wear a seat belt comfortably!

The adjuster is well made, and very easy to use. I have found that you unsnap it, with the straight part at the bottom, and the rounded part at the top, just thread the seat belt into the largest opening, and the metal part of the seat belt goes through the smallest opening, and then into the buckle part of the seat belt. Here's the part that makes it work: the part of the belt that goes across your lap will be at the bottom of the adjuster, and the belt part that goes across your chest will be at the top rounded portion of the adjuster. Snap the adjuster so that the two are separated by the snap. Now you can move it to adjust until you are comfortable and the belt is off your neck. Also, I am able to leave it on my seat belt when I get in and out of the car by just letting the seat belt go back to almost the beginning position.

title: Definitely not as strong or reliable as regular Bondo! Majorly flawed product.
text:
This stuff is just "okay". It definitely isn't the caliber of BONDO, by any stretch of the mind.

WHAT I LIKE ABOUT IT:

1. It makes your work piece light blue.

Love that. I use it for making pendants and other jewelry pieces from silicone molds, which I then paint and customize.

2. It sets up fast...sometimes. See below, because this stuff is NOT very predictable.

THINGS I DON'T LIKE:

1. There isn't the kind of performance reliability with this stuff that there is with Bondo.

I've used Bondo so long that I know that if I use a certain amount of hardening catalyst with the Bondo base, I will have a work time of such-and-such. This stuff, however, is woefully unpredictable. It also seems much more sensitive to temperature changes and light exposure, making it even less predictable.

2. It's light, yeah--but it's also flimsy. It dents and breaks easily. It's not at all firm like BONDO, once cured.

Because it seems to never really fully cure, it is easy to dent and break even weeks after it's supposed to be fully cured. It also doesn't drill or tool well--I have broken about a dozen pieces I've cast trying to drill a tiny hole into them in areas that aren't break- or pressure-prone. Whereas, BONDO drills aces. This stuff crumbles very easily.

2. It doesn't spread and spatula as easily as BONDO, and it is MUCH harder to level. It also bubbles more when being cast.

I don't know why. It just doesn't perform well when either being spatulaed, leveled, or cast in silicone. And it feels a bit harder to fully mix, as the more mixing you do, the quicker it sets up (sort of like BONDO, except that, with Bondo, it does so evenly. Not with this stuff. So you end up with chunks of hardened compound in your softer mixed compound...which renders it all useless.)

This stuff also turns brittle quickly and doesn't level even when you use vibration techniques on it, or to remove any bubbles. It leaves a ton of bubbles in casted pieces, no matter how evenly and timely you vibrate your mold.

All in all, I bought this because it was less expensive and lighter than BONDO...and I ended up getting LESS than what I paid for, because this is sub-par performing, so I really just wasted my money, altogether.

title: Used it to make non-slip, water-resistant fabric backing.  It's excellent for that!
text:
I wanted this to use to create non-slip, water-resistant fabric backing. This did the trick in one coat. I just applied it with a paint brush, in a thick coat. It dried quickly, and is so far working exactly as I intended for it to work.

I'll try to remember to update this once I launder the item. If you are trying this yourself, it should be washable in warm to cool water, but air dry it. Putting it in the dryer will probably cause a big mess for you and ruin the finish.

**UPDATE**

Since writing this review, I've used this for several non-traditional applications--mostly on launderable items--so I can update on its wash- and dryability!

I wanted some thick knee-high slipper socks with non-slip bottoms, so I bought a pair of thick ivory socks and applied 3 coats of this plastidip to the bottoms. After letting them dry for 48 hours, I was thrilled with how they turned out.

But when it came time to wash them, I forgot they were in the wash load and they were washed in hot water and dried at high heat.

To my surprise, they came out just fine! No problems at all--in fact, the dirt that had accumulated on the bottoms came out beautifully...I assumed they would look dingy, but they looked unworn!

So I've probably laundered and dried them 2 dozen times since, and I'm just now noticing that the finish needs to be reapplied, because they are starting to not be waterproof on the bottoms (I wear them outside sometimes, so I've no doubt that walking on concrete also impacts the wear). But they still launder to look brand new, and I'm convinced now, more than ever, that plastdip is the best stuff to make fabrics water- and slip-proof!

title: LOVE these.  Got them to make reusable wipe heads for my Swiffer Wet Jet, but use them for so many things around the house!
text:
These are really great shammies--they are basically the same exact things as Shamwows, just without the annoying commericals and name brand.
I use them all over the house and yard!

I have annoying but crazy-loveable small pups who are very, very (maybe too) family oriented. They are mat-trained, with their mats being in a room with linolium flooring. Problem is, they always want to be with their people, so when they do have to go potty, they do the doggy dash and often drip onto the floor (or sometimes miss part of the mat completely). So we keep a swiffer wet jet close by, since we are constantly having to mop the area. I started feeling bad about the environmental aspect of all the disposable mop wipes we were using for it and decided to make some pads I could throw in the laundry. And these are PERFECT for that.

Making them is easy--just take an unused mop wipe or duster pad and use it as a size template for your new pads. They cut easily, don't fray, wash well and, even though they say don't put them in the dryer, I always do and have never had any issues with it.

I also use them for cleaning rags--especially great for windows. I also use one in my kitchen to place delicate items I've handwashed to dry. I use them whenever we have a spill and I don't feel like dragging the wet-vac out, as well.

title: SO. MUCH. BETTER. (Than carpet...)
text:
Yes, they fit a little off. I rent my cars, and we live in woods in a rain forest. I literally can't step in the car without dragging pine needles in and they're impossible to get out of carpet. I have a 2017 Dodge Grand Caravan GT, and this covers very well about a half inch over each edge of the plastic step where you get into the car so I never have to vacuum it anymore and I'm so happy. To clean it in between renters, all I have to do is wipe it down with a wet cloth and maybe once in a while trying it up with some Armor All. This is cut my interior cleaning time in less than half. it cost me nearly $300 to get these for the entire interior but let me tell you it's absolutely worth it because I have saved so much time from my life in cleaning the car. I used to have to put blankets down inside the car so that when my family used it we wouldn't get it dirty in between rentals and then I'd still have to vacuum it and this is completely eliminated that. I have 10 year old twins and we all love to go hiking and do messy things outdoors and this has eliminated so much hassle from the stress of keeping the car clean for renters.

The first row is easily removed in the driver's and passenger's side and so I can take those out and really hose them down if I need it.

There is a gap between the front along the side of the door before the back row liners begin. I was thinking of trimming a small piece of vinyl and tucking it under the seat and under the plastic molding for the door in that gap which is about a foot long and about 4 inches wide. The good news is, there's just zero reason somebody would put their foot there, so in the meantime it's not really like a huge hassle and I can just quickly brush it out with a little broom.

The second row seats, yes you have to remove it if you want to stow and go, but you would have had to do that with the regular floor mats anyway. It fits in between where I have a broken piece in my vehicle and covers the broken piece so I don't have to spend $140 to replace a stupid little piece of plastic that was too cheap to begin with on the car to stand up to Everyday Use. the second row seats go along the sides and they go around the seat belt anchor, there's a nice little slit that opens up for you to slide it through and then it covers well. the seats anchored down into the little square holes shown in the picture just exactly right.

The third row seats, as someone has stated, don't quite fit exactly around the feet for the back row. Instead of cutting them, I just kind of held it up a little bit while I was lowering the seats and then just let it lay up against them. It's only about a half inch difference if you just scootch the mat a little bit forward toward the back of the second row seats. Which just needs to really happen anyway, because otherwise the floor mats for the 3rd and 2nd rows don't overlap at all, and then they leave some of the carpet exposed, which is what I exactly want to avoid any way. Sure, you could cut it, but I don't find it necessary at all in my particular car and I'd rather have the rim intact then have it channel pine needles and stuff down into the divots where the legs clamp into the floor.

title: My Car Tire's Best Friend
text:
While experiencing a drop in tire pressure indicates one SHOULD replace their tires, let’s face it – not all of us can afford to replace a tire.

And, not always does a tire constantly losing air need anything more than an “air boost” – I know because I have had and currently have a low-air tire.

I can lose air, pump up the tire – go for WEEKS without needing a “boost”.

I got this in the hopes of a “just-in-case”, but not wanting to have to use it. Silly, I know.

That said …

I have used this twice. And, the first time was a learning curve. Learned how to do the PSI deal, set for air, machine pumped up the tire, and shut off when done. LOVED IT!

That was a few months ago.

Last week …

I again saw my tire was low (actually my mom did) – I brought this out, and as I was loading the car with some stuff, I turned on the car’s motor – set air pressure, and let the machine work. Easy-peasy, less than 3 minutes – normal.

My mom was absolutely SOLD on this for any future cars we get.

And, currently it is on sale for around $20 – please, get one. Get a spare if you can!! Even at the marked out $28.99 – it is LESS than the cost of a new tire. And, this is about the size of an old 80’s lunch box – a tad bigger, and light enough to carry with ONE hand, fits in the backseat floorboard of a small sedan.

title: Nice, But Not Worth The Price
text:
Since I got my car in 2008, I’ve had a “9/11” license plate for personal reasons. And, since that same time I’ve used a NASCAR driver license plate frame for the back plate. The front of my car has its own “plate” holder.

But, since my driver is retired from NASCAR, I thought it was time I updated that frame.

This matches my plate and I LOVED the idea of the caps to cover the screws. Though I do park in my garage overnight and don’t leave my car for errands thanks to the pandemic. I either drive-thru, get curbside, or delivery.

I got the frame a while back and just couldn’t bring myself to remove my driver’s one. But, I finally decided to as I was installing a metal emblem on my car.

Now, the install itself was easy. The bottom of the frame has two “clips” in the back to slide the license plate into, and it is a SNUG fit. I had to work it a bit to get it in there. As my back plate area only has TWO (2) screws – that’s all I tried to use.

The screws were FAR too thin for my car, and I resorted to using my old ones. As a result, I couldn’t use the screw covers.

The frame itself is pretty, but doesn’t seem too durable. I didn’t need the tire cap covers, which are a pretty interesting idea.

As I’m not rough with anything, I think it’ll last a while. The last one was on my car for almost eight (8) years.

But, for nearly $17 … not too worth it. My NASCAR one cost less than that and was more durable.

title: Not the Water Pump For My Car

title: Genuine GM Replacement Part
text:
In 2019, the button on my original part started getting "loose" and I was AFRAID that it was going to bust, leaving me no way to "shift" from park/reverse/drive ... etc. Yes, it is an automatic, but you get the idea of moving it into and out of the gears.

I finally got some extra money and decided to order this part. Then, not feeling too "car savvy" ... I wanted to see how much a dealership would charge. As a woman, car maintenance and repairs are not my thing. Just last year I managed to do the third brake light bulbs.

Today (3/29/2020), I got the part and decided to run some errands. And, the button on my old was way too loose for me. Honestly, I was a bit worried. After getting home, and still pondering if I should call the dealership tomorrow (3/30 - Monday), I decided to look up videos on how to change it out. Not having the money to correct anything should it go wrong, yes I was hesitant.

After backing my car out of the garage (as I had little room to do what I needed to do with the car door open), I did what I was instructed to do:

1. Start car
2. Shift into Neutral

Now, I wasn't told to turn off the car, but I did. Since the parking brake doesn't work on my car, and I'm lucky enough to have a "steep" curb up into the garage, I decided to "straddle" the curb. Back end out, front in. That worked.

And, I installed this part myself. Yes, getting the silver part unlocked was tricky. After that? I used the tiny hex/Allen wrench/key to unscrew the old lever handle. Off it came. I then popped on the new part. Screwed it in, screwed the silver part in place. Started the car ... and no issue with the button!

As I purchased the extended warranty, I'm feeling pretty safe now. And, with it being a genuine GM part, I'm definitely feeling good about this.

title: Affordable Bulb
text:
Car maintenance can be pricey, especially if your income goes down and your car gets older. As luck would have it (or not) – both of those things apply to me. As I can do some things for my car to save money, there are other things I cannot do.

Replacing the headlight bulb is one of them.

Despite my car being 11, almost 12, years old; the dealership where I take it is friendly and professional and works with me when it comes to maintenance. The last service adviser had me in stitches!

But, they can’t control labor and part costs. This bulb and the labor would normally run me $65 to replace. Not feasible. Even the labor was too pricey.

I still had this pack from when I had planned to replace the bulb last year; but, as (bad) luck would have it, I couldn’t afford to replace it. Enter my friendly (and funny) service adviser. I got this installed for $0 cost on the last oil change. And, I am VERY appreciative he worked that out for me. Since I had left it at home and had to come back, he joked it would take 48 minutes to install. That was a nod to my favorite NASCAR driver - #48 Jimmie Johnson. He liked another (retired) driver, who I incidentally met once, and liked as well.

Anyway …

As it turned out – the installation took around 30-45 minutes. I was out the door and on the way. Since I’m not an expert at installation, I can’t rate it personally, but the time I spent waiting wasn’t too long, so I’m happy with it.

No negative comments about the bulb (and no recommendations for a better part) and no complaints about the install. I’m sure this is a fairly easy install for those well equipped to do it outside a dealership. The bulbs last a good long time, though my right sides go out more than the left (pretty sure it is a bad wire). This is the second replacement since I’ve had the car (got it new in 2008). The left side is still OEM. Three total bulbs in 11-12 years? I’m not going to be too upset.

I’m fairly happy with these, and I still have a spare.

title: Great replica of KITT’s license plate.
text:
This is the replica for the Knight Industries Two-Thousand (KITT)’s license plate which is even replicated on die-cast cars and holiday ornaments (sold separately). My license plate replica came with the standard “two” (2) CALIFORNIA MONTH/YEAR stickers. These were and still are the norm for the state of California. Other states, like Nevada, use a month/year single sticker for the registration.

Like other replica plates, this is thinner than standard issue California plates. I have a front plate from one of my grandmother’s cars. It was issued in 1982 and has the familiar gold/blue seven (7) character standard which began in 1980 and despite being warped, it is stronger/thicker than these plates.

They’re good for general display. They also pass the test for “show car” displays of the appropriate vehicle during special events (car shows, comic cons, etc.). It is as accurate as allowable by law.

title: Love Bug License Plate
text:
For anyone who has seen the original “Herbie the Love Bug” movies from Disney (The Love Bug, Herbie Rides Again, Herbie Goes to Monte Carlo, etc.) this is a metal replica of the famous Beetle’s license plate.

This is similar to the California license plates that were issued during 1963-1969, pre-dating the gold on blue six (6) digit/letter (1969-1980) and the seven (7) digit/letter gold on blue license plates (1980-1986).

It is a bit thinner than the standard California plate, which I have one from 1982 (belonged to my grandmother’s car) to compare it to. You can barely see the top of the “real” California license plate in the picture.

Since it is only for use like what I am doing with this picture – displaying on a wall with the Love Bug ornament or for “show car” displays, it passes the test and looks great.

It is, like the plates of that time, embossed and not screen-printed.

title: Third Brake Light Fixed! Same as Dealer Parts!
text:
As someone who needs to watch expenses; and having spent over $2200 on car repairs recently – I couldn’t afford to have the light bulbs replaced. I didn’t have the money for the parts and labor, even buying the parts on Amazon.

I bought three 2-packs (my light needs 3, so why not have a spare set for the next time) of these light bulbs and decided to get on YouTube for a tutorial.

Gathering up the courage and waiting until after dark due to the heat – I decided to change the bulbs on my 2008 Cobalt.

Installation wasn’t too easy, but it didn’t require any real “tools”. On the other hand, installation wasn’t so difficult I broke a sweat either – no cussing or crying involved. I did need a flathead screwdriver to loosen the “assembly” part from the trunk, but that was it.

Once that was done – I popped out the three burned lights, popped these in and snapped the assembly back in. Yes, they snapped right out and snapped in. That was the easy part. It took about five minutes since it was my first time.

They worked! Exactly the same as the bulbs I took out (which were the last dealer installed ones). They light up perfectly (as you can see in the photo).

Since I have a spare set, I won’t likely need them for a while (over a year or more). I wouldn’t hesitate to buy them again. Of course should they not last, I can always amend the review. But, for now … I’m pretty happy with them.

The steering wheel cover is cute....not too girly or overly flowered. It slides on easily and doesn't move around while driving or turning . The little coasters are small but still cute.
The keyring is HUGE but I still like it. My keys will not be lost in my bag anymore

title: Comfortable
text: I really didn’t like that this came in two pieces, it’s just not as snug and it’s not as easy to clean.

title: Great for the snowy icy winter
text: This arrived just in time for winter.  The ice scraper and brush can be separated or snapped together. I unsnap them when I put them in the backseat pocket so i don’t have to just toss it in the back. The windshield cover is great for icy weather, just because I have a nice scraper doesn’t mean I like doing it.

title: Sturdy
text: This is easy to get on, I like them better than some leather ones I tried. They are a snug fit. They fabric is sturdy and will do well even if you have dogs.

title: not very useful
text: This isn't very useful but it won't work at all unless you have a lot of room between your front seats. Also with anything heavy in the big pocket, it will tip over.

title: very useful
text:
This is a great way to organize your trunk so stuff isn't rolling around. You can have your winter stuff right where you need it, or your tools, or car cleaning stuff. If you aren't sing it, it folds up nicely.
This is waterproof and seems quite durable.

title: Fail
text: The idea is good but not so great in practice. There just isn’t enough room between the seat and console in my car for this to not be in the way for anyone sitting in the seat. It also isn’t too stable.

title: Lots of cushion
text: My dog is constantly putting her feet up on the console to see better. This covers it perfectly and has some nice padding  for her feet. It’s also nice for an arm rest. It slides on easy with two straps to hold it.

title: great new option
text: I like this so much better than other car freshener options. The wood balls can be reused once the scent is lost, just soak them in essential oil for a couple of weeks. There are 2 sets so they can be switched out. The holder clips easily to an air vent so the scent gets dissipated. It is not over powering at all.

title: Classic look
text: These are so great to sit on after trying some full seat covers that just seem so bulky. These covers stay in place while looking clean and basic. They are easy to clean and I definitely recommend if you have a dog and a new car.

title: Cute touch too as to your car
text: I’ve never had anything but factory issued floor mats in my cars. These are so cute and give a personal, decorative touch. They are well made and seem durable. They should fit in most cars and trucks.

title: Nice way to get more storage
text: I tried a couple of these and this is my favorite. The mesh bag is better than one with a harder shell, it’s more flexible and keeps things in the bag. It gives you some extra room and a place to keep things that you don’t want on the floor, especially for a longer trip, you can put in water bottles, snacks, tissues etc.  It clips onto the driver and passenger head rest with 2 carabiners. And there is a velcroed loop that goes under the lid to the armrest to keep it snug. There are also two straps at the bottom with hooks. I don’t know what they are supposed to hook on. Perhaps it depends on the model of the car. There were no directions so I’d anybody’s guess. I could have googled it but it fits great as is and I’d very handy.

title: Not very helpful
text: This is only useful for a couple things. It’s a nice durable clip that will definitely stay on the visor. But it doesn’t clip things to behind the the visor only off of it. It’s kind of annoying because it gets in the way of the driver so you have to use the passenger side visor. Not particularly useful in my opinion.

title: I don't recommend these
text:
I am really not a fan of these. They are very nice and definitely durable, they would last for years and really protect your seats. They don't fit particularly well, I don't like the zipper at the top so the head rest fits through. It looks ugly. The head rest part was too small so I had to tuck them under. They don't fit the seat part well, I wouldn't like driving far with these. I'm almost certainly not going to use them. Also the instructions are not in English, there are photos but they aren't helpful. The back seat is a disaster, so many parts to get coverage, velcro everywhere to cover the middle seat.
It's nice that the back of the front seat covers have pouches since the one the car has are covered but they aren't deep at all.

title: good for basic coverage, excellent fit
text: After getting this, I got some full seat covers but they don't fit as well as this does. It doesn't have the same coverage or protection as a full seat cover but it definitely helps. It was super easy to put on and it fit great, very versatile. So I guess it depends on how much coverage you need on your car seats. I wasn't worried about wear and tear so much as dog fur. This helps a little. I think for full seat covers you  need something specific for your car. This cover would work in most cars.

title: Not so great
text: This was easy enough to install but it’s not very stable because of the low front, it is easy to tip over especially if you have a dog in the backseat who will bump it with his head to see what’s in it or to get to you. It looks very inexpensive as well. I’m going to try a mesh one to see if that works better not having rigid material.

title: Very handy
text: Does anything get as dusty as the black interior of a car? I have a new car that I’m determined to keep clean. I keep the smaller one just under my seat and it’s very handy and dust nicely. I actually use the longer one to reach the harder places in my house as I don’t need it for my car. It works great wet or dry.

title: Cleans well, lightweight
text: I am determined to keep my new car cleaner than I did my previous one. My dogs shed more when they travel and I took them on a visit yesterday so there was plenty to vacuum. This plugs in to the car socket. It has a few attachments but I found the brush one the best for the dog fur. This picked up all the fur and detritus that finds its way to the floor mats. My car looked like new. The cord is long enough that I could vacuum my trunk as well and I could take it around the outside of my car and didn’t have to go through the back seats. It comes with a brush and wand and a longer hose. I think the attachments are supposed to also attach to the hose but they don’t. But it is enough to reach ask the nooks and crannies. And it packs up nicely in a nylon bag that takes up very little room. I can even lint brush in the bag. This is just as handy and important as an emergency kit as I’m sure I will need this much more often.

title: Protects windshield from ice and snow
text: This came just in time for the snow and ice season. It’s nice to not have to scrape ice off my windshield in the morning. It has straps that are held in place by being shut in the front doors. It can be a bit picky to navigate when it is windy. It would be nice if the cover was a bit heavier as it usually is windy when it’s snowing. But this will be a nice time saver!

title: Very handy pack
text:
This is a fantastic kit. All 89 pieces fit into a small, easy to carry and easy to store canvas bag. It even has a small pouch of salt alternative ecotraction. I'm most happy about the jumper cables. I have an emergency kit that I put together a couple of winters ago but I never thought about the jumper cables which engine should always have. I like that this includes work gloves. I have an extra pair of heavy winter gloves but they wouldn't be useful if I had to use my hands. The safety vest is a clever idea as well as a safety rain coat. The flashlight recharges by squeezing a pop out plastic piece on the side.
All the things listed below really do come in the kit. There is a list in the bag that lets you know immediately what is in it so you don't have to dig through if it isn't included.
This would make a great gift for anyone with a car!

title: clever!
text:
I was excited to get this for review, especially as I live in upstate NY and I don't have a garage to keep my car in. Unusually, I've only had a couple of chances to use this. It works very well, though it did feel more comfortable in my left hand but that wasn't really a problem. It kept my hand warm and is long enough to keep from getting snow in my sleeve. Occasionally, we get really thick ice and I think I would be better off using this very heavy scraper I have because it takes two hands to get through that kind of ice. But 95% of the time, this scraper would be enough.
This would makes an awesome gift because it is so unusual but practical. I'm sure i will be using it a lot more in the next few months.

title: This is a great gadget!
text: I got this as a gift for my husband for Christmas. He was very skeptical when he pulled it out of the package but as soon as he set up his keys, he loves it! He has 2 keys that don't fit in it, our car keys. Still, he likes how compact it makes his keys and how easy it is to find the key he is looking for. It was pretty easy to set up and also easy to change up when necessary. This really is a great gadget!

title: Great tool for car lovers or people that aren't good with cars
text: This is just like every other OBD car code scanner out there. It works great and is relatively easy to use. It does not get all the codes that you could get at a professional level, but the the basic need to know what is going on, it works really well.

title: LOVE IT

title: Thin seat covers
text:
This review is for the Blue & Black color, Full Set Seat Covers (Front + Rear Seats).

I put the front seat covers in my 2021 Chevrolet Silverado Truck. I have a backseat organizer, so right now I only need the driver and passenger seat covers. The fit is tight but with patience, I was able to get the seat covers on.

For me, they are just okay. I use my truck for farm work in the warmer months, so sometimes I’m pretty dirty when I get in. The seat covers will keep me from getting dirt and grease on the driver’s seat, but I don’t see them lasting very long. I have a similar set of seat covers made from the same neoprene like material, and they tore in six months.

I wish the material was more heavy-duty, but for my use, the seat covers meet the basic need of keeping my seats clean. So even though they might not last for a long time, they are better than the makeshift towel I was using before.

title: Fits 2021 Silverado
text:
I’m using this GXT Steering Wheel Cover in my 2021 Silverado. The external diameter of the truck’s steering wheel is 15 inches, and this cover fits. It’s very tight so that it doesn’t slide on the wheel.

An extra set of hands to hold the top of the cover in place while you pull it over the sides and bottom makes putting it on a lot easier.

I’ve had the cover on my steering wheel for a few days now, using it with bare hands and winter gloves. The faux fur does shed a little, but it’s not slippery. My hands don’t slide at all. The cover does get cold when it’s cold out, but it’s not as cold as touching the steering wheel itself.

The cover does add a little bulk to the steering wheel, something to be aware of if you have smaller hands.

title: Tight on Silverado seats
text:
This set of camo seat covers from BDK is okay. I’m using the seat covers in my 2021 Silverado. The front covers are a little too small. They fit, but the seat back and seat cushion cover are stretched to their limit, so when I sit, I can’t fully relax into my seat.

The front seat covers have a styrofoam piece that’s supposed to fit in the gap between seat back and seat cushion. But the covers are so tight I can’t wedge the styrofoam piece in there, so I can feel it the whole time I’m sitting in the truck.

I was actually able to get the seat covers on without removing the headrests, which was nice. I don’t love that you have to cut holes for the backseat cover, but I can understand that makes the covers more universal.

title: Don't stay on hand very well; good for cleaning
text:
I’ve tried these Microfiber Wash Mitts from Maxshine inside my truck and house. They are quite handy for cleaning small and hard-to-reach areas, but don’t stay on my hand very well.

I suspect the mitts are sized for male hands. I have small hands (women’s size small gloves) and I end up putting my whole fist inside the mitt to keep it on. The opening and thumb loop are big and not adjustable. I think an elastic opening or thumb loop would work better for anyone.

The mitts worked well on the interior of my truck: air vents, cup holders, all the nooks and crannies that are really hard to clean. The mitts were also handy inside the house for dusting. The microfiber is soft, I like that I don’t have to worry about scratching anything delicate.

I tried washing one mitt, they are machine washable on gentle cycle, with low heat. I hung it up to dry, and the mitt came out great. It performed the same after laundering.

title: Useful cargo net
text:
I have the 4' x 6' size of the TICONN Cargo Net. That size of cargo net fits in the bed of my Silverado 1500, standard bed length.

I can stretch the net out to take up the whole length of the bed, or I can use just a portion of the net. The 12 carabiners give a lot of flexibility (pun intended) on where and how you can secure the net. I’m actually more limited by the bedliner in my truck, and where it has openings to access hooks.

Right now I have the net stretched across the bed, using it like a board to keep items from rolling to the front of the bed. It works great for this, and I like it more than a board. Because it has some flexibility, I can push bigger items into the space without having to remove the net. And if I have something really big, just unclip the net and I’m good to go.

The net does come with a somewhat flimsy bag for storage. I’m not sure I’ll ever be able to fit the net back inside the bag if I don’t need to use it, since it comes neatly bundled and tied up inside the bag.

For me, this is one of those things I never would have thought about, but now I really like it. The net is super handy to keep in my truck to use if and whenever I need to secure items in the bed.

title: Great for eating in the car
text:
I wish I had this car steering wheel desk two years ago! I can’t believe something so simple makes such a big difference, but it has really leveled up my eating-in-the-car game.

The desk hooks onto the steering wheel of my Chevrolet Silverado truck; I do not have any cover on the steering wheel. It’s very easy to put on and take off, all you do is put the desk behind the steering wheel and tilt the “hooks” on the open portions into the steering wheel. The desk wobbles a little, but it’s steady overall; I have cut chicken fillets on top of it.

The desk is all plastic, so it’s easy to clean with a wipe if needed. It’s easy to store, I just toss it in the backseat of my truck. It could fit into the pockets on the back of the driver or passenger seat, too.

title: Reduces capacity of cup holder
text:
The center console in my truck only has two cup holders, so I thought this Car Cup Holder Expander would help with my lack of cup holders.

I have a Chevrolet Silverado 21, this unit did fit into the cup holders. The base of it has cushiony foam pads sticking out the sides, they look like fins. I had to bend them to the sides to get the unit to fit, so it does fit tightly into the truck’s cup holders. However, the fins don’t reduce any noise; the thing rattles as I drive.

This unit reduces the capacity of the cup holder. I couldn’t even fit a 16.9oz bottle into the bottom cup holder, only 1½ inch of the bottle fits. That’s too little to keep a bottle or cup steady.

As for the top cup holder, it’s not steady either. The top cup holder has three “arms” that expand or contract to fit around a cup. But when I put a cup inside, the cup leaned so far to the side I thought it would spill or fall out while I was driving.

I didn’t realize, but you actually get two of the car cup holder expanders. This pack is potentially a good value, if you use skinny bottles or want to put smaller cups inside.

title: Don't fit truck seats
text:
I think the Easyhouse Car Backseat Organizers are best suited for cars. I have a Silverado truck and even with the strap extended to its full length, the bottom strap does not fit around my seat. Without both straps, the organizer flops around and against the back of the seat.

The full length of the bottom strap is 40 inches.

The construction is just okay. I tried pulling on the pockets, to see if they would hold up to kids stuffing them, and did notice some threads loosening at the first tug. I like that most of the pockets (6) are made of mesh, but I don’t think the organizers are super durable.

The organizers have a slight plastic scent that did not disappear after being left to air out for 2-3 days.

title: Clear Kleen Towels
text:
I’ve tried quite a few brands of microfiber towels now, but I was still pleasantly surprised by how thick the Clear Kleen Towels are. Every time I use one, I’m surprised by the thickness, since a lot of my microfiber towels and cloths are paper thin.

They are very absorbent! I’m not about to go outside and wash my truck in freezing weather, but I have tried the towels inside the house, for spills and drying other large items. They really suck up water.

I washed and dried one towel to compare it to the other, and there was no difference. The towels wash and dry just fine, you simply have to be conscious not to use fabric softener or the towels won’t work as well anymore.

title: CargoSmart Aluminum Straight Fixed Ramp with Treads
text:
I have a pair of wooden ramps for loading equipment into my truck. Sure, they’re durable and custom built by my dad, but boy are they heavy. When the box with the CargoSmart Aluminum ramps arrived, I couldn’t believe it was so lightweight! I can lift both of the ramps with one hand instead of staggering about with the much heavier wood ones.

I like the included safety strap on each ramp, to help keep them in place. The straps don’t require extra fiddling. The large tread design helps keeps item from slipping while loading them in the truck. If you’ve ever had a heavy item start going backwards, well, you’ll appreciate the treads.

These CargoSmart ramps are going to make my life so much easier, I wish I’d gotten a pair years ago instead of using brute force to load up equipment.

title: Heroway Headrest Hangers
text:
These Heroway Headrest Holders are something I never knew I needed but are super useful! A great way to increase room for shoppings bags or to keep your purse in place while driving.

The hooks fit tightly around the metal poles of the headrest. I had to yank to get them in place, so I feel pretty confident they won’t suddenly fall off.

Bags hung from the hooks don’t rattle about or slip off.

The bottle holder attachment for each hook has limited use; I’d personally prefer each hanger to have two hangers.

title: Trunk Organizer
text:
I’ve been on a storage bin kick lately. It’s so easy to find uses for them. Using one in the car was the next logical step.

This particular organizer has a lot of configuration options. Using the included dividers (which velcro into place), you can divide the bin into two, three, or four compartments. There are four mesh pockets along one long side, and also two pockets on each short side. There’s even an included top that velcros into place.

The construction is somewhat flimsy; I’m not sure how long the organizer will hold up over time. Despite being shipped flat, my organizer arrived with one side panel already bent. The density board in the description feels like cardboard. I was hoping I could use this organizer to carry in all my grocery bags at once, but I feel that I’ll bend it further if I do that.

title: ACDelco ACOF-933-BK Black Deep Dish All-Climate Rubber Floor Mat
text:
I’ve always used floor mats in my vehicles to help keep the interior clean. Even though my truck has a plastic floor, I put floor mats in it because I’m that careful. That said, I’ve been using the same pair of floor mats for about ten years and they were pretty worn.

Enter the ACDelco Deep Dish All-Climate floor mats! I was immediately impressed by how heavy they are. The rubber is thick and feels high-quality, with no rubbery odor. I feel pretty confident saying these mats will last me at least a decade.

While the mats are trimmable to fit your specific vehicle, I didn’t trim mine. They are a little large in my Silverado, but do not move or interfere in any way with driving. I barely remember they’re in the truck. The “deep dish” is 1” deep and will work well to trap snow or spilled liquids.

From the picture, I didn’t think the back mat would fit the width of a truck’s backseat. I haven’t had a back seat mat that’s one piece before. To my surprise, it was a great fit! I also tried the back mat in a Malibu and the fit was just as good. The back mat could be trimmed too, but I left it as is for a little extra protection.

title: AmazonBasics Car Windshield Sun Shade, Medium
text:
I leave my truck parked outside in the summer when I’m working, and we all know what that’s like. A sauna, which is just what I want after working on the farm. No thank you.

So I thought I’d try this AmazonBasics Sun Shade. The Medium is a good size for my Silverado.

I like that the sun shade folds up … but how in the heck are you supposed to stuff it back in the little pouch?! I wish Amazon had included instructions. Sure, I can YouTube a video, but c’mon, Amazon. Give me a clue.

The weather is acting like we’re still in the middle of winter in Ohio, so I’ll update this review as I use the sun shade over the spring and summer, to see how well it works and how it holds up to a lot of use.

title: Clear Vision Wiper Blade
text:
I was not impressed by this product. First the wiper blade was tricky to install, and the adapters all felt very flimsy and cheap, like they would break if I messed up the first time.

When I read the description, I thought the wear indicator would be a cool feature, but seeing it in person changed my opinion. It just felt like an added gimmick, and not actually that useful. It's bulky and cheapens the look of the wiper blade.

Performance wise, the blade just smeared rain on my windshield. I replaced it with a cheap blade that did a much better job at a fraction of the cost. I did receive one ACDelco blade free through the Amazon Vine program, but due to the poor performance and look, I would not buy the product.

title: Works Great!
text: Used this to inflate air mattresses at a campsite. Worked perfectly!

title: Hubby approved
text: Perfect for my husbands new C-5, since it doesn't have the cargo hooks he needed to use his net. Folds down when you don't need it, well made. Zero complaints!

title: Perfect size!
text: I love it, absolutely the perfect size to hold my registration and insurance info. Fits easily in my glove box without taking up a bunch of space.

title: Well made, but it's pretty big
text: Well made and looks just like the product pics. However, it is HUGE, like it will take up your glove box. I only need it to hold my registration and a copy of my car insurance. Keep the size in mind when ordering.

title: Love it
text: This is probably my favorite sun shade of all time. Can't help but smile every time I see it. It is a pain to try and fold up, but perhaps it just takes a knack and a bit more patience that what I have. Otherwise it works as expected.

title: Pricey upgrades
text: It works, but you only get basic info unless you pay for each module every year. I could understand maybe a one time fee for an upgrade but most of us don't need this a bunch of times a year. For the price I would have expected better functionality out of the box. I waffled between 3 and 4 stars because of the high price only giving basic info, but hubby said other than the modules it was very easy to read and use.

title: Size chart may not be accurate
text: We followed the chart and ordered a medium for my husbands 2018 Rav4 and it's way too small. There are gaps around it and the sun visors can't hold it in place. He's going to use it anyway because these things never last long and he gets a kick out of the googly eyes. I would suggest you measure your windshield and buy accordingly rather than go by their chart. We really should have gone with a large instead of a medium.

title: Very thin but works as needed
text: This is being used to keep dust and general garage dirt (and kitty paws) off my husbands old Chevy. For those purposes it is exactly what we need. It is very thin though and I don't think it would last long actually exposed to the elements. If you are looking for a lightweight cover to keep a car "cleaner" this is fine, for real protection you will want something a bit more substantial.

title: I think it helped... maybe?
text: This is one of those things where it is pretty subjective unless you have a seriously filthy fuel system. Hubby swears this made a difference, I am less convinced. Either way it didn't hurt anything. lol

title: Pleasantly surprised
text:
Hubby rolled his eyes when I handed him these to try out. He is an amendment Mother's brand user, I can't tell you how many times I've been called outside to feel how smooth the hood is because he clay barred it...

He used this on his old Equinox and the leather bit on my car because he doesn't have leather seats in his. I would say it did a nice job of perking stuff up but it didn't "restore" anything that was seriously aged. Also to be expected. The least effective was probably the headlight wipes. They clean, but the headlights weren't magically new again as the package claims.

It's a nice package if you have realistic expectations or the word "restoration" when it comes to a car care kit.

title: Great value
text: This is great quality for the price. I was half expecting a semi-disposable set (the kind the butt seam rips out on) but was nicely surprised by the quality. It's not the highest end, but great for changing tires or even just having to go out into the yard during the rain. It did run a bit big, even considering you wear it over other clothes, and was too long in the pants for hubby so he tucked into his rain boots (he is 5'9 and all torso though).

title: Worked as expected
text: So far no issues, it's doing what it's suppose to. I will update this review if that changes.

title: Bit of a pain to install, but worked well afterwards
text:
This is not like changing a light bulb to put it mildly. Maybe some cars are already fitted for these to go right in, but mine wasn't and it took more effort than hubby had thought it should. He prevailed and said the quality was there, but they were a pain in the butt.

They are much brighter than my old ones, which takes some getting use to but they aren't a bad set if you know how to install or have the patience to figure it out.

title: Super easy assembly
text: Assembled in under 5mins. Great little tray below to hold odds and ends. Do not prop bare feet up on it though, yeowch the edge is a bit sharp. Rolls really well and the seat was comfortable. Goes nice and low although I do wish it went up just a smidge higher. Overall a nice little stool for the garage.

title: Cools and keeps the sweat out of eyes
text:
Hubby was the guinea pig for this one, and he tried it both with and without a helmet.

Without a helmet it kept his head pretty cool. He treated it like one of those magic towel things but as a hat. Drench, wring, wear.... magically cool. When it heated to body temp he just popped it off, waved it around and put it back on. It stayed on really well, even running around the backyard playing soccer with the kid. He may or may not have tried to touch me with it. I may or may have not shrieked and ran, because sweaty wet skull cap, gross. We may or may not be in our 40s and still act like children...

Under his mountain biking helmet it didn't really do much to keep his head cool during his ride, but it did keep the sweat from running down his face into his eyes. He said he never really noticed how much the sweat bothered him until it wasn't there. So it'll be a new addition to his gear.

Bottom line he loved it, both with or without a helmet so a solid 5 stars from him.

title: Cleaning solution is good, but applicator is meh
text:
The cleaning solution is great, if that was all this review was covering it would be 5 stars. However the applicator is large, ineffective, and wasteful. We replaced the coils (actually, I taught my 20 year old daughter how replace the coils) but the idle was still rough and the code was still faulting at P0302. Turns out, in the end her spark plug in #2 was seized, and once replaced with this NGK, her car runs fine now. We still replaced all 3 engine coils in the top half of the block and all 3 spark plugs since we were at it.

As far as value ... local parts store wanted way more and all they carried was Autolite, which I do not care for.

My daughter's car runs smooth with these new plus (and coils) no problems and no more engine codes.

When I saw this I liked that I could keep it plugged in all the time and the open the app on my phone to run a scan.  That way I am not searching around for the port in the car in the dark.  I opened the app and it found the reader right away.  I knew this car had a small evap leak so I wanted to see if the scanner picked it up.  I attached a photo of that part of the report.  It saves it so I can always look at it in the future or show it to my mechanic.  The buttons in the app are nice and big and self explanatory.  I really liked this tool.

title: Nice and heavy duty
text: This is a very heavy duty cord.  Looks like it will last a long time.  I haven't tried it out in a campground yet but it looks like it will work for my needs.

title: Does not fit a Jeep Grand Cherokee
text: I had high hopes for these covers and since the listing says "universal fit" I ordered them for my Jeep Grand Cherokee.  Wow were they too small for the back of the seats.  I included a phot to show just how far I got to before I could go no further.  I am very disappointed.  The quality seems good and the color goes well in my vehicle but....

title: Has all the right compartments but is flimsy
text: I needed something more than an envelope, what I was using, to organize my car papers.  I thought this product might be a great replacement.  I just loaded everything up into it and it holds my 3 insurance cards, 3 registrations and my repair receipts.  However, it is pretty flimsy/floppy.  The photos in the listing make it look hardier.  So, it will do for now but it won't last long if I had to go in and out of it frequently.

title: Nice and light and easy to adjust
text: I got this step for my small RV.  I had a similar one in the past but forgot it in a campground.  Although they both looked the same this one is much lighter.  Being light is both good and bad.  Good in that it is easy to move but bad in that it may move around a bit more easily when I don't want it to move.  This one is much easy to adjust the leg height and to unfold the legs.  The little buttons are easy to press in.  This seems like an obvious thing but the other one took a lot of press-in strength.  Overall I am very happy with the height adjustment options on this and the overall functionality.

title: Alternative to Hanging Freshener
text:
If you're looking for an alternative to a hanging air freshener, the kind that suspend from your rearview mirror, you might find this to be a good option.
Was hoping it would be a little more sturdy, it's pretty cheaply made. But that's not entirely unexpected.
I'll probably stick to spraying an essential oil blend every once in awhile in the car.

title: Very nice SAE extension cable
text: If you want to extend your SAE solar cable/adapter then this cable is perfect for you.  I have an SAE outlet on my camper so I currently use an SAE to solar male/female but this setup will allow me to extend the SAE then attach it to my solar panel cables.

title: This thing is great!
text: I got this in order to add another awning when needed while camping.  I thought I could set it up on the car and sit undern there should the camper awning be full of sun.  This tailgate tent is so easy to setup.  It literally took maybe 3 minutes to get it up in place once I attached all the strings to the fittings.  The instructions are permanently part of the bag and easy to follow.  I was able to get a nice tight fit so as not to allow bugs coming in.  I don't use my car for camping but it would be great for someone that sleeps in their vehicle while travelling.  It is also just as easy to take down.  It worked so well on my car I thought I would try it on my camper than opens at one end like a tailgate.  It worked beautifully.  I highly recommend this tailgater for anyone that needs one.  It is well made, good instructions, fits easily back into the bag and easy to setup and take down.

title: Does not work on all interiro car surfaces
text: This product did OK with my leatherette but not with textured vinyl.  It did the best on smooth plastic like cup holders.  Not impressed.

title: They did a nice job on one surface and horrible on another
text: I was hoping this product would do a general clean on any interior car surface.  However, it did a nice job on my leatherette but on the vinyl did a horrible job.  I was actually shocked.  I think I will go with a better more general cleaner next time.

title: Multi-surface
text:
Most cars with a leather interior have a combination of leather and faux leather. This product can be used on both, as well as almost every interior surface.
It doesn't leave a greasy film, and the scent isn't overpowering. Sometimes citrus scented things wind up smelling like bathroom freshener.
This one isn't so bad.

title: Very nice easy to read gauge
text: I really like the size of this air gauge.  So many of them are small and compact but when crouching by the wheel traying to check it, especially in bad weather, it is nice to be able to quickly read the gauge.  It also feels nice and sturdy in my hand.  You can swivel it to match your view and it glows in the dark.  It's a keeper.

title: Nice Cargo net except but string adjustment is a hassle
text: I have a camper where I use nets like this on the ceiling to hold various things.  This net is nice and well made but it has these strings on the outside to give you yet another place to put things instead of unzipping it or jamming something above the net.  Its a nice idea but you have to adjust the strings so they are not too slack if you put something in there for the strings to hold.  That's fine but when you then try and stretch the whole thing across the ceiling, like I did, the end folds over from the pressure of the tightened strings.  Now I could spend a long time trying to balance the stretch of the entire thing vs the tightness of the strings but then....so I left it.  You can see in the photo what it looks like.

title: Great to have for that lone rivet that needs replacing
text: I use to do a lot of riveting building an airplane.  This is not that kind of rivet gun.  This is a cheap quick and dirty if you have a lone rivet to replace.  I recently got a new camper that has everything put together by rivets so I got this to carry should one of them pop loose.  It comes with a variety of size rivets, and corresponding dies,  which should meet everyone's needs.  It also includes a small wrench which has a slot in the tool itself for storage.

title: Works nicely on my RV step
text: I took a chance on this that it would work for my RV step.  It works beautifully.  There is only one slight wrinkle in the middle and that is because the curvature of the step is slightly off from that of the rug.  I used the same holes in all 4 places that it has and it keeps it on nice and tight.  I then folded my step away, as if I am getting ready to hit the road and there was room for the rug.  Since I only have one step I figure I have 2 spares should I lose one or it gets terribly dirty.

title: Nice netting with a zipper
text: I got this netting primarily to put up on the ceiling of my camper.  I used bungees for each corner and cut off the included straps.  It comes with a small bag to hang between car seats and I did that also pretty easily.  The large net has a zipper so you can store things within it but you can also jam some things in between the ceiling and the net.  It looks pretty sturdy.  I am not sure how strong the zipper is if I put heavier items inside.  All-in-all a very useful kit.

title: Very nice looking plush towels
text: I am really impressed with these towels.  They are very thick and have a plush feel.  They are also heavy.  I think they will absorb a lot of fluid.  They also look real nice with a different color on each side.  I actually got them for doing cleanups in my camper but I would definitely trust these towels to use them on my car and truck.

title: Tropical Punch?
text:
Don't worry, this car air freshener does not smell like an oyster, haha!
To me, it has more of a tropical punch fragrance. Something that has some berry and citrus, maybe a little peach. Definitely sweet. And definitely not a tuberose, vanilla and champaca, as claimed by the label.
It's aromatic enough to get a good wiff every time you get in your car.
I thought it was okay, my spouse has an allergic reaction to it.

The hang tag is a piece of stretchy cord, enough to go over your mirror. If you really like the fragrance, this could also be used in a closet to keep your clothes fragranced.
Because it contains fragrance oils, you don't want it touching any sort of plastic or upholstery. If you use it in a closet, I would make sure that it actually touch your clothes.

title: Nice sturdy material should make application easy
text: I got this window film to put onto my UTV.  My window is huge and when the sun shines it is almost blinding.  I want to just put a strip onto the top of the window.  This material looks nice and thick enough to be able to handle it without being a pro installer.  I have to wait till the weather is warmer to do it but this looks like it will work well.

title: Nice small battery
text: I got this battery to experiment with powering outdoor lights with solar.  This is a very small battery with low amperage so I can only do something small.  Deep cycle type is the best for solar.  I also got a battery bag to charge it in as you need to be careful with lithium ion batteries as they can explode/catch fire.  For me this price point was perfect as a start.  The battery is competitively priced.

title: A good trickle charger to keep on your vehicles
text: I use trickle chargers for my UTV over the winter because the cold and lesser use tend to lessen the charge on my battery.  This one is a very typical design for these types of chargers.  It is very simple to use and read.  Basically you can connect it to the battery via the clips or you can screw kit down to the terminals directly.  Either way, you can disconnect it from the charger if you'd like when not using the charger and leave the wires on the battery.  I do a more permanent setup on my battery and screw them down to the terminals.  It's nice to then be able to close my battery compartment and just let the wires stick out to connect the charge when I need to.  There are lights on the charger that tell you when it is charging and when your battery is fully charged and in maintenance mode.  Maintenance mode just means it is sending a trickle of a charge when needed to keep the battery charge level maintained.  If you should accidentally reverse the polarity when you connect it then that light goes on to warn you.  It also comes with a nice storage case.  Overall, for the money this is a good trickle charger to keep on your vehicles that are not used regularly enough to stay fully charged.

title: Very nice polishing pads
text: I do 3D printing of some metal filaments.  I then need to polish the item out of the printer.  I use solutions for this with paper towels.  Having these pads is much better as they also add some polishing power.

title: Nice idea but
text: I was hoping I was going to like this set.  I live in a rural area with some fierce storms so having different snow options inn each car is a must.  The idea of this set is that you can interchange some parts, scraper, shovel, brush, handle, with the main pole.  First problem is it took all my strength to push the button in far enough to attach anything to the pole.  This is fine when the weather is nice, like today, but if it is stormy and cold it will be even harder to do.  These pieces should go together easily.  Second, the shovel is a joke.  It is so small I would be out there in the weather much longer than need be trying to get enough snow to make a difference, should I be stuck in snow.  Even the emergency shovels are 4 times bigger than this shovel.  So in the end, I just attached the scraper at one end and the brush at the other.  It does have telescoping ability so I guess that is helpful.  For the price, you can buy a nicer brush/scraper combo that extends for less money.

title: Very nice riveter with a lot of features
text: I really like this hand riveter.  I have a lot of experience with riveters as I spent year building a metal airplane.  Millions of rivets later, I can say that this hand riveter is very nice and will serve me well for the occasional need to rivet. Most hand riveters will come with dies to handle  a few different size rivets.  I like that the head on this also rotates and pivots. It is also great that it comes with a case that holds the tools and the rivets.  Al-in-all for the price this is a bargain of a riveter with a lot of nice features.

title: Very comfy cushion

It comes with 2 hooks that you put behind the seat which keeps it in place.  No instructions came with the cushion.  I suppose you could really use it anywhere you want a nice cushy warm cushion.

title: Impressed by the features but has some glitches
text:
I have to say that I am not an expert on OBD2 scanners. I bought a simple scanner in the past and it works fine for clearing some common codes and giving me some basic information about the reason for the code. I use it when I get an engine light on the display. When I saw this scanner I could see by the description that it had many more features than my basic scanner.

WI-FI
The biggest one you see right away is Wi-Fi connectivity. This allows you to download add-on features from the Internet directly to the scanner. Since the first thing the scanner asks you, when you connect it to the OBDII connector in the car, is to connect to a Wi-Fi network that was also the first problem I had with the scanner. It could not connect to either of the networks I have at home. I regularly use Wi-Fi in my garage and the car sits between the house router and the garage so it shouldn't be a problem to connect. I had to turn on my phone hot spot to finally get it to connect. It then asks you to check for updates. It needed one so I started the download. The download stopped a few times having lost connection to the Internet. I just restarted the download each time until it completed. It showed four different apps that needed updating but since it took so long for the first one I skipped updating them for now. The device does come with a USB cable so I assume I could bring it into the house and power it up with that to be closer to my router.

Your Vehicle
It asked me to select the brand of vehicle. Mine was a U.S. Ford.

The MANUAL
The manual is pretty sparse regarding how to use the meter. It basically just helps you go through the screens.

THINKSCAN Plus
This is the main screen you come to. I selected OBD. It detected all the protocols available to see, It then showed the functions available to me. I opened the Live Data Mode. It showed me a lot of features about my truck that I could explore. I had the ignition turned on but not the engine. In order to see one thing that didn't require waiting for the engine to get to running temperature, I selected Engine RPM. I could see that what was on my gauge also showed in more detail in the meter. I was able to run a diagnostic report which would list any issues I was having and some basic info about the vehicle, like the VIN. I was given the option to send the report by email so I did. I received the email with a link to the report online.

Software add-ons
There was a button in the main menu for ThinkStore. Going there tells you that you can select 2 add-on modules for free. The rest of the modules are $29.95 each.

Resources
I could look up Fault Codes, get links for learning and to videos.

All-in-all I was a bit overwhelmed by the features provided so I believe the increase in price is worth it.

title: Worked great out of the box but instructions are few.
text: [[VIDEOID:aa6a6fb964bf5869148dd99d52181f55]] I am sure glad I got this tester as I found out my truck camper batteries were dead.  Before I tested my truck I tested my Jeep Grand Cherokee battery.  You simply put each clamp on the pos and neg terminals of the battery and the device comes on.  You hit enter then you get a couple choices: first, what type f battery...mine was an AGM; second is the amount of cold cranking amps. I then went to my diesel truck to test both batteries there.  That is when I found them dead.  I have included pictures of the printout and screens.  The instructions are not that great but the device is very intuitive,  I wish they included more info on the meaning of each measurement as I had to look them up on the Internet.  Overall I think it is a very worthwhile device.

text: I obtained this winch because I wanted a 2-speed winch t replace my 1-speed.  My raft is only 100lbs but pulling it out of the water uphill takes a lot of strength with a 1-pound winch.  This is the winch I needed.  It is very sturdy and I would recommend it.

All the pieces are very sturdy and heavy and I don’t they will be harmed by my heavy truck camper.  I would highly recommend this product.

title: Very heavy duty
text: I obtained these to carry in my UTV for times when I gut stuck due to mud or snow.  They are heavy and seem to be able to stand a lot of beating.  I would highly recommend this product.

title: Good price

title: Big Dogs? No Problems!
text:
As you can see, this car seat cover fits my Grand Cherokee Summit but does leave some gaps. That's okay because I wanted primarily for a little protection when I take my dogs to the dog park or to the lake.
No doubt about it, it's durable. Heavy duty construction, and paw prints wipe up in a jiffy. Looks a lot better than my previous canvas cover.
Takes no time at all to put it on. Very straightforward.

title: Eats the Crumblies
text:
I was considering cleaning the nooks and crannies of my car with a toothbrush, but then saw this product.
It's a cross between a gel and silly putty.
Does it work?
It grabbed on to all kinds of crumblies, not just vent dust. Just keep going until it's more dirt than jelly.
Fantastic invention.

title: Sturdy
text:
Living in a log cabin, with neighbors few and far between, you really have to learn to be self-sufficient.
We've started investing in certain tools and some basic things for getting us out of a jam. This certainly qualifies. It's one of those things that when you need it you need it.
It was a good value, very sturdy for the price.

title: Bring it with
text:
This wash made our RV sparkle, and removed dirt, bugs, and bird droppings with minimal effort.
Unfortunately, we had parked too close to some trees and got some sap drops that needed solvent.
Still, it worked well on everything else, and I like that a little goes a long way, and it cleans safely.
The small bottle is the right size to bring with us.

title: Easy Spray
text:
This was used on our boat trailer, which was just uncovered and cleaned after a winter under plastic.
It comes out like a paint spray mist.
Although our outdoor gear doesn't take the beating it would in salt water areas, it's still gets rust and corrosion.
A couple of coats after detailing or even just a good cleaning helps protect all kinds of gear prone to rust damage.

title: No Mess, No Musty
text:
After being closed up all winter, our sailboat has all of the funk you'd expect from a less than new boat.
To make matters worse, the main stateroom has the original mattress, which is haunted by human funk, or at least my sensitive nose says.
While I wasn't crazy about the semi-floraly 'Figi' scent, it did make the boat more liveable and definitely less musty.
Pop, vacate, return and open 'er up.

title: Toddler Clean Up
text:
If this were just a little bit more inexpensive it would gain a star.
I found it to be too big to be in the car all the time unless stored in the trunk, and if it's in the trunk, it's just as easy to get the cordless dust buster from the house.
However, if you have toddlers, it's nice for fallen bits of Cherrios and such. When tested with dog hair, my cordless does better.
If you catch it on sale and you want one in the car all the time, it could work for you.

title: Terrific for touch ups
text:
We have a lot of leather furniture. In the living room alone, there are two couches, a chair, and two ottomans of leather. Leather is a great choice if your dogs are allowed on the couch but you don't want to sit in a pile of hair. If you have asthma, leather furniture is a good option because they don't attract hair and dust the way fabric will.

On the bad side, there is the occasional paw print. These wipes are fantastic for cleaning leather furniture in between the once a year cream cleaner. They remove surface dirt without drying, and you can't beat the convenience of a wipe

title: Ahhhhhh
text:
With a sailboat that's closed up during the winter months, the musty smell can be pretty strong.

OK, it can be downright vile.
I bought this slow release formula right after opening her up for the season, and it has definitely taken the foul factor down a notch. I confess that last year I also had a holding tank issue.
Much better smelling now.

title: Easy Way to Save the Seats
text:
With an American Water Spaniel that is a working flushing dog, the back seat always has a mish-mosh of old blankets and towels in the back seat.
As her DNA dictates, she is in and out of smelly lake water. My poor car was smelling like a swamp.
This cover is the best thing since sliced bread. It totally covers the back bench by slipping it on the headrests and folding down.
I still put a towel back there, but no more smelly seats...this cover washes down beautifully. A quick spray with an enzyme cleaner and wipe. The car smells like a car again, instead of my hard working girl!

title: 3D Squeak
text:
After my 3D printer started sounding like it had printed off a mouse, complete with the squeak, I knew it was time for a dab of this stuff.
High quality lithium grease. No more mouse. Great stuff to have around.

title: Multi-device Charging
text:
If you have a low wattage electric item that you like to bring on road trips, a power inverter is one heck of a nifty thing to have.
Not only can this one handle all your small devices that charge via USB, it can accommodate a small fan or any low watt 120 item.
Good thing to have in your emergency preparedness bag, too.

Product received to test, with the option to review.

title: Need Room? No Problem
text:
A few years ago I used and reviewed the [[ASIN:B003NBFKDK Highland 1042000 Hitch Mounted Cargo Carrier]]. It was a little disappointing although did the job.
This Curt carrier is little more expensive but a lot more solid. This is going to hold a lot more than a few suitcases.
Under an hour to install, and then it was time to test it on the road.

We loaded it with cargo that we estimate was about 200 pounds.
I hate pulling the boat or anything on a trailer, using this is like nothing at all. No difference in driving even when loaded down, no excessive sound or rattle, either.
In the fall it will be used while hunting, I'm confident it will be perfect for bringing game home.

title: Proud of Your Wheels?
text:
You'll love this.
Does it work?
Yes and No.

Application of this product is pretty straightforward. Put it on, let it sit, buff it out.
While that might seem easy, it is actually fairly time consuming. If you are one of those people that spent a fortune on custom rims, and a great day is buffing and polishing, this might be a joy for you to do, but for me it was a chore. A big chore.
It does exactly what it says it will do, it shines like crazy.
However, in my opinion, it doesn't really resist dirt after application.

If you are a car geek, you just might love this stuff, for most others it might be overkill.

title: Bring On the Flood
text:
We live on an island, connected by a small bridge. Once or twice a year, after heavy rain, the bridge floods and only those with trucks and ATVs can get on and off the island.
If we know it's coming, we park my truck on the other side, and use the ATV to ferry across.
Some neighbors are stuck, so we attach a cart and pick up mail and groceries.
To be honest, it's pretty fun!
The straps are easy to connect and disconnect with simple but strong clips.
Usually we use an extra rope for emergencies like floods. This is much better given the easy clips. Best of all, given that I can be all thumbs, there is no need to have to figure out the best knots to use.
It is also easy to store and doesn't take up much space.

title: Seal the Deal
text:
If you spend all that time and energy getting your car just right, it never fails. Either a bird leaves a little calling card or you accidentally park under a tree that is dripping sap.
I like this product because I know that all my work isn't entirely in vain.
Spots lift off of your car much easier after an application of this stuff. After testing a number of products from this brand, I'm quite pleased with the quality and performance.

title: Great Company, Great Product
text:
This is a battery tender (keeps it charged) for a Deltran Battery Tender's line of Lithium Iron Phosphate batteries.
These batteries are designed to replace Flooded, AGM, and Gel cell lead acid batteries in power sport applications such as ATVs, SeaDoo type watercraft, scooters, motorcycles, etc...any vehicle or watercraft that has a compatible Battery Tender battery.

This is a family owned company. Last year (2013) they started producing high output Lithium Iron Phosphate (LifePO4) Batteries and Battery Chargers.

To me, this is what makes me have a LOT of confidence in the product as well as the integrity of the company...California has some of the most rigid and strict laws in the country for safety and efficiency of consumer goods. We have all seen 'not shippable to CA' on certain products.
The following is from the Battery Tender website:
"Starting in 2013 all non-commercial battery chargers manufactured after February and sold in California must conform to the new “Appliance Efficiency Program” in coordination with the California Energy Commission.
