title: Impressive
text:
I bench tested the charger output across a range of programmable power supply conditions for advertised charge output functionality based on reviews. The charger inserts itself in a feedback loop between the battery and the charger's uP control. The uP firmware reacts with both amp and voltage output and adjusting to a firmware version of an optimized charge.

To be clear, there is no solution for answering the most important question, "How much longer will the battery last?". It's a great opportunity for someone to patent a device where the battery physicists can't find an answer. As a physicist, my answer is consistently, "Buy the next battery the same day this one goes out of warranty". The warranty life is statistically based on the results of design life testing of large sample lots. For any specific battery ... buy a new one the very day it runs out of warranty.

The system performs as advertised. The charger becomes a component in a closed-loop feedback cell when attached to the battery. That's a step function improvement over the old-school trickle charger.

My use is deep cycle marine batteries. These are different from car batteries. A deep cycle marine battery encounters all sorts of more complex transient and parasitic situations. In the worst case and through a series of unfortunate events, you can dissolve your aluminum boat in the water, pit the prop or sacrifice the season's sacrificial plate overnight.

Sophisticated, value for money charging system. Works great with marine batteries. It should work better on your car's battery. The best car battery solution is to buy a new battery on the day the warranty expires.

title: Aircraft fastening tech for DIY projects
text:
Excellent value.

The rivet nut (rivnut in the parlance) is a blind bolt fastener. A brief application note to the unfamiliar.

Rivnuts are installed from one side through pre-drilled holes without having or requiring access to the other side of the work to complete the interference fit nut lock in place. Hence the name 'blind bolt' fastener. Blind bolts and a quality pre-drill deliver inherent high tensile and shear strength to the structure. No wallered out pre-drill holes is a prime objective. I've been popping the range of blind bolt fasteners since I was a kid in Dad's hobby aircraft hangar. Now honestly, in aircraft, blind bolt fasteners come in several unique varieties. Rivnuts are both wonder and curse ... time and dew point excursions mean corrosion that will rot the blind joint flange off, which promptly falls into the frame structure and must be removed for FOD control. In the aircraft application, installers require training and certification. That's a brief intro regarding where and why these fasteners evolved.

In sheet metal, HVAC, vehicle structure, and wood projects, the rivnut is an excellent DIY solution to complicated fastening problems when you can't easily access the other side of the work, time for the rivnut.

Amjoy is a name brand in the technology. This Amjoy Rivet Nut Tool with a 16'' lever handle is a typical configuration and priced for DIY home use. Rivnut tool and die set price is directly related to precision tolerance requirements. You will see this same tool and die configuration priced >$1K for those applications.

Great tool & die set at a great price. Real value.

From that curiosity, I went to looking for the `optimum' plug at the best price for my latest plug change. There are cheap, middle and premium plugs to be considered. If you are going to spend the time on the knuckle-busting job of changing the plugs, why not put the 'best' plugs in?

Iridium plugs trump platinum plugs simply from iridium's place on the periodic chart of elements. I considered the `super-premium' plugs that incorporate mini-subsystems that can run up to $25 a pop. The high dollar, mini-system plugs incorporate inherently superior spark dynamics in the ignition cycle. But, on deeper consideration after checking the engine specs on-line... your vehicle's OEM computer will suppress these advantages in the 'greater' vehicle combustion optimization equation ... super-plugs require a super, non-OEM computer, to unlock the plugs capability. The high dollar, super-plug will be dumbed down by the OEM vehicle's computer.

So, I went the middling route for my Lincoln Navigator by shifting my electrodes one element left in the periodic chart and looked for the least expensive plug in that category. I watch fuel consumption and was amazed that these plugs upped the mileage over 10%. There are just not that many ways to get a real 10% improvement in mileage.

5-star ... the results exceeded my expectations. I received all 8 in one order. The odd-number purchase problem another reviewer provided must have been corrected.

There is nothing about this product that makes it worth buying over paper towels. In the pictures I am posting, I spill only 1/4 cup of water onto a tray. Once I drop the tablet, it expands a bit and stops. The rest of the cleanup (the vast majority of it, in fact), requires you to squeeze out the cloth and soak things up numerous times. Only for 1/4 cup.
My suggestion? Just carry a few extra napkins from the fast food place that gives you too many. It's as effective as this, and hardly takes up more room. Or you can buy a gimmicky cloth-paper towel.

Lastly, I see some people said they use them for washing their/others' hands or faces. I'm not sure how, since the hard little tablet requires water to soften and become an underwhelmingly skimpy towel. You'd do either of the following:

a) wash your face/hands, then dry with InstaCloth by rubbing your face with the hard little cylinder until it expands into a crumpled, starchy towel, and finally into --tadaa!-- a tiny porous washcloth much like the disposable face wipes that foam when you wet them. Sans the foam/soap. Or the convenience of an already expanded cloth

OR

b) you wet the InstsCloth first to make it into a washcloth type device, then do the whole soap thing, using the "cloth" to scrub, and then use something else to dry up. Unless you plan to rub a second pellet (aka option "A")

Yep. Still useless.

I see there are a lot of hiking applications out there. Maybe there is some use specifically for hikers that validates this superflous novely item's existence. I doubt it, but I'm not a hiker, so I can't say. If you're not a hiker (and possibly even if you are), this ranks among the most unnecessary products around.

title: It works but there are QC issues.
text:

Decided to open it up, maybe something came loose in shipping. That might be the case but the contact inside the inverter for one of the plugs came completely out of its seat. Normally those contacts are held in with tension or a detent - not on this, it came in and out of the seat with ease. The internal cable was connected to it so I put some glue on the seat and tried it out again. That seems to have fixed it, though I still had some problems with the contacts in certain positions.

Because of the lack of QC, I can't recommend it. The price is right, it works and it will be used infrequently but you shouldn't have to repair it straight out of the box, even at this price point.

However, if you need to do any kind of maintenance of batteries on an ongoing basis, this is a dream come true.

I immediately hooked up several LiFePO4 Lithium Iron Phosphate Deep Cycle batteries to mine, as I use them to run my outdoor solar and water pump system. With this 4 bank battery charger I'm able to keep a rotation of 4 batteries in, 4 batteries out for when my solar system needs maintenance, or simply when I want to keep the batteries 'up to spec' on cloudy days.

The genius thing about this is the fact that it is wet-rated as well as useful for reviving dead batteries just as much as maintaining good batteries. Because of this, I can mount this in my out building that is subject to higher moisture levels than the garage and not worry about it functioning day in and day out.

The thermal sensor helps keep batteries safely charging and will automatically cut out if things approach dangerous levels. For example, I was charging a battery on a sunny day last week and this device was able to properly shut the power to the charge when it began to overheat. Excellent.

If you need to charge several batteries, this is the one you want.

title: Easy and effective!

Installation was easy enough, I chose my size by measuring the distance between my bars and it fit within the range advertised.

When the item came it has a weather strip along the top that is cut to size and then two pieces of free strip. The instructions are mostly pictures, but they insinuate that you need to cut the extra strip to size to fit the inside diameter of your bar (between the anchors) and then additional space on the ends.

To accomplish this, I attached the bars and centered them and tightened them so I had an equal portion hanging in each side. I then measured the internal space and outer space and then cut my strip to size. I then hit an obstacle which was that the end caps take up some of the channel space, so substract the distance of those from your overall trim space.

Once I got through the rough cuts, it was quick enough to tighten down and install and it looks great!

title: Solves  A Smelly Problem
text:
My brother has three problems: a fast food addiction, a stinky dog and a car that is always in the shop. As a result he frequently borrows my car leaving me with one problem: a gross, smelly car. I thought I would give this product a try. The plastic device is easy to set up. simply press to open the cover. Peel the foil off the scented oil pack and insert. Close the cover, adjust the intensity to your liking. there are three choice: low, medium and high. Plug into the vehicle's 12 volt adapter. The device lights up and fragrance slowly builds.

The device itself worked well. The fragrance masks rather than removes the odor. I am somewhat sensitive to smells but the lowest setting resulted in an acceptable level of scent. The scent I received was "Hawaiian Breeze". I have never been to Hawaii and suspect that unlike this oil it doesn't smell like the candy aisle in the Dollar Store. In any event, it smells more like bubblegum than when "cool ocean winds meet the scent of fragrant tropical fruits, pineapple, and plumeria". I will definitely try a fragrance sachet more to my liking than this one. However it does work with a minimum of fuss and muss and remedies the problem.

I can't speak to how long it lasts but so far it seems to be doing the job. It is good for pretty much any metal object that is exposed to the outdoors not just trailers and boats.

title: Messy But Somewhat Effective

But if it is providing UV protection, that is a worthwhile benefit in and of itself. It seems to protect more than restore and it does seem to repel dirt and dust. If your expectation is to prevent further environmental damage, you will be satisfied with this product. The treatd areas looked better but no different than had they just been washed and waxed.

I do like that it is made in the USA. Thus far, I am neutral on this product. I can't say that the car is performing any better but it certainly is not performing any worse. Absent a drastic change for the better, I don't know that I will continue using. It can't hurt to try and it would be wise to consult a knowledgeable mechanic as well as your owner's manual.

title: More of a Project than I Anticipated
text:
I thought this would be a quick and easy solution to muffling the rattles emanating from a 1998 ford. I was wrong. The product is a fairly hard black vinyl with an adhesive back. Designed to be used on metal surfaces, it must be applied when temperatures are higher than 40 degrees farenheit. The surface must be thoroughly cleaned. The mat may be sized by cutting with scissors or in my case an exacto knife.
The backer is removed and the mat is positioned. Then ideally, the mat will fit securely and the offending noises muffled. If necessary you may use a blow dryer or heat gun.

Sounds great. But it isn't quite so easy. First, it being winter in NY, I had to wait until the temperatures rose. I had planned to use this in a door. But the material is inflexible, cuttable, but still inflexible. Worse, I couldn't get it to stick in position. So I wound up taking it off. My brother then took the remainder for the back floor of his suv. He had better luck getting it to stick using a heat gun. He is satisfied with its noise muting capabilities.

This product was not for me. Unless you are adept at accessing the offending parts and fairly handy, this requires significantly more work than the package suggests. When properly applied, it does seem to work. I wonder if the adhesion is effected by heat as well as cold. Obviously, the material becomes more brittle in the cold and does not adhere. Conversely, in high summer heat, does it melt or become gooey? I dodn't know. I think the product can perform adequately but unless you are experienced with this type of installation, I would pass.

Instead of using paper as recommended to feed the loops between the (very small) frame and the windshield gap, use some electrical tape. Where it calls for paper, Double a 24” length over on itself through the elastic loop to make the tape it stick to itself.  This will give you a thin, flexible and durable 12” feeder “tail” to fish through that little windshield gap. Then, when you’ve brought it around and fastened the elastic loop to the “hook” on the inside of the shade, a quick little trim with a scissor will easily release the electrical tape and you’re all set!

title: Excellent Kit
text: I purchased this kit, along with about eight others all from this designer.  Unfortunately I did not purchase them from Aamzon as I found them less expensive on another site, even when I paid shipping. I have finished about three of the kits and each one is excellent in quality and punches up exactly as the picture.  The background fabric is a very nice close weave, almost linen-like in appearance which punches very smoothly and neatly.  The designs are printed in the booklet of instructions for you to iron-on yourself.  I found I could iron-on the design at least twice, both times getting a nice clean and easily visible print.  The fabric is sufficient in size to stamp the design twice.  If you are new to needle punch the instructions are well written and clear and will guide the beginner to a beautiful finished project.  About the only negative I would comment on is that the floss, while sufficient to finish the project, is not quite generous enough to have much of anything left over on completion.  They obviously counted quite accurately when it came to floss requirements, not leaving any room for error.  I would like to have seen at least one strand remaining just in case there was some type of mistake.  They do, however, identify the floss colors by number so you could supplement with DMC floss if you found yourself in a position of being short flossed.  Overall this kit is excellent in all respects and I would highly recommend it for anyone who wanted a cute, quick needle punch project.

title: This restored badly faded brown leather to match the original
text: I could no longer find my favorite styles of my old boots and clogs.  One of my clogs celebrated 19 year anniversary in my shoe case. Very well constructed and functionally the pair is still going strong, but sadly they needed a lot of cosmetic lifts.  I used to wear them to work, but for the last 4-5 years I am only wearing in my yard as a garden shoes. The upper leather lost its original color of rich brown, and it's got scratches everywhere.  I decided to try this on, but I did not expect the entire tone blends well. I wiped the surface with water, then cleaned with dish detergent, wiped dry with paper towel and left the shoes outside for an hour to completely dry. I painted this conditioner with a piece of cloth, and I knew immediately that this would restore the beautiful brown leather once again.  The tow area and some upper was faded to beige and the side and back still had dark brown . The liquid was absorbed instantly and on coat brought the top and tow to look more brown than beige.  After I dried the shoes for a couple hours outside I applied the second coat.  This time I did it only the area needed more darkness.  Another hour of drying. Then I did the final coat entirely.  This time the shoes looked evenly brown and the originally dark area did not look any darker that it was, but the faded areas. I was so happy that I am now able to wear them to public again.  I would not say they look like brand new, but more than decent condition!!  I need another color now to restore my boots.  Thanks!

title: Great selection of high quality clips.
text:
I don't know about you, but I have rarely (if ever) removed one of these clips for various maintenance on my vehicles and been able to feel comfortable that they will ever be quite right again. Most of the time, I've truly felt the need to replace them.

This kit eliminates that worry. No longer do I have to worry about somehow ruining the integrity of the original and "hope" that it will work as intended. Simply replace the part.

I was concerned that these might be sub-par in quality compared to the originals, but that doesn't seem to be the case at all. Looking through the set gave me the confidence to use them without any worry. I honestly haven't seen any noticable difference in design or quality. Every one has fit and functioned just as intended with very positive engagement. No slop here.

The cases keep everything very well organized and identified. You won't be wondering if you have the right part. There is an adequate quantity of each of the fasteners, so most people likely won't run out anytime soon... if ever. The kit also comes with just about every fastener removal tool that you will need along with cable ties and washers. Looks like they have thought of everything.

In all, this is all the kit I will likely need. It's nice to have the peace of mind that I won't be scrounging around for a replacement part because I've ruined the original. For this reasonable price, I consider it cheap insurance.

text:
This is a great little kit for personal use or as a gift. It contains most everything you will need on a regular basis to keep your vehicle looking its best. I especially appreciate the extension handle for reaching spots like the roof of our Durango.

I like that the kit comes with a glove and a sponge, so that I can recruit "help" from my young sons. The variety of different brushes, from the heavier duty wheel brush to the more delicate detailing brushes, allow you to reach all those little nooks and crannies that a sponge just can't get to. The microfiber towels do a great job diying everything off once you are finished. This is really important here where we live since there is a noticable amount of calcium and minerals in the water, which will most assuredly leave water spots if left to air dry.

While the bucket is somewhat functional, I find that I prefer a regular bucket for actual use during washing and for hang'drying the towels when done. It will hold water, but it's easy to kind of collapse the side at various times. That's not to say that the bucket is not functional. Overall, I am very happy with this kit. I have zero regrets about getting it and actually wish I had done so earlier. It's a great value and very functional.

title: Just What I Wanted
text:
I was looking for a decent inverter to use while camping and on road trips and this one fit the bill at a price I was willing to pay. I've given it 4 stars because the plastic construction seems a bit cheap, but it feels reasonably sturdy and, barring any unforeseen circumstances, I think it will last for quite a few years.

For installation, I found that it fit perfectly into the opening exposed by removing the pull-out cupholder in my 2003 CR-V and with some head scratching, more than a little cussing, and a few hours work was able to run a section of 4 gauge wire from it, through the firewall, to the positive terminal on my battery. I grounded it to a piece of metal inside the central console with a much shorter section of the same wire. While I've not pushed it anywhere near its limit thus far, I feel fairly confident that I could get the full 400 watts out of it with this setup.

Some things to keep in mind about this product (and some things that others clearly did not, based on other reviews):
1) This is not a pure sine wave inverter (the price tells you that), and that comes with certain caveats. If you're uncertain what that means (as I was), do some research before buying to decide if the cons of being a modified sine wave inverter are worth the much lower price.
2) To get the full potential out of this inverter, it should be connected directly to the battery. Don't expect to plug it into your accessory outlet and pull 400 watts. The accessory outlets in most cars are protected by a 10 amp fuse: 12 volts x 10 amps = 120 watts maximum. If you don't know what any of that means, again, do some research.
3) If you do run it to the battery, use at least 4 gauge wire. Yes, it's a thick wire and it can be a pain to work with within the confines of a car, but you can't expect to pull 400 watts of power from your battery with doorbell wire.
4) This thing is only converting your car battery's 12 volts DC to 120 volts AC, thus it only works as well as the battery it's connected to. If your battery is in less than stellar condition, don't expect the full 400 watts.
5) If connected directly to your battery, this inverter will be able to pull power whether your car is on and charging the battery or not. The on/off switch will keep it from draining the battery while not in use, but if you're using it for something that uses a lot of power, it's not a bad idea to turn your car on.
6) If you're buying this to power something specific, check to make sure it's powerful enough before you buy it. Everything that uses power should have information on it that will tell you how many volts (V) it uses and at how many amps (A). Multiply the two to get watts. To give you an idea, hairdryers, vacuums, and the like generally start in the 1000+ watt range.
7) Finally, if any of this doesn't make sense to you, do your research. A little time asking questions on the product page, googling, and even watching YouTube videos of other people installing similar inverters will save you a lot of headaches when you go to do it yourself.

title: On F3 Spyder, Instable in Corners
text:
This review is specific to the CanAm Spyder, and my model is the 2018 F3 Limited. First, I struggled giving a 3 because this product is what is proposes to be, I received a decent quality product like the one shown, no surprises, and it mounted quickly and easily.

For what you get the price is a little bit high in my opinion, but I knew the price and I was satisfied.

The comfort and adjustments are as advertised. It solved the monkey butt problem I seeked to solved.

The first problem is that the F3 is a handling version of the Spyder... I like to drive aggressively. The seat raises you and therefore your center of gravity, and I noticed it right away... very negative. But that alone would not make me downrate this product, because of course this could be expected from the product as presented.

The real problem is that you lose all butt grip, and the top rolls over the bottom of the airhawk and gives it a shifty slide of 1-2". That instability takes away so much confidence in hard cornering and can even be dangerous when it lets go for that 1-2". The way a Spyder work you really need to squeeze and have a solid anchor in the center, just like with a wave runner. If you are familiar with wave runners, this same kind of lack of confidence can come from a big wet bathing suit that prevents you from having a confident seat in a hard corner, but on a wave runner, even then you can do some spirited cornering with your butt off the seat, something I have not yet found advisable on a Spyder.

My guess it his Airhawk serves its purposes for touring minded RT Spyder drivers. For me, I simply cannot use it, and now I understand my only route is a seat updrade or putting up with monkey butt.

title: Had one for G1, now for G2 Ridgeline
text:
I had the trifecta signature on my G1 Ridgeline for 5 years and it held up beautifully and was always easy to handle.

So I decided to go with the same for the G2. I am not quite as happy with this one as the first. A few differences: the handles that snug down the gate side are cheaper and operate more strangely. The canvas seems different not in a great way but I will wait for some sunshine to judge it more.

The rails and the cover do not seem to seal well, especially compared with the G1. However, one of the reasons I took the savings with this lower cost cover is that I was never concerned about bone dry... I never had any concerns with the G1 trifecta even though it was not a perfect seal. Here the side rails do not make great contact in the middle of the bedsides where the Ridgeline seems to have a mild deflection. The contact at the cab side is far less confident than it was in the G1, but again this is an area where the natural drains are so I am not too worried about it yet.

Aesthetically this is not as good a fit as the G1 either. It seems to sit a little high and it does not look great where it meets the gate spoiler.

Installation is very easy and requires only a T50 adapter. If you do not receive side rails, stop and do not try installing.

Know that there are many options out there (so many reviewers point to this vs. Honda OEM, but there are so many other options). This will serve me well enough and justifies the price point, but I am not certain why some of the changes like the securing handles. title: Nice but Bigger Change than Expected...
text:
You know these by now of course, look and feel great like a quality product. Very easy install, but be aware the rubber glue hardens up in mere seconds, so get that left grip in the proper position pronto. Wish Kuryakyn would throw in a 10-cent hex key for the caps, as it is a pretty small size, but you do not need it for installation.

Am sure I will get used to it, but the thicker grip actually made my hand numb up throttle side (my twin is a shaker). A lot of it I think has to do with where my thumb lands now, with a rubber pad now pushing in right under my thumb inside middle knuckle and catching vibes, whereas on smaller grips my thumb was pretty much clear of the grip with only the very inside of the larger thumb knuckle putting some pressure on. Have a little more trouble with gas and brake alternating in stop and go traffic as the grip takes up more of my hand so I seem to have a little less reach for the brake. The rubber pads don't seem to quell vibration, maybe just for grip. My grippy gloves get a little grabby with these too, and yesterday when it was very hot, sweaty hands in the gloves definitely contributed to a feeling of less throttle control (sweaty hand slip slightly inside the glove, the glove grabs the iso rubber and tweaks it slightly differently than intended... mind you, this is all pretty subtle but so is every throttle input). I point out all these things because I had not read about them before...

I still give four stars and do not at all regret the change as all these things I think I will adjust to in time. The geometry of thicker grips would suggest you get slightly more displacement for the same rotation, so should have more throttle control. Still, am going to add slightly more throttle slack and will need to lessen my own hand gripping considerably which ought to be a good thing, but was a little surprised these were not more comfortable than my old grips right out of the box.

title: Home run on this product!
text:
Ever since Amway came out with biodegradable products 40 years ago, the market has continued to expand it that direction. I have used numerous products over the years that really were gentle on my skin, but still did a great job. 3M makes some great products.

Well I had a big project this summer in a home shop. Metal shelving that had not been cleaned in 20 years. Oil, grease, split lawn chemicals, etc.... With the exception of lawn chemicals (because THEY are the problem when cleaning them up), I just sprayed, let soak in, and wiped up. NO gloves. Oil, grease, dirt (old, old dirt) and grime just came up without a fight. I was very impressed that there were no fumes, or issues with the product in contact with my hands. A few times I even sprayed my dirty hands with the product and then used a clean cloth to wipe off the product. Perfect.

I liked the fact that is was super safe to use, and it did the cleaning job it promised. Get some if you have a dirty mess to clean up.

title: not best choice for equestrian usage
text: I used the cleaner and conditioner on my horse’s bridle and my leather boots. The design is neat, and I suppose it would work on a large, wide surface, but on a one inch wide one (the bridle), I often found myself scraping the plastic edge on the leather itself. It was better on the tall, leather boot in terms of not scraping the leather so much, but when I pressed down harder, hoping to pick up dirt, I would inevitably scratch the boot with the plastic part as well.  The cleaner got VERY sudsy, so much so that I had to put it down and work the suds into the leather with my hands and then even wipe the suds off with a towel. The conditioner was just the opposite. I couldn’t tell whether it was working at all and bounced it against a hard surface several times to try to get the conditioner to come out. It did, but it was still hard to tell if it was covering the leather. If I pushed too hard on either the cleaner or conditioner, the sponge collapsed to nearly nothing, and I again was scraping the leather with the outer plastic shell. Both the boots and the bridle dried to a dull matte finish rather than a cleaner looking sheen. They felt fine to the touch—not sticky nor slimy. They also looked clean after I used both. I wouldn’t recommend this for horse people who are fans of Lexol.

I tried the vendor who responded right away with helpful hints like "Plug it in!". On the third email they said it was passed to tech support. I didn't need the clamps, but it comes with the ring terminal harness which I have connected to the battery.

When first connected to the battery, it goes through a 15 minute cycle and ends with a perfect 13.5v float to keep the battery maintained.

Overall I'm very satisfied and would recommend this product.

title: Perfect Daytime Running Lights
text:
Review for the 7 ½ watt white:

I needed DRL’s for my 2015 xTerra, and after researching for a while I found these. These are spot lights and are easily bright enough to be seen during a sunny day. They are TOO bright to be used at night with the low beams, so I added a relay to cut the circuit when the low beams are on.

As the attached photo shows, both lights draw just under 1 amp. This equals 6 watts each at 12.6v, which is lower than the listed 7.5 watt. However, they are still plenty bright enough for my use. One major advantage to the low current is that I power the lights directly from the ACC circuit, simplifying the wiring.

I almost took off one star due to two reasons:
1. The included hardware was missing two nuts and had no lock washers. Sloppy quality control.
2. There is NO warranty, implied or otherwise, that the lights are weather-proof. I have concerns that they might not last the winter.

Still, 4 ½ stars rounding up to five stars for now.

title: Great for Eliminating Bad Smells from Cars, But Device Blocks Cigarette Lighter
text:
Unlike other tree-shaped air fresheners that you simply hang from the mirror, the Glad Plugins Air Freshener works like other Glad home air fresheners, in that you plug it into an outlet. Since it's a car, the only outlet is the cigar lighter port, which is kind of ironic when you think about it - it's likely smokers will most appreciate this car air freshener, but they're not likely to use it because they need to keep the lighter open for their cigarettes. Perhaps Glad should consider making this a USB-friendly device instead.

As it is, the air freshener works well and gets rid of annoying food, cigarette or oil smells. My only complaint is that the price of refills is higher than that of your typical cardboard air freshener. However, this is partially offset by the longevity of the cartridge, which Glade claims last 60 days. So overall, a good product if you really have a problem with a smelly car.

title: Use it as either one or the other .. gas siphon or pump to blow up items
text:
Guys, dads and all women – this is an A+ item that I advise keeping in your car/truck and buy your wife, daughter or son and hubby one. An item that once the worst happens - you will cry that you do not have! Yeppers! I have inadvertently been that chick on the side of the road out of petrol because the old clunkers gas gauge gave out and I didn't notice until it was way past too late. Never mind that my nickname was also chick in the ditch. But yes if you travel a lot it is an essential emergency kit item. I have a small tote in my car full.

It is even sadder when you don't have a small gas can to rescue the day. Yes I know Gasoline is the product obtained after cracking petrol. But some Brits or UK peeps call it petrol. I really just wanted this to keep in the trunk of my car in my rather vast emergency kit. I have been to the middle of nowhere in the great white north where snow is waist deep and the next gas station or motel is a few hundred miles away. I have been stranded in the dead of night with no one in sight. Sometimes you just have to learn the hard way. In my car is a foldup shovel, bag of mixed gravel, roadsalt and sand, jumper cables, heat blanket, first aid kit, blow up pillow, hatchet, matches, fire starter, hat and mittens, snacks, pot, water and mre's. It has all come in pretty hand dandy! Just make it a habit to hide some cash in your car for an emergency to give a kindly person in exchange for some gas if you get stranded, if you don't have a small gas can full of back up gas. I don't condone stealing gasoline nor talking to strangers – but you may have to talk to one when stranded.

Yes it is easy to use. Trust me I am not an overly mechanical nor technical girl. Put the intake tube into the gas can. Put the outgoing tube into the gas tank opening. Prime it by pumping the handle a couple of times. Then pull the handle fully out. If you need to stop the flow before your finished, don't pinch the hose, depress the handle instead!

It is also pretty cool to whip out your hose at a pool party, camping or at the beach. This is also an air pump. No more huffing and puffing by mouth. Blow up all the beach balls, floats and what-nots. I am OCD and after using it I do give it a good thorough rinsing off, I use the garden hose. I wouldn't be able to have a strong gas smell emanate from it. Mine is also housed in it's own bag for storage in my trunk. I can never get things back into the package the same way it arrived. That is like being able to fold up a fitted sheet! I would honestly have to own two of these. One for gas and one for blow-up jobs. I would hate to go blow up that beach ball etc. and have some gas residue – yuck! All your nefarious activities and old school ways of sucking on the end of a hose are over! Haha I received this product at a discount or free in return for a review and my honest and unbiased opinion.

Six adults in a mini-van, plenty of room, at least for the people. Leaving for a 7 day cruise, driving about 200 miles to get there.
Of the 6 adults, 2 were young ladies with 16 outfit changes per day (this is an estimation but I never saw them in the same outfits twice). We tried to put the bags in the back of the van. It's a 15 year old van. Not sure when the shocks were last replace, but it should have been the trip before this one.
Anyway, putting this on the roof of the van helped to distribute the weight so much better, there was no more bottoming out when we hit a bump, the ride smoothed out.
It decreased mileage but not by a significant amount.
It is easy to use, it comes with a pad to go underneath the roof bag. The straps tighten it down and it's is weather proof as far as I can tell. Of course in Texas, that just means that the material doesn't melt and the straps don't burst into flames. This has become a great investment.

title: Crapped out after year and a half
text:

Original review below:

I just bought this 1.5 Ton jack from Harbor Freight Tools and here are my initial thoughts after use (jack was properly bled):

1) The lowering mechanism to lower your car is not consistent in its operation. More often than not it drops the car too fast. This makes it a little dangerous to lower it onto your jack stand. I got it to lower slowly a couple times but it did not go down all the way down. When I turned it a little more, it dropped fast again.

2) When I was jacking up the car, I hear creaking sounds coming from it. It makes me nervous, like its about to explode or fall apart.

3) The maximum height is not very high.

4) The carry handle is off center making it difficult to carry with one hand.

5) It doesn't take ridiculous pressure to jack up your car but it takes considerable pressure.

6) Jack point will scratch/dent whatever it lifts due to the metal lip. To avoid, use a real NHL hockey puck.

Pros:
Its good looking. Handle is pretty solid. Seems to roll around OK. Only a few pumps to max height.

Will update in the future.

title: Barely works for a Suburban (at lease in my setup). One mfg flaw.
text:
These have been some comments/questions about if this works with a Suburban as a tow vehicle. I think the answer is soft of, depending on your setup.

Well, I hitched up the Suburban and found that with my one bike/platform rack setup it will work if I put the bike on carefully and don’t do an extremely tight turn. I have everything adjusted as far back towards the trailer as possible.

I have to have the TV and trailer straight to open the back lift door, and then I need to have the bike pedal at 6 o’clock for it to clear.

In turns the tires/wheel holders come close to the Suburban. At the closest points in these pictures the back bumper was about 3” off the propane tanks, so that’s a pretty tight turn. I will have to be careful in extreme turns, but I think it will be OK. I did think about cutting it shorter, but that is clearly not an option.

So this is a single bike setup and two bikes would not work with my TV. If you had a truck or a vehicle w/o a flat back – or at least one not as big as a Suburban – you would probably not have any problems using this.

PS-One of the top holes on the cross bar is smaller than the other. It was very difficult to insert the pole end and hard to twist it (had to use a mallet). The other side was fine, so this is certainly a manufacturing flaw. As others have mentioned while installing it is not brain surgery, the instructions could be better. Thus the deductions in stars. Wish I could rate it 3.5.

title: Basic roof top cargo carrier with some design flaws - most of which can be addressed!
text:
Purchased this unit for two purposes. The first was to put on a Chevy Equinox. It has a rear center antenna so I needed a box that was fairly short in length. The second use was for a roof top carrier on our boat. I have had a Yakima cargo box in the past and that experience swayed me to Yakima over Thule. Everything stored in the cargo box will be light and bulky so I wasn't worried about the 135 pound useful load limit on the RocketBox Pro 12.

On the car mine started to gape open at the front. So many people have complained about this issue that I was expecting it to happen. I drilled a 1/4" hole through the center front flanges and put a releasable tie wrap to secure the front. Problem solved. Yes, it adds a few seconds to the loading and unloading process but no big deal. Too bad Yakima is making such lightweight lids that this is necessary though!! On the boat my speeds, even into the wind, are usually much, much less than the car but I still use the releasable tie wrap just to be sure.

Also, not really happy about the process of getting the latches to engage when shutting the cargo box. I guess this design is the best Yakima can do for a box that opens on either side. It does take patience to get the box closed properly!

I also used gorilla tape to cover the four mounting bracket slots in the floor of the box to keep water out. Not sure how this will work long term but it can't hurt.

I could have used the RocketBox Pro 14 for my two vehicles but I got a slightly used floor sample at a national sporting goods store's garage sale for only $100.83 so it was a deal I couldn't pass up!

title: Simple steps to install on 2007 Sienna, work great!
text:
These were super easy to install and really only took 5 to 10 minutes total.

You'll need:
- Something to hold the hatch all the way open.
- A screwdriver
- Work gloves if you have them, a lot of have cleaner if you don't.

Grab your parts, gloves, and screwdriver and get to work! Use something to hold the rear hatch open while you work. It has to be all the way open to make it easier to fit the length of the openers. Then, use a screwdriver to gently pry the metal clips that hold the ends of the tube and rod over the small ball ends connected to the car.
The ball ends we're really dirty. I had a rag to wipe them off, and a little white grease to clean and lightly lubricate them.
Once you have removed the parts from one side of the hatch, gently pry loose (but not all the way off) the metal clip from the rod, slide the end over the ball attached to the side of the van, and press the clip down to lock it in place over the ball. Then do the same to the one on the hatch end. Be careful, as your support might come loose.
Repeat for the other side.
My hands were filthy after replacing the lifts, so wear some gloves if you can.

The temperature here drops below zero, and that's when we started noticing the lifts not working well, and then they failed completely on a cold morning. I think I used one of my kiddos skis to hold the hatch open so we could get our gear in the back of the van.

This was easily the simplest repair I've had to do to my 10 year-old 2007 Toyota Sienna mini van. I installed these a few weeks ago. It's -1°f out today, and these lifts are working fine.

This is the first time we've bought such expensive floor mats for our cars, and we've decided that they are definitely worth what they cost. WeatherTech mats are far better than OEM carpet mats or the cheap Chinese junk that tries to look like quality at a bargain price.
Because they are designed for each model of car, they fit the contours of the car exactly, including the undulations designed into the floor of the car. As a result they stay in place because the raised edges fit perfectly against the side walls of the cabin. This fit keeps them from sliding around, and the high lips keep water and dirt from getting into the carpet. The molded design fits the lumps and bumps built into the floor, so these mats fit better than the carpet OEM mats that came with the car.

Perhaps I should’ve had an alignment at some point, even though it appeared to me and my mechanic that I didn’t need one yet, but I have still never had tires were down this quickly. Alignment or not.

Besides this outrageous wear experience, I can say that I haven’t like the tires since Day 1, and whatever day it was that first rained especially. They slide easily on tight curves and hydroplane like nothing else I’ve experienced. As one who also rides, I am scared for those who say they use this tire for their motorcycle.

Check out the photos. These are my two front tires. Wear is nearly identical on both sides. Not sure that the photos show this well.

This is totally a bummer living in Pennsylvania. There is no way I can get through the winter safely with these and who has the money to drop on four more plus the costs of labor and disposal?

Shame on this company and on Amazon for selling them. 9,000 miles is insane. Do yourself a favor and buy better tires.

The cost for these beads is reasonable and will save money over the life of the tires because there will be no rebalancing.  I recommend these beads.

The other day when putting it up the directional switch slipped sending my feeder straight down and the handle spinning uncontrollably. I thought it broke my hand at first, but just bruised it. If you need a winch for 300lbs, get a 1000lb winch. They just do not stand up to loads near what they are rated at.

title: Wouldn't have my motorcycle without one.
text:
I have been using this cup holder for about 8 years on my Harley-Davidson and it has been a great cup holder. I have one complaint, just one. Over time, the nipples that connect to the cup holder itself from the arms becomes tired. Riding down the road one day, I hit a bump an the cup holder separated from the big "C" arm. It was an easy fix. I rode over to Lowe's, I took of the cup holder and put the nipples of the two arms back in the holes, ran the serrated edge of my knife around the nipples on the inside of the cup and then bought two C clips to go in the groves. Now, w/the C clips, the cup holder will not bounce off the arm again. I gave it four stars because that seems like something an engineer at RAM Mounts should have thought of.

Update 10Aug21: I just bought my second cup holder to replace my old one; which I’ve had for many years now. After looking at the nipples that extend into the cup holder a little closer, it appears that RAM has recognized the problem. The ends appear to have been heated up and flared, which should hold the cup holder better. This cup holder fits and is strong enough to hold a 30oz Tervis Tumber. However, not a Yeti; they’re too big & too heavy.

text:

It took my hands quite a long time to get used to holding something thicker than the steering wheel without a cover. I really like how it feels on my hands, but they did ache after being held in a different position.

I don't do a lot of driving, however from time to time I will take a long distance trip. I finally took one after my hands got used to the cover and they didn't ache as much during and after the drive as they had on the same drive before I got this cover. So, the cover did do what I was hoping it would

I've not yet used it during really hot weather, but I didn't need to wear my gloves when it was cold in the FJ, compared to how I usually would have without the cover. title: Plug and Play, great color, and bright!
text:
So... buy these.

Pros:
1) They're plug and play and profiled just like regular halogen bulbs. No ballasts hanging off of them and no special mounting rings or what not.
2) Nice and bright and great color... matches the LEDs in my headlights perfectly.
3) Floods well, nice and bright, and the fill is smooth and even.

Cons:
1) Not so much a con but an observation. The fact that the light is adjustable for cutoff is a nice feature but it also means the mount rotates. Do be careful when installing so as to not damage the mounting ring. Good idea to glance through the very short instructions.

I've found in the past with non-halogen systems that there is a tendency to arc and fail, so I use a little dielectric grease on the contacts to protect the system. Did so in this case and no issues so far two months in.

title: I was skeptical at first... now I'm more than happy
text:
Having gone through the era of aftermarket add-on Xenon projectors, and aftermarket add-on HID bulbs, I was skeptical about these. LEDs have in the past either been too dim or not reliable. A friend of mine installed these on his car and I was sold. I have some requirements when it comes to these lighting systems.

1) They can't look like high beams to everyone else on the road.
2) They need to have a nice clean white color
3) They need to light up the road better than halogen

So for the first, these have a good cutoff. They do spill upwards a bit more than desired but that has also been good for vision. Having seen these from outside of the car they are bright but they're not highbeam bright. Shined against a wall they do have a cutoff but note that as they don't have auto-leveling they will still flash oncoming traffic when grading up. On the ground they're bright enough to negate any benefit from the foglights and they do a great job of lighting up the road when its wet.

The color is bright white, not blue, not yellow, just white. And as they're LED they don't have any shadows or lines or any halos, it is just clean even flood. Whatever it shines on also stays clean and focused so vision is increased substantially from halogen.

My favorite part is that there are no separate ballasts, it is literally plug and play. As a matter of habit I use dielectric grease on the connectors to protect the units and the bulbs themselves have an integral fan housing on the back, so be aware that if your bulb housings have little in the way of clearance, you may have to modify or go with a different unit.

100% happy with these bulbs, highly recommend and will continue to use and buy.

title: Amazing and cerakote tough.
text:
I've got a Nissan Xterra. After a little while the body plastics start to look like gray crushed velvet or raw primer. This is a forever circumstance with this car and I just lived with it, despite the car being sturdy enough to last a long time. I've tried Back to Black which works fine except much rubbing is required and the results don't last more than a week if that. In fact, that was the best product I've used to this point. And the heat gun trick is not long lived and not without its risks.

A couple of tips for you:
1) Wear a respirator. I don't mean a COVID mask, I mean a VOC respirator, or an NBC mask. The fumes are intense. Enough to make you stop. Also do not apply without wearing gloves.
2) Coat generously. I made the mistake of being frugal with the pads. While a little goes a long way, there's no need to stretch the pads as they dry. Fold the pads over so you have a new surface to wipe with, that definitely works to extend the mileage of each pad. Once those are used up, just open a new one. I coated the whole car's plastics with just three pads and ended up going back with a second coat with two more pads.
3) Take your time and do a detailed job. Because this stuff does such a good job of restoring the original color, every bit that you don't cover will stand out. Getting into the seams (cutting edges) is an important step. What worked for me is covering the hard to hit spaces first (while the pads are well-soaked) and then covering the easy spots after. Have a clean terry cloth standing by to wipe up excess.
4) There is some prep involved in that cleaning is needed to get any surface infections off of the plastic. As to how necessary it is... unknown but it will make your application go smoother if everything is clean and DRY. Importantly though, follow the instructions.

I was skeptical, not because of the quality of the product, as I've used Cerakote coatings before and have seen plenty of other reviews. I was skeptical because my plastics were in really terrible shape. For some of the surfaces the Cerakote covered and restored immediately. On other surfaces it looked like it only made a marginal difference. That coverage actually improved a week later, maybe because it needed to blend in. The second coat did even better. So take your time and be patient between application and drying.

Get this stuff! If you're like me and nothing else is working, and you don't want to spend every weekend recoating your car's plastics, use Cerakote. No rubbing/scrubbing required, just wipe on. You won't be disappointed with the results and even if you are, it will still likely be a vast vast improvement. Also... wear a respirator.

title: Likely closer to 4000k in temp but still very white and still bright. Cheaper and easier to deal with than HID kits.
text: I have my doubts about how color temperature is measured with these "super white" standard socket bulbs. Far too often I see bulbs rated at 5000k but in reality are 3000k at best.  These follow the same relative recipe.  I'm on my 2nd set of these same bulbs which are installed in a projector housing on my SUV at 80W and 7000k temperature, I would say these are roughly equivalent to 65W halogen at 3800k to 4100k temperature which is very close to the color temperature of an OEM HID lamp. It's not perfectly white, still has a tinge of yellow but is satisfyingly bright and white enough to be a substantial upgrade. Be advised however that the higher wattage output produces much more bright light to oncoming traffic.  My projector housings have a upper cutoff that prevents vertical spill and solves the problem of looking like high beams in any mode. So it would be a good idea to check the amount of spill your housings allow upward before you opt for the 80W version. You may consider trying the 55W first.

title: 16" is fine, but 26" attaches to my wiper arm incorrectly, preventing blade contact with the windshield
text: I bought some of these at Costco yesterday (16" passenger-side and 26" driver-side for my 2012 Honda CR-V) and installed them. The 16" passenger wiper is fine, but the 26" driver side blade is shaped differently than the original that I removed. The original is offset from the wiper arm, or, in other words, it has an attachment point to the side of the removable blade--closer to the hood of the car, so that the blade assembly sits further up the windshield from, or next to, the wiper arm. This Goodyear model, however, has a thicker metal assembly that attaches directly underneath the wiper arm, so it pushes the arm up away from the glass and the rubber blade does not fully make contact with the windshield. In my case, this means there is a roughly 12" oval area in the bottom center of the glass that does not get wiped, making these unusable and unsafe to use in the event of rain. I have replaced my original and will return this one to Costco, but as there was an issue at checkout with the 26" blade being from an old lot such that a manager had to enter it in Costco's register manually, I will look to see if there is a newer model or lot that attaches correctly to my CRV wiper arm.

Let dry for at least a minute. Remove the bottom plastic coating on the patch, and stick it on. If you have a clamp and two flat pieces of something, clamp them together. Now, wait. A long time. title: don't waste your time on this kit - you likely have half this stuff at home and the rest is cheaper at the craft store
text:
trying to repair a small burn hole in a faux leather olive green/grey/brown (fatigue?) color moto jacket, and this was the best do-it-yourself repair kit on the market with the highest rating, and it claimed to work on faux leather, burn holes, comes with a great mix of colors, etc. no biggie, i figured the jacket was pretty cheap and having it professionally repaired would cost more than i paid for it on clearance. but there are SO MANY PROBLEMS with this kit, and i have gone above and beyond making sure i follow the instructions, to the point of using super strong magnets to hold the repair area flat on top of a cookie sheet.

- let's start with the backing fabric. it is terrible. too silky to work with a polyester jacket lining, and the openness of the gauze doesn't want to retain any of the "repair compound" and keep it from seeping through.

- the "repair compound", as i've read from some other reviews, is the same consistency as elmer's white school glue. i've gone through SIX ROUNDS of the stuff, occupying my kitchen island for days trying to fill this hole - and it's not a big hole, maybe 0.5cm wide? it's supposed to shrink the hole and fill it up to be level with the rest of the jacket. i've tried all sorts of tricks at this point to see if there is anything i can do to make this work. initially i followed the instructions so there was no excess but that was a terrible idea. i have a sinking feeling my jacket, when i finally finish this entire process, will be glued to the cookie sheet, with the repair compound seeping through the backing fabric as well as the polyester lining of the jacket.

- it does not help that there are only 3 swatches for leather grains, none of which suit my particular piece. every time i apply a grain swatch overnight on top of the repair compound (and add some weight) it glues itself to the swatch and not the jacket.

- since my jacket color is way out there and not exactly one color even (it is supposed to look a bit faded in spots) i know i wasted a lot of paint - which i believe another reviewer said was latex, which would make sense unless we were actually working with real leather or pleather patches and dyes and bonding materials. i was able to correctly color match the spot i plan on fixing as i tested on a tiny area of the jacket where nobody can see, three slightly different variations of color. it should definitely be noted that it does dry darker than it looks in whatever container you decide to mix it in. this, btw, is not provided, so there goes some tupperware. on the bright side i am grateful i went to art school for so many years and worked in design for so long. unless you're a creative or crafty type and understand your color wheel the color guidelines won't help you much. also, only one pipette is included, a mini brush with a head far too large for a small repair such as mine, one sponge - for "feathering" and blending into the surrounding area. if you have any brushes i suggest you break out the brushes. and i wish i could have used less paint but mine was very liquidy even after hard shaking and trying to get a 'drop' of a color often resulted in far too much falling in and having to continue adding from there.

- the sealant practically ruined all the hard work i had done up to that point building up layers of glue and paint and trying to add texture along the way. it felt like nail polish remover on a hangnail and actually altered the original faded style dye job of my jacket itself, and aside from the big chunky glued spot seemed to thin it out so it ballooned around it.

all in all, had i known what this kit really entailed and that it wasn't really going to work on my problem, i would have used better materials, some of which i already own, like a tighter weave impermeable backing cloth like microfiber, a much better filler/repair compound (maybe gorilla glue or loctite for vinyl/fabric/plastic flexible adhesive), picked up small quantities of latex paints and the right brushes in only the colors i needed, used some scrap leather or even an old ruined shoe to add grain, and used basic weatherproofing spray as a sealant. total money i would have needed to spend had i used 20/20 hindsight is whatever the latex paints would have cost me. another cheap way to do this would have been to fill the hole to size with scrap leather or leather-textured vinyl/polyurethane using an x-acto knife, use a flexible adhesive as mentioned above to secure it, and then paint it to match with latex paints and blend. there are so many cheaper and easier ways to do this that would actually work. had i known all of this sooner i never would have wasted so much time and effort and energy on a shoddy repair with a WAY overpriced kit.

The instructions do not match the wiring diagram which has print that is literally microscopic! What you have are 2 Red Wires, 1 Yellow & 1 Black. The diagram references Blue & Green wires, which do not exist. The diagram illustrates an "electronic control " which I guess is the black relay box and below it the " connect the line box " which I assume is the Yellow square connection box. The diagram of the wires coming out of the connection box shows Red wires plugging into both the + & - posts of the horn with a Yellow wire going to the +? & a Green wire going to the -?. Then there is a single (non-existing) Blue wire going to the " steer device button ", horn button?

Now for the Connection Guide
1. Red line connect with Battery
2. Black line connect with Battery
3. Blue line connect with the button of the horn
4. Green Line connect with the high frequency nom
5. Yellow line connect with the low frequency nom
In there is no frequency indiaion, please repeat the above
4 & 5 step to find the best sound.

My guess is that 1 Red wire is connected to the + battery post and the Black wire to ground. The other red wire to the horn ( + or - negative posts not specified ) & the yellow wire plugs into the existing horn wiring harness.

title: AWFUL
text:
Been detailing for over 20 years.

This is terrible in a bottle. You think it’s easy - until you think you have removed the product. I think it took me 5 passes (across 2 days) and I was still discovering product - not shadowing, just simple removal. And, while using the absolute best MF towels. Did not matter. Garbage because you cannot rely on it whether personal or (and I doubt any professional would) pro use as I would not feel comfortable sending a customer home with this sort of situation occurring. Yes the bottle says 48 hours and/or shadowing MAY appear -it should say it will and the product will not be actually done for at least 48 hours and at that, still would not trust it.

Meguiars liquid hybrid ceramic is light years better, more product, cheaper, and reliable. Highly suggest you look past hype or pics. Anyone can get a vehicle to look good in a pic. The process is what matters and this makes your life miserable because it adds SO much time. Doubt many even saw the ongoing residue this leaves on any surface. Used this on a vehicle that was new, prepped ground up, full 2 step correction in a shop etc. caught this on a lighting deal and it’s not worth the time to return it but worth the time to write this for others. Move on. Ugh.

Edit: Customer Support - the bottle says shadowing may occur. Heck of a response instead of offering help or a refund. Not that I would even take it. The is snake oil and a problem waiting to happen if you actually know what you are doing. AVOID!!!

text: Get the best. Don’t think twice. Good quality and great kit. After this, you might just need a tire cleaning stuff brush, and maybe a tall wheel well but the brushes alone are great.

title: Great, but
text:
Ok so right off the bat, and shelf, Griots delivers a 1 step easy to understand and use ceramic. It gave show car luster and big depth meant to be appreciated and not so much a pop wow like an overly shiny spray and wipe. It’s still very glossy too, but maintains that traditional freshly waxed look. Very nice on metallics.

It was simple to use though just my opinion, it seemed to need more product vs less, and although it applied super easy, it does not slide for days.

For cut and and polish, they clearly had to find a proper balance and for the most part it’s fine especially to get some quick results. But it loses a star here because of its inability to cut generally. I think it’s designed for a super novice to get close to pro results. And you will.

But, even with an orange foam on a fantastically maintained but not ceramic coated white metallic suv, had to keep upping pad as I didn’t want to be so aggressive due to it not being so slippery. It is super safe so even on bare minimum correction cars, I found you had to be quite aggressive, odd because there wasn’t much going on with the vehicle it appeared generally great (I use Adam’s strip wash, find it perfect but isn’t too strong in the cleaning dept, but def great at getting through a waxed/sealed vehicle). Meguiars Ultimate Compound would probably power through in one pass what would take a couple more aggressive ones or higher cut pads per panel at a min with this. So I’m not sure yet…. but so far, that’s what I notice more than anything, along with amount of product needed. This all is in context obv to whatever your jobs condition is but the theme carried across many. If you are strip washing and doing everything ground up this will eliminate paint work time just a bit weaker on cut than anticipated but they do say fine scratches and that is actually more than accurate. So although I gave it 4 stars for something it comes out and says - maybe I just assumed it would have a tad more bite for a full on one step. If it’s not one, I’d make sure they just be more upfront about potentially needing to correct first/more.

All that, it’s still an awesome off the shelf easily bought slightly one step solution that I can use myself or for anyone. On such a well maintained vehicle just had me scratching my head. A MF might do the job far better, faster. Real easy to wipe off, that was huge actually. Never really needed a spray follow up. Comes right off and no dust. On and off done looks like you did alot more than you did. Hard to ask for more given the rest of its benefits.

text:
Install was pretty simple and it certainly fixed the issue of my 2003 Odyssey engine racing between 1000 and 2000 RPM as the vehicle sat running.

As usual, removing the two mounting screws from the old unit presented the largest challenge. The one part related problem I had with the IACV was the new gasket included with the unit. Though it was an identical shape & format to the original gasket, overall, it appeared to be about 2mm larger than it should have been so it was a significant challenge to make it fit together. At least the size difference was proportionate so even though the gasket didn't neatly lay directly into the grove/channel of the throttle body, it seemed simple enough to push in when mounting the IACV on to the throttle body.

title: Meh, it works, but has a few design issues
text:
It's all right, for what it is. The first nit I have is there was no picture on the package showing what it should look like after assembly. 10 minutes wasted on Youtube looking for a demo.

My second nit would be the sizing of the plastic tubing. They include a few custom nibs that fit into the tube and the other end goes into the bleeder valve. I wasn't comfortable with jamming it in with enough force to make sure it stayed in that tiny hole so I just cut a short piece of 1/4" tubing, placed over theirs on one end and the bleeder on the other end, problem solved.

Third, and maybe my biggest nit is the small capacity, which since you need to leave some fluid in the bottom to cover the end of the hose, is maybe 2 ounces. This seems like enough, unless you're bleeding new calipers, which come alone with lots of air bubbles and likely an extra empty cycle per brake.

All in all, it wasn't a total waste of money because it actually worked but I think I'll just use an old bottle and some tubing to make my own next time.

A 17mm wrench & 11/16" were both too small and the 18mm was just sloppy enough that turning the nut on to the thread, which did have a lot of resistance, caused the interior nut to spin. I ended up carefully placing a long nose vice grip on the nut and using that to crank down on the nut. Working that issue out took a bit of time but otherwise the install was very clean

title: Saw no improvement in record quality.
text:
Does this thing remove static? Yes. Is it needed if you take good care of your records? No. My typical process when I get a new or used record is to wet wash/vacuum them. I also store them in Mobile Fidelity anti-static sleeves. With this combo, I had zero use for the Milty zerostat. This would be great for a record straight out of a paper sleeve to remove the static, but if your record isn't properly cleaned, you're going to have more issues than just the static. After a good wet cleaning/vacuum, I have never had to use this as the record is almost static free at that point. One quick rotation with an anti-static brush takes care of any of the remaining static before play.

Final judgement: does the product work, yes. Is it needed for record collectors with a solid cleaning routine, I do not believe so.

title: 2018 Traverse Draw-Tite Hitch Installation Nightmare!!
text: I’m a pretty handy guy and I thought this would be a pretty easy project to complete!  I had my 16 yo son help me take the rear plastic and bumper off the 2018 Traverse.  That all went about as smooth as could be expected.  Then you think oh this should fit right in its place?????  NO, not even close! After watching a few more YouTube videos of others having the same issues here’s what we did.  First we tried aligning it and noticed the right side would not line up at all.  Easily 1/8 to a 1/4 inch from going on.  So we took a chain saw file and Dremel tool to start opening the mount hole so it would go on. It required all 4 mount holes to be drilled and filed before we finally got it to line up.  After that the back right side we used a longer bolt to suck the mount down and then replaced it with the factory one to be able to get the muffler back up in place.  The bottom 2 bolts including the muffler hanger were just close enough that they went in with the impact.  I’m glad I did it but would easily pay for it next time. It is a great hitch but install was a nightmare.

I hang my car key separately on the bottom section and my house keys on a ring on the bottom as well so they won’t fall off when I open and close it.

Heartily recommend!

title: Fantastic product for small dings but needs more cleaning fluid and not for "shaped" panels/angles.
text:
First off: 2011 Jetta TDI - Factory paint, outer skin feels as thing as recycle coke cans...
Situation: several small dings from door corners but also a significant dent in the right front edge of my corner panel from a hand (long story..) Thumb below dented in and fingers above..(pincher) I am not a mechanic nor do I have any experience doing body work of any kind..

This product worked flawlessly on the usual door dings I mentioned from corners of doors into the door panels. 2 out of 4 are virtually non-existent, 2 others there is only a slight 1/8" imperfection. Max. 2 tries per, to get what I wanted.
On the corner panel, which was more extensive, angles etc.. I would say after maybe 18-20 attempts, I got to a point where it isn't great but looks far better than it was. I simply could not round out the lines properly.

Good about this product:
1. Really easy to use if you do it right. Like another user clearly stated and my comments:
2. ZERO impact to my factory paint finish - the glue comes off the car very easy.
3. Low clean up requirements..(although see bad for details)

Bad
1. Lots of sticks..but nowhere near enough cleaner. Cleaning the rubber heads can be very tedious and found I used alot of the cleaning fluid. I am down to about 20% left after the 18-20 corner panel attempts. Would like to know what this stuff is or what substitute I can use for sure.
2. One other user suggest more rubber ends and I agree. This way you can work more while someone is cleaning another. Also, before I started using my finger nail, I hacked up the larger piece with a blade..Stick to your finger nail with fluid to get the rubber head clean.

Tips:
1. The rubber knob in which you put the melted glue on needs to be crystal clean AND dry before you try again.
2. The car surface also needs to be sparkling clean before attempting this.
3. Ensure the melted glue is evenly distributed on the knob and heaping enough to ensure when you put it on your car the liquid engulfs the rubber head.
4. Hold the head in place for a few seconds..don't expect it to adhere right away.
5. Do not twist the knob like you are reeling in a fish..go slowly and observe the metal lifting .
6. I recommend being in a shaded area..once the sun starting hitting my car..I seemed to either have less luck with the glue staying stuck..maybe just me getting tired..
6. Avoid using this on a dent bigger than 3-4 inches. And, like I said..be careful with "shaped" panels..you can do more harm than good.

I'll post a few picks and maybe a video if it works...

title: I've tried them all and this one is the BEST!!!
text: Okay....so I'm a buy two different and weigh each one out as long as there is a free return on it.  I read all or most of the reviews and go from there.  I purchased this one and another one that looked exactly like the MeeFar, here on Amazon.  By no means are they comparable.  The MeeFar is by leagues the FAR SUPERIOR and here is why... it's all about the way they have made the closing.  There is a zipper that goes all the way around it but then there is this GLORIOUS pull down excess/flap that has velcro which all completely covers the zipper.  I'm not talking a flimsy two inch protection overlap.  I'm talking a good 5-6 inches overlap.  The velcro is super sticky and has remained "grabby".  We travel from Maine to Florida and from Florida to Maine in all seasons and all kinds of weather.  From torrential rains to freezing sleet and snow.  This MeeFar has kept everything dry and safe.  There are straps with snaps and straps with hooks.  The hooks DID NOT damage my paint on the car and when we take the H2 the straps with snaps that click together are enough to hold the rooftop in place and not move or slide off.  The mat that they included also helps to keep the MeeFar in place  (in all honesty I think it's a rubber mat you put under your carpet but man this is a game changer). Seriously, you can pack this to the hilt or you can just put in a couple of pieces of luggage - this thing is staying put.  This is a purchase that I am truly grateful that I made.  It's even stayed on the roof when we had to skedaddle from a Hurricane with hurricane winds this MeeFar didn't slip or slide and everything was dry inside.  It's super easy to clean.  I just use  clorox wipes bc birds seem to find us where ever we go (if you know what I'm talking about).  The coloring has not faded at all.  The one thing I can mention - which is by no means the fault of the car topper.  Do NOT put anything meltable inside of it, if you do ... prepare to clean it.  Plus....remember, whatever temperature it is outside it will be in your topper.  So no liquids when freezing weather traveling and no meltable when high temperatures avail.  If you ever need to hose out this topper, allow it to air dry and then take a window cleaner and some paper towels and have at it.  To be super picky, after I've folded it up and put it back into the handy carrier - I tuck in dryer sheets -  Keeps critters, silver fish and tiny insects out and when you unpack the MeeFar, it smells lovely and clean.  The dryer sheets do not discolor the black in the least and oh yeah....the black has not faded at all.  I LOVE this MeeFar and so will you.  When and if it ever rips or bites the dust - I will rebuy this particular one in a heartbeat no hesitations.  Good luck and safe & happy travels.

title: This is a 1-man job...just don't forget to remove the spacers!!!
text:
I see a lot of folks had trouble with the installation because the struts appear to be too long. It's a lot easier if you remove the two "wrap-around" spacers from the back of the trunk hinges. With one hand, lower the trunk lid a few inches (don't let go) and with the other hand remove the spacer (one side at a time...comes right off with your thumbnail) then push the lid back up. Connect the bottom of the strut first, then use one hand to push the trunk open while using the other had to pull the top of the strut into place. It takes a little opening pressure to line them up, but they will go on without compressing the strut. Don't forget to put the plastic tabs back in!

Big improvement over the factory struts...the trunk lid is practically at zero-gravity now...no more slamming!

The photos make the decals look as if they are a matte finish,which they definitely are not. They are a high-gloss. I'm going to lay then out flat in the sun, or I might just throw them away since I already made trimming cuts on them. Live and learn.

O.K.: after attempting (and failing) to put these on my car, I feel like if there were better instructions, I could probably done an acceptable. For example, they don't tell you when you peel the white backing off...THATS NOT THE STICKER!!! There is a thin film that must be pealed off once the vinyl design has been positioned FIRMLY and any sort of bubbles(and there will be bubbles) are worked out of the decal. Be careful here as you could poke a hole in the vinyl.

In short, if instructions similar to these had been included with the decals, they might be on my car and not in the trash. I'm going to think on it for awhile before I decide to try again. They won't be these, though. As I mentioned I want a matte finish look and these do not.

title: Extra long gutter extensions
text:
These can be hard to install, depending on your campers construction. On my camper, I had to remove quite a bit of sealant and a couple of gutter screws needed to be removed as well. Once I removed the screws, the old gutter spouts can be pulled out and the longer ones put into place. Just make sure you mark where the screw will go through the spout, and pre-drill the hole in the spout. That way you can apply your sealant to the back side of the gutter and the spout. Key is to ensure you reseal the screw holes so that no water can enter into the camper. Last thing you want is water running down the inside corners of your camper. That is the #1 spot for ALL campers with rotted wood in the floors. The corners.
These do keep the water from running down the sides of your camper in light rain. But in heavy downpours, the small gutters installed by the camper industry, cannot handle the water flow, and the water will still run down the sides of your camper. So these gutter spouts are only really good for your AC condensation, or light rain. They do work as advertised under those conditions. But moderate to heavy rain is too much for the gutter system. No fault of the spout.
