Take a look at the Raybestos H17389 kit, it appears to be a closer match for the springs required for your this model of Forester!

There was no problem with the connector orientation being out of alignment with the original, as they include a replacement connector that was long-enough to compensate for the new position.  However, you will require a high-wattage soldering iron, solder, and flux; this is the only good way to attach the new connector to the wiring-harness (i.e., you have to cut-off the old connector).  This isn't disclosed when you purchase the alternator, whereas it was denoted on the installation documentation received.  Evidently there's a concern if you use the old connector due to increased resistance (corroded/dirty terminals) which might cause the old connector to melt/fail.  Overall, it wasn't too bad to install, and as stated, it appears to be of good quality (only time will tell). :-)  Gordon

title: Tests most types of batteries and sizes (rechargeable and non-rechargeable)
text:
Like a lot of families; having toys, remotes, game pads, etc. entails accumulating and buying tons of batteries
and it gets hard to keep track of.
Some batteries get taken out and swapped in other devices or toys or end up scattered in the living room, etc.
Sometimes I don't know if I mixed up a battery with a lot of juice left with one that is very low on juice.
Or just even knowing that a semi-new battery is borderline defective already.
Needed reliable and portable to test these remnants laying around the house so they won't go to waste.

After doing a bit of research there was a ton out there but decided to go with Lacrosse because I already liked their reviews
on their Battery Charging device.

So far this thing works like a charm. Immediately tells me which battery is low or still good (even rechargeables).
So far the meter stick either showed "good" or "low" at the same spots but I haven't been able to display in-between yet.
So at first I was thinking this was just going to show good or bad.
But then I tried some other batteries and it displayed levels of extremely good and borderline good too.
So it's not some gimmick as I thought.
All in all, this thing works and will save you from throwing away batteries or recharging the ones that are equally low.

title: Installed on 2021 Wolf Pup 16FQ with full glass door
text:
Cheaper on manufacturer’s web site, not Amazon. Watch for sales, too. I’m satisfied with it, but you should look over the feedback below before purchasing.

Pros:
All metal, heavy lock
Programmable key code, good instructions
Backlit
Fob, key or key code entry
Rubber gasket supplied for glass door is needed because glass has no “play”

Lots of videos to show how to install

Cons:

There’s a toggle switch to turn on and off the fob,s ability to work. If fob stops working, sometimes cycling that switch in and off will fix the problem.
Maybe it gets accidentally jarred while using the door to enter and exit the RV?

Key fob usage is not reliable. You can hear the deadbolt attempt to retract, but the door isn’t unlocked, and especially happens after moving the trailer. Then, try using the physical key and it will unlock. Following that, fob starts working.

Key fob locks and unlocks only the deadbolt. It does not lock or unlock the door pull. I sure wish it locked and unlocked the entire door mechanism.

If the deadbolt is locked and someone pulls the unlocked handle, neither the key, key code or fob will unlock the deadbolt. You have to manually push on the door to force the door pull to click closed, then all will work.

Bonus tool is useless. Won’t work at all on Phillips screws. Get your own screwdriver.

Does NOT install in 10 minutes. Allow about an hour and have two people.

Be very careful installing on a glass door. The opening is the right size, but there’s no “play.” Gentle, even, screw tightening is required. It’s tight and until you get it completely installed, you will think that it won’t fit.

title: Very Good Perfroming Inflator so far.....
text:
I received my JACO Smart Pro Inflator yesterday and put it to work today
on our BMW 430i X - Drive Convertible. This vehicle's tires are inflated to:
Front: 38psi, Rear: 45psi according to BMW. I was very impressed with this
inflator right out of the box. This inflator will be used on both of our vehicles
and will be stoyed within one of them. Outlined below is my review:

Pros:
Nicely designed, well made, fitted carry case. The material is very substantial
and comes with a small side pocket for storing the included needle valve accessories.
The carry handle is a big plus.

Pressure Settings:
The digital read-out is large and easy to read. Jogging up or down, using the control
buttons, will quickly achieve the desired air pressure. A "progress bar" is also shown
on the display along with a pressure read-out showing air being sent into the tire,
a very nice feature. Your Target Pressure will always be displayed along with the
status of air being introduced into the tire.

On/Off Switch
A useful feature. Although I used an outdoor 120V outlet, I turned the inflator
OFF when I had completed inflating each tire. The AC line cord stayed pluged
into the outlet.

Easy Programming:
This inflator has memory! You first choose the pressure, then set it, then begin
your inflation. The unit will remember your psi setting and begin to inflate the
tire once the ON switch is depressed. The unit also has an automatic SHUT-OFF.
Once the Target Pressure has been reached, it shuts down the compressor.

Valve Stem Coupling:
This inflator is fitted with a knurled brass screw-on valve stem coupling. I liked
this very much over one made from base metal or a thermoplastic material.
The valve stem coupling is a very important piece of the overall inflator.
An air bleed button is afixed adjacent to the valve stem coupling, a nice touch
for adjusting or tweeking a few lbs of air.

Overall Performance:
The JACO Smart Pro Inflator works quickly. I had no problem bringing all tires
up to specs within minutes.

Inflator Noise:
The inflator lets you know it's working however, it is not overly loud.

Cons:
The air hose is somewhat short. My outdoor convenience outlet is close by, however,
I did have to turn the car around once in order to reach the tires on the other side.
Also, there may be instances where an extension cord is needed to attach to the
AC line cord when using 115V power. Those issues are minor when considering
the performance of this inflator.

Conclusion:
I highly recommend this inflator. It's features are very useful and functional.
The unit works quickly, appears to produce more psi than needed, and will
prevent you from over-inflating your tires with the highly visible digital display
screen. Carrying an extension cord and a longer one for 12V use may be a good
idea..Hopefully this inflator will last a good number of years.

title: Perfect Fit for Our 2017 BMW 430i X drive Convertible
text: The MAHLE LX 3424 engine air filter was designed as original equipment fit for our 2017 BMW X Drive, twin turbo convertible (4 cyl), 250 HP. This filter was somewhat difficult to find from local auto outlet stores including on-line auto supply warehouses. However, Amazon had two at the time I purchased this one, lucky me. The installation was quite easy (once I analyzed the procedure). Turns out that the LH top body stiffener had to be removed to access one of the spring clips holding the filter housing in place (LH facing the front of the vehicle.) Then, the front center cowl gets removed which is held in place with neoprene push/pull grommets. I disconnected the Mass Air Flow Sensor switch cable to protect it during this work, although not necessary. There are about 5 spring clips that hold the filter cover in place. Once open, I vacuumed out the canister and replaced the filter reversing the removal procedure. Interestingly, Amazon referred me to another Seller which was showing a much less expensive price for this same filter. I thought that odd and would expect Amazon to Price Match and credit my purchased accordingly.

title: This tote needs to be redesigned
text: The hose fills and empties low on the tank so filing it requires some pressure to get the remaining liquid in the tote.  If you have a class A with a low connector, this could be very messy because you have to manipulate the hose to empty the contents into the tote.  The stop, at the back of the tote, is a good idea but it doesn't work. It will keep the tote from over-filling by stopping the air flow out of the tank but after you close the valve on the RV, you will have a very difficult time emptying the hose from the connector to the tote because there is no more air flow into the hose that allows the water to drain into the tote.  You would think that you could disconnect the hose from the RV and let the liquid drain but whatever liquid is between the valve and the disconnect will drain all over you.  You need to make sure you don't have more than 35 gallons in the waste tank before emptying into the tote.  There are two hollows by the hose which don't allow all of the water to drain out of the tote because if you tilt the tote, some of the water goes into those hollows and not out of the hose.  You will ALWAYS have liquid left in the tote no matter how much you raise (unless you decide to turn the tote over and drain the remainder through the top hole (I'm sure a big mess will result and not everything will make it in the drain). The connector with the hose and swivel connector is very weak.  If you tighten it too much, it breaks.  If you don't tighten it, it leaks or the swivel connector comes off spilling the contents all over you.  Someone suggested a 2" coupler cut to size and inserted into the hose to be able to tighten the hose clamp on the swivel connector.  I'll try that to see if I can get the hose to tighten properly.  Unfortunately, I purchased two of these (because of the name) so I will try to make these work as long as possible.  We have a 70g grey water tank so I figured two of these would do us just fine.... the aggravation has not made it worth it.

title: Made a big difference, size provided is limiting factor
text:
Mothers makes dependable well priced products. This kit worked decently but it left things lacking. I have a black 2006 Volvo S60R. It has been babied this past year (I've owned it for a month now), but in full sun and up close, you can tell it's almost 12 years old. I did things a bit backwards and waxed it the moment I got it (CarGuys liquid wax), and it shines like hell but the finish was still a bit rough and the amount of metallic in the black sapphire paint actually accentuates instead of hides swirls, scratches, etc.

This kit will likely only last you a single venture. The clay bars are very small. The spray bottle pretty much ran out right at the end. To be fair I was working in a do-it-yourself car wash so I could wash before and after and the wind was howling non-stop so that likely 50% of the spray didn't get to lay on the car anyway. But regardless, I wouldn't count on getting two goes from one bottle much less these two tiny bars. The kit was easy to use and comes with an absorbant wiping cloth as well. My only beef with the cloth is the huge Mother's branded tag on it.

I will say this made a noticeable difference in the slick/smoothness of the pain but I can still feel some imperfections, I likely needed to start out with a higher grade and work down to finer versions. Still, the beading and gleam after just clay barring and pre-second wash was impressive. It did catch on some of the rougher plastic body kit panels and where there's a deep scratch on one trim panel, but it cleaned up easily.

The finish I got after re-waxing after using this kit was noticeably improved, scratches etc still visible but the finish was such a smooth glossy sheen even in cloudy/overcast/darkening light.

Considering I find it even harder to take my eyes off my car, I'd say this product is worth it. I'm not 100% satisfied with either Mothers or Meguire's but until I find a kit with a bigger volume of cleaner and larger bars for a similar price, I'll keep buying this twice a year.

title: Nice sun shade, but the pouch is a very tight squeeze...
text:
I got this Magnelex Car Windshield Sun Shade with Storage Pouch for a new to me 2006 Saturn SES, which will arrive in a couple of weeks. It seems to be very nicely made, with a good thickness, especially in the circular areas. There seems to be some extra material in those areas that I wish went throughout the entire sun shade.
I'm used to having the cheap rectangular sun shades that fold up much the same as this one does. This one is a bit more fiddly, but within a short time I had it folded back up. I'm sure I will be able to fold it within a few seconds after a couple more times. The trouble came when I tried to place it back into the pouch.
It is obviously neatly folded by a machine and placed into the pouch to start with, but once the buyer takes it out, it can never be folded that neat and compact again. Therefore, it is quite a struggle to get it back into the pouch. Even then, part of it sticks out. The pouch should have been made a bit bigger to accommodate its final bloated state.
Because my car has not arrived yet, I could not try it for size, but it is in the list for the medium size sun shade. If there are any issues once I get it, I will come back and update. Aside from the pouch being a tight squeeze, this sun shade should do great at keeping my car cooler and protecting its surfaces from UV damage. It is a nice sun shade, and I would definitely recommend it!

title: Battery is dead, but the lights say it fully charged. 👺
text:
I have been on lockdown since March 16th and have tried keeping up with starting my car every week to every other week to make sure it stayed running. Well, needless to say, I must have messed up recently and went out and it almost started but didn't quite make it. I had ordered this little device, just in case that happened one day so I would be set.

I have tried following the directions given and also watching the video, but when I plug the device into my car's dead battery all of the lights just stay lit. They never blink, change the percentage, or anything. I don't think it is working at all. I hear some kind of clicking sound where it's hooked to the battery, but still, the lights are just all lit. It says it will show what percentage your battery is charged to, which should be minimal since only a few small things come on when I turn the ignition switch. But, by looking at it, my battery is fully charged and ready to go. It's not.

I am saddened because I have finally been given the all-clear to leave home by my doctors and this little device was my ticket out of here. But, it just isn't working. I hate to give it a bad mark, but it does nothing but light up.

title: Holds 60ml of water, but doesn't dispill quite that much. But, ohh it makes your car smell good!!
text:
I thought this little gadget was going to be a great idea and would help the air quality and calm my nerves in the car. It definitely does the trick. It has a few quirks, but overall I am very happy with how it performs.
Pros-
-It fits in a cup holder
-After running for a bit, you get a nice stream of "smoke".
-It's great for having your essential oil fix on the go. Especially, if your sick and need to have some sinus clearing or headache relieving recipe to help you feel better while driving.
-Also great for getting rid of other odors and germs in the car. I like to disperse tea tree and lavender all the time--they help with odors and can help keep your car free from germs flying around.
- It has extra ports to charge other devices.
Cons-
- It holds 60mls but will only use about 40 of them before it no longer disperses.
- Opening the lid to refill always leaves a little mess of dripping water and essential oils.
- The lid screws on, but if you turn it over it will spill. (I know you shouldn't turn it over. But, if you need to move it from one holder to another, it could happen).
- There should be some sort locking mechanism, to make it both spill proof and childproof.

As a lone driver, I think this is a great concept, but if you have small kids, I would be more careful to watch them closely so that they don't get into it. I give this a solid A and definitely recommend it.

If done right both ends will easily slide into place of the ball connectors of the trunk. Then press the clips back onto the housing to lock them in place. Trunk raises so much easier and doesn’t fall down on you.  Super fix at a reasonable price

title: Quieter than my pancake compressor. Speedy. Only light OR pump – not both. Only 8’ power cord.
text:
This pump works well. It pumps up quickly and compared to the pancake style air compressor I have in my garage, this is much quieter. I can’t be positive, but my tire gauge did show a higher PSI than I set the machine for. My tire gauge has been very consistent for me, but maybe it’s consistently 2-3 PSI low? Regardless, something to check for yourself. The pump does turn off by itself when it is up to the PSI you select. Anyone should be able to use it.

The cord is about 8 feet. This may struggle to reach back tires of larger vehicles. Another couple of feet would have been preferred. The pump has a light on it, but the light and pump can not both be on at the same time, so you can set yourself up with the light, but you’ll have to turn that off when you start pumping. I did not expect this shortcoming, which would be annoying late at night. It’s small and lightweight, and as an emergency item, will mostly sit in people’s trunks. Hopefully the plastic is up to hanging around in an environment that can bet quite hot. I’ll update this review if I have any issues.

title: Nice full glass bulb with no plastic base. Doesn’t dim well, flickers at lower light.
text:
This review is for the six pack A19 “40 watts” dimmable bulbs. Aesthetically, these are nice bulbs. They are full glass and do not have an unsightly plastic base holding circuitry. They are no brighter than a true old-fashioned incandescent 40 watt bulb at full brightness. They were slightly dimmer than expected and were dimmer than the opaque (white) bulbs they were going to replace (also 40 watt equivalent).

My issue is with the dimming – they dim poorly. They have about two stages – brightest, then suddenly dim, then off. In the dim stage, they do flicker, especially compared to other LED bulbs in the same fixture. I would say these should be used only at full brightness.

title: Smell nice, not overpowering, but short lived.
text: I really wanted to be able to rate these higher. They are cute, well packaged, and smell nice. They are not overpowering, but they also do not last. For one, I put it in a spare small bathroom that always has the door opened. This room is basically never used. After about a week, it was really difficult to smell it. After 10 days, you wouldn’t even know it was there next to you. For another, I put it in a small closet that always has the door shut. After two weeks you can still smell this one, but it is very, very faint. These are rated thirty days, but you really only give half that. Five stars for the niceness of the scents, 1 star for the longevity.

title: Better than the original filter, by far!
text: Great purchase. This filter costs less than half the price of an original Honda filter and is of much better quality. This filter is more rigid and fits in the compartment behind my glove box perfectly - snugly. The original was a looser fit which lead to more noise and less filtration as air could easily get around the filter. The 2016 Civic has a poor recirculated air feature (if you drive through a smelly area, turning on recirculated air does not stop the outside air from coming in) and this better fitting filter with activated charcoal helps with the problem. I will definitely use another Installer Champ filter when it comes time to change the cabin air filter again. I'm so glad I took a chance on this. Highly recommended.

Of course you won't need this when its raining, but do not forget to take it off in case it rains while the car is parked or you may get water in your car. Check the images to see what i mean. title: Works as Expected - Looks Great
text:
Why did I want to paint my calipers Red? I actually still can't answer that. But I did get a silver on black vehicle with 20 inch wheels that have an open pattern and I thought it would look cool. It does!

Process - I removed the wheels and I removed the calipers, although removing the calipers in not necessary. It just makes for a much cleaner job. The car only had a few hundred miles on it, so cleaning the calipers was very easy. I used some alcohol and then a damp rag and let them dry. I then put on a light coat, which did not cover very wall at all. I let it sit for 2 hours. I plied a second coat, let it sit for 2 hours. Then I applied a thick coat and let is sit for 3 hours. I put it all back together and wiped it all down. I didn't drive the car to 48 hours.

Color - Depending on the lighting, they can look Red or Orange red. With direct sunlight, the orange shows more. The images speak for themselves.

Overall - The process was fairly straight forward. You need to prepare and be patient if you want this to look good and last. I did 4 large calipers and still have more than half left. Plenty for any future touch ups. . As for longevity, it's still too soon to tell. I have now driven a bunch more miles and they loo perfect.

title: Does exactly what it says it does,. - Follow these directions
text:
Does exactly what it says it does,. This thing works great on everything I have used it on. The key is you have to drag the item across the device several time for the demagnification to work. If you just hold it in the middle, not only wont it get demagnetized, it may get more magnetized. I have used it on Tweezers, screw dicers big and small, teeny tiny screws from a watch, all with 100% success.

Directions: Press the button, hold the item with light pressure onto the surface of one side of the device. Drag the item from side to side with slight pressure down two or three times. More times for larger objects. Release the button when the item is on the side, not in the middle of the device. check, repeat if necessary. You should be good to go!

title: Wiring Kit and Horn Review
text:
I recently was almost run off the road on my Suzuki V-Strom by a driver merging onto the freeway. She was singing to a tune and never looked into the lane she was changing into, which happened to be mine. I blew my horn which had no affect at all. My factory motorcycle horn is about equivalent in volume to a person blowing their nose with a bad cold. My only option was to speed up and get in between her and the car on my left. Once I got clear I was determined to get a new horn.

I received my order in only 2 days using the standard ground shipping option. That was surprising since some of the stuff from Amazon lately has taken 2 weeks to get to me. I also ordered the optional wiring kit which came in the same box. I strongly suggest you get this kit unless you have a garage full of different gauge wires and connectors.

Installation,
It took me 2 hours to install this horn. [[ASIN:B000NPRTII Black Stebel Nautilus Compact Motorcycle Air Horn - Loud]] First it's not small so you have to find a suitable mounting place. Forget about mounting it where the existing hockey puck size horn is. Then you have to buy or fabricate your own mounting bracket because it doesn't come with any way to attach it to the bike. The one screw it does come with is stated in the instructions as having to be torqued to 50 foot pounds. For a horn? There are no written wiring instructions with the horn, but there is with the optional wiring kit. But unless you want to be confused, don't read the instructions and instead follow the wiring diagram which is the same on both the horn and wiring kit. The outcome was good but it took a lot longer then I expected. If you are not good with electrical wiring expect to spend even more time.

Bottom Line:
THIS HORN IS LOUD! It does exactly what it says it does. It corrects what I believe is a major safety flaw on most bikes and some cars.

Why not five starts:

The written instructions are confusing. Use the diagram instead.

title: Fantastic set but with one major flaw
text:
[[VIDEOID:32f76fe39b3a76182672d324c49ef9a2]] I was looking forward to getting my hands on this do-it-all inflator. And I was not disappointed when I received it.
The quality of the item and accessories are outstanding. Whoever designed the unit thought of everything – battery power, vehicle 12V power, different attachments and the preset function which was a big selling point for me.
I used the 20V battery power to inflate the wheels on our car. I preset to 33 psi and pressed the start button. As expected, the inflator stopped at 33 psi. However, shortly thereafter the real-time pressure reading has increased from 33 to 34.5 psi. This was unexpected and I was unsure at this point what the actual pressure is. I caught that in the video.
Fortunately I carry a pressure gauge in the glove compartment and the actual pressure was 34.5 psi. So the inflator went above the preset pressure by 1.5 psi. I had to deflate all the wheels by that amount.
So there goes the 2 stars deduction.

title: This Thing Is A Beast! (And That Is A Good Thing)
text:
I am impressed with the ratchet winch. I grew up using something very similar to help guide trees to the proper direction when cutting them down. We also used it to pull stumps out of the ground, after digging them out. This 5 ton ratchet winch makes those that I used growing up look like toys. This is a very sturdy, very well constructed heavy-duty tool.

I have already used it for cutting down a tree on our property. Place a chain around the tree to be cut (high up), another chain around another tree (low down), connect both ends of the ratchet winch to the chains, tighten, and the tree will fall where you want it to fall. The length of the cable on the device it not too long, but it is sufficient. It is a little stiff to release the cable, but it got better after using it a bit. The metal could be a bit smoother, but since you really should be wearing leather gloves while using this, that is not a big deal. I did have to take a file and smooth one section down a little.

A well made ratchet winch that does the job it was made for. Strong, sturdy, heavy duty, and at a price point that makes it attractive to the pocketbook.

title: Works great!
text:
We had previously tried vent clip phone holders. Was challenging to find a vent clip phone holder that would even work on Jeep vents. The ones we tried never seemed to be secure enough and would eventually fall off or sag. That's when we decided to try a dash mounted phone holder......much better solution!!!!

There were no instructions in the box which seems to be the norm anymore. There were instructions online. They were relatively easy to follow. It is secured with a screw, but could easily be removed if you do not want the phone holder anymore, sell the vehicle, etc....

It is a very sturdy "contraption". It does mount the phone much higher than a vent clip device. Took us a bit to get used to, but now we like this.

There is an American flag sticker on the phone mount that is visible when the phone is not in the holder. I would have preferred there was nothing instead. Not because it's the flag, but I just would have preferred an all black holder. I prefer that look instead.

Price wise this was one of the more fair priced I found compared to other similar devices.

Very pleased with this purchase.

title: WOW!  Great product and price point makes it even better!
text:
WOW!! Far sturdier of a case than I anticipated! I had seen the photos online and read the comments, but never truly know what to expect until a product arrives. The photos online are true to the product and it's as durable and protective of a case as it appears online.

I am using an iphone 10 with a protective case. The bike phone mount is spring loaded to easily adjust to different phone sizes. I'm able to quickly put my phone in to the bike mount and easily remove it when done riding. I LOVE that I don't have to take my phone from it's case before putting it in this holder. That's a definite plus for me. All of the photos online show phones withOUT a case in the holder so was concerned I may not be able to use the product while the phone was in the case. Checked that box for what I was looking for!

We often transport our bikes longer distances on the back of our Jeep. I prefer to remove these types of contraptions for these instances. The mount for the holder went on to the handle relatively easy and won't be too time consuming or difficult to remove if/when we are traveling. There were no tools required. There were instructions provided, but were not needed. I tend to be a "slow learner" and even I didn't need instructions! :)

The mount clamps tightly to my handle bar. There is not a lot of vibration and bouncing around while riding. Another plus!

This is a sturdy product and is exactly as advertised if not better. What makes it even more impressive is the price point! Thrilled with my purchase!

title: Love this thing!
text:
I'm not being melodramatic when I tell you I love this thing. I really do. I had been wanting a battery-powered air compressor for a while now, but have only seen stuff that looks like disappointing generic crap. I was sort of hoping one of my favorite 12v tool manufacturers would come out with something, but they haven't yet. But when I saw this thing, I immediately recognized that it appeared to be a serious product. Quick search confirmed, although it may be a relatively new company, they were serious when they made this.

Right out of the box, it feels, looks, - and even smells - great. This is quality, I can tell. It was less than half power, but I went out and took four bike tires from atmosphere to 55 psi, and then four car tires from 29 to 36 psi. The battery was now almost empty, but it did what I needed it to do!

Of course I have a big compressor, but that is a lot of overhead just to fill some tires, so I had been using this little thing that plugs into a car's 12V port (or using an AC adapter with the car port) - I actually sort of hate that thing, especially in my old garage, which was really tight, especially since I always parked so close to the walls to keep the cars apart from each other. It was time consuming, loud, annoying to spool back up, difficult to get to the tires to the point you'd have to re-run the power cord multiple times, and then it was hard to thread on the schrader valve. Also, if you put the unit on something, it would vibrate itself off and crash onto the floor.

This one takes about the same amount of time per wheel, although maybe a little less. Impressive regardless considering (not sure if that's a complete sentence, but you get the point).

This is still loud enough that you'd be smart to wear hearing protection (and I do), but it is quieter than the other, and surprisingly quiet in my opinion.

No spooling back up cables! No re-running power - or any - cables!

At first glance, I was disappointed that it didn't have one of those qucik-clip shrader value adapters, because I hate the loss you get when unscrewing a hose. But I was so happy how little of that there is with this one. I think it may be that there is just a deeper threaded piece to the adapter so that by the time you start depressing the valve, you're already holding the air in with the threads. Also, I think it makes a difference that the head turns very independently, so you're not there trying to turn the hose onto the valve's threads and you end up turning the whole hose. So that's a very, very positive thing. I will say, though, that the threads - both male and female - that connect the device to the hose are metal, but the female threads on the other end of the hose are plastic. That seems unfortunate, but I will be incredibly careful not to do anything to damage those, because the joy of it working as well as it does is too great to risk by not being careful and potentially ruining those threads by cross-threading.

It doesn't vibrate much, but I'm still going to be careful with it. And it must vibrate some because if you put it on a concrete floor, you'll get some scratches in the back, which is very sad since this thing looks and feels so nice. For that reason - and to keep the accessories with it, I'd love to have a protective case that wasn't too much bigger than the device, but that you could actually keep it in for the most part while using it. I think they do sell a kit, but I haven't looked at it.

Oh, and it's super simple to use, just a few very intuitive button presses, and it has a light you can turn on which is just great. Also can be used as a USB charger in an emergency (or anytime, but it seems prudent that it be your true emergency backup). Big backlit screen with big numbers that shows your actual pressure and your set pressure in a few different units (well, one unit at a time, but you can choose multiple).

This is a huge convenience, especially because bike tires always loose air quickly, and because you really should keep the right amount of air in your car tires. I'd never really consider myself lazy, but...even I can get lazy about stuff like that when it's such a PITA, which it is without this battery powered compressor.

Oh, I got an error message the first time I tried to recharge it. I assume it was just a "wait until I cool down" message, but the manual should tell you that. The manual otherwise seems pretty good. Haven't had that Error message since.

This is the kind of tool you're excited to show your friends.

title: Compared to another brand.
text:
I have another one of these by a different brand that I keep in the other car. Both are high end brands (I'd never bother having a generic safety device) with similar CCA ratings and from this same time period (technology more or less the same).

This is clearly awesome, incorporating all the features one might want and with the fanciest lights and tech, but it does differ from the other in a few ways worth considering:

The other one comes with a semi-rigid case, which I really like. This one comes with a soft bag, which is better than nothing.

That said, this one takes up less space, partly because it doesn't have the case, but it also doesn't NEED the case as much as the other one does because it does not need a special 18V AC-DC adapter.

The fact that this one charges via USB is one of its best points because that means you can "top off" charge it in the car instead of having to bring it in the house or hook it up to an outlet in the garage, running the risk of leaving it behind. That by itself sort of edges this one above the other in my opinion.

The other one has separate cables, which are a little longer, but use a proprietary connection (I think it's proprietary), while this one has short, hardwired cables that clip nicely onto the sides, making this super portable (both are very nicely sized compared to lugging around an old full-size jump pack).

Speaking of charging, both can be used as a battery pack for your cell phone and devices, but this one can actually high output charge (20v, at least 2A, I think) via USB-C, while the other only outputs via USB-A (5v, I'm guessing 2.1A). And this can charge itself via USB-C, and has an indicator light to show when it is charging in this way, so that is just as good if not better than the other's 18V adapter.

In a way, it is counter-intuitive to use this to charge your devices, as you don't want to lower its output potential in the event you need a jump, but to charge a phone (once) is pretty insignificant. And...most horror movies start with a dead cell phone, so this is a nice safety feature.

Both have lights and the safety features, with an override feature for super-dead batteries. Both are fantastic in just about every way. You know, if this thing had a semi-rigid case so you don't have to worry about it banging around in your trunk, I think it would very clearly be the winner.

title: Works great.
text:
Like a lot of other reviewers mentioned, this either doesn't come with a straw or they just fall off frequently, because mine didn't have a straw either.

This stuff is awesome. I haven't actually used it before this, but now I'm excited to have a drier alternative to WD-40 and other lubes. It's great for moving parts that spray all the liquid types away, and also good for when you want to keep it off an adjacent surface, particularly when on a vertical surface. Works great.

title: High capacity
text: This is an excellent replacement battery.  It has a very standard size, but has a 33% higher amp-hour rating than other batteries I have in this size.  Seems like these are supposed to be safer, yet otherwise comparable, to regular lithium ion batteries, so I feel pretty good about using them, even for home applications.

title: Fantastic Set.
text:
I really love this tool. This is one of those tools that just seems so well thought-out, engineered, and machined that it's a treat for a tool lover like myself. Yes, I only use rivet nuts rarely, and I already have a pull rivet tool, but this adds some functionality that I can use from time to time and be very happy with. (I didn't have any preconception about this before it came, because I was not familiar with Eastvolt, but I had come to the conclusion it was a "real" company).

Even the case is quite well engineered. It is not super strong, but as long as the flaps that click into place don't break off, it is sufficient. But I love how each rivet nut head and reamer head has its own case to keep the pieces together and from scratching each other. This also makes it easier to fit everything back into this tightly packed space and find what you need more easily.

The only thing that's just slightly imperfect is that to put everything back in the case, you have to set it back up for pull rivets. So if you use this primarily for rivet nuts, that might be a little irritating. Also, one side houses the tool and the other the accessories.

Oh, and the two reamer heads are both pretty large, at least compared to all the sizes of rivet nuts, so I thought the sizes were an odd choice. Frankly, it could use more sizes of rivet nut heads and reamers, but I'm guessing they have bigger kits for that; as it is, I feel like this is a fairly diverse and fairly specialized tool.

There is a halfway decent instruction sheet to tell you how to change out the pieces, but it is relatively intuitive. All the pieces screw on super smooth and work like a charm. The rivet nut holders can be unscrewed from the actual rivet nuts without having to turn the whole tool. It comes with a bunch of extra o-rings, which help hold these accessories in place. The pull rivet heads fit on the tool itself.

All this and even coated lightly with the sweet scent of gun oil. A very satisfying tool to have in ones chest.

title: Limited, but adequate, power
text:
This really isn't a bad little device. It's not awesome, but I didn't think it would be. It does have adequate suction and it will clean your car. Frankly, even though it's corded, it's still easier to deal with than a long hose on a shop vac, in which case it becomes cumbersome always switching sides of the car, having to drag the vacuum over, etc.

This makes a lot more sense, except I hate to run too much off the DC port on a car unless I have it up on a battery tender (or running, and I hate to run a car just to run a small appliance). Since it can run on 12V DC anyway, it'd be great if it had a battery, even if it could only do small jobs.

The little hose they give you is probably going to crack almost immediately, but if you're gentle with it, it'll work for a while. The crevice tool fits right inside the vac anyway. The bag they give you is a bit big for what you need, but anyway, you can keep this whole thing in your car if you don't have a garage or a place to put it. Anything is better than paying to use someone else's vacuum to clean your car.

Maybe not the best solution ever, but it will certainly work out well for some people in some situations.

title: Screws and Bumps
text:
I can't say I'm a fan of this system. Putting all these screws into the roof of my car is a little stomach unsettling. I didn't realize that was how it had to happen. You screw these flexible little pieces into the roof and then cover them with covers that snap into place.

That leaves bigger than desired bumps on the car roof, and the entire kit doesn't show any traits of great quality at all. A last resort, I guess, but I think I'll just try some fabric glue first and hope it works out.

title: Why the white?
text:
I have use for these all over the interior of my old BMW and both the interior and exterior of a middle-aged Toyota. They absolutely come in good handy, especially because you often break them getting them off (so if you're taking apart your interior to run wires, you'd be smart to have a set of these at your disposal).

I have another similar kit with similar pieces, and in that kit, everything is black. I may be missing something (like knowledge about a particular brand that for some reason would have both black and white components), but I don't see the point in having one of these be white; I certainly don't have any white mixed in with all the black in my two cars.

Anyway, quite useful, at least.

title: Simple, but useful
text:
This is about as basic as you get, but I think it's probably all anyone would really need (not everyone wants to drill and anchor stuff into their concrete garage floors, although I wouldn't mind...but at least if you want to change the placement of this, it won't leave you with extra holes).

It is basically a cut cross-section of an extruded 3-D plastic with reinforcing "beams" inside. It has a two-sided tape on the bottom to attach it to your freshly cleaned garage floor. The yellow is stickers you have to put on.

I can park very well, even in my small garage, but I see this as useful anyway. For example, if you want to park the one car front far enough to get the bike racks on the back and still not have the garage door come down onto the front of the car, you have just a very few inches of tolerance, which can be difficult to eyeball without getting out of the car. So...like they say: "for perfect placement every time".

title: Full featured.
text: This is a pretty comprehensive kit and provides a much more robust solution than I was originally anticipating.  Almost everyone can use the anti-rattle pads that these come with.  I'm still unsure if I actually like the "smoked" look or if it helps against cameras, but it doesn't hurt, and would probably look the best on a black car with a white license plate (like Maryland).  Regardless of the style, the kit is impressive.

title: Frequent Uses.
text:
This is a great set to have. I managed to use about 10 right away - between two cars - simply because I had so many that I never replaced; sometimes you can get away with that, but sometimes the trim pieces come apart and show a seam. So having this around won't allow me to be lazy in the future.

My tiniest nitpick would be that it is in a different shape and size of case than all the other "parts" cases out there. i.e., I have a pile of rectangular plastic parts cases that at least all make a uniform pile, but this one doesn't stack nicely; no big deal.

title: Perhaps perfect.
text:
This thing is just all around awesome. It's much smaller than my previous jump pack, and I imagine the battery will last longer since my previous jump pack was like carrying an extra car battery around whereas this is lithium. There are some really small power banks that say they can start a car, but I have my doubts about those. This, I absolutely believe in.

It really just oozes quality. Each part seems to be so well thought out and designed. First, it comes with a nice, semi-rigid case that holds everything nicely including the instruction manual (OK, if anything could be better, the instruction manual would be smaller length- and width-wise, and they'd give you one in just English and one in just Spanish so you could pick one and carry around less weight and volume overall). The complete case is smaller than my previous jump pack.

There are three port areas on the device that are all covered by a water- and damage-resistant cover which is held to the device by integrated tether so you don't lose them.

It also manages to integrate some other worthwhile security features, like the light - which can also do an SOS pattern in Morse code - and the USB ports (face it, if you can't keep a working cell phone, horror movies prove that you will be murdered), and the (external) "cigarette outlet" port so you can charge or use whatever other emergency devices you keep in your car that might not be available if your battery is dead.

And there are a lot of integrated safety features for people that don't know how to jump start a battery. The great news is that is what the override button is for, just in case it's a difficult battery to jump.

They ask that you charge it every three months, which is normal for anything with a battery. The reality is that it can probably go much longer, but this is an investment worth protecting, of course.

I've only ever used a few jump packs, but frankly, I just can't imagine a better one. Seems like they got it all figured out.

title: Thin and flexible.
text: In my E36 (BMW), I can get a regular (thickness) bit around my spark plugs, however, I can see how this thin wall is quite useful for the majority of cars.  Quality appears to be very good when you take into account that it is supposed to be thin.  The ball joint is not as smooth as some, but this is a function of its thinness as well.  Seems like a good choice for the job.

title: Slightly long for at least one use.
text: I had a place in mind for these in my van, but I actually suspected they wouldn't fit, and they didn't.  These are just a tiny bit longer than regular bulbs and that enclosure just wasn't having it.  However, I think found a great use for them on my Dad's trailer; they work quite nice there.  No complaints, just eyeball your space before buying to get a good idea if it can accommodate a few extra millimetres.

title: Nice size and good output.
text:
This does have enough output to fuel my niece's old Barbie car. I did have to change the leads on the car, but no big deal. I also hooked up some Battery Tender cables in parallel for easy charging. Pretty nice setup.

I keep an eye on any Li-ion batteries when charging, meaning I don't charge them unless I'm around the house. They obviously have many advantages over others, but I know some still randomly can be hazardous, although this claims to have various protection circuits. I don't doubt them, but I'm always careful. Nice replacement battery, and it'd be good for DIY electronics projects as well.

title: Gear Puller
text:
I am a bit skeptical of how this page is currently set up in that it has so many different products listed together, so one poor product might benefit from high reviews on the other products. Keep that in mind if you are researching diligently.

Anyway, I have the gear puller. And it is, admittedly, a pretty nice piece. It's a little better than its most simple counterparts, being well-adjustable, and for both inner and outer pulls. Coarse threads provide smooth and strong leverage that you need in something like this. Definitely a very solid product and a must for any sort of decent tool shop.

title: Cool tool.  Could it be improved?
text:
This is a really neat idea for a really neat tool. Of course - as a tool aficionado - I had to have it.

It is not nearly as large - even unfolded - as a regular 4-point lug wrench, but I can get enough leverage out of it - being fairly strong - as long as some cut-rate mechanic didn't over-torque the lugs with the hope that if you can't get them off, then you HAVE to come back.

Anyway, it is super cool, but I find it counter-intuitive that the largest socket points are on the static arms. It seems like you'd want the static arms perpendicular to the sockets that are likely to require the most force. So that's a little strange, but I could be thinking about it wrong.

So obviously this folds up nicely, but if you think about it, there's really no need to have a multi-size lug wrench in your car unless you for some reason have mismatched wheels or you're just hoping to be a hero some day when driving around randomly. And in the shop...I guess you have room for a regular one. So...I guess you don't really need it...but it is cool...so maybe you do. Up to you.

title: Medium sized bottles
text: Works well on my car, and I'm happy to have a trusted brand and a formula meant for cars so that I can be sure it won't cause extra wear on my paint.  You get quite a few bottles, but I've seen other packs that have fewer, but larger, bottles.  And I'm not entirely sure what the actual product difference is.  Anyway, these bottles are actually convenient to store, where the 64 oz. bottles are not.  Solid product.

title: Big Pack of Suds.
text: My car's sitting pretty.  For now and some time to come, with four big bottles of these cleaner.  Glad to have it that way - it will encourage me to wash the car more often and not skimp on the soap.  Glad to have cleaner specially formulated for car washing, as I don't want to take any chances with my paint.  Armor All has always been trustworthy...

title: Very useful and appears well-made.
text: This is a very nicely made tool.  My first grease gun, but it seems to perform quite smoothly.  I like that the line is flexible to allow you to get into tight spaces; for a second I had actually been wondering why this wasn't more like a caulking gun, but of course that would be a terrible design.  Definitely better than having to spread and pack grease by hand.  I like it.

title: Good hybrid.
text: I really like this type of wash that has the wax included.  It seems like it actually comes out cleaner than when you get wax bits stuck in hard to remove places after going through the trouble to wash the car.  And of course it saves time and therefore I'll do it more often.  It does seem to actually have a good waxing quality to it, so I'm happy with it and feel it is definitely a superior product to a straight wash.  Of course, a really, really good manual wax is still superior, but this doesn't preclude me from doing a manual wax as well.

title: Codes definitions built in.
text: I wasn't expecting much out of this because I have another "unbranded" OBD2 reader.  But I was pleasantly surprised that this has the actual code descriptions built-in, so you don't have to drag the manual with you every time...doesn't seem like a big deal, but this is a nice touch I wasn't expecting.  I didn't even bother looking at the manual - it was intuitive and easy to use (but I did know you needed the ignition (only) on to actually start reading codes).  This is easily my favorite now.

title: Simple.  Effective.  Black.
text: Simple.  Effective.  Black.  Can't beat it.  Everyone with a decent subwoofer should have this on their car...but honestly, it's a good thing to have even if you don't listen to good music loudly because it looks nice and clean and won't allow any scratching or rattling.

title: Simple and Effective.
text:
This seems like a no-brainer. I'm sort of surprised these backings are ubiquitous on all cars, even those that aren't blasting bass all the time. A lot of cars have rattling license plates, I've noticed, often with the driver being unaware.

This reminds me of something made in a 3D printer, albeit with some skill and a fairly large printer. Quality is good.

title: Great safety goggles.
text:
These are easily the best safety goggles I've ever had, hands down. And I have had plenty. These are so crisp and clear, but also conform to my head and temples the way a good pair of snorkeling goggles do (although not so tight like some snorkeling goggles can get). You sort of feel invincible when wearing the appropriate safety gear - and this is one of those times. Great for grinding or soldering or whatever you're doing where you need to guarantee nothing can get in your eyes.

They also fit over my glasses without any issues.

title: Menacing
text:
Wow, now I'm one of those people that annoys everyone else because my bulbs are an ultra cool shade. It does make the car look a bit newer, which is nice. Here I thought the yellowing of my enclosure was making the light look yellow, but I guess it was just the actual bulb.

My lights were already very bright compared to any car I've had in the past, but the cooler shade makes a lot of difference.

These seem like pretty good quality as well, so hopefully they hold up. I don't see why not!

title: Nice for custom installs.
text:
This is a pretty nice fuse block if you're doing some custom work on your car (or other DC application). Like all good DC components, it has a clear plastic cover so you can see what's going on in there. Obviously makes the most sense if you need multiple circuits in your trunk or farther away from the main fuse box, but great for multiple amps (take note of the per circuit rating) and/or lighting setup. Simple but effective,

Also would work well for building a camper van. Comes with a lot of labels for all kinds of stuff I hadn't thought of initially, although I won't be surprised if it's missing one you need (but that's what label makers are for. Nice.

title: Working
text: I had put some touch-up paint on my car to cover some minor scratches.  And it's always annoyed me how you can see the touch-up paint - even though it is OEM - in a certain light.  This kit sort of took the touch-up paint off and made my scratches almost disappear to the point where I definitely wouldn't bother with touch-up paint!  Great!  I was half afraid to try this on my beautiful car, but I should have done it years ago instead of living with scratches.

title: Slight reformulation.
text: This is great stuff.  Nothing I know of is more powerful (I'm not a pro mechanic, but I can definitely eat through some crust with this stuff).  Mostly seems like WD-40, but I can tell it is a bit different somehow, perhaps from the smell.  Comes with the old-school skinny tube for spraying in hard to reach areas.

title: All the accessories you could imagine.
text:
While this seems almost a little like overkill for a simple air pressure gauge, it's definitely easier and (more luxurious?) than an air chuck and separate pressure gauge.

To attach to a Schrader valve, simply press the lever, and push onto the valve. When you release the lever, it catches onto the threads. This is especially nice when you're doing a tire that needs frequent attention, because nothing sucks worse than stripping your threads (especially on your inflator), because then you have a fight on your hands every time.

It also comes with a pneumatic quick release, right angle adapter (which is nice, but means you'll have to use those threads, although at least the outside threads on rather than having to turn the entire adapter), core remover tool (which is great to have, although I'm not sure how often you'll actually need it), and even the tiniest roll of Teflon tape I've ever seen. So while my overall feel for the quality or "premiumness" of the product may be 4-stars, they just give you all you could ever want in such a package.

I hate AAA batteries, though, but what are you doing to do? I'd almost take an analog gauge in this type of setup just to avoid the batteries, but I'm guessing the batteries will last super long.

title: Perfectly sized.
text: This is a very nice little inverter.  It's about as small as any 12 to 120V inverter I've ever seen, and - although it's not inverting much power - it is enough for most laptops.  And this is what you really need if you're a road warrior working from your car.  Actually, I like that it's not oversized.  I don't live in my car, and therefore I don't need to run appliances on this thing.  USB ports are a bonus if you need them.  Easily fits - or even mounts - in a glove compartment.

title: Synthetic motor oil.
text: Seems like great oil.  I can't imagine it's not just a re-labeled major brand.  I've yet to be disappointed with anything straight-up branded Amazon.  I have no issues switching whatsoever as long as the price remains right.

title: Finally one that fits
text:
I had spent hours over the course of a few weeks trying to find LED replacement bulbs for the halogen bulbs in my Ancona (early generation) range hood. It was really frustrating because it didn't really seem like anything would fit, so I ultimately ended up buying a 10 pack of halogen lights. This was bothersome because these lights tend to be on a lot, and yet they're one of the only lights in the house that are taking more than 6 watts (40, when the unit is on with two bulbs, to be exact).

Anyway, these fit! Great design and great idea. They look great. At 2700k, I think they are just a shade warmer than the others (which I can only guess now are 3000k); some people might like brighter in the kitchen, but the actual light output did not decrease at all. I actually took a picture to upload with one of each beside each other, but it's a really rather boring picture since you can't much tell the difference.

This one fits, at least in my range hood. I can't imagine you'll find too many it doesn't fit in. Nice job. I'm thrilled.

title: Quick and easy, matching bulbs.
text: Fixed my lopsided headlights right up.  Easy change-out, and I do believe they are actually brighter.  Good deal!

title: C batteries bad.  AC adapter good
text:
I didn't have any trouble with false positives on this thing, as one reviewer mentioned. I am very careful not to bang it around, but I'm not sure having done so would have made a difference. I only have a couple of systems to check - and luckily they came up negative - but I like the specs as quoted. I also like that it comes with a case and a calibration solution. The case isn't fancy, but a case is just about always appreciated, especially when you have extra stuff you want to keep with the main unit (such as the calibration solution).

It's not an exceptionally fancy unit as far as looks or materials, but if it works, it works. You really don't want to pay for fancier plastic. I do wonder why it has to take C batteries, though. They are the same voltage as AAs, but presumably less mAh. Why not just make it use 2+2 AA batteries? No one has C anymore, and I don't wish to keep them on hand.

Oh...but it comes with an AC adapter. Just the fact that it will take one is great. Including it is really nice. You can always run an extension cord if you run out of C batteries. That's enough to put it back at five stars!

title: Plentiful bristles.
text: I often say that AmazonBasics stuff is too good and well made to be called "basic".  In this case, basic is appropriate, but this is a consumable item, so it would be foolish to make this too fancy.  It works as well as any wheel brush.  The bristles are thick and plentiful, but - like any brush safe to use on your wheels - you'll have to apply additional efforts and tools to remove thick grease and tar when you need to.  I'd buy it any time I need one as long as the price remains competitive.

title: A useful package.
text:
This thing is ergonomically and functionally impressive. All cords and accessories wrap up and store in a neat little rectangular brick, which stores in a neat little case that also holds the instructions. The instructions even contain some extra information - like standard inflation ratings on other blow-up items - to fill the extra space. You can't ask for much more in terms of storage and size.

And it works great. It would take you longer than 3 minutes to do a car tire from flat, but it's still quite fast, and it won't run down your battery. I love that it shuts itself off at the pressure you set. I have a big compressor in my basement, but I get sick of pulling the hose all the way out to the garage and starting it up just to fill up a couple tires (especially if it's just a bike tire I need inflated). This makes life much easier for this situation, but it's also quite tempting to leave it in one of the cars for emergencies.

Fantastic execution of a great device.

title: Worlds apart from my generic version
text:
This thing is some kind of work of art. My previous model was just some generic thing with a card insert labeled "Supco" that I got from my local refrigerant store. On that model, you could see the brazed joints, you had to really turn, nothing felt "hydraulic", the seals weren't confidence inspiring, there was no shut off valve, there wasn't a magnet, and there was no tethered cap on the side port you use for metering.

Until I received this Hilmor model, I had no idea that you could even get a valve core removal tool of such quality. It's an all brass beauty, one solid piece from what I can tell, with a smooth plunger and a shut off valve you can use when the plunger is fully extracted. The magnet helps keep the plunger close to the body when you're not pulling it out, and the tethered cap keeps dust and grime out, which is extremely important when dealing with AC systems, especially newer systems using the newer refrigerants (such as R-410a). And especially near vacuum gauge ports.

Like (actual real) Italian food, it is the simple things done really, really right that impress the most. This is one of those things.

title: Always needed around the garage and shop.
text:
I've been meaning to get some more of this (or a product like this) for a couple weeks now. I don't know why I've been so lazy. I've completed the following list in the last few hours:

1. Sprayed a squirt into the lock on my garage door. It gets hard to turn, probably because there is little overhang above that door. A squirt of this makes if feel like new.

2. Stopped my large garage door from squeaking when opening by a little spray where the wheels meet the track.

3. Cleaned some surface rust off my crowbars. Seems to have made the tools like new.

4. Cleaned my ~$100 tree saw blades and left on a coating of STA-BIL before putting them back in their sheathes. I feel a lot better about that now. Seems like the small tree pieces (saw dust) in the teeth can contain moisture, which could corrode over time.

Now I'm caught up. I won't allow myself to run out again, as I use this type of product often. I have no doubt whatsoever that this is as good as other brands.

title: Seemed to work on an old leaf blower.
text: You'll never know if it will work until you try, but I got an old leaf blower I found working without any major maintenance.  (Now that I know it works, I'll go back and clean out the engine).  I definitely think this was the determining factor in my case, so I'm psyched it worked.  I do not recommend purposely letting engines get gummed up by leaving them sit all year, but if they do, this is worth a try!

title: Lights and features.
text:
I have a few other battery chargers/maintainers as well, and while this has more features than most of the bunch, it is not generous with its included accessories. Here are some thoughts, listed:

- Bigger than I imagined, but on par with the others of similar amperage output.

- Sort of odd shape makes a lot of sense when you add the hanger clip and hang it on your hood's locking mechanism.

- Much more information (and more lights) on this thing than any of the others. Starts in standby mode, which makes sense. It tells you how charged the battery is while it's charging.

- This one apparently has an automatic pulse feature that is better for charging deeply discharged batteries.

- This one only comes with alligator clips. Most of the others also include ring terminals and/or a cigarette lighter charger.

- This one has a proprietary connection, but also comes with an adapter to a normal 12V DC plug. Odd combination. Usually proprietary connections are to get you to buy (exclusively) their stuff, but in this case they give you an out by allowing you to convert to the DC plug.

- If I just wanted a battery maintainer, a low output trickle charger is just fine. This one adds a bit of functionality with quicker charging (which did give a totally dead battery what it needed to just barely get a car started for me the other day), and a bunch of claims on smartness and greatness, with a lot of fancy lights to back it up. Somehow - being Bosch - I believe them, since they are well known for innovating designs and commanding knowledge of all things car- and tool-related. (hope I'm not getting soft, as this is perhaps one of the only times in life I'm not completely cynical). Anyway, it's a neat device that I'm happy to have around, and very useful.

...I do frequently use this and other trickle chargers to keep my batteries good while I'm away. Coming home to dead car batteries is no fun, and it happened to me a few times before I was clued in to such devices.

title: Works for '97 3-Series.
text: My center light brake light was out on my '97 3-series, so I made the two side bulbs new via this pack, and used one of those for the center light.  Works.

title: It works.
text:
It works. The plastic top of my last one came away from the metal over the years, and I was unable to use it properly with the plastic part detached. I don't love it because I expect the same will happen to this over time, but it's a quick and easy fix.

Note that in some cars and improper seal on your gas cap will set off the check engine light. A cheap OBD-II tool will turn it off once you fix the underlying problem.

title: Excellent tool to have
text:
I also have a 0.75A Battery Tender and a 2A model by another brand. For my purposes, I use them to charge batteries when I'm gone for a long time, because I've killed batteries less than 2 years old a couple of times due to long trips overseas. In such a case, the amperage really doesn't matter, because you're just keeping a float charge. The amperage matters when you want to quickly charge a drained battery (you'd do well not to let batteries get very drained, because - in the case of car batteries - they are never the same afterward.

This and the 2A model by another manufacturer come with the 12V adapter, which is really nice if you want to run it through a cracked window rather than let your hood open to attach it that way. This matters if you're charging outside a garage and don't want your car tampered with. I most like the permanent ring terminals for my trunk-mounted battery in one car.

Works well. I'd highly recommend any of the three models I have for anyone who goes away or otherwise leaves a car/generator/other sit for long periods of time.

title: Simple and effective
text:
I'll be honest with you - I don't see myself replacing the plastic liners on this thing given the prices I've seen for them on a cursory search. I change my own oil more for the convenience of doing it at home than because I'm cheap, BUT...I am too cheap to buy replacements.

All that said, this is still the best oil pan I've had. I've always had a low open pan for my old 3-Series BMW and a Wal-Mart special for the Corolla. Had to use that open pan on the BMW because the enclosed pan was too tall, tall enough to scrape on the bottom of the Corolla as well. This one is just a little lower, which makes it fit for both cars. It also covers more area and pour better than either of my others, so why didn't I have this useful, simple design in the past? I don't know, but I'm stoked to have this container.

It does have molded "feet" on the corners underneath, but the middle of mine is flexed just enough that it will push oil around if you happen to get it under the container. Nothing's perfect.

And for the record, the plastic sheet is a really good idea, but I sort of can't imagine paying more than $0.20 for something you're just going to use once and throw out. But, that part really doesn't matter to me. I've been wiping oil off of things with old newspapers for years. Why change now?

title: Great resource.
text:
I've come to love my Battery Tender Junior over the years. This Black & Decker model is similarly useful, but with some minor differences.

The BT model I have outputs 750mA and is packaged in a "wall wart" form factor. This sounds convenient, but because my garage outlets are the waterproof kind with little doors on them, I always use an extension cord and put the body in the trunk anyway (my car's battery is in the trunk). Even so, 750mA is completely fine for my needs because I use it just to maintain the battery when I am gone for long periods of time; before I had that setup, I killed a few batteries pre-maturely.

That said, this higher output version is nicer if you ever need to quick charge batteries or maintain a couple in parallel. In my situation, the form factor doesn't really make a difference except with this one, you don't need an extension cord.

Unlike the BT, this one comes with the cables for all three charging options (BT didn't come with the cigarette outlet adapter, if I am remembering correctly). I use the terminal rings and leave an extension hanging out from my battery for quick connect/disconnect. Love the simple outlets with cover to keep them from shorting. The clamps are good if you randomly charge different batteries, but I can definitely see the cigarette outlet adapter being useful, especially if you want to charge your car outside of a garage (you can run it through the window and still lock the doors). Note that if your cigarette outlet is wired to your ignition (i.e., it only comes on when the key is turned on), then you won't be able to charge or maintain via that method (unless you leave your key in and that seems inefficient). Personally, if I had an engine-compartment mounted battery with an inappropriate cigarette-outlet port, then I would run some long leads through the firewall into the glove box for easy, lockable access.

title: Not just for birds.
text:

I looked at some charts between a bunch of Hawk products. They basically showed that these perform even better than the higher models on the first two emergency stops, but then decrease in performance until they have a chance to cool down. That means that these are actually better than their higher end counterparts for a really aggressive driver like myself, but not as good if you're doing track racing.

Despite not really feeling a difference, I don't regret having bought them. My car deserves the best, and if there's any chance it'll keep me out of an accident, it's worth it.

title: Convenient.
text:
My first thought was that these seemed a little wasteful (to include expensive) compared to what you might get out of a liquid bottle. I still hold on to this caveat, but I now realize just how convenient they are for a couple reasons:

For one, when spraying down your dash or other areas you want to clean up, you often end up getting that oily stuff on the Windows, so then they need (re-)washed. These wipes give more control and make that less of a problem. Similarly, if you decide to spray a separate rag and use that to clean, you often end up using a lot of product with much of it going to waste, because a standard rag holds a lot of liquid. These rags are thin - which does mean they don't hold all that much liquid - but you're not wasting any of it.

They're also really good for the quick dusting. You still want to do a thorough job so that you don't see "shine streaks", but it's quick, easy, and painless with the wipes. Frankly, the whole process is a lot easier and you can do pretty much surface area per rag.

Also, the thinness of the rags allows you to clean air vents and the like much easier than trying to shove a thick rag in between each set of fins.

So, probably a little wasteful comparatively, but most likely worth it to save some time, still with great results.

title: New Type of Winch
text:
While I was skeptical about this product at first, it was immediately on arrival that I could tell it was a well made and well thought out piece of equipment. Clearly, it is a quality device with good hardware and design.

Here I had been worried I'd have to break out the corded hammer drill for the job, which led me to wonder if the chuck key would be able to turn while the chuck was around the drive shaft, but when I noticed how high of a gear ratio they used on this thing, I realized that even my 12v Bosch drivers can easily do the job, and that it would work without strain on the drill (the Warn manual specifies the drill should have a minimum 4 N-m of torque). Even better is if you use a 5/16" nut driver bit, it will fit around the shaft without having to tighten the chuck directly around the drive shaft.

The handle is ergonomic and it sets down nicely on its flat bottom. I think there will be times when you wish you could bolt it down somewhere, but any modification to its chassis would make it less portable. I already have a bolt down winch with a capacity of 2000 lbs., but of course it runs only on 12V DC.

This item has the usual lock/unlock spool feature, making it easy to pull out for hookup, and easy to lock for storage or winding.

The one thing you really have to remember is that 500lbs. is all you're going to get out of this device, and you have to remember to take friction and gravity into account. Like, if you're trying to pull a 500lb. device up a ramp without help or wheels, it won't work. This actually has a cutoff at 500lbs., which is a safety feature. It also has the same gauge braided cable as my 2000lb. device, which leads me to believe they take safety seriously.

I really like that the manual tells you how to winch safely and effectively, in clear detail that even a layman can understand. I consider myself well-versed in tools, but I still like to know how to use things the best* way that they can be used.

The only thing I'm lukewarm about, and the only reason I didn't give it five stars, is because I wonder how often I'll use this over a regular winch, or even versus getting a similar product that runs on AC, but has more power (Warn has one, for example). 500 lbs. is not a huge amount of pulling power, and you'll have to carry a drill to use it. So, if you always use a winch to load machines onto your truck, aren't you going to prefer a higher power DC winch? And if you need it around the house, aren't you going to prefer a higher power AC winch? Of course, if you can imagine uses for it away from your truck and house, and you always carry - or don't mind carrying - a drill all the time, then this may actually be more versatile for your needs. And for that matter, it is a nice addition to my DC winch, which is a real pain to use if you don't have a running vehicle nearby.

In summary, I think it's a great product, although relatively niche. If you have a good use - or better, two - in mind for it, then I expect you will be very happy with it.

title: Nothing to do with the sun.
text:
Having gone away from home for long periods of time in the past, I've come home to dead batteries quite a few times. I couldn't be more disgusted than having to drag a battery into Walmart or to some dumb kid in an autoparts store to try and receive my prorated warranty. I am now fully confident in my ability to be sure if the problem is the battery or the charging system, but in my past, my absolute worst fear was that I went through the above process for nothing, that there was nothing wrong with the battery after all.

And so for the average homeowner that maintains his own car, I think this is an excellent, simple and effective device. Of course there are more sophisticated battery testing systems out there that put a heavy load on your battery and analyze each individual cell (this is what they're doing when they test your battery before giving you that prorated warranty), but this will tell you with high certainty what is wrong with your battery or charging system in under five minutes. To me, a great device to have around.

One thing that bothers me: the name. As this product is manufactured by a company called Clore Automotive, how did this thing get the name "Solar"? I could be too cynical, but I swear they are trying to get the ignorant consumer to believe that this is some fancy solar powered device. In fact, it gets its energy from the battery it is testing. That part seems really cheesy and stupid, and if I was 100% sure of my suspicions, I'd probably drop my rating further. But hey, it's a simple device, and I like what it does.

Oh, by the way, it is smaller and better looking than I expected from the pics on Amazon.
