Since there is threading, the handle might be able to be attached to an extension pole if a longer reach is needed provided that you have a pole that fits the threads of the handle. I tried it with a few painting extension poles and none would fit, so it seems the threads are a non-standard size.

While this kit can be used for exterior windows, it's best suited to the interior since the exterior windows can be easily cleaned with a standard squeegee. It lets me clean the interior areas of the windshield that are very hard to clean by hand due to the slope of the windshield where it meets the dash. It's also great for cleaning the top of the dashboard since it can easily reach the far edges with minimal effort.

All in all, it's a very handy item to have to clean the car interior windows quickly and easily. Five stars.

title: Never fail performance; nice compact can
text:
I've been using WD-40 for decades and have never been disappointed in how it performs. This is a great size can to keep at hand, such in the kitchen cabinet, for when it's needed in the house. It comes with a dispensing straw taped to the side for accurate spraying.

Can't live without WD-40!

title: Excellent for mech mods
text:
This is an excellent way to keep bare copper contacts in a mech mod in good shape. It removes light to medium oxidation, protects and keeps contacts cleaner longer, and provides for better conductivity than other contact cleaners. It's also good for cleaning bare copper threading. It has help cut arcing way down, and improved performance. An easy way to keep mech mods in peak shape. It should not, however, be used on plated contacts since it's too aggressive and can damage the plating. DeoxIT Gold is the one to use for plated contacts -- the red is only for bare contacts.

It comes in a lot of different formats (dropper bottles, spray, cleaning wipes, cleaning tips). This version is the most economical since it's 25mls. The thin needle dispenser is great for minimizing waste -- only a small amount is needed per use. It comes blister packed, and made it through the mail with no problems at all.

title: Cheap build quality; so-so scent
text:
I'm not all that impressed with this car air freshener. The build quality of the holder is pretty low-end. It's functional, but not all that durable. You have to pop the two halves apart to insert the scent "pod," and it is held together by small, relatively fragile plastic pins. After only a few openings, it's starting to not hold together all that well. It has a gate on the back so you can adjust the amount of scent that is released by blocking/opening air slots to the pod. It's very hard to change the setting if the holder is attached to the car vent.

The scent "pods" are filled with liquid, but are backed with a material that lets the scent come out, but not the liquid. Thus, you can position the holder in any direction without concern about leakage. So far, zero leaks.

The scent is just so-so. It's a very artificial smelling scent that's sort of floral and sort of fruity smelling. It's a hard scent to describe, but it's not all that appealing. It reminds me of the industrial air fresheners used in public bathrooms.

It does work, and it does scent up the car, but it's not something I'd get again nor recommend it over more traditional car air fresheners. Three stars.

title: Decent build quality; useful features
text:
I'm pleased with the quality of this inflator. While it probably would not hold up to commercial-level use, for homeowner use it's more than fine, and appropriate for the price point. It has a decent heft to it, the air trigger depresses smoothly, the tire chuck is of good quality (and is double headed), and the tubing is decently thick but still has ample flexibility.

It has a button to deflate tires which is very handy when you overshoot the pressure. There's also a basic pressure gauge built in. It's an analog stick-type gauge that pops out showing the pressure. It's not ideal for tire inflation since it has a rather large margin of error and I want to get that as precise as possible. But it is handy for tasks such as inflating a wheelbarrow tire. It's still good to have for auto tires since it gives you a general idea when you're in the ballpark, and you can then check with a good gauge to make sure you're on the mark.

Good performance and good value for the price.

title: Some nice features, but lightweight build quality and non-accurate pressure reading
text:
I have mixed feelings about this tire inflator. It does have some nice features: the screen is large and mostly easy to read, the controls are simple, the dual sided chuck is handy, and having a deflation button is very useful. Unfortunately, there are also some negatives:

> the build quality is just average. It's workable, but the durability is clearly geared toward home use rather than heavy-duty use. It's not the type of tool that can take much abuse before failing.
> the hose that connects the tire chuck to the meter is short, making it a bit cumbersome to use in certain situations. An additional 2-3 inches worth of tubing would have been better
> the pressure readings are off. It reads about 1.8 to 2.0 psi lower than the actual pressure (tested using my reference gauges).
> the battery door is a major pain to remove and replace (the gauge takes 2 AAA batteries that are NOT included).

Balancing the pros and the cons brings me to a rating of 3 stars (average). It's workable and useful, but the cons (especially the pressure reading) don't make this a compelling purchase.

title: Unimpressive performance
text:
This car wash didn't impress me much. It's rather thin and doesn't suds much (although suds action is not a direct indicator of quality or performance). More significantly, it just performed so-so when it came to getting the winter's accumulation of gunk off my car. It didn't work any better than the generic store brands that I've used, which are priced better, and was not nearly as good as other premium brands, such as Mother's or Griot's Garage. I had to use as much or more compared with the generics, and much more compared with the premiums.

It's just average -- 3 stars. Not a compelling purchase. You can get just as good results for less money, or get better results by paying just a bit more.

title: Good for light tasks, but not ideal for tires/heavy use
text:
This is an OK solution for inflating items such as airbeds, balls and balloons. However, the build quality and performance fall short when it comes to more demanding tasks.

The overall build quality is less than I was expecting given the price. The casing is lightweight and, while I would not call it flimsy, it lacks the solid feel of a well-made tool. It comes with a single battery and a charger. However, the charger is hardwired for use in a car power outlet (what we used to call the cigarette lighter). If you want to charge it in the house, you have to use the included USB cable and your own power block since it does not come with one. A better solution would have been to have the charger have replaceable ends so you could swap the car power adapter with a conventional wall plug adapter.

It does charge fine via USB. It charges at 1.5A (measured with my inline voltage meter) which is a decent rate. There’s a bright, easily seen LED indicator that is red when charging and blue when complete.

Using the compressor is straightforward. The control buttons are a bit small, but the display is large and easy to read. Unfortunately, it is inaccurate when it comes to reading pressure. It read my tire pressure between 2 and 5 PSI off (verified with 2 other pressure gauges). Worst of all, it was inconsistent – sometimes it would be 2 PSI off; the next reading would be 4 PSI off, etc. If you do use this to inflate tires be sure to use a reliable pressure gauge to check the pressure since you can’t trust the accuracy of the compressor’s reading.

The tire chuck is not well designed. It’s cheaply made and does not maintain a good seal. I have a feeling it will be the first area of failure down the road. It also comes with adapters for bikes, balls and balloons. It does not include a carry sack or case for the attachments, which is a shame since they are small and easy to misplace.

Battery life when inflating tires is poor. If you need to add a few pounds of pressure to a single tire you’ll be fine, but if you need to add several pounds to more than one tire, the battery will run out before the job is done.

My ratings:
Overall build quality = 2 stars
Ease of use = 4 stars
Provided attachments = 3 stars
Suitability for light tasks (beds, balloons, etc.) = 4 stars
Suitability for tires = 1 stars

Overall rating 3 stars (average). It’s functional, but the limitations do not make this a compelling purchase.

title: Functional equivalent of the brand name version, but lightweight build quality
text:
This is pretty much the same device as the brand name Battery Tender (BT) but at a lower price point. While it functions fine, the build quality is far more on the lightweight side compared with the BT (which I also have and use regularly).

On the plus side, the battery cables are nice and long making it easy to use. It comes with both clips and terminal ring options, and the coupler for the cable ends is designed so that you can't attach them the wrong way. The indicator lights are small but mostly visible unless you're in sunlight. Operation is very simple and it has been working fine on my car battery (I use it for a vehicle that does not get driven much, so it's helpful to have one of these types of devices to keep the battery charged).

The downsides are mostly with regard to build quality. The alligator clips are not nearly as strong and well-made as the BT. The wiring is also not as beefy. The main unit is very lightweight and runs hotter than the BT. It's not excessively hot, but there's a clear difference that can be felt. That does give me some concern that it won't have as long of a service life as the BT (my BT is several years old and still working fine). Lastly, the indicator lights are not as large or clear as on the BT.

I can't speak to product longevity as of yet, but will update the review should the unit fail down the road.

Build quality = 3 stars; Functionality = 4 stars; Value = 5 stars. Overall rating 4 stars. Worth considering for light use, but if you need something that you can depend on long-term, it may be worth spending the extra money on the BT for the better build quality.

title: Lovely scent; very easy to use
text:
I love the scent of these sachets. It's a very natural lavender -- much more natural than any other lavender scent I've tried with the exception of some lavender essential oils.

I also appreciate how easy they are to use. The scented portion is sealed in a plastic pouch to keep it fresh in storage. When you're ready to use it, just open the paper envelope that contains the scent pouch, remove the plastic wrap, and put the pouch back in the paper envelope. Takes all of 30 seconds.

These are great for closets, under the sink, or anywhere that you want a nice, natural lavender scent. No complaints at all!

title: A must-have if you use mechanical mods
text:
This is a must-have item for maintaining mechanical mods. It does a wonderful job in cleaning contacts, even those that have been neglected. Once clean, a small amount of Deoxit Gold keeps it clean and in top shape for some time.

Dirty contacts result in poor performance and arching, with the latter often contributing to issues such as hot buttons. Clean contacts ensure you not only get the best performance, but you keep your mod operating safely. Of course, you also need to practice good battery safety in addition to keeping the contacts clean.

It can also be used to clean battery contacts for regulated mods but those can also be cleaned with less intensive cleaners (or just alcohol or a pencil eraser).

Fantastic stuff that works very well. A must-have!

title: Excellent for small engines
text:
I've been using this full synthetic 5W-30 in small engines (mower, generator) with excellent results. I had been using conventional 30 weight oil in them, but after finding out that Briggs & Stratton now allows (and recommends) synthetic for their engines, thought I'd give this a try.

Excellent results. I've been getting easier starting, and the wider range of temps that are workable with a 5W-30 synthetic makes it a better option than the conventional 30 weight for the cold. I can't post the link for the B&S discussion on the use of synthetics in their engines, but a search of them will pop it up pretty easily.

Absolutely no complaints, and the price per quart when buying the 6-pack is a good value for a full synthetic, especially a 5W-30.

title: Easy to apply and a nice shine, but you need to put in a lot of work
text:
On the plus side, this is easy to apply. It has a semi-thick cream consistency that spreads easily and, if applied with a sponge or foam applicator (not included), can easily get into any nooks and crannies in the rim, or any other metal object being polished. There is no objectionable smell. The bottle has a wide-tipped applicator nozzle that dispenses an ample amount but not so much that it gets wasted or makes a mess.

The hard work comes when removing it. It takes a lot of elbow grease to get the polishing compound removed completely. I used a micro fiber towel (not included) and, while it was nice to see all the black gunk that the polishing compound was removing from the rim, it took 10+ minutes and two towels to completely remove the polish.

The end result was nice -- a sparkling shine. However, I can get the same level of shine with other rim polishing products with a LOT less effort. While I can't fault the end results, it's not a product I would get again since I can get the same results with a lot less work. As it is, I gave up after two wheels since it was so much work.

This might be a good choice if you have an electric buffing wheel to cut down on the amount of hand labor for polishing. But, if you're applying and removing by hand, this is not an ideal product unless you are willing to put in a fair amount of work.

title: Well-designed (and ample!) storage space; mostly solid build quality
text:
This is a large storage bag! I knew the measurements from the product listing, but was a bit taken aback by how large it was once it arrived. This is the type of bag where, if you can’t fit an item in, you probably don’t need to be taking it along. The overall design is very well thought out and, with just a couple of exceptions, the build quality is very good.

The main compartment layout is just about perfect. The sides have dual-way zippers to allow the compartments to open up like a door on hinges. You can fold back the side and have full and easy access to the full inner compartment. The shell is made of very rigid plastic so it retains it’s shape.

Inside the main compartment there is a shelf that can be removed or repositioned (it attaches with velcro straps) plus a series of mesh pockets that include both open-top and zipper top configuration. The compartment gives you the option of having a huge open space for larger items or subdividing it into smaller compartments to keep smaller items organized and not have them bounce around when you’re on the road.

There is a zippered pouch on each side of the main compartment that has a really nice double zipper design to allow it to accordion out if it’s packed full, or maintain a slim profile if it’s packed lightly (or empty). Very well thought-out design touch.

The front compartments have big buckles on them but they are decorative – the actual closure is with a plastic quick-connect buckle. All are nicely sized and have inner pouches to organize small items. The buckles, however, are a little on the small side and not as heavy-duty as I would have liked.

The detachable top roll bag is also very well-sized and has a semi-ridged inner frame. It’s not as impact resistant as the main compartment, but it holds its shape well and bounces back into shape if you press on it.

The build quality is mostly very good. The majority of the bag is made of synthetic leather that does resemble a smooth grain real leather. It doesn’t feel like leather nor smell like it (the bag actually had a bit of a chemically smell – I needed to let it air out in the sun for a day to get rid of the smell). But, it’s a lot more practical than real leather with regard to weather resistance and ease of care. The seams are all very well stitched, fastened and/or glued – this feels very solid when handled.

The build quality does suffer a bit with regard to two areas: attachment straps and zippers. The straps are all nylon but, in contrast to the heavy-duty nature of the bag, the straps feel very lightweight. None have broken, but none really give me a lot of confidence that they won’t break. Thicker straps would be a welcome addition.

Some of the zippers, such as on the main compartment, are very good (just needed a little graphite to get them to unzip smoothly). Others, such as on the smaller compartments, are too lightweight to give me confidence they will stand up to any measure of rough treatment. The main zippers also lack a covering gasket to help keep out the weather and dirt. Dirt driven in at speed will really take a toll on zippers, and I’ve seen other bags that have a “flap” or gasket that covers the zipper to protect it.

But, on the plus side, this bag comes with a lot of extras, such as a shoulder strap, a back pack strap and a rain cover. While the less than ideal build quality of the straps and zippers bring my rating to 4.5 stars, I’ll round up since, at this price point, it delivers a lot for the money.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Nice looks, but underwhelming performance
text:
This is a nice looking knife/multi-tool set (especially if you’re a fan of Ford products). The performance and build quality, however, is rather underwhelming.

The multi-tool has the usual assortment of blades, screwdrivers, saws, bottle openers, etc. that is typically found in these products. The star of the show is the pliers. The machining on the jaws is excellent – the tips meet perfectly without the slightest gap. The individual tools are less impressive, with average to below average machining. Folding/unfolding the individual tools is difficult. The spring for the pliers is very weak and cheap – it reminded me of a spring from a ball point pen.

The overall folding action of the multi-tool is pretty good, as is the case (metal – it feels and looks like anodized aluminum).

The knife blade is not bad. It comes farily sharp and, after a few passes on a stone to hone it better, seems to be able to hold an edge for a decent amount of time. However, the folding action is stiff and cumbersome, and the grip is not all that comfortable. It has a belt clip which is very sturdy but way too tight to make it easy to use.

If you’re expecting the quality of a higher-end Leatherman or SOG at a bargain price, you won’t be pleased with this. If, however, you’re looking for a low-cost set, like the Ford logo, and can live with so-so performance, this is worth a look. For the price, it’s an average performer, so 3 stars overall.

title: Good protection, but not as slip-proof as the rear version
text:
This is the front bumper version of the Bumperduo. While it is very similar to the rear version in overall design, the fit is a little less secure when traveling at speed. However, it remains a good option to protect from bumps and scrapes especially if you need to parallel park often.

Both the front and rear versions of the Bumperduo are basically the same, in that they are a “rubber band” that is attached by bungee cords to the wheel wells. Installation of the front version is about as easy as the rear version, but you do need to remove your license plate when installing the front. That may be a problem if your plate is held by short screws, since the added thickness of the Bumperduo means the screw needs to be a little longer to grab the threads. Unfortunately, longer screws are not provided with the Bumperduo. Given the price point, I don’t think it’s unreasonable to expect them to throw in a few screws in various lengths.

Installation is pretty straightforward. Two tips: go to the Bumperduo web site since they have more complete install directions than the sheet that comes in the box. Also, unfold the Bumperduo and let it air out for a day (or at least a few hours) before install to get rid of the plastic smell, plus have the material be more pliable.

No complaints about performance in terms of protection. The material is thick enough to easily deal with a bump made while parallel parking (either when you’re the driver or when someone is parking in front of you). It’s not magic – a bang from another car will still dent your bumper, but it avoids getting scuffs and scratches from non-severe hits. It’s also good for some measure of protection against rocks and grit hits when driving, but the protection is limited to the area of coverage, which is smaller than a traditional front end car bra.

I was not as pleased with the fit compared with the rear bumper version. No matter how I adjusted it, it did make some noise and shift a small amount when driving at highway speeds. It was not so severe that I had any concerns about it falling off, but it was annoying at times.

As with the rear version, this is built for practicality, not looks. It’s better if you have a dark car since the black blends in better, but even so, it’s not what I would call sleek or pretty. But since this is designed for protection and not aesthetics, I won’t detract from the rating for that.

I will drop this to 4 stars due to the fit issue. It’s not a major problem, and one that probably won’t be noticed if you mainly do city driving, but it can be annoying at times at highway speeds.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Nice collection of handy items, but implementation has some shortfalls
text:
Overall, this is handy all-in-one tool to keep in the car. While most people will only use the tire pressure gauge, the window smasher tool and seat belt cutter are the type of items that, if you need it, you really NEED it. However, the tire gauge display is less than ideal, the cutter is not as easy to use as it could be, and the flashlight is very dim.

The build quality feels pretty solid. The handle is coated with a non-slip coating which is truly non-slip. The battery compartment door is a little fussy to open and close, but not a significant problem. I like that it uses 2 AAA batteries (which are not included) which are easier to find than the round disc type batteries. I'm running this with rechargeable cells (Amazon Basic brand) and it's working fine with those.

The tire pressure gauge is accurate. I tested it against three other gauges, and the variance was never more than 0.5 pounds. However, the display for the pressure is on the small side, and you have to look at it square on to see the digits clearly due to the fact that the display is recessed behind a plastic window. The decimal portion of the reading (it reads in 0.5 pound increments) is very small and hard to read even when looking at it dead on. The display shuts off automatically to help conserve battery life.

The seatbelt cutter blade is fairly sharp, but since it is inserted in the base where the non-slip coating is, the material you're cutting can get hung up in the blade notch. I tested it on some scrap nylon webbing and, while it did cut through, it was not quick or what I would consider to be easy. Plus, the blade had rust spots on both sides.

The best-made attribute is the window smasher. It is metal, has a nice, solid fee, and a sharp point.

The worst-made attribute is the flashlight. It's so dim that use is limited to tasks such as finding the tire stem at night, and even that is hard to do with the limited light intensity. It would be useless for something such as reading a map at night.

My ratings are 4 stars for the tire gauge, 2 stars for the cutter, 5 stars for the smasher and 1 star for the flashlight. Overall rating is 3 stars (average). It's worth considering if you're looking for an all-in-one solution to tire care and emergency use, but it's not an outstanding product.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Soft but supportive; steep angle makes it better for cars than chairs
text:
This cushion strikes a good balance between being supportive and being cushy. Granted, cushion comfort is something that’s hard to recommend since what one person feels is comfortable, another can consider to be horrible. For me, this is a nice middle ground that I think many people would consider to be comfortable.

The cushion build quality seems good – nice and springy, and it bounces back quickly once you get up. It does mush down pretty flat when in use. The velour cover feels nice and is tightly stitched. It has a zipper for removal/cleaning but unfortunately, the zipper is not well done. It’s very lightweight and does not extend the full width of the cover. Thus, getting the cover on and off can entail a bit of a struggle (and adding to the stress on the zipper).

The cushion has a pretty steep slant to it – more so than other slanted cushions I’ve used. At the back it measures about 3.5 inches thick; at the front it measures only about ½ inch thick. That steep of a drop made this very nice to use in the car but not as comfortable on my office chair. Again, comfort is subjective and also is impacted by a person’s height, weight, etc. I felt too tilted by the cushion when using it on an office chair, and also found it did not provide enough thigh support.

It has a nice wide and deep cutout to relieve tailbone pressure. That part of the design is perfect regardless of where the cushion is used.

The cover does not have non-slip grip points on the base. It was fine when placed on a cloth-covered seat, but was very slidy when placed on a wooden chair.

The zipper and the lack of grip points drops my rating to 4 stars, but this is certainly worth considering if you’re looking for a cushion that has a good-sized tailbone cutout that has a steep angle.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Better performance than any other synthetic chamois
text:
I have a black car and hard water, so water spotting is always a problem after washing. I’ve been using a traditional chamois for years which works well, but is rather fussy in terms of keeping it in good shape. I’ve tried a few of the “magic” microfiber and microfiber-like cloths and have not been happy with any of them (especially the orange ones that were all the rage a few years ago).

This, however, performs far better and even equals the performance of a traditional chamois. It feels much different than the usual microfiber material – it’s sort of rubbery, which makes it work much like a real chamois. There’s a smooth surface and a textured surface. I got the best results by doing the initial drying with the textured surface, wringing out the cloth, then sheeting it across the car using the smooth surface. It left the car dry as a bone and totally spot- and streak-free. Excellent performance.

The construction quality seems more than sturdy enough for a decent life span. It can be machine washed, but I prefer to hand wash it after use, wring it out, and store it back in the provided storage tube. You want to store it damp so it remains flexible. Like a real chamois, it will get hard if totally dry. It returns to a soft state when moistened, but for longer life, storing it moist will be best.

In addition to car drying it can also be used for washing windows, stone counter tops, glazed ceramic tile -- basically anything that you want to dry without leaving streaks.

I’m really impressed with this, especially considering the price. Very well made, works great, and easier to maintain than a traditional chamois. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Works fine, but still prefer Sea Foam for small engine use
text:
Small engines, be they 2 or 4 cycle, are not fond of ethanol blends of gas. You can get non-ethanol gas for 2 cycle engines (TruFuel is a popular brand) but it’s expensive and is not suitable for 4 cycle engines. Additives such as this will work just as well in protecting small engines from the detrimental effects of ethanol.

This worked fine in the small engines I tested it with (a 4 cycle mower, and a few 2 cycle powered tools). Good starting performance and fairly smooth running. However, it’s not as effective as my standby, which is Sea Foam. In addition to ethanol protection, Sea Foam offers better carb cleaning than this. I tried this in an very aging chain saw that I’ve been neglecting. Got it to run, but it was very rough. After draining the gas and refilling it with Sea Foam treated gas, it was much smoother (after an initial rough run).

But regardless of which product is used, some type of stabilizer/treatment is essential for small engines. Gas straight from the pump will really do a number on small engines.

title: Decent quick wax for cars; great for use on tile
text:
This is a decent quick spray wax product. It doesn't come close to the shine, protection and durability of a paste wax, however. I used this on half of my car hood and used my usual paste wax (Griot’s Garage) on the other half. The paste wax side was noticeably richer and deeper (I have a black car) and it felt super slippery to the touch. The Eco Touch side looked nice, but nowhere near as good as the paste wax side.

However, there’s a catch: it took me about 3 minutes to do the Eco Touch side. It took 20 minutes (10 of which spent waiting for the wax to haze over) to do the paste wax side. So, if you value spending less time and are willing to live with less gloss and protection, this will be a great choice.

I like that it has no scent – just a touch “waxy” smelling but as close to non-scented as you could probably get. It sprays on easily and wipes off/polishes with little effort. A micro fiber cloth is the best choice for spreading and polishing it.

But, while it may lack some punch when it comes to use on a car, it’s great in the bathroom on ceramic tile. It leaves a light coating of wax that’s enough to help the water bead up, limiting the amount of soap scum and mineral deposits that can accumulate on tile. I used car wax for that purpose in the past, but it was a major pain getting it applied and buffed. This was super simple.

While as a car wax – even allotting for the speed of application – I think this merits 4 stars at best. But considering how multi-purpose it is, I think it deserves a 5-star rating. Good for the car; great on bathroom tile.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Sturdy, stable and stylish
text:
While soft saddle bags usually look nicer than hard shell bags, they usually are not as practical or sturdy. These bags, however, are far more sturdy than other soft shell saddle bags I've come across.

The material is not leather, but it's a pretty close approximation of a heavy leather shell. It has a smooth surface with just a slight gloss to it. It looks and feels pretty close to the real thing but, unlike real leather, is a lot more water resistant. I poured water on the top and let it sit. No penetration into the material at all. Not only does that keep what's inside dry, it also allows for easy cleaning to get rid of dust and mud splatters.

The seams are all tightly stitched with rivets on the stress points, such as at the top lid. The inner box is made of hard plastic with a metal rib around the top for strength.

It has a double flap closure. The main flap is secured with quick release nylon tabs (the buckles are mostly decorative rather than functional). The tabs are anchored to the box using a bolt/nut that goes right through the inner box. Very, very secure anchoring, but the term "quick release" is a bit of a misnomer. It does take a bit of fumbling and pinching to get the tabs unhooked from their anchor points. It's not tough to do, but it's also not something that you can do with gloves on since the tabs are somewhat small.

There's a small loop at the base of the quick connect that can be used with a padlock (not included). However, the loop is so small that it would fit only the smallest size lock. A nylon shoulder carry strap is included with each bag should you want to detach them and carry them along.

Once the main flap is opened, there is a pair of left/right closure flaps that are held together with Velcro. I like that extra layer of security to keep the dirt out.

There's a small pouch on the inside with a velcro closure. That's a nice idea, but the pouch is so small that it's not all that useful. A larger pouch, or some movable velcro-mounted dividers, would have been better. I ended up taking some divider flaps out of an old camera bag and used them to partition the space in the bin to keep small items and tools from bouncing around.

The yoke flaps are held together with Velcro with a nylon strap as a secondary hold point. The yokes are attached to the bags using two metal screw posts that secure with a plastic nut on the inside of the bag. The holes for the screw posts have a metal washer reinforcement to ensure nothing tears or loosens up.

While the mounting is easy and feels secure, I would have liked to see something more than a nylon strap to act as a secondary hold should the Velcro give out. It feels very secure as-is, but I always like a bit extra in terms of redundant fastening methods.

All in all, this is a solid bag. The construction quality is very good, especially given the price. While the material is not leather, it looks pretty close to real leather and offers far more practical benefits (although nothing can replace the smell of good leather and how it looks when it ages!). Mounting is secure and simple. Well worth considering if you're looking for a saddle bag that works well without breaking the bank.

4.5 stars rounded to 5 since the shell looks and feels so close to real leather.
[Sample provide for review]

title: Leaves leather rich and supple; some issues with the scent
text:
Overall, this is a pretty good leather conditioner. It is not a cleaner – you have to start with clean leather by using either water or a leather cleaner. This product is only for conditioning and protection.

It goes on very easily. It’s a pretty thin consistency, which makes it, for me, easier to work with than conditioners that are the consistency of hand cream. The thinness makes it easy to get the conditioner into seams and crevices. But, be careful with how much you apply at a time – the thinness also makes it easy to run off and drip.

It comes with a sponge-type applicator that works well. It can also be applied by hand, with a paint brush or a micro fiber cloth. I found application to be very straightforward – just apply, let dry for an hour, then buff.

I used it on a leather vest, and was impressed with the softness and light sheen it left. It didn't change the black leather color, nor did it make the leather feel greasy.

It has a mostly decent scent that is sort of leather-like, but it is also somewhat strong when used using it in a closed room. The scent didn't linger on the vest after buffing, but it did hang around the house for some time. Given that, I wouldn't recommend using this in a car if you are sensitive to scents (or just find them annoying) unless you air out the car well.

Overall, a decent leather conditioner that gets the job done.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Looks great; good quality construction
text:
This is a very nicely made leather vest – far better than I expected given the price. The stitching is very well done, with even, tight seams throughout. Most of the seams are double stitched. This is not a vest that will fall apart anytime soon!

The lining is some type of synthetic material (I’d guess that its polyester). It feels very smooth and slick, and makes it easy to slip the vest on, even over a heavy sweatshirt or hoodie. The liner is a bit baggy in spots, especially around the edges. It’s not baggy enough to interfere with use or feel at all uncomfortable, but it is an area that could have been better stitched and sized.

The leather feels great – soft to the touch, but not so soft that it feels buttery. Nice and solid, with a good texture to it. I put on some leather dressing/protection that made it a bit softer, but even untreated it feels great. (I treated it mainly for water protection, not for any improvement in feel). The color is even throughout – no blotches or thin areas.

I like that the arm cuts are low on the shoulder. Some vests are designed with just a small band of material on the shoulder, which I don’t care for since it can be uncomfortable. I very much prefer the wider cut of this vest, both for looks and comfort.

The snaps are metal and hold well. They are black to blend in with the leather.

It’s sized well. I have it in XL and it fits great on top of a sweatshirt. Roomy but not baggy. As a reference, I’m 6 foot 2, 165 pounds.

The pockets on the front are real pockets, not just decorative as with some vests. They are big enough to put my hands in them. It also has 2 pockets on the inside, but those are just in the lining and are not reinforced. I wouldn’t trust that they would hold much of anything before the lining tears.

The vest is made in Pakistan.

One issue is that the one I received does not have an adjustable elastic cord side lace, as stated in the product specs. I don’t miss not having it, but wanted to point out that discrepancy with the listing. The product photo also shows the liner as having a diamond pattern. Mine does not, which contributes to the liner feeling baggy, as noted previously.

All in all, for the price, I don’t think you can get much better than this. Well made, looks nice, feels nice, and fits well. While the lining construction could be improved, this is still well worth a 5-star rating.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Handy tool for monitoring battery health
text:
I have a car that is not used regularly and am always concerned about the battery not having a charge when its needed. I've been using a float charger on it (a Battery Tender) which has been working out great. However, the charger doesn't give me any feedback as to the overall health of the battery.

This device solves that problem. It is very easy to use even if you're not experienced using test gear. It gives you a clear status on the battery health ranging from "green" (good battery that can hold a charge) to "red" (battery can't hold a charge and should be replaced). You can also go further and run tests on voltage, charge system and starting system conditions.

The only faults I found with the device is that the screen is very hard to read in the sun (best used indoors in a garage) and the manual is not very helpful for learning how (and why) to use the tester. That aside, it's a very handy device to have to assess 12v battery health without having to take it to a parts store for diagnostics.

title: Brilliant shine; easy to apply; great packaging
text:
I've used and liked a variety of Meguiar's products over the years and have rarely been disappointed. This wax is turning into one of my all-time favorites.

It applies very easily provided the car is in the shade (black cars plus sunlight = a surface that's way too hot for any wax). I'm especially pleased with the packaging - it comes in a tube much the same as toothpaste. The wax itself is gray colored and thick, and the tube makes it very easy to dispense without any mess or wastage. Very well done!

It can be applied with a buffer, but I just applied it by hand using the included applicator (a round piece of foam). Very easy to apply.

It buffs off easily after letting ir dry to a haze. I used a couple of microfiber cloths, turning them frequently and starting a new cloth when the old one got loaded with wax. I then did a final buff with a fresh micro fiber cloth. (While Mcguiar also makes the cloths, I get mine from Sam's Club - very inexpensive, and decent quality).

The shine was tremendous - this is why I got a black car! It looked so good I didn't want to take it out of the garage to keep it clean.

I can't speak to the longevity of the shine or the protection as of yet, but other Meguiar waxes have provided me with a very long-lasting shine. I'll update the review should this not prove to be durable.

If you have a black car, get this. The shine will not disappoint, and you don't have to work very hard to get the job done. Highly recommend!

title: Keeps my rarely driven car ready to go
text:
I don't drive much, and my car can sit in the garage for a couple of weeks between uses. I've been having a problem keeping the battery charged, especially in the winter. It's always started, but it clearly is struggling to get the engine to turn over.

My mechanic offered two suggestions: drive more or get a trickle/float charger. Since a charger was only about $20, I figured it was the better route to take rather than waste gas.

I looked at a couple of similar models, especially the Black & Decker BM3B model ([[ASIN:B0051D3MP6 Black & Decker BM3B 6V and 12V Battery Charger / Maintainer]]) since the price included attachments to plug the charger into the car's power outlet. However, since my car (an Infiniti) does not have a "hot" plug, those attachments would not have been of any use.

The Battery Tender Jr had a lot of good reviews, so I gave it a shot. So far, it's been working great. It took about 24 hours to bring my battery up to the full charge level. The unit is very easy to use, and all the attachments are well-made. The LED status lights clearly indicate the charge status. The only quibble I have is that the charger unit does not have a cord - it plugs directly into the wall (or, in my case, into an extension cord). The next model up in the Battery Tender line (the Plus) has a cord, and also charges faster, but also comes in at twice the price of the Junior. So I went with the Junior.

Very pleased with this, and highly recommend it.

title: Poor quality. Better choices are out there
text:
Bottom line: This is a cheap blower vac both in terms of price as well as quality. The performance is mediocre as a blower. The vac has a metal mulching blade, but clogs easily. Hard to switch from blower to vac. There are better choices available at this price point.

Main review: I was looking for an inexpensive blower vac to give as a gift, and this caught my eye. I've not heard of the brand before, but the price was attractive. Still, I was concerned about the lack of info available for it, so I got it at a big box retailer (the place with the folks in orange vests) so I could return it should it not perform well. Glad I did so, since I ended up returning it.

The build quality is pretty poor. I was not expecting it to be as solid as my Stihl blower vac, since it cost less than half as much, but the build quality was below even the low-priced brands such as Ryobi and MTD. Parts that get a lot of use, such as the pull cord and the choke lever, are way too flimsy to give any measure of confidence that they will stand up to a few years of use, even in a homeowner environment.

The blower tubes are thin plastic. I was also disappointed that the blower tube needs to be attached to the housing with a screw. That means you have to take out the screw every time you want to convert it from a blower to a vac. Not a good design.

The vac tube has a nice large diameter and, unlike the blower tube, attaches to the housing with thumb screws. The blower cage also unlatches with a thumb screw, unlike most others that require depressing a latch with a screwdriver. That's a good feature, but the value is minimized since the thumbscrews are mostly plastic and don't grip well.

It takes a 40:1 fuel ratio. Started up pretty easily cold. Not as easy to start when hot. There's a fair amount of vibration and twisting. It does not have cruise control.

Blower performance was mediocre. About the same as a mid-range electric blower.

Vac performance was frustrating. On the plus side, it has a metal mulching blade that is nicely sized and an easy to grip handle. But, the elbow tube connecting to the vac bag is too small in diameter to allow anything other than perfectly dry leaves to pass. It clogged constantly on items that posed no problems at all for my Stihl, Troy-Bilt or Worx. It did do a great job mulching dry leaves, but pick up anything that has a slight moisture content, and you're pulling the vac apart for unclogging. The bag is of decent size but thin and not at all heavy-duty.

Given all these issues I can't recommend this blower/vac. 2 stars for having the metal mulching blade and a small number of nice features such as the handles; 0 or 1 star for everything else.

If you want the best performance, you'll have to spend more for a Husquvarna (sp?) or a Stihl (Echo is also a good bet but only as a blower. Their vac performance is not as good). A lot more money, but much better performance and durability. If you want to keep it at about $150, look at the Toro 51984. It's not as capable as the Husky or Stihl, but a nice performer and the only under-$150 blower vac that I know of with a metal mulching blade. And don't forget electrics - while you're tethered to a cord, the Toro and Worx electric blower vacs perform very well. Certainly much better than the Southland.

title: Ineffective on hard water spots
text:
I had high hopes for this since other products in the Mother's line have performed very well for me. Unfortunately, this is not one of them.

On the plus side, the product is easy to use. It's a cream-like consistency (sort of the same consistency as hand lotion) and there is no objectionable odor. The instructions state to use the product with a microfiber cloth, rub well, add more if needed, then polish off with a clean cloth.

I worked on a roughly 6-inch square section of glass for 20 minutes with this. Went through about one-quarter of the bottle. Rubbed until my arm was hurting. The end result: no change. The water spots are still there and only -- and perhaps this is my imagination -- just slightly less visible. And I mean just slightly. At this rate I'd need to spend a couple of hours and a couple of bottles to clean the glass!

You can feel that there is some small grit in the cream, but it is either too soft to do any good, or there's too little of it. It feels much like SoftScrub (which I also tried with no success).

Their product photo shows a horribly-stained windshield that becomes crystal clear after using the product. Don't expect that to happen. Not even close.

On the plus side, it did not scratch at all, and it left the glass quite clean. However, I can get the glass clean using something such as Invisible Glass for a whole lot less than what this costs.

Hate to give this a bad review since I really like some of their other products, but this is not worth spending good money on. I'll see if I can use the rest elsewhere in the house, such as cleaning the sink. Really sorry that I wasted my money on this.

UPDATE 5/8/2012: The manufacturer responded (see their note below) and provided me with a refund for the puchase price. Kudos to Mother's for standing behind their products! While I still can't give a recommendation for this specific product, I have used, and will continue to use, many of their wax and cleaning products since they work very well.

title: Some excellent changes; some disappointments as well
text:
This is the third TomTom unit I've had (others are a One and a 740 Live). Of the three, this is hands-down a clear improvement. But, while it has some wonderful features, it also can make you want to tear your hair out.

Several improvements are worth noting. First is the user interface. The screens are not as cluttered, easier to navigate, but still offer the level of customization TomTom is always known for. Want a QUERTY keyboard layout? No problem. Want an ABCD layout? You can have that as well. Left handed? You can switch the menu layout to make it more comfortable. But, even with all these options I never got the feeling of "where am I?" when navigating the menus.

The routing is also top-notch. Years ago, TomTom routing was a clear notch below Garmin and Magellan. They caught up recently and, with this release, I would put them in the lead. Calculation times are speedy, lots of options as to the type of route to take, and re-calc's are so fast as to be almost instant. Big pat on the back for the developers in this area. LOVE the warning screens for car pool and toll roads -- highly usefule in my area.

The 5 inch screen size is comfortably large - noticeably better/easer to use than the standard 4+ inch models, but not so huge that it gets in the way. Excellent clarity in normal/shaded light; a bit washed out but still legible in sunlight.

Touch screen sensitivity is OK. Have to press hard, and helps to hit it with a fingernail rather than a finger. Not the best but workable. The same with the speaker - it's OK for the job but won't win any awards for sound quality.

Excellent mount. Very simple to use twist mount that works well with a Navmat holder. I like the small and sleek power outlet for the car with an indicator light.

Features lacking that I like on other GPS's are an easy to access turn list, and a "bing" sound to alert you to an upcoming turn. Not essential, but it would be nice to have. A split screen would also be nice - I have that on my Motorola GPS, and just love how they implemented it so you can see both the map and the turn list at the same time.

The biggest problem I've always had with other TomToms was having to use the Home software. That was horrible when it first came out, and, while it got better with later releases, it still was pretty bad. Doing an update was a bit of a gamble - it might work, it might not, or it might brick your unit. Spent a LOT of time uninstalling and re-installing Home (that's pretty much the first thing TomTom tech support tells you to do whenever there's any type of problem). Never got it to the point where it would update the maps on my 740.

So, I was looking forward to being able to ditch Home and use mytomtom online. But, unlike the online app Garmin has, this again is a poor implementation. Poor interface, poor design, and poor operation. On the plus side, it was a snap to install. But, using it to get an available application update was a pain. No status menus as to what was going on, it kept switching my location from US to UK, and relentlessly asked me to update my account to get their newsletter.

But the worst part about the online app is that it is a work in progress. According to the info on screen, map updating, map corrections/mapshare, new voices, and all the other options you could do with Home are "coming soon." I always get nervous when I see that, since coming soon could be next week or next year. According to posts on GPS discussion boards, TomTom has been saying these features will be "coming soon" for a few months. That is something to keep in mind if you spring for the unlimited map update version - it may be a while before you can actually take advantage of that.

I wrote a review years ago about a Magellan in which I said there is no such thing as the "best" GPS - all the major brands get the job done; it's just a question of the type of interface you like. I find the heated "Brand X" versus "Brand Y" debates rather amusing - sort of like the Chevy vs Ford debates of my youth.

So, I won't say this is the best GPS of the dozen or so I've owned, but it certainly does an outstanding job with routing and holds its own when it comes to an operational user interface. If they could only make the mytomtom application actually work well and do everything that is promised, this would be a 5-star unit. However, as it is right now, I'll have to give it 4 stars (3.75 probably would be more appropriate, but I'll round up).

title: Nice and thick, but so-so on hem quality
text:
These are thick, absorbent towels - more thick and plush than some of the hand towels you'd get at a big box typical retailer. But there are a few drawbacks, mainly with regard to the quality of the hem stitching and shedding.

I normally use microfiber towels for utility chores (I get them cheap at the warehouse stores). For some applications these Dr. Joe cotton towels are clearly better. They absorb more water, and do so quicker. Great for drying the car. The size is a good match for car work as well - not too big so that it gets in the way; not too small that you have to go through a bunch before the job is done.

They are not as good as microfiber towels when it came to applying and buffing wax. Microfiber distributed the wax more evenly, and picked it up faster. The cotton towels did well, however, when used for a final buff. The thickness really helps bring out the best shine.

The Dr. Joe towels are also handy in the kitchen - much better for drying dishes and sopping up spills than microfiber. Granted, they are not targeted for kitchen use, but they certainly are up to the task.

The downside is lint. These towels shed like mad in the first wash. There was less shedding in the second and third wash, but it still filled up the lint trap in the dryer. This shedding is also seen when using the towels for cleaning glass - lint stuck to the windshield and side windows, and there was some streaking. Microfiber towels are clearly better for glass cleaning.

My biggest problem was with the hem quality. After only one wash, two of the towels had frayed hems. After a second wash, the number increased to three. I re-stitched the hems on the frayed ones, and will probably do some preventative mending on the rest to (hopefully) stop that from happening.

Overall, a generally decent product but not outstanding.

title: Outstanding shine if applied properly
text:
I've used other Eagle products (their nano wax) with good results, so I thought I'd give this a shot since there was a rebate. So glad I tried it - it's the best shine my car has ever had! Plus, no white residue on black plastic trim.

There's one big catch, however - you can't let it dry or it's very difficult to buff out. You need to work on small sections. Wipe it on, then immediately wipe it off. A micro fiber towel works best for both application and removal. Working in the shade is an absolute must as well.

One person can do it, but it helps to have two people. One to apply; the other to wipe it off. Working on my own it took me about 15 minutes to do the car (an Infiniti EX). Two people could easily do it in less than 10 minutes.

I can't comment as of yet as to durability and longevity, but my car has never looked better. Even if it doesn't last as long as a conventional apply/dry/buff wax, it's so fast and easy to apply that I'll continue to use it. Highly recommend.

title: Nicely made, but not a good value
text:
I had high hopes for this product since keeping things organized in my trunk is challenging. I have a hatchback and always keep the back seats folded down. I am also not able to fully grasp the concept of "traveling light" so there's always a lot of stuff knocking about.

I have an organizer that I really like - it's made by Rola (their M.O.V.E. model which comes in various sizes and is sold by Amazon). It has moveable dividers, collapsible, and is perfect for keeping grocery bags and the like secure in the trunk. But, it's low, so tall things can topple out. I had been using an old plastic bin to carry taller items, and thought the Thule bag would be much better.

Well, it looks nice, but in terms of actual use, doesn't offer any more value than my $1.99 plastic bin. The Thule bin has the capability to collapse, but it's somewhat ackward to do - the metal rods are tough to wedge into place. It's a two-handed operation. The Rola design is much better/easier.

There's no dividers within the bin, nor are there any pockets on the outside. It's basically a nylon representation of a box, with a zipper on the top and handles on the side. The base is non-skid, but is not all that grippy. Stopping short caused the bin to slide quite a bit.

I wish I could be more positive about this since Thule does make some good products. While this is well-built (good zipper, nice stiching, and quality nylon material) it needs to go back to the drawing board -- either add more value to it by adding features such as dividers, pouches, etc. or drop the price by way more than half. As it stands, if you buy this you're paying an awful lot for something that is functionally equivalent to a plain box.

title: Good design, useful features
text:
I'm very pleased with this trash bag -- a lot of thought went into the design. The opening is set up so that trash can't escape if the bag tips over (not an uncommon situation in a car). The bottom of the bag has a velcro closure that you undo when you want to empty the bag. Lots of attachment options -- there's double sided tape with velcro if you want to stick it to the dash, and a strap if you want to hang it on the seat. Small enough so that it's not in the way, but big enough to take care of most trash that you'd encounter in the car.

Case Logic has never disappointed me with their product quality, and this is no exception. Nicely done, and very handy to have to keep the car clutter down.

title: Outstanding!
text:
While on the pricy side, the ICON blades really work well. Quiet operation, streak free, no chatter or skips. Well worth the price paid - you'll find a few dollars more will pay off in spades in a downpour!

I tried the RainX brand and they work well at first, but didn't last very long (about 6 mo). The Bosch wipers on my car are still going strong after 1 year, so when it came time to replace the Rain-x ones on another car, I went with Bosch.

Good price on Amazon and quick shipping. Highly recommend!

title: Handy to have
text:
This is a very handy device to keep in your car to deal with the inevitable need for keep your tires properly inflated. It's very compact - fits very easily in the trunk or in the back seat foot well. Everything stores neatly in the unit. Easy to use - just set the dial to the desired pressure and plug it in, either via an extension cord, or using a power port in the car. It shuts off automatically when the target pressure is reached.

It's pretty accurate, but you'll want to check your tires with a proper gauge to make sure the pressure is where it should be. So, if you need (for example) 33 lbs, set the B&D for 35. When it shuts off, check it with the gauge and (if necessary) bleed off any excess.

It's a bit noisy, but no more than other similar products in this price range. Build quality seems pretty good. I had a similar model from another manufacturer that only lasted about a year. The B&D product seems far more sturdy, and I'm hoping it will last. Had it for three months, and so far, so good. The two-year warranty is nice just in case.

It's not a replacement for a compressor. I have a small one in the garage, and use that when I'm home to inflate tires. But, when you're on the road, this can be a godsend, especially if you get a flat and find that the spare tire is very low on air (yes, I know I should check that regularly, but never seem to remember). Having the Air Station in the car is a lot easier than trying to find a gas station when you need air. Also very handy to have for bike tires.

The price fluxuates quite a bit - if you get it at a price dip it's well worth the price.

title: Smelly, but effective
text:
This stuff is great! Just spray it on, wait about a minute, then wipe off. Gets rid of the bugs that are plastered against the bumper that take forever to remove using soap and water. Also great for pine tar/tree sap. Haven't needed to use it for tar yet, but I expect that will come off just as easily as everything else.

The one downside is the smell - it has a strong petroleum odor that lingers. You definitely want to use this outdoors, and not when the car is in the garage. Keep the car windows up so the smell does not get inside the car. Also, be sure to use it when the car surface is cool and out of direct sun, and give it time to work - at least a minute - before wiping off.

I've used other Stoner products, such as Invisible Glass, and have been pleased with them as well. Good stuff to have to keep your car clean!

title: Flexible space, well constructed
text: Very pleased with this product -- very easy to use, the dividers offer a huge amount of flexibility, stays put in the car (no sliding around whatsoever). Opens and closes quickly.  Well-made.  I did not have any odor problem at all, as some of the other reviewers noted. Highly recommend, and would absolutly buy it again.

title: Junk
text: So disappointed with this thing!!  Don't waste your money on this!  Low quality straight from China, not worth $5.  Unfortunately, I opened it late to return or I would have requested.

title: kehoppingeps s
text: I use it to store extra shopping bags in my car.

title: Great wide scraper
text: I have used this several times this seasonand it works well. I was surpised and the width of the scraper when used. It does not look wider than any other but this seemed to ger a nice layer of frost off my windows with just a few scrapes.

title: Great roadside kit!
text: This is a great kit!! I hope I never have to use it but if I do I feel as though I would be in good shape to get myself up and running.  First Aid kit, ice scraper, tire inflator, jumper cables, a flashlight plus much more. This would be a great gift for a single woman with few people to call in emergencies and it would also be great for someone leaving home,like going off to college. With everything going on in the world it's great to be self sufficient and this kit helps with that.

title: Compact
text: With the bitterly cold winters here in Ohio, my car has been hesitating to start. This is great to carry around just in case there is an issue with getting your car started.

title: Great suction!
text:
I wish I had better pictures to truly show the difference, but these two shots are after about three minutes of minimal effort on the driver's seat floor mats in my car - I'm so glad the teens both have their own cars to dirty up now and I won't have to worry about their beach sand all over mine The vacuum easily sucked a ton of loose sand from the mats. That's a win in my book. Though the voltage is lower than my last hand-held vac, it seems to have better suction.

For once, I'm not even going to complain about manufacturers cheaping out and not including an actual plug-in charger. The USB connection on this one could actually come in handy if you run out of juice while working, because we have USB outlets and/or adapters in all of our vehicles. And you can operate the vac while it's plugged in. I don't know if you're supposed to or not, but you can.

It comes with a nice variety of tools, though mine was missing the cleaning gel. That didn't bother me much because I already have a jar of that stuff near every computer in our house (it's great for keyboards, too) but at a price point that's slightly above just the vac alone, the kit really should include all the consummables mentioned.

With three vehicles, we'll definitely get a lot of use out of this kit.

title: I love this stuff!
text:
I feel in love with cleaning gels when I bought a keyboard vacuum and a small package came as a free sample. Ironically, the vacuum was a dude. The cleaner was great, though.

This is about the most thorough keyboard clean you can get short of taking off all the keys. Dirt, hair, crumbs - it lifts everything. I would caution you to not reuse if you eat at your computer a lot. Excessive food crumbs will cause the whole batch to mold. Not saying how I know this, but I do.

title: NOT just for emergency use
text:
It's winter in Michigan, which means that if the day ends in a "y" my tires are probably low. After spending a chunk of time on a weekend afternoon driving to a series of gas stations trying to find a working air station, I was glad to find this pump. I'm probably going to buy one for my kids' cars, too. The one in college has trouble finding anything but coin-operated, and finding coins is another layer of hassle.

It worked easily with my Chevy Equinox. There were no issues with reaching all the tires, though it did help that there's also an outlet in the back of the vehicle. The pressure gauge was 1psi off from what OnStar shows but, then, OnStar disagrees with literally every gauge I've ever used on this vehicle. This is actually the closest match so far.

title: A much-needed retro fit
text: Easy (ish) to install, even for something that's not really in my normal skill set. It's much faster than my old plug-in charger, too. The on switch that's annoying to some is actually a feature, not a bug, for me. I'm old enough to remember killing car batteries with an alway-so CB radio.

title: Great for adjusting the seat belt to where you want it
text: I got this for when I need to drive my elderly Mom somewhere. She has a small body frame and the seat belt would rub or be very close to her neck. I have to connect the seat belt for her so being able to easily connect and remove this when not in use is great. It holds the seat belt in place and doesn't slide out of place. I would have preferred to have a plain front cover instead of the Eagle imprint but it is what it is.

title: Perfect fit for my Honda Ridgeline
text: Perfect fit for my Honda Ridgeline. Maintenance schedule recommends replacing the Air Filter every 15k. This filter is similar to OEM at a much lower price point. Why not replace the Air Filter at such a reasonable cost.

title: Better than OEM
text: I've used Puroma Cabin Air Filters for my other vehicles since I always trusted their air filter products. I did not hesitate to order one for our 2022 Toyota Highlander since I know it will be an exact fit and meet or exceed oem standards. The replacement air filter was indeed an exact fit as described and the materials used for the filtering appears denser than the oem filter. Cost of the Puroma was much cheaper than the actual oem filter as well. Happy with this item!

title: Nice foldable sun shade that covers the entire windshield
text: I have a 2022 Highlander Platinum and this fits pretty well. There are specific shaped shades for specific generation models of the highlander so this is not a perfect fit for the 2022 but good enough to cover the entire windshield with it held down by the sun visors. I really like that it folds up and stores under the seat since I do have the rolled up type shades and those take up a lot of space.

title: Solid quality and built to last
text: The oil filter wrench is exactly what I needed since it supports both the standard one-piece oil filter as well as the Toyota oil canister housing. It's high quality aluminum and will no doubt last beyond the life of the car. Will definitely make changing oil easier.

title: The smell of the rubber is too toxic!
text: As others mentioned, the rubber has a petro smell which is very strong! I soaked the mats in soapy water and let it sun for a couple of days which did not eliminate the odor. I did not want to risk this being in my car with my family so I returned it.

title: Perfect tuner lugs
text: Just what I needed for new rims. I still purchased wheel locks separately though.

title: Received 20 of the same 20mm washer
text: The description says 10 - 18mm and 10 - 20mm washers but I received two bags of the 20mm washers.  I opened it since I was in the middle of a rear differential change so I can't return it.

title: Makes it easy to clean the windows!
text:
Great tool for cleaning the hard to reach spots in the lower part of the front or rear windows! I should have purchased this years ago to make it easier!

Update: I filled out a survey card that was included in the packaging. When I sent it, the e-mail bounced since the mailbox for the company was full. I suspect if you ever needed support from the company Xindell you will never get it.

title: Great Quality!
text: Just what I needed for a Rear Differential oil change!

title: Very Useful
text: This is a very nice device to have in your vehicle.  It seems to be very well made, and is so incredibly useful not only for jump starting a dead battery, but to charge various electronics and it has a flashlight too.  Everything is conveniently contained in a plastic carry case which is easy to store somewhere in a car, truck, etc...  It came fully charged and ready to go.  I suggest taking it out at least once a month and making sure it is fully charged as the charge will slowly dissipate over time.

title: Big Wipes
text: These are basically large diaper wipes (but don't use these on a baby).  They clean anything you use them on just fine.  I have a large leather purse that had some stains on it and though the leather wipes got some dirt off the stains remained.  I think these would be convenient for wiping down leather car seats (though I don't have leather car seats), leather shoes and other leather items.

title: Works Well
text: As of this review this car rooftop cargo bags costs $44.99, which I think is a fair price for it.  It's seems to be durable and waterproof, and holds a lot of stuff.  We like to go camping every year and it's hard to get all of our stuff packed into one car with 4 people and 3 dogs.  This bag will definitely help free up a lot of room inside the car.  Our cars don't have racks so we use the straps as shown in the picture on the product page and it seems to hold well.  It comes with a piece of flat material similar to what you put underneath area rugs and that helps a lot with any abrasions made from any movement of the bag while traveling.  The only thing though, is a lot of straps come with it so be careful and don't lose any of them.

title: Quality Deep Cycle Battery
text: I selected this battery before completely checking the stats that I needed to replace the battery in my tennis ball machine.  Unfortunately I need a 12v 18ah and this battery is not powerful enough for it (12v, 6ah).  Nonetheless, I find it useful to power smaller items and it can be recharged via one of my solar panels.  It's very well constructed and I expect it to last a long time.  It comes very well packaged for shipping.

title: Seems to Work Well
text: Yep.  This stuff seems to do a good job.  My husband's old truck sits out in the sun everyday and the dashboard is dry and faded.  But now it looks really good.  Will it last a year?  I don't know but it looks great for now.

title: Works Well
text: This plastic oil pump works well enough for all of my uses which are very few.  If I was a mechanic or someone who regularly pumped oil on/into things I would opt for a more durable oil gun, but for people like me who use oil pump guns every now and then this is one is fine.  It works well and I can see how much oil is in it.

title: Quality Battery
text: This battery seems to be very well constructed.  I wanted an extra battery to have on hand if the power went out for a long time.  I had another battery similar to this one and it lasted for years.  As far as knowing how much charge it has you'll have to use a volt meter to measure since there is no voltage indicator on it.  But that's real easy to do and does not merit a deduction in stars.

title: Super Cute and Useful
text: As of this review I don't know what the set of flag car coasters costs so I can't rate that in my star level.  However, I really like these!  I especially like the red, shiny tire valve caps.  They perfectly match the beautiful red color of my husband's adorable little truck.  And having the American flag on the tops is extra special.  The foam backed round flag coasters fit my car's car cup holder perfectly and look great.  I like the rounded slot since it make taking them out very easy to do.  I'm kind of puzzled though, why two coasters have the stars in the upper left as normal, but the other two have them in the upper right or lower left side (depending on how you rotate them)  and not as pictured on the product page.  As far as the flag stickers go, I'm not putting them on our cars simply because I don't know if they will mess up the paint or not and I'd hate to have his red truck paint goofed up by a sticker.  I'll save those and give them to my daughter who likes patriotic things and will use them on something for sure.

title: Useful but Don't Put Heavy Items in It
text: As of this review this door organizer costs around $30.00.  I would not want to pay any more than that for it.  I have had it on the back of my pantry door for a couple of days now and have found it helpful but also somewhat cumbersome.  It doesn't come with instructions so I had to refer to the picture on the product page when assembling it.  If you have any shelving next to your door on it's inside swing, then this organizer will hit and the door will not fully open.  We now have to almost turn sideways to get inside our pantry.  The red basket-like plastic shelves are convenient for holding things but I suggest nothing heavy since it's only plastic on two thin, flat metal hooks holding the rack on the door.  I can see too much weight fracturing the plastic and it all coming down.  I have loaded every shelf up with large (but light weight) plastic spice bottles and their removal off the regular shelves has opened up some more space in our over-crowded pantry.  I like this organizer well enough, but it might be better on the back of a bedroom door full of socks, underwear and stuff like that.

title: Only Has Three Sides
text: This car net pocket handbag holder only has 3 sides.  One of the large sides is missing.  I think it should have at least been a side that went partially up.  I was hoping to fill it up with tennis balls but that's not going to happen unless I want tennis balls all over the inside of my car.  For me, I don't see any use for this.

title: Smells Like a Deodorant Stick
text: These car air fresheners are easy to hook onto vent flaps and look kind of like a big, light blue life saver candy stuck there.  When there's air passing through the vents over the air freshener you can definitely smell it.  It smells just like a regular deodorant stick that someone would use on their armpits.

title: I Like It
text: This buffer is pretty easy to use and did a great job getting my hubs old truck looking good.  It's not heavy and I found it easy to buff the truck with.  I wouldn't buy it though, if you're looking for something more industrial, but for an occasional buffing of the old wagon it works great.

title: Worked Very Well
text: It's taken a while for me to write a review for this battery charger simply because I didn't have a car battery that needed charging.  However, eventually our truck that rarely gets used, didn't want to start and it was obvious the battery was not fully charged.  Hubs connected this battery charger according the instructions (which are very good and detailed.  I like that because if I have to use it I want all the details in plain English to tell me exactly how) and few hours later the green charge light came on.  It's been real cold here for the past few weeks and the truck sits outside all the time in the elements and it was real cold when we tried to start it.  I'm giving this battery charger 5 stars for now because it was easy to use and worked like a charm charging the battery.  You just have to access to a 120v outlet to plug the battery charger into so if you are out in the boonies with no access to electricity it probably won't help you much.  It's small, easy to carry and I keep it in the box it came in.  So far so good with this battery charger.

title: Works Great
text: I have an old 1996 vehicle.  After locating the OBD port and connecting this scanner it told me I didn't have anything wrong with my car - no codes.  Be sure to turn the ignition on before having it scan.  It worked like a charm and is nice and small.  I have two scanners but this one is my favorite.

title: Works Pretty Good
text: I have an old 1996 vehicle and after I located the OBD port I was able to use this scanner.  I didn't have it completely connected the first time thought the scanner turned on.  After several attempts to read any codes and the scanner telling me it wasn't able to connect I rechecked the connection.  After that it worked fine and said my car didn't have anything going wrong with it - no codes were detected.  It's easy to use but the language only gives me a choice between French and Italian.....I guess I need to keep dinking with it though I read the manual.

title: Great For Road Trips With the Kids
text: I wish I had these about 14 years ago when my kids were toddlers.  These are great to put on the back of your car seats to keep all sorts of stuff in and off the floor and seat.  These connect to the head rest and have plenty of pockets and mesh slots for snacks, toys, napkins and all that stuff you need to take with on a road trip with the kids.  I don't see them lasting more than a couple of years but for $11.99 (as of this review), I think they're a bargain.

title: Easy to Use
text: This tire inflator is easy to use, and quickly inflates all 4 tires without much work from me.  As the other reviewers have succinctly described it's function, I will just say that I have two other tire inflators of differing brands and I think I like this one the best.  It's kind of flat so it's easy to store behind the seat of our old pick-up truck.

title: Great Idea but Didn't Really Work Well For Me
text: I like the idea of this swivel seat cushion but it's not working out real well for me.  I managed to pull my back out a couple of weeks ago and though I'm pretty much back to normal I want to try to not twist my back much for a couple more weeks so it can fully heal.  I put this cushion on my car seat and sat on it while I drove to pick up my kids from school.  It wasn't very comfortable to sit on and I don't have a big butt.  Also, it lifted me up making my legs get a little too close underneath the steering wheel and it was already set as high as it can go.  I liked being able to swivel around and more easily get out of  my car, that part was real good.  I think it's a good idea but it needs some more work.  The cushion is a little stiff and maybe should be a little bit bigger around.  Some car seats just aren't made to hold it (mine) so it might work really good in yours.  That's the only way I've used it so far and I know there are other uses for it besides putting in a car seat.  It seemed well-constructed and durable.

title: I Made a Mistake
text: I should have taken more time to thoroughly read the the stats of this radiator cap with temperature gauge.  It's for a Husqvarna dirt bike and I don't have one.  However, it seems to be very durably made and I think it would be a nice radiator cap to have especially since it tells the temperature inside the radiator.

title: Very Good Car Vacuum
text:
I like this car vacuum cleaner a lot. It's just like a regular Dust Buster and comes with some very useful accessories. It plugs into the electric port of your car and the ignition switch must be turned on though the car doesn't have to be running. The electric cord is VERY long and will allow access even in big cars - maybe even Limos.
