The suction and motor sound is just as powerful and loud as a Dust Buster and it really picked up a lot of trash in my car. It's not as good as using a shop vac but it worked fine. I drive a stick and having a wand accessory let me get a lot of collected dirt and junk out of the depressed stick bag. It's really intuitive and you don't need the scant instruction sheet included. This model does not have an internal battery that can be charged and will only run when plugged into the electrical port. Emptying the dirt cup is easy and they included an extra filter but I think you can wash them when they get all gunked up and get them ready to use over and over without having to buy more. The vacuum and all of it's accessories fit in the included bag though it's kind of a tight fit to get everything in it and zipped up but it's doable.

I like it a lot and we will definitely be putting this vacuum in our car on road trips. We can really trash up a car on vacation with eating and taking our pets so this will be really nice to keep it looking clean.

title: Works Well
text: The instruction booklet that comes with the KONNWEI KW600 Car Battery Tester is a lot to read.  I sat on my couch and carefully read through it all, pressed all the buttons and saw that what was happening on the tester's screen was nicely pictured in the booklet.  I took it to my car, attached it to the battery as instructed, went through a series of button pressing as instructed and voila! - my battery is good.  It should be since I just bought little over a year ago.  That's as far as I went with it.  I might do the other tests later but really, all I want to know is how good is my battery.  I guess I could have used a regular voltmeter for that........hmmmmm.

title: Great Tire Gauge
text: This tire gauge is definitely the most substantial gauge I've ever used.  I've always used those pencil style one and had to test the tire(s) several times until I felt confident about a reading.  With the Summit Tools gauge one reading seems to do it.  I don't have anything accurate to test it against but if it reads within a pound or two of the actual pressure I'm happy.  This gauge is easy to use and hold and I don't even need my glasses to see the reading.  Love it!

title: Good Idea
text: I installed this on my car's battery and that was a fairly simple process.  I can't say how well it works yet because my battery has not gone down below 11% charge.  My battery is old and needs replacing so it only has to be a matter of time before I know if this works like it should.  I think using this would be much more convenient that getting a jump start from another car or even attaching cables from an external battery pack that are made just for that purpose.  This review will have to be a work in progress but I will update it when I have more to say about it.  I will add though , that as of this review this battery protector costs around $65.00.  For that much (depending on which one is selected), you can purchase a battery pack which has other features like a flashlight and can charge electronics.

title: Works Very Well
text: Does this fit the back seat of my old Honda Civic perfectly? - No, but it's plenty close enough.  I wish I had had this cover years ago and it would have saved me a lot of cleaning and vacuuming.  It covers the back and seat but not the floor.  That's fine since I have other things to cover the floor with.  I use this when I have to take my dogs to the vet or on vacation or just when they're in the car.  It has holes for the seatbelts so my kids can sit on it and still be buckled up.  I may have to take it to a commercial laundry mat some day after it gets real dirty, but that beats scrubbing and vacuuming after one of my dogs gets sick or sheds a bunch of hair.

title: Nice to Have in The Car
text:
This is a good device to keep in your car at all times. It really is a pain when you go out to your car after work, for example, and see that one of your tires is real low or flat. I've picked up nails from time to time and if I had had a tire inflator that would have helped me out a lot to keep my tire inflated enough to get to the auto repair garage.

It's easy enough to use and after one time it all makes sense. The instructions are pretty good. I used it on one of my car tires and I guess the only thing that I found a bit difficult was getting the valve unscrewed fast enough so I wouldn't lose much air. It screws on instead of clamping on. But, I guess I could go one or two psi's higher to balance that out. The inflator worked fine for me though I read that other people have had problems with it. I hope it continues to work well and if it does not, I will update this review.

title: OK but Needs an Underglove
text: These are just average quality gloves and I don't think they will really last very long if used a lot by dirt bikers or other frequent users.  And a soft, thin glove needs to be worn underneath them because when I and my daughter closed our hands nearly into fists - like holding the grips on handlebars, they were rubbing the tops of our knuckles uncomfortably.  I might use these this winter on my bicycle if it gets cold enough, but not unless I have a pair of gloves on underneath.

title: Nice To Have in The Car
text: This is a great thing to have in the car.  It's small enough to keep in the side door pocket when not needed.  It can power a laptop with the standard outlet plug or recharge anything via USB cord.  The outer metal casing seems tough enough and the red color makes it easy to find.  I have a couple of similar car converters that I bought at least 5 or more years ago and they are still being used too.  Really, every car should have something like this just for back up in case you need a power source to run your laptop.

title: Very Useful Battery Booster
text:
This will be a review in progress because I don't have a dead car battery - yet - with which to test it. However, I can say that this battery booster seems to be solidly constructed, is a size (approx. 3" x 7") which is easier to keep in the trunk than jumper cables, though I wouldn't toss them out. What I find so intriguing about this battery booster is that another vehicle is not needed to jump start a dead car battery.

The ease of using it is remarkable - just plug one end of the included clamp cable into the end of booster box and attach the clamps to the battery terminals as you would regular jumper cables. Then start the car! I love it! And besides being able to jump start your car without another car, it has two USB ports for charging phones, laptops, etc... and a very bright led flash light. It also comes with a car electrical port plug so it can be recharged off the car battery while driving. When I first took it out of the box it was already 100% fully charged. It's advertised to be able to jump start about 30 times before needing recharging but I'd be happy if it just did it twice.

Again, I still need to find a dead battery but that shouldn't be too long. If it turns out to be junk I will definitely be back to update this review. I didn't want to wait until I had a dead battery to test it on to post a review because it already seemed to be so well made and the included parts are very durable. It also has a soft case to keep everything in and I might keep it all in the box it came it just for added protection in the trunk of my car.

title: WD-40 Specialist Superior Performance
text:
This is super good grease. The end where the pull tab was a bit bent up from shipping in a mailer bag but it was easy to repair. It fit my grease gun nicely and now it's so easy to apply to items that need grease. I first used it on my bicycle chain since this is the time of year that I love riding the most, and it's been raining a lot lately. I know regular WD-40 would work very well too, but since I got this can for review I'm going to squirt it on anything that could use it. Another reviewer said they used it on their garage doors so that sent me out to the garage and I greased up every part that bends or rubs up against something. It's so silent now!!! I don't have any machinery (other than my car) that I could use this on, but even for general household purposes it's really good stuff. My dad would have loved this stuff since he owned a whole shop of high-powered machinery in years past.

I was surprised to see the color of it - I've never seen blue grease before.

title: Amazon Basics Wheel Brush 2-Pack
text: These brushes are great for scrubbing the tires and wheels on a car.  I like how they get all the road dirt and grease off without a lot of hard scrubbing.  These are so much easier to use than a rag or sponge.  They are soft and don't scratch my wheel covers.  I guess the only thing I don't like about them is that they will only rest on their side if you lay them down.  I like the brush to be face down on the pavement and the handle easier to grab with soapy hands but they kept falling over.  No big deal really....just a bit annoying.

title: FloTool 10810 Battery Powered Siphon Pump
text:
I wish I had this pump a few weeks ago when the explosion in Alabama caused many of Georgia's gas stations to run out of gasoline. I had some gas in a can (learned my lesson way back in Katrina Days) just for such an occasion, but wanted to test the pump out so there was no emergency when I used this pump for the first time. I had refilled the can with fresh gasoline and used the pump to transfer some of it to our car's gas tank. Wow! So much easier! Before I had to heft the can up closer to gas spout and try to pour it into the tank using a long-stemmed, plastic funnel. It worked but was heavy, slow and messy.

This pump is really nice, though I hesitate to give it a full 5 stars so soon. I will only be using this for gasoline transfer and not for water unless it's going to get thrown away. I've never needed to transfer water so I'm not concerned about that. It takes 2 D cell batteries, seems sturdily built (basically all plastic) and pretty easy to use. Later, I will update this review to reflect how well the pump is still performing.

title: Camco 44512 Yellow FasTen Leveling Blocks
text:
I was hesitant at first to select these for review because I had no idea at the time how useful and practical they would be. I felt I took a chance on ordering them but am now very glad I did! These leveling blocks are quite awesome. I and my husband are very frequently using a long extension ladder around the house and have always struggled to get the feet of the ladder even on the ground before climbing up to do some work on the house. We've used bricks and boards and other assorted hard, flat pieces and it was usually precarious at best. These large square leveling blocks are wonderful to use for that. They are very stable and I can add as many as I need underneath one leg or both, and I feel much better going up the ladder knowing the feet are very securely balanced on top of these blocks. My brother has used leveling blocks (not these though) to keep up one end of furniture that he is repairing or refinishing up off the ground for easier access.

I have not yet needed to level our car for any reason, and we don't own a motor home that would need leveling when parked, but I can find a lot of uses for them just around the house. These are bright yellow and easy to see, made of very durable and strong plastic and are easy to stack together and carry using the black T-bar that screws down the middle of the stack. I deem this a very good and useful product!

title: Extech MN10 Pocket Multimeter
text:
This is a reasonably priced voltmeter (Multimeter) to be used for indoor basic household purposes. As of this review it costs $17.99. It's small and compact making carrying easier than the much larger multimeters.

What I like:

The inside fuse is very easy to replace although there is no place inside the voltmeter to store spares.
Battery compartment is easily accessible using a small Phillips head screwdriver.
The leads fit snugly into the voltmeter, and the points are nice and long. Endcaps are included to keep the points safe from damage.
Readouts are easy to see. The display has large numbers. But you will need your glasses to see the volt markings on the dial.

What I wish it had:
A stand to hold it upright making viewing it easier. As it is, it lays flat on it's back.
It comes with a 12v battery, but I would prefer it use a 9v battery for easier replacement.
No alligator clips are included which would have been a very nice extra.

It will detect a live circuit (outlet) but it seems to register it better if something is plugged into the outlet but it doesn't have to be turned on. (The voltmeter must be turned on.) I tested an outlet here in my office with nothing plugged in and the light on the voltmeter would faintly flicker, but when I plugged in a lamp which was turned off the light on the meter came on very brightly. I would always just assume it's a live circuit unless you know for sure you have cut off the power to it. Overall, very useful for indoor household current measurements, but not made for HVAC work.

title: Excellent Wiper Blades
text:
These came in the nick of time with all the wet, sleety, rainy and some snowy weather, but mainly it's been raining. I drive an old Honda 1996 Civic and these wiper blades were very easy to attach. The included instructions are very detailed - much better than other wiper blade instructions. The installation instructions include instructions on how to attach "J" Hook-Type (mine), Top Lock Style I, Top Lock Style II, Bayonet, Side Lock and Side Pin. The pictured illustrations are very detailed and clear.

I've been doing a lot of driving today with my new wiper blades going and they do an awesome job of wiping the windshield glass totally clear with minimal noise (squeak). Every wiper blade I have ever used on this car (and there have been many) have all squeaked a little bit, with some squeaking a lot more than others. These are very quiet in comparison. They really hug my windshield with no skipped spots. The box they come in can be recycled or composted. The blades have a piece of hard plastic covering the new blade rubber that needs to be removed before using. I removed the protective plastic strips after installation.

Overall - very good. As of this review I don't know how much these cost.

title: SOLAR BA7 100-1200 CCA Electronic Battery and System Tester
text:
I like this battery tester a lot so far. I am not inclined to understand complex displays, I want something to tell me if my car battery is good, bad or so-so. I connected the clamps to the battery terminals as directed in the instructions and 12.55 lit up on the LED screen and a green light came on saying my battery was good. I don't really know what "type" of battery I have in my car. I looked at it as best I could but I guess it didn't matter since the tester told me immediately the voltage it contained. I was curious about it's voltage because I think my battery is around 3 years old and I wondered if it was still holding a full charge or not.

This tester is very easy to operate, is extremely light weight, small and could easily fit into a car's glove compartment. My car battery is the only battery I've tested so far. I will take it over to my mom's house this weekend and test her car battery and any other batteries that fall within it's testing parameters. And it's great that this tester doesn't need any batteries of it's own to work. It uses the charge off the battery it's testing to power itself. Pretty cool!

title: These Are Very Useful
text:
It's great to go on a vacation or a long drive and have something which I can easily use to recharge my digital camera, android pad, Nintendo, iPod, and plethora of other small electronic devices while on the road and in the car. This worked great! I love that I can plug something into it that has regular household prongs and that it has a USB adapter for charging the small electronics. I would not plug anything that requires much voltage such as blow dryer or space heater, but for a small radio, cell phone charger or light, it works nicely! And it tilts so that if you need to adjust it somewhat you can do that.

I now keep one in each car. Really nice to have if you need to charge something along the way.

title: Awesome golf shoe
text: Attractive design and great traction. The only issue hubby had was on damper grounds but they clean off easily too. The comfort of the shoe is superb and perfect for a long day on the course.

title: Truly invaluable for comfort and ease, especially in the city!
text: When I watch my nephew, I sometimes grab an Uber when he is tired of walking after a long day in the city and I love that I can carry this around, truly lightweight and keep him safe when we are not in our vehicle (nowhere to park). He enjoys it too and it is very easy to get him strapped in and secured.

title: A GODSEND for our real estate office.
text: Three of our realtors have electric cars, and this has been amazing to have right at the office. Of course, they charge their cars overnight but sometimes between appointments, showings, last minute meetings and lunches and dinners, those miles add up QUICK, and now everyone is able to use the charger right at the office for their vehicles and keep their days on track without worrying about distance and time like they're on FOOT! Considering how much gas costs, this price is INCREDIBLE! The electrician we use for inspections installed it for us and we were ready to go. It is a good supplement to your regular charger or a backup for a work space but either way a device you cannot do without and shouldn't.

title: Works perfectly.
text: We have been using this during our small camping trips with no problem. It worked safely and the app was easy to set up and use. Truly gives peace of mind for hauling your precious cargo and getting from a to b in one piece.

title: TREMENDOUS reception in dead zones!!
text: Over Memorial Day Weekend, we headed up to Kezar Lake in Maine, and reception out there is very spotty. It is also VERY dark at night and is the last place you want to be stranded with no cell service. We love having this peace of mind with this booster and it has worked perfectly throughout our entire time there. This booster is perfect and actually necessary for those who drive in more remote areas because you need to be able to reach people for help if anything goes wrong. It is an investment in your safety and the peace of mind in others who now know they are able to reach you as well!

title: Lovely fragrance for dresser drawers.
text: I love the bright basil notes in these sachets and I've put them in my man's drawer for his t-shirts so he gets a nice pick-me-up as he gets dressed for work. They come in different fragrances so I am going to try something softer for myself, but these are a truly wonderful household and laundering item!

title: Affordable, Portable, and OH no so necessary!
text:
You don't realize how badly you need one of these until it's the middle of the night and your car starts shaking on the highway. Instead of having to find a gas station and get air, you can keep one of these in the trunk and make sure that doesn't even happen!

To use it is simple and its multi-use makes it a TREMENDOUS buy at this price. Just plug this into your lighter adapter, connect the nozzle you need for the tire/flotation device you are inflating, set the pressure needed, and fill 'er up! It works fast too. I also have a bike and I tightened up my tires on that as well, and am looking forward to using it during warmer weather for my silly pool floats.

title: Arrived damaged
text: Really disappointed. Return is a hassle

title: Sturdy Ice Scrapers
text: These ADORAMOUR Ice Scrapers are fairly heavy and thick. They come as a pair, which is great if you have more than one car. No snow or ice yet this season, but, now, we are very prepared. I am very happy with this order. Great product found on Amazon.

title: Great Buckets
text: These 3 pack collapsible buckets are sturdy and easy to use. When not in use, they fold up for easy storage. We used them to haul extra soil to our garden. We sprayed them clean, with the hose, dried them and folded them for storage until next time. Great product found on Amazon.

title: I liked the original look better
text: My model 3 came with the steel door still plate and it seems much better than these stickers.  I was not at all impressed especially since they were bent and I had to flatten them out as much as I could before putting them on.

title: It’s so convenient!!!
text: During the winter,  the only reason I take my EV to the gas station is to fill up my tires.  I dreaded having to do this and often times just ignore the alert.  With this pump; I can now leverage this and avoid the gas station altogether.

title: Premium cleaning cloths!
text: This works perfectly for using to dry my cars with.  Super soft; absorbs the water and easy to Rinse out.  Love the fact that it has a hanging hook to keep off the floors and to keep clean.

title: It works!
text: It inflates a bike tire in just a minute, charges quickly, screen is easy to read.

title: Good charger, tight fit
text: This car charger works well (I haven’t been able to test the full range of claims it has, but it works well as a phone charger and for passing through the DC outlet). It is a bit hard to attach since it fits very snugly in the socket, but that does mean it is a bit more resistant to being accidentally pulled out. If you are looking for a charger that you will be leaving in place, this is a good one. It is a bit large, but not too much so considering the number of ports that it has.

title: Great fit replacement air filter
text: Looks and feels exactly like the filter I replaced, fits perfectly, car runs great (and passed its smog check).

title: Works very well, saves time and aggravation.
text:
I've only been using this for a week, but so far it has been great. I've jumped my car 5 times (yes, I need to replace the battery) and the battery is still over 95%. I obviously can't speak to longevity, but so far so good.

It is very easy to use: hook the clamps to the battery (red positive/black negative), plug the blue end of the cable into the charger, press the little button next the the red light on the cable connector. It should turn green. Start the car, unplug the cable, disconnect the clamps, and go. The instructions warn not the crank the starter for more than 4 seconds (in my case, the battery is the only major issue, so the car starts immediately). This is so much easier to use than jumper cables (finding someone who can jump you, trying to get the cars positioned right, putting the cables away when you're done), and it takes only a minute or two.

The flashlight is very bright (although I do think the function change button is a bit awkward). I also haven't tried to use it for charging devices yet. but as a jump starter, it has already proven its worth.

title: I didn't know what I was missing out on
text:
I recently started using adhesive vinyl for crafts projects and was just using whatever I had handy for application and working out air bubbles. I grew up skateboarding and it's kind of like applying griptape. That said, I was putting in a lot more effort than necessary for a clean look.

The tools provided help with a clean, even application. I'd always opted for something hard and scraper-like but some of the soft ended rubber tools work wonders.

I gave 4 out of 4 stars because the knife included is flimsy and borderline dangerous. I almost sliced myself with the shirt/pants clip portion of the thing and it feels like it wants to fall apart in your hand. I didn't buy this for the knife but it's worth mentioning. Other than that, these tools have been very helpful.

title: Good for more than vehicles
text:
I didn't want to deal with long strips of LED lights and was looking for something to accent a few spots in my entertainment space. These work well with a sufficient power supply, key word there is sufficient. An underpowered supply will still toggle the red LEDs but you'll get none of the effects or other colors. Using an old laptop charger/pc monitor power supply I had leftover rectified that.

Adhesive backing seems to be holding up and they're in an area that gets extremely cold overnight and heated back up in the morning. Remote works but is contingent on an IR sensor I'm assuming, so it needs a proper line of side to the receiver to function.

Overall a solid product. I'd recommend it, permitting it fits your use case, as there are cheaper options.

title: Used for for everything
text:
OK I bought this product because it's the best value gram for gram than any other.

title: Worked well to clean my high windows
text:
I have high arched windows above the regular windows throughout my house and the only way for me to clean them without this device would be to get up and down the 6' ladder using a wet cloth. This telegraphing pole allowed me to stay safely on the ground and clean them using the microfiber cleaning head on the one side, then wipe the dirt and water away cleanly using the squeegee on the other side.

I'd recently had the house painted and they pressure washed it and left all of the windows a mess afterwards, so I was really able to give this a good test by cleaning those high windows. Cleaning with the microfiber head was similar to doing it by hand with a microfiber cloth - meaning I had to go over especially stuck on things like bird droppings with some extra oomph - but instead of needing to climb up and down a ladder to wash, rinse, and wash again I could do it on the ground where I didn't risk a fall and I could rinse and wash more quickly. I do wish that the microfiber head was just a little bit larger than it is though, but that's my only complaint.

The squeegee head worked as well as a hand held squeegee does (in my opinion at least). I found that it took more than one wipe at times, and it seemed to work better when I used enough pressure to press it more firmly against the glass as I brought it downwards - just like a hand held squeegee.

I hope the pictures I took show up well enough so you can see how dirty my windows were, and how clean I was able to get them using this high window cleaner. Overall I really like this window cleaning tool a lot because it did a good job, speeded up the process so I got done faster than I could have otherwise, and I didn't need to climb up and down a ladder to get the work done. In fact, I didn't even have to get the ladder out of the garage.

I purchased this high window cleaning tool at a reduced price for testing, evaluation, and review purposes.

title: Very well made and useful
text:
I received my Mas27 Car Trash Bag today and couldn't have been more surprised or pleased than I was when I took it out of the plastic bag and examined it. This is an extremely well thought out and very well constructed heavy duty polyester bag with 3.7 gallon PVC lined receptacle inside to keep it leak proof and easy to wipe clean.

It comes in an attractive cocoa brown fabric with appealing green piping, has an adjustable strap that goes around the headrest holder so the bag drapes down over the back of the seat. The opening of the bag has fabric covered wire to help the bag hold its shape and allow for the bag to be closed when not in use or to keep garbage out of sight. It has a handy Velcro closure at the top to secure it closed as needed and two wire mesh holders on each side that can hold water bottles, baby bottles, children's toys, or other items for convenience.

I looked the bag over and examined it carefully and then tugged at the seams a bit to test the stitching, and I'm very pleased with the quality of work. The seams are snug, no gapping when I tugged, the stitches are solid and even, and the stitches on the tabs on each side are not just double stitched, but stitched multiple times to ensure it's durability. Impressive work!

This car trash bag is built to last! REALLY built to last! It's hard to find things this well made at this price point anymore.

The seller just sent out an email with some suggestions I thought I'd share. "Here are a few tips on using the Car Trash Bag to prevent bad smell for your car."

1. Put a scented fabric softener sheet inside of the trash bag is a great tip to absorb the smell and freshen the air.
2. If you drink tea, pour some of the dry loose tea inside the trash bag. This will prevent or eliminate the smell. If you use tea bags, just cut them open and pour into the bag.
3. Wipe inside of the trash bag by a wet tower every two weeks.

I put this in my car this evening and took my daughter & granddaughter out to a show, and my 8 y/o granddaughter immediately laid claim to the bag as a toy holder. So here's another suggestion from me, if you have kids get one for trash & the other to hold their toys. Seems to work very well to help keep their toys organized and their hands busy when on a drive!

text:
Nice strong cross bars. Ignore instructions that tell you your Tahoe Rails must be 24" to 36" apart. Tahoe rails are over 48" and so are the crossbars in the kit. Note that you will need a hacksaw because both provided crossbars a sized to fit the front, but the Tahoe rails are narrower at the rear. I had to cut about 1.5" off the bar for the rear. The instructions also make no mention if the two black, long plates with bolts in them which are in the box. Take the bolts out and slide each plate, nuts down, into the end of the bar, then slide the bar onto its bar mount. The bolts then go thru the bars center and into the nuts that are welded on the bottom of the "black plate".
Other than above, these are good, strong crossbars and fit the 2021 and newer Tahoes. Chevy will eventually offer a perfect fit kit. If you want to have a no hassle install, just have your dealership do the install also.

title: No measurements = No Sell
text: Well, the ad has a picture showing two measurements;  the compressed length and the extended length.  Unfortunately the ad never provides the measures for the product.  This is typical stupid situation for many auto products...I can only guess that some secret parts manual has the clues which the advertiser doesn't feel he needs to provide in the ad.  There are 4 essential numbers that are needed; 1) Lift capacity per strut in pounds;  2) size of the socket on the end in fractional inches or mm's; 3) Fully extended length; and 4) compressed length.  Without that there is no way to know if it will fit.  Given that the ad provides none of these, I could not buy the product.  I will continue to look for other ads by smarter sellers.

title: Built in rubber ring does not prevent air leakage
text:
TL;DR version - if they didn't leak they're exactly what I'd want. I have managed to push them on tight and it work but cheapo ones have historically done better with no thought involved.

Backstory....

Because I live in a city of non-stop construction and crappy contractors who can't secure their load, as well as working at an office building with a hundred people or more driving in daily who drive on screw and nail-covered roads, I keep air inflators/jump starters in my and my wife's cars.

One of these gets used every time the temperature drops below 60f outside because, we're assuming, the rim of my wife's car shrinks just enough in the cold to cause a leak that nobody can find... three years and six tire shop visits and yeah... so I use an air compressor a lot just for her.

In use

There are three that showed with two different types. One has an air release button, the other two don't. The part you screw to your air hose has nothing but brass, does not have a rubber seal, and oddly does not leak at all. That side's perfect.

The side with the seal has a clamp, seal, and does leak unless you push it on tightly and then maybe rotate it slightly to cause it to tighten further.

I've been using air inflators with the cheap plastic handle clip on for over a decade and not had any issues. These brass with rings ones... issues. I set my wife's car inflating yesterday with the inflator and walked away - it's got an auto shutoff... I needed 15 pounds added and I figured I'd be back with a pound or two to spare. Got back and had 11 pounds to go.

Now, it's hard to hear hissing when you've got an air compressor going but you could hear hissing. Tire facing side of the equation and it was the brass fitting. Pushing the thing on harder stopped it and I swapped it for another which had the same issue. Both I found would not create a seal like the cheapo plastic ones. It's push it on hard, clamp down, maybe rotate and it works.

The metal part, manufacturing appears great. The connection, not so great. Surmountable, but not something you'd expect if you're purchasing a product where the second claim is how it's not going to leak.

title: Qi charger built like a tank
text:
I received some useful advice from the below review that finally pointed me to a solution for the Pixel 7 Pro not working with this. I'm leaving the original review down below but warning that if you've got a Pixel that's turning on and off and on and off when connected to this charger, it's an app called Pixel Stand (many thanks for telling me this Shawn) that has to be disabled in settings/apps, and probably not the charger. (It works after disabling that app)

I've updated the stars and headline, and other than the position of the side grips and being unable to charge through a really thick case I have no complaints... original review follows:

I'm going to preface this with this works with any Samsung I've thrown at it without a case on. It does not work with my Pixel 7 Pro for more than 10 seconds before the base powers off and on again. I think this thing could hold a truck but we've got some issues.

I've tried both attached to the battery and USB and a Pixel 7 Pro with/without case, Samsung Galaxy S21 Ultra 5G with and without case, Samsung Galaxy S9, and a Samsung Galaxy Note 8 without the case.

Pixel 7 Pro charges for 10 seconds, powers off, back on. With or without case. Completely useless as a charger for this.
Samsung Galaxy S9 works with or without its TPU soft case
Samsung Galaxy Note 8 only works without a case (although I have a fairly thick case for this one)
Samsung Galaxy S21 5G Ultra works with or without its soft TPU case however it will not fast charge due to the fast charger being incompatible.

I initially thought my motorcycle battery was bad (had two in a row replaced due to bad cells,) and took it to a USB charger that's fast compatible with everything. No change.

I took each one of those phones and placed them on a standard 15 watt Qi charger, and also on a non-standard special charger (just has issues) - all of them charged in their cases.

Next, we've got the side clamps... right in the volume buttons... oof...

I've got an attempt to reach the manufacturer in to determine if they think it's a bad unit (I doubt it, as it worked on three out of five phones,) but yeah - thick case, Pixel 7 Pro, buttons on the side. This has issues that you're not going to run into unless you 1) have a phone that's having issues with it immediately, 2) review / have a lot of phones just sitting around to test.

title: Does exactly what its supposed to do, no problems and no issues.
text:
Just to be clear, this is a review of the 10 foot cable, which seems to come and go on this page.

This is exactly what I wanted and needed. I have a "generator shack" next to my office/shop and the male 4-prong twist lock I had installed directly on the wiring from my fuse box failed. Right before Hurricane Matthew. So I got the correct socket, installed it on the interior wall of the generator shack and used this to reach it. It worked without a hitch, no failures, nothing getting hot or even warm, and powered me with 240 volts at 30 amps all the way through the hurricane. I use a double breaker to split 240 to 120 on both rails, or buss bars, in the service box. This powers a 240 volt water heater as well as all the 120 volt equipment. Electricity was off for about 36 hours here and the generator ran constantly, with the power transferred by this cord the whole time.

I do wish I could have found a 5 foot cord of equal quality and with the same end connectors as this has. That was all I really needed and the longer the wire, the higher the voltage loss. All-in-all this worked out just fine. It's now a permanent part of my emergency power installation.

When reviewing an item I usually start with 5 stars and take stars off for poor quality, poor engineering, seller issues, etc. There were no problems or issues with this cable. It did exactly what it should do, I got it in good time, the price was the lowest I could find for this type item on Amazon -- there's nothing to take any stars off of my review for.

title: Very happy with these so far ...
text:
I ordered these tire/rim combinations for my boat trailer. They arrived within a few days and were exactly as described.

The tires mounted on the rims are Eco-Trail brand, which is made by a company called "Qind". Qind is a Chinese manufacturer relatively new to the tire market having been in business since 1990. Still, the term "new" is relative because that's 26 years in the tire business. A quick search on the internet did not reveal any complaints or recalls regarding Qind or Eco-Trail.

The quality and composition of the tire is unknown. It's rubber with nylon bias-ply belting and that's about all I can tell. The tire sells for a few dollars more than the Kenda brand as a rule, so it might not be unreasonable to think these tires are in that same class and perhaps a marginally better tire.

A selling point of these tires is that they are "... a truly revolutionary tread design that gives the appearance and footprint similar to that of a radial tire." The tread design looks more than adequate to me.

The rims are hot-dipped galvanized steel. They look exactly like a hot dipped galvanized rim should look, with a good coating of galvanization (zinc) for rust proofing and some runs or puddling of the hot dip apparent but not obvious. The rim is made with two pieces of steel, the inner wheel where the "spokes" are is welded to the outer rim that grips the tire. This is standard for this kind of tire and rim combination and exactly like the OEM tires and rims that they replaced on my boat trailer. There are four welds solidly done with no apparent voids, dross or spall. This is important because this is a failure point for this type of wheel, there is significant torque on the wheel when cornering and backing and if these welds are not sturdy and solid the wheel can break at that point. These welds appear to me to be easily adequate to handle that torque and are at least as good as the OEM wheels that have lasted many years despite significant rusting.

The hot dipped galvanization LOOKS like hot dipped galvanization. If you're buying these tires because you want shiny silver rims of show room quality you're going to be disappointed. If you're buying these because you need the rust resistance that galvanization offers and don't really care if the rim looks like hot dipped steel, they're great. At this price point you have no reason to expect anything else.

I chose the galvanized rims for their resistance to rust. I launch my boat in salt, brackish and fresh water so rust is a big factor and a large part of the reason I needed to replace my old rims. The old rims were rusted to the point and at places where it was starting to worry me. The old tires were also having issues with dry rot/weather checking even though they had plenty of tread on them. One of the tires had a slow leak which I'm not sure if that was due to weathering, rust eating through the rim or a valve stem problem. Being as it was time to replace the whole tire and wheel anyway I didn't bother to try to fix that slow leak, I had just made a practice of checking and inflating those tires before towing which is always a good policy even with a brand new tire and rim.

While I do take my boat various places throughout the year, the vast majority of the time (like 9 out of 10 times) I only tow it 5 miles from my house to a ramp that has brackish water on a creek near the Intercoastal Waterway. So it's not like I put a lot of miles on my trailer tires. I've never actually kept track of the mileage but I'm sure it's less than 500 miles a year.

The valve stems on these rims are brass with a rubber collar rather than rubber with a metal insert. This is a very good system and is indicative of good quality.

The OEM tires were Load Range "B" and these new tires are Load Range "C". So they are a sturdier tire than the OEM tires. I went that route hoping to get a few more years out of them because Load Range "C" tires are a thicker sidewall and thus any damage, dry rot or weather checking has to penetrate deeper before it becomes an issue. The Load Range "C" tires are a bit of overkill but they should stand up better over time too.

The pressure rating of these tires is 90 PSI according to the sidewall. To me that seems like a lot, the old ones were 60 PSI. However, it is vital to inflate a trailer tire to at least its rated pressure and generally it is better to be slightly over-inflated than under-inflated. The tire sidewall for a trailer tire is thicker than a car/truck tire to withstand the weight of the load with minimal flexing. Flexing develops heat and ruins trailer tires, so pump your trailer tires up to whatever is stated on the sidewall, even if that seems a bit high as it does in this case. My compressor equalizes at exactly 90 PSI with these tires and I cannot get any more air into them, so I can just hit the rated PSI thankfully.

I just put these tires on my trailer a few days ago so I have no idea what they will be like for performance and longevity. The problem I've experienced with trailer tires in the past is that they do not wear out tread-wise. They fail because of age and things like dry-rot and weather checking. I park my boat trailer on wooden blocks to keep the wheels off the damp ground and cover them with wheel covers. It's not unusual to get 6 - 10 years out of a set of tires with this procedure. The price of these tires with galvanized rims is very attractive and that's why I chose this item. Time will tell if that's a good choice and if there's anything else to report in the future I'll come back and add to this review.

title: Working very well so far.
text:
I like this "bulb" so far. I needed this type of lamp base for the stern/all-around post light on my boat. LEDs draw much, much less from the battery and I've converted all my onboard lights to LEDs which saves a huge hit on my battery with the engine off and on my alternator when running at night with the engine on.

This lamp is very bright. That stern light is located on a post starboard aft and this thing lights up the helm and aft deck very nicely also. I have no doubt it can be seen for more than the legally required distance at night.

You do need to be sure that you have it oriented in the socket correctly. One of the contacts on the bottom is for positive and one is for negative. This doesn't make any difference with an incandescent filament bulb because it only needs to have current flowing through the filament to make the light shine. With an LED lamp there's more to it than that, there's a little circuit board and some electronic components that actually control and operate the LED emitters and that stuff needs to have the correct current flow direction. Just like most things, for instance the starter motor on an engine or a radio/stereo, most things need a positive feed and a negative ground.

So if you put this in a socket and it doesn't work, take it out and rotate it 180 degrees and put it back in. It's best to test most types of LEDs before you completely reassemble the fixture they're in. Put it in the socket, flip the switch and see if it comes on. If it doesn't, turn it a half turn and flip the switch again. When it works from a switch throw THEN put the light back together and you're done.

The orientation of the contacts on the bottom of the lamp is only an issue with lamps like these that have a symmetrical base, lamps with a contact on both ends (like a lot of dome lights in cars) etc. Other types of lamps will only insert and lock one way (I.E. 1157/1156 lamps) and the manufacturer has placed the contacts at the proper position for them to work.

Being as LEDs have incredible longevity compared to incandescent bulbs, you're probably done with working on that light for years unless something else in that circuit fails. On a boat there are always condensation and corrosion issues so time will tell if this lamp can hold up to that. If something fails it will be due to that. This lamp has been in service for a month or so now, it's been out on the water a few times and survived a bunch of thunderstorm downpours so I'm optimistic that it will hold up for a while.

Which is also why I bought a two-pack. If the one fails I at least have a fresh one (and a spare standby incandescent bulb) to keep me operating and legal until I can get a replacement. Being as I only installed, tested and use one of the two I don't know if they both work but I'm going to assume they do and I left the spare in it's electrostatic packaging safely protected from elements in the console.

title: Meh ...
text:
It worked, it's cheap but if you only need it for a once a year or every couple years job then it's good enough for that without spending 3-5x as much on a better gauge set.

Mine came with the plastic lens on the high pressure gauge laying in the bottom of the box. The lenses are very cheap plastic, made like a mayonnaise jar lid and they screw on. So don't freak out if you think you got a broken gauge, just screw the lens back on.

It doesn't have the high-pressure fitting that GM vehicles use on the high pressure side of the A/C system. So if you're going to use it on a General Motors vehicle AND you need a high side pressure reading then you'd better look into getting an adapter.

It finger tightened up just fine on the fittings I used it for and it doesn't appear to leak or waste coolant, so that's a plus. I had no signs of a leak (frost is a very good indicator of a leak) and they connected up to what they fit on exactly as they should. If you have problems connecting them then it's something else that's wrong, like your Schrader valve is protruding too far, the threads on the A/C connector are damaged, etc. It's just a really basic, cheap, set of gauges for very occasional use. They look impressive hanging in the garage though.

There are fittings on the back of the valve bar to screw the hoses onto when not in use. This keeps the hoses from picking up contaminants and keeps your "O" rings from getting lost between jobs so my advice is to use them. With gunk in the hoses and the "O" rings missing this isn't a cheap but useful gauge set, it's just cheap junk. If you use them like I do/will it can be a LONG time between taking this off the wall and using it so my suggestion is not to torque down the hose connectors so tight you compress your "O" rings to uselessness.

I bought this to use on a GM vehicle and considering I don't have an adapter I can't measure my high side pressure. So I put a half can of R12 (yes, I have a few of those laying around, eat your heart out) into the system and the low pressure side isn't out of spec so I'm hoping I don't have an overcharge condition. But because these gauges don't come with the right size fitting I can't be sure. I get good cooling which doesn't happen with an overcharged system so I can't be too far off and there IS a little wiggle room as far as the freon charge goes.

I'm not at all impressed with this gauge set but it got the job done for me so while I'm not thrilled with these El Cheapo gauges I'm glad I have the AC on my Blazer working like it should again. My laser thermometer says the temp in the cooling vents is below freezing, so gotta love that cold air on a hot summer day in a black truck. The compressor was cycling on and off rapidly and the air blew sometimes cool and sometimes not but never cold so all of that adds up to low freon. As far as I know this '94 Blazer has never had a freon recharge so I can't complain, losing a half or a little better of a pound of freon in almost 20 years is acceptable. Now with a half (maybe 3/4) can added to the system the compressor behaves like it should and I'm pulling very cold air from the condenser.

So I hate to bang on these gauges too much, they got me there and they got me there on the cheap. But be advised, you're not getting top quality equipment at this price. Without some kind of adapter you're not getting a high side reading on a GM vehicle either and they DON'T come with R134A connectors or anything else. If you want to use these with an R134a system you might as well buy better gauges with the correct connections already included. If you're servicing the AC on an older vehicle and you want to slide by on the cheap side of things, these do the job but barely.

Oh, and the description is VERY clear about what these are, they are NOT set up for R134a and the description doesn't say they ARE so don't whine if you tried to get by cheap and couldn't be bothered to actually read the product description or look at the pictures. If you bought this gauge set for working on an R134a system and nothing else then it's nobody's fault but your own. A set of adapters for R134a quick connectors is $14.70 which STILL makes the price of these pretty cheap compared to a higher quality professional set.

I did a reasonable amount of shopping around before deciding on these BECAUSE I wanted to work on an R12 system. I'm not really disappointed in them for the price point they sell at so don't be discouraged by the two star review. The two stars are because these ARE a cheaply made set of gauges but that doesn't mean they won't do the job for you. With the product description, my review and others you should be able to make a reasonably well informed decision on whether to buy these or not.

Edit 16 June 2016 --
I've used these gauges exactly twice since I bought them. The hook fell off and got lost so now I have to tie them to the hood to see them but they're still doing the job well enough. I bought some adapters for R134a connections for a newer vehicle so I could use them the second time. I charged an air conditioning system on a Jeep I bought a while ago and it uses R134a refrigerant. The system was completely empty after the repairs were done so I had to weigh the refrigerant, you can't go by pressure with R134a but I wanted to monitor pressures as I did the charging and they worked for that. I pulled a hard vacuum on the system and used these gauges to verify the vacuum was holding without leaks also. I ran my vacuum pump (through the gauges, with the gauges attached) for two hours, then shut everything off and let the system sit overnight and well into the next day. The system was under vacuum for nearly 24 hours and the gauges held up fine for that time. Who knows if they'll work the next time I need them but I feel that with the two uses I got my money's worth out of them.

text:
I use it to remove rust from motorcycle gas tanks.
Step:
1) insert a bunch of nuts and bolts and screws, wrap the tank in a shipping blanket and duct tape it tight, throw in the dryer and run on air dry for 30 min or so
2) shake out all the crud and rinse it out, water is fine.
3) (for very very bad tanks) use the electrolytic rust removal procedure. (Google it) it’s gonna take a while
4) clean out tank again, water is fine.
5) plug tank back up again and fill with this magic stuff. Wait a few days. Repeat if needed.
6) rinse out with acetone or 99% alcohol. DO NOT use water or it will flash rust and you’ll feel dumb (like me).
7) dry, and then seal with Casewell tank sealer (my fav). Now the tank will outlive your grandkids.

text:

title: Works Perfect
text:
This unit fits Ford vans from the 80s and early 90s, among other vehicles. A lot of Class B and Class C RVs were built on these vans... including ours. The steering is floaty and jittery. On tramlined or uneven roads, or in winds, even those from passing trucks, keeping the RV (or van) stable in the right direction can be an exhausting and finicky exercise.

The Monroe SA1930 is a bolt-on damper - sort of a shock absorber for steering jitter. Bolt one end to the frame, the other end to the steering (see the photos I uploaded), adjust and tighten.

Now the floaty RV drives a lot more like a car. Rides that used to require two delicate hands balanced on the arm-rests now can be done mostly with one hand, just as you do in a car.

The only flaw I've noticed is that the van requires the full travel (maybe a bit more) than the Monroe has for the full range. But I haven't noticed any impact in practice, with it installed for a month.

title: The G20 with an added button, needs relays.

It's a fine alarm, but it will cost a LOT more than what you pay. Most cars trigger the power door locks and the dome light with positive (+). Scytek only gives triggers of negative (-). You can make it work by adding relays but, at local store prices, that's 3 x $5.95 (for 3 relays) plus $5 for the blade connector pack so you're out another $20 and a bunch of space (relays aren't small.)

If you don't care about turning on the dome light when disarming, and you plan ahead and buy the relays first, it's a great alarm. Very configurable.

Note: this cover does not allow complete open access to the bed.....the 2-3ft section closest to the rear of the cab does not fold up, but instead stays secured onto the bed. I missed this little detail when I ordered it. My last folding hard tonneau cover folded one more time to where it would lean up against the rear window of the cab, allowing complete open access to the entire bed. Even so, this is a GREAT bed cover for what you pay. I've had it for 2 months now with no issues at all. Very well made and it seems it will last quite a while.

title: GREAT reverse lights for my 2014 F-150!
text: These were a GREAT upgrade from the stock reverse light bulb on my 2014 F-150! The stock bulb is a size  912 bulb and these fit perfectly. These were super easy to install. I had the housings removed, bulbs switched out, and housings reinstalled in about 10mins. As far as brightness and lumens over the stock bulbs, it is a complete night and day difference. Visibility and illumination of what is behind you is incredible. I bought 2 more similar bulbs (LEDs, size 912 replacement) from another brand/maker for the truck bed cargo lights (on top of the cab beside the 3rd brake light) and they fit perfectly there as well, so these bulbs will also work there as well. BTW - the 3rd brake light bulb is a size 912 as well, so these bulbs will work there as well. Once I upgrade the regular brake lights I will update the 3rd row brake light to this one so they all match lumens and brightness. I cannot comment on life of the product because I just installed them, but LEDs tend to last quite longer than standard bulbs. In a nutshell this is the best money spent to upgrade reverse lights on your vehicle.

title: Absolutely Ridiculous
text:
I rarely write any reviews on products, but this time I had to make an exception.

Our family loves our old Fords. I've always changed the oil myself on our Expeditions and F150's. I've occasionally used Seafoam in the crank case to keep things clean, but I heard about this product from a Youtuber named FordTechMakuloko who is an expert Ford mechanic. Anyway, if you're familiar with the 5.4L 3 valve Ford motor, it's a great motor as long as it's well maintained because there are tiny screens on the variable valve timing solenoids that if they get plugged up with sludge throws off the timing for the motor and makes it run rough.

Our Expedition has 200k and despite the religious oil changes with Mobil 1 synthetic and Factory oil filter... you're gonna have some carbon buildup after that many miles. The instructions said to use 2 cans of this stuff due to the 7 quarts oil capacity but I only used one. Ran it for about 15 min at 1200ish rpm and drained / refilled the oil.

Started it up and all I can say is WOW!. It sounds like a new motor. Before when you would start it up it sounded like a diesel. Valves chattering all over the place lifter noises. I though oh well she's an old gal, lets see how much longer she can last. Now I realize it was prob. just the VCT soledoids all along, she's still go a lot of life left in her. The diesel sound was even more pronounced when the engine was hot. You can still hear it now just faintly but waaaaaay better than before. And drivability! Acceleration is better and cruising is sooo smooth. It literally feels like a new car. I just ordered 3 more cans of this and will be treating the engine again (with 2 cans) during the next oil change. Can't wait till the wifey drives around for a thousand miles or so, I want to see how clean the oil stays now compared to before.

I also used a can on my F150 (140k mi) which was having a little misfire issue at high throttle. Since then, I have put the pedal to the metal trying to reproduce that issue and haven't heard a misfire since.

Great stuff! Highly recommended. My garage cabinet won't be without it ever again.

It seems the average you can expect is 6 to 8 hrs of cooling capacity, when on the internal battery, alone. Some folks report less, some, more; as per usual/to be expected, in the Reviews. :-)
Easy to move about with the extended handles; but, as others commented, it is a bit heavy. However... about the same as my older, ice-cooled cooler, when its loaded with all the 'ice blocks'. Excepting, here - no ice blocks needed!
Even the 37 L. unit I bought is quite roomy (I also like the convenience of the baskets). It fits well in the trunk of my sedan; whose trunk isn't particularly deep. Would have bought the next larger unit, but it wasn't on Sale; and it would have been an inch or so too tall to fit in my trunk, anyway. The larger units' heights would, of course, present little/no problem in a SUV or truck.
Looking fwd to using it in a couple of weeks for my monthly 'procurement tour' (errand run/grocery shopping) into Albuquerque, 65 mi.'s North.

title: Great Phone Mount.
text:
I have had several Phone Mounts for my motorcycles over the years and I can honestly say that this is the best so far. Previously I had considered the RAM Mount to be the top of the class. This KEWIG is great. I have more confidence that this will hold my Phone with a Firm Grip. The edges of the mount are nice and big I especially appreciate the fact that KEWIG provides several different options with the requisite hardware for attaching the Mount to your bike. Handlebar connectors with differing sizes as well as a stub for integrating into a Sideview mirror stem. (The RAM required you to also purchase whichever option you needed as a separate purchase) The one caveat here might be that the connection ball and joint on the mount itself are plastic and threaded and there is always the possibility that it is point of failure with vibration and exposure to the elements. Comparing it to the previous version it looks like they redesigned connector base of the mount to have it be mounted onto a rubber puck surrounded by a metal ring. Ostensibly to further increase vibration dampening. I find it interesting that KEWIG combines metal with plastic, as mentioned above I likely would have made the ball and joint out of metal as it will absorb a lot of vibration, elements and plastic threads are notoriously easy to strip.
Overall I am very pleased with this mount. On a purely selfish note I wish they had released this new design as the wireless charging version.

A definite recommend. Quality of construction, extra options and design are top notch.

title: Excellent product from every aspect
text:
Let's start with the quality of this product. I have to give credit to the designers/engineers who designed this product without cutting corners. The charger itself has a solid build and does not feel cheap. I will be honest, its a beefy unit! Even though the charging alligator clips are made of plastic, its not flimsy and has solid copper clips. I have owned a battery charger which is also a good unit but the clamps were made of cheap, flimsy plastic with probably aluminum clips. As a engineer myself, I would never cut corners on quality.

Regarding the charger operation: As my commute to work is pretty short, my car battery does not get fully charged and the voltage is slightly lower than 12.6V so now I charge the lead-acid battery and top-up the electrolyte every 2-3 months as its pretty dry in Phoenix. I really like the digital display instead of LEDs because I prefer to see numbers and you don't have to manually monitor the voltage with multimeter. The charging process just took few hours as I was only topping-up the battery voltage a little bit. The process went well without any issues. Since I had to install the battery back in my car, I couldn't verify the maintenance mode.

It would be good if the charger came with a carry bag. Overall, this is a great product from Hulkman. I would definitely recommend it.

Note: I am not posting any images for this review as there are plenty of images from other reviewers.

title: Great battery charger
text:
I would like to share my experience with this battery charger with respect to my Subaru Outback 12V Flooded lead Acid battery (490 CCA). Since my drive to work only takes less than 15 mins and that too at relatively low speed, I noticed that the battery voltage stayed around 12.56V which is on the lower side for the 12V battery. Got the same feedback from a mechanic who tested the battery for its condition. So, I used this battery charger to top-up the voltage as the battery itself is in good condition.
Its really easy to use and it raised the battery voltage to 12.9V in about 4 hours. I was monitoring the charger output voltage and case temperature frequently and didn't notice anything abnormal. Since I reinstalled the battery back in the vehicle just after charging, I did not use the trickle feature so can't comment on that.
I went for this model because slow charging/low current charging is always better for a battery as it minimizes internal power dissipation. It does take more time to charge but if we plan accordingly, there is no issue.
Things that I don't like: The battery clamps are made of flimsy plastic, I would have preferred metal clamps or at least better quality plastic clamps (probably cost-cutting measure!). The carry bag that came with it was a joke (really!). It gave the feeling of a Walmart grocery bag. Its better not to include carry bag than to put something like that. I bought a separate hard case from caseling which was a perfect fit for this charger. I am not taking off any star for these cons as it really doesn't affect the usage.
Overall, I am pretty satisfied with this charger for now. This is a cost effective product (with 5-year warranty) and I would definitely recommend it.

title: A good portable Tire inflator at budget price
text:
I am based in Lubbock where temperature variation can be ridiculous especially when it gets closer to November. We get sudden change in temperature (from 80F to below 32F) with incoming cold wave which results in severe drop in tire pressure (about 8 to 10 PSI). My main requirements were: compact, pressure display, auto shut-off, and low power consumption so I don't have to run it from the battery. I own a Subaru Outback 2018 and since I recently got an oil change done, the service center topped up the tire pressure. So, to test the Tire inflator, I had to deflate both the front tires to 30 PSI and set the tire pressure on the tool to 36 PSI. It ran off the 12V socket while the engine was running as per manufacturer instructions. It took less than 2 minutes (approximately) to reach the target pressure. The inflator does fill it up to 0.5 PSI above the target pressure to compensate for the pressure drop while unplugging the valve. The final tire pressure when measured using my analog meter was about 37 PSI so the accuracy of the tool is within +/- 0.5 PSI as per specs. The display readout is very clear during day and night.
A potential issue I noticed was the power cord was pretty flimsy especially when the inflator is rated for 10A. I did notice that the cable was getting slightly warm which would concern me if I was using it for longer time. Its good to have a long power cable (11 ft.) but if the higher resistance is not compensated by thicker gauge wire, then its a problem. I don't mind paying extra for that.
The air outlet tube did get pretty warm but I guess its normal unless you have an intercooler stage which is not feasible for a compact compressor.
Overall, for a price of $27.00, it is an excellent product which does the job. I will update my review after I get to use it more and I don't see that as an issue as it will be pretty cold in few weeks.

text: Bought these for my aged father who was having trouble seeing to drive at night. I tried them out myself before giving them to him. They did not work. Only thing it does is tint yellow. That was the biggest waste of money!” If you want night driving glasses, go to your optometrist and tell him or her “I need anti-glare night driving prescription lenses so I can see to drive at night!” My optometrist put it in my prescription glasses and I can see great at night when wearing my prescription eye glasses, if I leave home & forget to take my prescription eye glasses with me, I cannot see to drive at night. I tried to get my aged father to go to his optometrist to get prescription night driving glasses but he had just got his prescription renewed and didn’t want to fork out money for another pair of prescription eye glasses. Don’t waste your money on these glasses you see advertised on here or on tv, they’re all a bunch of hogwash. Now I’m over $30 out and stuck with a pair of cheap yellow sunglasses that I can’t send back! Waste of money. They don’t make 1 percent of a difference in seeing better.

title: Great add on for the engine (but with a warning)
text: One of the best things I put on my 2013 Fiat 500 Sport! The throttle response is smoother and quicker. And then when the tach gets into the 4-5K rpm range the sound is pure music to any gear head!!  The installation was straight forward and not difficult if you can follow directions and have basic tools. NOW THE WARNING: One of the steps (#17) is to install a vent fitting into the intake tube. The fitting is plastic and is breakable. I broke mine. It says to hand start it but I couldn't get it started and tried to use a wrench to get it started but it broke off in the intake tube. I called K&N customer service and they sent me a new vent fitting. In trying to get the broken piece out I screwed up the threads in the intake tube and then the new fitting wouldn't work at all. So I called K&N to get a new intake tube and vent fitting. They had me send pictures of the broken pieces and of the partial installation. I got a new intake tube and a new vent fitting. This time I got it hand started and hand tight and used a wrench for about 1/2 turn. The rest of the installation was no problem at all. In talking with  customer service I got the feeling that this a common problem. The vent fitting is the very weak link in a well designed intake system. Another company makes an intake system for the Fiat 500 but instead of a plastic fitting they have a metal fitting welded onto the intake tube. In spite of the problems I had I would still recommend the K&N system. I have used K&N products in most of my cars and all of my motorcycles.

title: MUCH CHEAPER THEN THE COMPETION!
text:
I own an assortment of holders and mounts from the other well known major brand and this is good but not perfect. Made of aluminum and less then what others charge for similar mounts. I actually couldn't find another exactly like this one that was made to fit a 2" bar. This fits 1 3\4" easily, however it was designed for a tight fit around a 1 3/4" bar and leaves a bit to be desired on a 2" bar.

It fits, but the circumference of the mount isn't formed to a 2" as you would expect and a little daylight shows at the top and the bottom when tightened down on a 2" bar. It's formed to a 1 3/4" bar. They should've formed it to a 2" bar and included rubber spacers to accommodate a 1 3/4" bar. That way it would fit a 2" bar without any daylight showing top and bottom of the inner circumference when tightened on a 2" bar.

Ball is a metal ball covered in a rubber like coating and true 1" so other items will fit tight with no problem. Hex on the ball to tighten it to the mount is oddly a 12mm wrench size then the typical 13mm/3/8" you find on others, but hey, it works and is machined to tolerance. It'll hold the same weight as the competition.

For the money I'll keep it until I can find another solution. I bought a 12" ape-hanger handlebar for my HD that is a beefy 2" in diameter. I need to mount a HH CB and a cell phone for GPS mapping. This will do for now. It's built well enough it's not going anywhere, I just don't like the gap on my 2" thick handlebar. You have to be looking directly at it to see the gap, but I'm a perfectionist and will look for another solution for my application, otherwise it's a quality piece! Good quality mount for the money, just be aware it's for a 1 3/4" application and not so much for 2" bar although it'll work as noted.

title: One Bad A** Steering Wheel Spinner Knob!
text:
I've had a bunch of these over the years on everything from farm tractors to semi tractors I drove over the road. This is one of the best steering wheel spinners hands down regarding comfort, ease of installation, and convenience.

Installed on the inside of the steering wheel it's out of the way folded down as well as safe because the only thing above the flat plane of the steering wheel is the edge of the knob that spins, and I mean very little of the spinner knob. For example, if the wheel was spinning fast because someone hit a curb or worse, the part that's above the wheel would barely bump your arm, and that's if your arm was flat on the steering wheel! At that, if you did contact it, it would spin right past your arm. You probably won't even feel or notice it as you'll be focused on get control of that steering wheel anyway. Watch out for those curbs and potholes!

Now it's real accessible when needed too! Just pull it up and it locks in place automatically! When you don't need or want it up, just press the button in the center of the knob and just that quick fold it down out of the way! Slick! If you're concerned about feeling the part that clamps around your steering wheel while driving, it's real smooth and shouldn't be an issue for most. If it bothers you, just put your steering wheel cover over it after it's mounted. Problem solved!

I like it so much I'm going to buy another one, or two. Enjoy!

title: This one's well designed!
text:
This is great! The skeleton pic is sealed in a clear, see through type of resin or polymer(?) attached to the bolt head! Not a cheesy stud with a sticker that will come off the first time you wash it. As well, the screw thread is timed just right to position the skeleton so that it's properly facing the rear, letting anyone looking from the rear know not to mess with your scooter!

Finger tight gets it aligned all but 3/4 of the way for me. Take a pair of standard pliers, (NOT a pair of vice-grips or channel-locks), open them to the wide position and use the teeth meant to bite on something (the middle of the jaw, not the ends) to grab the head of the bolt hard enough it won't slip, but not so hard you bite into the knurled head damaging it. Grip it tight but "DON'T SLIP"! Now turn it another 3/4 turn until it's lined up with the seat, the fender, and facing the rear. Trust me, it'll be torqued enough to stay in and not fall out. Done!

Using the stock Harley seat-bolt in the rear fender should work as above, because it should be the one machined to fit one way in the hole/slot in the rear fender that keeps it from turning while tightening. If it doesn't line up properly, look to see how much farther it needs to turn and which way to line up the skeleton properly. Then unscrew it making sure to keep the nut in it's current position and not let it fall to the floor by reaching up under the fender to hold it in place while unscrewing. "This is important".

Once it's unscrewed, lower the nut just a little being careful to hold it's position. "Don't turn it" and lose the position it was in. Now turn the nut left or right "only as far as needed" so the skeleton will be lined up when tightened down.

Hold it there and re-tighten the seat-bolt, keeping the nut in said position. This is what's called "timing the threads" so that the head of the seat-bolt is lined up when tightened down so the skeleton faces the rear. Enjoy!!!

title: Horrible Company..... Don't expect any customer service what-so-ever....
text:
I had to order these steps 3 times. Kept receiving the wrong product and had to send them back. Decided I would do the research to find the company's phone number so I could reach out to them. While doing so I left them an email through Amazon to ask about the quality because they had no reviews. Instantly each of their products had a 5-star review with no text. (Obviously the company just left a fraudulent review for their own product).

After doing a lot of digging, I found out that this company hides under three to four different names but all names lead back to the same address in New Jersey. They also have multiple phone numbers that lead to a call center where you won't find any help or info. You'll actually be lucky if anyone ever answers your call. Voicemails aren't returned. Very rarely will you ever reach an actual person. And when you do.... you'll find out that you wasted your time even trying to talk to them. They know nothing about the products. They can't do anything to assist you either. They are a generic call center that takes calls for many different products/companies. They are simply there to give people the illusion that there is a company with customer service.

This is a Chinese company and there is NO customer service at all.... NONE!

I'd stay far away from this company.

There is no doubt that this is single handedly the worst company I've ever run across that sells anything on Amazon.

Now for the details on the steps themselves.... I did finally receive the correct product and ran into a couple of issues with the steps:

- Prior to installing the steps, I hooked everything up to make sure that it would work. Had a couple of intermittent issues but ultimately they started working unexpectedly and I just figured that it was due to a loose connection. So once I got everything to operate I went through the process of hooking everything up to my RV.

- These steps are much narrower than your traditional steps on an RV.

- After installing the steps I realized that you typically have to push the manual control button to open or close the steps twice before they will work.

- There is an obnoxiously loud “beep” whenever you use the steps. Don’t ever plan on entering or exiting your RV quietly…. Whether you are opening or closing the steps or turning the light bar on/off, you get the pleasure of hearing this loud beep.

- There are also L.E.D.’s that constantly run inside the control box on this step unit. Which means that if you don’t cut power to these steps when not in use, they will constantly put a drain on your battery even when they aren’t opening and closing.

- The door switch: If you open the door before turning on the RV power to your steps (and the steps are retracted), the steps won’t automatically open. You must use the manual control switch to bring the steps to the position the door switch is in before the door switch will cause an automatic response. Normal steps will open if the door is open the moment power is supplied to the controller on an automatic step unit.

- These steps are also very shallow. When mounting the steps, if your mounting point isn’t almost flush with the skirting on the RV, you will have to come up with some sort of spacer that will lower your steps. These steps don’t drop much in the opening and closing process. If your skirting drops much, the steps will hit the Side of your RV. I purchased two solid steel bars to lower the steps so they would operate properly. Even doing so, once the step was installed, it still left the L.E.D. light bar too high and too close to the skirting on the RV and therefore blocks all the light when on.

- The hardware sent with the steps is useless.... You're going to have to plan on going and getting hardware that is the proper length.

- Be prepared to splice in a lot of extra wiring because they don’t include adequate lengths to hook this step up. And the wiring to the controller is hardwired. You cannot just unscrew a connector to replace the wire. You have to splice in wiring to the existing wires that are hardwired from the manufacturer.

This step looks nice compared to the standard black steps that you find everywhere for RV’s, but this manufacturer screwed up just about every single function the step has. You’d think that merely out of dumb luck they would have gotten something right. But it actually appears as though they went out of their way to make this product as badly as is humanly possible.

China went out of their way to set a whole new standard of “Poor quality” on this one.

title: There's Good and Bad here....
text:
First, let's start with the good:

This thing really pumps the fuel. I'm actually pleasantly surprised at how well this thing moves fuel or other liquids. I'd rate this thing at 5 stars for this alone....

BUT:

The cons.... The fuel pump has no filtering screen on the intake. If you suck up debris from a tank, you risk damaging the pump. I went down to Home Depot and picked up a metal screen strainer for a sink and turned it into a filtering screen for the pump.

Second, the pump is kind of short... I have a 5 gallon gas can and this pump will only reach about 2/3 of the way to the bottom of the tank.

Third, the outlet hose is very short. You really aren't going to reach very far with this. I think I may go find some hose for it so that it is more useful.

Fourth, this thing is made of the cheapest, thinnest plastic you can imagine! Think "Dollar Store" quality.

Overall, this is a great pump that someone tried to manufacture as cheaply as possible. The quality in this pump makes it worth about $5. However, if you don't mind doing a little upgrading once you receive it and you are extremely careful with how you handle it and store it, I think it could be a handy tool.

I haven't put much time on this yet, so we will have to see how it holds up to daily use. Right now, I will give it 3 stars as long as it continues to work and doesn't break.

Not to be crude, but you can actually stand up to take a leak in this toilet. Most RV toilets are far too shallow to use this way. This toilet doesn't have that problem.

It also has the swirling jet setup so that the toilet spins water around the bowl when flushing.
