I was hoping to find a surface mounted switch that would allow me to run a switch to the 12V L.E.D. lights on the ceiling of my RV. You cannot do that with these. You have to cut an opening in the wall. I also thought I would just make a small box that would allow me to screw into the wall and then mount the switch assembly inside of. You will need a good inch or more thickness to a setup like this because of the terminals on the back of the switch. After attaching your wires to them it will require a good deal of space.

They seem to be a little pricey for being a switch but honestly, compared to other sellers out there, these weren't priced too high. They really look nice. Value for money is one of those things that really comes down to each individual's personal opinion.

Very smooth operation to the switches. I've already installed one set in my RV and they look great. I hope they are durable and will last for years. I cannot tell how strong/durable they are at this time. They seem to be of good quality though.

Hope this is helpful to anyone looking!

title: Be informed about this product before you buy.....
text:
Buyers beware.... I'm going to try to be very descriptive here for everyone's information.

First, let's give credit where credit is due.... The grille looks very nice. Was actually impressed visually when it arrived. Looked better than the pics on Amazon make it look. Based on visual appeal alone, I would rate this grille at 5 stars.

Based on everything else about this grille, I hate to even give it 1 star. Manufacturing should get a negative star review.

A couple of things that really irritate me about this product...

First, the ad says that all hardware needed comes with it. This is NOT true.

When I uninstalled my factory grille, I held onto the bolts and nuts so I could use them on this new grille because no hardware (other than the studs) where included with the grille. My first mistake was that I assumed that the hardware I took off the truck would fit the new grille.

When installing the new grille, the first nut I tried to place on one of the studs appeared to fit (visually) because they are quite close in size. as I started to turn the nut, it cross-threaded and is now stuck on the bolt. You cannot get to the top of the stud to hold it in place and therefore I cannot remove this nut. Unfortunately, I cannot tighten it down or remove it.

Once this happened I went to find hardware that would work. Upon finding the nuts and bolts needed I went back to work installing. Here's the second major problem.... The studs that are in this grille are garbage. Very cheap, flimsy material. As I installed another nut on one of them I was lightly turning the nut (not even to the point where it was seated and ready for pressure to be put on it to tighten it in place) the stud broke in half. I cannot stress enough that I wasn't even close to putting tension on this stud/nut. Now I have a second point which has no support on the hood.

Again, this is a nice looking product. Haven't even had it out for a drive yet so I cannot speak about its durability yet. You better make sure you get the right hardware before you start the job and handle the install as though it is built of the cheapest chinese plastic available on the planet.

I'm going to see if I can add a couple of photos from my phone later to show some of the issues. I am not aware if Amazon will allow me to add them after I submit this review, but I will try.

text: The cover is very durable and waterproof. In September of 2014 we traveled from Michigan to South Carolina and had rain during the trip. I purchased the carrier and needed a cover to accommodate the 3 large suitcases, 1 small suitcase, 2 Pak n' Plays and 2 strollers, all of which we had to take on our trip, and it all fit inside the cover. We have a Large SUV, but all 3 rows of seating for 3 adults and two small children in car seats took up most of the interior space. I would recommend this bag to anyone using a hitch type cargo carrier to cover and protect their belongings from the weather.

My previous OBD2 tool was only a year old. Comparing this OBD2 to my old one is like night and day. It’s so much better and much easier to use. A 10 year old could operate it no problem lol.

Best part is there is little to no lag. My old tool would think and think for sometimes several minutes before giving a code. This tool is super fast and accurate.

A nice touch is the color screen. Good for low light conditions to read. Old one was black and white. Looks sleek!

Tested on 3 vehicles and worked flawlessly. The plug also goes it perfect. Not too tight not too loose. The tight ones worry me about damaging the vehicle. You won’t have this problem with this scanner.

I think anyone who drives a car should own one. Self diagnosing any issue before going to a mechanic and getting ripped off.

title: Washable? High flow? Fuel economy?
text:
This review is for the E-1990 filter as fitted to my 2010 Ford Escape.
Some have said that the filter is a tight fit, or simply does not fit the airbox. Granted, it IS snug, but if a little bit of filter grease is applied to the contact points, it goes right in.
I installed the filter, and drove the vehicle normally. It does take the computer a little time to compensate for the increased airflow thru the filter, so it might appear that the engine is not running well at first. Mine took a few hundred miles to recalibrate.
Observations: My average gas mileage increased .3 - .4 MPG. Not impressive by any means, but an increase nonetheless.
The real performance gain is on acceleration. Can't give numbers, but it's something you can feel in the seat of your pants.
The real gain, for me, is in the cost savings when replacing the air filter. 2 OEM type replacement filters cost about the same as a single K&N.
So, in 5 months, I've broke even.

text:
Bought these for my 2018 Wrangler JK. Installation instructions were clear, but it should come with additional hardware.

Example: instructions say to reuse the 3 main bolts under the Jeep. Problem was, those bolts did not exist. At first I thought it was just my Jeep, but I went up to the dealer lot and looked at a half dozen jeeps like mine and NONE of them had the bolts! These bolts should be included with the steps.

Another example: It came with the correct number of bolts and washers for the pinch weld holes, but no nuts! You have to have nuts to hold the bolts on! I had to go the additional hardware at Lowe’s.

As far as installation goes, take your time. Do not try to snug up one bolt at a time. You have to do them a little at a time. At times it looked as though the steps were not going to fit, but once you start tightening them down it all comes together.

Bottom line: very solid, look great, need to come with additional hardware.

1. Use 7mm socket to remove 2 screws from panel under steering wheel.
2. Start the engine and leave at idle.
3. Place both key fobs within reach.
4. Use a U.S. penny or dime to connect the prongs in the gray harness connection.
5. When the driver and passenger locks cycle, alternate pressing the LOCK & UNLOCK buttons on the fobs until the doors respond.
6. Find something fun to do with your remaining time; learn another language, read a book about parenting, or clean your gutters.

title: Tone It Down!
text:
I ordered 36sq ft. of Kilmat because I had just received 54sq ft. of Noico’s version of the same product. Math was never my best subject and I didn’t order enough material to cover the problem areas of my 1996 Bronco. Really, the only reason I bought Kilmat is because the shipping was 3 days faster. What I’ve noticed after installing both is:
1. It was easier to see when the dimples on Kilmat were depressed. This could be because the Noico surface was black and Kilmat was silver. Kilmat, 1 - Noico, 0
2. Kilmat was more rigid where Noico seemed more malleable. The rigidity made cutting to size a bit easier since the material wasn’t folding on its own. About 70% of the surfaces I coated were flat or had minimal angles but, cutting to avoid waste is important. Kilmat, 2 - Noico, 0
3. Having purchased Noico in both the 36sq ft. and 18sq ft. boxes, I noticed they contained different size sheets. The bigger box of course had bigger sheets. Again, waste is important. Kilmat’s sheets were smaller than Noico’s (large box) sheets but Noico’s (small box) sheets were smallest. Kilmat, 2 - Noico, 1
4. Kilmat was cheaper per square and sipping was faster. Also, Kilmat’s packaging, though similar to Noico’s, prevented the sheets from being bent/creased which meant easier install and less waste. Kilmat, 3 - Noico, 1
Overall, I can’t say one works better than the other for deadening sound because I used both of them. However, for the next project requiring sound deadener, I’ll buy Kilmat.

title: Keep Rollin, Rollin, Rollin!
text:
I got this to roll down Noico 80mil sound deadener in a 1996 Ford Bronco. The one thing I found is that this roller will not fit into the ribs of the bed. Knowing that, I would have also bought one about 1.5” wide as well.
Many reviews noted how the nut loosened but, I checked mine upon arrival and have tried to keep an eye on it throughout. It hasn’t been loose but, I can see how the nut could back off the threads in certain circumstances.

title: NO ECHO! EcHo, echo...
text:
Having only used Dynamat in the past, I was skeptical that a product half the price could perform. I was wrong. I applied this to just the rear cargo area of a 1996 Bronco. During installation I found the different size boxes contained different sized sheets. This probably something I should’ve realized while gathering a materials list but, I overlooked it and felt it was worthy of bringing attention. It helped in my case but it could play badly for someone using it in more cramped applications. Also, it’s important to understand that you don’t actually have to totally encase your vehicle to get positive results. For a budget project, I believe one could achieve dramatic reductions in road noise by ONLY coating the flat parts of stamped metal and/or areas where excessive rattling is expected.
The adhesive is strong and I trust it will hold for quite awhile as long as it isn’t molested in the future. I also found that the roller I used might have been a tad too wide (2.5”). If I had it to do over, I would’ve bought something closer to 1.5” as the contact surface would make for easier application.

*IF I HAD* to note a complaint, it would be that the sheets in the 36sq ft. box were folded so tightly that it made creases in the aluminum. Those creases required a little extra elbow work to remove air bubbles. The simple fix was to use a dental-type pick to make a small hole for the air to be pressed out. Now, they’re not noticeable.
Overall, I think Noico knocked it outta the park. If it performs as well as I think it will, I’ll purchase more of this product for a 1972 Beetle project and some of the thermal-based closed cell foam insulation (Noico Red) to be applied on the headliners, firewall, and above the exhaust routing.

title: Takes guts and muscle to pop off the side trim.  Just replace the screen!
text:
My 2015 Cadillac Cue system was frozen on the warning screen requesting you do not take your eyes off the road. I tried every hokie pokie remedy on You Tube with zero success. I knew the computer was still ok because it was responding appropriately to voice commands and changes not involving the touch screen. Hence the bold move to follow the YouTube fix of replacing just the touch screen.

We ordered the part and the plastic tools to remove the trim pieces, it arrived in 2 days as promised. Saturday morning we set out to fix the car! Damn, 1 hour and we still couldn’t get the trim pieces off... we were just too chicken to pop them off. NOTE: Be brave and just go for it... I guess?

We brought it to my friend and local mechanic who was able to complete the job. Originally he was charging me $250, it took him several hours, he had never done one before and I was fine with paying him... still way less than $1400 to the dealer. But... here’s where you may want to pay attention... there were some bubbles on the back side of the screen. He forgot to remove the screen protector. He did charge me an additional $75 for this oversight, which I gladly paid, as going back in to remove the protector took more of his time.. all said and done, the labor was $325 and my car is like new for just unde $500, it all works perfectly and he didn’t even leave a fingerprint or a scratch...so I’m very happy.

Lessons learned: Pop the damn side trim panel yourself and save $325, remove the screen protector film on the back of the screen, order the plastic tools and trust yourself, ALWAYS check YouTube before taking your car to the dealer

I set out three lights, so I had to install 9 batteries. In an emergency situation on the side of a busy highway. That's tedious and time-consuming. title: So far so good
text:
Bought just one and have used it for 5 days now, driving cross country in a semi-tractor. Conditions included various kinds of rain and mist, Winter road dirt/salt, and strong winds. I bought just one so I could compare performance to a cheapo Winter blade that's about two months old. Will update as I go.

So far it's been excellent. Huge improvement:
1. No skips or noise.
2. Cleans much better.
3. Can visually see how it maintains better contact with the contours of the windshield. The cheapo blade is crushing the middle and the ends just barely touch. This one is consistent.
4. The cheapo one had a problem with wind: when it got to the side of the windshield the wind would lift it off the glass. Not so with this new blade.

Soon to come: snow and ice. It's January in Buffalo NY, so it's going to be a serious test...

A note on installation: my wiper arm has the "hook" and installation is a little different: have to rotate the arm 90 degrees *then* pull it out, to snap it into place. other blades you don't need to rotate. Some reviewers, who thought the mounting was loose, didn't seem to know that.

The instructions are pretty lame. I can never understand that. Spend a few thousand on great instructions, then it costs zero extra money to make copies of it. Same printing costs as lousy instructions.

text:
Picked it up for an upcoming road trip. I like that it comes in the bag..I was worried I would have to keep it in the box. Haha.

This thing is a total beast, too. Metal and decent plastic. It's a LOT heavier than the pump we keep in my wife's car, BUT it also pumps a LOT faster. Comparative: Hers - 24PSI to 35PSI is about 6 minutes. Mine - 28PSI to 35PSI was about 3 minutes...after our trip, I'm probably going to put this one in her car.

Can work off a battery or the car lighter. That's handy to keep around the garage. Also comes with an inflation needle for other equipment so this is a must for sports families.

Absolutely love it and that you can set it to shut off at a certain PSI is awesome. I just wish I would have had this last year when I found out my spare was flat when I went to change a tire.

text:

The one with the table, though, is a bit low for my taste, but it will work for my kid....who actually sits in the back seat and will use it.

The Organizer:
Lots of pockets. LOTS. Places for pencils, crayons, papers, notepads, magazines...2DS...Kindle...Whatever. I like that the USB cable is extra long. it can reach all the way across to the other organizer that will hold my battery pack. It's a great idea these days to have ports easily accessible. This thing has places for water bottles and pouches for snacks. Wish I had gotten these years ago just for this one.

The Table:
Plenty of snack pouches. Large "windowed" pocket for a tablet. The way this mounts on the seat, I'm not too worried about it falling down. The velcro that holds the table in place is sturdy enough, but I don't think I'd be putting an actual laptop on here...Maybe a tablet with a keyboard at most. My oldest son will use it to hold his ereader and phone, I'm sure.

The fact that these are so easy to install makes it that much better. We can take them down and toss them in the trunk at tourist attractions without having to empty pouch by pouch. They can be rolled up or laid flat..no problem. The Organizer is by far the best part of this set.

title: Remote Starting Rocks
text:
The Alert 350-R I purchase on Amazon was not what you would call a "novice friendly" unit. The unit was intended for sale only to expert installers. The instructions that came with the unit were minimal and technical. Units sold in places like the big Marts have much more usable installation instructions for those who have never done such a project.

That said, the installation took me all day, in spite of the fact that I also purchased the applicable T-harness which was supposed to reduce, by 80 percent, the amount of work required for the installation. Not on my F250 SuperDuty. It does eliminate some work, but I'm not sure it was worth the $17 paid for it.

Installed, the Alert 350-R works like a champ. Tech support was English speaking and knowledgeable. The two times I felt that I needed their guidance, they were polite and very helpful. I am glad I made this purchase and am enjoying the benefits of having remote start capabilities on my vehicle. If you're not intimidated by going under the dash, stripping wires and making electrical connections, after you find the right wire, then go for it. Good luck!

I stumbled on these when searching for a real mans gas can, and voila!! No mower spilled gas on me and the mower and the lawn, no more back breaking lifting of a 5 gallon can to maneuver the poorly designed "no spill" spouts onto and into the mower tank.

It is like everything else you buy, where these crazy CA labels state all the fears and environmental and cancer concerns as determined by their "government for the people". I have spilled more gas on me and the grass, and vented more fumes into the atmosphere than I wanted to, because of the ridiculous "no spill" spouts sold today.

This little gem is like manna from heaven - I am buying another for my 2nd gas can. It is well made, works as advertised, no issues. Buy one!

title: Perfect fit ‘04 Dodge Ram 1500 quad cab
text:
This is a nice quality hitch. I put this on an ‘04 Dodge Ram 1500 and I really like that it doesn’t lessen my ground clearance. At first it looked like I was going to need to cut a notch in the plastic below the bumper but it turned out that I didn’t. You will need a floor jack or some kind of lift (or a couple of hefty friends) to get it in place. It took about two hours from the time I cut the box open until it was completely installed. The bulk of that time was figuring out the directions, they’re a little vague, and fishing the bolts and plates into position inside the frame. I had help raising it into position; getting the bolts lined up with the holes in the hitch without knocking them back inside the frame was tricky. We tied line onto the bottom of each screw and fed it thru the holes in the hitch which let us hold the screws steady while raising the hitch into place. I’m am fairly mechanical and my friend isn’t at all but it went on smoothly and without needing any alterations.

I originally bought this to use with a home snowplow but realized that I needed much heavier plow to handle my road. I’ve read about people using the front hitch for backing campers into tight spots and I can see where this would be pretty handy. I plan to use this for a bike rack instead of putting them on the back of the camper where they would be blocking a storage door.

title: Mostly great, one annoying issue
text:
I installed this shunt in my RV to monitor my SOC without having to look at the attached display (mounted at the foot of my bed which is mostly covered when the slide is in). It works great and I was really pleased with all the information I now had access to. Then I exceeded my inverter and it went into shutdown mode, requiring a power cycle. This resets the SOC to 100% regardless of the batteries voltage. When it first happened I was actually intentionally trying to run the batteries to 0 to check my banks actual total ah. Charged is 29.2v, when the inverter shutdown it was at 26v. I then had to power cycle... When I checked after it was then saying I suddenly had 100% but still at 26v. I can still just rely on the voltage but it would be nice if the unit could keep the % accurate after losing power (for less than a second).

Another thought after using this for the last 2 weeks is that unless you won't always have a phone handy (or need the extra relay/sensor capabilities of this monitor) I would suggest getting the Bluetooth only shunt. Based on the reviews Victron must have made substantial improvements to the app. I found it works flawlessly with a very good range (greater than 35 ft). I will agree with a few of the other reviewers though, the farther away the slower the unit connects.

title: Easy 4.5" 2wd lift
text:
Spindles went on easily, everything lined up and fit (for the spindles, the brake lines are a different story). I am no mechanic but I have installed lifts on several of my past trucks/suvs, so this may be an easier job for some but a much harder job for those that have little to no experience with swapping spindles. There are no instructions, although these are very similar to the maxtrac spindles that have a video for how to install them (if you do watch the video, I did not grind down the spindle and found no binding so that may not be applicable to these spindles).

The spindles are significantly heavier than the stock spindles, I don't know if this is good or bad. They also do not have holes drilled for the rotor guard, which honestly may be a good thing...no rocks stuck between them and the rotor.

After install of just the front, the top of the fender well is ~40.25" off the ground, the rear is ~38.75" (my truck did not come with any blocks on the rear). So to get it level I bought 1.5" blocks, not the 2" blocks that I've seen come with these as a kit. The 0.5" per side wider track width is hardly noticeable.

There were no problems getting the truck aligned to within factory specs, I included my alignment printout. The turning radius and drive are not noticeably different from stock.

The reason they get 4 stars instead of 5 is the brake line kit. The lines don't fit into the stock mounting brackets so you have to use 2 wrenches... PITA while brake fluid is going everywhere. The brake line kit also comes with adapters, my 2018 F150 did not need them.

All and all it is a very easy lift to install that allows you to keep very close to factory geometry without needing to ride on compressed coils that bump you around (spacer lift). I would recommend these spindles to a friend.

Edit:
I uploaded pictures of the 1.5" blocks installed (ReadyLift 66-2051 1.5" Rear Block Kit), I also added a picture of what the 0.5" wider track width looks like. With stock wheels and tires the fender wells front and rear are 40.25" high, perfectly level.

title: Paid for itself in a week!
text: I actually bought this to charge my 2009 Honda Metropolitan scooter which is something like a Vespa. However days after I bought this charger,  I was all dressed up to go somewhere, but my 2011 Honda Element was dead. There apparently was enough juice to turn on the lights, but when I turned the key in the ignition the motor was flat dead.  I called AAA to give me a jump, but I was told I already use my four service calls within the year.  So I asked how much would it cost to come out and give me a jump? AAA wanted $95! I live in a metropolitan area, so I am surely just minutes away from an AAA contractor, and in the past when this is happened they used a portable jumper and the guy was gone in less than 5 minutes. No way was I going to pay AAA such a high price, especially when I’m already paying them a lot for their premium membership! Luckily the thought came into my mind to try this little charger because I remember in the reviews some people say it even started their car.  I am not at all a mechanical person, so I watched a YouTube video on how to do this, then I hooked the cables and let the unit run for less than an hour because I really had to be somewhere. When I then unpowered the charger, removed the cables, and turned the key there was at first a very slight delay, and then it started right up! After a couple pumps of the accelerator it sounded as good as new, but I did go directly to a shop and had a new battery installed. I am not only super thrilled that this little charger did a great job on a fairly good-sized car, I felt great that it was simple enough for a dumb blonde to operate it successfully. Best of all, I didn’t give AAA the victory of gouging $95 from me in a near emergency situation. That’s why am taking the time to write this review!

title: Works Perfectly!
text: Since Covid, I’ve had so many issues with dead car batteries. I have a passenger car and have had to jump my car more times that I can count. When I first looked for a jumper I purchased the Schumacher SJ1289. It has the jump starter, portable power, and air compressor. It worked fine for almost a year. I had a flat tire and tried to use the air compressor and there was a hole in the hose so it would not work. I had never used the air compressor and I should have tested it once I got it. I contacted the manufacturer to get a replacement hose and they don’t sell them. I figured I would just use it to jump my car. 2 months later I try and jump my car and it would not work. I completely charged it and it was dead. I trashed it and saw these much smaller boost jumpers and purchased the NEXPOW 2000A Peak 18000mAh Car Jump Starter with USB Quick Charge 3.0. I watched some YouTube videos and it it appeared to do what I need it to do. I charged it and tried to use it and it would not jump my small passenger car. I was so disappointed and had to call road service. I returned that one and was on the hunt for another and found this one. It worked beautifully! Easy to use and jumped my car with no issues. The one thing that happened tho was after I jumped the car, I got out the car to remove the jumper and before I could even get out my car died. All the interior lights went off and my car would not even crank. I unplugged the cables and plugged them in and my interior lights immediately came on and my car started. This time I remained in the car and revved the engine for a few minutes and I was good to go. I’ve had to jump my car twice so far with this and it worked both times. After 2 jumps the charger is at 80%. I hope to get a lot of use out of this and hopes it lasts longer than the last 2.

title: Worked Great!
text:
Due to Covid, I don’t drive my car often. I’ve tried to drive my car to run errands and visit family and after sitting for a few weeks, my battery is always dead. I first purchased a Schumacher Jump Starter which has other functions like air compressor, light, charging station and more. After a year and a half use (approximately 6 times) it no longer will jump my car. So I purchased this battery charger and it worked perfectly. I knew I was going over my parents for Thanksgiving so I started charging my battery the day before. I let it charge overnight. I’m not sure how long it took to charge but when I went to start my car, the charger read “Off” so I figured my battery was charged. I put the key in the ignition and crossed my fingers! It started right up. Totally worth the money I spent.

The only thing I didn’t like was the cord length. It’s VERY short. I had to but an extension cord in order to be able to plug this in.

I’ve read other reviews and they stated that their charger didn’t come with instructions but mine did. Definitely worth the purchase!

Hence, I decided to see how to get the key cut on the new device.  Local locksmith said did not have equipment and referred me to a mobile locksmith specializing in these laser cuts who quoted me $65.  So I went to local GM dealer which did the duplicate for $15.  Reprogramming on my car is very easy:  just start the car with the old key, kill the ignition, insert the new device, turn the car on and presto...all done.  But in internet researching this I found some involve rewiring to reprogram, so I suggest you check this carefully for your specific vehicle before ordering as the reprogramming might be more than you wish to undertake. Be patient, it takes time to get Japanese trains if they are sent Japan mail. The Bachmann Plymouth switcher is not this quality and costs twice as much. Update...it WILL go through one section of smallest radius track provided there are larger radius track sections on either side creating an easement. I am using 2 of them on a very small layout and they pass through the tight corners smoothly with some wheel slip. Also the two axles in front are driven. The rear axle has pickup but is not driven. You can apply power to the back axle and test the unit easily.

title: MRC is my favorite choice
text: Momentum control is fantastic. This pack is just perfect for a small to medium G scale setup. I have 4 different MRC controllers and I prefer them over Kato, Bachmann, LGB, and Piko. In model railroads there is no limit to the amount of money you can go through in a hurry. There are very expensive power pack and throttle combinations available that provide fantastic options. I am primarily analog user, although one of my MRC packs enables DCC functionality like sound,speed, and lighting and can also be toggled to straight analog. That's about as far as I go for now in digutal. My tech 7 has enough power to run my trains with lighted cars and also accessories. For greater current demands I bought the MRC Power G a monster with 10 amps and a variable transformer fan cooled. The Tech 7 momentum control lets your loco behave like a real train. It will start very very slowly, reach the set speed, and slow down very very slowly. It has increased my enjoyment tremendously. MRC packs do not have wall transformer dongles, they are all in one so you can turn the entire unit off. They are a great value compared to other power packs. I get better, smoother running at affordable prices. I have not overloaded one yet and I light up as many cars and buildings as I can.

title: Saved our trailer, must have!
text: While in Nevada for work for nine months, the power went out in the trailer about five months in. I wasn’t running anything big so I know I didn’t trip a breaker. Turned everything off just in case and checked the power pedestal outside. The breaker did flip! I flipped it back on and smelled something horrible so I flipped it off. Unplugged the surge protector from the pedestal and the plug in was melting and the surge protector prongs were fried. Go to the office and of course the maintenance guy is gone for a week. I get him on the phone and he tried telling me it’s probably faulty wiring in our trailer and our fault. Hell no sir, I know pedestals are notorious for being a problem! We get an electrician there and he checks out the pedestal and sure enough, fried wires. title: If you were keyed, save your money.
text:
This product was purchased based on posted reviews for the purpose of repairing/covering up a new silver car that has been keyed and door swiped four times.

If your car was keyed with anything more than a very light scratch, this product will not help and in fact may even make a deeper scratch more visible. Mine has about a 5" very narrow vertical key job which did go through the clear coat at one point, but even where this sharp type scratch was the lightest this product hid very little if any of it. I followed the advice of posters here by rubbing across the scratch and reloading the micro cloth whenever the compound started to dry out. I continued this routine for approximately 20 minutes then finally quit when I didn't see any improvement.

If your "scratch" is more of a swipe/smudge type abrasion that only took the shine off your clear coat, this product did very well although I believe a quality rubbing compound would provide as good as or even better results.

Therefore I am disappointed in the value/effectiveness of this product for either of the purposes for which I purchased it.

(I live in Hawaii, land of never-ending hot and sunny days, so a good windshield shade is a must.)
I still strongly prefer fanfold (accordion) shades for their ease of handling, but this shade is pretty much unbeatable for coverage and, as semi-rigid frame shades go, much easier than most to fold. (You first fold in in half, then grasp the resulting rough disk on opposite sides and give a 3/4 twist to get three overlapping rough circles, which may need a bit of patting on the sides to equalize before stuffing the whole thing in the provided fitted sack.)
I thiink these shades will last a long time -- they're well made and (unlike accordion shades) have no built-in fatigue points (the folds in a fanfold shade, the roll ends in rollup shades). I have my doubts about the rather flimsy fitted sack, but it may yet surprise may and anyway it's not important enough to take off a star. Add very low price, fast service and shipping, and what more can you ask? 5 stars.

title: Heavy, Hot and Loud but it Beats Pumping
text:
This is a good product if it lasts. Anecdotally, it retains it's battery charge very well. I am using it again for the first time in approximately two months and the meter shows about 90% battery life remaining.

* Wear ear plugs. It must easily exceed 100db.
* Careful. The base where the hose plugs in and the hose itself get very hot.
* While holding, any shifting of the pump may cause the hose to loosen. Note that if it inflates very slowly the hose probably loosened.

Can't complain but my wishes are these:
1. I wish it had a screw-on valve connection rather than the lever lock-down type.
2. I wish you could just hold the up and down arrows to adjust the desired pressure. As it is you must constantly click, click, click in 1/2-PSI increments to get to the desired pressure.
3. Wish it had a threaded lock-down nut where the hose connects to the pump so that the hose could not loosen.

I own four or five bike pumps and this is the only one I own that doesn't suck. It's well worth carrying the extra weight to ensure that, if you DO get a flat, THIS pump will finish the job.

I hope it lasts.

title: Above All Else this Device Actually Works
text:
I have 3 pickup trucks, 2 fishing boats plus trolling motors, 2 motorcycles & a golf cart = a lot of batteries.
Reason for batteries to fail to hold a charge is the buildup on the plates of acid plaque similar to the plaque on your teeth a Dentist cleans. A battery can not recharge thru the buildup of this plaque. This is why a battery will weaken then be unable to recharge sufficiently.
This Device using the charge already contained in your batteries actually works & works well causing this plaque buildup to return to a liquid state. Note, charge must be above 12 volts.
Where previously a battery would be holding a 12.8 volt charge, after 2 days sitting on this device & then recharging, the charge would read 13.4 or even 13.8 volts.
This means the device works. On lead acid type batteries, make sure the water level is above the top of the plates both before & after using.
1 particular bad thing is the alligator clips are weak. I broke 1 & replaced it with a stronger clip I bought at a hardware store. Otherwise this is a perfect tool for increasing battery life.
Some electric battery chargers claim to have a battery restore cycle, they are weak to ineffective. I know, 2 of my chargers have these cycles. This device is FAR MORE EFFECTIVE.
BTW, I'm not a bot or a B/S reviewer. I bought this product & love it.

title: Works well, some issues on 2001 Yamaha Warrior
text:
Like - Cheap, works well. Got installed and ran a solid 4 hours on rocky and muddy trails, no issues.

2001 Yamaha Warrior 350

Dislike -
1. This came with a terribly cheap and thin brake line hose to goes to the reservoir.
2. The metal protection spring that runs around the hose is also too wide, and it will not fit through the factory pathway the hose runs through.
3. The actual hose itself is about 3 inches too short. I had to run to the store to buy proper length hose.
4. The connection fitting that goes into the reservoir line is poorly made/fitted. It is a plastic piece with a rubber seal. It is held into place by one small screw. If you put any sideways pressure on the hose fitting, it comes away from the body of the master cylinder, which unseats the o-ring and let's fluid out and air in. This may not be an issue under normal circumstances, but when I was trying to make a too-short hose fit, I found this flaw.
5. Finally, the adjuster rod for the brake pedal position is too long. This makes it so the brake pedal has to be pressed further down than usual. Still works, just annoying.

I gave it 3 stars because while it is not perfect, it works. The hose length was the biggest issue to be honest, because it requires you to get a new hose, spending more money. Maybe older year Warriors had a shorter hose?

title: Install The Hitch Without A Hitch! Tips For Installing
text: Firstly, the vendor and shipping speed, as well as the packaging are amazing, received the hitch the very next day, packaged in a heavy cardboard box, with the hitch wrapped and padded inside the box. Secondly, the hitch is very well made, excellent welds, paint quality, as well as thick metal. Some tools I highly recommend to purchase are the muffler removal tool, as well as a 10mm X 1.25 tap, and a little wire brush for cleaning out the holes. I lubed the rubber muffler mounts with Wd-40, and used the muffler removal tool to drop the muffler, easy. Next I could see that the threaded holes on the muffler side were corroded from the elements and road salt over the years. The bolts would not even start in the threads. I ran the tap through the holes, along with wire brushing and Wd-40, which made the threads like new again. Next I used the instruction sheet to measure and mark the rectangle needed to be cut in the underbody plastic. I used other reviewers tips to only cut the front, back, and muffler sides, with a box cutter, and leaving the side away from the muffler intact, creating a door that could be opened. I used a bungee cord to hold the door open. The two threaded holes that were under the underbody plastic were in great shape, so I sprayed WD- 40 in all four threaded holes to provide some rust protection and lubricant for the bolts to easily thread in. Following reviewers tips again, I put the muffler side of the hitch on the muffler, then put the left side through the cutout in the plastic, and threaded the middle U bolt by hand, to hold the hitch in place, as I was doing this alone. I threaded the left and right side bolts in by hand, then tightened all the bolts with a socket wrench. I finished the tightening with my torque wrench to the recommended pounds. I drilled holes in the door I had made in the underbody plastic, and used zip ties to stitch it securely shut. Securing the muffler again was simple, easily pushing the mounting tabs in by hand, no tool needed. All in all, I would say that prepping the threaded holes on the 2016 CRV was the mos time consuming task, everything else was easy, and I did this alone.  The hitch looks great, and I am hoping to get many years out of it. I highly recommend the vendor, as well as the Curt Hitch, just buy it!

title: I purchased these for my 2010 Nissan Cube. According ...
text: I purchased these for my 2010 Nissan Cube.  According to Amazon, this should have fit my vehicle.  This wasn't the first time doing breaks, I've done them for years.  The hardware/shims included with this kit do not fit my vehicle.  I always replace the hardware when doing breaks if it is included, but prying out my old hardware ruined them, so I had to stick with these.  The hardware was rubbing against something and making a grinding noise.  I took it to an ASE Certified Master Mechanic and he diagnosed the problem as incorrect hardware for the breaks.  He said the kit should have come with a second set of hardware as this size of break pad fits two different sets. title: Fixed slow window motor experience
text:

It was not slow but not super fast. I would normally just leave the window up and not care, it is freezing cold right now and would investigate later. BUT i was getting my windows tinted and needed it to go up and down for the installation process. The tint shop told me they have seen this before where the switch is just old and not making great contact. We swapped out a unit from other door and window worked great.
I explained that I had replaced the window regulator and the one I had just frozen and I could feel heat from the motor. I had used the switch from other door to slowly get motor to go down and actually did see how when I put it back to other door it also started to work slow. He recommended I go to salvage yard and get a replacement.
Well.. quick Amazon search and I found the exact part AND in a THREE piece set! I put one in the door that was faulty and the window went up and down faster than with the original switch and the switch from other door.
This went on my rear passenger door. i will be replacing the front and driver passenger door next week when I return from work trip. My front passenger door is very slow going up and down but it works. that will be the confirmation test for me.
I am EXTREMELY happy to find these parts and not have to go to dealer. Which are VERY pricey !

For the price you should definitely consider upgrading for a better experience

title: Update - 2/6/23 see below:  Easily fixed my dropped window problem...
text:

My vehicle is 21 years old. I have had to replace all but one window regulator. This one was the second time i've had to replace for this exact window.
Motor goes down quick, rolling window fully open. It goes up slow, closing window completely. it is what it is.
You definitely can't beat the price. I know these replacement parts are more expensive at big box parts dealers and will also fail in a few years. Just buying time with these.

Very easy to install, once you see a good quality video. The one window regulator that was still original to the vehicle died two days before I replaced this one I just purchased. I was able to compare the parts to each other.

Wouldn't you know it... the exact same piece was broken on both of them! I had kept all the other window regulators from vehicle, and other similar vehicle, and was able to use some pieces to fix ONE regulator. Not the case this time.

The part that breaks is a simple roller guide where one end of the cable pulley connects. They are all made of plastic and take a bulk of the operation stress.

The OEM plastic was a bit thicker than the new replacement one.

So for less that $50 for the part and your own labor, this is a great fix. if you have to pay someone... wow, just doesn't feel right.

I have personally replaced 10 of these on my own vehicles. Sounds like a lot, but the cars were worth the simple repair. 21 & 15 year old vehicles and this has been the most major repair on them. Not bad.

Thanks Amazon for finding the Old Stock at great prices! Usually at half to 75% off OEM prices.

title: Does what it says it does!
text:
First time using this type of tool. I did some YouTube research, watched a MotorTrend tv show that used a similar product. Looked like I could do the same.
First time using it was a bit difficult. I wiped down the area but not with alcohol as recommended. Made it harder to take off the glue stick residue. It did come off with wiping with my fingers, creating some friction.

Then I found some alcohol and it worked amazingly. It still stuck a bit. My next try i'm going to go ahead and wash and wax detail the area. The glue will do it's job and come off easier on cleaning. I'm sure of it. Areas of one dent was buffed out weeks ago to expose ripple dents. It was hard seeing where to place glue pod tools.
I'm happy with the results. In a few places I will need to use the "Dentless Wire Tools" that look like bent rods to fully smooth out what these could not get out. The wire tools were not able to get out some of my dents because they had a real hard ding/dent that needed to be popped out first.
My largest dent actually made a popping noise when the metal returned to its original shape. I didn't get a picture of it because I seriously thought this tool was not the right tool. It was!

The tool has foot pegs that slide in/out from dent hole. You can place one closer and one further away from dent to create the correct angle to pull dent towards it memory. Steel has memory and you are just pulling enough to get it back to its original shape.

I'm going to need more practice but I can see my self actually charging to fix friends door dings. I'll be perfecting my new skills using three of my own vehicles. I'm actually thinking of selling one of them after doing this. It dents easy in the parking lot but when it is polished looks fantastic. It is a deep blue Toyota. Could ask a bit more than I was hoping to ask.

I'll be ordering more of those puck things you stick to body. I was able to use four of them together to pull out my large dent.

Go easy when using the pulling tool. you don't have to yank the pod off. You want to gently pull on it so the metal starts to remember its shape. If you pull too hard you can pull the dent out and have a little peak left. I did that on first dent but used a plastic pin tool to "hammer/push" it back in gently. Looks almost perfect. It is in a location where it is hard to see.

Totally happy with this product! I can barter on price of next vehicle if it has many door dings!

text:

If you get this, Google how to install for your vehicle. The YouTube videos make the job easier. We had the original keys, still new and unused, to make sure we could use the exact same keys to lock and unlocke each door.

Could not figure out why my headlights would not turn on. I replaced fuses, directly wired the headlights and they turned on.

Turns out the turn signal switch had a dead spot on the PC board inside. yeah, I took it apart to test it.

Uhm... the part was like $100 so I only drove during the day. Turn switch worked but not headlights.

I searched and searched for a discounted price.
The Scion is Toyota. It has a Corolla engine... so I thought... does it have Toyota signa switch?

Yes, but plug design was a bit different. Took a chance since it was returnable and when i got it I could see that the plug difference was me cutting a piece of my cars plug to make it slide into the slot of the switch.
The locking piece was differen but once I cut that off, it stayed in because the steering covers kept it in place.

did I tell you I found it for 1/4 the price? Yeah baby!

title: Better than Dealer or Auto Parts house for the Price
text:
I purchased this for my 2006 Scion XB. Mine just died one day. Totally sucked. The price to replace mine with an approved factory part was expensive.
I went to the SCION Blogs and found others who said you could purchase this one and it will fit your cars tank. It may need to be "modified" a little bit depending on who you purchase from .

I believe I paid less than $20 as it was the last one someone was selling. I did have to modify it. I had to swich the plug it came with with the one that was on my broken one.

I had to cut the wires and solder them from one unit to the other. I had shrink tubing so once I soldered them the connection was safe.

Yeah.. the whole thing is inserted into gasoline. and the way the wires are on the device, there isn't a real hazzard, even with cutting and soldering. Had the plug been the same style to just use new plug, That plug is still inserted into gasoline.
As explained to me, the design is always wet and the wires in the gas are for the fuel sending unit to let you know how much gas you have.

Now... this pump is a little noisy at first, but once the engine is running you can't hear it. Actually I think I'm getting better fuel delivery and I do feel more horsepower. But that may be because the old pump was failing.

If you don't know if this fits, check Blogs for your vehicle make. Those folks are great at sharing how to keep your vehicle alive.

title: Finally Fixed! Blower motor resistor not burning out anymore. Fan replacement fixed that
text:

13 months after getting this, I am experiencing the same problems. Fan drawing too much current and overheating the Resister and Plug. It is freezing right now... no fan means no heat.

Kept losing the speed control or it just wouldn't turn on. I kept replacing the resister. Friend say, replace the motor, probably so dirty it is struggling and pulling too many amps.

Buy this and replace everything if your wires show any burn/scorch marks. Replace ONE wire at a time so the dial speeds up the fan motor correctly.

title: Good light output, but had issues setting up
text:
If you are considering putting LED head lights in your vehicle, DO YOUR RESEARCH! After trying a Sealight brand that did not work out I decided on Beam tech because I saw on YouTube a channel reviewing LED head lights listed on Amazon. Beam tech was in the top 5 I wanted it to be fan less as fans seemed to cause issues.
I was installing these in a 2006 Hummer H3 which requires an H13 type lamp.
The lamp needs to install perfectly vertical in my case. No matter what hole I used to adjust it would not allow that SO had to drill holes between the adjustment holes to get set right! I tried it out when it was dark and when I turned the high beams on I lost most the light. It was aiming way high! I wrote Beam tech and they sent me a photo of how the lamp should be set in. I had it reversed and need to clock them again 180' and drilling more holes. After that it worked however it was reversed from the switching stand point with the intrument panels
When I selected High Beam the Beam tech lights were in low beam and when selected low beam the Beam tech lights would produce high beam output! SO only thing I could do at that point was to cut the Harness on the Beam tech lights and reverse and solder the connections. Finally it worked the way it is suppose to! So just don't think you are going put these in with out knowing how they should be set up. You will blind other drivers!! Learn to adjust your lights if need be
The output of the Beam Tech is good and greatly improved visabiltiy. Just a real pain trying to get this set up and it should not be!! We will see how long they last.

UPDATE: June 2020 and one now is flickering on and off! I infact do not know how long it has been doing it as I do not drive much at night. Just noticed it.

title: they fit and work
text: Some directions would have been helpful.  I installed these on a 2003 4Runner. You can use a step ladder with other items to support the hatch. One side at a time remove and install. Removal: remove the upper bracket bolts on one side.  I was worried the lower ball pin bolt would round off because only an open ended wrench will go onto it unless the ball pin is cut off. The strut end seems pressed on the factory strut; there is no c-clip release from the ball pin. I got inside the rear corner access of the vehicle and put penetrating oil on the backside of the bolt; hard to get to- saturate a paper towel and drip it onto the bolt.  Too much may smell up the vehicle.  The back nut is welded in. After waiting a while that allowed me to get one of the bolts to move. The other one I cut the pin off so I could put a box end wrench on to get off.  Install: I put anti-seize on the new pin bolts and placed them in.  Then popped the retention pin out of the lower ball socket of the strut.  Inside the ball socket of the strut is a spring clip that will bind if it isn't set into its recess before putting them on. I put a little extra grease in the socket and set the spring clip into its recess.  It should slide onto the pin ball without protest.  If it binds take it off and reset the spring clip inside. I then placed the retention pin in and rotated it back onto the strut shaft. Then I put anti-seize on the two upper bracket bolts and bolted the top bracket into place. I don't recommend trying to bolt the upper bracket on first because the ball socket clips may bind up under that pressure. That's what happened to me so I unbolted the top bracket and set the ball socket on first.

title: Does not work as well as regular glass cleaner
text:
This is a cream / polish compound that you spread on your car window. It dries quickly and starts to crumble as you wipe it off. This is harder to apply and takes longer to apply than regular glass cleaners, and it does not work as well as regular glass cleaners. Cleaning the windows of one car uses up a lot of this small $11 bottle of cream. You can buy glass cleaner at a dollar store that lasts for many more cleanings. Regular ammonia or vinegar glass cleaners work well for most people, or Sprayway, which my house cleaner likes to use. A YouTuber did a review of car window cleaners and found that Windex and Invisible Glass were the top performers, and were better than the specialty car glass cleaners.

The company offered me $20 to delete my review, so I lowered my rating to one star.

title: Not impressed
text:
Regular glass cleaners containing ammonia, vinegar, or alcohol work fine, such as Windex. This glass cleaner worked well, but you have to rub all the product off with a dry cloth or it will leave a haze behind. Regular glass cleaner costs a couple of dollars. If this product does have an anti-fog property, that would be worth paying extra for, but that feature is hard to test. The prior anti-fog product I applied was cheap shaving cream from a dollar store, which works.

The foamy wheel and tire cleaner was disappointing. I thought it would do more than it did. My wheels had not been cleaned in a couple of years and had built up dirt. I first cleaned them with car soap and a tire brush. I then cleaned them with this Air Jungles product twice. The tires are cleaner, but most of the cleaning was done by manual brushing. All the areas I could not reach with the brush as still dirty.

I tried the wheel cleaner again on wheels that were cleaner and this product does very little on its own. The cleaning comes mostly from the hard work of scrubbing.

The current price is $18. This product would need to have noticeably superior cleaning ability to regular household cleaners to justify the price premium, but they do not in my testing.

title: Silicone Oil
text:
This product works to improve the appearance of your car. The main ingredient is silicone oil, aka dimethicone. It is a viscous liquid that is quickly absorbed. The areas that get coated have a darker color and a shine to them. The bottle says it works on rubber and plastic. Vinyl is a type of plastic, and vinyl is mentioned in the marketing text. In the car I treated, some of the textured vinyl on the door and steering wheel was starting to look faded. This product livened up those areas. You go through a lot of this product for one vehicle, especially if you are covering large areas, like the bumper, or are applying a second coat.

The ingredients are not listed on the bottle, but looking at the safety data sheet the ingredients are:
60-70% Inorganic Polydimethylsiloxane
1-30% Alcoholate
1-5% Fluoride
1-5% Butyl alcohol

You are supposed to wash your hands after using this product. I think the cheaper Armor All protectant product is mineral oil.

title: Household cleaners work better
text:

Regular household cleaners work better at removing dirt, such as dish soap, baby shampoo, alcohol, ammonia, and vinegar.

The chemicals in this are not listed and it does not have much of a smell. From the safety data sheet, this product is 15-20% sodium hydroxide (aka lye) in water, with some added ethylenedlamlnetetraacetic acid as a chelating agent that helps the soap work better. The MDS warns against getting this on your skin, in your eyes, and against breathing it. Other interior cleaners are safer to use.

title: Unintuitive controls
text:
This is the first electric tire inflator I have reviewed that measures the correct car tire starting pressure and it automatically stops inflating at the correct ending pressure. The three prior devices I reviewed all failed this basic functionality test.

While the basic functionality is good I cannot recommend this to anyone because it is so unintuitive to use. The buttons are strange and impossible to figure out without the manual. The power button you need to hold in for three seconds, then to start inflating you have to press the power button two more times. The button that controls the unit of measure also controls the lights depending on the length of hold and number of presses. I accidentally turned on a strobe emergency light and did not know how to turn it off without powering off the unit. I cannot let someone borrow this because they will not be able to figure out how it works without reading the manual. Three of the buttons are variants of circles. Orange symbols on an orange background can be hard to read. It is not that hard to make an inflator that is intuitive and the selection of inflators on Amazon is plentiful.

The inflator air hose should be longer. If the valve is at the top of the tire this will dangle because it cannot reach the ground, even for small tires. The display is hard to read in bright sunlight. It takes a while to charge. It is quite loud when inflating, louder than the other ones I have tested and it vibrates a lot.

This is a generic inflator being sold under multiple brands. The current price is $54, but this same product is being sold under a different listing for $45.

title: Cheap generic jack that does not look like a 2-ton jack
text:
This does not look like a 2-ton jack. It looks flimsy and when I used it, I was worried that it would collapse. If a jack collapses, there is a chance that it can do serious damage to your car, so you should look for an established brand. It did lift my Subaru Outback, which weighs around 1.8 tons. The two-ton rating is just a sticker on the jack that says 2T, which does not inspire confidence.

The ratcheting mechanism is somewhat unintuitive since the ratchet only functions when the jack is touching the car. You have to twist the jack up with your fingers until it touches the car’s contact point, then you can use the ratchet. This is not the typical mechanism and it took some troubleshooting to figure out why the ratchet was not working. I am more used to the raising mechanism found on the BIG RED top-selling scissor lift jack, which is a better lift mechanism. The ratchet mechanism on this jack makes it slower to lift the car.

This is a generic unbranded Chinese-made jack that is being sold by multiple companies under multiple different listings. The current price is $33.25. The same product is being sold by both CPROSP and Jchotry for $30. Reviews of this jack under the other listing suggest that it breaks easily, and I believe them based on how cheap this looks.

Scissor jacks are light-duty, only designed for emergency tire changes. I overused the one that came with the Subaru doing car maintenance for 10 years and it finally collapsed.

title: Does not work properly
text: While inflating, the device cannot measure the air pressure accurately so it does not know when to stop. When trying to inflate a car tire from 29 to 30 PSI, the device started filling the tire, but the measurement remained at 29. When I removed the inflator and measured the PSI with another device, the tire had gotten up to 32 PSI and it would have inflated to a much higher PSI without me stopping it manually. The main issue is that the marketing is wrong by promoting this as a car polisher This tool is not safe for polishing. Dedicated polishers have a bigger surface area and run at lower speeds.

title: Better than the WJL-6000 detector
text:
This is solidly better than the WJL-6000. The WJL-6000 was worthless as it beeped at random locations. This WJL-6000Pro does not suffer from that problem. This upgraded product shows a number indicating the level of detection, rather than having to rely on rapid beeping alone. This suffers from the same problem as the WJL-6000 in that it beeps constantly when in operation with no way to turn this off. I don’t need it to beep as a confirmation that it is turned on because this has an LCD display. Moisture sets this off, which means breathing on it causes the number to shoot up to 9. This product is susceptible to false positives, although most cheap detectors will have that problem.

This is not a product professionals would use. It is a cheap Chinese generic product. For an average homeowner or car owner looking for a leak, the current price of $28 is less than the cost of a diagnostic check from a professional. The user manual is a poor Chinese translation filled with errors. It requires four AAA batteries, which are not included.

I also have tested the Aprvtio LD-200, which is a higher-end detector that costs $100 more than this product. Using UV dye is a better way to detect a leak, but that is hard to inject if you are not a professional.

title: The jack feature works, but the other features do not.
text:
The jack function works well and easily handled my Subaru Outback. The cigarette lighter power cord is not long enough to reach all four jack locations without unplugging it and running it through a different door, which is a slight inconvenience that most of these powered jacks likely have. If this was just a jack it would be fine. Unfortunately, the other features are a letdown.

The light feature is mostly pointless because it illuminates straight forward and the angle cannot be adjusted to point at the area you are working on. You cannot illuminate the vehicle’s under carriage with the light.

The air pump feature did not work in my testing. The pressure reading was off by 4 PSI. Even after adjusting for that discrepancy, such that I would target 38 PSI if I wanted 34 PSI, I could not get this to inflate the tire. It would only deflate it. I could not figure out why. The controls are unintuitive. The default pressure unit is not PSI and you have to press the R button to toggle the unit choice. Why is the button labeled R? The air inflation tube is not very long, so if you have big tires, such as on a truck, you might have to hold this heavy unit up to get it to reach. The manual is a poor Chinese to English translation and is mostly useless due to the bad translation.

The current cost is $100.

title: Higher quality than the WJL-6000
text: I tested this against a less inexpensive WJL-6000 detector looking for a household HVAC 410a refrigerant leak. This LD-200 tool is noticeably higher quality. The main negative is that it takes a while to warm up before it starts to detect anything. The volume beeping on this can be turned off, which is great. The WJL-6000 has a persistent loud beep that cannot be disabled. The WJL-6000 was beeping at nearly everything and the beeping was not consistently reproducible. The WJL-6000 beeped around a new HVAC install that was unlikely to have any leaks. This LD-200 device detected nothing during my leak search at the highest sensitivity, so it was not helpful in finding the leak. It does beep when I blast a can of air near it, so I know it functions and it could be that the leak I was searching for was no longer an issue. The case this comes in is not great in that you have to twist the probe to a specific curl in order to get it to fit.

title: Works better than entry-level scanners
text:
The OBD scanner was better than the one I tried from Thinkcar. I was able to graph the coolant temperature in my 2010 Subaru Outback to help with my coolant flushing. This also flagged my ABS sensors as being old. The on-screen items are mostly spelled out in English, rather than being obscure unexplained initialisms that low-end products show.

The manual should be much better. The Help button on the device shows the software version number and nothing else. I noticed it freeze up on me once during testing. The navigation could be better and it took me a while to find out how to do things. It also repeatedly prompted me to select my car’s manufacturer from a long list.

The current price is $117, which seems expensive, although it did work better than other ones I tried. It comes with a carrying case.

For many of the features, it said my car was not supported, including the ABS and Airbag features, which are a reason this device is being sold at a premium. The marketing should better describe which cars are supported. It says my Subaru should be supported, but it is only partially supported. The manual and their Web site do not provide this information either. The Amazon page says to contact the company to figure out what features are supported for each car.

title: Popular cars are not supported
text: I was unable to get any useful information from this connected to a Subaru Outback 2010 and a Honda CR-V 2019. It is just a bunch of screens saying feature not supported. The only feature that worked was the one where it listed my cars VIN. The only data stream supported was duration the device was turned on. Another ODB2 scanner gave me data. These models of cars are popular, so having them not be supported is surprising. The manual is worthless. It does not describe how to use this properly and it does not describe what the abbreviations mean. There is built-in help, but it is so slow to use as to be pointless. It really needs an interpretation of all the acronyms.

title: Too many false positives to be of use for home AC systems
text:
This is too inaccurate to be of much use. Anything that touches the tip seems to set it off. This is detecting something, but it is not clear what. I have a home heat pump system that I know has an R410a leak and this thing started the rapid beeping at so many locations that it was unhelpful. The tests were not repeatable, such that some places that caused beeping no longer beeped when I tried again. I tested a non-leaking home 410a AC and this thing started beeping everywhere. I tried again later and it did not detect anything. Breathing on this causes it to start beeping.

I compared this to two other higher-quality detectors, including the successor product, the WJL-6000Pro. This product beeps everywhere just walking around my house. The other products do not. I am not sure what is setting this off, but it is too inaccurate to be of any use.

The constant loud beeping, even when not detecting anything, is annoying. It lets you know it is working, but a blinking light would work as well.

The supplied glasses and black light are useless without UV dye, which this does not come with. If you really want to detect a leak, you need to use UV dye, not this tool. This tool is a waste of time.

The current price is $41. I see the exact same product being sold on Amazon for $24. The part number is WJL-6000.

title: Better than Torin Big Red
text:
These are superior to the Torin Big Red 3-ton jack stands in that they have an extra locking bar for safety, more surface area on the base, and they come with rubber pads. These wobble a bit as the base legs are not level. The Big Red jack stands have the same problem to a lesser extent. The legs disperse the weight, so having one leg not touching the ground makes this more prone to failure. There are weld joints on the footpads, making them bumpy instead of smooth. The weld joints should have been smoothed off since the footpads are supposed to be flat.

3 tons is enough for a Subaru Outback station wagon or a small SUV.

The current price is $53. The rubber pads can cost $10 if purchased separately, so factor those in when evaluating the price.

title: Works well
text:
This is a good product to have in your car. Batteries over three years old have a higher risk of needing to be jump-started. It has a USB charger and a flashlight/strobe light feature. Everything I tested works fine. I did not evaluate how long the charge holds when left in a hot car during the summer, or a cold car in the winter.

The charger I got has 7,200 mAh of capacity.

The current price is $60. You can get chargers with more capacity and a bigger flashlight, for around the same price.

This lacks UL certification. It is made in China.

title: Has everything you need to work on your vehicle's trim
text:
This is a comprehensive set of tools and clips for working on car trim safely. One use case is running electrical wire behind the trim for a camera or radar detector, or upgrading your stereo setup. The replacement clips are an insurance policy in case you break these when removing the trim.

It comes in a zippered case, so when you want to work on your trim you can have all your tools in one bundle. It comes with a one-page sheet describing what all the tools do. It would be better if the binder had a plastic sleeve to store this page. You can tape it to the binder.

The quality of the tools looks good. The current price of $24 is in line with similar sets of tools. For most people, a smaller set of tools is all you need. The cost between a basic set of trim pry bars and this set is around $15, which most people can afford.

title: Lasted 3.5 years

title: Avoid this product. It is not a repair kit.
text:
I regret trying this awful product. The description says it is a repair kit, so I tried it on some cracks in a kitchen table chair. This did nothing to fix the cracks. The product box says it is a leather balm, so I thought I would use this to condition my chairs without the cracks. This was a big mistake.

This product appears to be a sticky black paint. Just like you would not use paint to repair a drywall crack, you would not use this paint to do any sort of leather repair. I can see the swirl marks from applying this product, and I cannot get rid of them. My chairs are noticeably worse after trying this repair kit.

The layer this puts on is sticky. The instructions say to let it soak in for a couple days, but this is not something that soaks in. It is a separate layer that after four days is still sticky. I have tried various products to remove this substance from the chairs or neutralize the stickiness and have not yet found anything that works.

Overall using this was a big mistake and it damaged my chairs instead of repairing them. This is not a repair kit and it is not a balm.

title: Stadium Lighting for Reading
text:
I'm addicted to alternative lighting so I was filled with joy when our power went out last weekend. I had maybe 30 different options for reading in the dark and this light proved far better than my 70 watt electrical light I normally read by. I sat and read for three hours until the power came back on without getting fatigued.

Yesterday I set this same light up under my desk when I was setting up a complicated computer system. It lit the entire area. Well worth the money.

Addendum: For the second time, I have replaced perfectly good lights with ones that were more attractive but seriously less functional. In this case, I replace the industrial flexible arm, wall mounted reading lamps with beautiful ones from Restoration Hardware only to discover that they only used 40 watt refrigerator bulbs.

No cause for alarm. I'll just order two more of these lights and put them on the end tables.

Addendum: My love for this light just keeps growing. The 23" fluorescent light went out on my aquarium and because that's non-standard, I had to order replacements. In the meantime my fish were learning to see in the dark. So I got the grand idea to hang one of these lights from a side shelf. Now the fish have light again and I have to order more of these.

title: Better than expected.
text:
I was really leaning towards getting a name brand light like the JW Speaker but Amazon discontinued the one I was looking at. I have heard bad reviews about the cheap overseas knock-offs but thought I'd give it a try (Amazon's selections of the higher end stuff seems lacking these days). I've tried LED bulbs in my reflector a few years ago and that was a disaster. I figured if I tried again, I would get the full assembly. These were surprisingly great. I'm sure they are probably not as bright as the expensive lights, but these were noticeably brighter than the halogens they replaced. The light has a distinct cut-off at the top so you don't blind oncoming cars. I believe the DOT rating is legit. It was not plug & play for a Hummer H2 as described - you will have to cut some of the rear shroud for this to fit correctly. You also have to get the plug adaptor (cheap & simple). I was worried that this may be too "blue" as it was described as 6500K, but its pretty white unless you are looking directly at it (it wouldn't be correctly aimed if this were the case). When looking directly into it, it has a very slight blue tint. The light pattern is pretty defined (not scattered). Great value!

UPDATE: It has been over a year and it has done so well I felt a need to post an update. This product DEFINITELY delivers! It has held up on long trips, harsh winters (there are no issues with snow), and even a minor fender bender. There is no flickering (I've experienced this on others, long term) and the light is still as bright as I can remember. I was seriously considering the JW Speaker version (but they discontinued their earlier version) and was skeptical with these being so cheap. I guess in actuality, the JW Speakers are just overpriced. These do very well & even if I have to replace the entire light in another year, the price would have been well worth it.

title: Not the best
text:
These are not very accurate, and they have a hard time shutting off when they’ve reached the pressure you set for them. They drain really fast as first, but then they drain air really slow as they get close to the set point, and then they just continually drain and seemingly never stop.

I wasted a lot of time to get these set up. I finally had them set so I could put them on a tire at the correct pressure and no air would come out. So I figured they were good to go.

When I tested them on full tires, I waited over 10 minutes for them to stop draining air (only going from like 38psi to the set point 30psi). I finally pulled them off and saw they drained the tires to 28psi and were still draining.

The biggest problem is they just start going so slow when they get close to the set point, and they will go past it because they don’t shut off automatically. This past time when I used them it didn’t bother me very much about what exact pressure my tires were at. These were set to 30 and they got me to 33 before I pulled them off because I don’t have all day and I don’t trust them to stop at 30.

title: Good value that fixed our non-charging issue

Remembered that the unit must be well grounded and found that someone (previous owner) had both grounding leads connected to the engine but neither to the regulator. I moved one of the grounding leads to the regulator and voila, charging 14+volts. Perfect! Left the new regulator installed but did not go back to confirm the original was bad. Just counted my good fortune and started cutting grass! No problems since. Fast delivery, good price and good part.

title: Easy to use and keeps water out of the bed.
text:
I like the shape, design and application. Perfect fit for the 5.5' bed on my 2011 f150 super crew. I needed something to cover my bed and secure the contents. I am satisfied with this choice.
The installation was a breeze. I used an impact and torque wrench to make sure it was exactly as the instructions directed. Once the side rails were installed, the cover fit in and clipped down perfectly. My 7 year old helped me and it took us less than an hour to install this cover.
I later washed the truck with a pressure washer and was very satisfied with the lack of water inside the bed. I did not directly spray water at any rubber seals, but did use quite a bit of water indirectly over the bed and around all the sides. The design runs water off over the bed rails and does not have the need for any drain, as the water never makes it into the truck bed at all. Important also is removal - and the cover takes about 30 seconds to fold back and remove - plus it is only 50 lbs, so anyone can remove it.
Looks good, works great, installation was a breeze. I like it, and would recommend it to anyone with an F150.
