We have something similar in our other car and it worked so well, I thought I’d try the ANLEM Car Purse Holder Durable Leather Seat Back Organizer Car Handbag Holder and we come away very happy with the choice. It looks nice - the pattern and material offer a little more “upscale” look and feel to the holder. My wife has a range of bags, so some fit better than others. However, we have found that we are more often using it for misc. items rather than her purse. She likes having access - and I drive when we are together - so she doesn’t mind keeping her purse by her and actually prefers using the ANLEM Car Purse Holder Durable Leather Seat Back Organizer Car Handbag Holder for items she doesn’t want in her purse or that we use often. We have things like Kleenex, masks, mask filters, and other items we’ll take with - depending on the trip. This keeps those items close at hand and easier to reach. This helps me as well when I drive alone - I can grab what I need and not keep them on the passenger seat. Overall we find the ANLEM Car Purse Holder Durable Leather Seat Back Organizer Car Handbag Holder to be a helpful device. It was easier to get on than we thought - easy buckles that are well sewn in. And while there are the two steps for attaching to the bottom of the seat, we could not figure out how to get them to stay on our car, so don’t bother - it still works for us just fine. We are happy with the ANLEM Car Purse Holder Durable Leather Seat Back Organizer Car Handbag Holder.

title: Works well, but...
text:
Out of the gate the AutoChoice Premium Car Seat Organizer with Leather Cover is a good, solid cup holder.

We have one that holds a single cup/can/glass, along with a long section for other items. It works great, but with a phone holder in our regular cup holders, this only added the second one. We still have times we need a third. So I thought this might work as a backup/partner to the other one (both are for passenger side only - we do not feel it’s safe on the drivers side).

I am right. This adds the second and third holders and works very well. Yes, there is a but...

1. It looks nice - in fact it matches our other ones (one for each car) perfectly. The faux black leather with red stitching looks nice (our opinion) and we like how it goes in both cars - this double holder matching it all perfectly.
2. This one has the same set up: a long section that slides between the seat and the center consul. It works well. And in this case there is a single padding that fits in there - protecting the seat as well as maintaining the hold. The other one we have as pieces that are not secure. We love that this one has a single piece and that it stay put. This means there is a quality here we really appreciate.
3. That said - this one is thick all the way around. it really stays securely in there.
4. That said - the thickness also means that the whole thing is thicker and does take up more room on the passengers side. My wife finds it okay for shorter trips or when it’s really needed, but she’d rather it only be used when we need it. It does take enough space that it feels like an intrusion. She tries to keep it as far forward as possible. But because of the second cup holder - rather than the thinner space needed in the other one we have for misc items like a phone or credit cards - this one is thick in order to allow for the cups. This means it takes up that much more room. If she’s not with me and I’m grabbing that coffee or something I can have it and not worry - extra cup space has been missed without it. But with a person there, we both feel like it’s not going to make the ride comfortable for the passenger.

We are keeping it in our backseat and it does get switched out when needed. And because of how it’s designed we can do that - easily slip it in or out - and we have no issue with having two of these for different purposes. This is a great holder and the extra cup space works great. But again, using it while having a person there is likely something to consider - it will take up a lot of their personal space. We highly recommend our two option set up - it works great! This AutoChoice Premium Car Seat Organizer with Leather Cover is great and we are happy to have it.

title: Fun, nice car coasters
text:
We like to keep a set of these in the car for our drinks - it can get messy without one. So I grabbed these silicone ones - we’ve never had silicone, rather always having those normal sandstone or whatever they are. Those are ... ok. They can work, some can do nothing. The last set we had were wiped out - really old after 4 years in our warm weather state. But they did great. I hope these silicone ones can live up to that.

I liked the Star Wars thing - it’s fun and we like the movies. So far they’ve been good. It’s only been a short time, so jury is still out and I will update as needed. But the material feels nice. They look nice - as you can see, it’s cool seeing the layers of characters. They feel nice - sort of a layered in the feel as well. And they are malleable - you can bend it to get it out. We like the look, the feel, now we wait on longevity. Again, so far they are working, but we’re not into the heat of the summer yet, nor have we used them enough to make a final determination. But we THINK they’ll be good.

title: It works, but leaves something on the table
text:
I got this for my wife and I to help get my car a little better organized. Between her purse and items we carry (including back up mask filters these days) stuff can get a little crazy. Things end up on the floor, on the backseat... So I thought this would help.

And for the most part it does. The 8sanlione Car Handbag Holder,Leather Seat Back Organizer is a very good organizer, but not perfect.
Pros:
* Looks nice
* Good size side-to-side
* Can reach when seats are split - large gap
* Holds a decent amount of items
* The hooks won’t stay, but with the straps at the headrests and the one in the center arm rest it stays in place well

Cons:
* A bit harder to get on - the way the straps are you have to loop them which is fine, but to figure out how much you need isn’t the easiest - It took me 3 times to get it just right.
* While it stretches when the seats are apart, when we adjust them it takes a bit to redo the straps
* The hooks will. not stay - I am sure I’m putting them where they are supposed to go, but they detach

It IS a good holder - but it’s 4 star good, not 5 star great. We like it and will use it, but if we start to get frustrated with the adjusting, we might abandon it.

title: Works as we need it to
text: With my wife usually keeping her purse on the floor by her feet when we drive I thought this might help her - keep it off the floor, keep it within reach, allow for holding other things. So far it works well. It arrives folded up - it’s easily collapsable. The materials are decent - for me this is where I mainly give it the 4 stars. I feel like they are decent, but not great - average rather than above average. In general it seems like it’ll last, but... for example, the netting seems good and it’ll handle most things, but the base feels like a hard cardboard and if you’re not careful, could be damaged. It is also somewhat narrow - meaning she can get most of her purses in it - and we have used it to hold things like packs of mask filters - but it’s a bit limited on the size of purse overall. Or limited on other bags - at present she is using a bag designed for baby strollers due to her broken foot and need to use a scooter - and it’s larger and a bit heavier and it does not fit. In other words, there are limits here and with my wife’s range of bags she won’t be able to use it for them all. Set up is pretty easy - unfold and attach the straps and such. Pretty easy to figure out. That said, it took some time to wrap and thread them - nothing difficult, but it’ll take several minutes - and a bit of effort getting them set into the different spots. Make sure you know which way your center console opens - I knew my car (which I did not get this for) has the center up front to back, but forgot her car is drivers side to passenger. This is designed for front to back - we just let that hang and it’s been okay. It still works. Overall it’s been decent and it works. She can get a smaller bag in and we have kept a number of things we have with - but it would be nice if it were a bit bigger, stronger, and held more. I still think it’s a decent holder and we’re glad to have it.

title: Works very well, but does not hold all sunglasses
text:
I have been making things frustrating forgetting to carry my sunglasses with me to and from the car. We have spots in the car to keep sunglasses, but they’re full these days and... so when I saw this case, decided to grab it. In general it’s a great, helpful item to have. But it’s not perfect.

1. It arrives in a nice box, wrapped, and ready to go.
2. It’s easy to put in. There is the clip on the back - just slide it on.
3. It looks nice - a black faux leather kind of look and softer inside.
4. I tried a few different types and begins of sunglasses - some work, some do not. I can easily get the aviator style in, the ones with metal frames, but plastic frames that more wrap were all too big and did not fit. I tried pulling it further open, but was unable to get it to the point where they would go in well.
5. It sits on the outside or underside of the visor - on your side, not the roof side.
6. When the visor is up in front of you I do see it, but it’s not bothersome and within the first 10 or 15 minutes I forgot it was there and wasn’t “seeing it’ any longer.
7. When the visor is out - extended towards the window - it fits - in our Prius - fine, not holding the visor any lower than normal.

Overall this is a nice holder and works fine. I do think one needs to consider 1. the kind of sunglasses and 2. how it’ll fit on the visor - 1. for protecting the glasses and 2. for safety in viewing. Beyond that, it seems well made and like it’ll last. I’m happy with this sunglasses case.

title: On one hand, it works great, but there are a couple issues
text:
This car organizer set on the surface seems great, and in many ways it is, but there are a few issues that keep me from being able to give it 5 stars...

1. Nice box. It’s presentation is great and certainly can up it as giftable.
2. There are 2 in the set. However, based on my experience, there is no way my wife or I would ever use the drivers’ side one. In either of our cars. It takes up too much room and as it slips out, seems way too likely it could cause safety issues.
3. They look great. We both really like the black with red stitching. It doesn’t really match our cars, but looks nice and stands out - it looks a bit classy and nice, and sets itself a part, which is nice. In not blending, it makes it easy to spot. But also looks nice enough that you are impressed.
4. But... there are pieces of material that line up along the base piece you stick between the seat and center. These are not glued in. I was holding it and the first fell out. Over time, several did. Not glued, they can be pulled out - or fall out - and while one might want to glue them in, it seems like it wouldn’t work - it’s odd. Why have them and not secure them? You can keep them off, but then those 4 areas sit open - between, but still. I would think it would make the plastic weaker. Anyways, it’s really goofy. This is my second reason for not being able to give it a 5.
5. It has nice room in the organizer. We already had one from another company, but in trying this, I feel like we get the same space and ability to keep those things you always seem to need or want at your finger tips. Alone I can throw my wallet in, if I pull out a credit card, I keep it there, I’ll lay my phone in... there are plenty of things. With my wife, she too throws things in. Our biggest addition are those wet wipe packs. So there are many ways to use it and we use it every time we’re in the car.

Overall it is a good thing - for the passenger side. It does not bother my wife, we can keep things nearby, and we use it every time. On the other hand, I cannot understand their design and assembly - why not secure these pieces? It’s a pain as you put it in and one alls out - hoping none come out and get lodged down there. And I cannot see how a driver’s side one is safe. So having the 2 set to me is a waste. But we will get plenty of use from the passenger one, so we are happy.

title: Good tool to have, a little improvement would make it perfect
text:
Living in a place with many bridges over bodies of water I wanted our cars to be equipped in case of an emergency. But these days it's not just an accident into water that might cause one to need to break into or out of a car window. I grabbed this bunch because 1. it has both the punch AND seatbelt cutter and 2. it was small and compact.

Pros:
It's small
It works very well and easily in punching out glass (see pics)
It's sturdy and feels like it'll last under many conditions

Cons:
Does not come with instructions (it's mostly easy to figure out)
Have no idea what the thing is in the last two pics
It does attach to the car with a sticky piece on the back of the holder, but what happens in an accident?
Being black in color I'm not sure how easy it would be to spot when in a state of panic.

Overall I think it's a great tool and it's being kept in one of our cars. Trying to figure out where to keep it was/is a challenge. We don't want nor have a space on the dash to attach it - and what happens when we get a new car? On the other hand, putting it into a center arm rest it might move around and get lost. We are working on an answer. We have no idea what the one item is for - is it for storage? Carrying it? No clue. It really easily broke the included glass - you place it against the glass, push down, and the inner piece will shoot out and break it - you'll feel the pressure which you know is coming, but is so fast and hard it's a little startling. It'll do the job, however. You can't really test the cutting part, but will have to trust that little blade in there will work - I can't image it won't. Being black it'll blend into a car, so not sure about that. But overall this thing seems like it'll come in handy - not that we ever want to need to use it. I'm giving it 4 stars because of the mounting - doesn't work as created for us, but someone else might like it. I just can't image it staying put in a major accident when you'll need it quickly. But yes, we are still pleased to have it and think it's good to keep around.

title: Feel and look great
text:
So I live in a warm weather state and didn’t really need these for warmth, but got them for that cool, classic, gentleman’s driving look. And they perform that duty well.

These leather driving gloves look and feel great. I decided on the black for it’s classic good look. It goes with anything in my wardrobe and on looks like they should. The one thing I don’t like (personal preference) is the lack of the holes on the back of the knuckles, but I deal. Otherwise, they are cool looking and I like when I’ve got them on. Again, not for temperature - and we’ve been warm until recently - but I’ve driven in colder temps from time to time when we travel and I’ll have these to wear for that as well.

The leather is nice - looking and feeling. It’s soft and confirms to my hands nicely.

The open fingers mean I can grip the steering wheel without issue, but can also change the radio, adjust my phone maps for GPS, or other things one needs their fingers for (safely, when driving or stopped or just when on).

Overall I really like these gloves and glad I grabbed them. They look cool, feel great, and I like how they class up the wardrobe when I’m in that mood.

title: Excellent Cup Holders!
text:
When my wife recently broke her foot the doctor put her on very limited restrictions. We got her a scooter so she could get around the house, but she has no way of carrying anything as the scooter requires both hands. So I found these and gave them a try. They work perfectly!

They’re made for strollers I believe, but easily can be used on a bike. But I’d never even thought about what one does when they have a medical scooter. I was having to carry everything for her, but that was not big deal - she could wait. But she wanted to be able to at least take a drink - and she cheats and gets them on her own sometimes. The idea being freedom.

It comes with two in the set we got. They are easy to use and attach. We lucked out - I wasn’t sure how it would work on the scooter, but the one attaches perfectly on the vertical bar. It claps strongly and in this case - note the pictures - for her to have as much of a drink that’s as cold as possible for as long as possible - it fits a very large tumbler. And that weight has not been an issue!

Overall we are thrilled with this choice and if for some reason it breaks, we have a backup. Down the road we can also switch it to bikes or whatever. Absolutely happy to recommend.

title: Love this arm rest cushion!
text:
I’m a leaner... I like to lean onto my right on - and the center - most of the time I’m driving. But wow, my arm can start to hurt - at least with our current car. So my wife will take the blanket we keep in there, fold it over, and put it there. But that’s a huge blanket and it can be too much, or fall...

I happened to see this arm rest pad recently and thought I’d give it a try. I love it!

1. The red was the only color available to me at the time. It is crazy bright. With other choices I’d likely have taken another color, but this is fine. And it it’s fun.

2. The materials and construction seem decent. I’ll admit, I’m thinking it’s a pretty thin piece of foam in there, so long term I’m expecting it not to last. I’ve already decided I’ll rotate it from time to time to give it even wear, but it’ll have a self life. No complaints though. It’s already given me enough comfort to make me happy.

3. It fits easily over the lid of the center - pop it up, use the 2 elastic bands, put them over, close. There is nothing impeded by having it on there, and it has stayed secure. I will say, it does have some play. It will sort of move forward or back - but note, it’s just 2 elastic bands - but you are not permanently attaching it, and you can rotate it to keep it from wearing out. There isn’t enough of an issue for me to care.

4. It is wide enough that both my wife and I can have our arms on it at once. That’s nice - we are both comfortable this way.

5. Our arrived with a slight mark on it. It would have been nice had this not happened, but it’s “fine” - we dealt with it.
‘Overall I am really happy with this choice and I’m glad I grabbed it. It works well and depending on it’s life time use, I would (as of right now) consider getting this same one again. Happy to recommend.

title: Nice looking, words as expected, happy to have it
text:
This appeared to be a nice-looking garbage and I wanted something a little nicer for my car, so took a chance. This is indeed an attractive garbage bag for a nicer car. It’s lighter color will stand out - unlike the black ones that often blend into a backseat/back floor area - this will be seen. But it’s design and look make standing out a nice thing.

We did not “test” the liquid aspects - spillage or leaking - but have had items with this type of lining and they have worked. It is well constructed so I have to think this would as well.

I was pleasantly surprised by the size. It’s very large and should hold a good amount of garbage - one keeping in mind it might be hanging (as ours is) and overfilling might caught a strain. But again, all the materials and construction are nice, so I have to think it’ll hold a large amount well.

The aspect like is the top: it has “slats” cut into the fabric so rather than having to lift a lid you simply stick the item it. I set mine behind me so I can’t reach it - my wife/a passenger would - but it is an easier way of tossing something. IronicallyI have a second on the floor so I can reach it (black, lid needing to be lifted) and only keeping it for my ease. I didn’t like having this on the floor between because of the seat, it was smashed down - not enough room the way my backseat is arranged.

There are a few ways you can set it out - I chose hanging from my headrest. There are also small pockets around which provide a little bit of extra storage - a nice addition.

Overall it looks nice, works well, and for having to have a garbage, it’s a nice addition and makes the use of a garbage appear nice, especially in nicer cars. Happy to recommend.

title: Nice set, plenty of items - room for more
text:
We decided we needed to get emergency kits back into our cars and after putting together one for our Prius, I found this for the other (non-hybrid). This set is larger than our other and includes jumper cables - something we cannot use on the Prius. Overall this is a nice set. There are one or two pieces we have switched to the other car, and there is room to add things we might decide to, but we really like this set overall as-is.

The bag is nice - larger, with good materials and zippers for presumed longevity. The items inside are plentiful and offer a great range of items one might need in an emergency. I like the combination of car/road emergency and medical.

There are items for medical needs like tweezers, scissors and bandages. For the car you have flashlight (needs batteries not included), small shovel, tire repair, tow rope, and tire pressure gauge. These are just some of the included items. We picked this one for our engine (non-hybrid) due to the contents.

Great set - some of the items do feel on the cheaper end of the spectrum, but nothing that won’t work in a pinch. And one can always add or exchange out.

Overall this is a nice set for peace of mind and keeping yourself or loved ones safe while on the road.

title: Really like this bag, pleasantly surprised
text:
My wife was skeptical when she first saw this bag, but we spent last week on vacation and two days in she went out of her way to say it’s a great little garbage bag.

She said she was surprised at how large it was - at first she thought it small. I found it the size I expected. It is - we now both agree - a good size.

She also doubted the dry aspect, but came away happy. We did not put anything wet in per se, but did put in many used wipes we used throughout the trip - it held that moisture fine. And based on our experience, we completely believe it would hold up to any liquids.

It fit fine in the back - I’m not 100% sure how she ended up attaching it, but she said it had several options and she was surprised and pleased that it sat well. And that connecting it was fine.

The way we put it in, I as the driver had little to no access, but she was able to reach easily - it also got the plastic bags we usually use out of the front seat floor area. This looks nicer, works well, and overall we are happy with it.

title: Very good, could be better
text:
I would say we are happy with this unit and do use it every car ride. But it could be better.

The cup holder is fine. It is set, so not adjustable and won’t fit overly large cups. That’s not a big issue - there is the one that is in the car. We got this because we also have a cell phone cup holder that took away one of our cup holders. This gave it back. So that’s been helpful.

It looks nice - it has a faux leather look with red threading that is nice. But it still has a cheap look. But it’s nothing overly problematic. It fits well in the seat, not secure, but that’s not an issue. It can be moved according to what my wife needs on that side. It can be easily removed. But so far she hasn’t had issue with it getting in her way.

There is a cord for charing phones. We do not plan on using it - we prefer Apple brand ones for safety of the equipment. I cannot speak to how well it works.

The pocket section is fairly small, unable to hold anything long. We still find ways to put things in it. Overall it does provide some helpful additional space.

We find it to be of use. I can’t give this 5 stars - it has too many just-misses. but it does work and it is helpful. I recommend it with eyes open and caveats.

title: We Really Like this Double Scraper by AmazonBasics!
text: Just received this Ice Scraper by AmazonBasics. It's made of a hard plastic and has both an ice breaker with serrated edge and a smooth scraper. What I like about it most is the handle. It's made of a dense foam-like material stitched in rows. It's wide and more comfortable for arthritic hands like mine and my husband's. The end of the handle has an opening for you to hang it from your tool wall during summer so it will be out of your way. And it will fit great under your car seat or in the glove compartment during those cold, snowy, and ice weather days. I cannot say yet how effective this scraper is because it's August and no snow or ice here yet. But here in Wyoming it feels like an early fall and possibly an early winter as our snow birds have already flown south. I can come back to my incomplete review once I actually use this awesome scraper.

title: It's Works for Slow Speeds
text:
This Camco Universal Clamp-On Towing Mirror is okay. It was easy to install and worked fairly well in slow speeds. However, while on the Interstate Highway at speeds over 60 it shimmed so bad that you couldn't quite see exactly what was being shown in the mirror. I was driving our Dodge Ram truck with a small trailer on the back. Our last load of moving to our new home...finally done. The Dodge truck mirror worked perfect but the Camco towing mirror just shook all over while at higher speeds. My husband joked with me that if the clamp-on mirror fell off to NOT turn around for it. LOL
It didn't fall off, thank goodness. So I'm not sure how Camco can overcome the shaking at higher speeds but it definitely needs tweaking.

title: Clean & Shinier
text: Got this Star Brite RV wash & wax for our RV. Of course. It did a really good job with removing the bugs and lots of dust ... since we live on a gravel road. We don't have any grime yet, as our RV had been indoors for 4 months, being repaired from a blow-out that threw us off the road and damaged the entire passenger side of a 40 foot RV. New windshield, new stairs, new mirrors, new awnings, new vent, repairs to sliders, new paints, etc. It hasn't had a chance to get real dirty yet as we just used it two weeks ago to move some of our belongings to our new home on a 15-16 hour trip. But this RV wash & wax does great from what I can tell. It seems cleaner and shinier which I really like.

title: Happy with Ultimate Bike Guard
text: We're extremely happy with Star brite's bike cleaner because it helps protect the finish from UV rays. That's a good thing. My husband has a dark red wine color Harley, and I have a restored purple 1964 Cushman. Both of which the paint needs to be protected from the sun since that's when you ride the most....on a sunny day. We're happy with the Bike Guard!

title: Happy with Product
text: We used this Star Brite Bug Off on our RV windshield and the front grill where dead bugs lay on the glass and chrome. It does a good job. And once treating these area's and driving further, it kind of helps where the bugs don't stick as much either. We're happy with this product.

title: Good Quality UTV Cab Enclosure!
text: My husband was so excited to see this Classic Accessories black UTV cab enclosure since he plans on purchasing a Polaris Ranger soon so he can haul tools with him while surveying our fence lines on 40 acres. We took the cab enclosure out of the box and examined it closely. Appears to be great and sturdy. It feels very heavy-duty and is made from ProtekX6 fabric that's water-resistant during rainy weather and has abrasion protection. It's supposed to attach quickly with the click-close straps and grip tabs. These grip tabs are to provide security to the cab's interior.There's a clear windshield, back window, and the doors so you can see out easily. For warmer weather, you can open the doors by rolling them up or by removing them for better ventilation. The cab enclosure is suppose to fit the Polaris Ranger 400, 570, or 800 from  Mid-2015 or newer. It comes with a two year limited warranty.  Classic Accessories make the best patio furniture covers too!

title: This Cleaner & UV Preventer is Magical
text: We started cleaning our dingy with this product and it works wonderfully. Our inflatable boat was covered with dirt, grime, and green mold since just kept outside during the winter.  It's so soft to the touch and looks brand new again! And to know it's protected from the sun rays is even better. Love it!

title: Love my Shiny Wheels!
text: My sporty wheels get all kinds of black gunk on them. I cleaned and used the Chemical Guys, and now my wheels are so shiny! Which I love. I'm hoping that this application will protect my wheels from all the salt on the highways this winter. But I'm very pleased with the way they look now. Thanks Chemical Guys!

title: I love my RV smelling good!
text: These packets work great for our RV. No more pouring blue liquid down the toilet! (So Messy!)Yay! I appreciate any product that keeps sewer gases from entering the main floor of our RV. That awful odor can run you out very fast. Well, maybe that would be a good excuse to go shopping instead. Ha! But that journey wouldn't last long enough as one has to return to their RV. This product keeps the odors intact in the black tank which is greatly appreciated by me. So drop this packet into your black tank and everything will smell lovely, even that new perfume you just bought! Smiles.....

title: Nice, cushy neck pillows with elastic loop on back to hold in place
text: You get two soft, cushy pillows. There's an elastic loop on the back to hold it in place on the car headrest. It does fit correctly on my car's headrest. The pink goes oddly well with my red exterior, black interior car.

title: Window Breaker Seatbelt Cutter might work but the instructions are useless!
text:
I can't see or feel were to pinch to release the keychain so I can access the seatbelt cutter, so I can't use it. Obviously I'm not going to try the hammer on my car window, but I can't push the hammer out at all even against cardboard. The instructions that come with the Window Breaker Seatbelt Cutter don't show how to do these things and, in the Amazon product video, the person's hand is not clear and the video moves too fast when it shows the seatbelt part. So it's useless at the moment, though I did get three of the devices! Sigh.

UPDATE: Ok, so I had a friend mess with this. You have to pull on the keychain while pressing in the sides of the keychain wedge at the front, pointy area. Good luck doing this during an emergency if it's difficult for a nimble, strong man to do in a low-stress situation. Leaving the wedge off, though, means no keychain, so your safety device probably won't be at hand when you need it.

UPDATE 2: You get three colors: black, blue, and green. The green seems to be a dud, too, as the hammer has no spring action (locked rigid) and the keychain wedge was difficult to get off. However, the blue one does allow me to push in on the hammer. I still can't get the keychain wedge off by myself, but the cutter can at least cut through thick (non-corrugated) cardboard.

title: Nice kit, but not sure what to use the wire brushes on
text: The nylon brushes (round brushes and one rectangle brush) are a stiff bristle that cleans dust from crevices and textured areas very well. The microfiber clothing cleans as expected. My car's vent flaps aren't very wide and the grab tab takes up a third of it (and gets in the way of this tool) so two-thirds of my vent flap looks great. lol. The vent cleaner is easy to use. The two metal brushes are impressive looking, but I'm honestly not sure what you use them for since they'll scratch things. Overall, I'm happy with this kit, though.

title: Sparkly. Slight fit issues.
text: The glass gems sparkle in the light. The bottom of the frame has two small hooks to hook over the bottom of the plate and then you screw the top in over the plate. One of the metal tabs for the screws partly covered the final "S" in Arkansas and a corner of the renewal sticker. This didn't cause any problems reading the plate, but it will make it annoying to get the yearly renewal sticker on. The plate holder on the front of my car is different than on the back, and this frame didn't fit quite right, though it did still fit.

title: Easy to add new tissues and attach to car visor
text: This tissue holder can hold normal-sized tissues. It measures 9" long x 4.75" tall x about 0.75" deep (plus the holder bars). The interior of the tissue area might hold 0.5" thick amount of tissues, but they'd be hard to pull out if packed that tight. A velcro strip holds the tissue holder closed. It's a little awkward to flip the holder flap out from under the visor-holder bars, but then you just slip the tissues in with their pull flaps exposed to the central hole so you can easily pull them out.

title: Small and portable, but it has a few quirks to watch out for
text: I like this small air pump, and it's relatively easy to use once you get the hang of it. The handle of the air compressor has vents to draw in the air, so you have to be careful that your hand is not covering these vents while it is working. The way you would naturally grab the handle, your palm covers the top row of vents. However, you have to hold the compressor while it is going because you need to keep straight the short hose connecting the compressor to the tire or ball. Also, you screw that short hose into the compressor and then screw the other end onto the tire (or adapter). Normally, this is not a problem. However, when adding air to my car tires, one connection was difficult to screw on and I accidentally turned the hose instead of the screw connection. When I turned on the air compressor, I heard a hissing and the tire pressure rapidly dropped instead of increasing. I realized that I had unscrewed the hose from the compressor as I was screwing the hose onto the tire. As long as you are aware this could happen, it should not be a problem. The car tire setting was in bar rather than psi. I simply chose the bike tire setting instead and change the psi down to the car tire pressure that I needed. The compressor will automatically turn off when not in use (even just moving between tires). I was pleased that, once that initial setting had been input, it kept the last setting used so I only needed to turn the power on and then the start button. This is small enough that you can easily store it in your car if desired. It has a lithium-ion battery that you recharge using a USB cord. The instructions were reasonably easy to follow and changing settings was not complicated. Overall, I'm pleased with this very portable air compressor. Just keep in mind that because it is small, it may take a little longer to fill a tire or ball than a larger, plug-in compressor.

title: Doesn't come with instructions, so check the pictures to make sure you're putting it on correctly
text:
Yes, it is possible to put this on incorrectly. If the elastic seems too short to reach the back tires and the front elastic too long, then it's upside down. We got this for our Prius, which we need to park outside, and it works very well to protect the windshield from the icy, snowy weather were getting right now. (It doesn't fit our 8-seater Sienna van.) I explained to the male of the family which side was up and how it was secured. I offered to pull up a picture, but he was sure that it was too obvious to need instructions. After 10 minutes of him being outside, I discovered that he had put it on upside down. The upper straps only reached the door handles, so he had hooked them there. The bottom straps were so long that he was sure I was incorrect that the hook was meant to attach to the hubcap and he had tried to drop the hook through the tire intending to pull the hook back around to the elastic strap. The hook had gotten stuck in wheel, which took him 10 minutes to get free again.

I had him look at the picture, and he understood how it was supposed to go on. This time, it went on quickly and easily and covered the windshields well. The straps hooked where they are supposed to. And it's easy to take off (though less so when there's a lot of snow on it). We are pleased with the product. But learn from another person's mistakes and you'll save yourself a lot of time and frustration. Oh, and it does come in a bag for storage, though it fits in so tightly that I'm not sure how we'll ever get it back in.

title: Absorbed well
text: This package contained two microfiber drying towels. They measure 16" x 24", are thick, and are made of 80% Polyester/20% Nylon. They do absorb very well and hold a lot of moisture, which also means they may take a while to dry. They also seem to polish while you are drying. They recommend that you wash the towels for the first use, which I did. Care instructions: Machine wash cold, dryer on low heat. Don't use bleach or fabric softener. Do not iron.

title: 4 piece rubber car floor mat set
text: This set of floor mats provides two mats for the front seat floor and two mats for the back seat floor. The back seat mats measure 18.75" by 13.25". The front mats measure 19.5" by 28" total length with 18" of that the larger, wider area and 10" of that a narrower section that fits in the pedal area. The top surface of the mats have a pattern (as in, they are not smooth) and the bottom has small spikes to help hold the mat in place. I have previously used floor mats that have a carpet top surface, and I like that those soak up any rain off my shoes so that my feet are not slippery on the pedals. These mats do not have that same advantage, but otherwise they are easy to clean and look nice. Not surprisingly, these mats do have a smell to them when you first open them.

title: Absorbent pad with waterproof layer on the bottom
text: This black, reusable pad measures 30" x 36" x 1/8" thick. The bottom side is a shiny, waterproof material to prevent leaks. The topper material is an absorbent material (made of polyester fiber, but it reminds me of felt). I put this mat under my old riding lawn tractor which leaks oil onto the garage floor as it sits between uses. It's preventing further oil stains, but I don't know just how much oil the mat could hold (like during an oil change) as I haven't tested that.

title: Pocket rubs against back of my knees. Doesn't secure well in my car.
text: This seat cover smelled bad (like chemicals) when I open the bag, though the smell has dissipated after a few days. The seat cover measures 20 inches wide and 19.5 inches from front to back. You secure the seat in place using two discs at the back that slip between the crack/gap at the back of the seat. The discs measure 2 6/8" across and are attached to elastic about 3" long. Unfortunately, the backside of our car seats are covered so that we cannot put these discs in place. The bottom of the seat has a nonslip coating, which helps and seems to be sufficient so far. There is also a 5 inch deep pocket hanging off the front of the seat cover against your legs. I don't care for how this rubs against the back of my knees, but the seat is comfortable enough. My dad, with his longer legs and different sitting position, doesn't have any problem with the pocket and finds this seat cover comfortable. There is also a hook attached to elastic at the bottom of this pocket, which you can secure to an "appropriate place," if you have one. There is a zipper on the bottom of the seat cover that allows you to access the inside. The charcoal is in fabric tubes that are inserted in fabric along the center of the seat which are in the fabric of the actual seat cover, so I don't expect any problems with leaks of charcoal. The charcoal appears to just be in the central ribbing areas. This seat cover appears well-made – good/stitching and materials. However, it doesn't quite work the way I had hoped.

title: 21.5" by 13.5" shades that cling to your windows
text: This pack contains three 21.5" x 13.5" sun shades for car windows. Not sure why they went with 3 as every car I've owned has 4 side windows. Anyway, I own a compact car and these fit in the front seat side windows. They're easy to put in place. You just put the shiny side toward the outside and smooth them onto the window. They cling to the window and easily come off. As it's in the winter, I can't say how well they will hold in a hot car or how well they will block out the sun shine, but they do look like they should work. You can see through the mesh from both directions. The shades fold to fit into an 8" by 8" pouch for easy storage. Make sure to get a good look at how they're folded before you unfold them. There are no directions or care instructions included with the shades. They are Made in China. The recycling symbol is number 20, PAP.

title: Good fit
text:
These fit fine on my 2018 Niro EX, and are slightly cheaper than the OEM version you buy direct from Kia. I found that they don't make too much noise, but like all roof rack systems, if you listen for it you'll hear a wind whistle that is mildly distracting. They hold 165 pounds, which is more than enough to support a roof-mountable cargo piece, or a few roof mount bikes.

One thing not mentioned on the page here is that you are not supposed to drive faster than 75MPH with these installed, which is certainly a limitation that should be given more prominence.

title: Quality supplies
text: This emergency kit comes with all the basics - jumper cables, ropes, flags, tools, first aid supplies, an ice scraper, and so forth.  What strikes me about it is that unlike a lot of other "kit" style bundle purchases, there are no poorly made products in here.  The flags are laminated, the scraper is high quality, the gloves have grips on the palms and fingers, the cords on the jumper cables are thick, yet supple.  This is a very nice kit to purchase for yourself or as a gift.

title: Outstanding!
text:
This device is potentially one of the most important things I've ever ordered.

It's main purpose is to act as a jump starter for your car. It has a lithium battery that you can charge at home in an outlet, then store in your trunk until you need it. Two days after I ordered mine, my neighbor's car wouldn't start, so I was able to test it out. It's super easy, and comes with an instruction manual for anyone who has never used jumper cables. Essentially, you clip it in, turn it on, and start your car - worked brilliantly.

Since it's a large battery, though, it's also useful for charging your phone with it's built-in USB, and it has an air compressor you can use at home as well. There's also a work light attachment you can use if needs be.

This really is an all-in-one solution to being stuck on the side of the road. With this device in hand, you can solve most of the day-to-day problems that might have you calling a tow-truck otherwise. Outstanding!

title: Does the Job
text:
This is a pretty basic scanner. It's nice that it has two buttons that will just quickly read what you need to without going into all the menus. You can tell it to just get code, or you can tell it to run the inspection readiness check with just one button each.

Inside the menus it has other options like checking your evap system, which was super-useful because that's what was wrong with my truck, and it told me the leak was fixed, but that the computer hadn't cleared all the evap failures from memory yet. I had to do a little online research to figure that out. But once I did, I realized this little unit provided me with plenty of information to refine my internet searching and repair efforts.

title: Easy To Apply, But No Better Than Turtle Wax Ice
text: Easy to apply & remove. No haze or leftover product after application & removal. Directions indicate to use included microfiber to apply (spray on to towel - not on to car) & remove. However, it's best to use a separate towel for each phase. I didn't notice any significant improvement over a similar product like the Turtle Wax Ice line. Honestly, I prefer the Turtle Wax spray applicator over an aerosol product like this. I may use it until the can is gone (you will probably get 2 or 3 complete applications for a standard size vehicle). Then will switch back to Turtle Wax.

title: OK Assortment, But Some Tools Are Way Too Abrasive
text:
Basic assortment of detailing tools, but some are way too abrasive!

The wash mitt doesn't feel like it has any rough spots that could scratch your exterior. As well, it's pretty thick & soft. The bag of brushes (boars hair possibly) are soft enough for interior work, but will also allow you to work on rims with these. And the vent cleaner tool is, well, a vent cleaner tool. The microfiber towel is very thin. I would put it on par with dollar store quality. That's the OK stuff.

However, I would stay away from all of the nylon drill attachments as well as the pack of mini wire brushes! They are indicating these to use for your rims. I would not use them on your rims if you care at all about micro scratching. They are pretty stiff. And with the mini wire brushes maybe you could sneak in the nylon bristle brush in the rims nooks & crannies, but even then I would be careful. And the buffing pads? Not sure what's up here, but the only ones I would go near my paint with are the yellow pads. The green & maroon are super abrasive (like 3M Scotch pads).

So, for the price you will get a few useful tools, but I would say half of them you don't want anywhere near your detailing toolbox.

title: An Inexpensive Set That Should Be In Your Toolbox
text: It's those times when you need tools like these & don't have them. And not having them only serves to make the job way harder than it needs to be. So, even if you do just the occasional service on your car, just pick these up now & throw them in your tool box. They are super inexpensive, well made & you get a great assortment. Just one tool for removing dash trim is worth the price of the entire kit (versus using something like a flat head screwdriver!).

title: These Things Are AWESOME!
text: I love our Mazda CX5, but it's a little limited on storage & the ability to keep things organized in the driver & passenger areas. There are only 2 cup holders in the Mazda (total). And that may seem plenty for normal people. However, between coffee water, etc.., my wife & I always have a lot of drinks with us. And it leaves us always juggling cups & bottles. These seat gap filler / drink holders are the answer! They look great, fit in the seat gaps perfectly &, not only hold your drinks, but give extra storage for things like your phone, glasses, etc.. They are also slim. So they don't encroach into your seat too much. Overall, I'm loving these. Simply push them down in between the seat gap & they stay put. Simple, yet super practical!

I won’t return it bc the options are slim outside of this same design. Could have been made with a little more concern and care to the customer.

title: Easy install, saved 2-300$
text: OEM part. The part is white instead of the black one that was originally there, but you can’t see it anyway, as it’s behind the glove compartment.  My fan was on high all the time and it was annoying on my 2010 Navigator.  I simply had to squeeze the glove compartment to let it down, take the panel off under the glove compartment (two trim plastic things with a trim tool), unhook there plug and remove two 8mm bolts.  Take out the part and reverse, don’t over-tighten.  You just saved 300$ and solved an annoying problem.  You need to work under where the trim is removed, but you still have to lower the glove compartment so you can see.  Your welcome.

title: Saved hundred.
text: These spark plugs are OEM, but fragile. Make sure you get a spark plug tool and break free for those rear plugs on Expeditions, Navigators and F-150’s.  They are a b#$&h to get to and break easy.  It took me a lot of time and effort, but the mechanics wanted 4-600$ for this maintenance item.  I used a pipe, break free a special socket and a pipe for leverage as they left rear one was seized so hard.  Good times.

title: These are good to prevent you doors from scratch other doors.
text: I installed this on a car door that has a nasty habit of catching wind and scratching other cars.  You only need a good cutter and a soft mallet.  After a few weeks the strip stayed in place and they look like space between the car doors and body.  The disadvantage is the metal inside rusts if exposed. If properly installed this isn’t an issue. There needs to be some way or attachment for wide areas near the top of the the door.  So far so good.  I probably wouldn’t use those for a new luxury car, mainly because up close they just look ok. title: Not specifically made for any vehicle, terrible instructions.
text: This looks great, but the instructions are useless.  It is basically a rectangular piece of painted sheet metal with holes. If you have the ability, this is cheaper, but after playing around with the broke one it is quite difficult to do.  After searching auto parts I found this on amazon prime about 100$ cheaper than other brands. I never heard of this brand, so I was concerned, but I figured it is Amazon prime, so I could return.  Installing the part consisted of six bolts and a plug.  Those ford plugs are a PITA, but got it unplugged. You have to install it down to get to two bolts. A gallon paint can is perfect size for resting the step while you take the motor off.  It took about a very leisurely hour, and could be done in maybe 20 minites.  It’s outrageous that dealers charge over 1100$ this.  The step works great so far and it was pretty much plug and play.  When the other side fails, I will get the same one.

title: Didn't Really Work With 2018 Ford F-150. Sent It Back.
text:
My overall comment on the Specter Performance Air Intake Kit is a sigh and a shrug. I installed it--easy to do with minimal instructions and tools. Ran it for a few days and frankly didn't see much improvement at all.

So several things. I tested this kit on a 2018 Ford F-150, Turbo 2.7 Ecoboost with a six inch lift. I also live in the Arizona desert and tested this in the month of June when it was nearly 110 degrees outside. We all know that hotter air negatively affects the performance of an engine. So in the Arizona desert, all I was getting was hot air.

Regardless, I saw no appreciable difference after installing the kit in either power or fuel economy. Granted, they don't promise better fuel economy, but neither did I see any real difference in power. Perhaps there was some, but I had no way to measure it. As far as I know, it did the job it was supposed to, only I couldn't tell without the right tools to measure it. There was a bit more growl to the engine with this kit, but frankly I don't care for more noise.

Instead, I returned the kit and got a K&N filter that goes into the old spot. This did seem to make a bit of difference in power and fuel economy over this kit. It was also much less expensive than this kit.

Overall, I am neither satisfied nor dissatisfied. I give it a very definitive shrug. Make of that what you will.

It stays on easily at high speeds. Flaps some, but nothing significant. I live in Arizona, so hasn't rained. But I did go through a carwash and it kept the bed dry. I did not use the included foam insulation any where as I didn't seem to need it.

One person can fold and un-fold it--though you have to walk back and forth to both sides to do so. I do like that it is a quad fold, so the footprint when folded completely is smaller than what a tri-fold would be, covering less of the truck bed. There are straps to hold the folded cover down while driving and carrying cargo at the same time.

Haven't driven it enough to tell if it has had any impact on gas mileage, but there might be a small increase.

Overall, happy so far!

Most of the time, we can use a air pressure gauge if needed to test the air pressure, but if we're pumping up a bike tire or a soccer ball, we do that by feel, and the functions tend to just get in the way of that.

It pumps air, will pump up a tire (eventually). It does tend to overheat after long use which bothered me. It doesn't seem to have enough ventilation to keep it from getting hot when pumping up a car tire.

If I need another, I won't be getting this one. I'll use it until it breaks and then get one that just pumps air.

title: Fixed the Death Sway

The longer, lower control arms were all that we replaced because we just couldn't get the bolts off the smaller, higher ones. But even replacing the bottom control arms completely fixed the death sway. Since my son drives this most of the time, I am happy that he is driving safer now.

I would certainly recommend this product.

title: Rear Shocks Didn't Last Long

Within six months of replacing the rear shocks, I could tell that they were shot already. I wasn't happy with that. The front struts seem to be going strong still, so happy about that as they were the harder to replace.

Do it yourself replacement was fairly easy. We needed to rent only one tool for the struts to get the spring off the old and then on the new. The rear shocks were simple to replace, but again, they didn't seem to last long, and its not as if we take the Pathfinder 4-wheeling or anything. It is used almost exclusively around town.

I did have a regular tent, but I hated that it was separate from my car - where I have all my stuff!  So I took a chance on this one and it works. text: I am doing updates to my older mobile home in preparation to sell it.  I have a master bathtub that had a couple of small soft spots and I watched videos on how to fix the issue.  I followed the videos, drilled a hole in the soft spot area, filled the hole with expanding foam until it comes out the hole.  I then allow the foam to dry, cut the expanded foam so it is flush with the hole and allowed the foam to "cure" for 24 hours before using this epoxy filler to cover the hole.  Once I finished the repair I used a kit to paint the ugly beige tub to a nice, crisp white.  You can't even see where I fixed the soft spots and I feel better knowing that whoever buys my home has a decent bath tub to stand or sit in.  This stuff works as it should.  Just wish people who make this stuff would understand that clear directions would make it easier for those of us who use it.

title: For those with arthritic hands/fingers this is a life-saver
text: First off, I lived through the Texas blizzard in February 2021 without power for 5 days.  20 degrees outside, and it was maybe 35 in the house.  I was lucky enough to have moved to Texas from the northeast and had a plethora of blankets to wrap myself in as a way to survive the cold.  I had a bag of white bread, peanut butter and jelly that I ate pretty much 3 times a day along with a 24 pack of soda cans that sitting on the floor in the kitchen were as cold as if they'd been in the refrigerator.  But since then I have worked to be prepared should that happen again.  I bought a 10K BTU kerosene heater (the square style that heats up the front, not the back of the heater.  I also have a smaller, round kerosene heater that does heat 360 degrees around it.  I purchased a 2.5 gal container of kerosene and did what everyone says to do - fill and burn for at least 30 minutes to burn off the smoke and smell.  Now, I knew both my heaters came with the squeeze pump syphon and I doubted my arthritic hands would last very long in pumping the kerosene into the heaters...so I bought this electric one.  I really wish they would put in a pair of D batteries as it is a size many people don't have just lying around the house.  I did happen to have 2 D batteries, but then, I have also prepared with having pretty much every size battery I might need in an emergency.  I even have a case for my batteries so they are easy to find!  Anyway, I loaded my D batteries in this syphon, opened the kerosene container, pulled the kerosene tank from the larger, square heater and opened the tank on the smaller round heater.  I put the pump section of the syphon in the kerosene container, the tubing into the larger heater's removeable tank, pressed the pump's on button and boom!  It was a fast fill - maybe 2 minutes to get the large tank nearly full.  I then screwed the piece that delivers kerosene to the bottom of the heater (and to the wick), turned it over, slide it in and immediately heard the glug glug of kerosene entering the wick/burn chamber.  I then stepped to the smaller, round heater, put the hose in the hole in the tank section, turned on the pump again and I doubt it was more than 90 seconds until I turned it off while watching the "empty-full" needle jump up.  Of course I then started both heaters - man, they warm up FAST!  But being done with this electric syphon, I unscrewed the top, removed my 2 D batteries, screwed the top back on, hooked the hose to the little holder on the side and slide the syphon back in the box and stored it next to the kerosene container that has maybe a half gallon left in it.  I'm ready for a black out in frigid weather!  At least this time my house won't be 35 degrees inside!  And thanks to this electric syphon, my hands were not tortured to use the squeeze syphon.  Oh, now you don't have to have D batteries on hand - inside the pump section are two pieces that allow you to run it on 6 AA batteries (3 to each piece).  Still, I would get the Ds as they are so much easier to drop in and take out.  All in all, I love this syphon and if you have issues with your hands, then definitely get this!

title: Mounted on my tiny houseboat roof
text: I actually do have an inverter window a/c unit if it gets just too uncomfortable when I'm on the river, but this  roof vent is situated in my small bathroom that has both a small shower and a porta potty.  The bathroom is next to the galley/kitchen  - both areas that most need air exhaust!  But of course, it can also pull nice, cool area into the small space and I have to say, this fan does a great job of both.  I have the remote for it velcro'd to the side of the boat control area.  The voice control works well if I'm near it.  If I were in the kitchen area which is a bit further away, I would need to talk louder for it to hear me.  The fan is what is the most important and it works GREAT!

title: I think people have their own preferences for portable toilets
text: I lived on a houseboat 24/7 for 3 years.  One thing I did when I chose this toilet was to purchase a large package of rapid dissolving toilet paper.  It truly does make a difference in the use of a toilet like this.  I am older and simply cannot make it to a campground facility if I'm not within like 3 steps!  Just old and my bladder is weak.  So what I can say is that I am a larger lady and this is a very sturdy toilet that holds my behind well enough that I don't feel afraid I'd break it!  I did also get some scent material to put in the water tank that helps when doing my business and I found some stuff to put in the black water tank to neutralize the smell.  That's the best of this toilet for me - I can do what I need to in it and will a few additions (fast dissolving tp, scent and neutralizer), it works perfectly for my needs.  I guess the only down size is the emptying part, but hey, that's a part of being a creature with an in and out system!

title: I have a greenhouse that I want to use all four seasons
text: Late fall through winter, I had been nursing along a very few hardy plants in my greenhouse, but decided that it was time to make it a year round place for plants.  This heater, from all the videos I've watched about heating spaces (like basements, garages, workshops and such) is the best.  For it's size, I was a bit skeptical and yet when I set it up and tested it, oh buddy!  It puts off the HEAT!  Now, it's not yet time for heating the greenhouse, but this diesel heater was a very easy install and will be just what I need when the cold weather does come in earnest!  What I really like is that it uses very little electricity (I do have lights in the greenhouse so I sure didn't want something that could trip them off when powering up) and the heater seems to sip the fuel so I should be good for a while before having to add more.

title: I have been building a tiny houseboat/home
text: I watch a lot of videos on RVing and renovating trailers and such to get ideas for my tiny houseboat.  Granted, houseboats have to float which is a bit different, but the basic things - kitchen, bed, bath/shower facilities, heat and air - all have to be addressed or at least considered.  I had really been thinking about the different ways to heat my little houseboat.  I mean, I already had propane for hot water heating (shower/sink) and dual propane stovetop so had considered a propane heater, but they tend to be larger units - even the Little Buddy isn't all that little when talking about a tiny houseboat!  Granted, this isn't a tiny unit, but the way it is made, it is more...amenable to install in such a way as to not take up valuable space that could be used elsewhere.  By that I mean tucked into a spot that would probably be wasted.  What's more important is how well this diesel heater heats!  I set it up before installing it to be sure that this is the heater for my little home and oh man!  This thing is awesome!  When I am cruising down the river on a cool fall day, admiring the color changes (breathtaking along the river banks), I know that when I tie up for the evening, I will stay warm if the temps dip lower than I'd like for the night.  Should be a fairly easy install when the houseboat build is at that point.  Now I know why everybody talks about having a diesel heater - this one works GREAT!!!

title: For my son who has a BMW
text: I have a similar OBD II I use on my Toyota and love it.  I did try a style that was a hand-held unit that attached to my car and while it worked okay, I wasn't as happy with it because the cord between the plug in and the hand unit was not very long so I was just frustrated having to hold it "just right."  That's why I like this style - bluetoothed to the app on my phone, the little unit functions without a cord and my phone can go with me as I read the app's findings.  So, this one being made for BMWs is for my son and when he downloaded the app, plugged the unit into his car, he was really impressed with the diagnostics.  These truly help when you feel something is going on with your car - either you hear it or you see the check engine light (or other light) come on.  Definitely worth having it for your car and your peace of mind!

title: I have an older Toyota Camry
text: I love my little tank of a car - she is a 1999 with over 200K and she just keeps on running!  Why would I want to trade her for a newer model that I will have a payment for each month?  But of course, at her age (like me) she needs to be monitored a bit more closely.  That's why I put the tire pressure monitor on her four tires.  I recently changed out two of her tires and had the other two moved to the back (front wheel drive).  These help me to monitor the two older tires as well as the two new ones so that I get the best gas mileage and of course, safe ride.  It's kind of funny - I'm sort of running out of room on my dash.  I have an Echo Auto, and a head's up display that allows me to watch my speed (plus a few other things) and now the tire pressure monitor.  My car may be older, but she does have some nice tech stuff that helps her and me!

title: I have installed them on a double axle 6x12 trailer
text: I'm building out the trailer to be my "tiny home" while camping.  It's important to be aware of the tire pressure and that's why I have attached them.  So far they are working great - I'm still building out my trailer so have not taken it anywhere, but in testing them, they will be invaluable to ensure that my trailer is riding along with fully-inflated tires or after a few days at a campground, they haven't lost air before I pack up and get back out on the road.  If you haul horse trailers, motorcycles, etc. these would be an excellent way to be sure you're on the road with good tires all around.

title: I have a few 12V XXAh batteries
text: I put XX in the subject line because I have two small emergency set ups - one has 3 12V 15Ah LiFePO4  batteries and the other has 3 12V 18Ah LiFePO4 batteries, but I have a few odd batteries such as one 6Ah and another 8Ah.  I used this charger to get both of the odd-one-off batteries as they can be used for emergencies, but can't be tied to the two emergency systems mentioned as the Ah needs to match.  But even with my portable systems, I make sure they are charged up for camping or when the power goes out and that's easiest done with this charger.  I do have a solar panel to charge the batteries, but it's also helpful to have a faster, electric way to get them charged up.  Excellent to have on hand for other battery uses (charging up electric lawn mowers and such).

title: My third 15Ah lithium battery
text: I watched a video on creating a portable emergency power system in a milk crate and while I have not had the money for a 100Ah (or higher) battery, for emergencies, chaining together three 12V 15Ah gives me 45Ah at the ready should my power go out.  I have it tied to a 1200W pure sine wave inverter, a battery tender and a portable, foldable 200V portable solar panel.  The milk crate makes it easy to move this in and out of the house so I can recharge the batteries should the power outage last longer.  It can also be used on a camping trip as all the parts are easily stowed in the car.  This battery is about the same as the other two 15Ah batteries I have and even chained together, they fit in the milk crate well with the inverter.  Great for my emergency power!

title: I wish it came with a usb cable to charge power banks directly
text: What I have is several fountains in my yard to make sure the wild birds have water to drink and to take a bath in.  The thing is, I changed out the solar pumps with USB pumps so they would continue to bubble water 24/7 so no algae forms (in stagnant water).  Of course, with USB, I need a power source.  What I have done with this solar panel is attach it to a 12V 18Ah lithium battery that is attached to a 12V 1700W truck inverter that has four USB ports. I have the battery and inverter covered by a waterproof box and four of my fountains are attached to the inverter.  It's working great - the solar panel, battery and inverter keep the fountains working.

text: Wanted it to work, but if it cannot be updated, then it is basically worthless and at this price, that's just unacceptable.

title: I have a fairly old Toyota that just keeps on running
text: Older cars get short shrift by people - if you have a car that has over 250K and you've kept it up, changing oil, tires, belts, etc. and it keeps running like a champ, why would you trade a paid-for running vehicle for a newer one that may or may not last as long plus you have to pay monthly payments on?  Me, I like my old girl - she gets me where I want to go in comfort and safety.  So, her paint finish isn't so great and I decided to use a wrap on her.  Sort of a face lift if you will.  She went from white to sapphire blue with a few hours' worth of work, the wrap that I purchased and this kit.  I did watch many videos and took off many body parts to ensure the wrap was "fully wrapped" and after I finished, my little Camry looked like she just rolled off the showroom floor!  Now, having done the outside, I plan to try wrapping some of the dash and center console pieces to give her a new interior.  I already added some pretty black and white leather seat covers (both front and back) and added new floor carpets with a bit of sapphire blue bling around the edges.  I have a nice, paid for car that looks better than half the cars out on the road and I accomplished that with this kit (and the wrap)!

title: Wish it had come with a reamer/cleaner for the screw on applicator
text: The idea behind using this adhesive was outdoor wood tiles.  See, the tiles are supposed to "snap" together and while you can get them snapped, they don't stay that way!  They slide apart every time you try to move the stupid tiles.  I mean I like them and want to use them but if they refuse to stay together, then they are useless.  I snapped together two tiles upside down and used this adhesive on the snapped together spots.  The box of wood tiles held 36-12X12 inch tiles.  What I wanted was a pathway in a dirt part of my yard and having the path 3 feet wide by 12 feet long works for my area.  So I will be working up two tiles at a time, snapping and gluing them together until I can make a 3x6 foot section and then another.  The slatted wood looks nice and still allowed water to drain down to the soil, yet keeps my feet off the dirt.  This adhesive, being waterproof is just what I needed for this project.

title: My car is older but my daughter has a 2021 vehicle that this works on
text: My older car won't work with this OBD2 unit, but I know my daughter had been interested in the one that I have used in my car to identify a couple of issues recently.  I took this one over to her place to plug into her own car and explained my own experience with the OBD1 unit I used to identify a couple of issues with my own car.  Her car appears to be working just fine without anything being "thrown" on this OBD2, but having gifted this to her, we used it so she is familiar with how it works and should her car have some odd sounds or one of the images on her dash, like the check engine light comes on, she will be capable of plugging this unit in to find out what may be the problem.  It will also give her some leverage when having to deal with the repair shop and what they tell her.  This unit is similar to mine and it is so easy to use!  All the systems it can access, you will really know what's up with your car before taking it into the shop!

title: I had a set of leather covers and did not like them
text: Okay, they looked nice, but I just am not a an of leather seating.  I live in the southwest and there just isn't anything more gross than slick sweat on leather...yuck!  Plus the leather ones were so hard to put on that I only got the driver's seat one on!  These are more my style and I really like them.  They are easy to put on and very comfortable to sit on.  My car is white and has little color in it, so these do provide a bit of color inside the car - my car's original fabric seats are gray, the carpet is gray, the dashboard is gray...so having this little bit of color does make my older car look better inside.  The price is good and as I mentioned, these slipped on easily enough and look good on.  Great buy for my older car!

title: This is my preferred OBD scanner
text: The other one is larger and good in it's way, but this one is my preferred scanner as the phone interface with the car section that plugged in at the base of my steering column was excellent.  So I'm sitting in my car with the app open and this tiny piece shown in the posting was plugged in.  Immediately it finds the source of my check engine lighting up and then gave me websites/videos that would explain the issue for me so I have an idea of what to expect either in terms of pricing to fix it or buying a part and fixing it myself.  If you have little money to spend on car repairs and feel comfortable doing a bit of car repair on your own (which I do), getting this OBD will assist you in deciding how to spend your money.  Worth the price, most definitely.

title: Had a light go off on my dash
text: It was the check engine light and I decided that once and for all I would try two different styles of OBD's so I could decide which one I liked the best.  I really like this one because it is larger, easier to hold and the screen is very easy to read.  This OBD found the issue in very little time and I was able to go online and see recommendations on what to do to fix the issue.  Had I known how easy to use and helpful the information it gave me about my car, I'd've bought this OBD a long time ago!

title: You need this in your car!
text: I love that this is both for jumping your car and putting air in a low tire.  That's such a needed thing for just about anybody and everybody that owns a car.  There will come a day when your car's battery does the dead thing on you or you walk out and find one of your tires is low.  Nice a compact, this is perfect to store in your car.  Gift it to your mom, your daughter, your son - anybody - it's a surprising gift, but worth it!

title: Became part of a camping shower system
text: Not a great pump, but for what I wanted it for, this works okay.  LOUD!  But considering this is attached to a rechargeable LiFePO battery and then an attached hose submerged in a bucket of water, the other hose attached to a propane on-demand hot water heater, I can take a shower when I'm out camping...so long as this pump continues to work.  It does not seem to be a really robust build, but I'll find out in the weeks and months to come...

title: My car may be older but it can have bling!
text: I do have some sparkle - I love the blue rhinestone "decals" I added to the mirrors on both visors as well as the cupholder covers.  These lights as that extra bling, where the rhinestones sparkle!  This was easy to add to my car and the app works great to manage the lights.  I tend not to mess with them - I pick a color and leave it alone and while I have tried the lights to music, I found it too distracting to have them changing to music so I tend to keep that part of the app off.  I like my little, older car and blinging it out with these lights makes her still look pretty to me!

title: Added to my boat build
text: I am following the plans and building a small, trailerable boat that's 8.2 feet by 28 feet and these lights I added five to the bow, five to the stern along the roof line.  I have large enough windows along both port and starboard sides for the string led lights to make my boat visible in the evenings.  These lights are what I needed to be sure, if other boats are nearby, they will see my boat in the twilight.  These are very bright and easy to install - I'm glad that I put these on my boat build.

title: Building a boat from plans
text: Not a large boat - a trailerable size of 8.2 feet by 28 and am using some unique/alternative techniques to boatbuilding.  But that's part of why this pump works for me.  I have a hot water on demand unit that is plumbed for both the galley sink and the shower on the other side of the adjoining wall.  RVs and trailerable boats share quite a few things in common, the first and foremost is making the space and systems do double-duty whenever/wherever possible.  This pump does that for my galley and head - only one sink as there's no reason to have two within a couple of feet of each other and then the shower.  I am learning most of the connections as I work through this build, but that's the point.  When I'm done, should anything happen that needs repair, I will know everything about the system and can do what needs to be done.  Testing this pump (attached to the 60 gallon bladder that will be under the floorboards) with my water on demand heater gave me the confidence my build/system will work for me.

title: Used this in my houseboat build
text: I am retrofitting a larger, but trailerable vee-hull older boat, enclosing it to be a tiny-home houseboat.  A 25 foot boat with a beam or width of 8.6 feet making it a legal (no permit required) and trailerable boat.  Being on the river, I thought it might be nice to have this fan pulling fresh air through the interior while "under sail" (meaning I am moving with the help of the outboard motor).  This was easy for me to install since I am still making the finishing touches to the interior 12 x 7 living space of my floating tiny home.  The roof also has a pair of 400W solar panels for off-grid cruising so I am also very cognizant of power drains on my system that resides in a pair of 12V 100Ah lithium batteries.  This fan is a much more efficient way to stay cool than the roof-mounted A/C unit that I do have as well.  But on the water is a bit different than on the road - higher humidity levels, obviously, which can be both better or worse depending on the temperature.  Anyway, I'm very pleased with this fan's install and I believe once I get to take my tiny houseboat out on the river, it will make my time inside more comfortable.  It is very quiet and I do like the ability to manually open/close it should I have issues.  Nice unit worth having in your RV, boat, even a regular tiny house.

title: Be aware that this is a modified sine wave inverter
text: Nothing really wrong with a modified sine wave inverter other than the fact you may want to watch what is plugged into it as the power can fluctuate somewhat as compared to a pure sine wave inverter.  That being said, I attached this to one of my emergency power 12V lithium batteries rated at 80Ah and then plugged in my corded drill to do some work outside.  No problem at all!  Let's say you are working on building a house (in progress) and don't have access to electricity yet, then this is a wonderful inverter that can be attached to your vehicle's battery (do keep your car running so as to keep from draining your battery) or as I did, with a stand alone (or also attached to a solar panel to provide free power) battery.  I have purchased a lot to build a house on and this inverter will ensure I can work on site prior to having the electric company stall a meter and make grid-tied electricity available.

title: Of the inverters I have tried, this one is okay - just okay
text: It's not the best of the inverters I've tried, but it works okay.  The build quality is not the highest and I have to say, this one is not the inverter I reach for when I need one.  Best to look at other, higher quality inverters if you need one.

title: I have a pair of batteries I keep powered up (with solar panel) to use with this
text: I am working on a few projects that are not able to just plug into house power and this inverter has enough power (with my charged up batteries) to run a concrete vibrator while pouring concrete piers for my house build or the circular saw for cutting the boards for the foundation atop the concrete piers.  These are just examples, but the point is that a new house site isn't the place you would find a place to plug in power tools unless you have an inverter attached to a battery.  This inverter is working great for my projects and will see more use in the next several months.

title: I'm using this wired in parallel to another 18Ah battery
text: This is my "quick-rigged" emergency power source for short term.  I have a 3000 amp pure sine wave inverter connected to these batteries.  I also have a battery tender so I can see how much juice is left in the "battery bank."  I also have a 200W portable/foldable solar panel so that I can charge my batteries up.  I live in Texas and during the February when we had the blizzard, I was without power to my house for five full days.  I've made sure that never happens again.
