The 3000W inverter attached to this (and the other) battery allows me to run an electric griddle and cook a hot meal on a freezing day even if my house has no power!  Good, small size for storing when not needed, too.

title: Not at all easy to get on and I have a CAMRY!
text: When I saw these,  thought they would look nice in my Toyota Camry - an older car - and keep the original seats in better condition.  I pulled out the pieces and watched the video...looks like a 10 minute install, right?  I am so frustrated with them that the pieces are in the trunk of my car.  Pulling the back piece on my small car's seat was a 20 minute struggle that still didn't allow the cover to seat properly on the car's upright section.  When I'm feeling a bit more ZEN, I will try again.  For now, these are sitting in pieces in the trunk of my car.

title: I have 3 solar panels and 2 12V 45AH batteries for use with this inverter
text: And this inverter is the heart of a quick and portable off-grid system for me.  I haven't mounted it yet, but probably will when I get to that point in renovating a small, older, camping trailer I bought for cheap.  As a kid, my parents took us tent camping and then switched to a truck and bed camper, but both tent and camper were rather "crude" as far as today's standards go and I'm no longer that little kid.  I like having lights and a refrigerator as well as hot water when I'm out in more primitive camp sites.  This inverter, tied to the batteries (that are charged by the solar panels) gives me the power I need.  I have kept this as a portable system just in case the electricity goes out in my house from a storm or some other issue (such as a car accident that takes out a transformer) - with the batteries wired to this inverter, I can still use my microwave, plug in an electric skillet, even plug in the induction cooktop and make dinner.  I have a couple of other power stations for use with my laptop and keeping my phone charged, but this inverter allows me to use more traditional, much higher wattage appliances that the other power stations could not handle (most are 200W or less).  This inverter, at 3000W, can handle most any higher-wattage appliance, though it is also dependent on the amount of stored energy in my batteries as to what I would use during a blackout, but the best part is having an inverter that allows me to actually choose what I need to plug in.  This one easily hooks to my batteries and the display allows me to see at a glance the stored power available (in my batteries) as well as what power is going out (to what is plugged in and is using the batteries' power).  This inverter (and my batteries and solar panels) gives me a certain peace of mind - so that I feel more in control when camping or when black outs occur at home.

title: I also have these same skeletons as vent scent guys
text: The clip on vent skeletons are smaller than these two guys and I did get all three - the hear/see/speak no evil skeletons for my car's three vent areas in the dash.  I LOVE them - they are so cute and silly!  When I saw these mirror hanging skeletons I had to add them to my car.  Maybe I am a bit warped, but I do love these little skeleton dudes!  I did shorten the string on one so they don't hang at exactly the same length and interfere with each other.  The only thing I would wish for is that I received all three of the guys like my vent dudes - three of them in the see/hear/speak no evil set up.  If you or someone you know loves the skeleton artwork, these guys would be a great gift to yourself or others.

title: Nice little car trash can
text: I wish it was offered in other colors.  I love blue and would have been so happy with a light-medium-dark blue (whichever - I just like blue) instead of black as I have added a steering wheel cover, floor mats and a console cover that have blue as the main color.  This was easy enough to hang on the back of the passenger seat's head rest so that it is out of the way but easy for me to use.  I have saved every plastic bag I get when shopping and use them as the liner for this small trash can for my car.  That way it is easier to remove and keep the car clean from trash and easy to throw away.  Not a bad trash bag - just wish it came in colors.

title: Like it, but am having trouble getting it on
text: I am older and have arthritis in my hands/fingers and it is really hard for me to work with stiff material that needs a LOT of pushing/pulling to get it on the steering wheel.  At the moment it is in my car and I am trying to find a day when my hands don't hurt as much...if that doesn't work, I may get the type that can be sewn on so that I'm not fighting to get the cover on.  I do understand the cover needs to fit snugly on the steering wheel, but it's almost too difficult to put on for someone like me.  I love how the cover looks - would love it more if I could get it on my steering wheel!

title: Blue is my favorite color
text: Black, of course, is the main color and for a good reason - it is the "tough" part that puts up with the dirty shoes 'n stuff that gets set on the floor boards of my car.  The sparkly bling is a dark blue - I would have loved it to be a brighter, lighter blue, but still, blue is my favorite color and these add a bit of girly bling to these mats and my car.

title: Where I could use these, they do look nice
text: I have an older Toyota Camry and the bling in this kit only fits on so many places.  Where it fits, it looks nice, but I had to just play around with the larger pieces to see where I could place them.  Oh well...guess that's the thing about generic kits, right?  Might fit one car perfectly and not another one.  Where I was able to add them, they look nice...

title: Excellent for what it is
text: I have a 5000W inverter that is my emergency (no power to the house) back up which runs off of LIFPO4 batteries which I charge with 200W solar panels, but this inverter is my car emergency power.  It's NOT going to run a microwave or anything that draws serious power, but for charging phones, tablets and even batteries for tools needed while out and about, then this is the right one for that job!  What I love about it is the size - my 5K inverter is really big and VERY heavy!  This little guy is about the length of a cell phone, but of course, thicker and a bit wider.  That means it is easy to store even in a small car.  See, I have emergency items I carry at all times in my small car - I have a couple of bottles of water both for drinking and if needed, for a radiator issue, a quart of oil should I find my car is really low on oil, a portable air pump should a tire be low/flat and an electric jack should that flat tire not be able to hold air and needs changing.  That being said, it really is imperative to be prepared for emergencies and in a car, having an inverter like this small one is perfect - no more dead cell phone because you forgot to charge it before leaving the house, no screaming kids finding their tablet is dead and they can't watch the movie you downloaded for them!  If you are camping and using air mattresses or possibly stand up paddleboards at the lake, it is much easier to have an electric air pump that the old, takes forever bicycle hand pump.  For the price, for what it can do for you in many situations, this is a great small converter.

title: I'm an older lady, but this would be great for almost anyone
text: I love that this is a 2 for 1 item that will cover the two most often occurring car issues while away from the house - a flat tire (that may not hold air, but you won't know until you try pumping it back up) and a dead battery.  Jump that battery and you should be able to get home without having to rely on strangers to jump your car or worse, calling a tow truck that will cost you $$.  With the pump, instead of using the donut spare tire most cars have, if you can pump the tire up and get yourself to a tire store for a replacement, that's better than taking off the bad one, putting on the donut which would take a lot of time - you'll get to the tire store sooner.  The dead battery I've had happen in a parking lot of a mall and there is nothing more frustrating than to come out to find your car not turning over and finding no one is close to you that could help.  Having this jumper to get my car turned over and on the road again, I can get to an automotive store to have the battery checked to see if it needs replacement or not.  At least I can get myself where I need to be when using this 2 for 1 car machine that works quite well for emergency situations.  Good for mom, dad, teenage kids (show them how to use it) - great as a gift for someone who has just gotten their driver's license, too!  Excellent tool to store in the car for those just in case moments.

title: My niece has a larger pickup tent
text: She has a big, full size truck so her truck bed can accommodate a larger truck bed tent.  My nephew loves to go camping, but has a smaller truck and I thought this one would work for his particular truck.  It fits fine, but having seen my nieces' truck tent and comparing this one to the larger one, I can say that they both seem to be made well enough to keep the rain off those inside the tent.  The one big difference between the larger truck tent and this one was an awning which would have been nice.  I mean, this tent is such a nice, small bundle to throw in the truck along with y'know, a chair, a small cooler and grill and having an awning would make it nicer to sit out while camping.  Other than that, this is a really nice little tent for an on the go young man (or couple) that like to take a quick weekend camping trip to get away.  Again, just wish this one had an awning to provide a bit of shade and place to sit out after a nice hike.

title: Heavy duty car jack, plus
text: This handled case is fairly heavy for an old lady, but you know what?  It isn't any fun trying to manually jack up a car if you have to change a flat tire either!  I have an emergency kit in my car and this electric car jack is a part of that kit.  I also have a couple of liter bottles of water should my radiator overheat, a container of oil and paper funnel to use should I need to add oil, a small air compressor, an electric jump starter and a few other things.  Cars are great when they run, but when you have problems?  Man, cars can be a pain!  If you have an emergency kit stored in your car's trunk or a box in the back of your SUV, it gives you some feeling of freedom from relying on others to do what you CAN do on your own.  This electric car jack takes a great deal of the pain and irritation out of getting your car lifted enough to change a flat tire - even if its just to put on the donut to get you to the tire place for a full-size replacement.  This car jack is really cool how it moves smoothly, though it is a bit loud, but I'm not terribly worried about that since it's cranking up a 2000 pound car without my "muscle power!"  The impact wrench is such a great addition, too if you have ever used a lug wrench that some cars include with the manual jack, then you know about cracked knuckles, cursing under your breath, trying to kick the lug wrench to get a lug nut to move.  Another thing I do carry in my emergency kit for hard to remove lug nuts is a small can of WD-40, so spraying a bit around the back of the lug nut and then putting this impact wrench on it, bam - lug nut off!  I highly recommend this for your husband, for your wife - even adult kids - anyone who drives, actually!

title: Excellent 2000W inverter
text: My first 2000W inverter did not have the LCD display on it.  I'm no expert, but I have been putting together portable solar systems for emergencies/camping use and of course, the inverter is the "business end" of the system.  With this 2000W inverter, I can pretty much power what I need - a microwave or ceramic heater, for example, when the power goes out.  Now, of course, this inverter has to get it's power from somewhere and I have invested in some used 32Ah LiFePO4 batteries and have wired them in series so that they produce 128Ah (amp hours) and hooked the 4 batteries to the inverter.  My 200W solar panel may take a bit of time to recharge the batteries, but that's the beauty of an emergency system.  It can be recharged so that I have more power the next evening.  VERY happy with this 2000W inverter.  Excellent quality and power for the price.

title: Versatility in an emergency unit made to be in my car - excellent
text: Being an older lady, I have for many years kept emergency items in my car.  Bottles of water should my radiator overheat, a bottle of engine oil and a funnel, emergency flares and a few other items.  I now have a very important item - a jump starter and tire inflator for those emergency situations as well.  The other thing I added was a heavy-duty jack that uses air to pump up my car - should I need to change a tire if it cannot hold air.  I do believe every parent, mothers and fathers alike, should teach their children who are just learning to drive how to handle emergency situations and be prepared to handle it when it happens.  In order to do that, you needs the proper tools and THIS jump starter and air compressor helps with two fairly common issues - finding your car's battery dead and walking out of your house to find a flat tire.  Having an air compressor to check whether the tire will hold air and a jump-starter so you don't have to rely on strangers to help you jump your car's battery - both issues make this tool well worth the value (and price) to have in your car.  Get one for yourself or for that new driver in your family.

title: Getting up off the ground in a truck tent is so worth it!
text: I mean, wherever the truck can go, I can camp!  Doesn't matter if the ground is a bit bumpy, rocky or whatever since my tent and sleeping spot is high up off that ground!  This tent takes a few minutes to set up, I then add a piece of egg crate foam across the bottom, then my sleeping bag.  I like that this has an awning where my chair and a small folding table can stay out of rain or the hot sun of the day.  Great for parking near the lake for a day of fishing or getting close to some good hiking trails and after a day out on the lake or the trails, I have a comfortable place to sleep.  This tent fits my truck bed well (do be sure to check the size to see if it fits your truck), has great ventilation (I also have a solar/USB fan to help) and is definitely rain-resistant.  Stores fairly small for those spur of the moment weekend trips.  I would definitely recommend this to anyone (if it fits their truck bed).

title: For emergency, power-outage use
text: I have set myself up for short term emergency  power outage preparedness after having dealt without power for a few days.  So now I have a pair of these 12V 16Ahr batteries wired in series (and another pair of 12V 18Ahr batteries as back up when these are being charged) so that I effectively have 32Ahr when these are attached to the 2000W inverter.  I can still power many items in the house like the microwave so long as I'm not just using over and over and over when the power is off.  I also have a pair of solar panels that can charge these (and my other pair of batteries) so that even if the power is off for a few days, I have the ability to keep this battery powered up and ready for use.  Always good to be prepared and this battery gives me the peace of mind I need should the power go off tomorrow.

title: This is one of my solar batteries
text: I'm no expert by any stretch of the imagination but I have been working with solar panels, MPPTs and inverters paired with batteries to understand the way I can create and store power for use when needed.  I am one of the millions of Texans that suffered through February 2021's blizzard.  My own home was without power for 5 full days - outside temp was around 20 degrees, the inside temp around 35 degrees Fahrenheit.  During this past year I have done what I can to ensure that if the Texas grid goes down again, I will have light, heat and the ability to heat and eat/drink hot food and drink.  At the heart of this preparation has been learning to pair up the materials in a portable solar system so that I don't have to cook on propane on my porch, but can plug in an induction cook plate to the 2000W inverter powered by a set of these batteries that, once I'm done, take the batteries out and hook them to the solar panel to recharge.  For my emergency set up, this battery (as a pair to create 36Ah) is perfect!

title: I have a 5500W inverter, so this is my "second in line"
text: Having been without power for days during a blizzard and going camping with electronic equipment, I have developed a couple of rigged systems.  This inverter I have attached to a 12V 100Ah battery that is also attached to a solar panel.  I can take it camping and keep my small camping fridge going without a problem.  I can use the small portable a/c unit on for a few hours during the heat of the day, plus have my laptop plugged in at the same time.  The 5500W inverter is larger and quite a bit heavier, so it is my home emergency use one while this one is a bit smaller and quite a bit lighter - much more portable for use during camping.  Excellent inverter for the price and my intended use.

title: Testing for now, but this will work for my RV
text: I have purchased a couple of 12V 100Ah batteries, wired them in parallel I can potentially have 200Ah available at 12V that can be fed through this inverter to be used by pretty much any electrical item you can plug in.  I went without power for five days last February during the blizzard in Texas - 20 degrees outside, it was barely 35 inside my house without any power.  I have made some changes to ensure that never happens again.  And this inverter, tied to a pair of batteries that I can recharge through solar panels does make me more energy independent.  I am also working on renovating an older RV and this inverter will eventually be a part of the RV's electrical system (with the batteries I have now and the solar panels).  I'm really impressed with how this inverter is just a workhorse of power.  It is pricy, but considering some other inverters I've looked at, this is not overly expensive and is, in fact, a fairly decent price for the wattage you have to work with - I mean, plug in that camp fridge, the portable a/c, or a heater for the hunting blind.  This inverter can handle it!

title: This is a big part of my car emergency kit
text: There are certain things I expect may happen with a car - one being a dead battery, another is a flat tire among a few less common occurrences, but those two seem to be the biggest, most common issues that happen.  Whether they happen when you are at home or you come out from shopping and find the car won't start or notice one of your tires are flat - that's an immediate need for a fix-it solution.  With the battery, this jump starter is THE emergency tool to have in your car.  I have used this once on my car's battery and boom - it worked!  That's the point - having a tool with you that is just like that - boom, works!  I make sure once a month that it is fully charged and then put it back in my emergency car kit.  It is definitely one of the main tools that gives me peace of mind having it charged and available AND HANDY in my car!

title: Only 3 ah but it is a good test battery for my test solar system
text: I have a basic system - 200 watt solar panel (2), I have several batteries now, all 12V, but with different ah, so can't attach them (my mistake), an MPPT to control the power traveling from the solar panel to the battery and then an inverter to draw off power for my use - for emergencies, for camping or whatever.  I may have a way to go, but I'm learning and this battery is one of a few that has helped me to learn and understand how to harness solar power.  That's a big thing for me coming from such a small battery!

title: Practicing my solar hookups with different batteries
text: I am working on an emergency system - I have 2-200W solar panels to charge a few different batteries.  I also have a 3000 watt and a 5500 watt inverter that I can connect to different batteries to produce power during emergencies or if I am camping or away from the electrical grid.  See, I spend 5 days last February without power during the Texas blizzard and I have been beefing up my emergency stash - see, I got a couple of the power stations and realized they did NOT have the power to turn on an electric pot or kettle should I want hot food during 20 degree black out days!  With the two inverters and a battery like this one, I can plug in a grill and make a grilled cheese sandwich to warm me up.  Now, with my solar panels I can charge this battery (and my other batteries) up so it can be reused.  Not bad, right!

title: This is great for younger kids as well as older people
text: I have no arm strength - I'm in my late 60s with arthritis and trying to use the regular jack that is often found with the spare when you are looking to change a flat.  Not that I expect to change a flat every other day or anything, but when I am stuck out with a flat, the last thing I want to do is put that silly, cheap-o jack under the car and spend a bunch of time hand cranking that jack when I can use THIS electric jack that can easily pump up my car without killing me!  It is strong and works great!  I plugged it into the cigarette lighter and it took a very short time to pump my car up.  Now with the impact wrench, I did have to pull a small can of WD-40 from my own emergency car kit to spray the lug nuts before using the wrench.  It did remove the lug nuts once I added a squirt of of oil.  This kit is definitely one that can help out ANYONE, but I feel that it's perfect for young people who don't always have the money for a tow truck as well as older folks who just don't have the muscle to do it "by hand."

title: I have a small car but wanted the ability to pull a small trailer
text: Not like I'm trying to pull a 30 foot camper behind me, but having such a small car, I cannot fit a full size piece of lumber in my car when I'm doing interior updates to my house.  So...I found a small trailer my car can tow and had this hitch installed. At the same time they installed the lights cables so I am "legal" with the trailer's lights.  I can now order a full size sheet of plywood to replace a damaged piece of subflooring and pick it up with my trailer attached to this hitch.  Someone would say, "Just by an SUV, truck or mini-van," and I would, but I'm conserving my money with a paid for car (how many out there can say they don't have a car payment) and for a total of $300 for the small (used) trailer and having the hitch installed, I'm happily on the road to the local home store for items I couldn't carry home inside my car.  This hitch is great - it does not rattle and handily pulls my trailer without problem.  Works for me!

title: Car emergency kit worthy!
text: You know they say to keep blankets, bottled water, matches, etc. in your car, and that's all fine and good, but I also like having this in my car so I can get my car up and running again without having to call a tow truck or on the help of passersby to jump a dead battery.  This isn't just for dead car batteries either and that's a big bonus - charge your phone or tablet, if it's night, the light on this is very bright!  I appreciate that this came in its own case - so much easier than just being one of those things in my emergency "car stash."  This is first on my list of get YOURSELF out of trouble - I also keep a bottle of oil with a paper funnel and a large, liter bottle of tap water in case the radiator springs a leak - both happen enough to people out on the road so being able to replace leaking oil or radiator fluid so I can get home or to the auto repair place is well worth stashing in the car.  Oh, I also have a heavy duty pneumatic jack.  Emergency kit for my car and this battery charger is EXCELLENT to have on hand.

title: Just what I needed for my car
text: I am a slob, what can I say?  I'd stop at the mail box (group one for several homes on my street), pick up my mail and then sit in my car, open stuff...so most of it being trash, I didn't see the point in bringing it into the house just to throw away...it got dumped on the passenger's side foot section.  And that pile grew for days.  Now, after I cleaned out that section of my car, I don't want that happening again, so I got this trash can that I can use appropriately.  I do have plastic grocery bags an use them as a liner to keep it easy to empty - just take out the plastic bag, tie the top and put it in the outside trash can.  I have placed several plastic bags in the bottom so when I fill one up and throw it away, I have the replacement right there, ready to go.  I mounted this on the back of the passenger seat - I can still reach it, but it isn't so...apparent when I open my car door.  Silence your inner slob - get this trash can for your car!

title: I have four of these 12V Lithium batteries
text: And they have been hooked together and along with a battery tender, attached to a 200W solar panel as my first solar power set up for emergency situations. I have a 2000W inverter that I can attach to the charged batteries and use some power tools or other electric devices.  I decided to try this out with my 1200 watt single plate induction  cooktop.  The reason being that I spent 5 days without power during the Texas blizzard in February 2021 and I have been working to make sure that I do NOT have that happen again.  So, during the day I have this solar panel to charge the batteries and the battery tender tells me when my batteries are fully charged.  I can then bring them in, attach the inverter to the battery set and plug in my cooktop.  It worked GREAT!  I so have a couple of those power stations but what I realized is that they might power my laptop, but this "larger" one I have is 300W - 300W will NOT power anything like the induction cooktop that is 1200W.  I found that most of my electric cookware is at least 600W...so...not useful, not helpful for making hot food without power.  This battery, along with three other batteries gives me a few hours of power without relying on the grid at all.

title: I bought this to bring new life to my old car
text: I have a Toyota Camry - an older model - that is paid for and runs like new.  Why have a car payment when I have a zippy little car that works better than many cars people are still paying off!  But she is older and looks a bit drab.  This film was used on the interior - around the PRNDL stick, the arm rest and the radio section - so the center between the driver and passenger seats.  An area that I see the moment I open the door.  The color shift of this film is just my color combination and applying it was not too hard.  I did bring my craft heat gun out to the car and used it to assist the vinyl in molding to the car's plastic pieces more easily.  It wasn't like the easiest thing I've ever done, but it certainly was not the hardest!  When it was adhered, I left the windows slightly cracked and made sure the car was in shade so the sun didn't cook the interior while the vinyl was...setting?  Whatever, I know it needed a few hours before I checked to see if every corner/side adhered properly and if not, I was prepared to use a drop of super glue to get it solidly affixed.  Thankfully, when I checked it in about 3 hours, the film was firmly stuck to the center console pieces and man, it looks good!

title: I got this with the hopes it would work when I borrowed my nephew's truck
text: He actually has two trucks - a smaller one and then one of those monster trucks...well, maybe it isn't a real monster truck, but I have to hang onto the handle inside the truck just to get up into it and it really helps if someone is behind giving me a boost!  Anyway, his smaller, regular truck would be good for a camping trip I had planned and he was okay with it.  I had gotten this tent and thought, with the blow up mattress and sleeping bag, I'd be good.  I have a nice cooler, a portable charcoal grill and lots of other camping stuff for a night or two away from home.  This tent did fit the bed of his truck...sort of.  Not really sure why anyone would narrow the front section so that it doesn't fit the bed properly.  That just seemed odd...like whoever designed this didn't actually test out the original, completed design to be sure it fit a truck bed.  Any truck bed.  I have an SUV tent that I can't use right now because my SUV died an untimely death, but I had used it before the SUV's death and that tent fit as it should, was reasonably comfortable and what's interesting, actually was made to fit MANY SUVs from Dodge to Suzuki, my SUV tent was designed properly.  That's the real point here - design and quality control seemed to be less important than getting it out on the market.

title: This has been helpful with my first solar/battery set up
text: I am learning how to set up a permanent solar system to provide portable power.  I have four 12V Lithium batteries that I connect to 2-200W solar panels and in putting it together, I like being able to actually see the charge level and this has helped me.  I am waiting for a battery minder, so this may be replaced as soon as I get the battery minder, but as I said, I'm learning how to set up a solar power system that I can take with me in my RV that will power everything when off grid.  I have updated/renovated an older RV so having propane for hot water and cooking reduces the electric load and so far, I think what I have is a good start, however, I'm pretty sure I'll be adding 2 more 200W panels and a few more batteries.  I do have a 3000W inverter so that should handle the loads in the RV.  Anyway, this charger allows me to charge up the battery(ies), but also to monitor what load each battery is carrying before I hook them up (via the inverter) to a power tool or other kitchen appliance.  Excellent to have on hand!

title: I mentioned in another review my battery bank
text: This is also a battery included in my first-ever stab at a solar power energy system for my own use.  See, I have a power station which was around $300 and I didn't realize until after I got it that it's max output was 300watts.  Now, if you go into your kitchen and look at, say, an electric kettle, you'll find it runs from probably 600watts to possibly 1200watts depending.  That means the $300 power station can't EVEN run that kettle!  So, I have 2-12V-200watt solar panels wired together and attached to a bank of four 12V Lithium batteries (including this one) with a battery tender so I can monitor their charge level as well as a 2000watt inverter.  With my little set up, I CAN run that electric kettle and mine (at 600watts) doesn't run the batteries down too much when producing boiling water for a cup of tea.  The point is that this battery (and its "brothers") are teaching me about creating a more permanent and powerful solar set up so I won't be without power should a weather or other unforeseen event occur.  Nice, smaller, lightweight battery to start with!

title: I am actually experimenting with my first solar set up
text: I have a pair of 12V, 200watt solar panels joined together and attached to this battery plus three other 12V Lithium batteries.  Granted, the Amp Hours (10) on this battery (and the others I have are similar) is not high, I am experimenting with building more of an emergency system that works better than the $300 power stations that are being sold.  The reason is the watts those power stations are rated at - not one typical appliance in your home aside from say, a laptop, could be powered with a $300 power station as most are rated at 300watts or less.  I even bought a small electric pot thinking I could use a power station with it to heat water, soup, etc. but then realized it is a 600watt electric pot!  So, back to the batteries here, I hooked up my solar panels and a 30amp battery tender so I could see how fast I sucked the juice from the batteries when I used a 12V, 2000amp inverter to plug in my electric pot.  Considering the pot is only 600watts, it really didn't seem to suck too much power from the batteries before my soup was hot, so for my first test, this (and the other Lithium batteries) battery are helping me to figure out and refine my own emergency power on a budget.

title: Using this along with 3 other 12V Lithium batteries in a solar set up
text: I have a couple of the smaller, yet expensive all the same, power banks and to an extent, they are helpful, but even the most powerful of those can't power a small kitchen appliance!  600W is almost minimum for an appliance - I have an electric pot that I had hoped to use with one of these power banks and while the banks have plugs on the side, as soon as I plugged in this small pot, they refused to work!  So I did invest in a couple of solar panels, this battery (and 3 others), a battery tender and a 2000W inverter.  NOW, I can actually plug in the pot to the inverter and it heats up.  This battery works great in tandem with the 3 others as a way to store solar energy to be used later.  This battery is light weight compared to other types of batteries and while I may not be an expert, I believe this is a very safe battery to use in a solar (or any other) set up.

title: These are SO cute and fun in my car!
text: I do have a thing for skeleton/skull stuff and when I saw these hear/speak/see no evil guys, I just had to have them.  I opened the little scent disc packets, slid them in the back of each one, popped on the clips and attached them to the vents left, center and right of my car's dash.  They are just so cute and funny that each time I get in my car they make me smile.  Love them!  The only thing I wish is that they had come with a choice of scents on the discs - what they came with are citrus-y which isn't bad, but I'd prefer something more floral like jasmine or rose scents.  Other than that, I just love these little guys that give my ride a unique look!

title: I have this set up at my house as an emergency power source
text: I have a couple of the (my opinion) overpriced power stations that through their wattage couldn't power much of anything like an electric kettle rated at 600w and most power stations are around 300w until you get into the thousand or more ones...so...I was able to secure a few LiFePO4 12V Lithium batteries that are tethered to each other.  I have 4-200w solar panels that charge the Lithium batteries, a battery tender so I can check on the charge level and this power inverter.  This is my first solar power set up and while it may be somewhat limited, it is better than many other ways I can think of to be prepared for power issues across the grid.  This power inverter can provide power to that electric water kettle and I do have a couple of low-power electric pots so I can heat up soup and other foods.  This inverter has worked with a couple of my small fans as well.  I mean, until I can get a fully-developed system up and running, this, for me is an adequate system when the power goes down.  This inverter is working perfectly for y needs.

title: Learning to connect a simple solar set up
text: I have a couple of deep cell batteries I've connected and a solar panel that connects to them as well as this inverter.  I am just learning how to set up a solar power source - the inverter being the "business end" of the set up.  I do have a few more pieces in the set up, but the main, essential pieces are the "collector" or solar panel, the "bank" where you save the collected power from the solar panel, meaning the batteries, and then the user-end of the set up - the inverter - where you can plug in appliances/machines that need power to run, thereby using the power from the sun you've collected and stored.  This inverter is working great in teaching me how to set up a full-size solar power set up.  It has also taught me that during a black out from bad weather or whatever, with a few batteries at full storage capacity, I can still power a few essentials until power is restored and even if it is a few days, I can replenish the batteries with the solar panels.  This inverter has taught me a lot and it works great with power tools when I need power away from a corded power source - like building a cabin where I have no grid power!

title: I have a 1999 Toyota Camry
text: My car just keeps on running - sturdy little car and it's paid for, which is what I love about it.  I mean, it gets me where I need to go and doesn't suck down gas like the bigger cars out on the road - paid for and still saving me money!  Anyway, she is an older girl like her owner and from time to time needs a good, thorough cleaning.  I did use this on the pillars between my front and back windows, I used it rather sparingly on the dash and the plastic on the doors.  The last place I wanted to try is not listed here - the sides of my tires.  I have used tire shine before and like how it makes my old car look.  This is not as shiny on tires as actual tire shine, but it works to make them look newer.  When I was younger a guy told me that tire shine isn't just for looks - that tire sides are subjected to heat and dirt and all manner of yucky stuff which dries out the rubber and can contribute to micro cracks due to the rubber getting stiff and inflexible.  Tire shine keeps the rubber a bit softer and more flexible to withstand the yuck better.  So, in the absence of having any tire shine this time around, I tried this product and think that it will serve that purpose for the moment on my tires.  The other surfaces look much better as well.  My neighbor was surprised when I said my Camry was a 1999.  She looks good with this stuff shining her up, making her look pretty!

title: Works for my needs, but that wasn't for a car!
text: I live in a mobile home - an old mobile home - with a covered porch.  Some previous owner tried to "seal" the space between the mobile home's roof and the patio roof with...duh...expanding foam!  Let me clue y'all in, expanding foam doesn't make a seal against anything on a roof!  So...this is good for the underside of cars for salt spray 'n all that, right?  I got up on my ladder, leaned as far over as possible and sprayed an even coating of this along the seam between house and porch.  Had to move my ladder to the other side of the porch and do the same.  I was able to affix a good layer of this stuff and after allowing it to cure for a day before testing it out, I got my hose, aimed it over the section of the roof where the porch is located and let the water rip.  I didn't want to waste a bunch of water, but spray enough to see if any of the water made it through this new layer of sealant.  Turned off my hose, went up on the porch and...DRY!  No drips, no moisture - woo-hoo!  I may end up getting another can to beef up the layer that's already there, but at the moment, I'm just happy to have a dry wall for once!

title: Never ever wait for an emergency to happen again
text: Not like it happens often - the last time it was my daughter with a flat tire.  She came out of the UPS facility where she was mailing a package and found the passenger rear tire was flat.  She called her boyfriend who has a bad back and then called me - her old mom.  I had this set already in my car for when something like happened to me, but hey, a mom would do anything to help her own child, right?  She wasn't too far from my house and I was there before her boyfriend showed up.  This whole case may be a bit heavy, but it wasn't all that bad pulling it out of the truck of my car and getting the jack set up on her car.  Man, it was so fast and easy I was surprised but glad at how well it lifted that section near the tire.  Why get the tire iron out when this kit comes with an impact wrench that makes getting the lug nuts off without too much trouble.  I might suggest tucking in a small can of WD-40 so if you have some stubborn lug nuts to get off, the WD-40 sprayed around the sticking one or two will make it easier.  Anyway, having done all that, I was able to put the full-size spare that my daughter elected to purchase when she bought her car.  Now she can drive for a little while before going into the tire store and getting the flat replaced.  Her boyfriend showed up after I got the second lug nut off and said he would take over...I let him, but ladies, you really need to learn how to do some car-related emergencies on your own and feel confident that when things like this happen, you are equipped to take care of them yourself.  One of the best ways to do that is to get this kit.  Learn how to use it at home, if you must, but be sure it is in your car for that emergency that may come tomorrow or maybe never happen...but just in case you will be prepared!

title: I have an old Toyota Camry
text: But it looks amazing for its age.  A 1999 that is mechanically sound, is paid for and not a bad little car to drive.  Why should I get another car and have to pay for it every month?  I pulled out my pressure washer, added on the foam gun and got my car really clean before testing this product.  While the car was still wet, I sprayed this ceramic coating on my car and then followed the directions to wash it off.  Like I said, my car looks darn good for its age and now the water just rolls off it and I'm hoping that means the dusty wind can't deposit more grit on my car with this coating, but I'll have to wait a while to check on how that works out.  For now, it is clean and shiny and repels water which is great!

title: I keep this set in my car
text: Have you ever been to a flea market and found that great table (or chair or chest of drawers...) you really want but once you get it to your car and realize it's not gonna work...the newly-bought item can't fit inside your vehicle and if you load it in the truck, it's going to need something to tie it down?  That is exactly why I have these in my car!  I don't have an SUV or a truck but I can fit a decent sized chair or table in my car's trunk; however, I need something to hold it in place and keep the truck from banging open or closed on my new find.  Bungees are great for this and having them ready and waiting in this bag is perfect!

title: Works great on my small car
text: I had to, for the first time, put on my car's doughnut after one of my tires must have picked up a nail, brad or whatever on the road.  I was lucky that it didn't blow, but when I stopped at the post office, I came out and found the tire had gone flat.  The tire place wasn't too far away so I got this jack out and it quickly raised my little sedan enough to remove the flat tire and get the doughnut put on.  This has replaced the flimsy hand crank jack that came with my car and while it is larger, it fits in a corner of my trunk along with some other emergency things I keep with my car - a couple of jugs of water just in case the the radiator develops a leak (had that happen to an older car), a quart of oil, hazard cones and an electric jumper cables.  Always better to be prepared than stuck waiting for someone to come help you when you can help yourself, right?  So, because of this jack, I was able to get on my way within about 20 minutes, drive to the tire store and while I wasn't expecting to have to buy a tire, at least my car was fixed up within about 45 minutes.  Had I not been able to change out the flat to doughnut (or had the really awful jack that came with the car), the time I spent that day would have been much, much longer dealing with a flat tire.  This jack is a bit heavy, but man, does it do what I need it to do and quickly!

title: I've had these before, but forgot to take them out of my old car when I sold it
text: I kept them in the car - just as these are now in my new car - because sometimes I take my car to a quick drive through car wash and I would rather stop after coming out and dry my car than to let any streaks with hard water scale form if it dries on its own.  These are great - I "slap" them against the car flat, slide it along to soak up the water, and then ring it "dry" so I can slap it against the surface again.  We need tools that work well for whatever we are doing and these chamois cloths are a great tool to keep your car looking its best after a home or drive through wash.

title: I have used both the accordion and the twist/pop open style shade
text: I actually like the accordion expect for the fact that it can't be made small enough to store easily in a car.  The twist/pop time is smaller, but man, I have wrestled with those things and considering the size when open, they are crazy-big and hard to control when you are inside the car, trying to either put them up or take them down.  You almost have to get out of the car to do one or the other (pop to put up or twist to take down).  This is my first time trying the "umbrella" style and I am happy - much happier than with the other two styles - with it so far.  I like that it is small enough to store in the center arm rest compartment when not in use.  That, in itself, makes it the best of the sun shades I've used so far.  Considering I live in a very hot, sunny climate during the summer months, I would NEVER park a car without having a shade up in the window - not if I wanted to sit down in the car seat when wearing shorts!!!  Plus I have seen cars that the dash suffered from too much sun over its lifetime - cracking, splitting, peeling away...I have an older car that most folks who look at it and find out it's a 1999 are surprised - it looks and runs like a much newer car.  The key is in taking care of it both inside and out and having a good sunshade like this one is made for the windshield, it goes further than you would think to extend the life of a car's interior.

title: I have a fairly old car
text: If I had enough money to purchase a new car outright, I might just do it, but in the meantime, I have an older Toyota Camry that has over 200K miles on it and keeps on going and, of course, it is paid for.  Never underestimate that fine feeling of NOT having to pay a monthly car payment!  Anyway, because my car is fairly old, I have an "emergency kit" in my car.  I have a couple of bottles of water should the radiator overheat, I have two bottles of oil with a funnel and plenty of paper towels.  I also have an air jack (looks like a cylindrical balloon inflated with air) and a small air compressor to use with the air jack or to inflate a tire.  Now with this jump starter, I think my car's emergency kit is fairly well-rounded.  I mean, we can't plan for everything that might go wrong when we are out on the road, but having the basics like in my car kit gives me peace of mind that I won't just be stuck waiting for someone to come help me.  BTW, I also have a small emergency kit in my car for ME - water, crackers, a blanket, a candle and waxed matches.  I keep a small power pack charged up in my car as well - no horror movie, cell phone is dying when I'm on a road far from home!  But back to this jump-starter - my daughter's boyfriend had one similar to this and actually used it on his car one day when it wouldn't start.  I haven't had to use this one yet, but I am confident that when I need it, it will get juice to the battery and my car will start.

title: Working great on my older car
text: I don't know how long the wiper set had been on my old car.  I bought it very well used a couple of years ago and because I don't drive very often, it has been a good older car for me.  Starts right up and while I don't go very far in it, it has been very reliable.  However, recently when trying to clean the windshield I could tell from the smeary streaking that the wipers needed replacing.  These were easy to put on and now when I clear the windshield, it's CLEAR!  Nothing like a new pair of windshield wipers to boost my confidence while driving - knowing that if it begins raining, these wipers will allow me to see unimpeded.

title: I have an older car
text: Wish I could afford a new car, but if I must keep up an older car, I can still make it look better than most people's newer cars!  About once a month I will clean my car - throw away any trash that may be in the car, vacuum the seats and carpets, wash the windows inside and out, wash the car and then protect surfaces.  I do scrub my wheels - the hubcaps so they are clean. Using this product for the first time (after I added wax to the car body), I sprayed a bit on the tires and wiped the product around the clean tires to make them look nearly new.  I then used a clean, barely damp cloth, sprayed this product on the cloth and wiped down my dashboard.  Like my tires, the dashboard looks almost new.  If someone were to look at my car today, they would be surprised to find it is a 1999 considering how good it looks.  It pays to take care of your car and this product makes it look GOOD!

title: Nice portable refrigerator or freezer
text: I'm giving it four stars because I have another portable similar to this one and it actually has two different compartments that allows me to have both refrigerated and frozen items in the same portable.  This one is smaller and probably the reason why it's an either/or portable.  Not that my other one is as big as a dorm size refrigerator/freezer, but I would liken it to that type of unit.  This one is much smaller than that - I shouldn't go on about size, but when camping, it somewhat depends on what you can pack in that will stay cool/cold/frozen and for how long.  Based on what I've experimented with this portable, it does cool down really fast - that's great!  Okay, takes a bit longer to get to frozen temps, but that's to be expected.  As for what it fit, I put 6 cans of soda, a sealed tub of ready-made egg salad, a small loaf of bread, another tub of potato salad and last, a tub of sliced fruit.  Now I did use square and rectangular sealed plastic containers and really packed them full, but what I put in this portable refrigerator was enough for some friends and I to spend several hours by the lake after being cooped up for a year with COVID.  We are all older and have been vaccinated, so our "party" was spending a nice day at the lake, outside, being with people and having a good time - and having cold drinks and food packed in this portable refrigerator made the day much more pleasant.

title: I am an older lady on a fixed income living alone
text: I try my best to be able to do for myself and having emergency car items like this battery jumper makes it so much easier on me and gives a peace of mind to driving.  I also have an older car so having this does make my life easier when I am out and about.  I believe in having an emergency box in my car - this jumper is in it, obviously!  I have a tire pump, a liter of water for the radiator, an unopened bottle of oil and a few other things.  I would whole-heartedly recommend having this battery jumper in your car should you come out either at home or in some parking lot and find your car doesn't want to start.  Instead of feeling powerless, you will have a way to get yourself on the road without having to trust in strangers to help you!

title: Great to start off my camping trip
text: I take a charged battery with me as I have an inverter I can attach to the battery to power a few things while camping.  I also have a solar panel that, while I'm out will keep the battery's charge up as well.  So when I have a camping trip planned, I plug in one of these battery chargers and wait for the solid green light on the front to tell me that it's fully-charged the battery.  I'm just not into primitive camping and having the ability to plug in a few things when I'm camping is a great relief to me.  This pair of trickle battery chargers make it easier to get ready for my camping travels.

title: Great for drying my clean car
text: I have an older car, but there's no reason why I wouldn't keep it looking as good as I possibly can, right?  I do clean both inside and outside about once a month or so.  Drying the car off, I also have a buffer so I can wax the finish as well.  The blue towels I've used before - they are great for getting the most water off the car's surface, getting it dry almost immediately.  That's important if you are going to wax the car, so I can appreciate having these towels in with my car cleaning caddy for the couple of hours it takes to make my car pretty again.  Worth adding to your own car cleaning set if you, too, like having a nice-looking car!

title: Glad to have this product
text: I mix it up by the soda bottle - the liter size.  I've marked on the bottle how much of this concentrate to add and another line for the amount of water.  Makes it easy for me to fill my car's windshield wiper fluid.  I have a couple of used soda bottles filled so that I always have some made up.  This stuff works just fine and the price is excellent for how much I get.

title: Much, much better than the other one I had
text: The other roof cargo carrier seemed like a fairly decent one, but in the end, it was way too heavy for me to put on the car myself (some type of faux leather that was very heavy vinyl) and even trying to tighten it up using the roof racks on my SUV, I could NOT get it to tighten properly.  I had to get my next door neighbor guy who was over 6 feet tall to tighten up the straps and even he had trouble!  This one was a breeze by comparison.  Now, understand that I am an older lady just over 5 feet tall, so tightening straps to the roof rack requires a step ladder, but I also needed a step ladder to add items to the carrier.  That's a little bit of a problem since you can't actually secure a soft-sided carrier to the roof of your SUV unless you already have your stuff packed in it.  So...that's a little glitch in the design of these soft-sided roof carriers - add all your stuff before you zip it closed and then tighten the straps down on the roof racks.  This one, the straps tightened down properly.  It works, but has it's own set of issues that you must understand in order to use it.

title: Nice set of cleaning brushes
text: I have used sponges for the most part on the interior (and exterior) of the car and had okay results - generally better results on the exterior of my car than the interior.  These brushes allow me to get into more crevasses like around the vents than I could with sponges.  Lightly spraying the brush with a bit of cleaner helped me to get the interior looking good in very short order.  I am very happy with these brushes to keep my old car looking good!

title: The last step for an exterior "clean" on your car
text: After washing and waxing the car, after cleaning the wheels so the aluminum shines, the last part of the exterior "cleaning" of my car is adding the tire shine.  This product works great - the tires shine and make your car, regardless of age, look new.  I mean, once you have washed and waxed the car and cleaned the rims so they shine, if you DON'T use this product, your car is going to look old no matter how new your tires are because the tires will be dull and make the car look older than it is.  Shine up your car's tires with this product, stand back and take a look at your car.  Betcha you'll love your car again just like the day you first brought it home!  This product is fast and easy to use and the results are fantastic - great stuff!

title: This works great!
text: I have always taken care of my cars by washing, waxing and cleaning the wheels so they look good.  This spray cleans fast - I also use a large soft brush for the majority of the wheels and use a small brush for crevasses, but didn't need to use them as much with this cleaner.  I will definitely purchase this again to keep my wheels looking bright and clean!

title: I have been a bucket suds person most of my life
text: And then I moved.  The area I live in, dust and sand is always in the wind and being deposited on my car - they even talked about the Saharan sand this past week!  So working with this foam gun made my car washing time a bit easier.  I have always done a quarter of the car at a time since using a bucket of suds takes longer to apply and in the heat of summer, you really don't want the suds to dry on the car.  This foam gun allows me to suds-up that same amount of the car, then switch quickly to water and clean it off so that in walking around my car, it took me about 20 minutes.  I have had a buffer for quite a long time since waxing always takes longer, so this foam gun cut my washing/waxing time altogether by about a half hour.  That's a big deal when standing in 90 degree heat!  Glad to have it and will be using again soon...after then next coating of Saharan sand on my car...

title: For emergency use?
text: I have an emergency, portable power generator - a small one - that seems similar to this one other than it doesn't need to plug into the car's cigarette lighter to be used.  I do think having both this one and my little power generator in the car for emergencies (or for camping trips) is a good thing, especially if you have a portable solar panel that can charge up items as well.  Don't want to drain your car's battery!  Other than that, this is a good little one with enough outlets.

title: I was hoping this would be good
text: It's not terrible, but I was hoping this would be the good thing for me to clean the inside windshields without turning myself into a pretzel trying to get to the corners.  The cleaning tool is not all that sturdy-feeling in the hand and the covers don't seem to clean well.  I ended up taking an older damp-mop (washable) cover, cutting it in two and adding some elastic to hold it on this tool.  At least the older mop head actually cleans well. So as far as working well as it came to me, no - the cloth on it is not useful and the tool itself requires (at least to me) a light hand in using it so you don't damage the handle.  The bottom line is did it clean my windows - yes, but only with some intervention (using an old mop head) on my part; hence the 3 stars.

title: The brush by itself is great
text: Based on how I would normally use this, I wouldn't keep it attached to the hose when washing the car.  The brush is excellent for both scrubbing the car clean with liquid soap and then spraying water on the car and scrubbing the car again with this brush to get all the grime off.  I also live in a mobile home in an area where dirt cakes just about everything regularly so cleaning the sides of my home keep it looking better (considering it's older).  Being able to add all the pole sections to this brush will allow me to scrub the sides of my house without having to get up on a ladder.  Nice brush - just not great to be hooked up to a garden hose in my own opinion - but as a brush, it cleans wonderfully.

title: My current old car purchase...
text: I just purchased a 1999 small sedan that had no tinting on any window, so for the time being, I am using these to adhere to the windows and keep the interior of the car cooler.  I did purchase a windshield cover, but for the side windows I have used these when I park my car at work out in a large parking lot where the sun beats down on it while I'm working.  That's Texas heat, so any way to keep the sun out of my car is important!  These adhere easy and area also easy to take off.  Dark enough to keep the sun off the seats and the interior of the car, when I get off work, it's more pleasant getting into the car.  Hot but the upholstery isn't burning hot!

title: Easy to use and seems to be working
text: I am easy on carpet and upholstery in my car, but I just bought a "gently used" car and wanted to make sure this car's mats and seats were protected so that can keep it's interior as clean as my other car.  Hard to give a great rating when you just put the protector on since it takes a while to know whether or not it is working, but it appears to be doing what it's supposed to!

title: Not the easiest thing to install, but take it easy and it will work for you
text: I recently bought an older car that none of the windows has tint applied.  I downloaded and watched at least 3 different videos on how to install window film and found that it is similar to the window clings I used on my house for a few windows (bathroom and front/back door) - using water with a bit of liquid soap mixed in, squeegee-ing the bubbles out, etc.  The difference between the house windows and these for the car would be the more exacting nature of cutting/installing the film.  It isn't impossible - it just takes some care and consideration.  Have a heat gun or a hair dryer than can blow fairly warm air along with a sharp exacto knife (be careful using it around your windows) or other sharp cutting instrument and a few different squeegees and to facilitate everything - a sprayer with water/liquid soap to use with the cling both in cutting and in final placement.  I used this film on the back windows since this is 35% tint.  Most states don't have laws regarding the back windows and the percentage of tint used - front windows are a different matter - so using this film on the back windows in most states is not a problem.  Be sure to check the laws of your state.  Tinting windows does help keep the sun's rays out of your car and saves the interior from damage.  If you feel you have the patience to follow the videos you can find online to install the tint correctly, it is worth it!

title: Excellent clings
text: I don't have a baby, but I do have a car without tint on the windows and I do like having these clings to cover a large portion of the windows.  I park in a large parking lot at work and I do use a window shade on my car's front window, but with the untinted side windows, lots of sunshine is flooding into the car.  With these clings, I can block at least a decent amount of sunlight from the car's interior until I can afford to get the windows tinted.  The clings are so easy to use - just place the smooth, plastic-y sides against the glass, lightly press on the cling to get the cling to adhere and it sticks just that easy.  If you do have children that have complained about the sun in their eyes when sitting in the back seat, these clings are perfect for making them more comfortable while driving.

title: I had one like this for my suv
text: I recently purchased a smaller sedan and the one that I used in the suv that is similar in style is way too big for the sedan's window.  The suv shade is a stowable type that bends around and stores just like this one.  I had used that one for several years and was very proficient at closing it, so for me, this folds easily.  My only suggestion is for those who have trouble, locate the elastic band, hook one hand through it, and then grab opposite corners of the shade and twist in opposite directions to collapse it.  With the elastic band wrapped on your one hand, slip the elastic around the collapsed shade and it's closed!  Anyway, this one fits the sedan as they are not connected and can overlap however much is needed to fit the car window.  I'm happy because I use shades regularly to not only keep the interior cooler when the sun is shining, but to help keep the dash, the seats and other interior areas from the brutal effects of the sun day in and day out.  This shade is my favorite style because it does collapse to a small (maybe a foot across) size and yet pops up to a incredibly large pair of shades that can literally cover any car window from small to large.

title: Everyone has a preference
text: For those who try to keep their car in good running order by using a gasoline additive, everyone seems to have their own preference.  Mine happens to be Seafoam.  The reason is that I have owned a few decent cars in my day and the first time I purchased a can of Seafoam to add to a tank of gas, it was immediately clear that the car was running better than it had prior to the Seafoam being added to a tank of gas.  I used it in an old S-10 that ran and ran and ran - the engine turned over and ran strong for years.  I used it in a Grand Prix GTP with a high performance engine and that car ran smooth and strong for several years.  I used it in a Lincoln Mark VIII again, with a high performance engine in it when the car was quite old and it ran like a top.  Once a month (or so), add a can of Seafoam to a tank of gas in your car and then let it work - you'll car will run that much better for you!  At least that's my opinion on Seafoam...as I stated, people swear by their own personal preference and Seafoam is mine!

title: Sometimes you have to see the proof for yourself
text: I have used Armor All products on my car for several years, but this is the first time I've used this product on my car.  Normally I wash my car, dry it and add wax, let it dry and then rub it to get the shine.  This product does it all, giving me a shiny car with very little trouble.  Now, I still spend time to get my tires looking nice and black, but once done, my car looks better than any car wash company could do, but then, it's just a bit of money to them...to me, it's MY car!  Try this product and be proud of your ride, too!

title: I have recently built an "emergency kit" for my car
text: I have a small kit in the car for me - bottled water, candle, a blanket, hand crank radio and some snacks.  But we all experience issues out on the road with our cars and those can be the most frustrating, lonely, scary times because we are usually not anywhere near family or friends who might be able to help and even if we can phone one of them or a car service to come out, we are stranded waiting by the side of the road.  Talk about feeling vulnerable, right?  So, I have a kit with a jug of water (radiator overheats), disposable spout and quart of oil (if the oil light comes on), I have an emergency tire inflater and if the tire doesn't hold the air, an easy to use hydraulic jack so I can put the doughnut on to get me to a tire place.  So that doesn't cover every emergency, but with this jump starter, I think I've finally added the last really important thing to my car kit.  Y'know, when you go out to the store, come back to your car and find it won't start...this is what I needed so I didn't have to ask some poor soul to help me.  Just use this to jump start my car, run to the auto store and have them check my battery to ensure it's okay or drop in a new one so I don't have my car go dead on me again.  Moms, dads and kids - I would highly recommend making up a car kit whether you have a 2002 or 2020 car - can't hurt to be prepared and having this jump starter is a great way to begin building your emergency car care kit!

title: So much better than the included jack
text: I've used a few jacks in my day and at one time I had a wonderful hydraulic jack that was heavy as sin, but boy did it work.  Here is a smaller, lighter version of my old hydraulic jack and I couldn't be happier with it.  Don't get me wrong, it isn't a lightweight, but I can pick it up and it works great for my smaller SUV.  I have it in my car, in my emergency box which has flares, disposable oil filters, a can of oil, a bottle of water, a portable tire pump and a few other items.  Best to be prepared than stranded waiting on others to come help you and with this jack, if my tire was blown, I'd have little trouble jacking up the car with this jack and take the ruined tire off.

title: I have a tool kit in my car
text: And this is a part of that tool kit.  I am very impressed with this tire inflator, not just because it works well, but because it does not require an exterior power source while inflating a tire.  That's a huge deal being able to simply walk to whichever tire is low and pump it up without fighting with a cord even if it is just plugged into the cigarette lighter.  Of course, it can do more than car or bike tires.  Balls and balloons can be inflated as well.  A versatile tool that is packed in my car tool kit next to disposable oil funnels, a container of oil, hazard flashers and a few other items that make it easier on me should I have an emergency out on the road.

title: Tried another cover that just refused to fit
text: I made sure - my SUV's steering wheel is 15 inch and that's what I requested.  The other cover I tried everything to get it to slip over the wheel and finally threw it in the back seat in frustration.  This cover; however, seemed to be a bit thinner and maybe had a bit more give to it as I had no trouble putting it on my car's steering wheel.  I like it and it helps me with a comfortable grip while driving.  Good product!

title: Mine was a "split" from a "star"
text: It worked well enough - my windshield had a "star" impact point, but from either side, a split horizontally had extended about 6 inches.  The good thing is that the star and split were very, very low on the windshield (about 3 inches above the dashboard almost dead center between driver and passenger sides).  I had to take a step stool out to give me the height to reach across and work the repair of the star and splits.  I can barely see it now so it should be good for a while until I can save up enough money to get the entire windshield replaced.

title: I haven't yet had a chance to use this but...
text: I moved back to Texas recently where things like hail come out of a clear blue sky when tornado tails are dipping in and out of swirling clouds and I've seen my fair share of hail dents from when I lived here before.  I thought it a good idea to have this kit so I could deal with the small dents soon after they occur and mitigate any residual paint damage.  I've seen these kits work before so believe this will work great when I need it.

title: I don't really have a good place in the front seat for a trash bag
text: These solved that problem - hanging them on the passenger's front seat headrest gives me a place to put trash that is easy for me to get to.  Very useful for keeping my SUV a bit neater and cleaner on the inside!

title: Sadly, it does not fit my polisher
text: I am going to see if a friend of mine who works on cars can use this as I'm not spending more money just to get this to work.  Manufacturer needs to list polishers this fits and/or offer an adapter that could make it usable for those whose polisher it does not fit.  I don't work on tons of cars so my tools are limited - guys who work on their own and other folks' cars usually have a much more diverse set of tools and might find this useful...

title: I used to have some cool cars...
text: Back in the day when I made decent money and was young and full of myself!  Yep, long, low and lean, I loved speed and cars that looked like land sharks.  Instead of paying others to clean my babies, I would wash them, scrub the tires and rims, use chrome shine and tire shine, and of course Armor-all on the dash and much of the plastics inside the car.  I never had special brushes - I used old toothbrushes and beat up paint brushes.  Now I drive an SUV and while I'm not as finicky with it as I was with the Porsche 928 I had, I still like to keep it clean and neat.  This set of brushes allows me to get into all the vents and other odd little nooks and crannies so that I can keep my later in life car looking nearly as good as the faster cars of my youth!

title: One star off because I'm short and can only reach so far!
text: So okay, it's not the squeegee's fault that I'm short and can't reach the middle of the window without some elevation, but it might have been kinda cool if they'd included a removable handle that could add maybe two-three inches of "reach" to get to the center of the windshield for me and other short folks.  Otherwise, it works well to remove water and/or window cleaner from  the windshield.

title: I haven't been stopped and asked for license and registration...
text: Not ever!  But I have this holder in my SUV's glove compartment with the registration and current insurance information so that if I am ever stopped, it is much easier to provide the required/requested documentation.  Even if I never get asked that question, having the registration and insurance documents in a neat holder makes it easier on me when renewing plates and whatnot.

title: I have put together a small container of useful items to keep in my car
text: These are one of those things.  I have a container of oil, an emergency tire pump and a few other things including these disposable funnels.  They don't take up any room and should my oil light come on at some odd time when I happen to be out and about, I don't have to worry - I have a disposable funnel and a quart of oil to get me back on the road.  At least long enough to check why my oil was so low.  As I mentioned, I do have a small container with items that will let me get down the road and I would definitely recommend anyone who has long commutes or just spends a lot of time driving, to get an emergency kit of their own made up - these disposable funnels would be one of the things I'd recommend being in there!

title: This sun shade works wonderfully - so much better than the last one I tried
text: Last one supposedly allowed you to work the window pane, but the silly thing was too small for my SUV's windows!  This one fit much better and since it is magnetic, it's very easy to put on and take off should you need to.  Works well on my Nissan's window, but of course, cars and SUVs are all different - measure your window to see if it fits your own vehicle.

title: I am so frustrated...
text: I checked the size of my steering wheel in my Nissan Murano to ensure it was the correct size for this steering wheel cover.  Received it, took it to my car and...it is sitting on the floor of my back seat.  I have done what the instructions said, even used a long-handled screwdriver to leverage the cover on and no luck.  It kept popping off on one side or another as soon as I'd get it settled on another section.  This is not my first steering wheel cover so it's not like I haven't tried traditional and alternate methods to get a wheel cover on.  I'm sure it would be a nice cover had I been able to get it settled on my car's steering wheel.

title: This is how you clean a car!
text: I have a battery powered drill so this works well for me - having the polishing/buffing pads that I can clean my car with is great - makes my car look cleaner and better than trying to do it by hand.  I used to have an actual buffing machine but somewhere along the way, it got lost.  These pads more than make up for the buffing machine and helping me keep my car in good shape!

title: This is an okay drying towl
text: I prefer the absorber towels that you can twist to get almost all of the water out of them and keep using them to dry the car.  Not to say this is a bad towel - it isn't.  But it can't be wrung out nearly dry like the absorber type of towel and when you are trying to dry your car, time can be the most important thing.  You don't want streaky marks from left over water drying on your car, right?  So, I guess if I were to suggest anything - get two or more of these if you prefer this type of towel.

title: Once you wash your car, do you stop there?
text: I don't have the car I want at the present time, but in the past I have had several cars that I loved dearly - fast cars, long, low, sleek and could fly down the road.  I took pride in those cars and instead of paying someone else to wash them, I took car of them myself.  I may not be as great at it as a professional detailer, but I can pretty much match what a detailer does - clean and vacuum the inside of my car, clean the inside of my windows and all the plastic (dashboard) and interior chrome and then put a protective coating on it to keep the inside neater for a longer time.  Then the outside of the car, shampooing and scrubbing the wheels and last, a protective coat on the chrome hubcabs, the tire slick to make the tires shine and a gloss shine for the body.  That's where this ceramic refresh comes in - the car is now clean and dry - adding this high gloss coating keeps the clearcoat and paint in shape longer.  I mean if you've ever seen the clearcoat/paint peeling off a vehicle, you can understand what I'm saying here.  It doesn't take that long to do a good job on your car on a nice Saturday morning, for instance and it lasts longer than you think!

title: Cars get dirty, wheels get grungy!
text: Considering your wheels are what carries your car around in all sorts of weather, it isn't surprising that they are the dirtiest part of your car (with the exception of your undercarriage which you don't see) and because of this, they need a special cleaner.  Spray this on first, let it set for a little while and THEN begin washing your car.  By the time you are down to the edges of your car's body, the wheels' grime should have dissolved with the use of this wheel cleaner.  Shampooing, spraying down the wheels should get most of it off.  Might need to use a scrub brush depending on the type of grunge (asphalt, tar, etc), but at least this cleaner will have loosened what it can.  Definitely worth the effort if you take pride in how your vehicle looks.

title: On nice days
text: I prefer washing my car myself - I do a better job than the places that charge me to do it.  Starts with a good shampoo and cleaning, right?  Of course, that's just the outside!  I do clean the inside of my car first, vacuum it out and wipe down all the plastic/chrome pieces and then put a protective coating on them to keep the inside cleaner for a longer period of time, but THEN I start the process on the outside.  Windows, car body and scrubbing the wheels - all need a good, sudsy shampoo to get the outside clean before moving on to the finishing steps (chrome shine, tire shine).  No, people that charge to do it - they don't do what I can do and yep, all starts with a good shampoo and this one works great!

title: I like having this in the car
text: I have a memory foam pad on my office chair and figured I'd try this one in my car.  Not that I drive long, long distances, but having a bit of cushy tushy comfort is well worth it even if you are just driving to the grocery store!  I imagine someone who drives 30 minutes or longer to and from work would find this to be a wonderful addition to their morning and afternoon drive!  Nice addition to my car seat!

title: Very well made portable fridge/freezer
text: My parents had the large, heavy duty coolers for camping trips but nothing like this!  For tailgating, for camping or a long road trip, this is a great portable fridge/freezer.  It can hold a great deal, but then, for me, I put it in the car before filling it up as I would have trouble lifting it full into the car.  I did put the handles on, but even with handles, it can get heavy (for me) to lift when full.  I like the touch screen - puts everything needed to maintain this mini-fridge within easy reach.  A bit on the pricey side, but well worth it when a nice cold drink is needed on a hot summer day at the campground!

title: Haven't actually used it yet, but better to be safe than sorry!
text: Sure, if need be, I could call a tow truck and hang around and wait should I get a flat tire, or I could use this kit and carefully drive myself to a tire center to get a replacement for the flat.  Considering money is often an issue for me, having the option to get myself back on the road and to a place where I can get a replacement tire - save the tow truck money for a good replacement tire!
