Great to keep in your car/SUV just in case!  I mean, I've been driving down the street and made it to work, come back out at the end of the day and found my tire is flat, having run over one of those large box brads or a big nail and didn't even feel it, the tire making it until I parked and going flat during the day.  At the time, I didn't have this kit, but that would have saved me - call the tire center, tell them I'm on my way and need a replacement tire, use this kit and get my car there without damaging a rim or costing me more for a tow...perfect!

title: I never liked the kind that a piece of metal slides out
text: I have always had one of the slide types in my car and just never liked using it.  This digital one is so much easier to use and identify how much air is needed in the tire.  I'm quite happy to throw out the old slider style and replace it with this one.  Try it - you'll be happy with it!

title: Nice inexpensive set to use and then discard
text: I have a couple of small wire brushes that were "made to last" but after a time, the wire has bent forward/down to a degree from all the use.  These brushes have good bristles on them, but they are inexpensive and the bristles don't seem to be as well attached to the handles as my old ones.  Considering their price, I can see these being used for a time and thrown away, but I guess the best part of that is, the bristles won't get bent down from use - fall out maybe...but for this price, they can be replaced easily enough.

title: Groovy!
text: For real, these have grooves in the mats to help with mud and yuck that gets tracked into your vehicle.  These fit my Nissan Murano well enough and I am happy with them.  They do need to be left out for a bit to allow that strong rubber smell to dissipate before putting them in the car, but that's the only downside I had with them and they don't de-gas a rubber scent in my SUV now.  Upcoming yucky winter weather...glad to have these so that I can keep my car's carpet in better shape!

title: I am moving and need the extra space in my car when driving cross-country
text: Movers are taking most of my stuff, but there are things that I just have to keep with me.  My SUV will hold a decent amount, but this roof top carrier will ensure I have all the room needed to take what I want with me.  I purchased this one in particular based on the reviews as well as the price.  After winter is over and I am fully settled in my new place, I will be taking some camping trips and this will come in handy for carrying extra stuff with me.  Always worth having a way to store stuff on a road trip, whether long or short!

title: Nice and stretchy!
text: For children sitting in  their parents' cars with the sun beating down - this helps shade a baby's face from too much UV rays from the sun.  It is easy to attach (and reposition to a window.

title: I gave 4-stars for light weight because these are...
text: too sturdy to be seen as light weight!  That's a good thing, but in rating for being light weight, I can't in all good conscious give 5-stars for something that is hefty.  Not that I cannot pick them up, obviously, but the point of using these is that they should be weighty in order to support the weight of a 350-500 pound off-road vehicle when loading into the back of a truck.  That is what these are made for - attach to 2x8 boards in a length that will be easiest for getting your vehicle into the bed of the truck, slide the ramps into the bed next to the vehicle, and you're good to go!  I got these because years and years ago my ex jerry-rigged a pair similar to this by getting a pair of heavy-duty hinges, cut an 8" piece off the length of wood, screw the hinge to the two pieces and voila, a pair of ramps.  This was a much better solution for me but in similar style!

title: This is HUGE, but that was the point
text: I followed the chart for buying the right one - my Nissan Murano is listed as the largest size.  So I bought the largest one and yes, it fits across my SUV's front windshield, but because it is SO big, it is somewhat difficult to manipulate.  I mean, I'm an average sized woman - 5' 4" and this screen is probably nearly as tall as me!  Getting it folded up or unfolded with the driver's door closed is a PITA!  I normally open the driver's door and pull it out to fold/unfold it and make sure I know where the elastic band is or it will pop back open (without the elastic band to hold it closed).  It does work though - just not an easy window cover at times.  I should say that the reason I bought this one in particular has to do with camping in my SUV.  I have an SUV tent, a mattress for the back of my SUV and this cover is to cover the windshield so that I can sleep without people being able to look in and see me sleeping.  I have covers for my side windows as well.  For what I bought it for, it works perfectly.  For keeping the sun out of my SUV, it also works wonderfully.  It's just takes a bit to get it unfolded or folded.

title: Happy to receive this!
text: My rear window blade on my Nissan Murano was nearly useless - the rubber was damaged so it no longer cleared the rear window.  At the moment it is raining, but the moment I can get out and change it, I'll have this one on.  Not my first rodeo in changing blades - it's an easy change and I'll be happy to have a new wiper blade in the back window!

title: Such an elegant men's watch!
text: I knew it had BMW on it, but it does not overwhelm the watch - and it is a great-looking men's watch!  The box is an excellent gift box.  If you are looking to get a watch for the man in your life, and especially if he loves cars, this is a great pick!

title: These don't work all that well on windows with vent visors
text: I really didn't think my window's vent visors would cause such an issue with these, but they did.  Trying to pull them over and get them tight against the windows is nearly impossible.  Of course, these aren't customized to specific cars and they aren't expensive, so I guess it's on me not to expect too much, right?

title: Works, but not without some pain!
text: Okay, so writing a review on a product that will give you smooth skin, but of course, requires ripping the hair out by the root (re: pain) is a bit difficult...first, you have to make sure the beans are not too hot when applying to your skin - don't want to burn your skin instead of removing the hair.  I waited until my daughter could try this with me - a backup to make sure I was following directions and that we both understood the process as this was my first time trying this method.  I did a test patch on the both of us to make sure it would not cause irritation.  No redness or rash appeared after 30 minutes so we both worked a strip of leg at a time.  She shaves more often than I do (being retired and not wearing dresses as I used to), so this was a great test of length and removal.  It did appear that my leg hair came off easier (being longer and perhaps more trapped in the wax) than did spots on my daughter's leg.  All in all, these wax beans work fine so long as you follow the instructions, especially on heating the beans.  To keep your legs (and other areas) hair-free longer, these wax beans are worth it.  Oh, and the four-stars is just because it does hurt to pull the hair out with the wax!

title: Didn't "install" this...

Using oars can get me around, but when I get tired of rowing, I like being able to stow the oars, attach the battery to the trolling motor so I can spend more time out on the lake.  Nothing nicer than spending peaceful time on the lake, right?  I also have a solar panel attached to the battery so that if I use the motor too long, the battery won't be totally drained and strand me out in the lake at the end of the day.  For what I use this battery tray for, it works great - the strap holds the battery in place and it is sturdy for my use.

title: So excited to use these!
text:

I am quite happy with how they work - the slats make them easy to pick up, even for a small woman, and slide in next to whatever has been loaded and unfolding them, setting them up to load or unload is also easy. It would be great if they were lighter-weight, but considering they are rated to hold some serious weight on each rail, that's not really an issue at all. If you are moving larger, heavier items in and out of the back of your truck, SUV or minivan, this pair of ramps will help you get the job done with less muscle strain and damage to whatever is being loaded.

Update: my neighbor helped me load my moped into my SUV using one of the rails and then I let him borrow them so he could load his nephew's ATV into the back of his brother's pickup. They had been using 2x4's to get the thing in the truck. Both my neighbor and his brother were very appreciative as these rails made the job of loading the ATV so much easier. Glad I had them for me and for them!

title: Slime let me down
text: I needed to repair a rubber gasket on a rock tumbler.  After searching I decided on Slime as they are usually pretty good (love the tire sealer).  Kinda very let down.  There are 2 types of patches, and I can only guess the thicker ones are for actual tires, while the remaining are for tubes.  The tubes of cement are tiny and the directions are a complete joke.  They talk about placing the orange side down and leaving the plastic coated side up.  Well NOTHING is orange, and the directions never say to remove the plastic film.  I used up a tube and a half just for my one repair (5 patches total).  They never mention letting the cement set up or how long to let the patch dry or even adding talcum powder to the repair after it has set to keep foreign objects from sticking to it.  Also no mention of applying to a clean dry surface.  Thankfully I have made many repairs and have an understanding of what the proper method of repair is.  I pity the person who tries this for the first time with no other knowledge, as the repair is going to fail for them if they follow the directions given.  I will say there is a nice supply of small patches and the suffers are very nice as well.  I won't be purchasing this kit again and Slime has really let me down.

title: Fits the older (2008) 8kW
text: My 2008 generator started acting up last winter.  It was not running test cycles and had to be started manually when we lost power (what a pain).  This spring I worked on it to no avail and burned up the starter (ok it didn't catch fire but it was smoking).  I tried to get a service guy to come out, but they all wanted $250 just to come out to take a look (I would have paid it, but that was in addition to any repairs and parts, he gave me a phone estimate of over $500).  Yea not happening.  I got my possibly future son in law to help me remove the starter (not the easiest thing to get out).  My wife and I removed the original battery and installed the new starter and battery and gave the Genny a tune up and oil change while we were at it.  It now starts right up, does it's weekly test with no issues, and is running a lot smoother.  I'm about average when it comes to mechanical things (I can change a battery, oil, and manage minor repairs).  Swapping the starter is a pain as it is held in place (along with a spacer that falls off and into the bottom of the engine) with Allen bolts that are way too long and difficult to get out.  THere is also the throttle springs over rev limiter that have to be removed and bend out of the way, but other than that it was a straight forward swap.  Overall I'm glad I saved myself the $500 and now I'm ready for power outages.

title: not designed correctly
text: I have struggled for years with grease guns and fittings and zerks.  When I came across this "leak free" locking coupler I convinced my self that all my grease issues were solved.  Nope not even close.  First there is a major design flaw with this unit.  when you engage the lever the Jaws retracts into the body of the coupler.  When you try to place the jaws on a zerk they retract too far so unless your fittings are ultra long (like 3/4 of an inch) it is a major struggle to get the Jaws to grab (you have to depress the lever only part way and hope the Jaws grab).  Horrible.  I tried this on every fitting on my tractor, trailers  and lawnmower with the same results.  The next major issue is the diameter of the coupler.  FORGET about anything resembling a tight space.  This barely fit my tractor front loader fittings and was useless on my mower deck and wheel bearing (where I really need it the most).  I gave it 2 stars because if you do manage to get it clamped onto a fitting it does not leak.  I guess back to the drawing board for me as I will only use this on my small finger pump grease gun that I use to freshen up my trailers bearing buddies as this the only fittings this work on consistently.

title: Not good but great customer service!
text:
While I love the concept of bypassing those new stupid spill (not spill proof) cans, these just don't work the way they should. The spouts worked for the most part and I was able to use one of the new screw tops but my other can didn't work with either cap (guess I have one of those 5% that don't work?) I was able to use the spout with the original cap so I thought I had a winner. Then I went to use the spout caps on the ends. Well they don't fit (not even close) The spout caps are threaded and the spouts are not. The spouts also are a larger diameter than the caps so you can't slide the keepers over them even if the caps where to fit. Very frustrating to say the least. In typical overseas production I have a bunch of parts that don't work for anything. I did find the stopper caps (that go into the screw caps that everyone tossed out as who takes the spout out for transport?) do fit the spout ends, but there is no seal and they will pop off if the cans heat up and expand. I didn't even bother with vent plugs as my cans are all full and yup need to have them empty before you drill them. I decided to keep these as I do have one can that is nearly unusable with the "safety" spout (Yea Midwest I'm talking about your garbage system that requires 3 hands and a a monkey wrench to use) so I swap out spouts to use it to fill them then put the garbage spout back on for transport. On a side note NEVER purchase a Midwest can. The only way that company is going to learn is if we all refuse to purchase their non standard impossible to use junk. Also avoid this set as it just does not work the way it is supposed to. Oh and if your wondering why I did not return the can, well turns out you can not return a can once it has had fuel in it (so basically you do not know you have garbage until you use it and can not return it- hmmm isn't that handy)
UPDATE! The company reached out to me and offered a partial refund! They processed it quickly and included an extra $1 over the offered refund for my time. This is outstanding service! I also did find 1 can I had that these actually worked well with (surprise- it is NOT a Midwest can!) SO I salvaged 1/3 the order and got a 1/3 refund. No harm no foul. The vents they include are actually usable for the Midwest can nightmare. I installed one and now I only need 2 hands and the monkey wrench so they move up to 4 stars for some functional usability and for the amazing customer service. If they redesign the spout cap configuration, I would purchase again knowing that they stand behind their product. Well done!

title: Work well on most cars
text: These lights work well on most cars.  We had a challenge installing them on a mini van as there was not an easy way to contain the wire end (it pulled out of the socket.  The lights are nice and bright and give great night time view.  I did get some flashes as people thought I had high beams on.

title: a pain to use
text: This are a bit odd to use. The drapes over the window (like a bag) and kind of wraps around.  Didn't work great on my Jeep as the windows are more squared.  On the Subaru it worked better but was still a pain to put on and take off.  They do keep the car somewhat cooler but ours kept getting filled with air and billowing when the wind blew hard.  No way you could drive with these on and no way I would trust these to protect a baby in a hot car even for a short time.  I did try these to keep snow off the windows and they worked ok for that but did freeze to the window and we're a pain to remove.  Not as useful as I had originally hoped.

title: Great on my trailer
text: Installed these on my trailer and they work great.  Super easy to install and easy enough to wire up.  Included plugs worked perfect for my application (4 pin connector).  I used some zip ties to secure the lights just as an added assurance.  These work so much better than standard running lights.  They can also be cut to size for a more custom install if needed.  SO far completely separate proof.  No complaints.

title: nice and bright
text: I tried these out on my trailer.  They are somewhat easy to install if you have ever wired up trailer lights. I ended up rewiring the trailer to add these to the existing lights.  They come with a standard 4 pin trailer light pigtail but if you have the 7 pin plug you will have to make (or purchase) and adaptor.  The lights are nice and bright and add an additional level of safety to any vehicle.  They adhere very well and I have not had any issues with the tape letting go even in the rainy slushy garbage we have on our roads this time of year.  Do be sure to clean the area you want to stick these to as any grease or oil (or wax) will prevent them from adhering very well.  These lights work as expected with no flickering or dead spots.

title: A bit big for a mini
text: Got these for a mini Cooper countryman.  They came up as fitting this car but they are a bit large (we worked for a half hour getting this to fit right AND used a lot of safety pins underneath to assure it would stay tight).  Pretty easy to install (despite our particular needs) but do plan on spending some time to get it secured.  So far it has stayed in place and we had no trouble getting a car seat installed over this.  Seatbelt holes are well stitched and lined up for the most part (the car seat tethers did need a bit of creative maneuvering but that is more a quirk of the car).  The split back seats still work as do the headrest.  Can't compliant to much as they are cheap and can be made to work.

title: Fits perfect
text: My daughter has a 2019 Crosstrek and low and behold the door has actual frame (unlike my outback that had a frameless door).  We picked these up as they were so much more economical than other offerings.  These fit perfect and have 3m tape so I know they will stick forever (seriously I had to remove some of that 3m tape that was like 10 years old and it was a nightmare to remove it!)  These were easy to install and nearly foolproof as the Crosstrek has a very simple easy design.  These come down far enough to leave the window cracked even in pouring rain and we like them in the winter so we can leave the windows cracked to allow the wet carpet interiors do hopefully dry out and bit.  There is no extras with these (prep pads, directions, etc) but the price is about half the price so well worth it.  They shipped in a plain box but we're wrapped in a foam bag and we're undamaged and scratch free.  Love the way these look and preform.  Zero complaints.

title: Works but slow
text: For an emergency use compressor this is very handy to have.  I have several full size compressors at home and this will never even come close to replacing those but as an emergency roadside inflator this works well.  I timed it out to take a tire 17 inch tire from 25 to 32 pounds took 15 mins.  I also inflated some pool toys (these went a little quicker at about 5 mins).  Compressor is loud and vibrates pretty strongly (as all these small 12 volt ones typically do).  Make sure your car is running when using this as it will kill a battery pretty quickly.  Loved the detachable cord design (all my other ones end up getting the cords ripped out by accident) and the included inflation tools.  The case is good enough to store this and a few other emergency items in and tucks away under my trunk board (inside my spare tire).  This is a must have for anyone who drives as it could mean the difference between a minor inconvenience along the side of the road or a very expensive tow and tire repair.

title: Well made wedge
text: This is a well made window wedge.  This will work better on cars without window frames (a lot of Subarus didn't have frames).  Not easy to use on framed window and if your not super careful damage can occur (including glass breakage).  This tool is also handy for getting under panels to pry them out (like the interior light panels for my jeep).  You can also use this as a way to work frozen doors open.  The tool is most likely nylon and is very durable.  It is a little gentler on paint than a metal tool would be but again use caution.  Very handy for a do it yourselfer.

title: Nice and bright
text: This light bar is nice and bright.  Good clean white light trending towards a slight blue (ever so slight) tint.  Easy to wire up (I found a multi Port LED light switch with on off buttons so I use that).  Mounting bracket is very robust and easy to mount and adjust.  Wire is a bit light in my options but it does the job and doesn't get hot.  Do take some time in the evening to aim this light as it is pretty bright and could compromise other drivers (and possibly get you a traffic ticket if you happen to blind a police officer).  I also recommend a on off switch as in some states these off road light are illegal to use on paved roads so you will want a way to turn them off.

title: simple but effective
text: This is a simple but effective siphon.  I use it to transfered kerosene from my can into my heaters.  Works with a minimum of mess.  It does help if the can is higher than the tank (gravity speeds up the transfer)  Do be careful if there is something in the receiving tank because when you first start pumping there will be air in the tubing that will have to be evacuated and may cause bubbles or gurgles if the tube end is submerged.  Almost use caution when removing the tubing from either container as there will be some back flow from the tubing.  Also note that this is not for thicker liquids like oil as the suction just won't move the liquid.

title: A great storage solution
text: I have a Jeep Renegade and storage can be an issue with this compact Jeep.  I usually carry way more junk than I need so I tried to trim it down when I got the jeep.  This has allowed me to once again carry all those little oddities the (screwdrive set, extra bags, gloves, raincoat, hat, kleenex, papertowels, extra cell phone charger, extra sunglasses etc). without taking up the limited cargo space.  I don't carry backseat passengers often but had my granddaughter jump in the back seat after I installed this.  She is pretty small but said it really didn't take up much space as it is on the seat back and not on the floor.  I climbed back there and yes it does take up a bit of leg (knee) room but the jepp is pretty compact in the back seat in the first place so not a deal breaker.  We also put one in the wife's Forester and had the same results: a little loss of leg room but not a deal breaker and the additional organization really makes this a winner.  Super handy if you have kids (or grandkids) as this gives them a place to put all the junk they haul with them (every trip we take with them is like a freaking jungle expedition with the amount of stuff they haul).  This is super easy to install and took less than 5 mins to get all adjusted and secured.

title: Great light, no directions
text: THis is a very well made light bar.  It is very bright and is nearly bullet proof.  Mounting hardware and bracket also are well built and more than adequate for the bar.  There are ZERO  installation instructions included and there is not a on off switch.  After a lot of extra wire and a switch I got it installed.  I also wasn't thrilled with the lighter weight wire leads (14 gauge).  I used 10 gauge to wire up the switch and power leads.  Light draws less than 10 amps (thats what I have it on).  No flicker that I can detect.  Heat sink works well.  Overall I nice light bar just be aware that there is no installation instructions and no switch or extra wire.  If your familiar with wiring up 12 volt lights this is a breeze to wire.

title: Works well on a good battery
text: I tried this out on all the families car batteries (all nine of them)  All the batteries test out good to excellent.  This is super easy to use.  Just clamp it on and start up the car and take your reading.  I did test it on a bad lawn mower battery and it told me the battery was bad.  I really like having this around and it accurately diagnosed a charging problem in one of your cars (we knew there was a problem but didn't know if the battery had been affected).  Also helpfully for any 12 volt battery that you need to test.  Saves you time and guess work

title: Good quality and only a minor install hiccup
text: These fit my renegade 99%  the 2 rears were super easy no drill install.  Just unscrewed the factory screas and reuse them to do the install.  The front passenger I did use one screw in the top (predrilled the hole) and with a few taps of the hammer I was able to reuse the uncarriage push dart.  The drivers side has a slightly different configuration and the push dart still worked but had to really struggle to get the factory screw back in place.  I drilled the top hole and installed and decided to drill the second hole from the top just for some insurance.  Well there is no metal backing that spot so ita just into the pastic.  I put the crew in and didnt over tighten it so all was good.  These look great and despite the package being completly destroyed in shipping they did arrive undamaged.  My only wish is that they had the jeep logo on them.  Install took 45 mins including time to move the jeep around to avoid the mud and to turn the front wheels.

title: Works wonders and saves a lot of frustration
text: I just did a hood decal on my jeep and this kit worked wonders and made the install almost flawless.  I didnt use the sheet cutter but did use the small knife to cut out around the squirt nozzels.  The squeegees were a life save and between the felt side and the rubber side we were able to squuze out 99.99% of the bubbles (we used the wet install). I didnt have any real tight spot or corners but I did use the small squeegee tool to press down and around the sqirt holes.  This kit is a must have for all but the smallest of vinyls.

title: Second try worked better than the first
text:
I have a jeep renegade with the funky sillouette blackout around the edge. My insurance company wont do chip repair and wont approve an oem windshield so i gave this a go when I got a nice stone chip. First and foremost this is a well made kit and the suction cups stay put. Direction are clear and easy to follow. Despite my best efforts (even using a heat gun and a uv light as it was a colder cloudy day. This didnt do a lot to fill in the chip. Im going to try again when its warmer and sunny but I dont have high hopes. One other note the resin smells HORRIBLE. I slilled a little on my hands and despite washing with everything I could think of (incleding acetone, alcohol, industrial hand cleaner, kerosene) i could still smell this 2 days latter. Oh and it triggered a migraine for me so there is that. WEAR GLOVES!
Update I tied a second go and it worked much better. Still can see the chip but it is a lot less noticable. Of course the smell gave me another headache but I did wear gloves and it helped a lot.

You do want to be careful how you place this as the ratchet is strong enough to crack plastic interiors and dent steel side walls. Beam is full and no noticable halo or shadows but that also depends on a good headlight diffusor/ reflector combo.  Do be carful not to get finger (or any) oils on the chip as that can cause them to burn out (just like a halogen).  I like how these work in the rain and mist also.  They are brighter than a halogen (at least perseption eise) but dont cause other drivers to flash you.  Just a nice product all the way around

text: I got this in exchange for my honest review.  These arent the best crossbars out there.  They have a somewhat cumbersome attachment procedure that involves inserting a key to unlock the attachment screw then using a long hex wrench to tighten the mount clamp, then slippimg on the endcap and then relocking the attachment screw port and removing the key.  Then over to the otherside to repeat the procedure.  Then you need to  repeat the same procedure to center the bars.  Uggh.  These wont be coming on and off quickly thats for sure.  The clamp also locks the bar in place so adjusting is time consuming to say the least.  The bars are robust and look strong enough for the intended purpose.  You do get 2 keys so that is good but if those locks corrode up your going to have trouble using these.  I tried these out on a Chrysler townn and country mini van and they barely fit so do be aware of your vehicles rail spacing.  Directions were clear and well written and the clamps are well padded.  These are an inexpensive universal type bar that will work but are not near as nice as factory bars.  I did like that these are flat bars as some factory bars are curved and getting things like baskets to fit them can be a real challange.  I will probably move these over to my jeep and use them only with my softside luggage carrier durning the warmer weather.  I have a feeling one winter here in the notheast and the salt will have completly ruined the all important key lock.

title: OK BUT>>>>
text:
First of all this is available at a certain tool store that gets in a lot of freight from a harbor! The dollar amount you would spend is a lot less. Because this is a single bolt mount it is near impossible to generate enough torque to hold this in place. That being said it may require you weld it to your ATV. I have a Polaris Magnum with that funky offset draw bar and I have been looking for way to fabricate a bolt on offset 2" hitch reciever to no avail (YET). This is handy to have as long as your pulling in a straight line on a level or uphill surface. Go down hill or make a turn (especially to the left) and this will twist and could allow the trailer to jacknife into the atv (it happened to me- luckly no real damage other than a cut tire). THis item does have a usefullness if your good at welding (I'm not- at least not enough to try this), or have a way to frabricate a better mounting system.
UPDATE: Well I decided nothing ventured nothing gained and build an extention for this. I measure the angle and length and took a piece of 1/4" by 3" stock (what I had laying around- it probably should have been 1/2" by 4"), gound out the shape of the adaptor, and welded it on. Then I took a length of 3/4" pipe and welded that to the bottom of the extention. I drilled a hole thru the center of the extention (the middle of the pipe) and bolted the whole thing down. The pipe fits neatly into the rear hole on the Polaris Magnum towbar, and keeps the the entire unit alligned. With 2 bolts attaching the hitch adapter the entire unit is twist free and very stable. The welds were easy enough to make with a flux core wire feed, and even my poor skills (or lack there of)were able to "glue" the adapter and extention together. THis is a much better unt that actually functions.

title: Not great
text:
I used this GPS on a trip to Sardegna and Sicily. This is my second Garmin auto GPS.
This GPS showed several problems that made it perform in a poor way:
The "shortest time" route can send you on weird routes that are not short time or reasonable. We went from Alghero to Olbia and trusted the GPS. We ended spending three hours going though a winding mountain road. When we arrived, we mentioned that to a locals and they said "you went via Bosa, right"? Well, the GPS sent us via Sassari. On other occations the GPS forecasted arriving at 4:30, and after disregarding it, following road signs suddenly forecasted 4:15. This means that the obvious route wasn't the GPS route.
Traffic? Two days ago I was on a highway where there was an accident, but the GPS reported nothing.
In Europe it was common that the roads where I had to turn were so zoomed out that I had to force the zoom in manually to know which one was the right one. Also, road labels would appear just over where the road make two turns, blocking them from view.
If on a typical old town, for the GPS all roads are good when in reality some are too tight. In one ocasion we had to remove a neighbor's trash can to make the turn, while the locals were helping not to scartch the car. Also, several roundabouts were depicted as crossings, so maps need more updates.
The unit can be put in either landscape or portrait mode. You can control the brightness but not the contrast.
The user's interface is not great. To set a saved waipoint as home is far from obvious. It has "apps" for some functions. Why!? Was Garmin trying to follow a techno-fad?
Conclusion: If you use this GPS in Europe, ask the locals first, follow the road signs second and then use the GPS. It works to show you where you are, but second guess it for directions. I guess some may say that a GPS can't be perfect but you may get better routes any online service before departing.

Update:
I never got any traffic valuable traffic information with this GPS. Apparently there is another charger that has a FM receiver (sold sepparately). Whether you may get any information with the other one, well, read the feedback. The charger included with this unit is the TA20. At this point "Lifetime Traffic" looks like a joke. With this one you will be stuck in traffic for a lifetime.

title: Easy to use but takes a lot of time to dry.
text:
When this kit arrived, I realized that I made a mistake since it doesn't have actual adhesive, and "compound" is basically mix of glue and paint. I have Tear Mender and I used it to patch the tear from underneath the torn leather. When it was completely glued together and dried (in about 15 minutes total) I used compound to fill the hole and paint it. While I was trying to level the inside of it with the leather I discovered that it takes forever even for a very thin layer to cure (to dry out), so you have to be really patient and wait about 24-36 hours for it to completely dry. I even tried to blow dry it, but well :) it didn't work. Have to be patient. Plus I have a black couch, so I need black only. This kit does not have enough black for an 1" hole. I had three holes in my couch. Each of them was just a little less than 1/3" and I didn't have enough of black compound to fill the hole and to level it with the edges of the leather.
Customer Service is amaozing!!! They reached out me after reading my review and offered one more set for free to complete my couch repair. Selling single color is their work in project, so eventually they will start selling compound by single color. Overall I like it. Just be very patient due to long drying time.

text: This battery replaced my Cub Cadet zero turn mower battery. This battery is significantly smaller and lighter than traditional batteries, but it’s very powerful for it’s size; don’t let the small size fool you. It comes with one spacer block to adjust the height for an optimal fit in your battery box. I also like the terminal set-up with a choice of using them on the side or the top, whichever is better for your needs. You cannot use a conventional charger with this, so it does require a specialized charger for the lithium battery. I’m not sure about long-term performance as of yet, but I’ll update the the review with any issues. Five stars.

title: Seasonal Car Cleaners FTW!
text:
I’m a person who doesn’t care much about deep cleaning my car all that often, but I'm loving this kit! Some of it I’ll leave to my husband to apply like the tire cleaner and fully washing the car, but I am totally all about wiping down my interior with the candy cane scented solution, and the cinnamon detailer smells good for a car cleaner too! The included cleaning cloths are helpful, and each product is easy to use.

This is beyond creative to make car cleaners into a holiday-themed set with seasonal fragrances…very fun and festive, and it even makes me think of these as the car version of the coffee houses with all of the seasonal flavors (I'm rooting for a Sugar Plum cleaner next year...lol). The scents are family-friendly and everything is high quality. I recommend this for any car lover, but could also be a charming motivator for anyone who needs to clean out their car.

title: Small But Powerful

I installed it today in 30 degree weather (taking some creative measures to fit the space) and it started right up! It comes with spacer blocks to adjust the height for an optimal fit in your battery box. I also like the terminal set-up with a choice of using them on the side or the top, whichever is better for your needs. You cannot use a conventional charger with this, so it does require a specialized charger for the lithium battery. I think it's worth the money if it holds up as long as they claim. I'll update with any issues. Five stars.

title: Nice Reduction In Vibration

I did notice that it’s not as refined from a workmanship standpoint compared to my Curt hitch, which seems to be a little better quality overall, however, this one stands out in its function.  I also want to mention that it does take a little longer to remove this one and swap it for another hitch ball mount when I need to, as the tightening/loosening factor on this model takes extra time. title: Great Idea, Nice Quality, Would Prefer A Different Scent
text:
This wooden air freshener is such a great idea! It’s basically like one of those wooden ornaments I use on my Christmas tree, but it comes with a bottle of fragrance oil that you drip/soak onto the wood. The instructions caution that too much oil can potentially drip onto your car surfaces on really hot days, so I decided to only use 8 drops at the very top of the cutout to help avoid drips in the car. The scent soaks in very quickly and emits fragrance in the car very well (it's also much easier to use than my reusable car clip where I soak the felt discs). I don’t know yet how often I’ll need to add fragrance to keep it noticeable, but I have a feeling I’ll need to refresh the wood about twice a month—It’s very easy to use.

The Cool Breeze scent isn’t my favorite, but it’s still nice—It’s like a softer men’s cologne scent with a little dash of fresh beachy notes to it. I’d love to see the fragrance line expanded so I can pick out my favorites (I prefer vanilla and fruity scents). Great concept in general, but this scent is best for those who love fresh and masculine notes. Still 5 stars, because it can be used with any fragrance oil and the quality is great.

title: Very Good Quality Wiper Blades For The Price - Replaced Bosch Icons In My Cars
text:
Fall 2016 update: I've been using AERO blades for a while now, and did another comparison. On my 2010 Hyundai Sonata, 2010 Toyota Rav4, and work vehicles, these blades are still the best blades I've tried in this price point, having compared them to Bosch Icon, Rain-X Latitude, Michelin Stealth, Valeo Frameless, and Motorcraft All-Season.

These Aero All-Season blades leave the best streak-free wipe, out of any blade I've used, with no dead spots or streaks for an entire season. For an abuse test, I swapped them out on one of my older vehicles, and they are effective well past 9 months through a reasonably harsh winter. I got almost 1 year 3 months out of one set, before they eventually stopped performing well at the edges. You should replace them every 6 months, but - depending on your climate - you could probably get a full year of use from a single set. Only the Bosch Icons have lasted longer for me (1 year 6 months on a work van), but they didn't perform as good as the Aero All-Seasons did out of the box. After 3 months, to about 5 months, the Aeros and Bosch perform just as well. The Bosh Icons pull ahead just a little at around 6 ~ 7 months, but I usually replace them by then.

They are very quiet, even across dry glass, second only to the Bosch Icons. When they are brand new, I get a little skidding when trying to wipe debris off of dry glass, but it stops after one or two regular uses in rain. Once in a while, I'll get one of the 24" blades that is a little stubborn to install, but will eventually go on with a little extra force. Once installed, the blades are fairly easy to remove, but I've never had one fall off. Some of the other blades are VERY difficult to install and VERY difficult to remove (looking at you Rain-X). I like that they're secure, but I want to be able to change them without having to use a tool or excessive force in case I have to make a change away from the garage.

The AERO All-Season blades, in all of my comparison tests and extensive use, are my personal favorite for every car in my garage or work fleet. They perform the best from day one, perform well even past 9 months, are one of the quietest, are easy to replace, and are very well priced in a set.

Original Review: Well, I've used this through several rough summer and winter seasons; the Aero blades definitely perform as nicely as the Bosch Icon blades, which I liked very much and used for years. The blades perform well just as long as the Icons did, and are actually a little easier to install (the locking cover is a little less stubborn to open when uninstalling). The Icon's are a tad quieter across the windshield in side-by-side tests, but my novice ears honestly couldn't tell any difference if they weren't side-by-side. Applying a little Rain-X to the windshield pretty much neutralized all noise for up to 3 weeks of steady use, during the rainy season. For the price, I'm sticking with the Aero's in my 2010 Rav4 Limited, and 2010 Sonata.

title: Install sucks
text:
I like this step for my Super Duty. I have the factory tailgate step but sometimes it is in the way of what you are loading or unloading.

The reason I couldn't give it a 5 star rating is the install. The manufacture tells you to use a 20mm deep socket but on a Super Duty the socket won't fit over the lower bolt because it is too long. I can shallow socket over it but the cutout or side access doesn't line up to get an extension or a ratchet handle on even with a wobble extension. I don't want to grind it out to accommodate alignment so my last choice was a short swing, flex head ratchet end wrench which I have on order. Seems like their design engineers really could have planned that part better.

Update: So, I ordered my new, very expensive 21mm flex head, ratcheting end wrench, which I will likely never have use of again, and that will not work either. The head of the wrench won't clear the edge of one of the assembly bolts to fit over the bumper nut. Neither will a regular end wrench but without the flex there is no way to swing a regular wrench anyway.

I had originally hand tightened the lower bumper bolt thenbwas able to turn it another half turn or so with the deep well socket at an angle, barely contacting one side of the nut, then I ratcheted the top nut tight. Apparently those two bolts are actually a single "U" bolt. When the nuts were off of the bolts moving one loose bolt mirrored movement on the other. Perhaps tightening the top one after partially tightening the bottom will have put enough tension on the bottom one to keep it tight.

In the end I would suggest to someone buying this for a Superduty, try installing it with a regular 21mm socket if you don't already have a deep one because I don't think you would need more than a standard socket and an extension, and tighten the lower bumper bolt as far as you can before the top bumper bolt.

title: Not necessarily the right fit for a '95  - 97 Subaru
text:
Purchased this for a 1995 Subaru Legacy Wagon with split folding rear seats. The front covers went on fairly easily, although the amount of drag from installing over fabric as opposed to vinyl made it a bit chancy that I would rip them. The headrest covers (got 5, car only has 2) just did not fit. Installed one, it ripped because it was too small, and it looked so bad I decided the original fabric was in good enough shape, and a close enough match, to just do without. Strike 1. The cover for the seat portion of the rear seat went on easily enough, although if those hooks are "S" hooks, then I have to thank the manufacturer for giving me a start in learning the Chinese alphabet; actually looks more like a small Greek Delta. But, with the help of a pair of needle-nose pliers, I squished down the open leg so they would hold. I would have preferred completely separate covers for the split back, with a notch for the hinge, but they did provide zippers so that it should be fairly easy to segregate the two parts if I ever want to do so.

The fabric is pretty much what I expected, a nylon/polyester knit over a thin foam for the functional parts. If you rip it, it will run. All that having been said, the seat covers will do; they look much nicer especially in the front, which were pretty worn, torn and stained.

Now for the really good news: I was really pretty impressed with the mat quality; the pleather borders around the plush is a nice touch. Again, not necessarily a good fit: the gas door release is directly at the front left corner of the driver's seat, and the mat covers it.

Overall, a decent value for $26.

title: Really good product for a good price.
text: I have been using this fuel treatment in all my engines big and small for the past year now and believe I'm qualified to write that I feel it is one of the best fuel treatments available, and I also feel the price isn't bad considering the amount of fuel it can treat. I initially bought it for a 10 year old Explorer V8 that was stumbling and stalling at stop signs and stoplights during the warm-up cycle in cold weather. Engine diagnostic equipment couldn't provide a code that helped and mechanics told me to simply keep the fuel system clean so I started using this product. Now I've always believed in the benefits of a top oil (especially now with older engines having to use fuel with more and more alcohol in it) and that led me to this particular additive. Over time it cured the stumbling and stalling problem, and the Explorer is noticeably more responsive to the throttle. The cruise control also started working after 5 years with no one being able to detect a problem, that may just be coincidence because I can't explain how this product could help that situation, but nothing else did and it's working great now. The really small engines are easier to start now so it also helps (probably in older carburetors) with lawnmowers, chain saws, leaf blowers, string trimmers and so on (use this product in addition to regular 2-cycle oil). Don't expect an increase in gas mileage, I did think this product should boost it a bit but I haven't seen it on any of our four vehicles to date.

title: THESE ARE TOYS! - NOT for driving or fog
text:
Just received these an hour ago. You get what you pay for. These do in fact dissipate 6.15 Watts@12.3V as a pair. About 3 watts each. Since the efficiency is not listed, I will guess that they are about 75 - 80 lumens per Watt. So 450-480 lumens as a pair. Light color is narrow-band daylight.

They have no lens and are omni-directional so, THEY CANNOT BE USED AS DRIVING OR FOG LIGHTS without a focusing lens or reflector.

The 18 inch hook-up wires are very thin, I would guess 28 gauge or smaller.

At 12.3 Volts they got to hot to touch after just 15 minutes. Not sure how well these would work on a plastic car bumper for extended periods of no airflow.

Fun toys but they are nothing more than toys. The pair of these will light up the boot of my car very nicely.

ADDENDUM:
I tested these for a couple hours with a current limiting resistor and they stay cold. My kit bag only had a 7ohm 50W in it. But If I did the calculations correctly, these need to be limited to 210mA of current so they stay cold. I calculated the load at 55 ohms. I measured the car voltage at 13.8V. So a 5W dropping resistor of 10 ohms should do the trick to keep these from melting your car bumper.

These do only dissipate 2.4 Watts together as a pair if a proper limiting resistor is used. Still pretty bright, but not the same as when they dissipate 6 Watts and burn things.

USE AT YOUR OWN RISK

title: Recommended
text: I replaced the OEM filter which was solid black with these. Definitely easier to see the fuel. They work well and fit my motor. Price wasn't bad either. I'd recommend them.

title: The rear clip is my only concern
text:
Just installed, no issues there. The holes lined up within specs. Only one concern - the rear ones use double sided tape a clip for the top. They do supply another screw for an "optional" hole that needs to be drilled. Since my truck has less than 1,000 miles I'm not going to drill a hole, yet. However if the clips don't hold I'll have to.

Front guards are really nice and are secured well with no drilling.

The paint guard tape supplied isn't an exact fit. I'm guessing it's a generic pattern. Not a problem as they do cover the area that needs to be covered. You won't need the amount of water/soap solution they describe, but the mixing ratio is the important part.

They do look nice and are well made. I'm sure they will last for years and protect as described.

title: I recommend it
text:
Attractive, easily installed, fits perfectly. Now keep in mind I just installed it and have only driven about 100 miles with it installed.

A big plus is it doesn't use tape. You just remove and replace some plastic push connectors under the hood. I was very pleased with that!

title: Almost perfect
text: The cover is easy to install, looks great and does keep the bed dry. All in all it should be a 5, but I've tinkered with every way possible and can't keep it from bouncing/rippling at higher speeds. It's not noisy and doesn't appear to be anything that will immediately damage the material, but I'm sure - long term - it will cause extra wear. I'll follow up if it fails within a year or so. Take the rippling away and it's perfect!

title: Compact, Accurate - tough to read in bright sunlight
text:
First, they do light up and read accurately. They do seem water tight. Smaller that expected, but honestly that's a good thing for the application I used it for. The only negative is the numbers are difficult to read in bright sunlight.

Only installed for one day so we will see how longevity goes.

title: It's what I needed
text:
Needed a larger tank for vacation trips and big water days. This was the ticket. Haven't had it long, but the vent in the top seems to work to releases the expansion gas. I like the gauge on top, but it's not like the one on your car.

Not a negative, but for those considering this tank, keep in mind it's not portable. With 12 gallons of gas inside you won't be lifting it up and in to your boat.

title: Installation - Not recommended for the weak
text:
The style is very nice. I like the feel. It doesn't slip around the wheel. However:

Instructions on installation are incredibly poor. I'm in very good shape and above average strength. I really struggled getting this darn thing on. Average temperature day, as specified I stretched it out before attempting to install it. I did eventually get it on, but lets just say I won't have to go to the gym for a day or two. Literally worked up a sweat! Had to resort to using some plastic tree felling wedges to get it on - that worked, but be careful of damaging it!

Of course once I got it on - 20 minutes probably - I noticed it wasn't lined up perfectly. Only about a half inch from being perfect so, I Tugged and pulled and tried rubbing lightly and with force. It isn't moving. I'm going to wait for a sunny hot day to try it again. There's no way I'm pulling it off - even if I could - and reinstalling.

title: I cannot recommend these too highly!!!
text:
This is one of the best set of tires I have ever owned or driven on. For decades I have been an exclusively Michelin buyer & driver. I had only bought Continental tires once & hated them. When I began to look into buying tires for an AWD Cadillac STS, I was very surprised by the research I did and the reviews that I read. So, I took a chance, based on others recommendations. These tires have been excellent on wet and dry ground. They wear extremely well, so far. After more than 25,000 miles they were still looking fairly new. If I could fault them in any way, it would be that they are a little soft on hard turns, and are a bit noisy on badly paved roads--not too bad though! They are fun to drive on and handle well in almost every way. If I could fault them in any way, it would be that they are a little soft on hard turns, and are a bit noisy on roads with poor pavement conditions--not too bad though! They hardly ever hydroplane--it takes torrential downpour to happen, or an unavoidable incredibly large puddle to appear, before this occurs. They drive well in snow and have better than average traction on ice. These would be a confidence-builder to anyone afraid to drive in snow on highways or major thoroughfares. I was forced to have to drive home one evening in over 12 inches of unplowed snow. I was genuinely surprised by the grip and control I had while driving a good number of miles. I am sure that some of this was due to the car's all-wheel drive, traction control, and ABS braking. Still, I say these tires are a winning combination to work with these. I cannot recommend them too highly. These allowed me to look forward to the snow!

With the performance package on my STS, these are the rear tire size. The front tires are a different size: [[ASIN:B004QGZLJ4 Continental ExtremeContact DWS All-Season Tire-235/50R18 97Z]].

title: I cannot recommend these too highly!!!
text:
This is the best set of tires I have ever owned or driven on. For decades I have been an exclusively Michelin buyer & driver. I had only bought Continental tires once & hated them. When I began to look into buying tires for an AWD Cadillac STS, I was very surprised by the research I did and the reviews that I read. So, I took a chance, based on others recommendations. These tires have been excellent on wet and dry ground. They wear extremely well, so far. I have over 25,000 miles on them and they look fairly new still. They are fun to drive on and handle well in almost every way. If I could fault them in any way, it would be that they are a little soft on hard turns, and are a bit noisy on roads with poor pavement conditions--not too bad though! They hardly ever hydroplane--it takes a torrential downpour to happen, or an unavoidable incredibly large puddle to appear, before this occurs. They drive well in snow and have better than average traction on ice. These would be a confidence-builder to anyone afraid to drive in snow on highways or major thoroughfares. I was forced to have to drive home one evening in over 12 inches of snow. I was genuinely surprised at the grip and control I had while driving a good number of miles. I am sure that some of this was due to the car's all-wheel drive, traction control, and ABS braking. Still, these tires are a winning combination to work with these. I cannot recommend them too highly. I am looking forward to the snow!

I am purchasing a single tire at this time because I slammed into a huge pothole with sharp edges at pretty good speed and it weakened the sidewall with a small bubble. I am surprised that this was all the damage that was done! It sounded and felt a lot worse than that.

text: Forget reviews that say these do nothing, they still hit a deer.  Hey, nothing's 100%, but I'll tell a true story about deer whistles here:  Back around 2000 or thereabouts, the Farm Bureau Insurance folks in MS started giving these away.  The MS Highway Patrol put them on all their cars, having hit over 300 deer in the previous year.  With these simple devices on their vehicles, the next year they hit something like 3, and those were hit because one or both had come off in car washes.  That made me a believer.  You'll see deer perk up their ears and stand still or move away.  For such a small amount of money, it just can't hurt to have these one, and I have them on everything, including motorcycles.  Once you're over 35 mph, the whistle effect works and you're safer.

title: Get the right size!
text: I ordered an XL and the one they sent at first was a L.  Now, one big plus for these helmets is the ability to adjust the inside "band" for lack of a better term.  I was able to get the L on my head, but even loosening the band as much as possible, it was quite tight.  So I returned it and they're sending me an XL.  The return was super easy and as soon as it was on its way they shipped the XL I had originally ordered.  So unless something weird happens, I'll be very happy with this helmet.  The pull down eye shade I think will come in handy on sunny days and just to keep stuff out of my eyes, but I'll still probably wear shades as well.  Good quick return after the original wrong size sent.  Measure your head, and realize that these days most things coming from China, in my opinion, are not sized for our big American heads.  :)

title: A review and an install tip....
text: When I first bought my K longhorns, they were out of 1" clamps so mine came with larger clamps.  I read here that some folks used RIVCO clamps (1") and they worked.  I tried them, but they didn't do the job for a couple of reasons.  But here's the kicker:  I put on the K 1" clamps and they kept slipping no matter how tight I tightened the bolt on the clamp.  So I went to forums and someone said a guy at K told him to ditch the middle washer!  I tried it and it did the trick.  Now both my longhorn footpegs are solid, and I've no idea why they want that middle washer in there, but getting rid of it sure did make life easier, and my pegs don't move now when I put weight on them.  Great footpegs, the Longhorns, and now you can easily get the right size clamps here.  Also, doesn't hurt to watch a Youtube video or three about installing them.

Well...  no.  They don't fit right, and there is a key part that doesn't match up with the Kurakyn longhorn highway pegs, so barring trying to somehow file/cut off some steel and beautiful powdercoating on the rivco's, I'm sending them back.  And now all of sudden there is a suppy of the perfectly matched 1" clamps made by Kurakyn, and those are the ones you want, if you need 1" clamps.  Who wants a 90% solid attachment to highway pegs?  Not me.  And  Amazon is a third cheaper than buying them from K, looks like, with free shipping.  The blacked out highway pegs are the bomb, by the way.  Look great, super adjustable, good quality.

title: A motorcycle keychain is a different animal....
text: You don't want a lot of keys on your bike's keychain, and I like this one.  You put your belt through it, and then it has what looks like a tiny seatbelt release button with your bike's manufacturer's logo on it, and down drops the key to your machine and another one or two.  I keep just the bike key, key to my Viking saddlebags, and a house key, and so there's no heavy weight dangling from the ignition, which on my bike is on the left hand side. title: Run small, order a size larger....
text:
The large fits me perfectly, but I'm between a medium and a large, and normally a large pair of gloves that are too big, long in the fingers, is fine. But for riding I did want snug gloves and the large is perfect on me. I saved a few bucks getting a pair from the seller someone had tried on and returned, and notice that has happened several times. If you normally wear a large, I'd think these would not work. Order up.
Also, I have a suggestion for the seller: Just change out the sizing tags! Your large gloves will not fit a man who normally buys large, so call those medium, which is honest. Your XL gloves are probably actually large for us Americans. Just sayin'.... Since this is an ongoing complaint by customers, switch the sizing tags in the gloves and you'll get fewer returns I'd think.

title: Nice helmet, especially for the price....
text:
Good looking, well made. Hey, if you don't want to have a real helmet, and are more worried about how you look in a mirror - mushroom head haters need not apply - you aren't paying attention: We only get one head. Protect it. It's a tight fit but I'm sure it'll break in, and you don't want a loose helmet. For the price, and it being a Bell, I'm very happy with the helmet.
As an update, all helmets should fit you snugly. I put on a knit hat and then the helmet, wore it for maybe 15-20 minutes in the house, took it off and the knit cap off, and put the helmet back on. It felt broken in already like I'd worn it for many rides! So, if you think it's too tight, try that simple trick and maybe it will help you break it in a bit before you even ride. It's winter here so that's why this occurred to me.

title: My third Xelement item....
text: I have a concealed carry vest from Xelement that I like a lot, and years ago had their "Executioner" armored jacket, and it was great.  Decided to go with this one this time, the "Frenzy" jacket, since it does have a little reflective piping, not much but a little.  I'll add that descriptions vary regarding inside pockets, but it does have two gun pockets inside secured by snaps just like their vest.  And inside there are elastic loops for a pistol and also for a spare mag, so that's very nice.  The leather is good, and also the venting and the use of stretchy cloth make it a good 3 season jacket.  You can pay twice as much for a jacket of this quality, but I'll stick with Xelement.  One note:  I'd work the zippers, all of them, and there are a lot, and add a touch of vaseline if they are hanging up.  My experience has been if you do that when you first get the jacket, the zippers will function forever, or a very long time, with no further maintenance.  Also, as to size, I'm 5'10" and 160 lbs and ordered an XL as I always do.  A large would have fit me far too tight.  After all, it's not like we always just have on a t-shirt underneath these jackets.  The zip-out lining is also a nice feature, but won't keep you very warm on a cool day, so sweatshirt/hoodie and a t-shirt under the jacket is my cure for spring and fall cooler rides.

title: This fits my 2021 Honda Rebel ABS SE perfectly....
text: Was a little hesitant about buying this - it is not cheap!!! - but the product page here on Amazon says it will fit a Honda Rebel 500 from 2017-21, and the manufacturer's website says this seat, model 84000, will fit the 2021, which is what I have, and Amazon was about forty bucks cheaper than direct from Mustang, so I gave it a shot and put it on today.  Fast shipping, and it fits like a dream.  No idea why Amazon says when i put in my bike's year and model it warns me it will NOT fit my 2021 Rebel 500, because it fits.  Here's a tip:  the old seat which is quite hard, and I have two artificial hips, brand new like the bike and need more cushion than the OEM seat, has one advantage over the Mustang.  The tabs at the back of the seat where you screw the seat onto the bike have built-in rubber bushings.  Since the Mustang just has metal tabs with no cushion at all, there was a slight movement, rattle, after screwing the new seat on.  Short trip to the hardware store for 4 rubber washers and problem solved.  Fits very tight, looks great, and for people like me who need the extra cushioning, this is a great seat.  Is it worth over three hundred bucks?  Literally of course not, but then again, life is short, and bike rides should not have to be shorter, so I would recommend buying it here, since Amazon does save you about forty dollars over the direct from Mustang price.

title: Worked when others have failed.
text:
This unit worked were others have failed. The ball joints that I was trying to remove were on a 1999 Miata. Since they are the original items there was nearly 20 years of corrosion holding it on. I purchased a older ball joint tool here at Amazon years ago, but it failed to budge the studs and it broke in the process. The GearWrench unit came highly recommended by other reviewers here so I decided to give it a try. Within a few minutes of using this tool the ball joint separated from the driver side knuckle with a satisfying 'bang'. However, on the passenger side I had to use a combination of hitting the knuckle (where the ball joint stud threads through) with a hammer, and heating the same area with a propane torch, before this tool could knock the stud out. So sometimes you need a combination of heat, beat, and hope.

As can be seen from the attached photo, the GearWrench units (silver in color) is larger in size, applies more force through a larger screw with a finer pitch and being position further from the pivot point, and has some height adjustability to accommodate different size ball joints . The older unit (black in color) bent the pivot pin from all of the force I was applying before. I'm just glad that it didn't snap in half

title: Works well after one week, error code has not returned after 20 trips.
text: After some research into the P0446 code that was produced by my 2001 Toyota Avalon I tested the vacuum switching valve on the charcoal canister and found it to be faulty. After all this Toyota has over 203,000 miles on it. I purchase this Dorman part as a replacement and after one week of operation and over 20 trips the error code has not returned. This generic replacement for the vacuum switching valve is Made in China. It's dimensions are nearly identical to the Toyota part, and the vacuum hoses fit snugly on to the nipples. The threading on the part to secure it to the charcoal canister were not smoothly formed so it took more effort to screw it back on. The electrical connector has a nice firm fit as well and clips on the the factory connection securely. Since this component is under the vehicle and exposed to the environmental elements, lets see how well it holds up to winter and the salt sprays common to my area. To be continued

The imposter light was actually not bad. The light was bright, and the pressure switch seemed to function. It came with 2 cr2016 batteries labeled Chao Chuang. Looking at the Amazon site this light is usually listed as LED-237-2BK(5)-p under various names, and costs between $.81-2.29. For that price it is a good deal (as to long term durability---??) AS it is, The actual LRI proton II light is about $ 7-10.
I have sent the imposter light back to Amazon, and will see if they make this right. Since many of the reviews have stated this type of problem, WHY has AMAZON not fixed this?

title: Really like it but it smells
text:
This organizer has about everything you could want in a trunk organizer. It's made of a fairly thick canvas, (not the thin, shiny fabric others have.)

I especially like that the cooler is stored in its own separate pouch till I need it, but then it also fits in one of the cubicles when full. Similar units had permanently attached coolers, or they were stored in one of the cubicles, leaving only 2 full size available without having to deal with a smaller opening made by the cooler's zipper. It's also has a good amount of insulation and plenty of room. The cover that fits over it to keep the sun out is great if you don't have tinted windows. That, and the dividers sides are pretty sturdy. It's very versatile and fits both horizontally and vertically in a Honda CRV.

I the only issue I have is the smell just won't go away.

I let it air out for about a week when I first got it. Then I sprayed with Frebreze, but here I am over a month later and it still stinks.

It almost smells like a cat urinated on it. Maybe it's unique to my order as I didn't see other reviews complain about it.

I passed the return window so I sprayed it with a stronger freshener made for pet odors and I'm hoping that takes care of it.

It's far enough back in the SUV that it's not overwhelming, until I open the trunk. Then it hits me in the face. I had left one cubical stocked with items I like to keep on hand but I've already had to wash the towel & sneakers I had in there over the last month as the fabric absorbed the smell.

It would definitely be a five star if not for this smell.

title: Beautiful, but will it stay? 2021 Ford Escape Nope!
text:
Update 2 weeks later. As suspected, the tape on the longest horizontal edge did not stick. I can easily press down on that side and hear the tape try to tack, but then pops back up. Therefore, I only have 1 strip of tape holding the plate down. I don't even think the sides are sticking. Very disappointing. I've owned my brand new car all of 30 days with a flimsy strip of tape holding this down. I suspect as soon as the car washes start, that may be the end of the adhesion. I followed all the directions, but the 2021 ford escape does not have a completely level surface , and the tape is just not strong enough to grip. How disappointed now that I am stuck with it until they fall off and leave behind a mess on my paint job.

Excited to peel off the protective layer, these are beautiful. Just installed them today. I followed the tips and directions, but I am somewhat surprised to hear the 3M tape "unsticking" near one end that is closest to the interior of car. The 2021 Ford Escape's sills curve upward slightly on each end (there is no 100% level area). As I was pressing down for some time, as instructed, when I let up I could hear the tape lift off right around that slant upwards. If these begin to settle in permanently, I will add the star back. But I should not be hearing the tape pop back up, and this is a chance I took with a car I haven't yet had 30 days so far.

title: As Expected with Fit, Quality, Condition - Simple Installation but You Tube Helps those First Timers
text:
My car's rear wiper had rubber tearing away from the wiper blade. Wiping with torn rubber can mark or etch the glass on the hatch and my mechanic offered to put it on for me. (There is no profit for auto mechanic shops to sell a gazillion blades for every make).

First, it came out of the package in expected condition. No oils or anything like some reviewers. Just a brand new wiper blade. Secondly, it fit perfectly to my make and model. Third, the instructions are in English. Okay, about that third part...keep in mind, I am rarely involved with wiper blades, I read and re-read the instructions, something about separating this and that and outward arrows. For me, after trying several maneuvers, gave up and went to You Tube to actually see someone doing it. Wow, how simple that made it. So, if you are not used to changing out wiper blades, it might help to watch first. This does not detract at all from my rating, because the instructions were correct. It was my interpretation that got off kilter.

title: Meguiar's Does it Again - Top Performance Cleaner
text: Great all purpose cleaner by one of the premier companies in the car detailing business. All of their products never fail to amaze me at their effectiveness. This cleaner is great for cleaning interior surfaces, running boards, wheels and tires, prior to applying any dressing onto a clean surface. This really cleans, as evident when dressing an auto for final show - usually I note dirt and contaminants continue to come off with the dressing rags, but this one leaves behind very little dirt. Not to be used as a car wash, by my standards, but only because it is designed to be a cleaner and not a protectant. Usually, Meguiar's Gold is used for washing the exterior, but this is good for getting bug remnants off if needed. Overall, anything in the Meguair's line is going to be over and above others I've tried.

title: Works at the root cause of aging and neglect - Really works
text: This is a good protectant because it restores natural oils or moisture needed in plastics and vinyls. It is not high gloss, but does add a sheen to interior parts. Also, the fact that it has UV protection prevents further fading to the original color. I have always used Meguiar's products and nothing else on my vehicles, and people tell me all the time that my cars look like they are in mint condition, even when I let housekeeping go too long. There aren't any added chemicals that don't belong on vehicle parts, and the results (and restorers) last a long time. If you go too long between regular cleanings, this product will make up for lost time. I love not having that greasy feel like most other protectants cause - there just no other comparison to a Meguiar product which actually works at the root cause and not just fix the symptoms.

title: Keeps the polished, waxed and deep conditioned paint like new -  Will not use anything else
text:
The Meguiar's Gold Classic will always be my favorite. The syrupy mixture is just the first sign that it adds protection and shine to the paint, as well as conditions. We used the Meguiar's deep crystal (purple) and regular car washes by Meguiar's recently, but over time the paint lost its' luster. Happy to return to the Gold Class so my car's paint will rebuild that deep polished appearance. It is great for removing contaminants, but will take a little more elbow grease with this formula. Generally, if you start with a well polished and waxed vehicle, the Gold formula will retain those properties. Used on a long neglected or improper car wash application takes a little more effort to get back down to the overcoat to start fresh again. I only wished my local stores carried this so there would not have been a gap between washings. I will use nothing else, as nothing else performs this well. (I have cleaned, polished & waxed vehicles in the past and followed up with Gold, and the results are identical). Great product.

PS - The seam on the plastic bottle leading up to the cap was molded poorly enough that when un-screwing the cap sliced my finger pretty good. If I could rate a packing review for the actual bottle I would say that this hazard caused me TWO injuries, since I forgot about the seam issue later on. Yikes!

title: I see the light now....
text: This is a terrific set of safety lights. Installation was as easy as could be and only took a few minutes. You might look at these and think they couldn't be very bright but, surprise, these really put out the light. The flashing patterns add additional safety with the frequent changes. I was really kind of blown away with the ease of installation and the efficiency of the lights and the distance from which they can be seen, especially at night. The magnet that goes on the door frame to turn them off is very powerful so exact location is not necessary and you can test your setup because the magnets can be moved until you use the adhesive pads. The 3M adhesive is very strong and lasts a long time. Clean the area around the pad before you attach the light or magnet because you have a few minutes to relocate either before the adhesive really sticks. As soon as I installed a set on my car I ordered another set for my other car. More than 6 months later they are still working well. I highly recommend these flashing lights for your safety.

title: Poor explanation of what they really are. Be careful if you're looking for waterproof lights
text:
I buy lots of stuff from Amazon. I would rate these no stars if I had a choice. They have an ok return policy, but if you happen to open an item and then find out it's not as advertised, then you won't get your total expense back. I researched LED waterproof tail lights for my boat trailer for hours and then settled on this Wesbar kit. It leaks more than Noah's boat. Submersible anything, in salt water, that is not waterproof lasts for about two trailer dips in the sea. $64 bucks for these and I could have gotten the 10 dollar ones with the 357 bulbs that last about the same time. (No longer)Totally disappointed. This product is expensive for what you get.

I'm going to backtrack a little on this review. Although I still think the light set is overpriced, because the electronics are sealed, the lights work as advertised, so far. I've have them under water, without disconnecting about 10 times and they are still working fine. Before I installed them, I sealed around all of the exposed edges and especially where the connection wires exit the shell. In the Chesapeake, the saline content is between 20-30%. I'll have a better indication of how they last when I'm in Florida where the saline content is around 60%. Soooo. I'm going to give them 3.5 stars for now. [[ASIN:B001VD5NPM Wesbar LED Submersible Trailer Light Kit - U80]]

One last thing. Lots of products listed on Amazon should have a better explanation to make it easier for the consumer to make a decision.

title: Fits Hitachi RB24EAP blower, but you have to take the whole thing apart to replace
text: Hitachi RB24EAP replacement coil. Was surprised how much of the blower you have to take apart to get to it (both the green sections and the fan have to come off) but its not technically that difficult to do. You will need Phillips and two different sizes of hex wrenches as well remove the fan which is held on with a bolt (mine was loose as well but came off easily with a crescent wrench). The one to take off the coil is 4mm hex and its on there really tight. Notice that it does have a gap in there between the engine and the coil, you will need to spin that around a couple times to see what the gap is as it passes the magnets. I used a couple pieces of paper together to estimate the gap. Once you loosen the coil and replace it, you will have to make sure the clearance is the same and it doesn't rub on the motor. Then reassemble. Because of the way you have to take everything apart, the wires and trigger will come out, so take a picture before you take off the left side (looking from the back) so that you see the routing of the wires and trigger. Fired up after putting back together. I replaced the coil because the blower would run for a while then would stop for no reason and no spark, until it cooled down then it would work again. Coil overheating and stopping working was my diagnosis.

title: As Advertised

title: Prone to Warpage?
text:
Bought a pair of these at a good price compared to Subaru/Brembo STI rotors which cost ~$660/pair from an online discount Subaru dealer.

they seemed to perform pretty well initially but I started getting severe brake shudder after using the rotors for about 12,000 miles. I checked the rotor runout with a dial indicator and it was 0.006" which is twice the factory allowed spec. i ended up having to get the rotors turned (two cuts) to get the runout back within spec which eliminated the brake shudder.

as far as appearance the black center section remained rust free through winter driving which included exposure to road salt.

UPDATE: We used to have mandatory annual safety inspections. The tire store tech severly overtorqued the lug nuts on our SUV when he pulled the wheel to check the brake pads. Now i'm wondering if they did the same thing to our Subaru and that may have caused the rotors to warp?

title: Upgrade Your Hanger Bushings
